## 2026-09-15 — M51 Increment 4 / T4: the promise is named as the promise, and the worktree axis takes its **own row** rather than being folded into an index axis

The cut's substance lands unchanged — *"Before phase 6, all-or-nothing"* is stated as **the promise** every row serves, the config-layer row's *worktree untouched* is corrected to describe **that axis's index mechanism** and explicitly not a claim about the working tree, and `validation.md` registers `finalize.rollback-conflict` (blocking · neither tier — un-keyed · outside `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`) in the per-increment shape its three siblings use. The M45-audit sentence in this log (*"every path jigc's own staging contributed"*) is kept **true** by T3's restore rather than narrowed by an edit at the 1.0 pin. Three writing calls the cut left open:

**The worktree axis is a sibling row, not an amendment to the index row.** The cut said *"the row gains the worktree axis"*; written out, that puts a **4a–6** axis inside a row whose first column reads **5–6**, which is a false cell in the column that exists to say *when*. The captures differ in span for a real reason — the worktree capture must precede `gitignore::ensure` and the stamp refresh, both of which run before the stage — so the axes are two, and the table already carries two rows for the milestone record on exactly that idiom. The correction to the index row's parenthesis **points forward at the new row**, so neither locus can be read alone and reach the pre-M51 conclusion.

**The promise gains a *stated exception*, because without one it is now false in a cell the product deliberately enters.** A compare-and-swap refusal leaves jigc's bytes on disk: the restore would have to overwrite a third party's edit to be all-or-nothing, which is the loss the family exists to prevent. Writing *all-or-nothing* flat and letting the row carry the exception is the shape this task exists to end — a promise in one place, contradicted by a mechanism in another — so the exception is stated where the promise is, bounded (*only where restoring would destroy someone else's bytes*) and obligated (*every such survival is named* by a blocking finding). That is a **narrowing of the promise's wording to what the code does**, and it is admissible here where narrowing *"every path jigc's own staging contributed"* was not, because that sentence is made true by the fix while this one is made false by the CAS decision the fix requires.

**The cut's line cites were already stale at the cut's own commit** (`1c89033f`: `finalize.md:178` is the `1 preflight` row and `:183` carries no header), so both loci were resolved by their quoted content — the parenthesis holding *worktree untouched*, and the *Before phase 6* lead — which is unambiguous in the file. No roadmap byte is moved for it: the cite drifts again with every wave, and the roadmap prose beside it names the clauses.

*Done:* `dev/gate` green (full, unscoped), the inventory-equality arm in `crates/cli/tests/config_layer_preimage.rs` on `repo_posture.rs`'s three-link mold — **red first at the section-absent panic**, since T3 had minted the code, wired it to every door and registered it in `FINALIZE_FAMILY` while the inventory named it nowhere — and the grep check over the reconciled clauses exits 0. Link 2 is **driven rather than read off a registry**: this family's production-side set is *the rows of `CONFIG_LAYER_SPECS` the transaction rewrites*, not a member enum of codes, so the arm compares the codes a raced `ConcurrentEdit` run renders against the same door failing the same way with nothing racing, and asserts the difference **is** this increment's literal.

## 2026-09-15 — M51 Increment 4 / T3: the worktree rollback is **compare-and-swap**, and the third value is what makes it one

The finalize transaction rewrites exactly two files in the worktree — `.jigc/.gitignore` (the shared amend) and `.jigc/version` (the stamp refresh) — and until now rolled back neither: the four captured-pre-image axes are all **index** axes, so a refused finalize restored the index and left ` M .jigc/.gitignore` / ` M .jigc/version` standing while its own frame said *"nothing was committed"* (driven at `93407e98`). Both now restore, no exemption taken. What follows are the elaborations the cut did not name, each of which was a fork:

**The pre-image is not enough; the family needs jigc's own post-write image, and `None` there means one thing only.** D4's restore is compare-and-swap, so every entry carries the bytes jigc wrote and restores only while the file still holds them — which the Phase 4a capture cannot supply, because jigc has not written yet. So the write sites report: `gitignore::ensure`'s report decides whether anything was written at all, and `refresh_version_stamp` reports from inside itself. The value is `Option`, and the two readings it must **not** conflate are *"jigc wrote nothing at this path this run"* (the fan-out arms never refresh the stamp; an amend that finds nothing missing writes not a byte) and *"jigc wrote identical bytes"* — only the first may never be rolled back. Two dispositions fall out of that and are stated in code: **a path jigc never wrote raises no conflict however much it changed** (there is nothing of jigc's to put back), and **`pre == post` is a no-op, not a conflict** (jigc's write destroyed nothing, so a concurrent edit over it lost nothing either). A read-back that *fails* leaves `post` at `None` and the entry is treated as never-written: jigc cannot prove what it put there, and the safe direction is not to overwrite. Symmetrically, a *current* file that is unreadable takes the conflict arm rather than the restore arm, for the same reason in the other direction.

**The two writers hang off different roots**, so the family resolves each path through a declared `ConfigLayerHome` rather than assuming one: `gitignore::ensure` is handed `jigc_root` — in a fan-out the **main** checkout's `.jigc/`, which the worktree binds to — while `write_version_stamp` writes under `repo_root`. They coincide in the ordinary single checkout; the enum exists so the case where they do not is decided rather than inherited from the index axis, which keys both at `repo_root`.

**The disposition joins the shipped pathspec list rather than starting a second one.** `jigc_config_layer_pathspecs()` becomes a projection of `task::CONFIG_LAYER_SPECS`, whose three rows each answer *does finalize rewrite this?* — two `Rewritten`, and `.jigc/config` `Untouched(<reason>)`, which is §6/A1's named trap written down: a worktree pre-image over a **directory** is a different shape (absent-means-delete over N files, including files this run never saw). One enumeration, two families, so a fourth pathspec cannot join one without answering the other — and the fence's driven half lifts the staged set out of the binary's **own** stage-failure message rather than restating it, which is what catches the real hazard (a stage that grows a pathspec no row covers). Applied mutants: the directory promoted to `Rewritten` reddens it, and so does a hand-pushed fourth pathspec.

**The conflict is printed beside every door's frame and never in place of it**, through one helper (`task::carry_rollback_conflicts`, the `gitignore::emit_ack` shape this increment already ships) that renders the house finding line to **stderr** whatever the format — presentation beside the result, so the `--format json` document on stdout still parses as one value — and folds the code into the door's `Outcome` so the invocation log names it. The door's own error is untouched: a hook rejection keeps its verbatim stderr and its frame, a stage failure keeps its routed `finalize.stage-failed`. **The one Err arm that builds no `Outcome` provably carries no conflict**, and that is a property rather than a gap: `finalize.retire-untrackable` is adjudicated one statement above the unlink, which runs *before* `gitignore::ensure` and before the stage's refresh — so on that arm jigc has rewritten neither file and the family is uniformly never-written. `finalize.rollback-conflict` is registered in `cli::render::FINALIZE_FAMILY` (producer `cli::task`, keyed at **the file path**, so two raced paths are two findings and never one `(code, null)`) with its contract sub-table row; `design/validation.md`'s inventory row is T4's.

**The conflicted pre-image is preserved, not discarded** — parked in the gitignored `.jigc/displaced/` workbench (`relocate`'s `WORKBENCH_SUBDIR`, already an `ENTRIES` member) under a process-unique name, so a second refused finalize parks beside the first rather than overwriting the only copy of those bytes; the finding names **both** paths and the act that reconciles them. When the park itself fails, the finding says so rather than naming a path that is not there.

**`version_stamp_rollback.rs`'s two *"index-only, by declaration"* assertions are flipped in the same commit** — they pin the behaviour this task reverses, so they are the atomic unit, not collateral. The confidence audit's minor item 3 declared the residue acceptable on the ground that both files are jigc-owned maintenance the next store-writing op rewrites identically; that is false of a file the **user co-owns**, which is what G-18 and F3's spike drove.

*Done:* `cargo test -p cli config_layer_preimage::` (4 arms: the manufactured `{stage failure, hook rejection} × {untouched, concurrently edited}` space over both files, the absent-pre-image delete, the never-written no-op, and the totality fence) and `cargo test -p cli version_stamp_rollback::` pass; `dev/gate` green full and unscoped. The suite's injectors are real git and run **inside** the transaction — a rejecting `pre-commit`, and a **required clean filter** on a file under `.jigc/config/` for the stage cell — so the race axis is a genuine interleave rather than a simulation. **Declared bound, unchanged:** the single capture point covers the finalize arms only; `gitignore::ensure`'s three non-finalize callers (`setup`, `milestone create`, `milestone provision`) are covered by T1's amend, not by this capture.

## 2026-09-15 — M51 Increment 4 / T2: the ack's **channel** is decided by the door's JSON arm, and `setup`'s field was refused by M48's own fence

Every door that amends `.jigc/.gitignore` now names the entries it appended, from one renderer (`render::gitignore_amend_line`) over T1's report, with the caller set ⇔-fenced as `gitignore::IGNORE_DOORS` (four production writers, four `Names` rows, zero exemptions). One thing the cut did not anticipate decided *where* the line goes, and it is worth pinning because it will recur at every pinned envelope until Increment 5:

**Carrying the report as an eighth `SetupSummary` field fails to compile against M48's standing text/JSON parity fence** (`crates/cli/tests/text_json_parity_axis.rs`), which destructures that struct **exhaustively, no `..`**, and makes every bound field name its envelope key. That is the fence working, not obstructing: a value the text prints and the envelope withholds is the gap it exists to catch. Closing it means declaring a key on a pinned envelope — the one-way act **D5** governs and Increment 5 owns — so the field is refused and the report rides beside the summary instead (`gitignore::emit_ack`; `setup::run` returns the pair).

So the rule the four doors follow, stated once rather than per door: **a door whose `--format json` arm is a structured, pinned object prints the line beside it** — stdout on agent/human text, **stderr** under `--format json`, the shipped Stream-discipline shape `migrate`'s byte-floor advisory already uses — **and a door whose whole ack rides the envelope's `text` key puts the line in that prose**, where a driver reads it with no second channel. `setup` and `finalize` are the first kind; `milestone create` and `provision` the second. The beside-channel is *not* a parity gap being hidden from the fence: it is the same sanctioned non-gap the composed-output advisories ride, and under JSON the fact is emitted, not withheld.

**The finalize row names three doors over one writer** (`jigc task finalize` and both `jigc milestone finalize` arms all reach `task::try_execute_finalize_plan`, which prints nothing itself). The (a) fence enumerates *writer* sites and cannot see a caller that dropped its ack, so the pairing is its own fence: in every production fn that runs the shared executor, executor calls == `emit_ack` calls. Proven red by an applied mutant — deleting the `squash: false` arm's call reddens it at *2 time(s) / 1 time(s)*.

*Done:* `cargo test -p cli gitignore_writer_acks::` passes (4 arms: the ⇔ fence, its detector-discriminates arm, the executor/ack pairing fence, and one driven cell per registry member with a hard panic for a member without one), and `dev/gate` green full and unscoped.

**Basis — driven or source-read at `8a2cd510`, not carried from the settle record. Two readings correct the record's own wording, and one of them decides where the loss actually is.**

- **The D4 cell reproduces verbatim at this sha.** The advocate's own spike ([`advocates/f3-spike3.sh`](completions/artifacts/M51/advocates/f3-spike3.sh)) re-run: a worktree `.jigc/.gitignore` carrying `# my own note - secrets live here` + `my-private-dir/` and missing `displaced/`, a rejecting `pre-commit`, `jigc task finalize` → **exit 1**, *"nothing was committed"*, the file rewritten to canonical `ENTRIES`, `git status --porcelain` **empty**, and `git log --all -p -- .jigc/.gitignore | grep -c my-private-dir` → **0**. Increments 1–3 did not touch it.

Increment 3's `setup.dirty-install-path` guard does **not** fire here, and that is structural rather than accidental: its predicate is a conjunction (*differs before the install writes, **and still differs** once it has*), and the whole-file clobber is exactly what makes the second ask read clean. So at `setup` the bytes die **silently and unrecoverably at exit 0 with nothing committed to point at** — not *landed*; the priority the roadmap's declared bounds record still inverts the same way, and `setup` is still the caller that justifies the amend. *(This also makes true what [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md):52 and [validation.md](design/validation.md)'s Increment-3 row already classify `.jigc/.gitignore` as — a file `setup` **merges into** rather than rewrites whole.)*

With T1 landed and T3 not, a hook-rejected finalize leaves the user's line intact but keeps jigc's appended entries (and a refreshed `.jigc/version`) in the worktree — so T3's red step is *"the transaction did not restore what it rewrote"*, never a byte-loss repro, and the roadmap's *Proves* sentence is delivered by T1 and T3 **together**.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 3 / T2: the dirty-install predicate is **two asks of one question**, and the door does not stage what it refuses

`jigc setup` now refuses its install commit over bytes it did not write (`setup.dirty-install-path`, `--force` the single consent). Two elaborations the settle and the cut did not carry, both forced by driving rather than reading, recorded because each changes what the guard *is*:

- **The predicate is dirty-before-the-install ∧ dirty-after-it**, not the single pre-write ask alone. The pre-write leg is the settle's (§1) and is what makes idempotence and upgrade clean by construction. But it refuses over paths `setup` **regenerates whole**: the cut's own shipped-decision warning (`adapter_artifact.rs:476`) was one instance, and the full gate found a second no artifact names — `managed_vs_foreign.rs`'s documented *"re-run `jigc setup`"* recovery route, which meets a stale `.jigc/version` **by design**. Asking the same git question again over the settled pathspec immediately before the commit **derives** the discriminator (*does `setup` preserve what it finds here?*) instead of enumerating it as a per-path ownership list a new install path could be forgotten out of — and it is the honest reading of *"would this commit carry bytes `setup` did not write"*, because a path whose pre-existing bytes the install overwrote carries none. `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, a wrapped foreign `pre-commit`, a populated `packs.yaml` and a floor-carrying `.jigc/.gitignore` are subjects (merged, so the bytes survive); `.jigc/AGENT.md`, `.jigc/version` and the guide artifact are not (rewritten whole). *Declared bound:* an uncommitted hand-edit of a regenerated artifact **on an upgrade** is dirty on both legs though the user's bytes are already gone — a loud false alarm `--force` clears, never a silent sweep.
- **The refusal stages the install paths it will commit and holds back exactly the ones it names.** The roadmap's *"the eight install paths stay written and staged"* reads past the index-only cell: `git add` on an `MM` path (worktree == `HEAD`) replaces the adopter's staged blob with the worktree's bytes, so staging-then-refusing re-enacts the very loss the index axis was added to catch — the blob named by no commit and no index entry — one step earlier. Data loss beats a message that reads slightly wide over one listed path, and the finding lists those paths, so which are held back is on the surface.

`--no-verify` is **kept** at this door on §5's re-recorded basis, corrected in the source: the user-hook half is struck with its falsifying datum (setup preserves a pre-existing hook and then skips it — re-driven), and the self-trigger half now carries the whole behaviour, which it can only do because this refusal closed the cell the struck half was covering. *Joined, not created:* `run_setup` funnels through `Outcome::failure()`, so this code reaches the printed surface and not the invocation log — M50's declared identity-funnel class.

Cut [Increment 3](implementation/roadmap.md) (*`setup` refuses its install commit over bytes it did not write*) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `61f05c01` (tree clean; Increments 1 and 2 landed in full). **Basis — driven or source-read at `61f05c01`, not carried from the settle record. Four readings the record does not carry are recorded here; two of them are load-bearing on the cut, and one is a defect no artifact names.**

- **The increment's own cell reproduces at the current sha** — Increments 1 and 2 did not touch it. Driven in a `bare` rig: `CLAUDE.md` committed, then edited and **never staged** (` M CLAUDE.md`) → `jigc setup` **exit 0**, `git show HEAD:CLAUDE.md` carries `UNSTAGED WIP SECRET` inside `chore(jigc): install jigc workspace config`, and `git status --short` is **empty**.
- **The rejecting-hook cell reproduces too.** Driven: a pre-existing `.git/hooks/pre-commit` rejecting `AWS_SECRET`, plus an uncommitted `AWS_SECRET=hunter2` line in the committed `CLAUDE.md` → `jigc setup` **exit 0** and the secret is in HEAD. Setup **wrapped** the user's hook (its managed block is spliced in ahead of it) and then skipped it with `--no-verify` — §5's falsifying datum, re-driven.
- **The pathspec is eight paths on the default profile, measured rather than counted from the source.** Driven: the install commit carries `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/skills/jigc/SKILL.md`, `.jigc/.gitignore`, `.jigc/AGENT.md`, `.jigc/config/.gitkeep`, `.jigc/config/packs.yaml`, `.jigc/version`, `CLAUDE.md` — the `pre-commit` hook at the default `.git/hooks/` is not committable and is correctly absent.
- **A third cell is silent data loss, it is in no artifact, and it decides the predicate's shape.** Driven: `CLAUDE.md` committed as `v0`, edited to `v1-STAGED-ONLY` and `git add`ed, then the **worktree** restored to `v0` (`MM`, worktree == HEAD, index ≠ HEAD) → `jigc setup` **exit 0**, HEAD carries `v0` + jigc's line, `git status` is clean, and `v1-STAGED-ONLY` is named by **no commit and no index entry**. A literal worktree-only comparison is blind to it. So the predicate is **both axes** — *a path HEAD records whose **index or worktree** bytes differ from HEAD* — which is what B1's own correction offers (*"keep `decide_carryover` **and** add the worktree axis"*) and what "dirty relative to HEAD" means in git's own vocabulary; mechanically it is one `git status --porcelain` over the pathspec, asked before any write.
- **Untracked (`??`) is excluded, and that is a stated green cell rather than a silent narrowing.** Driven: on a **born** HEAD an untracked `CLAUDE.md` carrying user prose is committed into the install commit today at exit 0. It stays that way, for two recorded reasons — M30 audit finding 1 (`setup.rs:1617-1625`: setup owns making its install footprint tracked, or the first managed commit leaves it untracked) and Increment 2's `SETUP_UNBORN_EXEMPTION`, which keeps the on-ramp open; excluding `??` is also what makes an **unborn HEAD clean by construction**, with no special case: every pre-existing file there reports `??`. Nothing is lost in this cell, and the two committing-door cells above are exactly where bytes die.
- **The guard must be pathspec-scoped and must ask the *conditional* pathspec, or it breaks a shipped decision.** *(Source read + driven.)* `setup_refuses_to_clobber_a_user_modified_guide_and_routes_it` (`adapter_artifact.rs:476`) installs, **hand-edits the committed `.claude/skills/jigc/SKILL.md`**, and re-runs `setup` expecting **exit 0 + an advisory** (M48 Increment 10: a user-owned guide is dropped from `guide_file`, so the pathspec never claims it). A candidate set built from the *unconditional* path list would refuse there and contradict M48. `guide_ownership` is already decided **before any write**, so the conditional set is computable pre-write; the same holds for `seed_secrets_gitignore`'s zero-commit signal, `resolve_hooks_dir` + `committable_hook_path`, and the `git_path_ignored` filter. Driven, separately: an unrelated staged `feature.txt` is untouched today and must stay a green cell.
- **Two cites in the increment text are stale and are corrected here before anything is edited** (the Increment 10 discipline, applied early). *(Source read.)* `finalize.md:159` is the *parallel hand-editing* bullet; the *"Every task-minting door"* sentence the scope widens lives at **`finalize.md:173`**. `setup.rs:1603`'s `--no-verify` rationale moved under Increment 2's insertion and is now at **`setup.rs:1611`**. `surface-contract.md:123` and `assistant-adapter.md:52` resolve as written. The guide cites Increment 9 owes resolve too: `MIGRATING.md:38` and `QUICKSTART.md:176` carry the gate's subject, and the *"jigc never passes `--no-verify`"* universal lives at **`MIGRATING.md:39`** and **`QUICKSTART.md:161`** — two homes the roadmap's Increment 9 row names without cites.
- **The refusal reuses Increment 2's shipped seam, and the identity is free.** *(Source read.)* `commit_install` already stages, then re-probes posture, then commits, surfacing `InstallCommitRejection::Posture` as a blocking finding through `install` → `run` → `render::setup_block` → exit 1 — so the refusal lands beside it as a sibling variant and needs no new surface. `setup.dirty-install-path` has **zero** occurrences anywhere in `crates/`, `design/`, `packs/` or `implementation/`. `force` is already classified `ArgToken::Plain(PlainValue::Other)` and `setup`'s `BehalfDoor` row carries `argv: &["setup"]`, so adding the flag reddens neither M50's total argument classification nor Increment 2's leaf registry; `Command::Setup` becoming a struct variant is a one-line change to `cli::tests::setup_parses`.

The restoring half is Increment 4's amend-to-union (`gitignore::ensure`'s `setup` caller is named in its declared bounds). The finding states what is true — no install commit was made, the install files are written and staged — and claims nothing about the worktree.

- **The un-sniffability measurement holds, and it is the reason the seam subject must be typed.** Driven: a provisioned fan-out worktree answers `git -C <wt> symbolic-ref -q HEAD` with **exit 1** — byte-identical to a user's detached HEAD. A path-shape or exit-code guess at the seam cannot separate them.

**Why this order.** T1 and T2 are the two vocabularies, each inert and each gate-green alone: the probe cannot be built against a door set that does not exist yet, and the registry cannot be fenced against a predicate that does not exist yet, so neither depends on the other and both must precede T3. T3 is the increment's headline and lands third because it is the first task that *changes behaviour*, and it is kept atomic because the guard, the two class postures and the stale-comment strikes it forces are one motion the gate cannot split. T4 follows T3 rather than merging with it: a signature change across seven commit sites is its own inseparable unit, and landing it after the door refusal keeps the door's commit boundary readable — the door guard is gate-green with the seam untyped, and the seam re-probe is gate-green once the subject exists. T5 is independent of T3/T4 in mechanism but sits after them because the posture guard **closes the driven instance of the frame's own wrong diagnosis** (`fatal: cannot do a partial commit during a merge` is now refused at the door), so the non-hook arm is written against the residue rather than against a cell the wave removes. T6 is last because it states what the five before it shipped, and its mechanical arm asserts equality against codes that do not exist until T1 mints them.

**Declared bounds carried to the executor.** (i) **The `GIT_DIR` redirect is declared OUT** — the claim's symmetric half — with its rationale quoted and its scope **reopenable and recorded as such**; ~15 fake-`.git` fixtures depend on the no-shell-out property and the `dirname(common-dir) != toplevel` shortcut is **not a discriminator**, since a legitimate linked worktree has the identical asymmetry. The family closes over **three of four** driven members. Leaving the cell unmentioned is forbidden; a row that says *not answered, and why* is required. (ii) **Refusing the unborn member at `jigc task finalize` narrows an edge path M21 built, and that is deliberate rather than accidental**: no locked design doc promises a finalize on an unborn HEAD (`design/project-setup.md`'s zero-commit section is about *seeding*), no suite drives one, and the documented on-ramp runs `jigc setup` first — whose install commit births HEAD. What changes is that `jigc start` before `jigc setup` on a zero-commit repo now refuses at finalize, routed at a first commit; the mint-side empty-tree sentinel is untouched, since `jigc start` is `neither`. (iii) **An unanswerable probe reads as no breach** — a deliberate fail-open on the shipped `nothing_staged` precedent, recorded with its reason, because the alternative turns the fake-`.git` unit fixtures into refusals. (iv) **`migrate-corpus`'s relocation arm is not a `move_doc` caller** (`fs::rename`, driven-free but source-verified at `migrate_corpus.rs:373-375`), so its posture obligation is the committing one, not the mover's. (v) **N20's state clause is not reusable on faith** — the hook clause may be false for a non-hook failure at the same door, and the axis is the proof, not the assumption. (vi) **None of the three codes joins `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`**, which mirrors door identities; the executor re-runs `invocation_log::tests::registry_mirrors_the_declared_members` and the anti-collision test. (vii) **Flow 52's arm 2 is Increment 11's**, per the roadmap's own cut — an arm written here is scope creep; what this increment owes arm 2 is the registry and the behaviour it iterates. (viii) A new suite file is registered in **exactly one** group root (`autotests = false`; `tests/test_target_registration.rs` fences both directions). (ix) **The wave's honest bound binds here too**: zero schema-hash movement, zero `schema-version` bumps, zero corpus migrations. (x) **The frame's hook-shaped sentence for a *`CommitRejected` with a non-hook cause*** (git itself refusing, e.g. `core.bare`) is **not** in this increment's scope — it carries no charter row; its driven instance at `milestone create` is closed by T3's operation-in-progress refusal, and the residue is named here rather than left silent.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 2 / T6: the design docs state what shipped, and the inventory registers the three codes

Two loci, and the load-bearing one is **implemented rather than narrowed**.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 2 / T5: a non-hook boundary refusal keeps the frame that was built for it (N20)

**The frame was never missing — it was built in full and then thrown away.** `surface_commit_rejection` rendered only on the `CommitRejected` downcast and fell through to `invocation_log::operational_failure` for everything else, discarding `frame.code`, `frame.survived` and `frame.rerun` at all seven construction sites. So a `git merge --ff-only` that refuses to overwrite ordinary untracked main-checkout WIP exited 1 with `error_code: null`, no route and no word about what survived — with the record left `status: active` and every provisioned worktree still holding its code, none of which anything said. Shipped: a second typed marker `task::CommitFailed`, applied at each door's **transaction boundary after its rollback has run** — the executor's `Err` arm (`task finalize` + both fan-out arms), `commit_record_transaction` (the four record-only doors + `jigc task discard`), the rename transaction, and `commit_migration`'s stage.

**It got its own render arm, and that was the finding rather than a detail.** `render::commit_rejected` hard-codes *"Fix the hook's complaint"*; a second caller would have shipped a law-1 lie at ten doors at once, and a route an operator cannot follow. `render::commit_failed` states the same three things and names **no cause at all** — *"Resolve the cause above"* is true whatever the cause was, and git's own bytes are printed verbatim immediately above it. The closing `then re-run …` shape is deliberately the rejection frame's, so **one** lifter reads the emitted bytes of both cells.

**The state clause is not reusable on faith (G-47), and one cell proves it.** The axis is `COMMITTING_DOORS × {hook rejection, non-hook failure} × {is the clause true?}`, and the answer is not uniform: `migrate-corpus`' hook-cell clause says the migrated bytes are *"written and staged"*, and in the non-hook cell **the stage is exactly what failed**. That door therefore states a second clause on `RejectionFrame::survived_non_hook`, and the sweep asserts *that* one against a driven `git diff --cached` showing nothing of it staged. Every other door reuses its clause because its rollback runs identically on both cells — asserted per door against the repository, never against the sentence.

**`already_typed` is a hand list, so it bought a fence.** Four typed errors pass through unmarked because a door's surface discriminates each **after** the marking runs — `CommitRejected`, `StageGitFailure`, `OwnerArtifactBlock`, and any `BlockedFinding` (the `repo.*` posture refusals T4 raises among them). `OwnerArtifactBlock` was **found by the suite, not by reading**: marking it once turned flow-20's `owner-artifact.present` block from a routed exit-3 `ValidationReport` into a generic frame at exit 1. `task::tests::typed_errors_pass_through_the_commit_failure_marker` now asserts all four pass through *and* that a bare `anyhow` is marked, so the list cannot go stale silently.

**The third sweep is the same `COMMITTING_DOORS` iteration with the same hard `panic!` on an unclassified member**, ten doors, **no hook installed in any fixture** — so nothing in any cell can reject anything, which is what makes the hook sentence's absence a real assertion. Causes are ordinary rather than exotic: a stale `.git/index.lock` (the residue of a killed git) meeting the stage's `git add` or the rename's `git mv`, a promote destination that is a regular file, and the headline `--ff-only` over colliding untracked WIP. Per door: exit non-zero with HEAD untouched, the door's `error_code` read back **from the invocation log** (never the printed text — the `Outcome::error` membership check is a compiled-out `debug_assert!`), exactly one route lifted verbatim and equal to that door's own re-run, the clause verified against the repo, and neither the hook diagnosis nor the rejection assertion anywhere. **EC-37's knob-independence is driven, not quoted**: both `finalize.fan-out.squash` arms reach the one seam that lands the commit on the live checkout, both frame identically, and each logs its own distinct identity. Non-vacuity by applied mutation: re-pointing `commit_failed` at the hook sentence reddens the first cell on that clause alone.

**Out of scope and named rather than left silent:** a `CommitRejected` whose cause is **git itself** rather than a hook (`core.bare`, a partial commit during a merge) still renders the hook sentence. It carries no charter row, and its driven instance at `milestone create` is closed from the other side by T3's operation-in-progress refusal, which never lets that run reach a commit — which is why T5 sits after T3: the non-hook arm is written against the residue, not against a cell the wave removes.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 2 / T4: the commit and move seams take a typed subject and re-probe before the act

**The door adjudicates the user's posture once, before anything is resolved; the seam is where the act happens, and it is not the same moment.** T3's guard runs at `Cli::dispatch`. A per-task finalize then validates, promotes, retires and stages before it reaches `task::git_commit_capture`, and the milestone boundary runs the user's hooks in a worktree sharing the same `.git` before it reaches its `git merge --ff-only` — so a hook, a concurrent process or an earlier phase of the same run can move HEAD in between (`settle-record.md` → Review amendments §3, Codex 2). `cli::repo::SeamSubject` is that re-probe's subject, threaded through `git_commit` / `git_commit_capture` in place of the bare `&Path`, so **a caller must say which checkout it is**, and verified immediately before **every** `git commit`, before `move_doc`'s `git mv`, and before the live-checkout fast-forward.

**What it verifies is repository identity and the expected ref, not *HEAD is attached*.** The subject records the canonical per-worktree git dir and the **value** `git symbolic-ref HEAD` returned when the act was decided; `verify` asks three questions in order — identity, then the posture family filtered by act and by the subject's stated exemptions, then ref drift. The family's own three `repo.*` identities cover the detached / unborn / operation-in-progress members. Ref **drift** deliberately mints no fourth code: the three name *postures*, and a checkout that moved between the door and the act is not one — it refuses with both refs named and `git switch <the ref this act was decided for>` as its route. A probe that cannot answer still reads as **no breach** on both new comparisons, the module's standing rule.

**Typed rather than sniffed, because sniffing is provably wrong here, and un-forgeable because the handle is the evidence.** A fan-out worktree answers `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` with exit 1 — byte-identical to a user's detached HEAD — and the throwaway worktree the squash:true combine commits in is **not a registered sub-task**, so T3's `posture_subject` legs classify it *live* and would refuse jigc's own commit site. Driven as an applied mutant: with `SeamSubject::dedicated` building the live discriminant, both fan-out arms and the fast-forward arm fail with `blocking · repo.head-detached` on jigc's own commit. So the dedicated variant has exactly **one** constructor and it takes a `&DedicatedWorktree` — neither a path nor a boolean, the two forgeable shapes M50's audit condemned in `fanout_worktree_paths`' `is_dir()`. `DedicatedWorktree::add` was already private to `task.rs` with private fields, so §3's *"constructor private to the worktree type"* needed no visibility change; the new work is the subject.

**The move seam's subject is not a parameter, and that is the decision.** There is one `git mv` in the product and no mover ever runs in a fan-out worktree, so a `&SeamSubject` parameter would carry no choice — while a subject threaded in from a caller would be a **stale** expectation by the time it reached the `mv`, the opposite of what §3 asks. `git_commit_capture` is told its subject because it genuinely cannot tell live from dedicated; `move_doc` can, and builds a fresh one at the act. Its act class is `SeamAct::Move`: *operation in progress* only, the same split the door makes.

**`jigc setup` re-probes under its `Exempt` row rather than skipping the seam.** Its install commit is `--no-verify` by recorded design and reaches no shared seam, so it carries the exemption explicitly — `SeamSubject::live_exempt(repo_root, &[HeadUnborn])`, the M30 rationale quoted at `cli::SETUP_UNBORN_EXEMPTION` — and refuses detached and operation-in-progress after the writes and the stage, where everything above it has already run. The refusal is a new `InstallCommitRejection::Posture(Finding)` carrying the probe's **own** finding: dressing a posture as *"`git commit` was rejected"* would be a law-1 lie, because git rejected nothing.

`commit_seam_posture` drives all five cells: the two live interleavings **in-process** against the real `task::git_commit`, because *build the subject → move HEAD → enter the seam* is an ordering no race can be made to stage through the binary; the dedicated cell as the **full fan-out boundary through the real binary at both commit models**; the move cell on a live `MERGE_HEAD` with the index asserted byte-identical after; the fast-forward cell through the binary with a `pre-commit` hook that fires **only** inside the combine worktree and moves the main checkout's HEAD onto a second branch at the same commit — so a seam that did not re-probe fast-forwards it cleanly at **exit 0**, which is the red. The stated arm (§3's un-forgeability) is a **source** claim and is read off `repo.rs`, because the assertion is that a call does not exist. `task::git_commit` and `relocate::move_doc` widen to `pub` for exactly that in-process drive: the seam is what this task types, and an axis suite that could only reach it through a door would be testing the door.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 2 / T3: no posture reaches a door that commits or moves, and the two classes refuse different things

**One guard, at `Cli::dispatch`, whose subject is the T2 row.** `cli::cli::refuse_on_posture` reads `BEHALF_DOORS` at the **parsed** leaf and applies the posture family by class: a **commit-on-behalf** door refuses the whole family minus the members its own row states as `Exempt` (only `jigc setup`, only *unborn*); a **mover** refuses `OperationInProgress` **only** — a `git mv` lands in the index and which commit it joins stays the user's to decide, while moving a tracked file out from under a half-finished merge is not; a **neither** door answers nothing. The refusal routes through `invocation_log::operational_failure`, so it is as legible in the invocation log as on stderr, and it carries **no override**: the route names the git command that resolves the state.

**The leaf identity is read off the parsed command, never off the process argv.** `Command::leaf` is an exhaustive match (the M50 `milestone_id()` precedent), so a verb added anywhere **cannot compile** until someone says which leaf it is. The exhaustive match fences only a *new* variant, though — a variant mapped to the **wrong** door still compiles and would hand the guard another door's class — so `leaf_reads_the_parsed_command_back_to_its_own_door` parses **one argv per leaf**, ⇔-fenced against the real clap tree, and checks the answer against the door the argv itself reaches on the longest-classified-prefix mold. Proven red by an applied mutant (`Command::Ingest => &["migrate"]`).

**Two driven placement constraints held, and the second forced the increment's typed subject one task early.** The not-in-a-git-repository answer still fires first (the walk-up answers `None`, so the guard does). And `finalize.milestone-sub-task` still answers a `jigc task finalize` run from **inside a provisioned worktree** — that worktree is detached, so a naive door-top would have replaced a tested, routed refusal with a posture the user cannot resolve (re-attaching a fan-out worktree's HEAD is not a repair). So `cli::repo::posture_subject` ships here: a `PostureSubject` whose discriminant is a **private** enum and whose only constructor demands three legs — `.git` is a **file** (only a real linked worktree keeps a `gitdir:` pointer), the path is the one `engine::milestone::worktree_path` mints, and the last component is a **registered sub-task** in the shared workbench. The registry leg is what makes it an answer about jigc's own provisioning rather than about a directory shaped like one; no caller can forge the variant, which is the class M50's audit condemned in `fanout_worktree_paths`' `is_dir()`. **The exemption is exactly one member wide** — a merge left un-concluded *inside* a dedicated worktree still refuses — driven, and proven red by a mutant that moves the exemption to the unborn member.

**`--carry-staged` stops concluding a user's merge as a consequence of the ordering, not as a second mechanism**: the operation-in-progress member refuses first, `MERGE_HEAD` survives, and the flag keeps its documented consent (*carry my staged work*).

`posture_door_axis` drives **every acting row from its own argv** × the family's five states — a row with no cell is a hard `panic!`, never a skip — plus the three named cells carrying the baseline's driven damage: `jigc setup` on an unborn HEAD still installs **and still commits** (and still refuses detached and merge), `jigc milestone create` on an unborn HEAD writes no record and no file anywhere under `.jigc/` pinning `4b825dc`, and `--carry-staged` under a live `MERGE_HEAD` refuses with `MERGE_HEAD` intact. The rebase cell is the sharpest: a stopped rebase detaches HEAD as well, so a committing door answers `repo.head-detached` there and a mover answers `repo.operation-in-progress` — the two classes, visibly different, in one state.

**Two stale claims struck with their falsifying datum, not silently rewritten.** `task.rs`'s `EMPTY_TREE_SHA` and `git_head` doc-comments, and `cold_start_zero_commit.rs`:9-11, all promised *"the first finalize diffs against the empty tree"*. Driven, `jigc task finalize` on a fresh `git init` now exits non-zero naming *land the repository's first commit with `git commit`*. The **mint** half stands untouched — `jigc start` is `neither`, adjudicates no posture, and still pins the sentinel. This narrows an edge path M21 built, **deliberately**: no locked design doc promises a finalize on an unborn HEAD, no suite drives one (`cold_start_zero_commit::` is green unchanged because every one of its finalizes runs after `jigc setup`'s install commit has birthed HEAD), and the documented on-ramp runs `jigc setup` first — which is the one row exempt from the unborn member, for exactly that reason.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 2 / T2: every clap leaf says whether it commits or moves on the user's behalf

Minted `cli::cli::BEHALF_DOORS` beside `VERB_KINDS` — a **total** classification of all **47** clap leaves into **commit-on-behalf** (10) / **move-on-behalf** (2) / **neither** (35), fenced ⇔ against the real clap tree, so a verb added anywhere **reddens until someone answers it**. It carries no error identity, so `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`'s derivation and its anti-collision test are untouched (`invocation_log::` green, unchanged). Nothing consumes it yet: T3 wires the posture guard, Increment 3 the staged-set guard, T5 N20's cause vocabulary.

**Two invariants are typed rather than tested**, which is the one shape choice the plan left open. `ActsOnBehalf` carries its payload per variant: `CommitsOnBehalf { argv, exempt }` · `MovesOnBehalf { argv }` · `Neither`. So a **mover cannot state an exemption** — a mover exempt from the one member it adjudicates would adjudicate nothing — and a `Neither` row cannot carry a runnable argv it has no claim to. A hand-list could express both; the type refuses to.

**One door, one class, and the class is decided at the source, not by the verb's name.** `crate::relocate::move_doc` is the **one** `git mv` primitive and its own doc-comment names its four doors (`config set docs-root`/`placement-root`, `jigc relocate`, `jigc rename`), so the mover class is `config set` + `relocate`; `jigc rename` both moves and commits and is classified **commit-on-behalf**, because the commit is what makes the whole posture family relevant. `migrate-corpus` is commit-on-behalf and **no** mover: its relocation arm is an `fs::rename` (`migrate_corpus.rs`:373-375) staged once at its own commit boundary — the one row a reading of the roadmap's mover list would have got backwards.

**The ⊆ is asserted, and the one member it cannot see is asserted by name.** `COMMITTING_DOORS ⊆ commit-on-behalf`: each door label is mapped back to its leaf by dropping the leading `jigc` and any parenthesised commit-model arm, then resolved against `VERB_KINDS` on `freeze_enforcement.rs`'s longest-classified-prefix mold. That is **ten rows over nine leaves** (`milestone finalize` is two commit models, one leaf), which is why the ⊆ alone is not a membership rule: `jigc setup` commits on the user's behalf, passes `--no-verify` by recorded design, and therefore carries no rejection identity for any `COMMITTING_DOORS` row to hold — so its membership *and* its `Exempt(HeadUnborn, reason)` are asserted by name, the reason quoting `setup.rs`:1617-1625's M30 audit rationale verbatim.

Proven red by the two applied mutants the plan named — a leaf's row deleted (`jigc doc list`: *"must carry exactly one BEHALF_DOORS row"*) and `setup`'s row flipped to `Neither` (*"it must be classified CommitsOnBehalf"*) — each reddening the fence written for it and no other. A third, unnamed mutant checks the argv fence bites: `rename`'s argv pointed at another leaf is caught as *"reaches `jigc migrate-corpus` instead"*.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 2 / T1: the posture family becomes one probe with three identities

Shipped `cli::repo::posture` — the family's one home over **HEAD detached** · **HEAD unborn** · **an operation in progress** (`MERGE_HEAD` · `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` · `BISECT_LOG`), each a blocking `Finding` on §10's mold (`repo.head-detached` · `repo.head-unborn` · `repo.operation-in-progress`, a `Route::human` naming the git command, no override) carried by the shipped `render::finding_error`. `head_is_unborn` is reused as verified; the other two were net-new. No door consumes it yet (T3 wires it), so nothing else in the suite moved. `design/finalize.md`:31's promise now has a probe behind it.

Two elaborations the plan did not reach, both decided at the build and both discovered by **driving** rather than reading:

- **The probe answers about the repository it was handed, or not at all.** A shell-out from a directory whose `.git` is a fake or broken **walks up and answers about a real ancestor repository** — the module header's binding hazard reappearing as a *verdict* rather than as a path. Driven: the fake-`.git` cell nested in a detached, mid-bisect ancestor was reported as detached. So `posture` resolves `repo_root`'s **own** git dir from the `.git` entry (directory, or a linked worktree's `gitdir:` pointer) and asks nothing when that resolution fails or lands on a directory with no `HEAD`. That is a stronger rule than the plan's fail-open, which only anticipated *cannot answer*; it is also what keeps the ~15 fake-`.git` fixtures answering nothing instead of inheriting an enclosing repository's posture.
- **The operation-in-progress member needs no shell-out at all, and is per-worktree for free.** The markers live in the *worktree's own* git dir, so reading them there is both the correct per-worktree answer and the walk-up-free one. Driven: a merge started in a linked worktree leaves `MERGE_HEAD` under `.git/worktrees/<name>/` and the main checkout's `.git` has none — a `dirname(git-common-dir)` answer would have got that backwards.

**Two driven facts the rows now carry.** A stopped rebase **also detaches HEAD**, so that cell legitimately answers two members and the row asserts the whole set rather than the one it came for; `git bisect start` leaves HEAD **attached**, which is what isolates the bisect cell. And the measured un-sniffability is pinned here: a `--detach` fan-out worktree answers `repo.head-detached` byte-identically to a user's detached HEAD, which is why T4's seam subject must be a **type** and not an inference.

**The `GIT_DIR` redirect is declared out as a row, never a silence** — the module header quotes `repo.rs`:1-16 verbatim, states that the quoted rationale scopes *jigc_home binding* rather than a posture probe's shell-out (the standing rule for that being `DECISIONS.md` 2026-05-31 → Git invocation), and records the reopening condition. `repo_posture::the_git_dir_redirect_is_declared_out_of_this_probe` **drives what the bound costs**: with `GIT_DIR` exported, the probe's own query answers about a different repository, and the probe answers about neither more nor less than the path it was handed.
