## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 1 / T6: the path-argument registry, its ⇔ fence, and the cell it found

Shipped **`PATH_ARG_OCCURRENCES`** — a code-side registry keyed by **`(leaf, argument id, conditional arm)`**, fourteen occurrences over the six path-bearing arguments (`path` · `file` · `from_file` · `from` · `target` · `value`), each arm carrying **one stated rule or one stated no-rule-and-why as a typed value** ([settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M51/settle-record.md) → D1 part 3, as amended by §2).

**The derivation is the point, and it required splitting `ArgToken::Plain`.** `Plain` was total over *ids* and silent about *path-ness*, and its own doc-comment said so (*"nothing can check `Plain` from the outside"*) — which is exactly where this increment's driven damage sat. It now carries `PlainValue::{PathBearing, Other}`, so the question is **asked of every argument that ships**: answering `PathBearing` reddens `cli_parse::every_path_arg_occurrence_is_registered` until every occurrence of that argument carries a row, and joining the registry reddens `path_arg_occurrence_axis` until every arm is driven. **Both mutants were applied**: a row removed, and a leaf's argument renamed (`#[arg(id = "doc_path")]` on `jigc unmanage`) — each red with its own sentence. The two **named near misses** are written into `PlainValue`'s own doc rather than left to silence: `title` reaches a path only *through the mint* (the verbatim override is `--slug`, which has its own family and registry), and `workflow` selects a pack resource resolved against the loaded model.

**The ⇔ fence is over occurrences, not deduplicated ids** — `path` is `jigc migrate`'s source-to-be-retired *and* `jigc unmanage`'s lookup key — so a new leaf reusing an existing id cannot inherit a rule nobody asked about it.

**The axis found one live cell, and it is a fix rather than a pin.** `jigc config set docs-root ':!docs'` landed at **exit 0**; a task then authored an `adr` and `jigc task finalize` reported `1 file committed` while the promoted doc — written to `:!docs/decisions/probe.md` on disk — matched the *exclude* pathspec and reached **no commit**, leaving the store calling `managed` a doc git has no copy of (the `:(top)` spelling is sharper still: the stage matches the same-named file at the repository top, committing a file nobody named). A root knob prefixes **every** managed doc's path, so its first component is the first component of every pathspec the movers hand git, and `git add -- <path>` prevents **option** parsing, never magic. **No new code**: the leg joins the shipped `config.unusable-root` under `unusable_root_reason`, whose route widened in the same motion — the fifth shape under one code, on the same five-reasons-one-code precedent T5 used, and the **same narrowing the sink already takes** (`ValidatedRetirement::adjudicate` refuses a recorded path on `starts_with(':')`). Asked of the **first** component only: git reads magic at the start of a pathspec, so a directory named `:x` deeper in the value is an ordinary literal and refusing it would refuse a legitimate home (driven: `docs/:weird` still relocates).

Three dispositions decided at the build, each written into its row rather than argued in a commit message:

- **`target` at all four `config` verbs is a stated no-rule** — the `#` tail is resolved against a **closed vocabulary** (the workflow's resolved include list, the step body's declared `{{fill:}}` points) *before any write*, so only an id the model already declares ever names `.jigc/config/steps/<id>.yaml` or `fills/<id>.md`; the axis asserts that by **code** (`config.anchor-absent` / `config.fill-point-absent`) at all eight cells, which is a stronger claim than "accepted".
- **`from` at `jigc relocate` is a stated no-rule** — the prior home is a *prefix* matched against the committed spellings `git ls-files` reports, never a path opened or handed to git; every escape shape selects nothing and relocates nothing. Driving it at all needed a **manifest-less fixture pack**, because `relocate` refuses a frozen doctype before it parses `--from`, and every doctype both shipped packs carry is frozen.
- **`path` at `jigc unmanage` is a stated no-rule** — the token is a lookup key over the recorded store, and the verb leaves the bytes on disk by definition.

**The suite drives 120 cells through the real binary** over three bases, each **copied** per cell (`pinning.md` §4), and after every cell re-reads a canary planted **outside** the repository; every refusing cell re-asserts `HEAD` and `git status --porcelain` unmoved. A `NoRule` row's claim is checked, not assumed: its refusals must carry **no** path-rule code.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 1 / T5: a root value that does not read back as itself is refused (EC-27)

Driven at `b9e13cf`: `jigc config set docs-root '   '`, `' '` and `'  x  '` all exited **0**, and `jigc config get docs-root` then printed `docs-root =      (project)` — a reading no operator can tell from unset — while every managed doc would finalize under a directory literally named three spaces. `normalize_root_value` folds `.` and `..` and never trims, so a whitespace run survives the fold as an ordinary `Component::Normal` and reaches the store as a home.

**No new code: the class joins the shipped `config.unusable-root`**, on that code's own five-reasons-one-code precedent — the operator's fix is the same as for a file-shaped, absolute or symlinked root, *supply a different root* — which is how EC-27 lands **by membership** in the path-argument registry rather than in Tier 3 under an unshared predicate ([settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M51/settle-record.md) → D1 part 5; **G-30 closed**). `cli::config::ROOT_KNOBS` is the one home, so the rule binds `placement-root` by construction rather than by a second edit.

Two elaborations decided at the code, both narrowing what *"a value that reads back as itself"* means:

- **Edge whitespace, over every component — not any whitespace, and not the leaf.** An interior space (`my notes`) reads back as itself and names a home the operator can see and type, so refusing it would refuse a legitimate root; a tab never reaches the leg at all, since `engine::write::check_value`'s control-character floor refuses it two steps earlier under `config.value-rejected`. The subject is **every** component (`docs/ notes` names an invisible directory exactly as `  x  ` does) — the correction the on-disk walk beside it already had to take at M50 (`README.md/sub`), applied here before it could be driven wrong.
- **The leg is lexical and sits after the absolute leg, before the on-disk walk.** A value refused twice over keeps the stronger sentence: `/tmp/x  ` still answers *an absolute path*, the reason that survives trimming.

The refusal's **route was widened in the same motion** — it enumerated *"never a file, an absolute path, or a path through a symlink"* and would have understated the fourth shape it now refuses, which is law 1 on the surface the refusal itself prints.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 1 / T4: a step source is read as a source, and the handoff family takes its explicit disposition

Shipped **`config.step-source-untrackable`** on §10's mold at **both** occurrences of the `file` argument (`jigc config insert-step`, `jigc config replace-step`), asked **before the read** by one shared predicate, `trackable::source_read_reason`. Driven at `dddc11a5`, `jigc config insert-step … .git/config` exited **0** and copied this repository's git config into `.jigc/config/steps/config.yaml`; that the copy then **composes** — `repositoryformatversion = 0` rendered into the step text `jigc start` hands the agent — is the baseline's own drive ([baseline-tokens.md](completions/artifacts/M51/baseline-tokens.md) §2d), relayed and marked as such. The rule is §2's — **readable · no `.git` component · not reached through the workbench** — and an **out-of-repo source stays admitted**: the caller names it and the bytes land in the next diff, so refusing it would narrow a shipped affordance (a team steps library at `~/steps/foo.yaml`) to close nothing.

**The `--from-file` family takes the registry's stated no-rule-and-why, and that is a decision, not an omission.** §2's heading swept `from_file` in beside `file`; the decomposition left both dispositions open and required this task to decide one **per occurrence**. Decided **no rule**, on two grounds:

- **The increment enumerates four codes and none is a `from_file` identity.** Enforcing would mint a fifth under §10's mold, outside the increment's own declared scope — and folding three doc/config doors under `config.step-source-untrackable` would be the unlike-rules-one-banner shape M50's Settle refused.
- **The discriminator is driven, not argued.** At all three `from_file` occurrences `-` is a **declared channel of the same door**, so a path rule would refuse a *spelling* while `cat .git/config | … --from-file -` hands over the identical bytes. At the `file` doors it is not: `echo body | jigc config insert-step … -` answers `could not read source step file -: No such file or directory`, so the path token is that door's **only** channel and a refusal there refuses the outcome. A fence the door's own `--help` defeats is a false completeness claim on the record — the shape this wave was chartered to correct.

The disposition is written once, at `doc::read_handoff`, as six rows (three leaves × two conditional arms) with a pointer at each of the three call sites — which is also why the M51 registry is keyed by `(leaf, argument id, conditional arm)`. It states what it does **not** claim: the route floor at those doors stays open (four miss shapes, bare `anyhow` + errno), disposed nowhere by this paragraph.

**The workbench leg is the *transient* workbench, not `.jigc/` whole — and the narrowing was forced by the gate, not chosen.** The first cut asked the shipped `is_workbench_root`, which refuses any path under `.jigc/`, and the full gate reddened `e2e_audit::scenario_7_structural_op_shifts_composed_bytes_vs_no_override`: it writes its source step to **`.jigc/config/extra.yaml`** and inserts from there. That is not a fixture convenience but the contradiction §2 itself names — its argument against the *destination* predicate is that `is_workbench_root` *"refuses any path under `.jigc` — precisely where `insert-step` **writes**"* — so a whole-tree refusal would have re-committed the error §2 struck. `.jigc/config/` is the **committed** cascade layer; the transient subtrees are the ones `.jigc/.gitignore` declares. The leg therefore reads **`gitignore::ENTRIES`** (`tasks/ index/ state/ milestones/ worktrees/ logs/ displaced/`) rather than restating a list: a subtree becomes transient by joining that constant, and a second list here would be one edit away from lying. The suite carries both halves — `.jigc/state/` refuses, `.jigc/config/` lands — so the narrowing cannot silently regress in either direction.

Two further elaborations decided at the build:

- **The leaf IS canonicalized here — the opposite of `place_inside`'s rule, for the same reason.** There the leaf is the *subject* of a later retire, so resolving it would retire the wrong path. Here the door is about to **read bytes** and the read follows the link, so the bytes' real home is what the rule must be asked of. Driven: `ln -s .git/config sneaky.yaml` is refused, and the refusal names `.git/config` — which is also how *"not reached through the workbench"* is **satisfied** rather than merely tested for.
- **The `.git`-component test is asked of the repo-relative tail when the source is inside the repository**, and of the whole resolved path when it is not — so a repository that itself lives under a directory named `.git` does not refuse its own ordinary files, while an out-of-repo `.git/` file still refuses (driven: a second repo minted with `mktemp -d` + `git init`, its `.git/planted.yaml` named as a source, refused with the code; the refusal quotes the host path, which is the law-1 carve-out T1 already took for a source with no repo-real spelling).

*The code keeps §10's name though the rule is a source rule and not a trackability one: the identity was fixed at the Settle, and renaming a settled code to improve its adjective is churn a 1.0 pin does not need.*

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 1 / T3: the retire sink re-validates in the same function as the unlink

Shipped **`finalize.retire-untrackable`** and the typed pair that makes it structural rather than remembered. T1 closed the `jigc migrate` **door**; what the door produces is a line in a mutable, gitignored working area that `finalize --approve` reads back one commit closure later and hands to `remove_file`, so between those two moments the value is **caller-supplied again**. Driven at `c5f7a85`: rewriting `.jigc/tasks/<id>/source-path` to an absolute host path deleted a file in another tree at **exit 0**, inside a commit that said it had migrated a document; the `.git/`-component spelling did the same.

Three elaborations decided at the build:

- **Two types, not one, because the two halves are two different claims.** `engine::state::MigrationSource` carries **provenance** (*these bytes were recorded as a migration source, and they are non-empty*) and replaces the raw `read_source_path`, which is now private to its loader — so no consumer can hand a bare string to a destructive op, because none can obtain one. `cli::task::ValidatedRetirement` carries **admissibility** (the normalized literal path **and** the repository identity that answer was bound to), and only it reaches the unlink. The split is forced rather than stylistic: admissibility needs `git` and a symlink syscall, and `crates/engine` hosts neither — zero `Command::new`, zero `symlink_metadata`/`read_link` — with `engine::validate`'s injected `tracked` as the shipped precedent for a CLI-supplied predicate.
- **`target()` joins the *bound* root, and that is the hole itself.** In Rust `root.join(<absolute>)` **is** that absolute path, so the old `repo_root.join(retirement)` escaped the repository at the one call that mattered. Binding the root into the value is what makes the join unable to mean anything else.
- ~~**Pathspec magic is a sink property and is asked only here.**~~ **Struck the same day, with its falsifying datum** (`d934746`, and the colon half at the validation of this increment). The true half stands: `git add -- <path>` prevents **option** parsing and nothing else, so a recorded `:(top)…` reaching `stage_migration` is a pathspec rather than a file name. The half that made it a *sink* property — *"at the door the same token is already refused for the unrelated reason that it names no readable file"* — is a claim about the one token the axis suite had planted (`:(top)README.md`, which names nothing), not about the rule. Driven: `*.md` names a file that exists, so the door read it, was told **tracked** by a `git ls-files` answering about six other files, and `--approve` unlinked bytes no git object held; a **staged** `:colon.md` made the door report `migrate.source-untracked` — *in neither this repository's index nor its HEAD* — about a path `git ls-files --stage` printed, routing to a `git add -- :colon.md` that exits **128**; **committed**, that same source was admitted at exit 0 and refused only here, one whole authoring later. So the class is asked **once, in the home the door and the sink share** (`crate::trackable::resolve_source_token`), and the axis suite's two magic cells now both name files that **exist**, so the struck premise cannot be restated as a green cell.

**The refusal is of the whole transaction, not of one step.** It fires **inside** the commit closure, so the shared `Err` arm runs the captured-pre-image rollback (promote out of the worktree, every scoped index axis restored) before anything surfaces — and it is **re-raised, not reframed**: it is neither a git failure in jigc's own stage phase nor a hook rejection, and dressing it as one would tell the operator to satisfy a hook that was never consulted. The shared error funnel prints the house findings line and records the code at exit **1**, §10's mold. `finalize.retire-untrackable` moves from `render::FINALIZE_NON_MEMBERS` into `FINALIZE_FAMILY` — the mechanism that list was written to run — keyed at **the file path**, because two inadmissible retirements in one plan must be two keys and not one `(code, null)`.

**Declared bound: `jigc task validate` does not preview this refusal, and that is the design rather than a gap.** The recorded value exists before the commit, so a preview is *possible* — and it would be a green that means nothing, because the whole ground for re-asking at the sink is that the value can change between any earlier check and the unlink. A second, non-authoritative answer is exactly the false green §2 exists to close, so the check has one home and it is the one statement above `remove_file`. It therefore mints no `GATE_COVERAGE` row: the transaction's promote/retire phase is already enumerated there as a later-phase member.

**A sibling defect was driven and is carried with a trigger, not fixed or hidden.** `engine::file_state::ConflictBlock::task` composes `jigc unmanage <source>` as a `Route::mechanical` **eagerly** on every migration finalize, so an ordinary committed source named `docs/old (draft).md` fails the route fence's `shell_safe` leg and panics `--approve` at exit 101 in a debug build. It is pre-existing (reproduced at `abd81df`), its subject is a route's quoting rather than a path's admissibility, and the engine cannot call `crate::task::shell_token` — so it is recorded in [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → M51, and **the test that routes around it says so**: the end-to-end pathspec arm drives `:/…`, while `cli::task::tests::every_pathspec_magic_spelling_is_refused_at_the_sink` sweeps the parenthesised forms at the predicate, so the leg stays swept over its axis and the narrowing is visible rather than silent.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 1 / T2: an untracked migrate source refuses, and the Settle's own G-5 prediction is falsified

Shipped **`migrate.source-untracked`** on §10's mold — a blocking finding with a locus and a `Human` route naming `git add`, asked of the adjudicated spelling before the mint. The predicate reuses **`task::path_in_index`**, made `pub(crate)` and **shared rather than copied**: it is the same call `stage_migration` already makes, whose skip comment (*"an untracked foreign was never in the index (nothing to stage)"*) describes exactly the silent-loss cell, so two spellings of one question could have let the door admit what the stage then drops.

Three elaborations decided at the build:

- **The predicate is the index *or* `HEAD`, not the index alone.** The decomposition's shorthand — *"KNOWN TO GIT (the index, not HEAD)"* — was written to justify **admitting** a `git add`ed-but-uncommitted source, and taken as an exclusive rule it refuses a cell the product ships on purpose: a user who committed the foreign file and then **pre-staged its own deletion** (`git rm --cached`, worktree bytes intact) is absent from the index **by design**, because M40 F7 discriminates the retirement pathspec on the index precisely so that pre-staged deletion still lands (`design/finalize.md`; `carryover_gate::the_migration_retire_pathspec_is_exempt` drives it). Driven, the index-only reading reddened that suite. Git holds a perfectly good copy of those bytes, which is exactly what the warrant asks — *git-recoverable* — so the union is the predicate, with `task::path_at_head` as the second leg. The index leg alone is still what makes the printed route **sufficient**.
- **The leg is asked after the read, not beside the three location legs.** `git ls-files` answers *no copy* for a path that does not exist at all, so asking first would answer a typo'd `<path>` with a `git add` that cannot match it, in place of the read fault that names the real problem. It is still before the mint, which is the property that matters.
- **Its own code, not a fifth reason under `migrate.source-untrackable`.** That code's legs share one fix — *name a different source*; this one's is the opposite — *keep this source and stage it*. A different act is a different identity, which is also how §10's table lists them.

**G-5's re-drive was owed at decompose, and the Settle's prediction did not survive it.** The Settle recorded that the leg makes the packs' fenced sentence (*"the deletion staged, so the removal lands in the same commit as the canonical doc (a `git rm` in effect)"*) true by refusing the one cell that falsified it, so **no pack repair was owed**. Driven end to end on `dev/jigc-rig fresh`: because the predicate is the **index**, a source that was `git add`ed and never committed is **admitted**, and on `--approve` the worktree file goes, the commit carries **no row** for it, and `git log --all -- <path>` is **empty** — the same surface silence as the untracked cell, one cell over. The sentence is therefore **repaired in both packs**, not left standing: it now says what each admissible cell does, and the repair keeps all three fenced `finalize.promote-clobber` tokens plus `surface_polish`'s three assertable fragments, so no fence had to move. 144 compose goldens regenerated; the diff carries nothing but the new paragraph.

*The staged-only cell is priced, not a defect left open:* the index leg is what makes the printed `git add` **sufficient**, so nobody has to commit a foreign file in order to be allowed to retire it (M50's `write.not-present` lesson). What the wave owes such a cell is that no surface claim about it be false — which is what the repair buys, pinned by an arm that asserts the behaviour of **both** cells and the statement in the same test so prose and binary cannot drift apart again.

**The fixture repairs are the leg's own blast radius, and they were derived from the gate, not guessed:** 25 tests across 12 suites migrated a source git held no copy of. Each is repaired by staging that source, never by relaxing the arm — including `migrate_rollback`'s two rollback cases, whose subject is a foreign original **absent from every commit**: they now `git add` without committing, so the cell (nothing in `HEAD` to `git restore` from, the retire byte-capture the only thing that can bring the bytes back) is preserved exactly, and their prose says *absent from `HEAD`* where it used to say *untracked*.

The deny floor's blanket permit for `migrate` + `finalize --approve` **stays**, and its recorded warrant (*"only a reviewed, in-repo, git-recoverable file"*) is now **true rather than restated** for the committed cell and **honestly stated** for the staged-only one.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 1 / T1: the `jigc migrate` door adjudicates its source path

Shipped **`migrate.source-untrackable`** on §10's mold and one shared CLI-side adjudicator, `trackable::resolve_source_token` — resolve the caller token to a repo-relative spelling **or refuse one that lands outside the repository**, then ask `untrackable_reason` · `is_workbench_root` · `unusable_root_reason`'s **symlink** leg of the resolved value. Three elaborations the Settle did not reach, decided at the build:

- **The symlink rule is asymmetric between the leaf and its ancestors, and that is the rule.** `place_inside` canonicalizes the token's *directory* chain (so `/var` vs `/private/var`, and a symlinked ancestor, resolve to the same in-repo file) and **never** its final component. An ancestor link is only a route to the bytes — resolving it records the same file under a spelling git can record — while the leaf **is** the subject: recording a link there retires the link and leaves the bytes, so it is refused.
- **The shared leg, the door's own sentence.** `unusable_root_reason`'s symlink leg is extracted (`config::symlinked_component`) and asked by both callers, but its *sentence* is not shared: the root knobs' names `RD`-staged docs, which is not what happens to a source, and law 1 is a rule about the sentence.
- **The door reads the caller's spelling and records the adjudicated one.** The adjudication has already proved the two name the same file; a read fault is the one refusal whose subject is the string the operator typed and can edit.

*(D1 part 1's "shipped predicates, no new capability" is struck in the doc-comment, as §2 requires: the resolve-or-refuse step is a new rule.)*

**The gate was red at this task's base, and the red was the planning commit's.** `fa2710cb` wrote **`finalize.retire-untrackable`** — T3's planned code — into `implementation/roadmap.md`, and `finalize_family_registry`'s arm 6 refuses any `finalize.*` identifier a live doc names that neither registry declares. Driven at `abd81dff` with this task's changes stashed: the arm fails there too, so the red predates the build. It is fixed rather than committed past, and without pre-empting T3: the code joins **`FINALIZE_NON_MEMBERS`** with its reason, which is exactly what that list means today (no production producer mints it) — a row in `FINALIZE_FAMILY` would redden arm 1, which derives membership from the production scan. When T3 mints the producer, **arm 2 reddens on that row and forces the move**; the mechanism does the bookkeeping, not a person.

## 2026-09-14 — M51 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 1](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the path-argument registry, its door, its sink, and the trackedness leg*) into **9 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `f8007e64` (tree clean; no increment landed yet). Every basis below marked *driven* was exercised through the real binary in throwaway `dev/jigc-rig fresh` corpora; the rest are marked source reads. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 51 Increment 1; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M51/settle-record.md) → **D1** and its amendments **§2** and **§10**; [charter.md](completions/artifacts/M51/charter.md) → EC-1 · EC-7 · EC-27; [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → The `jigc migrate` verb · Retire-the-foreign-original · The review gate; [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename` (the destination rule) · Content handoff; [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Placement · What a root knob refuses · Concurrent writers; [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → Rollback discipline; [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The route floor · Severity inventory; [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md); [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → the three laws · the route floor; [overrides.md](design/overrides.md) → Native-file id = filename basename; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §4; [dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → Gate.

**Basis — driven at `f8007e64`, not carried from the roadmap or the Settle. Four of the record's readings moved under measurement and are corrected here.** *(The drives used `target/debug/jigc`. Production code is unchanged since `21ffc0d4`, the sha `1.0.0-rc.14` was built from — the only `crates/` diff is `tests/foldback_truth.rs` — and every cell below is an **acceptance at exit 0** on the build where `debug_assert!`s are live, i.e. the stricter posture, so each transfers to release a fortiori.)*

- **The Tier-0 cell reproduces, and the mechanism is `Path::join`.** In a `fresh` rig, `jigc migrate <absolute-path-outside-the-repo> --as changelog` exits **0** and mints; the recorded `source-path` is the **absolute host path verbatim** (`repo_relative_source_path` strips only a `repo_root` prefix, and there is none to strip), and `retire` computes `repo_root.join(<absolute>)`, which `Path::join` resolves to the absolute path itself. The external file is the unlink target.
- **The `.git/`-component cell is a second destroy cell, and it is sharper than the record states.** Driven: `jigc migrate .git/config --as adr` exits **0** and records `.git/config` **verbatim**; `retire` would `remove_file(<repo>/.git/config)` — the repository's own config, inside the commit closure. Not previously named as a distinct destroy cell.
- **The `../` cell is NOT a byte-loss cell, and a red step written as one would never go red.** Driven: `jigc migrate ../../<outside>/keepme.md --as adr` exits **0** and records **`victim.X3Z6ro/keepme.md`** — `repo_relative_source_path` **pops** every `ParentDir`, so the traversal is folded away and the recorded path names a file that does not exist in the repo. `retire`'s `NotFound` arm is a silent no-op, so the migration lands claiming a retire that never happened while the real foreign file survives unmanaged and unmentioned. The harm is a **law-1 false success**, not destruction; the refusal is still owed (the caller's named subject was never touched), and the red step must assert the **ack**, never a surviving canary.
- **The symlink cell escapes on the READ, not the delete.** Driven: an in-repo `link.md → <outside>/target.md` migrates at exit 0 and records `link.md`; the retire would remove the **link**, leaving the outside bytes. The harm is that the door read content from outside the repository into a managed doc — the same class as the step-source harm below, one door over.
- **The workbench cell records `.jigc/wb.md`** and would retire a workbench file (driven, exit 0).
- **Leading-colon pathspec magic is a SINK cell, not a door cell.** Driven: `jigc migrate ':(top)README.md' --as spec` already exits **1** at the door — no readable file is named by that token, so the shipped read-failure route fires. The refusal §2 asks for is owed where the token *reaches git*: the recorded path fed to `git add --` by `stage_migration`, i.e. after a working-area rewrite. A door-level red step for this cell would be green for the wrong reason.
- **The step-source harm reproduces verbatim.** Driven: `jigc config insert-step --workflow single-task --after implement .git/config` exits **0** and writes the repository's git config into `.jigc/config/steps/config.yaml`, from where it composes into step text an agent reads as instruction.
- **EC-27 reproduces on all three shapes.** Driven: `config set docs-root "   "`, `" "` and `"  x  "` each exit **0**, and `config get docs-root` reads each back visually indistinguishable from unset. *(Source read:* `normalize_root_value` (`config.rs:548`) folds `.` and `..` and never trims, so a whitespace run survives as a `Component::Normal`.*)*
- **An absolute *in-repo* spelling must keep resolving, and there is a standing pin that says so.** `crates/cli/tests/migrate_retire_safety.rs:426` drives `migrate <canonicalized-absolute-in-repo-path>` and asserts the recorded path is `docs/changelog/changelog.md`. §2's *"resolve to a repo-relative path, or refuse an absolute one outright"* is therefore **one rule with two outcomes** — resolve when the token lands inside the repository, refuse when it does not — and that test is the red line. It also means the three predicates are asked of the **resolved** value, so `unusable_root_reason`'s absolute leg is inert at this door and its **symlink** leg does the work.
- **The two predicates that need a visibility change are private, and the third is already reachable.** *(Source read.)* `is_workbench_root` (`config.rs:622`) and `unusable_root_reason` (`config.rs:677`) are private `fn`s; `trackable::untrackable_reason` (`trackable.rs:55`) is already `pub(crate)`.
- **The CLI-side-sink reason is true, and its load-bearing half is the git shell-out.** *(Source read.)* `crates/engine` hosts **zero** `Command::new` and **zero** `symlink_metadata`/`read_link`. `untrackable_reason` shells out to `git rev-parse`/`ls-files` and the trackedness leg needs `git ls-files`, neither of which the engine may do by invariant. The engine's own precedent for exactly this shape is `validate.rs:2251`, where the owner-artifact gate takes **`tracked` as a CLI-supplied predicate**.
- **`read_source_path` has five CLI consumers and three engine ones — the "five" is the CLI set, and two of the five want a boolean, not a path.** *(Source read.)* CLI: `task.rs:1296`, `:1426`, `:1794`, `:2491`, `doc.rs:5809`; engine-internal: `finalize.rs:405` (`plan_retirements`), `:472` (`plan_clobber_guard`), `state.rs:1482`. `task.rs:2491` and `doc.rs:5809` use it only as `.is_some()` (the migration discriminator), so a typed value that satisfies them is a predicate, not a path.
- **The four codes are free, and none belongs in the mirror.** *(Source read.)* `migrate.source-untrackable`, `migrate.source-untracked`, `finalize.retire-untrackable` and `config.step-source-untrackable` have **zero** occurrences anywhere in `crates/`, `design/` or `packs/`. `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` is derived from `COMMITTING_DOORS` and mirrors **door identities**, so per §10 none of the four joins it and the anti-collision unit test stays green.
- **The carrier ships.** `render::finding_error` → `render::finding_line` (code · message · locus · route), read back by `render::blocked_finding` so the invocation log records the identity printed; five production sites already use it at exit 1. No new rendering, exit code or envelope is needed for the four refusals.
- **The trackedness leg's blast radius on the suite is real and was measured.** Of the 55 suite files that drive `jigc migrate`, **26** carry at least one call whose source is never `git add`ed **by name** (`migrate_review_gate.rs:179` is the exemplar: `init_repo` runs `git add .` *before* `HISTORY.md` is written, then migrates it untracked). Some of those 26 are error-path arms whose source does not exist at all and refuse earlier; the exact repair set is what `dev/gate` names when the leg lands. `tests/support/trial_corpus.rs` **already commits** its foreign source (`build_migrated`, `:656`) and needs no repair.
- **The review hold names no file today.** *(Source read,* `render.rs:4176-4252`.*)* Its JSON is `{review, task, source, rewrites[]}` and its text says *"retire the foreign original"* without naming it; `plan.retirements` is in scope at the branch (it already reads `plan.promotions`). `text_json_parity_axis.rs:186-200` carries `migrate` as `Tier::Judgment` / `DeclaredOut`, whose stated reason is about the **fidelity delta** only.
- **EC-7 reproduces exactly as amended.** *(Source read,* `e2e_audit.rs:261-283` against `adapters/claude-code.yaml:11-36`.*)* `floor_patterns()` `break`s on the first non-`- ` line, which is the comment at `:32`, so it scrapes **20 of 22** and cannot see `Bash(jigc uninstall:*)` or `Bash(jigc milestone discard:*)`.
- **One clause of the scope needed a reading, and it is resolvable from §10 rather than a fork.** §2 says `file` **and** `from_file` take the source rule, while §10's mint table names one identity for it (`config.step-source-untrackable`, at the two `<file>` doors). §10 states its shape is *"decided once for the family"*, so minting a sibling identity under that mold for a `from_file` occurrence that enforces the rule is settled machinery, not a new decision — and a `from_file` occurrence that does **not** enforce it takes the registry's *stated no-rule-and-why*. T4 carries that disposition explicitly; nothing is left to a later task.

Build **one shared CLI-side adjudicator** — resolve the caller token to a repo-relative path **or refuse an absolute one that does not land inside the repository**, then ask all three shipped predicates of the resolved value: `trackable::untrackable_reason` · `is_workbench_root` · `unusable_root_reason`'s **absolute and symlink** legs. `is_workbench_root` and `unusable_root_reason` take a visibility change; *"shipped predicates, no new capability"* is **struck** in the doc-comment that records the rule, because the resolve-or-refuse step is new. Validation runs **immediately before the unlink, inside `task::retire`** — not once before the commit closure is entered — and **git pathspec magic is refused** (a leading `:` in any recorded path that reaches `git add --`). The refusal fires inside the commit closure, so it **rolls back the whole transaction** on the shipped captured-pre-image discipline. No new code: the operator's fix is the same as the three existing shapes — supply a different root — which is that code's five-reasons-one-code precedent. *Done:* a new arm in `cargo test -p cli root_knob_rules::` — `config set docs-root "   "`, `" "` and `"  x  "` each refuse non-zero with `config.unusable-root`, a reason naming the whitespace, and one route; **`""` and `.` stay admitted** (the flat layout both knobs document); the same three cells refuse at `placement-root`, since `ROOT_KNOBS` is the one home. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/config.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/root_knob_rules.rs`.)*

Then the **axis suite** drives every occurrence over `{absolute, ../, symlink, .git/ component, workbench root, untracked in-repo, leading-colon pathspec magic, the - sentinel}`; a row with no cell is a **hard panic**, never a skip. It lands **after** the rules on M50 Increment 1's recorded ordering rule: run before them, the suite would pin the defects as expected output. *Done:* `cargo test -p cli cli_parse::` green including the new occurrence bijection, **proven red by an applied mutant** (a row removed, and a leaf's argument renamed); `cargo test -p cli path_arg_occurrence_axis::` green with every occurrence × every cell driven through the real binary and every disposition asserted — including the rows whose disposition is *no rule*, which assert the **accepting** behaviour their reason claims. **If the ⇔ fence finds an occurrence the rules do not cover, this task closes it.** Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, a new `crates/cli/tests/path_arg_occurrence_axis.rs`, one group root, and any door file a discovered occurrence needs.)*

Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `design/auto-migration.md`, `design/write-commands.md`, `design/storage.md`, `design/finalize.md`, `design/worked-examples.md`, `design/validation.md`, `design/command-output-contract.md`, `crates/cli/tests/migrate_source_rules.rs`.)*

**Why this order.** T1 is the Tier-0 fix and must land first — the increment's whole byte-loss risk sits in its first commit, and every later task's predicate has one home only once T1 mints it. T2 follows because it is the same door and the same shared adjudicator, but it is the one task that reddens the existing suite, so it is kept separate to keep T1's commit boundary clean. T3 is next because the sink is the *second* place the same token arrives and the only place a working-area rewrite can still reach; it depends on T1's adjudicator existing. T4 and T5 are the two remaining rule families, each independent of the others and each gate-green alone. T6 lands **after** all five because a registry whose axis suite runs before its rules pins the defects as expected output — M50 Increment 1's recorded rule, applied. T7 follows T3 so the hold and the sink read one typed value rather than two. T8 is test-only and independent; it sits before T9 so no later profile edit lands under a scraper that cannot see it. T9 is last because it states what the eight before it shipped, and its mechanical arm asserts equality against codes that do not exist until T1–T4 mint them.

**Declared bounds carried to the executor.** (i) **A descriptor-held traversal is REFUSED**, with its reopening condition: the substitution it would close needs a second writer inside the repository during the commit closure, and jigc is single-writer at a work unit ([storage.md](design/storage.md) → Concurrent writers bounds the one exception, and it is the shared `.jigc/` caches, not the worktree) — if a door ever writes the worktree concurrently with `finalize`, the narrowing is insufficient and the primitive is owed. (ii) **`finalize.retire-untrackable` refuses the whole transaction**, not one step. (iii) **The `../` and symlink cells are not byte-loss cells at HEAD** — driven above — so their red steps assert the ack and the absent task dir, and writing them as canary-destruction arms would ship arms that never went red. (iv) **The leading-colon cell is a sink cell**, driven: the door already exits 1 for the unrelated reason that no readable file is named. (v) **An absolute in-repo spelling stays accepted**, pinned by `migrate_retire_safety.rs:426`; the resolve step must be canonicalization-safe on both sides so a symlinked repository ancestor cannot turn an in-repo path into a refusal. (vi) **The deny floor's blanket permit for `migrate` + `finalize --approve` STAYS**, and T2 is what makes its recorded warrant (*"a reviewed, in-repo, git-recoverable file"*) **true rather than restated**; the warrant is already recorded in the Settle, so no new prose is owed — and nothing may add a comment **inside** the profile's `deny:` block before T8 lands, since that is the truncation EC-7 is about. (vii) **`from_file`'s three occurrences take an explicit disposition in T4**, named there and not deferred to T6's registry. (viii) **The out-of-repo source stays allowed at the `file`/`from_file` doors** — refusing it would narrow a shipped affordance twice over, and the driven harm was reading `.git/config` into composed step text, not out-of-repo-ness. (ix) **None of the four codes joins `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`**, which mirrors door identities; the executor re-runs `invocation_log::tests::no_registry_member_collides_with_the_finding_inventory`. (x) **Flow 52's arm 1 is Increment 11's**, cut after Increment 9 so EC-28's name-ceiling row can join it — an arm written here is scope creep. (xi) A new suite file is registered in **exactly one** group root (`autotests = false`; `tests/test_target_registration.rs` fences both directions). (xii) **The wave's honest bound binds here too**: zero schema-hash movement, zero `schema-version` bumps, zero corpus migrations.

**Scope coverage, bullet for bullet** ([roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Increment 1 *Deliverable* + *Grouped scope*): **the occurrence-keyed registry over six `ArgToken::Plain` members, ⇔-fenced over occurrences, with the eight-cell axis suite** → **T6** · **the door's three predicates and the resolve-or-refuse step, with *"no new capability"* struck and `is_workbench_root`'s visibility changed** → **T1** · **the `file`/`from_file` SOURCE rule, out-of-repo source allowed** → **T4** · **the trackedness leg, its `git add` route, and the permit's warrant made true** → **T2** · **the CLI-side sink, `ValidatedRetirement`, all five `read_source_path` consumers, the private raw read, validation in the same function as the unlink, and pathspec magic** → **T3** · **the exit-4 hold naming what it deletes, in text and as the declared `retires` key** → **T7** · **EC-27 as the `value` row's stated rule, joining `unusable_root_reason`** → **T5** · **EC-7's scraper repair, fixed as G-43 decided** → **T8** · **the four codes registered in `validation.md`'s inventory and out of `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`** → **T9** (registration) with each code minted in **T1/T2/T3/T4** · **the seven design-doc moves** → **T9** · **flow-52 arm 1** → **Increment 11**, per the roadmap's own cut. Nothing is deferred out of the increment, and nothing rides along to *"a later task"*.

## 2026-09-11 — M51 planned: eleven increments, risk-first

**The decomposition is cut** ([roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → *Milestone 51 — the evidence-check wave (the unadjudicated-axis wave): decomposition*), against the fifteen Settle decisions, the nineteen review amendments, the [envelope-key census](completions/artifacts/M51/envelope-key-census.md), the [acceptance design](completions/artifacts/M51/acceptance-design.md) and the [gate-halt discharges](completions/artifacts/M51/gate-halt-discharges.md). **The claim is unchanged and carries two symmetric honest bounds** — the `Plain` family ships as a classified registry with one stated rule or one stated no-rule-and-why per member, and the posture family closes over **three of four** driven members with the `GIT_DIR` redirect declared out — because stating one bound and not the other is the false-completeness shape this wave exists to correct. Acceptance: **flow 52**, nine arms, each naming the kind of set it iterates, plus the per-axis review on `1.0.0-rc.15`, held in one home and not restated in the roadmap.

- **1 — the path-argument registry, its door, its sink, and the trackedness leg** (D1 · §2 · §10 · EC-27 · EC-7's scraper repair): occurrence-keyed over six `ArgToken::Plain` members, ⇔-fenced; the door **resolves-or-refuses** an absolute token then asks **three** predicates, not the two D1 named; the sink is a typed `ValidatedRetirement` validated in the same function as the unlink, with pathspec magic refused; an **untracked in-repo** source is refused with a `git add` route, which makes the deny floor's warrant true rather than restated; the exit-4 hold names the file `--approve` retires.
- **2 — the posture family and the total leaf classification** (D2 · §3 · §10 · N20): every clap leaf classified commit-on-behalf / move-on-behalf / neither with `COMMITTING_DOORS ⊆` asserted; movers refuse operation-in-progress only; `setup` exempt from *unborn* with the M30 rationale quoted; the subject typed and **re-probed at every commit, move batch and fast-forward**; refusals carry **no override**, so `--force` at `setup` means only Increment 3's consent.
- **3 — `setup` refuses its install commit over bytes it did not write** (D3 · §1 · §5 · §13): the predicate is **worktree-vs-HEAD, per path, before any write** — the `StagedSnapshot` pair is withdrawn as an index probe against a worktree pathspec commit — the files stay written and staged, `--no-verify` is kept on its surviving self-trigger half, and the two locked sentences widen **scoped to the commit-on-behalf class**, since as a universal they are false at HEAD.
- **4 — the config-layer pre-image and amend-to-union** (D4 · EC-18 · §6): the amend lands first with a byte algorithm so the capture is idempotent; the restore is **compare-and-swap** over the two named files, emitting a rollback-conflict finding rather than overwriting a concurrent edit — the same loss in the other direction.
- **5 — the `EnvelopeArm` registry, the 57 dispositions, and the evolution policy** (D5 · D6 · §7 · §9 · §12): 60 arms, four proofs, production-side, hosted where all 47 leaves already reach a real success; **53 declared · 4 deleted · 7 `Unpinned(<reason>)`**; `relocated`, `--dry-run findings` under the corrected equal-set fence, N15's `--task` arm, and `doc list`'s `orphaned` state **declared here and produced at Increment 8**.
- **6 — the 22 unknown-id doors emit the findings envelope** (D7 · §8 · F-11): a code inside a message is not a key, so the flattened arm leaves F-5's harm unrepaired; a wire change on 22 verbs, shipped as a declared registry row inside the open window, with `command-output-contract.md:202` split — behaviour made true, provenance struck.

## 2026-09-11 — M51 Settle: fifteen decisions, every fork resolved robust after an independent advocate

**Fifteen decisions, and every fork went robust** ([settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M51/settle-record.md); the six advocate cases archived beside it). That is a result rather than a posture: each fork was argued by an independent `robust-advocate` against a proposer who did not author it, three advocates **conceded scope against their own interest** (F7 refuses `schema_version` on ~40 envelopes and the doc-side markdown parser; the small-forks brief argues the *cheaper-looking* arm on EC-6; F1 concedes a named list with a fence over it is an acceptable landing), and what the cheap arms kept failing on was one shape — **each would have shipped a false completeness claim on the record at the 1.0 pin**, the exact failure this wave exists to correct.

- **D1 — EC-1: the registry arm, door *and* sink.** A door-only guard was falsified by the baseline — a benign token at the door plus a rewritten `source-path` still deletes an arbitrary host file at exit 0 — and `ArgToken::Plain` is total over *ids* and silent about *path-ness*, the same complement that produced M50's HIGH; so six members, one stated rule or a stated no-rule-and-why each, ⇔-fenced, with the sink validated CLI-side because the engine has no subprocess and no symlink syscall. The deny floor **keeps** the blanket permit for `migrate` + `--approve`, with the reason recorded: a guarded migrate destroys only a reviewed, in-repo, git-recoverable file.
- **D2 — EC-2: refuse, as a posture family of three.** The one-liner probe was *measured* at **1 of 3** implementable cells and false-greens both that lose bytes, `finalize.md:31` already **promises** the third with zero probes in either crate, and the fan-out exemption cannot be sniffed (every worktree answers `symbolic-ref` exactly like a user's detached HEAD) — so it becomes a typed argument, `--force` the single consent, and a **new superset registry** holds `jigc setup`, which no seam-placed probe reaches. `GIT_DIR` is declared out with `repo.rs`'s rationale quoted, its scope reopenable.
- **D3 — EC-26: `setup` refuses its install commit** over bytes it did not write — driven, it swallows a staged intermediate *and* the unstaged WIP into `chore(jigc): install jigc workspace config` and leaves a **clean tree**, and with a pre-existing hook it commits the user's `AWS_SECRET` line under `--no-verify` while installing a `SKILL.md` promising it never does that; the guard binds the **commit**, not the install, so bootstrap stays non-circular. Re-tiered to Tier 1 on `assistant-adapter.md:52`, the leg-1 citation the charter did not carry.
- **D4 — EC-29: the transaction restores the worktree.** The cheap arm's premise is false in the doc it cites (*"worktree untouched"* is a clause about the restore's mechanism), and the driven cell is **unrecoverable loss reported as "nothing was committed" under a clean `git status`** — reached by the ordinary upgrade → finalize → hook-rejects sequence; `DECISIONS.md:4788` is kept true rather than narrowed, and any per-path exemption is stated with its reason.
- **D5 — EC-3/EC-5: mint the pinned-envelope registry first.** The contract's own rule — *an undeclared key on a pinned envelope is a defect* — **quantifies over a set that exists nowhere**, and a `keys:` column derived from today's output would bless **17 accidents into contract**, where `Unpinned(reason)` is the reversible door; the 17 keys are disposed before the pin, `hook_output` on a read verb deleted, and the *"add `schema_version` to ~40 envelopes"* reading refused on the record.
- **D6 — EC-9 refused, EC-8 taken.** The publishing floor was **decided post-v1 by the human twice** and its trigger fires *after* the call, so it stays on its trigger with going public kept in view; the versioning policy lands in an internal home **and** the guide body, because `design/` never ships to an adopter.
- **D7 — F-5/F-11: make the declared contract true.** `command-output-contract.md:202` claims the flattened error carries the code and locus *"exactly as the agent-text surface does"* — driven false at all 22 doors — and the engine already ships `finalize.no-task`; F-11 takes code + route now, its envelope disposition being one row of D5's registry.
- **D8 — counts fenced, not rewritten.** CLAUDE.md's *"thirteen `CELLS` rows"* was 63 when written and is **64 today** *[Corrected 2026-09-11 at the design review: it is **63** — `awk '/pub const CELLS/,/^\];/' crates/cli/tests/support/write_miss_cells.rs | grep -c "^    Cell {"` returns 63, and the 64th `Cell {` match is the `struct Cell` declaration at `crates/cli/tests/support/write_miss_cells.rs:108`; the count has not moved since the evidence check. The decision — fence, don't rewrite — stands without the datum.]*, five prose homes still say nine committing doors, and the fence built for this class **became an instance of it** (`== 69` banned, and the tree is 69); historical counts are dated-bracketed, not re-pinned, and EC-14's two refuted members are recorded as **corrected, not fixed**.

## 2026-09-10 — The 1.0.0 evidence check: two blockers no trial reached, and M51 chartered on the boundary the human drew

**The check, and its verdict.** Run on `1.0.0-rc.14` built from HEAD `bd348a83` — five Opus reviewers plus one independent, unseeded Codex source review, every driving reviewer on the release binary, none running cargo and none editing a repo file; the gate green at that HEAD, **3341 passed / 0 failed**. Two independent conclusions: **not 1.0-ready as rc.14 stands** — **two data-loss-at-exit-0 defects that no trial reached, both driven live and both outside every M50 registry** (**EC-1**, `jigc migrate <absolute-path-outside-the-repo>` records the path and `finalize --approve` **permanently deletes the external file**; **EC-2**, no committing door asks whether HEAD is on a branch, so `task finalize` lands prose on a branchless commit and destroys the only other copy in the same act) — and, separately, **the rc.14 trial's evidence holds and is *stronger* than its record**, whose single strongest stated caution against the 3/3 headline is **false as written**: B3-strict read the plant through `jigc doc show … --task` at tool call 3 and its `find | xargs cat` was tool call 7 and was **denied**, making it a **fourth** VERB-first arm under the stricter posture. [VERDICT](completions/artifacts/evidence-check-1.0/VERDICT.md).

**M51 is chartered, and the human drew the boundary** ([charter](completions/artifacts/M51/charter.md); [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → *M51*): the wave takes **every row of the ledger (EC-1 … EC-43)** plus the fix-shaped rc.14 rows **F-5, F-9, F-11** and the carried defects **N15, N20, N23**, and leaves post-1.0 the four **capability additions** — **because capability additions are additive after 1.0 and surface and contract fixes are not**, the criterion being the human's own: *"everything that becomes impossible or expensive to change once people start using the product. Now it's cheap."* EC-36 makes that line checkable by pricing per *mechanism* (text · additive key · envelope shape · schema-version bump + migration · schema-format change) rather than per *contract touched/not touched*.

**F-3, F-8, F-10 and F-13 stay post-1.0**, each keeping the trigger it already carries: **F-8** is a frozen `adr` `schema-version` 2→3 **plus a shipped corpus migration for every adopter** and **F-3** a change to the **schema-definition format**, itself frozen v1 — both priced by EC-36 as expensive-but-additive, not one-way — while **F-10** is a **new verb** and **F-13** is what the trial record itself calls *"a **design** question, not a fix."*

**The acceptance instrument is a per-axis review, not a trial** (the human, 2026-09-10) — eight axes on the built and installed `1.0.0-rc.15`, one Opus driver plus one Codex source pass each, under a **`VERB_KINDS` coverage fence on the review itself**: **both blockers were found by driving an axis and neither is verb-shaped**, which is exactly why four consecutive trials and every M50 registry missed them. Whether a blind trial **also** runs before the call is fork 9. **Then the 1.0.0 call, which is the human's.**

## 2026-09-10 — The trial that follows M50: the duress cell moves 1/3 → 3/3, and nothing blocks

**Why it ran, and what it settles.** M50's VERDICT declared its second claim-half — whether the
orientation variant moves the duress cell — **unprovable from inside the wave**. It is now
measured from outside it: **3/3 across two transports**, against the 1/3 that routed F-5 and the
orientation fork into M50. The reading of that number is the human's, beside the 1.0.0 call.

**Decisions taken during the trial, each recorded where it was made rather than after:**

1. **Breadth: full regression net + a blind milestone arm** (the human's, 2026-09-09) — over a
   39-file rc.13→rc.14 diff, a headline-only trial would have left most of it reached by nothing
   but its own unit tests going into the 1.0.0 call.
2. **The fold-back fence was inverted, not suppressed** — the gate was **red at the sha the
   handover certifies green**. M50's audit-closing commit `95c79be6` rewrote CLAUDE.md's M50
   sentence and did not touch `foldback_truth.rs`, whose own doc-comment says the fence must
   *invert* when the audit lands. Inverted here, with the cited verdict artifact now checked
   against the filesystem, because an unchecked citation is how it got there.
3. **A mid-trial answer-key amendment, recorded as one** (the human's, 2026-09-10) — B2 asked the
   operator to settle a product judgement and **none of the seven entries matched**, which is a
   halt by the key's own rule. A new `project-judgement` entry was added **reusing
   `title-authority`'s already-screened reply verbatim**; only the pattern is new, and it was
   checked not to swallow four neighbours. It changes which questions the key *reaches*, never
   what it *says*, and it could not touch the headline — measured twenty invocations earlier.
4. **The apparatus gained a write channel** — the trial's only adapter bypass was invisible to
   `run.py observe`, which fenced *reads* and not *writes*. Closed with a heuristic transcript
   half and an **exact corpus-reflog half**, fenced against B1's archived transcript rather than a
   mock. Recorded because the lesson generalises: **a channel fenced on one direction of an axis
   is fenced on none of it.**

**Findings: 13, none blocking**, disposed with triggers in
[decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → *The rc.14 trial's findings*.
Zero data loss, zero corruption, zero regressions. Two arms that looked like regressions were the
instrument meeting M50's **declared** `task discard` change — driven on both binaries before the
word was used.

**Carried, in writing:** the conversion ledger is **open**; a fan-out boundary is unmeasured on
this binary and **F-13 says why**; and the instrument produced seven defects of its own this
round, which is the strongest single caution against reading 3/3 as settled.


## 2026-09-09 — M50 completion audit: four findings, four fixed, and every one a larger class than reported

**The audit found four; the fixers found the classes.** 1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 2 LOW, **all confirmed live before any fix and all fixed axis-complete**, re-verified **3341 passed / 0 failed**. Nothing deferred. That every finding was larger than its report is now true of **four consecutive waves** (M46, M48, M49, M50) and is recorded as a property of the audit instrument rather than a coincidence: the auditors find the *instance* reliably and the *class* only when someone drives the axis afterwards.

**The HIGH was M50's own claim turned on M50.** `jigc milestone add-from-spec` read a doc from **outside the repository** at exit 0, seeded a sub-task from it and landed a commit naming the foreign source — while `jigc doc show` refused the identical token, because the family-4 guard covered the doors a registry could see and that registry rested on `DOCTYPE_ARG_IDS`, a **hand-maintained allowlist of clap argument names**; this door's argument is `spec_addr`. Adding the name would have closed the instance and left the mechanism, so all three `*_ARG_IDS` lists were deleted for `ARG_TOKENS`, a **total** classification of every argument of every leaf verb, with the three vocabularies as projections and a ⇔ fence proven by two applied mutants. **The fixer refused to claim a derivation that is not one:** clap carries an id, a help string and a value name — never the field's type or where the value flows — so address-shapedness cannot be *computed*, and **totality is what makes it asked**. Its declared bound is carried, not buried: `ArgToken::Plain` catches *forgetting*, never *mis-answering*.

**The MEDIUM's real axis was 31 sites, and the recommended fix was declined with measurements.** `render::blocked_finding` had two production consumers, so a code named on the surface was named in the invocation log at two doors of ~34. The sweep moved the funnel to where membership is decided — **8 of 10 driven doors** dropped the code before, the two working doors as controls, so the fix reads as the table going uniform, and `config.*`, `pack.resource-missing`, `workflow-refs.*` and all 11 `rename::RefusalKind` refusals now name themselves too. The orchestrator recommended routing the new codes into the pinned envelope; the fixer **refused**, on two grounds now written into `command-output-contract.md`: both guards build `Finding` with `location: None`, so the key would be `(code, null)` — **strictly less informative than the flattened message**, which names the offending address verbatim — and enveloping at the one door owning a block arm would trade a within-door divergence for a cross-door one in the same code. It also **falsified the finding's premise**: `store.malformed-slug` is not the first `store.*` outside the envelope — `rename` flattens `store.not-found`, the very code `doc show` envelopes — so the divergence is the **door's**, predating this wave.

**The two LOWs were law 1 and a third destroying door.** The printed-path rule bound only the four destroying/provisioning doors: the shared `untrackable_reason` composed 3 of its 5 reasons from absolute paths and had four callers, one of which M50's own Increment 2 had taught to work around it locally while leaving the predicate — fixed at the predicate, plus **4 read-path sites, not the 1 reported** (`store.not-found` *and* `store.unparseable`, both engine arms plus `engine::milestone`'s copies), so one JSON object had been naming one file two ways. `repo_relative` moved into `engine::path` as a pure render-against-a-root function; the engine stays empty by invariant. **The remainder is countable, not hand-waved:** 79 producers across 11 files, each with a measured count in `UNSWEPT_PRODUCERS`, so closing one reddens the row. *(Corrected 2026-09-09: this entry, the VERDICT's declared bound 2 and the RC-rc14 handover all said **60**; the table sums **79**, and the per-file counts — the half a test checks — were right all along.)*

**And `jigc milestone discard` destroyed a sub-task's staged prose at exit 0 while `jigc task discard` refused over identical bytes.** Contested, so it went to the human **against an independent robust-advocate**, never on a lone recommendation — and it is recorded as a **basis-has-changed reconciliation, not an override**. M46 decided that door's narrating arm deliberately, on the warrant *"its worktree refusal already carries the consent"* — driven **false in the only cell where bytes die**, because an agent authoring through jigc writes into `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/`, which is not inside the worktree (its `git status --porcelain` was empty while the staged doc held authored prose). The guard-killer counter was driven false too: `add-task` and `provision` stage nothing, so the guard fires only after real work exists — a **strictly better** false-positive profile than the `task discard` guard already accepted, which fires from the instant of mint. Exactly one cell of the driven 2×2 changed. `team-ready-state.md`'s falsified sentence was **struck with the datum**, so the M50 sentence eleven lines below is now true as written; one doc had been proving both.

**Planning's instrument failed twice and the delegation instruments caught both.** The `adr → research` edge was settled on the orchestrator's reading that *"the pack already shadows `commit`"* — true of the **files**, false of the **shipped composition**, where dev wins and that shadow is itself already inert; a spike refuted it, and the design review then refuted its replacement for the **same shape one level out**. The rule is on the record: *a claim about how the composed product behaves is not established by reading the files it is composed from.* Both were caught **before decompose**. And in the other direction: **three of three robust-advocates and four of four fixers corrected the brief they were handed**, each against its own interest.

**`1.0.0-rc.14` built and installed after the fixes, not before**, with the ten version-bearing goldens regenerated in the same motion and their diff verified to carry nothing but the version string — the convention `milestone-completion-workflow.md` records as having broken exactly once (M45 closed without its bump and its trial would have logged itself `rc.8`). **The 1.0.0 call was deliberately not taken:** the product case is strong, and the *instrument* case argues for one more measurement, because the wave's second claim-half — whether the orientation variant moves the duress cell — is unprovable inside the wave by design. [VERDICT](completions/artifacts/M50/VERDICT.md).

## 2026-09-08 — M50 Increment 13 / T3: the degenerate-id sweep comes back empty, and the disclosure decision is recorded rather than assumed

**Decided:** D13's three owed acts land together. **(i)** The post-hoc sweep of every archived RC invocation log for degenerate-id calls is **run, and its subject, predicate and denominator are stated** — `files=28 records=3351 | tokens examined=4201 | refused-by-is_slug=0`. **(ii)** **No adopter disclosure is owed**, recorded here as a decision with its ground, never by silence. **(iii)** [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)'s observer-briefing entry is **filled from the twelve increment records**, not from memory, with its trigger intact.

**The sweep, verbatim and re-runnable — run from the repository root at `f993930`.** The three door sets are **derived from the shipped registries**, never a remembered list: `DOCTYPE_DOORS`' `DoctypeArg::Address` rows (family 4), and the `WORK_UNIT_ID_DOORS` / `SLUG_DOORS` rows (families 1 and 2), each row's own `argv` giving the position its id or override arrives in. The predicate is `engine::slug::is_slug` transcribed as one regex — non-empty, `[a-z0-9-]` only, no leading, trailing or doubled `-` — the same predicate `work-unit.malformed-id`, `store.malformed-slug` and `write.malformed-slug` all ask.

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import collections, glob, json, re, sys
# Door sets DERIVED from the shipped registries, never a remembered list: DOCTYPE_DOORS'
# `DoctypeArg::Address` rows (family 4) and the WORK_UNIT_ID_DOORS / SLUG_DOORS rows
# (families 1 and 2), each row's own argv giving the position its id/override arrives in.
src = open("crates/cli/src/cli.rs").read()
K = {"WORK_UNIT_ID_SLOT": "<id>", "SLUG_OVERRIDE_SLOT": "<slug>",
     "WORK_UNIT_ID_DOOR_PAYLOAD": "payload.yaml", "SLUG_DOOR_SOURCE": "foreign-changelog.md"}
addr = {tuple(re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', d))
        for d in re.findall(r"\(&\[([^\]]*)\],\s*DoctypeArg::Address\)", src)}
flags, pos = set(), {}
for door_lit, arg, argv_lit in re.findall(
        r'door:\s*&\[([^\]]*)\],\s*arg:\s*"([^"]+)",\s*argv:\s*&\[(.*?)\],\s*\}', src, re.S):
    door = tuple(re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', door_lit))
    toks = [K[m[1]] if m[1] else m[0]
            for m in re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"|\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\b', argv_lit)]
    i = toks.index("<slug>" if arg == "slug" else "<id>")
    if toks[i - 1].startswith("--"):
        flags.add(toks[i - 1]); continue
    n = expect = 0
    for j, t in enumerate(toks[len(door):], len(door)):
        if expect: expect = 0
        elif t.startswith("--"): expect = 1
        elif j == i: pos[door] = n; break
        else: n += 1
    else: sys.exit(f"no positional index derived for {door}")
# engine::slug::is_slug: non-empty, [a-z0-9-] only, no leading/trailing/doubled `-`.
is_slug = lambda s: re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*", s) is not None
def candidates(argv):
    # Deliberately over-approximating: a flag is read wherever it appears, and every
    # `:`-bearing positional at an address door yields its head -- may add, never miss.
    out = [(f, argv[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(argv) else None)
           for i, t in enumerate(argv) for f in sorted(flags) if t == f]
    out += [(f, t.split("=", 1)[1]) for t in argv for f in flags if t.startswith(f + "=")]
    door = next((d for d in (tuple(argv[:2]), tuple(argv[:1])) if d in pos or d in addr), None)
    if door is None: return out
    p, expect = [], 0
    for t in argv[len(door):]:
        if expect: expect = 0
        elif t.startswith("--"): expect = 1
        else: p.append(t)
    if door in pos:
        k = pos[door]; out.append(("positional id", p[k] if k < len(p) else None))
    if door in addr:
        out += [("address slug head", re.split(r"[#/]", t.split(":", 1)[1])[0]) for t in p if ":" in t]
    return out
files = sorted(glob.glob("completions/**/*invocations.jsonl", recursive=True))
records, seen, refused, absent = 0, collections.Counter(), [], []
for f in files:
    for line in open(f, errors="replace"):
        if not line.strip(): continue
        records += 1; rec = json.loads(line); argv = rec.get("argv") or []
        for where, tok in candidates(argv):
            if tok is None: absent.append((f, where, argv, rec["exit_code"]))
            else:
                seen[where] += 1
                if not is_slug(tok): refused.append((f, where, tok, argv, rec["exit_code"]))
for f, w, t, a, c in refused: print(f"REFUSED-BY-is_slug {f}: {w}={t!r} exit={c} argv={a}")
for f, w, a, c in absent: print(f"NO-TOKEN-IN-POSITION {f}: {w} exit={c} argv={a}")
print(f"files={len(files)} records={records} | doors: address={len(addr)} "
      f"positional-id={len(pos)} flags={sorted(flags)}")
print(f"tokens examined={sum(seen.values())} {dict(seen)} | "
      f"refused-by-is_slug={len(refused)} no-token={len(absent)}")
PY
```

**Zero is a result here, because the denominator is stated.** The sweep examined **4 201 tokens** in a family-1, family-2 or family-4 position across **3 351 records** in **28** logs — 1 970 `--task` values, 1 727 address slug heads, 460 positional ids, 44 `--slug` overrides — and **not one** of them is a token `is_slug` would refuse. The seven residual records carry **no token in the position at all** and are adjudicated rather than swallowed: five are `--help` short-circuits at a positional-id door (clap prints help and exits 0 before any id is read), and two are `jigc doc list --task` with the value missing, which clap refuses at **exit 2**. Neither shape reaches a path join, so neither is a degenerate-id call.

**What makes the zero informative rather than vacuous: the doors were used.** `jigc task discard` — the door whose empty-id cell removed the repository at exit 0, W-13 — appears **35 times** in the archive, every one of them with a well-formed id. So the class M50 Increment 1 closed was never *exercised* in a recorded trial: the destruction was reachable and never reached. Every defect of the family in the record (`task discard ""`, `task discard "../.."`, `doc set-slot … --task ""`, `doc show 'research:../../outside'`) was found by **driving at plan time**, which is the instrument working — and is why the sweep is a check on the field record rather than a source of new findings.

**Two bounds, stated because they bound the claim.** The subject is what the invocation log recorded: a call made where the log knob was OFF, or before the log existed (M17's self-hosting run has no `invocations.jsonl`), is outside it — and `log_invocation` reads `args_os` lossily, so a non-UTF-8 argument would appear as `U+FFFD` rather than as its bytes. Against that, the log is written **after dispatch on every path including clap's own error arm** (`main.rs`), so a refused call is logged exactly like an accepted one and no exit code hides a record.

**No adopter disclosure is owed — decided, not assumed.** The class M50 Increment 1 and Increment 2 closed includes silent, uncommitted data loss at exit 0, which is the shape that would ordinarily owe a disclosure. It does not here, on two grounds that are checked rather than remembered: **no third party holds the binary** — every release through `1.0.0-rc.13` was installed on the operator's own host or built from a pinned sha inside a trial container, and the 1.0.0 call has not been taken — and **there is no root `CHANGELOG.md` in this repository** to land a disclosure entry on (the `changelog` doctype ships and homes at the repo root; this repo has never adopted an instance). Recording the decision is the point: a wave that closes a data-loss class and says nothing about disclosure cannot later be read as having considered it.

**The briefing entry is filled from the increment records, and it is longer than the plan's floor.** [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → *The trial that follows M50 — protocol inputs* now carries M50's declared behaviour changes as a two-tier list — *met on every arm within minutes* and *met on the arm that reaches it* — each item naming the increment that landed it. The plan's floor named ten items drawn from Increments 1–5 plus `1799a2d`; deriving from all twelve records rather than from that floor found the rest — all twelve build increments are represented, and Increment 5's `also open:` block is the push half of the very finding the next trial re-measures — and three of them are the ones an unbriefed observer would most likely score as a regression: **the two exit-0 → non-zero flips** (Inc 1), the **`deny` floor's two new members** (Inc 3), which make a worker's `jigc uninstall` / `jigc milestone discard` a *harness* denial rather than a jigc answer, and **`1799a2d`'s milestone-boundary tightening**, under which a fan-out that landed clean on rc.13 may now block. `engine::result::SCHEMA_VERSION` **2 → 3** (Inc 5) is carried in the same list because a driver pinned to 2 is the one adopter-shaped consumer the trial can contain.

**The line citations that move, named rather than left to be rediscovered.** Filling a one-line entry with a twenty-line list grows `decisions-pending.md` by **19** lines, so every citation into that file below `:185` shifts by 19: the three live ones are **`:510` → `:529`** (the empty-`--task` admission, cited by the M50 [settle-record](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) and [gap-findings](completions/artifacts/M50/gap-findings.md) as fired trigger #1), **`:513` → `:532`** (the unquoted adoption-route path token, this increment's T2 precedent for carrying a plan-time observation) and **`:541` → `:560`** (the un-markered listed-pack path). The dated artifacts that cite them are **not** rewritten — they are records of what was true when written — so the standing rule holds and is restated here rather than assumed: a citation into this ledger is located by **content**, and the line number is a convenience that decays (`DECISIONS.md` → 2026-08-09 M47 Inc 11 T7, *the record-truth targets are located by content, because the Settle's line numbers have moved*).

Nothing anywhere encodes the destruction as expected output.
