## 2026-09-07 — M50 Inc 11 / T3: the Fix phase becomes a fan-out, and §3 stops contradicting the step it composes

**The contradiction is closed in the shipped bytes.** `packs/methodology/steps/fix-gate.yaml` said *"One fixer per finding, **strictly serial over the one shared working tree**"* while [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) §3 said *"Triage fixes should ride it … **That is the encode**"* and its Orchestration bullet said *"each confirmed fix is its own agent"*. The step now composes what §3 named: partition the confirmed findings by each fix's **projected write-set** (a finding spanning two files is one sub-task, two findings landing in one file are one sub-task), then `config set finalize.fan-out.squash false` · `milestone create` · one `add-task … --workflow fix-task` per partition · `provision` · `execute` · `join` · `finalize`. §3 and the Orchestration bullet were rewritten to state the same rule; *"Until that lands, the interim mitigation is …"* retires, and [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)'s chartered increment is marked **SHIPPED** with the two points where what landed differs from the argument as it stood (D11's write-set partition, and `fix-task` without `allows-create`).

**The shared-artifact exclusion ships as a rule, never as this repo's instances.** The pack ships to adopters: *"a test-registry root a new suite has to be listed in, a generated snapshot set, a lockfile or manifest, the doc every fix folds back into"* — no group-root count, no golden count. (The roadmap's *624 goldens* is stale twice over: the tree held **622** at `aa98d1b` and holds **634** after T2's twelve, and this task adds none — it rewrites 18.)

**The plan's hypothesis about the knob was falsified by driving it, and the step states what is true.** The decomposition expected the `config set` write to be *"left uncommitted after the round"* on an established repo. Driven twice — once with `.jigc/config/manifest.yaml` **untracked and new**, once with it **tracked and modified** by a prior committed round — the milestone's own `finalize` carried the config layer into its aggregate commit both times, leaving `git status` clean. It is not fixture luck: every jigc commit boundary `git add`s the `.jigc/config` + `.jigc/.gitignore` pathspecs (`task.rs:3307`). So the step says the knob **is a project setting rather than a per-round flag** — the write lands uncommitted, the round's finalize commits it, and it stays in effect until you set it back — which is the fact an orchestrator needs and the opposite of what the plan assumed.

**One composing context was not in the plan's blast radius and is in the shipped one.** `fix-gate` is included by `increment.yaml` as well as `completion.yaml`, so the round now composes into both — coherent, because an increment's blocking findings are the same independent-by-construction set, and because [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md):17's seriality binds *Execute* (each task builds on the last), not Fix. That is why **6 `start--increment--*` goldens moved alongside the 12 `*--completion--*` ones**: 18 rewritten, not 12.

**The done-criterion's `grep -c "strictly serial" over packs/ is 0` resolves to one file, and the reason is stated rather than the grep satisfied.** `packs/methodology/steps/execute.yaml` still says *"Run the tasks strictly serially: they share one working tree"* — the **increment spine** rule, mandated by increment-workflow.md:17 and pinned by `increment_workflow_compose.rs:192` and `methodology_delegation_prose.rs:152`. Deleting it to make a grep return 0 would contradict a locked doc to satisfy a count. The substantive half of the criterion — *the composed `completion` walk carries no serial-over-one-tree rule* — holds exactly, and arm 1 asserts the retired sentence is **absent** from both composing walks.

**Acceptance** — `crates/cli/tests/fix_phase_fanout.rs`, three arms over the `[dev ▸ methodology]` pack-set a real `jigc setup` installs. Arm 1 asserts the partition rule, the shared-artifact rule, the fallback and the seven-line sequence on the composed bytes of **both** composing workflows, and the retired rule's absence. Arm 2 is the done-criterion's named arm: the emitted `add-task` line is lifted off the composed bytes, has its two placeholders substituted and **nothing else**, and runs verbatim at exit 0. Arm 3 drives the **whole round** from those bytes over a two-partition fixture — including each fixer's own emitted `Spawn:` line — and asserts two per-fix commits each owning exactly its partition's path (read back from `git show`, never from the ack), the config layer inside the aggregate commit, and a clean tree.

**Declared bound, recorded rather than discovered:** this repo is **not self-hosted** (no `.jigc/`, no `docs/`), so M50's own completion audit cannot run the composed Fix phase here. What ships is the pack composition and the design of record; the first real run is an adopter's, or this repo's after the port that follows 1.0.0.

## 2026-09-07 — M50 Inc 11 / T2: the fixer's walk becomes a composed workflow, so the Fix phase has a unit to fan out

**Shipped.** `packs/methodology/workflows/fix-task.yaml` + `packs/methodology/steps/fix-finding.yaml`. `jigc milestone add-task <m> "<finding>" --workflow fix-task` now exits 0 (it was refused with `workflow-refs.unknown-workflow` naming 33 loaded workflows), and `jigc milestone execute <m>` emits `` Spawn: `cd .jigc/worktrees/<sub> && jigc workflow fix-task --task <sub>` `` off the sub-task's **recorded** minting workflow — so the Fix phase needed **no new fan-out-bearing workflow**, only an id `--workflow` accepts.

**The composition, and why each part.** `fix-finding` → `gate` → `author-commit`, all three methodology-local: the include of an id **both** packs ship (`author-commit`) resolves per-origin-pack, and only the composed walk shows which won, so a cross-pack reach would be invisible in the source. `creates-task: true` + `selectable: false` with `suppressed: {reason, expires: never}` — the `sub-task` mold, and the shape M43's suppression fence requires. **No `allows-create`**: a fix that would revise a settled decision is *contested* by [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) §2(b) and belongs at the human gate, not behind a create-gate the fixer can reach on its own. **No `finalize` step**, which is the point of the unit: the milestone's finalize is the round's only commit boundary.

**The step carries the brief, not the loop's prose.** `fix-finding.yaml` states the axis-derivation rule (*an audit finds a defect by hitting it — one repro, one site — so the sites it reports are a lead, not the scope*; derive the class, report its **full membership**), that the red test **is** the finding reproduced and must iterate that axis rather than pin the reported site, and the **two isolation constraints** a worktree fan-out needs: `git add` your own paths *inside THIS worktree* (never a sweep, because a sibling fixer is mid-edit in its own), and never `git commit` / never `jigc task finalize` here. §3's own remediation — the serial rule it replaces — is T3's edit, not this one's.

**Acceptance.** New `crates/cli/tests/fix_task_workflow.rs` (registered in `groups/g_methodology.rs`), three arms over the `[dev ▸ methodology]` pack-set a real `jigc setup` installs. The happy arm **runs the emitted `Spawn:` line verbatim** — its own `cd` target and its own argv, split off the composed bytes and executed as written — because those bytes are the contract an agent runs, and a rebuilt equivalent can pass while the emitted line is broken. Both omitting contexts are swept: the dev pack alone still refuses `--workflow fix-task` with the routed code and mints nothing, and the router front door does not offer a `selectable: false` workflow. Blast radius: 12 new `*--fix-task--*` compose goldens (start × 6 states, workflow-preview × 6) and the 6 `describe` goldens, which gain the catalog line with its hidden-from-the-catalog reason. No orientation golden moved — the front door never listed it.

## 2026-09-07 — M50 Increment 11 / T1: the landing ack names every commit, and every landed file names the sha that landed it

**The `squash: false` boundary is a chain, and the ack described it as a commit.** Driven at `97581b6` on a two-sub-task milestone: three commits land, and `committed.hash` named the aggregate alone beside a six-entry boundary-wide `manifest` **of which that sha owns four** — the two per-sub-task shas, the entire product of the knob, appeared nowhere, and `sub_tasks[]` carried no sha. On the surface a fix-round orchestrator reads to answer *"which commit landed this fix?"*, that is a law-1 lie, not a thin ack. Closed **additively** ([command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → the M50 declaration, which rides this commit because an undeclared key on a pinned envelope is a defect): `committed.commits` (every commit oldest first, each `{hash, subject, paths}`) and `committed.sub_tasks[].hash`. `manifest` and `files` keep their meaning exactly — boundary-wide membership, one entry per path — because the Settle prices a correction there as a **break**.

**The shas are read back from git, not carried out of the commit path — a departure from the decomposition's own mechanic, on the red step it demanded.** The plan had `chain_commit` hand each sha out through the shared executor. The suite's red step (i) requires the assertion to be made against `git rev-list` on the **main checkout**, because the chain builds its commits in a dedicated worktree and fast-forwards main — and once the assertion lives there, so should the producer: `boundary_commits` reads `<pre-boundary-HEAD>..HEAD`, so completeness is a property of the *range* rather than of every commit site remembering to report itself, and no executor signature moves. Only the **sub-task→sha** pairing needs the chain's own knowledge (the id-ordered code-carrying set), and it is guarded by a length check: if the landed chain is not `ids + 1` long, no sub-task hash is claimed rather than a wrong one asserted.

**Attribution is a channel beside membership, with the multi-claimant rule stated rather than left to the reader.** A path *can* be landed twice — a sub-agent that staged a file at a promoted doc's destination has its per-sub-task commit land it and the aggregate land it again. It stays **one** manifest entry (the whole-range diff de-duplicates by construction), and its owning sha is the **last** `commits` member listing it, the commit whose bytes are at HEAD; naming the first claimant would name a version that was overwritten before the boundary ended. The agent text prints the same shas — a `commits (oldest first, …)` block **withheld on a single-commit boundary**, where the header hash already names it and the block would restate the manifest under a heading, so its presence is itself the signal that the landed set is partitioned.


## 2026-09-07 — M50 Increment 11 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 11](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the fan-out Fix phase*) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `aa98d1b` (tree clean; Increments 1–10 landed). Every behavioural claim below was **driven with the release binary built from that HEAD** (`cargo build --release`, `target/release/jigc`) against throwaway `mktemp -d` repos, unless it is explicitly marked a source read or a golden read. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 50 Increment 11; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D11** (partition by projected write-set; shared artifacts excluded; serial fallback) and ordering constraint 4 (*N12 lands before D11's pack work*); [gap-findings.md](completions/artifacts/M50/gap-findings.md) → **G** (fork 8's fit question) and **N12**; [baseline-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M50/baseline-ledger.md) → fork 8 (*the primitive is 100 % built, the pack composition 0 %*); [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) §3; [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → the pre-1.0 additive-key window and its discharge; [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → `fan-out` finalize (the two squash modes).

**Why:** the rule that a confirmed fix gets its own agent has been prose since M38 and was broken at M38, M42 and M49 — the encode already named in §3 (*a confirmed finding becomes a milestone sub-task, provisioned into its own worktree, joined at the barrier*) is unbuilt in the pack, and the envelope a fix-round orchestrator would read to attribute each fix to a commit is wrong.

**Basis — driven at `aa98d1b`; nothing carried from the roadmap, the charter or the gap-findings unverified.**

- **N12 reproduces, and its numbers are fixture-dependent — so the gap-findings' *"2 of its own 4"* is not restated as the defect.** Driven: a two-sub-task milestone under `finalize.fan-out.squash: false`, each sub-task staging one worktree code file and one authored `commit:<sub>` doc, lands **3** commits (`df8d37c` *feat: rework the low cache path* → `src/low.rs`; `08593a2` *feat: rework the zed cache path* → `src/zed.rs`; `05a4611` the aggregate → `.jigc/.gitignore`, `.jigc/config/manifest.yaml`, and the two promoted ADRs). The `--format json` envelope reports `committed.hash: "05a4611"` beside `files: 6` and a 6-entry `manifest` — of which that sha owns **4**. The two per-sub-task shas appear **nowhere** in the envelope, and `sub_tasks[]` carries exactly `{id, docs, code_files, provisioned, worktree_unreadable, discarded}` — **no `hash`**. The whole product of `squash: false` is the per-fix commits, and the envelope names none of them.
- **The `squash: true` cell is honest, so the axis has a true member.** The same fixture with the knob at its default lands **one** commit and the envelope's `manifest` is exactly that commit's five files (`files: 5`, `git show --name-only HEAD` identical). The fix is owed over `{squash:false × code-carrying, squash:false × code-less, squash:true}`, not over the reported repro.
- **The mechanical cause is two seams, both discarding what they hold.** `crate::task::chain_commit` (`task.rs:4478`) commits each sub-task in a dedicated worktree and returns only the folded hook string — each commit's sha exists at that instant and is dropped; `milestone_landed_summary` (`milestone.rs:4836`) then builds the manifest from **one whole-range** `git diff --name-status --no-renames <pre-boundary-HEAD> HEAD`, which is precisely where per-commit ownership is lost *(source read)*.
- **The parity fence is the compiler, so the envelope change and its fence repair are one gate-green unit.** `text_json_parity_axis.rs:1399` (`milestone_finalized_parity`) destructures `MilestoneLanded` **exhaustively** and `render::milestone_finalized` is registered `Tier::Fenced`, so a new field on `MilestoneLanded` or `SubTaskContribution` cannot compile until the fence carries it *(source read)*.
- **The additive-key window is open and its form is stated.** [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → *the pre-1.0 additive-key window* closes **at the 1.0 pin**, not at a wave name, and every addition is *"declared here, in its own paragraph, as it ships"* — *"an undeclared key on a pinned envelope is a defect, not an addition"*. So T1's shape rule is **additive only**: no pinned key changes meaning (the Settle prices a `files`/`manifest` correction as a **break**), and the declaration rides the same commit *(doc read, cited)*.
- **The fan-out primitive the Fix phase needs is shipped and reachable by an id the pack can name.** Driven end to end: `jigc milestone add-task <m> "<intent>" --workflow decided-task` exits 0, and `jigc milestone execute <m>` emits `Spawn: cd .jigc/worktrees/<sub> && jigc workflow <recorded-workflow> --task <sub>` — the Spawn line names **that sub-task's recorded minting workflow**, not the fan-out step's `run:` target, so the Fix phase needs **no new fan-out-bearing workflow**: `jigc milestone execute` composes the shipped `milestone-execution` (hardcoded at `milestone.rs:59`) over the fix round.
- **T2's red step is already run.** `jigc milestone add-task <m> "<intent>" --workflow fix-task` exits **1** today with `blocking · workflow-refs.unknown-workflow — no workflow \`fix-task\` …`, naming the 33 loaded workflows and a route. Neither `fix-task.yaml` nor `fix-finding.yaml` exists in either pack *(`ls`)*.
- **The round must run under `squash: false`, and the knob is reachable.** Driven in a set-up repo: `jigc config set finalize.fan-out.squash false` exits 0 (*"written to `.jigc/config/`, uncommitted"*) and `jigc config get` reads back `false  (project)`. Under the default `true` the round lands **one** commit for every fix, so there are no per-fix commits to attribute — which is also why N12 is the prerequisite rather than a rider. The `config set` write is not staged, so it does not trip the carryover gate at the round's mint doors.
- **The contradiction is live in the shipped bytes, and the golden pins it.** `packs/methodology/steps/fix-gate.yaml` reads *"One fixer per finding, **strictly serial over the one shared working tree**"*; `crates/cli/tests/goldens/compose/methodology/start--completion--*.txt:44` carries that sentence in all six fixture states; `implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md` §3 says *"Triage fixes should ride it … **That is the encode**"* and its Orchestration bullet says *"each confirmed fix is its own agent"* *(source + golden read)*.
- **A `fix-task` workflow needs no `allows-create` for its commit doc.** `should_provision_commit_doc` (`start.rs:420`) keys on `creates_task` alone and `selectable` is *deliberately not* a provisioning gate, so a `creates-task: true, selectable: false` workflow owns and authors its own commit doc exactly as `sub-task` does *(source read)*. `describe` renders every workflow — selectable or not — as *"<id> is <description>. Reach for it when <usage>. It is hidden from the router catalog: <suppressed.reason>"* (`describe--describe--fresh.txt:69`), so `description:`/`usage:`/`suppressed:{reason, expires}` are all owed; `when:` is not (the catalog shape fence scopes to `creates-task: true && selectable: true`).
- **Every workflow costs 12 goldens, and no count may be copied into the pack.** Each workflow carries 6 `start--<id>--<state>` + 6 `workflow-preview--<id>--<state>` captures; the tree holds **622** golden files at `aa98d1b`, not the **624** the roadmap's scope sentence carries forward from M49 — so the pack's shared-artifact rule ships as a *rule*, never as this repo's instances or counts *(`find | wc -l`, golden listing)*.
- **Declared bound, recorded rather than discovered at build: this repo is not self-hosted** (no `.jigc/`, no `docs/` at `aa98d1b`), so M50's own completion audit cannot run the composed Fix phase here. What this increment ships is the pack composition and the design of record; the first real run is an adopter's, or this repo's after the port that follows 1.0.0.

**The tasks.**

- **T1 — the landing ack names every commit the boundary made, and attributes every landed file to the sha that landed it (N12).** The `squash: false` chain seam (`crate::task::chain_commit` → `try_execute_finalize_plan`'s `ChainPerSubtask` channel) carries each per-sub-task commit's sha out instead of dropping it, and `milestone_landed_summary` stops deriving ownership from one whole-range diff. On the envelope the change is **additive only** — no pinned key changes meaning: `manifest` and `files` keep their **boundary-wide** membership (the doc-comment's own scope) and *gain* attribution, `sub_tasks[]` gains its own commit's sha (absent/`null` for a code-less sub-task and for every sub-task under `squash: true`), and the agent-text arm prints the same shas so the fence stays satisfied from one struct. `text_json_parity_axis.rs`'s exhaustive destructure is extended in the same commit — it cannot compile otherwise. [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) gains the **declaring paragraph** for the addition, in the form the window's discharge requires (an undeclared key on a pinned envelope is a defect, not an addition), and [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → `fan-out` finalize states what the ack says about the N+1 chain if the text shape moves. *Done:* a named suite driving the real binary over the cell set **{`squash:false` × code-carrying sub-task, `squash:false` × code-less sub-task, `squash:true`}** and asserting, per cell, (a) every sha `git rev-list <pre-boundary-HEAD>..HEAD` yields appears in the `--format json` envelope, (b) each `manifest` entry's owning sha **contains that path** — cross-read from `git show --name-only <sha>`, never from a reconstruction of what the code just wrote, (c) `sub_tasks[].hash` is that sub-task's own commit under the code-carrying cell and absent/`null` in the other two, (d) the agent-text arm prints the same shas; plus `cargo test -p cli text_json_parity_axis::` green; `dev/gate` green. **Red steps to prove, not assume:** (i) that the shas the chain hands out survive the fast-forward onto main (the commits are built in a dedicated worktree and ff'd — assert the envelope's shas against `git rev-list` on the *main* checkout, not against what `chain_commit` returned); (ii) that a path landed by more than one commit in the chain still yields **one** manifest entry, with the rule it resolves by stated in the doc-comment rather than discovered by a reader. *(files: `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/text_json_parity_axis.rs`, a new suite registered in exactly one group root (`groups/g_milestone.rs`), `design/command-output-contract.md`, `design/finalize.md`.)*

- **T2 — the fixer's walk exists as a composed workflow: `fix-task` and `fix-finding`.** `packs/methodology/workflows/fix-task.yaml` is minted on the `sub-task.yaml` mold — `creates-task: true`, `selectable: false` with `suppressed: {reason, expires}`, `description:`/`usage:` (both rendered by `describe`), **no `allows-create`** (a fix that would revise a settled decision is *contested* and belongs at §3's human gate, not in a fixer's hands). It composes `packs/methodology/steps/fix-finding.yaml` — the per-finding discipline the sub-task owns: **derive the axis and report its full membership** rather than fixing the reported site list (§3's brief rule, M46's four corrections its ground), the red that *is the finding reproduced*, the gate, and the two isolation constraints a fanned sub-task cannot break (`git add` your own paths inside **this worktree**; never `git commit`, never `jigc task finalize` here — either strands the work outside the milestone boundary) — followed by the commit authoring, which reaches methodology's `step:author-commit` and therefore keeps its `read.staged-read-back` declaration and its `jigc doc show … --task` read-back. Prefer methodology-local steps: a cross-pack `{{ include: step:… }}` where **both** packs ship that id resolves by precedence, and the walk that actually composes is the only evidence of which won. *Done:* `jigc milestone add-task <m> "<intent>" --workflow fix-task` exits 0 (red today: `workflow-refs.unknown-workflow`) and `jigc milestone execute <m>` emits `Spawn: cd .jigc/worktrees/<sub> && jigc workflow fix-task --task <sub>`; `jigc workflow fix-task --task <sub>` composes a walk whose bytes carry the axis-derivation rule, both isolation constraints, and the staged read-back; the pack-load fences stay green (`cargo test -p cli suppression_fence:: catalog_shape_fence:: read_back_fence:: stated_at_fence::`); the 12 new `*--fix-task--*` goldens and the moved `describe`/orientation goldens are regenerated (`UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 cargo test -p cli compose_goldens::`) and their diff reviewed; `dev/gate` green. *(files: `packs/methodology/workflows/fix-task.yaml`, `packs/methodology/steps/fix-finding.yaml`, a named suite registered in one group root (`groups/g_methodology.rs`), `crates/cli/tests/goldens/`.)*

- **T3 — the Fix phase becomes a fan-out, and §3 stops contradicting the step it composes.** `packs/methodology/steps/fix-gate.yaml`'s *"strictly serial over the one shared working tree"* is replaced by the composition D11 settled: partition the confirmed findings by each fix's **projected write-set** — a finding spanning two files is one sub-task, two findings in one file are one sub-task — then `jigc config set finalize.fan-out.squash false` (or there are no per-fix commits at all), `jigc milestone create`, one `jigc milestone add-task <m> "<intent>" --workflow fix-task` per partition, `jigc milestone provision`, `jigc milestone execute` (whose `Spawn:` lines are the fan-out), `jigc milestone join`, `jigc milestone finalize`. **Shared artifacts are excluded from the fan-out and applied serially after the join** — stated as the *rule* (an artifact every fixer would have to edit: a test-registry root, a generated golden set, a manifest, the doc every fix folds back into), never as this repo's instances or counts, because the pack ships to adopters. A round whose write-sets **cannot** be made disjoint falls back to the serial rule, stated up front rather than discovered at a blocked join. The three-round cap and the two-case human gate are kept verbatim. `implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md` §3 and its Orchestration bullet are rewritten to state the same rule the pack now composes — the M38/M42/M49 breaches stay as the *ground* for the encode, and *"That is the encode … Until that lands, the interim mitigation is …"* retires, since it has landed. *Done:* the composed `completion` walk carries the partition rule, the six-command sequence and the fallback, and **carries no serial-over-one-tree rule**; a named arm drives the emitted `jigc milestone add-task … --workflow fix-task` line **verbatim** against a real milestone and asserts exit 0 (it is a mechanical instruction in prose, so nothing else fences it); `grep -c "strictly serial"` over `packs/` is 0; the `start--completion--*` / `workflow-preview--completion--*` goldens are regenerated and reviewed; `dev/gate` green. **Red step to prove, not assume:** drive the whole sequence once end to end on a throwaway two-partition round and record what the knob write actually does on an **already-committed** config layer — `finalize` stages the config layer on its *first* commit, so on an established repo the knob change may be left uncommitted after the round; the step states what is true rather than what is convenient. *(files: `packs/methodology/steps/fix-gate.yaml`, `implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md`, a named suite registered in one group root, `crates/cli/tests/goldens/`.)*

**Ordering.** T1 first — the Settle's ordering constraint 4: the envelope is exactly what a fix-round orchestrator reads to attribute a fix to a commit, and building the pack composition on top of an ack that names no per-fix sha would ship the round before its own read-back. T2 second: T3's step emits `--workflow fix-task` as a literal command line, which the binary refuses until the workflow exists — landing T3 first would ship a step whose central instruction fails. T3 last, so the composed walk it pins is the finished one and its goldens are regenerated once.

## 2026-09-07 — M50 Increment 10 / T3: a pack-resource miss names the pack it searched, with a code and a route

**One literal answered at four sites and lied at all of them.** `crates/cli/src/start.rs`'s shared `read_pack` — serving `jigc start`, `describe`, `validate`, `upgrade`, `ingest`, `doc list` — plus `config.rs`'s two hand-copied knob reads (`config get`/`list`, `config set`) and `doc.rs`'s task-bound workflow read all said *"the embedded pack is missing `config/knobs`"*, with no finding code and no route. Driven on a manufactured two-pack composition (a throwaway dev-pack copy as the `JIGC_PACK_DIR` base, a throwaway methodology copy listed over it — `Pack: methodology/0.1.0 | dev/fs-local`), the embedded pack is **not in the composition at all**: the sentence named a pack that was never searched, at a door whose flattened text is the whole machine contract ([command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → *outside the envelope*). One producer now answers for all four — `start::pack_resource_missing`, reached through the shared `read_pack` the other three modules call instead of re-reading the pack — carrying `pack.resource-missing`, the searched pack-set, and a route.

**The per-site identity split does not hold, and the reason is the accessor, not the sites.** The decomposition proposed *the origin pack at `start.rs`, the pack set at the other three*. `PackSource::origin_pack` **falls back to `self` when no constituent owns the id**, so at a **miss** — the only state this finding exists for — it names the precedence winner rather than what was searched: the same lie one word over. So the producer names **its receiver's own provenance** (`provenance_segments()` × `provenance_entries()` — the `<id>/<version>` the `Pack:` header renders, each with its resolving path, highest-precedence first) and no site is special-cased. That turns out to be honest *per door* rather than uniformly composite, which is the sharper form of the split the roadmap was reaching for: `start::load_catalog` is handed a workflow's **origin pack** by the pack-local body-reference rule, so a `config/commands` miss there genuinely searched one pack and says so, while the two `config` doors and `doc`'s create-gate hold the composite and name both. The acceptance asserts the *absent* half too — a pack a door never looked in must not be named.

**The route is `Human` by adjudication, and the acceptance follows it instead of running an argv.** No jigc verb restores a pack resource, and under a `config/knobs` miss `jigc start`, `describe`, `validate`, `upgrade`, `ingest` and `doc list` all block on this very finding — so a mechanical route would either repair nothing or hard-reject, which [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) names as law 2 failing one level down and which M46's PT-1 already caught once (*a route that, followed exactly, changed nothing*). The task's done-criterion asked for a runnable argv; driven, that is unavailable here, so it is **replaced by a stronger check, not dropped**: each of the four cells reads the pack roots out of the **emitted message** and the file name out of the **emitted route**, restores the resource into the **lowest-precedence** root named, and re-drives the same door expecting success — a printed path that is not repo-real, a set that named only the winner, or a route that does not repair the state all fail there.

**The code joins no `CHECK_INVENTORY` row** (the `workflow-refs.unknown-workflow` / `milestone.unknown` precedent — it is a read fault, not a probe check), and the family joins `command-output-contract.md`'s declared *outside the envelope* list in the same commit, or that document's completeness claim would be silently false.

## 2026-09-07 — M50 Increment 10 / T2: a blocked join stops narrating a success it did not have

**Driven at HEAD, `jigc milestone join` over the shipped `join.same-doc-clash` fixture opened `joined milestone:cache-hardening — 0 doc(s) merged`, closed with the routing footer, and only then printed the block** — so the one door in the fan-out that refuses a merge narrated a completed join on stdout (law 1) and put its verdict *after* the line an agent reads as the end of the output. Two halves, two fixes. The **headline** now states the verdict: an outcome carrying any blocking finding renders `join blocked: milestone:<id> — <k> blocking finding(s); <n> doc(s) would merge, nothing committed`. The **order** now puts the house finding line first, before the stdout ack. **Stream discipline is untouched** — the finding is still on stderr and the ack still on stdout; what moved is what stdout *says* and when the block is written, not which stream carries it. The body under the headline is deliberately unchanged: under a block the overlay is the merge the join **would** have produced, which is the diagnostic the contending sub-tasks are read against, so suppressing it would trade one law-1 defect for a hiding one.

**The envelope joins the contract it already rides, and the integer does not move.** `--format json` carried `findings` with **no** `schema_version`, while the block envelope a refused write returns carries it beside the same key (driven: `doc create adr` under a workflow whose gate lists `[]` returns `{"schema_version": 3, "findings": [...]}`) — so of the two envelopes that hand a driver a blocking finding as *data*, one was version-checkable and the join was not. It now carries `engine::result::SCHEMA_VERSION`, **read, never retyped**: the integer is global, so a literal `3` here would survive a bump silently. This is an addition to an envelope, **not** a projection change, so the Settle's ordering constraint 1 (*any item moving the integer joins Increment 5*) is satisfied by moving it nowhere.

**One neighbour checked and deliberately left alone.** The ledger's N10 says the join was unversioned *"unlike every other findings envelope"*; driven, that is too strong — the `DocAck` **success** acks (`set-field` / `create` / `author` / …) also project `findings` with no `schema_version`. They are a different family (a write ack, not a report of what refused), they are out of this task's deliverable, and widening to them would move a pinned contract shape the Settle sized nowhere in this wave — so the observation is recorded rather than acted on, and the join's fix is not presented as closing a class it does not close.

**The acceptance drives the merged read, because two pipes cannot prove an ordering.** The arm captures stdout and stderr into **one file** through a cloned fd — the interleaving an agent actually sees — and asserts the blocking head appears at a lower offset than `cli::render::ROUTING_FOOTER`, with the finding's code cross-read from the *same* fixture's `--format json` run and the footer taken from the constant rather than spelled. The clash fixture is extracted to one helper both arms drive, so the `finalize` block and the join-surface block cannot drift on what a clash is. All three legs were shown red against the HEAD binary first, including the merged-order leg, which was driven rather than inferred from the two separate captures.

## 2026-09-07 — M50 Increment 10 / T1: every text render of a finding reaches the house renderer

Eight sites re-implemented one shape, and **four of them dropped the identity**: `describe` / `doc` / `start` / `task`'s `finding_to_err` rendered `finding.message` alone, while `config` / `milestone`'s funnels and `milestone`'s two stderr loops hand-copied the `severity · code — message` head. Driven at HEAD, `jigc describe` over a malformed workflow definition printed the same sentence on both surfaces — text *and* `--format json` — while `workflow-refs.missing-front-matter` existed only inside the binary, so a text-scraping driver had no `(code, target)` to key on and a JSON-reading one had none either. All six funnels are now a **one-line delegation** to `render::finding_error`, whose `BlockedFinding::Display` **is** `render::finding_line`, and the two milestone loops render that same line; the head is extracted as `render::finding_head` — the `<severity> · <code>` identity the ` — <message>` follows, which is exactly the half that went missing.

**The bytes at the two hand-copying modules were proven unchanged, not assumed.** The hand-copies and `finding_line` differ on the route-less-advisory `   (no action needed)` suffix and the trailing newline, so the delegation was captured before and after over twelve `config` + `milestone` doors (including `milestone join nosuch`) against binaries built from HEAD and from the change: **byte-identical, diff empty**. What did move is only what should — the four headless funnels and the two loops gained the head.

**One behavioural widening, recorded because it is real and not printed.** Only `cli.rs`'s `rename` arm and `task.rs`'s `discard` arm read the carrier back (`render::blocked_finding`), so a `milestone::finding_to_err` error raised inside `settle_discarded_sub_task` now downcasts where it previously did not: `jigc task discard` logs that refusal's **finding code** instead of one more anonymous exit 1. Same exit code, same printed bytes — `surface_commit_rejection`'s fall-through already printed the identical operational envelope — and it is what the carrier exists for.

**The sweep gains a second checked token and a third verdict, and the set is derived from the sweep.** `MESSAGE_SITES`' `Carries` verdict now owes **both** renderers (`finding_head` + `finding_locus`), because M49 checked the locus alone and four funnels passed it while printing no head at all — a check of one is a check of a strictly weaker claim. The decomposition named *two* legitimate relays; driving the sweep found **three** — `migrate_corpus::relayed`, `pack::def_load_failure` and `render::corpus_migration`, each disposed with the shape it composes and why the house line is not that shape — and `Relays` still owes the locus, so M49's fence is kept rather than traded. In the other direction the eight repaired sites hold **no row at all**: they read no `.message`, and a site that cannot re-implement the shape is not one the fence needs to watch.

**The acceptance drives, and cross-reads.** One named door per funnel-owning module — `jigc describe`, `jigc doc create adr --title T`, `jigc task validate <id>`, `jigc start --workflow <unknown>` — each asserting its **first stderr line** against `blocking · <code> — ` with the code read out of the *same run's* `--format json` `error` string, never spelled in the test. The manufactured state is a dev-pack copy with a broken `single-task` and **its manifest removed**: pack-load's eager front-matter sweep would otherwise refuse first through `pack::def_load_failure`, and a manifest-less constituent is skip-on-absent **by design**, so this is the shipped posture in which a definition defect is supposed to reach the lazy compose-path loaders these doors are — not a trick to dodge a fence. `flow9_seam`'s clash arm gains the same cross-read for the blocked join, shown red against the old loop before the fix was restored.

**`command-output-contract.md`’s complement clause is corrected in the same commit.** *"discards the `Finding`, keeping only `message` + `route`"* is false of what ships: the funnel **flattens** the finding, so the code and the locus ride inside the `{"error": …}` text. The envelope still projects **no `code` field and no `key`** — the declared bound is unchanged — which is what keeps these families a complement to the key claim rather than an exception to it.

## 2026-09-07 — M50 Increment 10 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 10](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the finding-render class and pack identity in errors*) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `bc595f1` (tree clean; Increments 1–9 landed). Every behavioural claim below was **driven with the debug binary built from that HEAD** on `dev/jigc-rig` corpora (`fresh` / `committed-singletons`, with `--pack-from-dev` and `--workflow <id> <file>` for the manufactured-pack arms) unless it is explicitly marked a source read. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 50 Increment 10; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D14** (N10 and N19 are admitted to a tier here) and ordering constraint 1; [baseline-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M50/baseline-ledger.md) → **N10** · **N19** · the coverage table's *finding text renders* row; [planning-gate-record.md](completions/artifacts/M50/planning-gate-record.md) → **T1-8**; [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → *outside the envelope* (`:202`) and The stable finding key; [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → law 1.

**Why:** the same `Finding` reaches an agent with its code at one door and without it at the next — so a text-scraping driver can key on `(code, target)` at `config` and `milestone` and cannot at `start`, `task`, `doc` or `describe` — while a pack-resource miss blames *the embedded pack* for a resource of a pack read off the filesystem, route-less and code-less at all four of its sites.

**Basis — driven at `bc595f1`; nothing carried from the roadmap or the gate-record unverified.**

- **The split is live and is exactly two-and-four.** `jigc config set no-such-knob x` → `blocking · config.undeclared-key — …` + route; `jigc milestone join nosuch` → `blocking · milestone.unknown — …` + `at:` + route. Against that: `jigc start --workflow no-such-wf "probe"` prints `no workflow \`no-such-wf\` — …` with **no head**, though the finding it flattens carries the code `workflow-refs.unknown-workflow` (`start.rs:3628`); and a workflow definition broken in a manufactured pack yields the identical headless `workflow definition has no \`---\`-fenced front-matter block` at **`jigc describe`**, **`jigc task validate <id>`** and **`jigc doc create adr --title T`**. Four doors, one shape, no code.
- **The mechanical cause is two hand-copies, and the house form is already public.** `config.rs`'s and `milestone.rs`'s `finding_to_err` each build `format!("{severity} · {} — {}", code, message)` by hand; `describe.rs` / `doc.rs` / `start.rs` / `task.rs`'s do not build it at all. `render::finding_line` is private — which is *why* two modules copied it — but **`render::finding_error` is `pub` and already delegates to it** through `BlockedFinding`'s `Display` (`render.rs:4275`, `:4304`), and four doors (`migrate` / `relocate` / `rename` / `task bind`) already refuse through it. The shared home exists; six funnels do not use it *(source read)*.
- **`milestone.rs`'s two stderr renders print `finding.message` bare** — `blocked` (`eprintln!("{}", finding.message)` then `at:` then `route:`) and `dispatch_join` (the same loop) — so the milestone module both *has* the head in one function and *drops* it in two others *(source read)*.
- **`dispatch_join` narrates success before it reports the block.** It `println!`s `render::milestone_join`, whose agent-text arm opens `joined milestone:<id> — N doc(s) merged` and closes with `ROUTING_FOOTER`, and *only then* loops the blocking findings to stderr — a law-1 lie about a join that committed nothing. Its JSON arm is `serde_json::to_value(outcome)` plus `milestone` and `no_docs_from`, and carries **no `schema_version`**, unlike every other findings envelope (`jigc start --format json` and the `write.*` reject envelope both carry `"schema_version": 3`) *(source read + driven for the two comparanda)*.
- **All four `read_pack`-family literals reproduce, and each names the wrong pack.** On a `--pack-from-dev` rig (a real directory pack, `Pack: dev/fs-local` in the orientation header, so the identity is demonstrably in hand): deleting `config/knobs.yaml` → `jigc config list` **and** `jigc config set docs-root docs` both exit 1 with `the embedded pack is missing \`config/knobs\`: no pack resource of kind config with id \`knobs\``; deleting `config/commands.yaml` → `jigc start --workflow quick-fix "probe"` → `the embedded pack is missing \`commands\`: …`; deleting the recorded workflow of a live task → `jigc doc create adr --title T` → `the embedded pack is missing \`quick-fix\`: …`. Route-less, code-less, and the pack is not embedded.
- **`origin_pack` cannot name an origin for a *missing* resource.** Its default body returns `self`, and `CompositePack`'s override returns the first constituent whose `read` **succeeds**, falling back to `self` when none owns the id (`packsource.rs:196`, `pack.rs:2044`) — so at a miss it answers the composite, whose un-overridden `own_pack_id` reads `config/defaults` through precedence and names the winning pack. The honest identity at a miss is the **set**: `provenance_segments()`, overridden by `CompositePack` to concatenate every constituent (`pack.rs:2074`), which is what already renders the `Pack:` header. T3 drives this rather than trusting the roadmap's per-site split *(source read, marked; T3's red step settles it)*.
- **A new operational code needs no inventory row and must clear one collision test.** `workflow-refs.unknown-workflow` and `milestone.unknown` are both minted outside `CHECK_INVENTORY` (`result.rs:331-363`), so severity-tunability is not owed; the one binding check is `invocation_log`'s `no_registry_member_collides_with_the_finding_inventory`, and `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` holds no `pack.*` member *(source read)*.
- **The blast radius of the head is test bytes, and it lands in the same commit.** `crates/cli/tests/anyhow_route_spans.rs` asserts **emitted stderr bytes** at exactly these doors, and the blocked-join suites (`flow9_milestone_join.rs`, `flow9_seam.rs`, `milestone.rs`, `milestone_join_collision.rs`) assert the clash render — so the change and its forced repairs are one gate-green unit, not a task each *(source read)*.
- **`command-output-contract.md:202` becomes false the moment T1 lands** — *"[`finding_to_err`] **discards the `Finding`**, keeping only `message` + `route`"* — and its correction rides T1: the flattened text will carry severity, code, locus and route; what stays true is that the envelope projects **no `code` and no `key`**, which is the declared funnel exception itself.
- **Only two doors read the carrier back.** `render::blocked_finding` is consumed at `cli.rs:797` (`rename`) and `task.rs:296` (`task discard`) alone, so routing the six funnels through `finding_error` cannot silently re-shape any other door's `Outcome`; `task discard`'s survivable-frame path is the one place a new downcast could divert, and T1 asserts it does not *(source read)*.

**The tasks.**

- **T1 — every text render of a finding reaches the house renderer, and the sweep checks the head as well as the locus.** The six `finding_to_err` funnels (`config.rs`, `describe.rs`, `doc.rs`, `milestone.rs`, `start.rs`, `task.rs`) delegate to the shared `render::finding_error` carrier instead of re-deriving or omitting the head; `milestone.rs`'s `blocked` and `dispatch_join` render each finding through the same house line (`render::finding_line` lifted to `pub(crate)` if the stderr-loop shape needs the line rather than the carrier). `located_finding_text.rs`'s `MESSAGE_SITES` gains a **second checked token** — a `Carries` row's enclosing body must reach the head renderer *and* the locus renderer — and a **third verdict** for the legitimate relays that render a finding's words inside their own framing rather than as a findings line (the roadmap names two; the set is **derived from the sweep**, and a site the roadmap did not name — `pack.rs`'s `def_load_failure`, `render.rs`'s `corpus_migration` — is disposed with a stated reason, never skipped for not being on the list). Every test and golden the head break forces is repaired **in this commit** (`anyhow_route_spans.rs`'s emitted-bytes arms; the four blocked-join suites), and [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md):202's *"keeping only `message` + `route`"* is corrected in the same edit to state what survives (no `code`, no `key` in the envelope) and what changes (the code and the locus now ride the flattened text). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli located_finding_text::` green with both checked tokens and every row disposed, plus a named driven arm per module — `jigc describe`, `jigc doc create`, `jigc task validate <id>`, `jigc start --workflow <unknown>` each emitting stderr whose first line matches `blocking · <code> — `, the code cross-read from the same run's `--format json` `error` string so the assertion cannot pass over a reconstruction; `dev/gate` green. **Red steps to prove, not assume:** (i) that `config`'s and `milestone`'s emitted bytes are **unchanged** by the delegation (the hand-copies and `finding_line` differ on the route-less-advisory suffix and the trailing newline — if a shipped finding trips either, the task records it rather than absorbing it); (ii) that `task discard`'s rejection framing is unmoved now that a funnel error can downcast to `BlockedFinding` at `task.rs:296`. *(files: `crates/cli/src/{config,describe,doc,milestone,start,task,render}.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/located_finding_text.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/anyhow_route_spans.rs`, the blocked-join suites, `design/command-output-contract.md`.)*

- **T2 — a blocked join stops narrating a success it did not have, and its envelope names its version.** `dispatch_join`'s stdout narration must not read as a completed join when a blocking finding is present, and the routing footer must not stand between the reader and the block; **stream discipline is kept** (findings stay on stderr, the ack on stdout — the fix is what stdout *says*, not which stream it uses). `render::milestone_join`'s JSON arm gains **`schema_version`** from the shipped `engine::result::SCHEMA_VERSION`, i.e. the integer **does not move** — the Settle's ordering constraint 1 sends any item that moves it to Increment 5, which has landed, so this is the envelope joining the contract it already rides, not a bump. *Done:* a named arm over the shipped `join.same-doc-clash` fixture asserting (a) the clash run's **stdout** contains no completed-join claim, (b) the blocking finding is legible ahead of the routing footer in the merged agent read, and (c) `--format json` carries `schema_version` beside `findings`, with `engine::result::SCHEMA_VERSION` read from the constant rather than retyped; `cargo test -p cli text_json_parity_axis::` still green (the fence is text→JSON directional, so an envelope-only key must not redden it — asserted, not assumed); `dev/gate` green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/flow9_milestone_join.rs` or a named sibling.)*

- **T3 — a pack-resource miss names the pack it searched, with a code and a route.** The four sites — `start.rs`'s `read_pack`, `config.rs`'s two `config/knobs` reads, `doc.rs`'s recorded-workflow read — stop saying *the embedded pack*: each names the pack identity **already in hand at the site** and each becomes a routed blocking `Finding` (one code, one route) instead of a bare `anyhow` `with_context`. The code joins no `CHECK_INVENTORY` row (the `workflow-refs.unknown-workflow` / `milestone.unknown` precedent) and is checked against `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`'s collision test; because it only ever flattens, it joins [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md)'s declared *outside the envelope* list in the same commit — a family that reaches a funnel and no key needs its exception declared, or the contract's completeness claim is silently false. *Done:* a named test driving **all four** sites on a manufactured two-pack composition (deleting `config/knobs`, `config/commands`, and a live task's recorded workflow), asserting exit 1, a first stderr line matching `blocking · <code> — `, the **packs actually searched** named in the message, and the emitted `route:` argv **run verbatim**; `dev/gate` green. **Red step to prove, not assume:** the roadmap's per-site identity split (*origin pack* at `read_pack`, *the pack set* at the other three) rests on `origin_pack`, which falls back to `self` at a miss and therefore names the precedence winner rather than the searched set — T3 drives each site under two composed packs and picks the accessor that is **honest**, recording the correction if the split does not hold. *(files: `crates/cli/src/{start,config,doc}.rs`, a new `crates/cli/tests/` suite registered in exactly one group root, `design/command-output-contract.md`.)*

**Ordering.** T1 first: it is the class, and it is the only task whose fence change and behaviour change cannot be separated — delegating a funnel removes `finding_locus` from its body and reddens the shipped sweep, so the render fixes, the sweep's second token and the forced byte repairs are one gate-green commit or none. T2 second: T1 makes the join's block *legible*, and T2 is what stops the door lying about it — two defects of one door that T1's renderer leaves standing. T3 last, so its new refusal is asserted through the house renderer T1 installed rather than against a shape that is about to move.

## 2026-09-07 — M50 Increment 9 / T3: the fence gains the address-shape × declaredness cross, and `validation.md`'s universal becomes checkable

**A fence with one axis is satisfied by one cell of every column it does not have.** The shipped fence over `write_miss_shape_axis.rs` (`every_doc_write_verb_taking_a_section_hop_answers_an_undeclared_one`) asked only *does each `doc` write verb drive **one** `write.unknown-section` row* — so it was green while the undeclared-section column held one cell of eighteen, and green again while the address-shape column held none. It now carries the cross: **`MISS_SHAPES`**, thirty-nine rows, one per `(verb, address shape, leading-hop declaredness)` the verb rejects, **each carrying the code it must earn**, totalled against `CELLS` **in both directions** — no row may claim a cell nothing drives, and no driven cell carrying an address-shape verdict may sit outside the table. The coordinate names the question and the code names the answer, which is why the code is part of the row: at `#a/b/c` under a declared leading hop a verb answers `write.unknown-section` (a later hop declared nowhere) *or* `write.not-present` (the item never minted), and only the first is this cross's business.

**The verb half is derived; the shape half is manufactured, and says so.** The verb axis stays `VERB_KINDS ▸ doc ▸ Write`, the table already fenced against the clap tree. The shape half deliberately departs from *enumerate the registry*, in `crates/cli/tests/support/shape_space.rs`'s idiom and for its reason: `engine::address::Fragment` supplies hop counts and **no verdicts** — which shapes a resolver rejects lives in four hand-written `match` arms — and **declaredness is a property of a fixture**, not of any registry, since nothing in the codebase knows that `releases` is declared and `no-such-section` is not. A fence looping a table here would enumerate hop counts, find nothing attached, and prove nothing. `FIXTURE_SECTIONS` is pinned against the fixture schema text so a renamed section cannot leave it quietly wrong.

**A third disposition, because two could only be satisfied by silence or by eighteen batch rows.** `jigc doc author` carries **no address argv at all** — a payload's section ids and `set:` keys are lowered onto the five addressed verbs' own resolvers — so it joins neither the rows nor `NO_SECTION_HOP`: it is `COVERED_BY_LOWERING`, and its three shipped `CELLS` rows are the witness that the lowering carries the code through rather than re-deriving it. The assertion is two-sided: at least one of those rows must carry an address-shape verdict, and **none** of them may carry a `{addr}` argv (a row that does belongs in the cross). `NO_SECTION_HOP`'s two members are re-dispositioned against the widened axis, and **`doc rename`'s reason now records a driven fact rather than a shape claim**: its `#fragment` refusal is *routed and followable* (`route: run jigc doc rename <doc> --to <title>`) but carries **no code** and rides the `{"error": …}` envelope — the last bare-sentence write reject on the `doc` surface, and Increment 10's, not this cross's.

**The widening bought six cells on its first run, and the red proves the fence bites in both directions.** Direction 1 reddened at T2's HEAD naming six rows nothing drove — the ≥4-hop address under an **undeclared** leading hop at all five addressed verbs (every column above holds one dimension fixed: the address-shape rows all sit under a declared leading hop, the undeclared-section rows all stop at three hops) plus `set-slot`'s `#<undeclared>/<hop>`, the one two-hop undeclared cell no other verb had left open. All six were already **correct** at HEAD — rank 1 answers before the id chain is walked, so every one is `write.unknown-section` however deep the address goes — and all six were **undriven** until the cross demanded a witness. Direction 2 was shown red separately, by deleting one `MISS_SHAPES` row: the `CELLS` row that drove it is reported untabled by name.

**The second property is the envelope itself.** Naming the miss and routing the recovery are both properties *of a finding*; the defect this increment closes is one seam earlier — a reject that never became one. So `every_write_miss_answers_inside_the_finding_envelope` drives every `CELLS` row and asserts the pinned `ValidationReport` shape (`schema_version` + a non-empty `findings`) with **no top-level `error` key**. It is the one assertion that reddens when a resolver regresses to a bare `anyhow` *whatever code the row expects*.

**And `design/validation.md` stops asserting a universal a reader cannot check.** *"It is now true at every door"* — the sentence M47 increment 6 left as an advisory and M49 turned into a claim — is replaced by the **named fence** that holds it, with the manufactured half declared as manufactured and the three dispositions spelled out, so the doc points at the thing that would go red rather than at a reader's willingness to believe it.

## 2026-09-06 — M50 Increment 9 / T2: the two `Result` resolvers' remaining bare arms adjudicate

`field_target` and `slot_target` — and the `undeclared_section_guard` they share — return **`Result<_, Finding>`**, the same type-level closure T1 installed at the two `Option` resolvers: an error type a bare `anyhow` cannot inhabit, so the escape `DocFailure`'s blanket `From<anyhow::Error>` opens is closed by the signature rather than by a later grep. M49 reached these two resolvers for the undeclared-**section** miss alone; every *other* unmappable shape kept the bare `{"error": "no field addressed by …"}` / `{"error": "no slot addressed by …"}` envelope — code-less, route-less, outside the finding envelope — at `set-field` (both flags), `set-slot`, and `jigc doc author`, which reaches both resolvers through `apply_leaf`'s `SetField` / `SetSlot` arms.

**Seven cells, and the declaredness dimension crosses this arm once, not twice.** M49's rank-1 `undeclared_section_guard` already answers the undeclared *leading* hop at both hop-bearing forms, so what was left is the declared side: `write.wrong-shape` — the genuine declared-shape defect — at a bare `<type>:<slug>` with no fragment (either verb) and, at `set-slot`, a declared section that hosts no prose slot (repeatable, or simple and slotless) plus an item address with no slot leaf hop. The **exception is the single hop** `#<name>` at `set-field`: it names no section at any hop — a field-id search across every declared section — so `write.unknown-section` there would be a law-1 lie about sections that all exist. Driven, not reasoned: `set-field <changelog>#owner` resolves *through* the declared header section that carries a field of that id. It is an undeclared **leaf**, so it earns `write.unknown-field` at `--value` and `--unset` alike, with the miss's `at` naming the search the form performs rather than a section it never addressed.

**The bound is rewritten, not kept.** `design/validation.md`'s closing sentence — *"it keeps the resolver's own **no field addressed by** sentence"* — is falsified by exactly this task, so it now states what survives (never `write.unknown-section`, with the driven datum) and what changed (an unmatched single hop is an undeclared leaf), and records that the surviving bound is a **type**, not a promise.

**The sentences differ per cell because the defect does; the code does not.** A `set-slot` at `#<section>` whose section declares no slot **is** the form the verb takes, so T1's *"`{uri}` is not that form"* wording would itself be a law-1 lie there — T1's helper is split into `ranked_shape_reject` (the shared rank-1 + target stamp) and the form-sentence `unmappable_address` over it, and the section-level cells supply their own sentence: *is repeatable — it declares no section-level prose slot* / *declares no prose slot* / *a per-item prose slot carries its leaf hop*. One unreachable bare arm was **deleted rather than given a code**: after the guard passes, `field_target`'s `UnitLeaf` section lookup cannot miss, so its `None` arm was a sentence standing over a state that cannot arise.

**The fixture gains one ingredient, and it is a *header* section.** `set-slot` at a declared, slotless section had no target anywhere in `write_miss_shape_axis.rs`'s changelog (`overview` declares a slot; `staged` / `releases` are repeatable), and every fields-only section in both shipped packs (`adr` `status`, the `spec`/`commit`/`arch-doc` headers) declares `header: true` — so the fixture mirrors the corpus rather than manufacturing a shape no doctype has. The batch door's inheritance was driven both ways: the same payload key over `#meta` blocks with the code and route, while the legitimate `set: {overview: <<…>>}` still lands at exit 0.

## 2026-09-06 — M50 Increment 9 / T1: the two `Option` resolvers adjudicate

`add_item_target` and `remove_item_target` take the `Schema` and return **`Result<_, Finding>`** — an error type a bare `anyhow` cannot inhabit, so the escape `DocFailure`'s blanket `From<anyhow::Error>` opens is closed at the **type** level rather than by a later grep — and the four bare `with_context`s die with them (`run_add_item`, `run_remove_item`, `run_retitle_item`, and `apply_leaf`'s `AddItem` arm, the batch door). One ranked reject at each (`unmappable_address`): rank 1 asks the shipped `engine::write::undeclared_section_splice` about the **leading** hop → `write.unknown-section` from the engine's own sentence; otherwise `write.wrong-shape`, minted through `engine::write::generate_error_finding` so the per-code route map stays the one owner, naming the form the verb takes and claiming no absence. `write.not-present` earns no cell: nothing has been looked for in the corpus yet.

**Thirteen `CELLS` rows, not the plan's eleven — derived by driving, not by reading the plan.** The decomposition gave the item verbs four shapes each; the axis has **five**, because the address-shape dimension crosses the declaredness one twice, not once. `remove-item` / `retitle-item` reject three shapes (no fragment · a 1-hop section · a 3-hop `#section/item/leaf`), and both hop-bearing shapes take a declared **and** an undeclared leading hop: `#releases` → `write.wrong-shape` while `#no-such-section` → `write.unknown-section`, and `#releases/1-3-0/summary` → `write.wrong-shape` while `#no-such-section/9-9-9/summary` → `write.unknown-section`. The plan's count crossed only the 1-hop shape. `add-item`'s three (no fragment · 2-hop declared · 2-hop undeclared) stand as planned. An agent's report is a lead, not a measurement — the count came from driving the debug binary over the suite's own fixture through `dev/jigc-rig`.

**The red-step assumption is discharged, and both halves stand.** The plan warned that the `write.wrong-shape` cells sharing one target (`{addr}` with no fragment, at three verbs) might trip the debug key-discrimination assert, in which case the sentence would keep and the target would go. They do not: `debug_assert_keys_discriminate` is scoped to **one serialized slice**, and each of these rejects is one invocation emitting one finding, so the collision the assert forbids cannot arise across separate calls. Driven under `cargo test` (debug posture), all four seam asserts pass — so every new cell carries `key.target` == `location.address` == the full write address, the matrix property the suite asserts over every row.

**One declared bound in the suite is retired because this closes it.** The M49 header's *"at `remove-item` the same string names no item at all … and left as it is"* was true of `#releases/1-3-0/bogus` at HEAD and is now false: that address earns `write.wrong-shape` at both item verbs (the leading hop `releases` is declared, so rank 1 has nothing to say). The `set-field` single-hop bound is untouched — that is T2's resolver and its own sentence.

## 2026-09-06 — M50 Increment 9 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 9](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the write-miss route floor*) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `c599aae` (tree clean; Increments 1–8 landed). Every behavioural claim below was **driven through the real binary** — `cargo build --release` at that HEAD, on `dev/jigc-rig committed-singletons --binary target/release/jigc` corpora, over both the fixture-free dev pack (`adr:…`) and the shipped `changelog` — unless it is explicitly marked a source read. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 50 Increment 9; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D10**; [baseline-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M50/baseline-ledger.md) → §1 row 6 (W-15's prescribed fix, **refused at razor leg 1**) and **N18**; [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The `write.*` route split (`:77`); [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Every write resolves its address before it moves bytes (the rank *shape → item presence → leaf declaration*); [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → The stable finding key.

**Why:** five `doc` write verbs answer an address miss with a bare `{"error": "no … addressed by …"}` at exit 1 — code-less, route-less, outside the findings envelope — so a driver keying on `(code, target)` sees nothing and an agent is handed no recovery, at eighteen cells rather than the one W-15 reported.

**The charter's prescription stays refused, and the class is enumerated instead.** W-15 asked for `write.unknown-section` at the section-only `set-field` miss. Driven, that hop is a **field-id search across every section**: `jigc doc set-field adr:some-choice#status --value x` *resolves* (the `status` section's `status` field) and is rejected on the value, while `#nosuchfield` finds nothing. Minting `write.unknown-section` there would be a law-1 lie about declared sections, so the bound is **kept** — and the cell still stops being bare, because the truthful code is `write.unknown-**field**`: no section declares a field of that id, and `jigc doc schema <doctype>` answers exactly that. The bound was always *never `unknown-section`*, never *stay silent*.

**Basis — driven at `c599aae`; nothing carried from the roadmap, the charter or the trial unverified.**

- **Eighteen bare cells, not "~10".** Every one exits **1** with `{"error": …}` on `--format json` and the bare sentence on text. `add-item`: no fragment · 2-hop over a **declared** section (`#releases/1-0-0`, `#context/x`) · 2-hop over an **undeclared** one (`#nosuch/x`) — all three `no section addressed by`. `remove-item` **and** `retitle-item`, identically (they share `remove_item_target`): no fragment · 1-hop **declared** (`#releases`, `#context`) · 1-hop **undeclared** (`#nosuch`) · 3-hop `#section/item/leaf` (`#releases/1-0-0/link`) — `no item addressed by`. `set-field`: no fragment · 1-hop matching no declared field, at both `--value` and `--unset` — `no field addressed by`. `set-slot`: no fragment · 1-hop at a declared **repeatable** section (`#releases`) · 1-hop at a declared **simple, slotless** section (`adr:…#status`, a **frozen dev-pack** shape) · 2-hop `#repeatable/item` (`#releases/1-0-0`) — `no slot addressed by`.
- **The control cells already answer, which is what makes these a sweep gap.** At the **same** addresses: `add-item #nosuch` → `write.unknown-section` + the schema route; `set-slot #nosuch` → the same; `set-field #releases/nosuch` → `write.unknown-field`; `add-item #context` (a declared simple section) → `write.wrong-shape`. So [validation.md](design/validation.md):77's *"it is now true at every door"* is **false at `remove-item` / `retitle-item` / the 2-hop `add-item` form** — the same miss, one door over, with no code at all.
- **Six producers, one class, and every other `with_context` in `doc.rs` is an I/O fault.** The address-miss bare producers are exactly `doc.rs:1385` (`run_add_item`), `:2082` (`run_remove_item`), `:2208` (`run_retitle_item`), `:3670` (`apply_leaf`'s `AddItem` arm — the batch door), and the two closures `field_target`'s `no_field` (`:6116`) and `slot_target`'s `no_slot` (`:6228`). The other nineteen `with_context` sites read or persist bytes. **No test, golden or pack file asserts any of the four sentences** — only three doc-comments and `validation.md` mention them (source read + grep across `crates/`, `design/`, `packs/`, `implementation/`).
- **`add_item_target` / `remove_item_target` are the two resolvers M49 left behind.** They still return `Option`, so every caller `with_context`s a bare anyhow; `field_target` / `slot_target` were lifted to `Result<_, DocFailure>` at M49 Inc 11 T3 for precisely this reason and their *remaining* bare arms are the residue. `DocFailure` carries a blanket `From<anyhow::Error>` into its `Orchestration` arm, which is the mechanism that makes a bare miss the path of least resistance (source read).
- **`doc author` needs no second guard, and its `add-item` arm does.** `apply_leaf` lowers `SetField` / `SetSlot` through the same `field_target` / `slot_target`, so a fix there reaches the batch by construction ([write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md):97) — driven: a payload leaf at `#releases/9-9-9/nosuchleaf` already answers `write.unknown-field` with the schema route. Its `AddItem` arm re-wraps `add_item_target` at `:3670` and is the one batch site the resolver lift must also reach.
- **The codes are the split's own four, and `write.not-present` earns no row.** All four bare misses are answerable **from the schema**, so all four route the shipped `jigc doc schema <doctype>` read; at no bare cell is any item *named and absent*, so minting `write.not-present` — whose route is a `doc show` over live item ids — would name an absence nothing asserted. Twelve cells earn `write.wrong-shape` (the address form does not name what the verb writes), four earn `write.unknown-section` (rank 1: the leading hop is declared nowhere), two earn `write.unknown-field` (the single-hop `set-field` form). `write.wrong-shape`'s schema route is followable *because* `doc schema` has projected the settable **write addresses** since M43.
- **`doc rename` and `doc show` are outside the deliverable, and neither is a silent narrowing.** `jigc doc rename adr:x#context --to Y` answers with a sentence **and a runnable route** (driven) — not bare; its missing *code* is the finding-render class [Increment 10](implementation/roadmap.md) owns. `doc show --task <id>` with no address (baseline **N16**) is a **read** verb; the deliverable names write verbs.
- **Posture bound, stated rather than assumed.** The census above was driven **release**, where the `Finding` seam's four debug asserts (route presence, placeholder substitution, key discrimination, `stamp_target`'s URI-normal target) do not run. Today's cells emit no `Finding` at all, so release/debug cannot differ *at HEAD* — but every cell below starts emitting one, so each task's red step runs under `cargo test` (debug) and that is where those asserts are first exercised.

**The tasks.**

- **T1 — the two `Option` resolvers adjudicate, and the four bare `with_context`s die.** `add_item_target` and `remove_item_target` take the `Schema` and return `Result<_, Finding>` — an error type that **cannot carry a bare anyhow**, so the escape `DocFailure`'s blanket `From` opens is closed at the type level rather than by a later grep; the callers `.map_err(DocFailure::block)`. One ranked predicate at each: rank 1 asks the shipped `engine::write::undeclared_section_splice` about the **leading** hop → `write.unknown-section`; otherwise the address form names nothing the verb writes → `write.wrong-shape`, whose sentence says which form the verb takes (`add-item` mints into a repeatable section; `remove-item`/`retitle-item` address `#<section>/<item>`) and never claims an absence. Eleven `CELLS` rows join in the same commit: `add-item` × {no fragment → `wrong-shape`, 2-hop declared → `wrong-shape`, 2-hop undeclared → `unknown-section`} and `remove-item` **and** `retitle-item` × {no fragment → `wrong-shape`, 1-hop declared → `wrong-shape`, 1-hop undeclared → `unknown-section`, 3-hop `#section/item/leaf` → `wrong-shape`}. Every row is a `CELLS` row; none joins `NO_SECTION_HOP`, which holds *verbs* that carry no section hop and none of these is one. *Done:* `cargo test -p cli write_miss_shape_axis::every_write_miss_names_its_own_miss_and_routes_the_recovery` green with the eleven rows, each asserting the code, the emitted route **run verbatim**, the staged bytes byte-identical, and `key.target` == `location.address` == the full address (the matrix property); the shipped `every_doc_write_verb_taking_a_section_hop_answers_an_undeclared_one` still green; `dev/gate` green. **Red step to prove, not assume:** the four new `write.wrong-shape` cells at the *same* target (`{addr}` with no fragment, at three verbs) must not trip the debug key-discrimination assert — if they do, the sentence stays and the target does not, and the task records which. *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/write_miss_shape_axis.rs`.)*

- **T2 — the two `Result` resolvers' remaining bare arms adjudicate, and the declared bound is restated where it is now false.** `field_target`'s `no_field` and `slot_target`'s `no_slot` stop being `anyhow` closures; both resolvers (and the shared `undeclared_section_guard`) carry `Finding` as their error, same type-level reason as T1. Seven `CELLS` rows: `set-field` × {no fragment → `write.wrong-shape`, 1-hop unmatched at `--value` → `write.unknown-field`, the same at `--unset` → `write.unknown-field`} and `set-slot` × {no fragment → `wrong-shape`, 1-hop declared **repeatable** → `wrong-shape`, 1-hop declared **simple with no slot** → `wrong-shape`, 2-hop `#repeatable/item` → `wrong-shape`}. **The single-hop `set-field` bound is kept and narrowed in the same commit**: [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The `write.*` route split, whose closing sentence *"it keeps the resolver's own **no field addressed by** sentence"* T2 falsifies — rewritten to state what survives (never `write.unknown-section`, because the hop names no section and `#status`-style hops resolve against **declared** ones) and what changes (an unmatched single hop is an undeclared **leaf**, `write.unknown-field`, schema route). The slotless-simple-section row has **no ingredient in the fixture** — `CHANGELOG_SCHEMA` declares none — so it is driven either by extending that schema (with every `CELLS` row's byte-identity assertion repaired in the **same** commit, since a new section renders into `provision()`'s doc) or by its own named test in the same file on the dev pack's `adr:…#status`, the shape this plan drove; the choice is the executor's, the coverage is not. *Done:* the same axis test green with the seven rows under the same four assertions, plus the slotless row green wherever it is driven; `cargo test -p cli doc::` green (the `field_target` alias unit tests are hit paths and must not move); `dev/gate` green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/write_miss_shape_axis.rs`, `design/validation.md`.)*

- **T3 — the fence gains the address-shape × declaredness dimension, and `validation.md`'s universal becomes checkable.** The shipped `every_doc_write_verb_taking_a_section_hop_answers_an_undeclared_one` has a **verb** axis only and is satisfied by *any* one `write.unknown-section` row per verb — which is how eighteen cells stayed invisible under a green fence. It gains the cross: a `MISS_SHAPES` table, one row per (verb, address shape, leading-hop declaredness) the verb's resolver **rejects**, each carrying the code it must earn, asserted total against `CELLS` in both directions. The shape half is **stated as manufactured** in the file's own header, in `support/shape_space.rs`'s idiom and for the same reason: `engine::address::Fragment` supplies the hop count but nothing in code enumerates *which* shapes a resolver rejects, and declaredness is a property of a fixture, not of a registry — a suite that looped `Fragment` would drive the parseable forms and report an axis it never reached ([baseline-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M50/baseline-ledger.md) → the coverage table's `write-miss shapes` row, *partial*). The **verb** axis stays derived from `VERB_KINDS ▸ doc ▸ Write` and grows a third disposition beside `CELLS` and `NO_SECTION_HOP`: `doc author` is **covered by lowering**, with the reason stated and its three shipped rows as the witness, so the fence cannot be satisfied by silence and cannot demand eighteen batch rows either; `NO_SECTION_HOP`'s two members (`doc create`, `doc rename`) are re-dispositioned against the **widened** axis, `doc rename`'s reason recording that its fragment refusal is routed (driven) and that its missing code is Increment 10's. [validation.md](design/validation.md):77's *"it is now true at every door"* is corrected in the same commit to name the fence that holds it rather than to assert a universal a reader cannot check — statement == fence, the rule this repo already applies to `is_route_exempt` and `ROUTE_PLACEHOLDERS`. *Done:* a named test (the widened fence) red at T2's HEAD against a deliberately removed `MISS_SHAPES` row and green with the table complete; a second named arm asserting the **envelope** property over every `CELLS` row — `--format json` carries `schema_version` + `findings` and **no top-level `error` key** — which is the deliverable stated as a property rather than as a count; `dev/gate` green. *(files: `crates/cli/tests/write_miss_shape_axis.rs`, `design/validation.md`.)*

**Ordering.** T1 first: it is the larger motion (a signature change at four call sites, one of them the batch door) and it is what makes `validation.md`'s undeclared-section universal true at the three doors where it is false.
