**Declared bounds carried to the executor.** (i) **Findings at orientation are real work, not a file read** — the Settle's *"two enumerators that already ship"* holds for five keys and not the sixth; the sweep shells out to git, spawns the `doc-code` probe and materializes `.jigc/index/edges.json`, at the door the adapter runs on `SessionStart`. (ii) **`orient.rs`'s and `render.rs`'s doc-comments are corrected in the same commit that falsifies them** — this milestone's fold-backs exist because two planners inherited exactly such a sentence. (iii) **No second bump**: T2 and T3 add no key to any versioned envelope, and the composed `{task, text}` projection is untouched by construction. (iv) **Whether orientation's rendered findings also ride the invocation log's `finding_codes` is the executor's call, but it must not be silent** — `Outcome::with_findings`' doc-comment enumerates *"the report-bearing verbs (validate / finalize)"*, so either the third verb joins that sentence or `run_orient` states why it does not. (vi) **The variant carries no workflow catalog** — bootstrap state 3 carries none and D3's key list names none; a reader who wants the catalog runs the router form, which is what T3 makes state-aware. (vii) **`jigc start --task <id>` and `jigc workflow <id> --preview` are out of scope** — B8 names the bare, router and `--workflow` forms, and the resume door already names its own task through `task_state_lines`.

**Scope coverage, bullet for bullet** ([roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Increment 5 *Deliverable* + *Grouped scope*): **a third `OrientationView` variant carrying the active set (id, workflow, intent, base, staged, findings-as-data), collapsing bootstrap's states 3 and 4 so no second bump is owed** → **T2** · **the selection rule stated per `start` form — bare renders the variant** → **T2**; **the router and `--workflow` forms name the open task without suppressing a second mint** → **T3** · **the `Run:` directives include `task discard`, naming Increment 3's consent or conditioned on `staged`** → **T2**, resolved to the consent arm on driven evidence (the mint itself stages `commit:<id>.md`, so the other arm would render never) · **`describe`'s definitions arm gains `origin_pack`** → **T1** · **one `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2→3 for both, with an explicit intentional-bump test on the `rejected_demotions` precedent** → **T1** (the bump, the test, and the whole measured fallout), with T2 and T3 adding no second bump · **fold-back: `render.rs:94-96`'s dead premise deleted** → **T2** · **[write-commands](design/write-commands.md):167 corrected to what ships with a *triggered* ledger entry for the remainder** → **T2** · **[introspection](design/introspection.md):56 narrowed to content against [doc-read-surface](design/doc-read-surface.md):167's home** → **T1**. Nothing is deferred out of the increment and nothing rides along to *"a later task"*.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 4 / T4: `uninstall` stops taking the workbench bytes no index has a copy of

`jigc uninstall` opens with `remove_dir_all(<repo>/.jigc)`, guarded by two refusals — a fan-out worktree holding content (M47) and an open task's staged docs (M46/M49) — that rest on **one** ground: *no commit has a copy of these bytes*. Stated over the whole tree that ground covers a third set neither guard looks at, so blocking **`uninstall.untracked-workbench-file`** now refuses over it: a path under `.jigc/` outside the transient `gitignore::ENTRIES` prefixes that no index carries.

**Added, never substituted.** `tasks/` and `worktrees/` are *inside* `ENTRIES`, so the literal reading — *everything untracked under `.jigc/`* — would have swallowed the two subjects M46 Inc 2, M47 Inc 3 and M49 built guards for and answered them with the wrong code and the wrong route. They are excluded by construction, and the acceptance drives that separation: a staged task doc still draws `uninstall.staged-prose`, never the new code.

**In the index is the line, not committed.** `git ls-files --cached` lists a staged add, and a staged add is `git checkout -- <path>`-recoverable after the teardown takes the working-tree copy — so an in-index file is **narrated, not refused**, joining the loss narration `DESTROYING_DOORS` already owes at this door. The untracked conjunct is mandatory rather than a nicety: a fresh `jigc setup` **tracks every non-transient path it writes**, so without it the guard would fire on every ordinary install.

**The behaviour change is stated, not discovered.** `jigc config set` writes `.jigc/config/manifest.yaml` and tracks nothing, so an `uninstall` after any `config set` now refuses until that delta is in an index or `--force` consents — before this it destroyed the project's whole recorded cascade delta at exit 0. Not a fork: `design/project-setup.md` → G5 states the guards' one provable ground and explicitly refuses to discriminate authorship, so a file jigc itself wrote is not exempt from the rule jigc's own guards run on.

**The subject is a derivation, not a registry** — a path computation over the seven `ENTRIES` prefixes plus one `git` query — so a prefix added to that constant narrows the set automatically. The probe fails closed under the same code, on the shipped `unverified_worktrees_finding` precedent. Ten fixture failures across two suites were repaired in the same commit, all one shape: corpora that hand-write `.jigc/config/*` (and let a jigc verb seed `.jigc/.gitignore`) while skipping the `jigc setup` that tracks them — an uncommitted fixture artifact must not decide a verdict on the freeze or worktree axis those arms are declared on.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 4 / T3: a root the store cannot describe is refused before it is written

The home rule asks *whose* directory a root-knob value names; this asks whether the value is a usable root at all. Three shapes are not, all three driven at HEAD on a `committed-singletons` rig, and blocking **`config.unusable-root`** now refuses each at every `ROOT_KNOBS` member in the step-2b position — after `check_value`, before anything moves and before the knob lands, for the reason 2b and 2c already state.

- **File-shaped** (`README.md`) — the knob lands at **exit 0 with every move failed**, and `jigc doc list` then drops the re-rooted docs from the store surface **entirely**. That is worse than the Settle's N5 records (*"every move failed"*), and it is the exact state `run_set`'s own rationale says must not exist, produced by the door that states it.
- **Absolute** (`/tmp/elsewhere`) — silently reinterpreted as repo-relative by `trackable.rs`'s `trim_matches('/')`: the mover stages `R docs/roadmap.md -> tmp/elsewhere/roadmap.md` while `jigc config get` echoes `/tmp/elsewhere` back, so the knob and the store name different homes for one doc.
- **Through a symlink** (`linked`) — git records the link, never a path through it, so the move stages `RD`: an index entry the worktree has no path for, leaving `doc list` and git permanently disagreeing.

**Two elaborations the shapes force.** The symlink subject is **every existing component of the value, not its leaf** — a symlinked *ancestor* (`linked/sub`) reaches the identical `RD` state, driven separately. And the walk starts at the repository root and **never canonicalizes the root itself**: a repo legitimately sits under a symlinked ancestor (every macOS temp corpus lives under `/var` → `private/var`), so an ancestor-canonicalizing form would refuse every root in every such repo. A value naming no component at all (`""`, `.`) is the repo root and stays admitted — the flat layout both knobs document, and what `docs_root::` / `placement_override::` / `corpus_migration_backstop::` require.

**One code for all three, with the reason in the message** — `config.untrackable-root`'s five-reasons-one-code shape, on the ground that the operator's fix is identical in each case: supply a different root. Neither this code nor `config.workbench-root` joins a registry, following its precedent.

**The refusing arm ships with an admitting arm, and that is not decoration:** a predicate that refuses everything satisfies "refuse three shapes", so `ROOT_KNOBS ×` {unset, the repo root, an existing directory, one jigc must create} is driven to exit 0 on its own corpus per cell, asserting the knob reads back **and** that the store still describes both managed docs — the property the file-shaped cell broke.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 4 / T2: jigc's own workbench is not a home for managed docs

Both root knobs took `.jigc` and moved the committed docs there at exit 0 — driven on a `committed-singletons` rig, `docs-root .jigc` staged `R docs/research/root-knob-probe.md -> .jigc/research/root-knob-probe.md`, and `placement-root .jigc` reaches the same state — into the one tree `jigc uninstall` removes **whole** (`setup::uninstall` step 1 is `remove_dir_all(.jigc)`). Blocking **`config.workbench-root`** now refuses it at every `ROOT_KNOBS` member, in the shipped step-2b position: after `check_value`, before anything moves and before the knob lands, because a warn-and-proceed loses the bytes at exit 0 and a landed knob with no move leaves the store pointing at a home no doc is at ([storage.md](design/storage.md) → Placement gains the rule's home, where `untrackable` had none).

**A separate predicate at the knob door, not a widening of `config.untrackable-root`** — `.jigc` is a path git records perfectly well; what disqualifies it is ownership. `trackable.rs` is untouched, since its stated rule (*a gitignored destination stays permitted*) is what `relocate`'s squatter displacement into `.jigc/displaced/` depends on.

Two elaborations, both driven rather than inferred: the comparison **folds case** (`placement-root .JIGC` staged `docs/roadmap.md -> .JIGC/roadmap.md` while the bytes landed in the real `.jigc/` — index and worktree naming different directories for one file), which is the rule `trackable.rs` already applies to `.git` for `core.protectHFS`/`protectNTFS`; and only the value's **first** component is asked, because the workbench is exactly one directory and a nested `docs/.jigc` is not it.

**One falsified claim corrected in the same motion.** `untrackable_home_axis`'s gitignored-bound arm used `.jigc` as its exemplar, and `.jigc/roadmap.md` is **ignored by nothing** — `.jigc/.gitignore` lists only the transient subdirs (driven; `.jigc/displaced/x.md` *is* ignored). The arm is re-based onto a root the fixture's own `.gitignore` covers and now **asserts** that it is ignored before moving, so the bound it exists to pin (*ignoring is not untrackable*) is pinned on something.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 4](implementation/roadmap.md) (*family 3: `ROOT_KNOBS`, the home rule, the value rule, and `uninstall`'s third subject*) into **4 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `2e7850d` (tree clean; Increments 1–3 landed). Every basis below was **driven on the binary built from that HEAD** in throwaway `dev/jigc-rig` corpora, or measured by a **spike that was applied, gated and reverted** — unless it is explicitly marked a source read or a grep. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 50 Increment 4; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D8** (the home rule, the value rule, `uninstall`'s added third subject) · *Ordering constraints* #5; [charter.md](completions/artifacts/M50/charter.md) → Tier 1, W-14; [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Placement (`placement-root`, and the census's declared-or-resolved axis); [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Teardown / cleanup (G5), *the two states that refuse the teardown outright*; [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → the three laws · the route floor; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §4 (the fixture substrate); [dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → *a grep is not a fence*.

**Why:** both root knobs accept values that leave the store describing a home no clone can reproduce, and the teardown then removes the bytes without naming them.

**Basis — driven at `2e7850d`. Two of the record's stated facts were sharpened by measurement and one of its premises does not hold across the shipped corpora.**

- **Both knobs take the workbench, and `docs-root` reaches the identical loss.** On a `committed-singletons` rig, `jigc config set placement-root .jigc` exits **0**, stages `R docs/decisions-log.md -> .jigc/decisions-log.md` and `R docs/roadmap.md -> .jigc/roadmap.md`, and `jigc doc list` then reports both as `managed` under `.jigc/`. On a `refs-post-hoc` rig, `jigc config set docs-root .jigc` moves `docs/research/context-loss.md → .jigc/research/context-loss.md` the same way. The axis is **both knobs**, as D8 states.
- **`uninstall` then destroys all of it at exit 0, naming none of it.** Continuing that rig with one hand-dropped `.jigc/notes.md`, `jigc uninstall` prints `- removed .jigc/` and exits **0**; afterwards `notes.md` is gone with no copy anywhere, and the two relocated managed docs are gone from the worktree (recoverable only because their `R` renames sit in the index). The teardown's narration named neither the docs nor the untracked file. This is W-14 reproduced whole.
- **The workbench predicate must fold case, and this is driven, not inferred.** `jigc config set placement-root .JIGC` exits 0 and lands `decisions-log.md`/`roadmap.md` **inside the real `.jigc/`** on this machine's case-insensitive filesystem — the same reason `trackable.rs`'s `.git` component test compares case-insensitively (`core.protectNTFS`/`protectHFS`). A case-sensitive predicate is a hole on the majority filesystem.
- **The value rule's three shapes, each reproduced.** **File-shaped:** `placement-root README.md` exits 0, prints `could not relocate (… File exists (os error 17)) — move it by hand` for *every* doc, lands the knob — and `jigc doc list` afterwards **silently drops** `roadmap` and `decisions-log` from the store surface entirely (worse than the Settle's N5 records: not merely "every move failed", but two managed docs vanished from the index read). **Absolute:** `placement-root /tmp/elsewhere` exits 0, creates `<repo>/tmp/elsewhere/`, `doc list` reports `tmp/elsewhere/roadmap.md`, and `jigc config get placement-root` echoes back `/tmp/elsewhere`. The mechanism is `trackable.rs:59`'s `let relative = relative.trim_matches('/')`, which is precisely why the shipped `config.untrackable-root` check does not catch it. **Symlinked:** `placement-root linked` (and `linked/sub` — a symlinked **ancestor** is enough, driven separately) leaves `git status` at `RD` for every moved doc — a staged add whose worktree path git considers deleted — while `jigc validate` reads through the link and reports the store clean at **exit 0**.
- **The predicate must examine the components of the *value* only.** On macOS the corpora live under `/var/folders/…`, where `/var` is itself a symlink; an implementation that canonicalizes the repo root or walks ancestors above it refuses every fixture in the suite. `""` and `.` carry zero components and stay admitted, which `docs_root::`, `placement_override::` and `corpus_migration_backstop::` all require.
- **`.jigc` as a root is asserted as *working* by a standing test, so the home rule's repair is forced in the same motion** *(grep over all of `crates`, `design`, `implementation`, `packs`: exactly three sites)*. `untrackable_home_axis::a_gitignored_root_still_relocates_because_ignoring_is_not_untrackable` runs `config set placement-root .jigc` and asserts the move lands — its doc-comment says *"it must keep passing"* — and the bound it pins (*ignoring is not untrackable*) is real and must survive; its module doc-comment `:26` and `config.rs:366`'s comment both state in prose that `placement-root .jigc` keeps working. No other test or golden sets either knob to `.jigc` or a child.
- **The home predicate cannot be folded into `trackable.rs`.** That module's doc-comment states the opposite rule by design (*"a gitignored destination is a perfectly trackable path"*) and its unit test `an_ordinary_or_merely_gitignored_destination_is_admitted` lists `.jigc/roadmap.md` and `.jigc/displaced/roadmap.md` as **admitted** — `relocate`'s squatter displacement into `.jigc/displaced/` depends on it, and that path is not a root-knob door. The new predicate is a **third, separate** one at the knob door; `trackable.rs` is untouched.
- **`uninstall`'s guard blast radius is measured, not estimated — an applied spike, gated, reverted.** With the third subject spiked into `uninstall`'s step 0, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` yields exactly **10 failures across 2 group targets** (~3 150 otherwise green): `freeze_enforcement` ×5 (`every_door_blocks_on_a_drifted_frozen_schema`, `a_shape_changing_project_schema_shadow_blocks_every_door`, `a_presentation_only_project_schema_shadow_composes_clean`, `a_drifted_slug_rule_blocks_every_door`, `a_manifest_omitting_the_slug_rule_blocks_every_door`) and `uninstall_worktree_guard` ×5 (`uninstall_still_tears_down_a_repo_with_no_worktrees`, `uninstall_still_tears_down_when_every_provisioned_worktree_is_clean`, `the_clean_teardown_still_names_the_ignored_bytes_it_destroys`, and both `uninstall_route_*` arms). Spike reverted; tree at `2e7850d`.
- **All ten are fixture-shaped, and the suites that drive a real `jigc setup` stayed green** — `uninstall`, `flow48_acceptance`, `flow49_acceptance`, `staged_prose_consent_axis`, `adapter_artifact`, `format_json_success_axis`, `text_json_parity_axis`, `not_in_repo_axis`, `leftover_probe_fail_closed`. The ten fail because their corpora hand-write into `.jigc/` without an install commit (`uninstall_worktree_guard::set_squash_false` writes `manifest.yaml` directly; `freeze_enforcement` writes `packs.yaml` and `config/schemas/adr.yaml`), leaving `.jigc/.gitignore`, `.jigc/config/packs.yaml`, `.jigc/config/manifest.yaml` or `.jigc/config/schemas/adr.yaml` untracked. On a real `jigc setup` the whole non-transient set **is** tracked (driven on a `fresh` rig: `.gitignore`, `AGENT.md`, `config/.gitkeep`, `config/packs.yaml`, `version`), so D8's premise holds exactly where it was stated.
- **But there is one reachable *product* cell the Settle did not price, and it is named rather than discovered.** `jigc config set <knob> <value>` writes `.jigc/config/manifest.yaml` **untracked** and says so in its own ack (*"written to `.jigc/config/`, uncommitted — commit it with your next commit"*), so after this task an `uninstall` following any `config set` on a fresh install refuses until the operator commits or passes `--force`. **This is not a fork.** [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Teardown / cleanup (G5) states the guards' one provable ground — *no commit has a copy* — and explicitly refuses to discriminate authorship (*"the probe cannot tell prose someone typed from the pristine skeleton `jigc start` mints, the skeleton is in fact the dominant cell, and it refuses over both on the one ground it can prove"*). The locked doc answers the cell; the plan states the consequence as an **intended behaviour change** and puts it in T4's acceptance so it ships visible, exactly as Increment 3 / T2 did for `jigc task discard` needing `--force` from mint onward.
- **The `ROOT_KNOBS` pair is exactly two hand-written sites** *(grep)*: `config.rs:319` (the empty-value canonicalization) and `:368` (the untrackable check). The per-knob dispatch at `:387` (`key == "docs-root"`) and `:397` (`key == "placement-root"`) are the two **re-point movers** — one each, not the pair — and are deliberately not collapsed. No other module carries the pair; `start.rs:3248`/`:3336`, `pack.rs`, `render.rs` and `route_fence.rs` each name one key for its own reason.
- **`config.workbench-root` and `config.unusable-root` are free namespaces, and neither joins a registry** *(source read)*. The shipped `config.*` family is `undeclared-key`, `value-rejected`, `untrackable-root`, `step-id-collision`, `anchor-absent`, `nested-fill`, `fill-point-absent`, `shadow-id-collision`; `config.untrackable-root` is a member of **neither** `engine::result::CHECK_INVENTORY` nor `cli::invocation_log::ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` (2 hits in the whole tree), and these two follow it. Its shape is also the precedent for **one code per predicate with the reason in the message** — five distinct reasons ship today under `config.untrackable-root`.
- **`uninstall.untracked-workbench-file` is free** *(grep: zero hits)*, and the `uninstall.*` family already carries eleven per-condition codes, so a third guard code is the house shape rather than a new one.
- **The conjunct is *in the index*, not *committed* — sharper than "tracked", and it is what makes the rule true.** `git ls-files --cached` includes a staged add, and a staged add is in the object DB, so `git checkout` recovers it; the `.jigc/tasks/` bytes `staged_task_prose` refuses over are **gitignored** and therefore never in the index at all. So *in the index ⇔ recoverable* holds, and the two guards' grounds are one ground stated twice.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** The one place the record left room — whether `.jigc/config/manifest.yaml` after a `config set` is a false positive — is answered by the locked doc quoted above rather than chosen.

- **T1 — the two root knobs get one home.** Mint `ROOT_KNOBS: &[&str] = &["docs-root", "placement-root"]` in `crate::config` with a doc-comment stating what makes a knob a member — *its value names a repo-relative directory that every managed doc's home resolves through, and re-pointing it **moves committed docs*** — and both hand-written `matches!(key, "docs-root" | "placement-root")` sites (`config.rs:319`, `:368`) read it. The two per-knob re-point movers (`:387`, `:397`) are **not** collapsed into it: each dispatches one knob to its own floor, and merging them would be a different change wearing this one's name. Behaviour-identical; **no printed byte moves**. *Done:* a new `crates/cli/tests/root_knob_rules.rs`, registered in **exactly one** group root (`g_config.rs`, beside `untrackable_home_axis`), carrying two arms — a source fence that reads `crates/cli/src/config.rs` through `include_str!` (the `milestone_record_fresh_clone::no_home_still_says_the_record_lacks_the_minting_workflow` precedent) and asserts the pair literal appears **nowhere**, red at HEAD with two occurrences and green after; and a derivation arm asserting every `ROOT_KNOBS` member is a declared knob in the pack's `config/knobs.yaml`, so a renamed knob cannot leave the registry silently stale. The fence lives in a *different* file from the one it scans, because a fence whose own assertion message carries the literal it forbids can never go green. `cargo test -p cli config_read:: docs_root:: placement_override:: untrackable_home_axis::` green with assertions **unchanged**. Full unscoped gate green (`dev/gate`). *(files: `crates/cli/src/config.rs`, new `crates/cli/tests/root_knob_rules.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/groups/g_config.rs`.)*
- **T2 — jigc's own workbench is not a home for managed docs.** A third predicate in one home beside `ROOT_KNOBS` — *this path is jigc's workbench* — applied at `run_set` to **every** `ROOT_KNOBS` member, placed with the shipped step-2b check: after `check_value`, **before** anything moves and before the knob lands. It mints blocking **`config.workbench-root`** with the reason in the message and a route that names a home outside `.jigc/` and `jigc config list` for the value in force, following `config.untrackable-root`'s shape. Its subject is the value resolving to `.jigc` itself or any path under it, compared **case-insensitively per component** (driven: `.JIGC` lands docs in the real `.jigc/`), and it keys on **neither gitignore nor trackability** — `trackable.rs:19-23` requires a gitignored destination to stay permitted and `relocate`'s squatter displacement into `.jigc/displaced/` depends on it, so `trackable.rs` is untouched and this is a separate predicate at a different door. **This is one atomic motion:** the guard reddens `untrackable_home_axis::a_gitignored_root_still_relocates_because_ignoring_is_not_untrackable`, whose gitignored exemplar *is* `.jigc`, so the arm is re-based in the same commit onto a gitignored root that is not the workbench (a `.gitignore` line the fixture writes for a plain directory), preserving the bound it exists to pin — *ignoring is not untrackable* — and its module doc-comment `:26` plus `config.rs:366`'s comment are corrected rather than left asserting a behaviour the binary no longer has. [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Placement gains the rule's home, where `untrackable` has none today. *Done:* new `root_knob_rules::` arms over `ROOT_KNOBS × {.jigc, .jigc/displaced, .JIGC}` — six cells, each asserted **refused and inert** on all three facts the shipped `assert_refused_and_inert` helper checks (the finding is raised with `config.workbench-root`, **nothing moved**, and the knob did **not** land) — plus the re-based gitignored arm green; `cargo test -p cli untrackable_home_axis:: placement_override:: docs_root:: orphan_detection:: unmanage::` green. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/config.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/untrackable_home_axis.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/root_knob_rules.rs`, `design/storage.md`.)*
- **T3 — a root the store cannot describe is refused before it is written.** The same registry, the same placement, one blocking **`config.unusable-root`** carrying the reason — one code per predicate, on `config.untrackable-root`'s five-reasons-one-code precedent — over the three shapes D8 names, each driven at HEAD: a **file-shaped** root (`README.md` — the knob lands with every move failed *and* two managed docs disappear from `jigc doc list`), an **absolute** value (`/tmp/elsewhere` — silently reinterpreted as repo-relative `tmp/elsewhere/` by `trackable.rs:59`'s `trim_matches('/')` while `config get` echoes the absolute form), and a **symlinked** root, refused when **any existing component of the value** is a symlink (driven: a symlinked *ancestor*, `linked/sub`, reaches the identical `RD` state). The predicate walks the components of the **value** starting at the repo root and never canonicalizes the root itself — on macOS the corpora live under a symlinked `/var`, so an ancestor-canonicalizing form refuses every fixture — and `""`/`.` carry zero components and stay admitted. *Done:* new `root_knob_rules::` arms over `ROOT_KNOBS × {file-shaped, absolute, symlinked leaf, symlinked ancestor}`, each refused-and-inert with `config.unusable-root`; **admitting** arms for `""`, `.`, an existing directory (`docs`) and a not-yet-existing one (`notes`), which is what keeps the refusal a rule rather than a new gate on the door; `cargo test -p cli placement_override:: docs_root:: corpus_migration_backstop:: unmanage:: untrackable_home_axis:: flow50_acceptance::` green. [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Placement's rule paragraph extended with the value half in the same voice. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/config.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/root_knob_rules.rs`, `design/storage.md`.)*
- **T4 — `uninstall` stops taking the workbench bytes no index has a copy of.** A **third** step-0 guard beside `dirty_fanout_worktrees` and `staged_task_prose` — never replacing them, since `worktrees/` and `tasks/` are *inside* `ENTRIES` and the literal reading would re-open the defects M46 Inc 2, M47 and M49 built guards for. Its subject is every file under `.jigc/` that is **(a)** under no `crate::gitignore::ENTRIES` prefix **and (b)** absent from the index (`git ls-files --cached -- .jigc` — the *index*, not `HEAD`: a staged add is in the object DB and therefore recoverable, which is exactly why the conjunct is trackedness), minting blocking **`uninstall.untracked-workbench-file`** that names each path, with **`--force` the single consent** — the same word the door's other two guards use. A file that *is* in the index is **narrated, not refused**: `narrate_teardown` gains its third clause beside the worktree and staged-prose ones, because the shipped teardown removed a tracked `.jigc/roadmap.md` and `.jigc/decisions-log.md` naming neither (driven). **This is one atomic motion, and its cost is measured:** the guard reddens exactly **10 tests across `freeze_enforcement` and `uninstall_worktree_guard`** (enumerated in the basis above), all because those corpora hand-write into `.jigc/config/` without an install commit — so the fixtures are repaired in the same commit, and `freeze_enforcement`'s `FREEZE_DOORS` row for `uninstall` keeps `clean: CleanExit::Zero`, since an uncommitted workbench file must not decide a verdict on the *freeze* axis. [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Teardown / cleanup (G5)'s *"**Two** states refuse the teardown outright"* becomes three in the same edit, with the third's ground stated as the two existing ones' ground. *Done:* a new `crates/cli/tests/uninstall_workbench_subject.rs`, registered in **exactly one** group root (`g_milestone.rs`, beside `uninstall_worktree_guard`), driving the real binary: **(a)** a hand-dropped `.jigc/notes.md` blocks with `uninstall.untracked-workbench-file`, the path is named, **nothing is removed** (`.jigc/`, `CLAUDE.md`, the settings file and the guide artifact all still present) and the route names `--force`; **(b)** the reachable product cell — `jigc setup` then `jigc config set docs-root notes` then `jigc uninstall` — blocks on the untracked `.jigc/config/manifest.yaml`, asserted as the **intended behaviour change** with the locked ground quoted in the arm; **(c)** `--force` tears the same corpus down at exit 0; **(d)** the `ENTRIES` complement holds — a staged doc under `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/` still draws `uninstall.staged-prose`, never the new code, so the three guards stay distinct subjects; **(e)** a file **added to the index** at `.jigc/kept.md` does **not** block and **is named** by the narration before the removal (the fixture stages it with `git add` rather than through a root knob, so T2's refusal cannot invalidate the arm). `cargo test -p cli freeze_enforcement:: uninstall_worktree_guard:: uninstall:: staged_prose_consent_axis:: flow48_acceptance:: flow49_acceptance:: destroying_doors::` green. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/setup.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/{freeze_enforcement.rs, uninstall_worktree_guard.rs}`, new `crates/cli/tests/uninstall_workbench_subject.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/groups/g_milestone.rs`, `design/project-setup.md`.)*

**Why this order.** T1 first because D8's ordering constraint #5 puts `ROOT_KNOBS` before both predicates that read it, and because it is the one task that changes no behaviour — landing it alone proves the registry is a pure refactor rather than hiding a rule inside one. T2 before T3 because the home rule is the increment's *Proves* line and because it shrinks the state space T3's fixtures have to build. T4 last for two reasons: it is argv-disjoint from the knobs, and its narration arm needs a tracked file under `.jigc/` — a state T2 would forbid reaching through `config set`, so building it after T2 forces the fixture to the honest `git add`, whereas building it before would pin a route T2 then closes.

**Declared bounds carried to the executor.** (i) **`trackable.rs` is not edited.** Its rule (*a gitignored destination stays permitted*) is load-bearing for `relocate`'s squatter displacement, and both new predicates are separate ones at the knob door; a "fix" to `trim_matches('/')` there would change three other callers that pass computed repo-relative paths and is not this increment's. (ii) **One code per predicate, reason in the message**, on `config.untrackable-root`'s shipped shape; splitting the value rule into three codes is a decision this plan does not carry. (iii) **Neither new `config.*` code joins `CHECK_INVENTORY` or `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`** — verified at plan time; the executor re-runs `invocation_log::tests::no_registry_member_collides_with_the_finding_inventory`. (iv) **The `uninstall` refusal after a `config set` is intended and is stated in T4 arm (b)** — it is not a licence to exempt jigc's own written files from the subject, which is the discrimination [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → G5 refuses by name. (v) **This increment guards the *door*, not the resolved cascade** — a project whose `manifest.yaml` already carries `placement-root: .jigc` from a hand edit or a pre-fix run keeps resolving it, exactly as a hand-edited manifest already bypasses the re-point floor ([storage.md](design/storage.md) → Placement); no corpus migration is owed, because a cascade value is outside every `schema-hash`. (vi) **The `.jigc` literal stays inside the new predicate**, not minted as a repo-wide constant: 91 `join(".jigc")` sites exist across 21 modules, and a constant used by two of them would be a false single home. (vii) **A new suite file is registered in exactly one group root** (`autotests = false`; `tests/test_target_registration.rs` fences it both ways). (viii) **`ENTRIES`' complement is a derivation, not a registry** — a 7-prefix path computation plus a git query — and Increment 13's flow-51 arm must say so rather than dressing it as a code-side registry, per D8.

**Scope coverage, bullet for bullet** ([roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Increment 4 *Deliverable* + *Grouped scope*): **`ROOT_KNOBS` replaces the two hand-written `matches!` (`config.rs:319`, `:368`)** → **T1** · **the home predicate — *this path is jigc's own workbench* — refusing `.jigc` and its children at both knobs, keyed on neither gitignore nor trackability** → **T2**, with the case-folding half added on driven evidence (`.JIGC` lands in `.jigc/`) · **the value predicate: a file-shaped root, an absolute value, a symlinked root** → **T3**, with the symlink subject widened from the leaf to any existing component of the value, driven · **`uninstall`'s added third subject — under no `ENTRIES` prefix and untracked — leaving M46/M47/M49's two guards intact, a tracked one narrated not refused** → **T4** · **the rule takes a home at [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Placement, where `untrackable` has none today** → **T2** (the home half) and **T3** (the value half), one paragraph written in two commits. Nothing is deferred out of the increment, and nothing rides along to *"a later task"*.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 3 / T3: the safety floor denies the two human-owned destroyers, and the self-collision paragraph stops claiming a reach it never had

**Shipped.** `Bash(jigc uninstall:*)` and `Bash(jigc milestone discard:*)` join the Claude Code profile's **`deny`** safety floor ([settle-record](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D9**). T2 gave `jigc task discard` the same staged-prose refusal `uninstall` already carried, but a refusal an agent can consent past with `--force` is not a floor: both of these doors delete bytes that exist in **no object DB**, and spending them is the operator's call. `deny` is the only surface the profile can say that on — it **blocks**, and the profile has no prompt key to express anything softer (`AdapterAllowlist` carries exactly `permit` and `deny` under `deny_unknown_fields`). It reaches **already-installed** repos because `inject_deny` is append-if-absent and runs on every `setup`; narrowing the `permit` instead would have reached **zero** installs, the permit being a prefix pattern injected purely additively and never pruned — and pruning a user-owned settings file is what M48's refuse-to-clobber posture refuses. `remove_deny` is `inject_deny`'s exact inverse and is driven off the same profile list, so the teardown round-trip carries the two new patterns without a line of teardown code.

**`jigc milestone provision` is deliberately off the floor** (D9's own B6 re-settle, and not an omission): ordinary provision destroys nothing — its destruction sits behind the same `--force` under M48's fail-closed leftover classifier — and denying the verb an unattended fan-out runs would park that fan-out on a decision nobody is watching, which is exactly what D11 makes the fan-out the wave's Fix-phase mechanism to avoid. The new test asserts that **absence** as well as the two presences, so a later "while we're here" addition has to argue with a stated reason rather than slip in.

**Pinned against the loaded profile, not the golden.** `the_deny_floor_carries_the_two_human_owned_destroyers` reads `load_profile("claude-code").allowlist.deny` rather than the `claude_code_profile_bytes_are_canonical` snapshot, because a golden is *re-accepted* when it moves: a later profile edit that reshuffles or rewrites the floor would drop either pattern silently and `cargo insta accept` would bless it. The two inline snapshots (the profile bytes and the deny-merge JSON) are updated as the mechanical consequence; the load-bearing assertion is the new one.

**The design correction ([assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md) → No self-collision, `:89`).** That paragraph closed with *"the floor constrains the agent, not the CLI"* — a claim about **who the floor reaches**, drawn from a survey of jigc's own `git add`/`git commit`/`mv` shell-outs and nothing else. It never contemplated the third case: the agent asking **jigc** to perform the deletion, where the destroying request is the agent's and the hands are the CLI's. That case is precisely these two verbs. The sentence is replaced by the narrower one that actually holds — the floor never blocks jigc's *internal* shell-outs, because those are not the agent's Bash tool, and where jigc's own *surface* is the destroying door the floor does reach it, deliberately. The floor's listing gains a **third bullet** rather than an addition to either existing one: these are neither destructive shell nor a secret read, they are `jigc` verbs permitted by the blanket `Bash(jigc:*)` prefix permit like every other verb.

**Bounds, unchanged and restated rather than quietly widened.** This is still *ergonomics, not a sandbox* — a `deny` rule reaches the **agent's Bash tool** and nothing else: the human running either verb in their own terminal is untouched (the point), and an agent that reaches a subprocess some other way is not sealed, exactly as the secret-read twins are a floor and not a seal. It ships in the **claude-code** profile, the only profile that ships; a future profile inherits the design bullet, not the bytes.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 3 / T2: `jigc task discard` refuses over staged prose, and `--force` is the single consent

**Shipped.** The second destroying door takes the shared guard ([settle-record](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D1**). `run_discard` calls T1's probe scoped to its own task between `TaskArea::resolve` (Increment 1's malformed-id refusal, still outermost) and `crate::milestone::settle_discarded_sub_task` (which **commits** the record — a refusal after it would leave a committed record settling a sub-task whose area survives, the lying-record defect M49 closed, re-opened by its own fix), and blocks with **`task-discard.staged-prose`**: its own code, never `uninstall.staged-prose`, on the shipped `uninstall.dirty-worktree` / `milestone.dirty-worktree` per-door precedent. It joins neither `CHECK_INVENTORY` nor `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` — it is a door refusal, not a probe result and not a commit-phase rejection. The refusal travels through `render::finding_error`'s carrier and the dispatch reads it back with `render::blocked_finding`, so the identity the surface prints is the identity the **invocation log** records (the `rename` precedent, M49 Inc 11 / T4) instead of one more anonymous exit 1. `TaskCommand::Discard` gains `#[arg(long)] force`, and `discard_rejection_frame` echoes it into the re-run, like `finalize`'s `--approve` / `--carry-staged`.

**The stated behaviour change, asserted rather than discovered.** `jigc start` stages `commit:<id>.md` **at mint**, so the guard's population is every minted task, pristine skeleton included: **an ordinary `jigc task discard <id>` now needs `--force` from the moment the task exists.** The one cell that stays bare is a `milestone add-task` sub-task before its first re-entry, which stages nothing — and that cell is what proves the guard is keyed on staged bytes rather than on being a task. This corrects D1's *"authored prose no commit holds is a different population"* rationale while leaving D1's decision intact, and it is pinned in the acceptance rather than left to be met in the field. The predicate was **not** narrowed: exempting the skeleton is a redesign of `uninstall`'s shipped, doc-of-record guard, would have to land at both doors or the pair re-diverges, and is outside this increment.

**One correction to the plan's own basis, found by building it.** T1 landed the fail-closed refusal as a single `Finding` keyed `uninstall.staged-prose`, which at *this* door would have told an operator who ran `jigc task discard` to *"re-run `jigc uninstall`"* — the cross-door misdirection the pair exists to close, reintroduced by the sharing that closes it. So the probe takes the **caller's** fail-closed builder (`unverified: &dyn Fn(io::Error) -> Finding`): the install door passes `unverified_prose_finding`, the task door `discard_unverified_prose_finding`. The measurement stays one probe; only the refusal names a door. T1's fail-closed test keeps its assertion and gains the task door's cell.

**The route/instruction axis was swept in the same commit, because two standing fences assert the printed route runs as printed** (`pre_guard_repair_route::the_migration_source_route_does_not_promise_a_review_it_does_not_get`, `write_not_present_route::a_broken_staged_source_names_the_discard_escape_hatch`) — a guard landing without the sweep is a red gate with no in-scope fix. The axis is *every shipped surface naming `jigc task discard` as an argv a reader is expected to run*, and `--force` is inert when nothing is staged (the shipped `uninstall --force` precedent), so the consent is named unconditionally: `start.rs` ×3, `doc.rs`, `setup.rs` (the pair's mutual route), `cli.rs` (the `uninstall` long help + the `discard-write` curated tip), `engine::finalize` ×6, `engine::file_state` ×2, `engine::write`'s shared `discard_span`, `engine::state`'s serial-collision route, and the `author-migration-completion-record` pack step with its **12** compose goldens. **Two axis members the plan's grep did not name** (`engine::state`'s `task.serial-collision` and `engine::write`'s `discard_span`) were found by re-deriving the axis and closed here, as the plan's bound (ix) required. **One repair beyond appending a flag:** `finalize.base-mismatch`'s task arm and `base_overlap_finding` named the bare verb, so appending the consent would have produced `jigc task discard --force` — unrunnable. Both bind their task id already, so the exit is now **substituted** rather than placeheld (M43 P6: a placeholder derivable by the caller is a route-floor breach).

**Blast radius, re-measured rather than trusted:** 23 tests across 8 group targets, not the plan's spiked 19 — 20 from the guard and 3 from the route text the plan's spike did not carry. All repaired here; a driven discard whose intent is *throw the task away* gains the consent, and a route assertion moves to the emitted bytes.

**Acceptance.** New `crates/cli/tests/staged_prose_consent_axis.rs` (registered in `groups/g_milestone.rs`), four arms over **one** workbench: (a) both doors refuse the same staged bytes, each under its own code with exactly one route naming `--force`, the files byte-intact after both; (b) each door's `--force` performs **its own** post-condition (`uninstall` takes `.jigc/`; `discard` takes the one area and still acks the dropped set with its transient marks); (c) the sub-task cell discards at exit 0 with no consent and its record settles; (d) a freshly minted task refuses its own discard, then the printed consent runs as printed. `commit_rejected_axis`'s discard arm is driven **with** the consent so the frame's echo is pinned. Design fold-back: [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → **Abandoning a task** (new), the serial-collision route · [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → the per-sub-task terminal's fourth property · [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → the refusal's route names the consent · [validation.md](design/validation.md) → the two dead-end rejects' escape hatch.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 3 / T1: one staged-prose probe, one home, and it can answer for a single task

**Shipped.** `staged_task_prose` and its fail-closed `unverified_prose_finding` move out of `crate::setup` into **`crate::task`** — the module that already owns a task working area (`staged_doc_ids`, the probe's own subject, lives there) — as `pub(crate)`, gaining a `only: Option<&[String]>` **scope** parameter. `crate::setup::uninstall` passes `None` (it takes the whole workbench) and `narrate_staged_prose` passes its own `only` straight through, so the after-the-fact `retain` is gone and the scoping now happens **before** an area is probed at all: a door that will not remove an area neither names it nor is blocked by its readability. No door's behaviour and no printed byte moves — `uninstall_worktree_guard::`, `milestone_teardown_loss::` and `flow48_acceptance::` are green with their assertions **unchanged**. The law-1 doc-comment travels verbatim: the probe measures **staging**, never authorship, and the machine-minted skeleton is the dominant cell.

**Two new tests in the home's own `#[cfg(test)]` module**, both red first for the right reason (the scope parameter landed unused; the sibling leaked into the scoped answer, and the sealed sibling's `Err` reached the out-of-scope caller). `the_staged_prose_probe_answers_for_one_task_without_naming_its_sibling` drives a two-task workbench — each area carrying the `provenance.json` a directory-emptiness probe would trip over — and asserts the scoped call returns exactly the named task's sorted `<type>:<slug>` ids while the unscoped call still sees both. `an_unreadable_docs_dir_refuses_in_scope_and_is_none_of_the_doors_business_outside_it` pins the **fail-closed** arm, unpinned at HEAD: a present-but-unreadable `docs/` (mode `0o000`) is an `Err` carrying `uninstall.staged-prose`, in scope and unscoped, and is invisible out of scope.

**One fault-path behaviour difference, stated rather than absorbed.** The narration used to enumerate the whole workbench and filter afterwards, so an unreadable area belonging to *any* task suppressed the warning for *every* task. Scoping at the probe means an out-of-scope area's unreadability no longer silences a warning the door owes — strictly more truthful, unobservable on every non-fault path, and the doc-comment's best-effort sentence now says *in-scope* rather than *workbench*.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 3](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the destroying-door consent pair*) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `39cd84d` (tree clean; Increments 1–2 landed). Every basis below was **driven on the release binary built from that HEAD** (`target/release/jigc`, `1.0.0-rc.13`) in throwaway `dev/jigc-rig` corpora, or measured by a **spike that was applied, gated and reverted** — unless it is explicitly marked a source read or a grep. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 50 Increment 3; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D1** (the shared guard, `--force`, `DESTROYING_DOORS` refused) and **D9** (the deny floor takes the two human-owned destroyers, `milestone provision` dropped from the carve-out); [charter.md](completions/artifacts/M50/charter.md) → Tier 0; [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md):150 (the two states `uninstall` refuses, and *the subject there is staging, not authorship*); [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The lifecycle · `jigc task discard <sub-id>`; [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md) → the `deny` safety floor · No self-collision; [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → the three laws · the route floor.

**Why:** the two doors already disagree about the identical bytes, and the disagreement is a data-loss path the shipped surface actively routes into.

**Basis — driven at `39cd84d`.** The Settle's stated *population* for D1 moved under measurement and is corrected here.

- **The contradiction reproduces, both halves, on one state.** In a `refs-post-hoc` rig holding one live task with two staged docs, `jigc uninstall` exits **1** with `blocking · uninstall.staged-prose` naming `commit:ground-the-vision-in-research, vision:vision` and removing nothing — and `jigc task discard ground-the-vision-in-research` exits **0** and removes them. `--force` does not exist on that door: `jigc task discard <id> --force` is clap exit **2**, *"unexpected argument `--force`"*.
- **The guard's real population is every `jigc start`-minted task, not "authored prose".** Driven over four workflows (`quick-fix`, `record-decision`, `plan`, `do-research`, plus `dev-task`) and over `jigc migrate NOTES.md --as adr`: **every** mint immediately stages `docs/commit:<task>.md`, so `staged_task_prose` is true for a task that has done nothing. A **`milestone add-task` sub-task stages nothing** at mint (`docs/` absent), so the empty-staged cell is real and reachable — it is the sub-task cell, not the ordinary one. This is exactly what [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md):150 already states for `uninstall` (*the probe cannot tell prose someone typed from the pristine skeleton `jigc start` mints, the skeleton is in fact the dominant cell, and it refuses over both on the one ground it can prove*), and it **corrects D1's rationale**, which dismissed M46's `--force`-reflex counter-evidence on the ground that *"authored prose no commit holds is a different population"*. The population is the skeleton plus the prose, and the decision is unchanged by that — D1 settles the mechanism (the shared guard, both doors, `--force` the single consent) and the locked doc that owns the predicate defends refusing over both — but the **consequence is bigger than the record anticipated and is stated as an intended behaviour change: an ordinary `jigc task discard <id>` requires `--force` from mint onward.** No genuine new fork: nothing here is undecided, and narrowing the shipped predicate (at *both* doors, or the pair re-diverges) would be a redesign of `uninstall`'s guard, which is neither in this increment's scope nor this plan's to authorize.
- **The blast radius is measured, not estimated — an applied spike, gated, reverted.** With the flag and the guard spiked in at `run_discard`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` yields exactly **19 failures across 7 group targets** (~3 100 tests otherwise green): `e2e_audit` ×4, `format_json_success_axis`, `doc_rename_in_task` ×3, `task_lifecycle`, `task_bind` ×2, `subtask_discard_record` ×2, `planning_gate_forcing`, `singleton_running_doc`, `slug_override_axis`, `pinned_facts::file_state_transactional`, `pre_guard_repair_route`, `write_not_present_route`. All one shape. Spike reverted; tree at `39cd84d`.
- **Two of those failures are standing fences that assert the printed route runs as printed**, which is what makes the route repairs *forced in the same motion* rather than a taste call: `pre_guard_repair_route::the_migration_source_route_does_not_promise_a_review_it_does_not_get` (*"the preserving exit must run as printed"*) and `write_not_present_route::a_broken_staged_source_names_the_discard_escape_hatch` (*"the emitted `jigc task discard` must exit 0"*). A guard landing without them is a red gate with no in-scope fix.
- **`--force` is inert when the guard is clean** — the shipped `jigc uninstall --force` doc-comment says so and the flag behaves that way — so a route may name the consent unconditionally and still run as printed in the sub-task cell where nothing is staged. That is what settles the route wording rather than a per-site conditional.
- **Placement is load-bearing, and the order is: resolve → guard → settle → remove.** Increment 1's `reject_malformed_work_unit_id` runs inside `TaskArea::resolve` (`task.rs:871`) and stays outermost. The guard must sit **before** `crate::milestone::settle_discarded_sub_task` (`task.rs:462`), which **commits** the milestone record: a refusal after it would leave a committed record settling a sub-task whose working area survives — the lying-record defect M49 closed, re-opened by the fix for it.
- **The rejection frame must carry the flag it was invoked with.** `discard_rejection_frame` (`task.rs:500`) builds `jigc task discard <id>` as the copy-runnable re-run; after the guard that argv refuses in exactly the state that printed it unless the run's own `--force` rides along. `commit_rejected_axis` pins that re-run.
- **The pack itself instructs the door.** `packs/methodology/steps/author-migration-completion-record.yaml:14` tells the agent, on the refusal rung, to *"author nothing, run `jigc task discard {{task.id}}`"* — and a `jigc migrate` task stages `commit:<task>.md` at mint (driven), so that instruction refuses. **12 compose goldens** carry the line (`goldens/compose/methodology/{start,workflow-preview}--migrate-completion-record--*.txt`), regenerated with `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 cargo test -p cli compose_goldens::`.
- **The route/instruction axis is 12+ shipped sites across both crates** *(grep, disposed by reading each)*: `start.rs:1866,1997,2086` and `doc.rs:5653` (`Route::mechanical`), `setup.rs:2458` (`uninstall.staged-prose`'s own route — the pair's mutual route), `cli.rs:2081` (`tip_task_discard_write`), `task.rs:500` (the frame), and engine-side `finalize.rs:520,1222,1277,1302,1360,1374,3101` and `file_state.rs:341,365`. Appending `--force` keeps every one parsing at the `Route::mechanical` CLI-seam fence and keeps the engine-side `route.contains("jigc task discard")` assertions true.
- **The code is `task-discard.staged-prose`** *(source read)*: the namespace is free; the per-door precedent is the shipped `uninstall.dirty-worktree` / `milestone.dirty-worktree` sibling pair and `staged_prose_finding`'s own doc-comment (*"**Its own code**, not the worktree door's … would name the wrong subject"*); the `task-discard.` prefix is the one `ERROR_TASK_DISCARD_REJECTED` (`task-discard.commit-rejected`) already uses. It joins **neither** `engine::result::CHECK_INVENTORY` nor `invocation_log::ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` — `uninstall.staged-prose` is in neither, and the guard is a door refusal, not a probe and not a commit-phase rejection.
- **The fail-closed arm of `staged_task_prose` is untested at HEAD** *(grep: no suite asserts `cannot check .jigc/tasks/`)* — so the extraction has a real red to buy rather than a refactor with none.
- **The deny half, verified in code and by grep.** `adapter::inject_deny` (`adapter.rs:713-760`) is append-if-absent over `permissions.deny`, preserving every user entry — so two new patterns reach an installed repo on its next `jigc setup`, with no prune of a user-owned file; `remove_deny` (`:1026`) is its exact inverse and `uninstall` already round-trips the floor (`crates/cli/tests/uninstall.rs:219`, the *deny safety floor* row). The floor's literal lives in exactly **three** code places — `crates/cli/adapters/claude-code.yaml` and two inline `insta` snapshots in `adapter.rs` (`claude_code_profile_bytes_are_canonical` `:1494`, the deny-merge snapshot `:2610`) — plus two in `design/assistant-adapter.md` (`:84`, `:119`); `e2e_audit.rs:303` only checks a **foreign** entry survives, so it is unaffected.
- **The deny cannot collide with jigc's own composed surface** *(grep over `packs/`, `crates/cli/pack/`, the bootstrap `AGENT.md` writer)*: **no** workflow, step, or bootstrap text names `jigc uninstall` or `jigc milestone discard`. The one place a reader is told to run `jigc milestone discard` is `MIGRATING.md:40-41`, addressed to the operator; blocking the *agent's* Bash there is the intent of D9, not a collision.

- **T1 — one staged-prose probe, one home, and it can answer for a single task.** `staged_task_prose` + `unverified_prose_finding`'s fail-closed discipline move out of `crate::setup` into a shared `pub(crate)` home both destroying doors call, gaining a **scope** parameter (*the staged docs of this task id*) that only the after-the-fact narration can express today (`narrate_staged_prose`'s `only:`). `uninstall`, `milestone discard`'s narration and every finding text stay **byte-identical** — this task changes no door's behaviour and no printed byte; it is the *home* the increment's scope names, landed before anything depends on it. The doc-comment carries the law-1 sentence with it verbatim (the probe measures **staging**, never authorship, and the skeleton is the dominant cell). *Done:* two new named tests in the shared home's own `#[cfg(test)]` module — the scoped probe over a two-task workbench returns **exactly** the named task's sorted `<type>:<slug>` ids and nothing of the sibling task's, and a **present-but-unreadable** `docs/` yields `Err` rather than an empty set (the fail-closed arm, unpinned at HEAD, pinned here); `cargo test -p cli uninstall_worktree_guard::`, `cargo test -p cli milestone_teardown_loss::` and `cargo test -p cli flow48_acceptance::` green with their assertions **unchanged**. Full unscoped gate green (`dev/gate`). *(files: `crates/cli/src/setup.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, one new or existing CLI module for the home.)*
- **T2 — `jigc task discard` refuses over staged prose, `--force` is the single consent, and every surface that names the door still runs as printed.** The guard calls T1's home scoped to the task, placed **after** `TaskArea::resolve` and **before** `settle_discarded_sub_task`, minting a blocking **`task-discard.staged-prose`** through the shared `render::finding_error` carrier: the message names the task and its staged identities (the addresses `jigc doc show <addr> --task <id>` takes), and the route leads with the reachable reads and lands on `jigc task discard <id> --force`, the same three-exit shape `uninstall.staged-prose` prints. `TaskCommand::Discard` gains `#[arg(long)] force`, documented as the consent to destroy docs no commit has a copy of and **inert when nothing is staged**; `discard_rejection_frame` carries `--force` into its re-run whenever the run had it. **This is one atomic motion** — the guard reddens 19 tests across 7 group targets (measured), two of which fence *the printed route runs as printed*, so no later task may repair them: the route/instruction axis is swept in the same commit, derived as *every shipped surface naming `jigc task discard` as an argv a reader is expected to run* (the 12+ sites above, disposed one by one — an argv gains the consent; a sentence merely describing the verb's effect states it), the pack step's refusal rung with it, and its **12** compose goldens regenerated. *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli staged_prose_consent_axis::` green, registered in **exactly one** group root (`crates/cli/tests/groups/g_milestone.rs`), driving the real binary over **one** workbench state with four arms — (a) both doors refuse the same bytes, each with **its own** code (`uninstall.staged-prose` / `task-discard.staged-prose`), each carrying exactly one `route:` line naming `--force`, and the staged files **byte-intact** after both refusals; (b) each door's `--force` performs **its own** post-condition (`uninstall` removes `.jigc/`; `discard` removes the area and acks the dropped set, transient marks intact); (c) the **sub-task cell** — a `milestone add-task` sub-task with nothing staged discards at exit 0 **without** `--force` and its record settles, proving the guard is keyed on staged bytes and did not become a blanket refusal; (d) the mint cell — `jigc start --workflow <w> "<intent>"` then an immediate discard refuses, which is the stated behaviour change, asserted rather than discovered. Plus `cargo test -p cli pre_guard_repair_route:: write_not_present_route::` green (the two standing run-as-printed fences), `cargo test -p cli commit_rejected_axis::` green with the frame's re-run carrying `--force`, `cargo test -p cli compose_goldens::` green after the regeneration, and all 19 measured call sites repaired. Design fold-back in the same commit, because a rule stated in one place and violated in another is the disease this wave names: [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Lifecycle · `:180`'s abandon-and-retry route, [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) (the shared guard, D1's home), [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md):150 (its route names the consent), [validation.md](design/validation.md):86 (the two dead-end rejects' escape hatch). Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/src/start.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/src/setup.rs`, `crates/engine/src/finalize.rs`, `crates/engine/src/file_state.rs`, `packs/methodology/steps/author-migration-completion-record.yaml`, 12 files under `crates/cli/tests/goldens/compose/methodology/`, a new `crates/cli/tests/staged_prose_consent_axis.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/groups/g_milestone.rs`, the 19 measured suites, `design/write-commands.md`, `design/team-ready-state.md`, `design/project-setup.md`, `design/validation.md`.)*
- **T3 — the safety floor denies the two human-owned destroyers, and the self-collision paragraph stops claiming a reach it never had.** `Bash(jigc uninstall:*)` and `Bash(jigc milestone discard:*)` join the profile's **deny** list — `deny` blocks rather than prompts, which is the correct semantics for an action whose owner is the human, and injection is additive so it reaches installed repos on their next `setup` without pruning a user-owned file. The `permit` is **untouched** (narrowing it would reach zero existing installs and would have to enumerate all 47 `VERB_KINDS` leaves), and **`milestone provision` is deliberately not denied** — M48's fail-closed classifier already guards it and D11 makes the fan-out this wave's own unattended Fix-phase mechanism. [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md)'s floor gains these two as **their own bullet** (they are not destructive shell or secret reads), and `:89`'s *"No self-collision … The floor constrains the agent, not the CLI"* is corrected on the record: it reasoned only about jigc's own `git` shell-outs and never contemplated jigc performing an **agent-supplied** deletion, which is what an allowlisted `jigc uninstall` is. *Done:* `cargo test -p cli adapter::` green with both inline snapshots updated and a **new** `the_deny_floor_carries_the_two_human_owned_destroyers` asserting both patterns are in the shipped floor and stating why, so a later profile edit cannot drop them silently; `cargo test -p cli uninstall::` green — its shipped *deny safety floor* row now round-trips the two new patterns — and `cargo test -p cli e2e_audit::` green, the foreign `Bash(shutdown:*)` entry still preserved. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/adapters/claude-code.yaml`, `crates/cli/src/adapter.rs`, `design/assistant-adapter.md`.)*

**Why this order.** T1 first because it is the only piece with no behaviour change: the home and its per-task scope land while every printed byte is still provably identical, so if the extraction is wrong it is caught against a suite that has not moved. T2 second because it is the increment's whole risk in one commit — 19 forced repairs, two run-as-printed fences and a pack instruction that becomes false the moment the guard lands — and nothing in T1 or T3 can absorb any of it. T3 last because it is argv-disjoint from both: no test, route or golden the first two touch reads the adapter profile, so a T2 that needs a second round leaves the floor's correction landed rather than stranded.

**Declared bounds carried to the executor.** (i) **The stated behaviour change is that an ordinary `jigc task discard <id>` now needs `--force` from the moment the task is minted** — driven, not inferred, because the mint itself stages `commit:<task>.md`. It is asserted in T2's arm (d) rather than left to be discovered; it corrects D1's *"authored prose is a different population"* rationale while leaving D1's decision intact. (ii) **The predicate is not narrowed.** Exempting the pristine skeleton is a redesign of `uninstall`'s shipped, doc-of-record guard ([project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md):150 defends refusing over it), it would have to land at **both** doors or the pair re-diverges, and it is outside this increment's scope — named here rather than absorbed silently. (iii) **`DESTROYING_DOORS` membership stays refused** (D1): its subject is worktree-shaped paths probed for git linkage, which would refuse every live task; a `DESTROYING_DOORS` row for `task discard` appearing in this increment is scope creep, not thoroughness. (iv) **`jigc milestone discard`'s sub-task teardown keeps narrating rather than refusing** — [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md):96's *visible, not prevented* bound is deliberate and this increment's pair is `task discard` + `uninstall`. (v) **`QUICKSTART.md:170-172` and `MIGRATING.md:40` still say the door is safe, and they are Increment 13's**, priced there because `setup.rs:69-70` `include_str!`s both into the shipped `SKILL.md`, so an edit moves `jigc-body-blake3` and engages M48's refuse-to-clobber path. Named landing: **Increment 13**, not "a later task". (vi) **[bootstrap.md](design/bootstrap.md)'s state-3 `Run: jigc task discard` directive is Increment 5's** (Settle B9): it is an undelivered design today — no shipped renderer prints it — so this increment repairs no orientation directive and Increment 5 inherits the consent obligation. (vii) **`--force` on `discard` narrates nothing new before removing** — the existing ack still names the dropped set afterwards, where `uninstall --force` narrates first; symmetry there was considered and left out of a minimal cut, and is not claimed as delivered. (viii) A new suite file is registered in **exactly one** group root (`autotests = false`; `tests/test_target_registration.rs` fences it both ways). (ix) **The 19-failure number is a spike measurement, reverted** — the executor re-measures with its own gate rather than trusting this entry, and a twentieth failure is a finding to close here, not a note.

**Scope coverage, bullet for bullet** ([roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Increment 3 *Deliverable* + *Grouped scope*): **`uninstall`'s staged-prose guard extracted to a shared home** → **T1** · **and applied at `task discard`, with `--force` as the single consent** → **T2**, with the forced route/pack/test sweep in the same commit because two standing fences assert the printed route runs as printed · **not `DESTROYING_DOORS` membership, whose subject would refuse every live task** → bound (iii), refused on the record · **`Bash(jigc uninstall:*)` and `Bash(jigc milestone discard:*)` join the adapter profile's deny list (deny blocks; the profile has no prompt, and `inject_permit` is additive so a narrowed permit would reach zero existing installs)** → **T3**, with the additive-injection and inverse-removal legs read in `adapter.rs` and the permit left untouched · **`milestone provision` is deliberately not carved out** → **T3**, stated with D9's two grounds · **[assistant-adapter](design/assistant-adapter.md):89's *"No self-collision"* paragraph corrected** → **T3** · **Design: [team-ready-state](design/team-ready-state.md), [project-setup](design/project-setup.md):150** → **T2**'s fold-back. **Proves** (*the two doors cannot contradict each other by construction; the floor's text matches the permit's reach*) → **T2**'s arm (a) — one state, both doors, one shared probe — and **T3**'s floor fence. Nothing is deferred out of the increment, and the two items that genuinely belong elsewhere (the shipped guides, the orientation directive) name their increment rather than "a later task".

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 2 / T3: the unmovable destination stops being a code-less bail that prints the host's filesystem

**Shipped.** `jigc rename` asks the trackability question at **its own** pre-check — gate (g), beside the dirty-tree, in-flight, fixed-identity and collision arms — through a new `RefusalKind::UntrackableDestination` carrying **`write.untrackable-destination`** (namespace verified free) and a `Repair::Judgment`: the destination is the doctype's home plus the new slug, and jigc cannot tell which of the two the operator meant to change, nor whether the *home* (a submodule, an embedded repo, git's own directory) is the thing to move. `RefusalKind::ALL` is **eleven**, and the M49 axis sweep drives the new row through `drive_refusal`'s `prepare` closure rather than asserting it.

**The defect reproduced first, driven at `7f0899d`** (T2's commit, so the reproduction is of the tree this task starts from). With `git init docs/decisions` — the adr doctype's own home turned into an embedded repository, reached with a **well-formed** slug and a **well-formed** address, so the arm survives T1's and T2's guards and is not dead code — `jigc rename adr:single-node-cache --to "Distributed"` answered from *inside* the transaction with `relocate::move_doc`'s bare `anyhow`:

    refusing to move `docs/decisions/single-node-cache.md` to a destination git cannot track:
    `docs/decisions/distributed.md` is inside another repository
    (/private/var/folders/nj/…/jigc-rename-…/docs/decisions) — a submodule or an embedded repo…

No finding code (so the invocation log recorded one more exit-1-with-nothing), no route, and the **host's absolute filesystem** on the surface — neither repo-real nor a typed identity, which is law 1's own clause ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md)).

**The message is composed from repo-relative parts, not sanitized.** Three of `trackable::untrackable_reason`'s five branches build their prose from an absolute path (the canonicalized root, the git dir, the owning toplevel), so interpolating the reason and scrubbing it afterwards would leave the leak one branch-edit away. This door states the fault at its own altitude instead — the destination, repo-relative, and what the move would cost — and the *shapes* to check move into the route, where they are a reading list rather than a claim about which one fired. No host path can reach either channel by construction rather than by wording, and the new arm proves it by searching for **the fixture's own root in both spellings** a macOS temp dir answers to (`/var/folders/…` as handed out, `/private/var/folders/…` once canonicalized), on the text surface **and** inside the `--format json` `{"error": …}` envelope — not for a spelling of the leak, which a reworded leak would slip past.

**`write.untrackable-destination` is a mint, not a reuse, and it is the family's code rather than this door's** — the same disposition T2 took for `write.malformed-slug`. The three other callers of `relocate::move_doc` (`jigc relocate`, `migrate-corpus`'s relocation arm, `finalize`'s promote/retire) refuse the identical fault with the shared bare bail carrying no code, so there was none to reuse; the code is minted here and is the one those doors join when they converge. `config set docs-root|placement-root`'s `config.untrackable-root` is **not** that code and is not reused: its subject is a knob value, not a doc destination.

**The primitive's guard stays, and is not now dead.** `move_doc` still asks — for its other three callers, and for `rename` as the layer under the gate. Declared bound (vii) of the decomposition is discharged as written: the same fault at those callers stays code-less, and this task neither closed nor widened that gap.

**Scoped to a run that actually moves**, exactly like the primitive's own check: `!is_retitle`, so a retitle-only — which rewrites the doc at the path it already occupies — is not asked to relitigate a path the store is already reading from.

**Carried from T2 and discharged here:** `completions/trial-driver/arms/walk/18-surface-batch.sh` claimed *"all 9 of `RefusalKind::ALL`"*. It is now eleven, and the arm states the subset it reaches (nine) with the reason for each member it does not: `write.malformed-slug` is driven whole by `slug_override_axis.rs`'s six-door sweep, and `write.untrackable-destination` needs an embedded repository planted at the doctype's home — a corpus mutation that would poison every cell after it. Counts corrected, no cell added: a walk arm is an echo of the fences, not one.

[write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md): *"ten states"* → **eleven**, the mint list names both family codes with their reasons, the judgment list gains this one's, and step 2 states the unrecordable-destination check with the exit-0 `git mv` mechanism it exists for and the declared bound beside it.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 2 / T2: the sixth `--slug` door refuses, and the door set becomes the clap tree's own

**Shipped.** `jigc rename`'s `--slug` override is validated where `new_slug` is derived — **above** the `doc_path` that builds the destination and above the empty-slug arm — through a new `RefusalKind::MalformedSlug` carrying **`write.malformed-slug`** (namespace re-verified free) and a `Repair::Judgment`: the id is the caller's to name, and a mechanical argv may carry only a declared `engine::finding::ROUTE_PLACEHOLDERS` member, which a slug is not. The message reuses `crate::task::WORK_UNIT_ID_GRAMMAR`'s **one** shipped spelling, so six doors state one grammar rather than six.

**Both defects reproduced first, driven at `b32def1`** (T1's commit, so the reproduction is of the tree this task starts from). `jigc rename adr:keeper --to "New Title" --slug '../../src/pwned'` exited **0** and committed `docs/decisions/keeper.md => src/pwned.md`; `--slug ''` blocked with `write.unslugable-title` — `` `--to "New Title"` slugs to nothing `` — about a title that slugs fine, then routed the caller to *"name the id yourself: `--slug <new-slug>`"*, i.e. to repeat exactly what had just failed.

**The registry is derived, and the derivation is proven by applied mutants rather than asserted.** `SLUG_ARG_IDS = ["slug"]` plus `SLUG_DOORS` — six rows (`start`, `migrate`, `rename`, `doc create`, `doc add-item`, `doc rename`), each carrying a runnable argv with `SLUG_OVERRIDE_SLOT` where the value goes — fenced **⇔** against the real clap tree by `cli_parse::every_slug_door_is_registered` on the shipped `every_doctype_door_is_registered` mold: the ⇔ over every leaf, each row's argv actually parsing against the real CLI and landing on the leaf it names, and every declared `arg` being a `SLUG_ARG_IDS` member. Proven **red twice by applied mutants, both reverted**: removing the `doc rename` row → *"`jigc doc rename` carries a `--slug` argument (true) but its SLUG_DOORS membership is false"*; renaming `Rename`'s clap field to `slug_value` while keeping `--slug` on the wire → *"`jigc rename` carries a `--slug` argument (false) but its SLUG_DOORS membership is true"* — the second is the mutant a fence written over *spellings* rather than argument **ids** would have missed.

**The `start` row's argv is the minting form on purpose.** Bare `jigc start "<intent>" --slug '../../x'` exits **0** with the override inert — the cascade default composes the router, which mints nothing — so a row written that way would pass while proving nothing. The row carries `--workflow single-task`.

**The tree arm needed a driven fixture fact, and its first version was a masking test.** Written without `src/` on disk, `a_traversal_override_commits_nothing_out_of_the_docs_root` **passed at `b32def1`** — the escape was refused for an unrelated reason, because macOS resolves `..` physically. With `src/` present the same call lands the commit, which is the red the arm now pins. Same shape as T1's `docs/research/` fixture fact, one family over.

**`write.malformed-slug` is a mint, not a reuse, and the record says why.** The five sibling doors refuse the identical value with a bare `anyhow` carrying no code, so there was none to reuse — declared bound (vi) keeps *how they render* out of this increment while *that they refuse* is what `crates/cli/tests/slug_override_axis.rs` proves (six doors × three cells: `""`, a traversal, an absolute path that really exists; each blocking non-zero, naming the token as typed, stating the grammar, and leaving the committed doc at its own slug). `RefusalKind`'s doc-comment now reads *"two of the three mints"* and names the third as the **family's** code — the one those doors join when they converge.

**Surface, not only behaviour:** `jigc rename --help`'s `--slug` said only *"Override the derived slug"* while its five siblings state the verbatim-and-validated discipline. A door that refuses without saying so is the half-measure this wave exists to stop, so the sentence lands with the guard. [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md): *"nine states"* → **ten**, the mint list gains `write.malformed-slug` with its reason, the surface line states the override's discipline, and step 1 says the check runs before the destination path is built.

**Observation, carried rather than fixed:** `completions/trial-driver/arms/walk/18-surface-batch.sh` hand-enumerates *"all 9 of `RefusalKind::ALL`"* and drives nine named refusals. T2 makes it ten and T3 makes it eleven; the count is a walk-arm echo, not a fence, so it belongs to the increment's close (or T3, where both members exist) rather than being edited twice.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 2 / T1: the slug head of a caller-typed address is checked before it names a path

**Shipped.** `crate::task::reject_malformed_slug_head` — one predicate (`engine::slug::is_slug`), one blocking finding (**`store.malformed-slug`**) through the shipped `render::finding_error` carrier, one route (`jigc doc list`, the family's discovery verb, carrying `WORK_UNIT_ID_GRAMMAR`'s **one** shipped spelling of the grammar — reused, not respelled). Applied at the **three** user-address parse boundaries the nine `DoctypeArg::Address` doors reach: `doc::parse_verb_addr` (seven `doc` verbs, nine call sites), `task bind`'s own `Address::parse` (whose refusal was route-less and now routes), and `rename::parse_addr` (which hand-splits on `:` and never called `Address::parse` at all). **Not** inside `engine::address::Address::parse`: the planning spike measured that locus reddening `doc_read_surface`'s law-1 fence, because `doc schema --format json` advertises type-level addresses carrying `<slug>`.

**Both defects reproduced first, driven at `23487ab`.** `jigc doc show "research:<absolute path outside the repo>" --format json` served the outside file's prose through the **1.0-pinned** contract at **exit 0**, `slug` echoing the absolute path; `jigc rename 'research:../../src/planted' --to "Captured Doc"` exited **0** and committed `src/planted.md => docs/research/captured-doc.md`. A third the plan did not name, found by driving the door set: `jigc doc add-item 'roadmap:../..#milestones' --title M --task <id>` and `doc remove-item` both exited **0**, minting and mutating a staged identity no door could address afterwards.
