**`crates/cli/tests/address_slug_head_axis.rs`** — the axis is `cli::cli::DOCTYPE_DOORS ▸ DoctypeArg::Address`, the registry `cli_parse::every_doctype_door_is_registered` already fences ⇔ against the real clap tree; nine doors × three cells (`../..`, an absolute path that really exists, a space-carrying non-slug), a door with no cell a **hard panic** rather than a skip, plus the two **tree** arms (the pinned JSON prints no byte of a canary planted outside the repository; the traversal rename lands no commit and leaves `src/planted.md` in place — the fixture creating `docs/research/` first, because macOS resolves `..` physically and without it the call is refused for an unrelated reason) and the disposition arm below.

**The disposition arm needed a production change, and the planning basis was wrong about which half.** Driven: a hand-dropped **unstamped** `docs/decisions/OldDoc.md` already answered `unregistered` + the ingest route, but a **stamped, conformant** `docs/research/OddName.md` answered `research:OddName … managed` at exit 0 — after the guard, a `managed` row for an identity every door refuses, and the sharpest form of the lie, since the refusal's own route names `jigc doc list`. `jigc validate` compounded it, promising the file would be *"baselined on its next author or finalize"* — an author that can no longer happen, which is verbatim the promise `is_unadopted_foreign`'s own doc-comment forbids. The repair went to the **shipped discriminator**, not to `doc list`, because [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) states the rule: *"`doc list` reads that same discriminator; it never grows a second one."* So `is_unadopted_foreign` gains an **identity leg** asked before the byte legs and after the unversioned-doctype precondition — jigc's own writer names every doc it wrote `<slug>.md`, so a file at a managed home whose identity is not a slug was produced by no jigc operation, whatever bytes it carries; a hand-typed stamp is not evidence of jigc's hand, the path is, and the path says no. The advisory gained a **cause**, because stating the byte cause over an identity fault would be a law-1 lie about a file that is stamped and parses clean — one code, one route, two tails. `engine::index::instance_slug` mints the identity-from-path rule **once** (a placement singleton's slug is its type id, never `CHANGELOG`) so `migrate_corpus`' path-keyed caller asks the same question the enumerator answers.

**Two shipped fixtures were falsified by the leg, and driving says the leg is right, not the fixtures.** `flow50_acceptance` and `completion_record_audit_vocabulary` both hand-wrote a `completion-record` at `docs/completions/M99.md` / `M1.md` — a name the mint cannot produce, since `id-from: title` slugifies (`dogfood_record_schema` asserts the real mint lands `completions/m16.md`). Both corrected to the slug, and `worked-examples.md`'s matching JSON example with them.

**`doc_barrier`'s two arms are reconciled in this commit, which is why the guard and the reconciliation are one commit.** The escape address is now refused one layer further out; both arms assert that answer, their **sibling-area byte assertions unchanged**. **The barrier is not retired** — `is_slug` admits no `/` and no `.`, so its integration trigger is unreachable, which is exactly the state in which M45 retracted a guard as dead code on a false belief and left five resolve seams unguarded. It stays as defence in depth over the **resolved destination** (a different question from *is this token a slug*) and keeps its **direct** proof at `doc::tests::barrier_predicate_accepts_in_area_and_rejects_escaping`. [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md)'s *"the malformed address is deliberately not a member"* clause is corrected: it stays off `RefusalKind` because the fault is the address-parse class's and **that class now carries its own class-wide code**, not because minting one would fork it.

**Declared bounds, both recorded with triggers in [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → condition-keyed.** (i) **`jigc ingest` still adopts an unaddressable identity** — its classifier is `conformance_gate`, not the discriminator, so it verdicts `docs/research/OddName.md` *adoptable* and registers it; a different door with a different subject, named in neither the increment's scope nor its file list, and the shipped `adoption_route` already names a repair that works (`jigc migrate <path> --as <ty>`, driven). (ii) **`engine::validate::adoption_route` emits an unquoted path token**, so a committed foreign file whose path carries a space aborts `jigc validate` at the debug `Route::mechanical` argv fence (exit 101) and prints an unpasteable route on release — **driven at `23487ab`, therefore pre-existing and independent of this change**, and the reason the disposition fixture uses space-free names while the axis still drives the space-carrying cell. (iii) `WORK_UNIT_ID_GRAMMAR` **keeps its name and its home**: bound (iii) of the decomposition sets the move trigger at three families and this is the second, so the literal is reused and its doc-comment now names both consumers. (iv) `packs/methodology/schemas/completion-record.yaml`'s header comment still claims `id-from: title` mints `completions/M16.md`; it is a comment, never a printed surface, and it was false before this change — left alone rather than edited into a frozen pack file out of scope.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 2](implementation/roadmap.md) (*families 2 and 4: mint identity and the address slug head*) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `e4b12d8` (tree clean; Increment 1 landed). Every basis below was **driven on the release binary built from that HEAD** (`target/release/jigc`, `1.0.0-rc.13`) in throwaway `dev/jigc-rig` corpora, or measured by a **spike that was applied, gated and reverted** — unless it is explicitly marked a source read or a grep. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 50 Increment 2; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D2** (the predicate, the refusal, the four families' table) · *Ordering constraints* #3; [charter.md](completions/artifacts/M50/charter.md) → the claim's first half; [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename` · Content handoff (`add-item --slug`); [structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md) → Addressing · IDs: provenance and minting; [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → the three laws · the route floor; [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md); [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §4; [dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → *a grep is not a fence*.

**Basis — driven at `e4b12d8`. The Settle's stated seam for family 4 moved under measurement and is corrected here.**

- **Family 4 reproduces through the 1.0-pinned JSON, at exit 0.** In a `committed-singletons` rig, a conformant `research` doc written to a `mktemp -d` **outside the repository** is served by `jigc doc show "research:<abs-path>" --format json` at **exit 0** — `sections.question` returns the planted canary and `slug` is the absolute path. Relative traversal reaches the same place: `doc show 'research:../../../etc/hosts'` resolves `<repo>/docs/research/../../../etc/hosts.md`.
- **Family 4's rename arm commits an arbitrary in-repo file into the docs root.** With `src/planted.md` committed, `jigc rename 'research:../../src/planted' --to "Captured Doc"` exits **0** and lands the commit `src/planted.md => docs/research/captured-doc.md` (H1 rewritten in the same commit). **Fixture fact the acceptance must carry:** the doctype's home directory must exist on disk first — macOS resolves `..` physically, so with no `docs/research/` the `is_file()` probe fails and the same call is refused for an unrelated reason. The first attempt was refused exactly that way; `mkdir -p docs/research` is what makes the defect reachable.
- **Family 2 escapes the docs root, and the three consequences the Settle names are all real.** `jigc rename research:cache-study --to "Pwned" --slug '../../src/pwned'` exits **0**, commits `docs/research/cache-study.md => src/pwned.md` — and afterwards `jigc doc list research` prints *no committed `research` docs*, `jigc doc show 'research:../../src/pwned'` serves the doc, and `jigc validate` exits **0** with no finding about it.
- **The family-2 guard also closes a law-1 lie nobody listed.** Driven: `jigc rename vision:vision --to "New Vision" --slug ''` blocks with `write.unslugable-title` — ``` `--to "New Vision"` slugs to nothing ``` — which is false (that title slugs fine; the emptiness came from `--slug ""`), and whose route tells the caller to *"name the id yourself: `--slug <new-slug>`"*, i.e. to repeat the thing that just failed. `is_slug("")` is false, so the new guard answers first and the lie goes.
- **Six `--slug` doors, five refuse byte-identically, the sixth is `jigc rename` — all six driven.** `start --workflow single-task --slug '../../x'`, `migrate README.md --as adr --slug '../../x'`, `doc create adr … --slug '../../x'` and `doc rename adr:zed … --slug '../../x'` each exit 1 with the shipped literal *"`--slug \"…\"` is not a valid slug — use lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens (no leading, trailing, or doubled `-`)"* (`doc add-item` shares `doc.rs`'s `reject_malformed_slug` with `create`/`rename`); top-level `jigc rename … --slug '../../x'` exits **0**. **And a cell that would false-green:** bare `jigc start "<intent>" --slug '../../x'` exits **0** — the cascade default composes the router, mints nothing, and the override is inert by design — so the axis row for that leaf must use the **minting** form or it proves nothing.
- **Five sites cite a precedent that does not exist at its cited home** *(source read)*: `start.rs:98`, `cli.rs:108`, `doc.rs:180`, `doc.rs:205` and two test module docs (`slug_override.rs:6`, `add_item_slug.rs:9`) all describe the discipline as *"`jigc rename`'s `--slug` precedent"* — while `jigc rename` is the one door that does not implement it. T2 makes the five true by construction; none of them needs an edit.
- **The Settle's *"family 4 at address parse"* is right about the layer and wrong about the function — established by spiking both loci.** A `ParseError::MalformedSlug` variant added inside `engine::address::Address::parse` compiles only after two shipped exhaustive fences (`doc.rs`'s `address_parse_guidance`, `crates/cli/tests/address_parse_error_axis.rs`'s `variant_name`), and then **reddens `doc_read_surface::a_doctype_nested_to_the_cap_advertises_only_addressable_addresses`** — the law-1 fence asserting that *every address `jigc doc schema --format json` advertises parses*. Those addresses are **type-level**: the instance parts are placeheld (`doc.rs:4411`, `changelog:<slug>#…`), and `<slug>` is not a slug. The engine grammar must stay placeholder-tolerant; the guard belongs at the CLI verb boundary — which `parse_verb_addr`'s own doc-comment already names, *"the one place a human/agent types an address … `Address::parse` is **untouched**"*.
- **The blast radius at the corrected locus was measured, not estimated.** With the check at the verb boundary, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` over **all 14 test binaries** yields exactly **2 failures** (~2 300 tests otherwise green), both in `crates/cli/tests/doc_barrier.rs`; `doc_read_surface` and `unknown_doctype_axis` are green. The spike was reverted; the tree is at `e4b12d8`.
- **Those two failures are *forced*, which is why family 4 is one task.** `doc_barrier` is M8's write-time `--task`-scoped barrier; both its arms drive the escape address `commit:../../../<subB>/docs/commit:pwned#summary` and assert the refusal text contains `"outside"` and the sub-task id. The new guard answers first, so the assertion fails with no in-scope fix outside the same commit. **And the structural consequence must not be missed:** `is_slug` admits no `/` and no `.`, so after the guard **no `is_slug`-valid slug can escape a task's `docs/` area** — the barrier's only integration-level trigger becomes unreachable. It is defence in depth over the *resolved destination*, a different question, and it stays.
- **The nine `DoctypeArg::Address` doors reach three different parsers** *(source read, corroborated by the spike)*: `doc.rs::parse_verb_addr` (nine call sites over seven `doc` verbs), `task.rs:1925` (`task bind`, its own `Address::parse` with a **route-less** message), and `rename.rs:852` (`parse_addr`, which hand-splits on `:` and never calls `Address::parse` at all). A guard at any one of them covers a third of the class — which is why the door set, not the function, is the acceptance.
- **The rule already ships on the other half of the same grammar** *(source read)*: `engine::write::check_ref_shape` (`write.rs:6208`) applies `is_slug` to the `<slug>` body of every `<type>:<slug>` **ref value** written into a doc. Family 4 is that identical question, never asked at the door.
- **The unmovable-path arm is reachable with a *valid* slug, and it leaks the host filesystem — both driven.** `move_doc`'s `untrackable_reason` refusal, reached through `jigc rename`, is a bare `anyhow` with **no code and no route**, and two of its branches print an absolute host path: ``` `docs/research/../../../escaped.md` resolves outside the repository at /private/var/folders/…/repo ``` and ``` `docs/research/renamed-study.md` is inside another repository (/private/var/folders/…/repo/docs/research) ```. The second is reached by `git init docs/research` followed by an ordinary `jigc rename research:cache-study --to "Renamed Study"` — a **well-formed** slug — so the arm survives T1 and T2 and `flow37_rename::drive_refusal`'s `prepare` closure can build the scene.
- **The population the guard newly refuses, both halves driven, so T1 disposes it rather than discovering it.** A hand-authored **stamped** conformant `docs/research/Odd Name.md` lists as `research:Odd Name  …  managed`, is served by `doc show --format json` at exit 0, and `jigc validate` says nothing about it. An **unstamped** `docs/decisions/Some Old Doc.md` lists as `unregistered`, and `validate` raises `schema-conformance.unadopted-instance` with an `ingest`/`migrate` route and exits non-zero. After the guard the second is routed and the first is not — a surface calling `managed` an identity every door refuses.
- **`malformed-slug` is a free code namespace** *(source read)*: zero hits in `crates/`, no `engine::result::CHECK_INVENTORY` member, no `cli::invocation_log::ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` member.
- **`SLUG_ARG_IDS` is one member, `"slug"`** *(source read over the clap tree)*: six leaves carry it — `start`, `migrate`, `rename`, `doc create`, `doc add-item`, `doc rename` — and no leaf carries a mint slug under any other name (`old_slug` is a doctype **address**, already a `DOCTYPE_ARG_IDS` member).
- **Family 2's blast radius is grep-measured, not driven** *(stated honestly)*: no test anywhere drives `jigc rename --slug` with a malformed value, and every `--slug` literal in the suite is a well-formed slug. The executor's own gate is the measurement; this entry is not.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** The one place the record left room — *"family 4 at address parse"* — was settled by **spiking both loci and running the suite**, not by choosing.

- **T1 — the slug head of a caller-typed address is checked before it names a path (family 4).** One shared CLI helper beside Increment 1's `reject_malformed_work_unit_id`, minting a blocking `Finding` through the shipped `render::finding_error` carrier: predicate `engine::slug::is_slug`, one code for the family (**`store.malformed-slug`** — the namespace is free, and `store.*` is the namespace the read and write doors already share for identity faults), the message naming the token the caller typed, and **exactly one** route that **states the grammar** — byte-identical to the one shipped sentence Increment 1 fenced — and names the family's discovery verb (`jigc doc list`), never `jigc describe`, which lists doctypes and answers nothing about a slug. Applied at the **three** user-address parse boundaries — `doc.rs::parse_verb_addr`, `task bind`'s own parse (whose refusal is route-less today and gains the route with it), and `rename.rs::parse_addr` — and **not** inside `engine::address::Address::parse`, whose placeholder tolerance `doc schema`'s type-level projection depends on. **This is one atomic motion:** the guard reddens `doc_barrier`'s two arms (measured), and no later task may repair them, so the guard, the reconciliation and the barrier's retained proof are one commit. *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli address_slug_head_axis::` green, registered in **exactly one** group root, iterating `cli::cli::DOCTYPE_DOORS` filtered to `DoctypeArg::Address` — the shipped bijectively-fenced registry (`cli.rs:1549`, `:2239`) — **all 9 doors × 3 cells** (a `../..` traversal, an absolute path, and a space-carrying non-slug), each exiting non-zero with `store.malformed-slug`, naming the token, carrying exactly one `route:` line, and a row with no cell a hard panic rather than a skip; plus **two tree arms, because the text alone passed at HEAD's exit 0** — `doc show 'research:<abs>' --format json` prints no byte of a canary planted outside the repository, and `jigc rename 'research:../../src/planted' --to <t>` lands **no commit** and leaves `src/planted.md` where it was (the fixture creating the doctype home first, per the basis); and **one disposition arm** proving no surface still reports `managed` for an identity every door now refuses — the stamped and unstamped non-slug populations both answering with a state whose route runs, using the shipped `unregistered` value and `ingest` route rather than minting a new state or code, and recording the result if driving shows the shipped discriminator already answers. `cargo test -p cli doc_barrier::` green with both arms reconciled to the new outermost answer, their sibling-area **byte** assertions unchanged, and the containment predicate keeping a direct proof — it is not deleted. `cargo test -p cli doc_read_surface::`, `address_parse_error_axis::` and `unknown_doctype_axis::` green **unchanged**. [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename`'s *"the malformed address is deliberately not a member"* clause corrected: it stays off `RefusalKind` because the fault is the address-parse class's, and that class now carries **its own class-wide code** — not because minting one would fork it. Full unscoped gate green (`dev/gate`). *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/rename.rs`, a new `crates/cli/tests/address_slug_head_axis.rs`, one group root, `crates/cli/tests/doc_barrier.rs`, `design/write-commands.md`.)*

The registry lands **with** its guard, never after its acceptance (Settle, *Ordering constraints* #3). *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli slug_override_axis::` green with **6** derived doors × 3 cells (`""`, a traversal, an absolute path), each refusing non-zero and naming the grammar, the ⇔ fence proven **red by an applied mutant** (a row removed, and a leaf's `slug` argument renamed); `cargo test -p cli flow37_rename::` green, including `every_rename_refusal_carries_an_identity_and_an_exit` sweeping the widened `RefusalKind::ALL` and one arm asserting `jigc rename … --slug ''` no longer claims the **title** slugs to nothing; `cargo test -p cli cli_parse::` green including the new bijection fence. [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md):128's *"nine states"* becomes ten. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/rename.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/flow37_rename.rs`, `design/write-commands.md`.)*

**Why this order.** T1 first because it is the widest class (9 doors, three parsers), it is the one that leaks bytes through the **1.0-pinned** `doc show --format json`, and it is the **only** task carrying a forced cross-suite repair — `doc_barrier`'s two arms — so if the barrier reconciliation turns out to need a rethink it surfaces on the first commit, where it is cheapest, rather than the third. (iv) **The `doc_barrier` containment predicate is not retired.** After T1 no `is_slug`-valid slug can escape a task's `docs/`, so its integration trigger goes unreachable — that is exactly the state in which M45 retracted a guard as dead code on a false belief and left five resolve seams unguarded (`DECISIONS.md` → 2026-09-04). It stays, with a direct proof. (v) **Families 1 and 3 are out of this increment** — a `--task`/`milestone_id` cell here is Increment 1's, already landed and fenced by `work_unit_id_axis.rs`; the two root knobs are Increment 4's. A cell for either appearing in this increment's axes is scope creep, not thoroughness. (vi) **The other five `--slug` doors keep their bare-`anyhow` refusal**, which is route-less and code-less — the M49 PT-A shape not yet applied to them. ## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 1 / T3: the resolve half joins the minting discipline, and the grammar sentence gets one source

**Shipped:** the rule T1 and T2 built now stands in the docs that own it. [structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md) → Work-units and runtime identity gains **resolution** as minting's other half — an id arriving from outside is checked against the same grammar *before it is anything else*, because `.jigc/tasks/<id>/` is built by joining that token onto a path, so it becomes a path component before any door has asked whether it is an id. [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → 1. Preflight and [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Task-id collision & resume both specified *exists* where the rule is **a valid id that exists**, and now give the two-answer form. `write-commands.md` → Enforcement at every `jigc task bind` is the sharper of the three: its convergence rule was written for a **wrong** id, not an **invalid** one, and it now says so — converging there would route a caller to a roster the token could never appear in.

**The grammar sentence is fenced where it is stated, not merely written down.** `malformed_work_unit_id::the_design_doc_states_the_shipped_grammar_verbatim` reads `design/structural-grammar.md` off the workspace root and asserts it carries the shipped literal *verbatim*, plus the code. The chain is what makes it a fence: the suite's `GRAMMAR`/`CODE` consts are spelled out rather than imported (a test comparing emitted bytes against the constant that produced them proves only that the constant equals itself), and every other arm in that file asserts the **emitted** refusal carries them — so `doc == test literal == what the binary prints`, and a reword of `crate::task::WORK_UNIT_ID_GRAMMAR` cannot ship without reddening the doc arm. That is M45's *statement == constant* discipline applied at the one place the rule is stated in prose no compiler reads.

**What is deliberately not pinned, and why.** The two-answer form at the other three loci is verified by reading, not by a byte-assert: those sentences state *which of two answers a door gives*, not a literal the binary emits, so an equality test over them would pin editorial wording rather than a contract — and the answers themselves are already fenced by `work_unit_id_axis.rs`'s 25 doors × 4 cells. The stated verification command:

    grep -n "work-unit.malformed-id" design/finalize.md design/write-commands.md
    grep -n "must exist; otherwise reject with\|for a nonexistent id\|Resolve task .<id>.\." design/finalize.md design/write-commands.md

The first prints the three loci (`finalize.md:29`, `write-commands.md:182`, `:305`), each carrying the malformed → grammar / well-formed-but-unknown → roster split. The second exits **1** with no output: the bare *exists* wording is gone from all three.

**The four resolve seams' doc-comments moved with the rule.** `TaskArea::resolve`, `ActiveTask::resolve`, `resume_in_repo` and `reenter_in_repo` each stated the old one-answer rule (*"a task that does not exist rejects with the task-list route"*) directly above a body that now answers twice. A doc-comment that survives the change it describes is the same drift the design docs had, one layer down.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 1 / T2: the door set is the clap tree's, and the mint side becomes a fence

**Shipped:** `WORK_UNIT_ID_ARG_IDS` + `WORK_UNIT_ID_DOORS` (`crates/cli/src/cli.rs`), the shipped `DOCTYPE_ARG_IDS`/`DOCTYPE_DOORS` mold applied to the second identity a caller hands jigc, and `crates/cli/tests/work_unit_id_axis.rs` — **25 doors × 4 cells** through the real binary. T1 guarded five **resolve seams**; a seam is not a door, and the seams were counted by reading the source. The ⇔ fence (`cli_parse::every_work_unit_id_door_is_registered`) makes the set the binary's: a leaf verb carries a row **iff** one of its clap arguments is `id`, `task` or `milestone_id`. Proven red by two applied mutants — a row deleted, and `task discard`'s `id` argument renamed to `task_id` — each naming the offending leaf.

**The fence checks the row, not only the membership.** Each row's `argv` is parsed against the real CLI and must land on the leaf the row names *and* deliver the id through the argument the row declares, so `arg` is measured rather than believed and a row cannot describe a door it does not reach. The registry carries the runnable argv (with `WORK_UNIT_ID_SLOT` where the id goes), which is what lets one row serve all four cells instead of four hand-written argvs per door.

**The derivation found no 26th door and no uncovered cell.** All 25 doors × the three malformed tokens (`""`, `../..`, and the fixture's own **absolute repository path** — the exact value whose resolution was the data loss) already answer `work-unit.malformed-id` at HEAD, so T1's five seams are complete over the door set. That is the point of deriving the set rather than accepting it: the claim is now checked where membership is decided.

**The fourth cell is the guard's over-fire fence, and its route rule is derived too.** A well-formed but unknown id must keep its unchanged roster answer — every task door `` no task `<id>` ``, every milestone door ``milestone `<id>` does not exist`` — and must **not** carry the grammar refusal, which for a mere typo would be a law-1 misdirection. The route is asserted against two shipped registries rather than a remembered list of strings: its leaf verb must be a `VERB_KINDS ▸ Read` verb or a leaf named by an operator-typed `engine::state::MINT_DOORS` door. Stated honestly, because the axis measured it: the *message* converges per family, the *route* does not converge across all 25 — `jigc workflow` points a missing task at `jigc milestone list-tasks`, and `jigc milestone discard` at the same verb with its M47 state-truth clause. Both are unchanged by M50 and both satisfy the rule; converging their prose is not this task's subject.

**The mint side is a fence, not the sentence the planning basis recorded.** The basis' *"no shipped mint can produce an id the new guard would refuse"* was a source read, and it is the one claim whose falsity would **strand a live work unit** — an id jigc minted that every door then refuses. `every_mint_door_produces_an_id_every_door_accepts` drives all five `MINT_DOORS` members with deliberately hostile input (`  ÄÖÜ Straße —— re-DO the *WHOLE* thing!!  `, and for `jigc migrate` a hostile source **path**, since that door alone passes its id to the mint through the `slug_override` bypass), then checks every area name on disk twice: against `engine::slug::is_slug`, and by feeding the id back through a real door. A member with no cell is a hard panic. Proven red by mutating `migration_task_id` to emit `Migrate-…--…`.

## 2026-09-05 — M50 Inc 1 / T1: the milestone guard is one door-top, not nine, and the log identity is declared owed

**Shipped:** `work-unit.malformed-id` — one blocking finding, `engine::slug::is_slug` as the predicate, a `Route::human` stating the grammar byte-identical to the sentence the three `--slug` doors already ship — at the four task-family resolve seams (`TaskArea::resolve`, `ActiveTask::resolve`'s explicit-`--task` branch, `resume_in_repo`, `reenter_in_repo`) and at the milestone side. `jigc task discard "../.."` no longer empties the repository at exit 0; the two exit-0 false greens (`task validate ""`, `doc list --task ""`) close; the phantom `.jigc/tasks/docs/` mint closes. Acceptance: `crates/cli/tests/malformed_work_unit_id.rs`, eight arms through the real binary over `support::trial_corpus`, each asserting the **tree** and not only the text.

**Elaboration pin — the milestone guard lands once, at `MilestoneCommand::dispatch`'s top, not at nine door-tops.** The plan's *"the top of each of the nine milestone doors"* is satisfied strictly better by the single point every one of those doors already passes through, above `dispatch_join`/`dispatch_finalize`/`dispatch_execute` and above the shared `reseed_cache`. Its subject is `MilestoneCommand::milestone_id()`, matched **exhaustively**, so a verb added with an id it forgets to declare does not compile — the guard's subject cannot silently shrink, which nine copied call-tops could. The declared bound (iv) is honored: the ask sits above `reseed_cache`, and that position is **driven, not asserted** — with a committed `milestone-record` filed under the malformed slug `probe-`, `jigc milestone execute "probe-"` at `HEAD~` rebuilt both `.jigc/milestones/probe-/` and the sub-task working area from that record and composed at exit 0; the guard refuses before either appears, which is the suite's position arm.

**N24 disposed by driving, and no third source found.** `post_commit`'s `remove_dir_all(cleanup_dir)` has exactly the two production sources the plan derived (`TaskArea.dir`, `milestone_dir(…)`), both now downstream of the guard; a real `jigc task finalize` and a real fan-out milestone boundary both land green and both remove their areas (arms f).

**Declared bound, narrowed deliberately: the guard's identity is on the printed surface, not yet in the invocation log.** T1's plan text says the code *"rides the existing funnel and the invocation log records the identity it printed."* The first half ships; the second does not. Only one funnel in the codebase reads `render::blocked_finding` back (`cli.rs:790`, `jigc rename`); the eight funnels this guard reaches all return `Outcome::failure()`, and they are **shared** with every other `finding_error` producer (`task.rs:1881`, `migrate.rs:178`, `relocate.rs:123`, `rename.rs:877`). Teaching them would move the log for findings outside this task's subject, untested by this task's acceptance — the incomplete-fix shape M45 chartered a whole wave against. So the real class — *every operational funnel records the identity of a `BlockedFinding` it prints* — is named here as a pre-existing gap this guard joins rather than creates, and is a sweep of its own, not a rider on this one.

Cut [Increment 1](implementation/roadmap.md) (*family 1: the resolve seams*) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `5dc6c35` (tree clean; no increment landed yet). Every basis below was **driven on the release binary built from that HEAD** (`target/release/jigc`, `1.0.0-rc.13`) in throwaway `dev/jigc-rig` corpora, unless it is explicitly marked a source read. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 50 Increment 1; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M50/settle-record.md) → **D2** (the predicate, the refusal, the stated behaviour change) · *Ordering constraints* #3 · **D13**; [charter.md](completions/artifacts/M50/charter.md) → the claim's first half and its falsifier; [structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md) → Work-units and runtime identity; [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → 1. Preflight; [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Task-id collision & resume · Enforcement at every `jigc task bind`; [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → the three laws · the route floor · the error-code namespace; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §4 (the fixture substrate); [dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → *a grep is not a fence*.

**Basis — driven at `5dc6c35`, not carried from the charter, the roadmap or the Settle. Two of the record's stated facts moved under measurement and are corrected here.**

- **The headline reproduces, and the ack lies while it destroys.** In a `fresh` rig holding one live task, `jigc task discard "../.."` prints `discarded task ../..` and exits **0**, and the repository is afterwards **empty** — `.git`, `.jigc`, the tracked files, all gone. `Path::join` resolves the traversal and `is_dir()` answers about the *resolved* path, so `TaskArea::resolve` hands `remove_dir_all` the repo root. The same call in a rig where **no task has ever been minted** is refused (`.jigc/tasks/` does not exist, so `stat` on `tasks/../..` fails), which is why the destroyer needs a corpus with a task in it — a fixture fact the acceptance must carry, not a coincidence to trip over.
- **The `""` axis is the same seam and it also false-greens.** `Path::join("")` yields the *parent*, and `.jigc/tasks/` is a directory, so every family-1 guard passes for the empty id. Driven on one `committed-singletons` rig: `jigc task discard ""` → `discarded task ` at **exit 0**, `.jigc/tasks/` and the live task inside it removed; `jigc task validate ""` → *"no findings — the task validates clean"* at **exit 0**; `jigc doc list --task ""` → *"jigc doc list — no docs staged in task "* at **exit 0**. Two of the 25 doors currently answer a malformed id with a **success**.
- **N3 is worse than the ledger records it, and it is a family-1 member.** Driven: `jigc doc set-slot 'vision:vision#thesis' --from-file f --task ""` exits 1 — and **creates `.jigc/tasks/docs/`**, after which the pinned `jigc task list` reports **2 active task(s)**, the second being a phantom named `docs`. Its own refusal text routes to `` `jigc task discard ` `` — an empty id, i.e. the route names the destroyer of the previous bullet. One unvalidated token produces a poisoned roster, a broken route, and a pointer at a data-loss door.
- **The seam count is five, and the milestone half is not one of them by the same mechanism.** *(Source read, corroborated by driving.)* `TaskArea::resolve` (`task.rs:759`), `ActiveTask::resolve` (`doc.rs:5379`), `resume_in_repo` (`start.rs:1906`) and `reenter_in_repo` (`start.rs:2024`) each build `tasks/<id>` and gate on `is_dir()`. The milestone side has **no single seam**: `milestone_dir` is a two-line join in the engine with ten CLI call sites, only **four** of which carry a `if !dir.is_dir()` refusal (`milestone.rs:2027, 2862, 3195, 3422`), and **every one of the nine milestone doors calls `reseed_cache` — which itself calls `milestone_dir` (`:1909`) and can rebuild sub-task areas — *before* that check**. So a guard installed only at the four copied `is_dir()` checks would sit **below** a filesystem-touching call, which is exactly what D2 forbids. Driven confirmation that the four checks do not hold the line: with `.jigc/milestones/` present, `milestone list-tasks ""` and `execute ""` answer *"could not read the task list for milestone ``"*, `provision ""` / `finalize ""` answer *"could not read the shared base pin"*, and `milestone add-task "" "do a thing"` mints a **routed** `milestone.area-io` block whose route says *"resolve the underlying I/O condition (a disk or permissions problem)"* — a law-1 misdirection about a malformed argument. `milestone discard "../.."` is stopped only by the **incidental** absence of a sibling `tasks.json`, not by a guard.

One `ActiveTask` variant ships, collapsing states 3 and 4 so no second bump is owed, sharing **one** global `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2→3 with `describe`'s `origin_pack` key.

**The razor refused two product-shaped items with citations — the teeth it was missing.** The charter's exclusion list was four entries and all four were build/trial infrastructure. ## 2026-09-04 — four harness defects fixed, and the sweep for their siblings chartered as its own wave

An external study read the build harness as a system and reported four defects. **Three CONFIRMED, one PARTIAL** — its mechanism and cause exact, its diff wrong: `.claude/commands/milestone-plan.md` names **11** of the fourteen planning gates and **3** are missing (`deliverable-reachable`, `claim-driven`, `quote-attributed`), not the four reported; `census` has been present since the same week it was minted. A **third staleness the report missed**: the step said the table is the bar *"until the doctype is pack-encoded"* and that `planning-record` *"will enforce"* — it shipped at M49.

**The enumeration was deleted, not corrected.** [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md):54 says the gate set is *"stated here and nowhere else"*, and `1d38c8c`'s remedy for the same failure in `milestone-planning-workflow.md` was to **delete** the stale copy. Same remedy here — which also dissolves the fence's tension: at 11 gates in one paragraph, naively adding `.claude/` to `GOVERNED_TREES` would have reddened **on that very file** (the floor is 8). Deleting first made the scan addition safe with no exemption machinery, and `crates/cli/tests/planning_gate_home.rs` is now the **first fence whose subject is this repo's own `.claude/` harness** — every prior `.claude/` reference in the suites is either the adapter's installed artifacts inside a *throwaway* repo (`settings.json`, `skills/jigc/SKILL.md`) or a prose mention in a comment.

**The gate-evidence predicate was worse than reported, and its sibling had already been fixed elsewhere.** `/test result:/` is not merely scope-blind — it is **undelimited**, so it also matches test *names* (`test result::tests::…`, 16 of 17 matches on `cargo test -p engine --lib`, because `crates/engine/src/result.rs` has a `mod tests`). The identical bug was fixed in `dev/gate`'s counting awk at `4171e10` — **one commit before HEAD** — and never swept into the JS. The predicate now keys on `dev/gate`'s own verdict (`GATE: PASS` **and** the full-mode totals line), which rules out a red gate, a bare `--quick` run, and the **accidental** scoped paste — `dev/gate` accepts no scope arguments and emits the totals line only on a full run. **It is not proof of provenance, and this record does not claim it is:** the predicate tests pasted *text*, and both lines are assemblable from two sanctioned fast invocations (`dev/gate --report <log>` runs no cargo and prints the totals line over any log — driven over a `cargo test -p engine` log; `--quick` reaches `GATE: PASS` without running tests). The code comment carries that bound with its measurement; **an earlier draft of this entry asserted unforgeability and was corrected by the cross-model review** — the wave's own law-1 failure, in the entry chartering the wave about it. No binary count is hard-coded: that would mint a new drift point against `crates/cli/tests/groups/`, and the count already lives in `dev/gate` where it is derived. Two new `dev_gate_report` arms pin the two literals the harness consumes — the second a **source scan**, because the totals line has two producers and fencing only the rendered one leaves the consumed copy free to drift (proven with a mutant that reddens the source arm and not the rendered one).

**Three review rounds, and each found the previous had swept to the reported instance rather than the class** — this repo's own complete-fix contract, turned on this work. The transient-halt axis in `milestone-build.js` has **four halt constructions and five printed arms**; the first fix covered three and two. Two of the three *gating* role files still prescribed the retired `test result:` instrument, twice over. And the old predicate would have **rejected a correct `dev/gate` paste** — the harness and CLAUDE.md's own tooling guidance were mutually incompatible. Two pre-existing siblings of the reported classes were fixed with them, both in the same file: the RESUMING block told operators to **REVERT uncommitted work** (contradicted 72 lines below and by [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md):98 — obeyed literally it destroys the gate-green-uncommitted third state M48 lost 511 insertions to), and `/returned no result/` matched **LLM-authored prose**, so *"the census grep returned no result"* reported a real design blocker as *"nothing needs fixing"* at exit 0; that one is now a harness-set flag, unreachable from the LLM-filled schema.

**The sibling sweep is chartered as its own wave, deliberately not as M50 scope** ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → *The harness-surface wave*). The claim: **every fence this repo built stops at the repo's own tooling** — the three laws and the axis-iterating substrate bind the product, and the harness every delegated agent acts on is held to neither. It carries M46's three-leg razor so it can refuse. **The boundary is stated rather than assumed**: M50's criterion is about the product at v1, which almost nothing in the sweep meets, so exactly one item is routed to M50 — `jigc task validate ""` **panics at exit 101** on `1.0.0-rc.13`, the un-swept sibling of M49's own *"one of them panicked at exit 101"*. That class was **sized, not assumed**: of seven id-taking doors driven with `""`, one panics and `task discard ""` acks at exit 0.

## 2026-09-04 — the milestone boundary gates the commit docs it commits, and the axis is the leaf set

[validation.md](design/validation.md) stated the door list is complete — *"for every finding the trailer counts, that door gates as hard as the two task doors"* — and it was **false at HEAD**, found by an independent robust-advocate. The gate's doc set was written as *the merged docs with a committed home*, which is the **promote plan's** subject, not the **boundary's**: a fan-out's transient `commit:<sub-id>` doc declares no home, and under `squash: false` it is rendered into that sub-task's commit message. Driven both ways on `1.0.0-rc.13`: `jigc task validate <sub-id>` blocked at exit 3 on an unfilled leaf and `jigc milestone finalize` landed the same omission at exit 0, subject `: no type set here`.

**The reported cell was `type`; the class is the doctype's author-required leaf set, and it has two members.** `summary` lands an empty-subject `feat:` commit through the identical hole — a *worse* failure, since a subject-less commit is not recoverable by reading it. Both are now driven at the milestone door, and the test **derives** the set from `jigc doc schema commit --format json` and asserts equality with the arms it iterates, so a third author-required leaf reddens the suite rather than silently shrinking the axis. Three membership questions were asked and answered against the binary rather than assumed: the transient doctype set is **`commit` alone** (the only schema in either shipped pack declaring neither `location:` nor `placement:`); `ref-resolves` was **already covered** — the engine `join`'s per-sub-area cross-area ref walk sees a transient doc's outgoing refs, so a dangling `implements` blocked at both doors before this change, which is why the un-gated class is the presence/value families and not the whole conformance family; and `jigc task validate <sub-id>` in the sub-task's own worktree **already blocked**, so the hole is the boundary's alone, not the sub-task's.

**The claim is made true rather than softened, and the one carve-out is stated with its reason.** The gate's subject is now *everything this boundary commits* — the persisted merged docs **plus** the transient docs it will render into a commit message. The predicate is untouched: the same `engine::validate::validate_task` entry over the same families, handed a larger set (the M45 gate is extended, never relaxed). The **`squash: true`** mode is genuinely different and is carved out on the record: the aggregate message is CLI-synthesized and **no** commit doc is read at all, so gating one would refuse a milestone whose committed output is entirely correct — pinned as its own test, alongside the negative half (a `squash: false` sub-task that stages no code contributes no commit, so its commit doc is never rendered and never gates). That makes the knob an **input** to the gate rather than something it is independent of, which is the honest statement: which docs the boundary commits is exactly what the knob decides. The transient subject is keyed on the *very set the render uses* — `code_carrying_worktrees`, now one producer for both callers — because a gate keyed on a parallel derivation would either skip a doc that lands or block one that does not, which is this defect's own shape one layer out.

## 2026-09-03 — the `dev/` tools' first triage: a generator the static fence could not see, and a count that lied

Eight findings against the two tools shipped the same day, all reproduced before they were fixed. Two were blocking, and both are the same shape — **a tool whose claim about itself was checked in the wrong place**.

- **`dev/jigc-rig` emitted and ran arbitrary shell, and the fence was blind by construction.** `--schema` / `--workflow` passed the caller's name through raw into a double-quoted path while every sibling interpolation used `sq()`, so `--schema 'adr"; rm -rf $PACK; echo "'` emitted exactly that command, `--schema 'adr$(touch …)'` **ran** and still exited 0, and `--schema ../../../x` wrote outside the rig root with no metacharacter at all. The fix is both halves — `sq()` at the two sites **and** a slug rule (`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*`) refused at parse time, because quoting alone leaves the `..` face standing. The lesson is the fence's, not the tool's: `dev_rig_parity.rs` scans *files under `dev/`*, and the rig **writes** its commands rather than containing them, so the scan read the generator and never the generated — its allow-list even blesses `printf 'rm -rf %s\n' "$D"`, a generator of the shape. A **runtime** arm now drives `--print-only` with twelve adversarial names and asserts over the emitted bytes; it reproduces the defect exactly (`EMITS a recursive removal of a variable path at line 84`). The static allowance stands *because* that arm exists — a printed `rm -rf` is a defect once the print is executed, and the print is now scanned.
- **`dev/gate` counted test *names* as test *binaries*.** `/^test result:/` undelimited also matches `test result::tests::alpha ... ok`, so `engine/src/result.rs`'s `mod tests` inflated a 17-binary run to **33** — and the wrong figure had already reached a commit message. Matched on the first two *fields* instead; the tool is corrected and the history is not rewritten. The count exists to prove the run measured something, so an inflated one is the lie it was added to prevent. The report layer (totals · failing names · error lines) is now three functions behind **`dev/gate --report <log>`**, which runs no cargo — so `crates/cli/tests/dev_gate_report.rs` fences it over fixture logs in milliseconds, not behind a five-minute gate run. That flag exists for the fence and is not a second implementation: the live run calls the same three functions.

**The same-set claim is narrowed on the record rather than softened.** The rig gains a **`bare`** state — a git repo with one commit and no `jigc setup`, the only state from which `setup` itself, the adapter install, `ingest`, `migrate-corpus` over a never-adopted corpus or the leftover classifier can be probed, and the most common reason agents hand-built a repo anyway. It is deliberately **not** a `State::ALL` member: `TrialCorpus::build_over` runs `setup` for every state before it dispatches, and `compose_goldens` sweeps each composed surface × every state — a corpus with no `.jigc/` has no composed surface to golden, so joining would mean ~100 goldens of a corpus that cannot compose, or a per-consumer exemption at each sweep. So `dev_rig_parity.rs` carries `RIG_ONLY_STATES` — the name **with its reason**, asserted non-placeholder — and a second divergence in either direction, or a stale exemption, still reddens.

**The five advisories, each a real defect, each driven.** The documented `eval "$(dev/jigc-rig X)"` **cannot fail** — status is lost through the command substitution, so a broken rig returns 0 and the caller's probe runs against the *previous* corpus; the documented form is now `rig=$(dev/jigc-rig X) || exit; eval "$rig"`, in `CLAUDE.md` and in the tool's own header, which is the same "status lost through a shell construct" family the sibling tool exists to prevent. `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin dev/gate --quick` printed three bare `FAILED 127 (0s)` lines with no detail, indistinguishable from a red gate; 127 is now reported as **DID NOT RUN**, naming the missing binary and saying it is not a verdict about the code. `--repin` printed `jigc-rig: FAILED (exit 1)` in the middle of a re-pin that went on to succeed — the `ERR` trap is inherited into the command-substitution subshell and fires there even though the failure is *handled* outside it; the rule now stated and applied at both such sites: a substitution whose status the script itself reads clears the trap, so the only report is the handler's. `--binary` accepted a **directory** (`[ -x ]` is true for one), reading as a validation it was not. And a relative `SCRATCH` resolved against the caller's cwd, planting a corpus **inside the repo** that — by the tool's own no-teardown design — nothing ever reaps; a relative root is now refused rather than silently resolved, because a corpus in the tree is the failure, not its spelling.

## 2026-09-03 — `dev/jigc-rig`: the shell front door onto the fixture builder, and a teardown that does not exist

A scan of 139 subagent transcripts measured the cost of not having one: **48 agents hand-built a jigc throwaway repo**, 92 ran `git init` (331 invocations), **71 wrote `rm -rf` on a shell-variable path** to tear those rigs down (390 calls, against 40 uses of the prescribed `mktemp -d`), and 14 committed `drive.sh` files across M23–M35 reinvented the same rig for six milestones. **22 agents read `crates/cli/tests/support/trial_corpus.rs`** — some grepping for `fn set_slot`, `fn jigc_ok` — and then hand-rolled its API in bash anyway, because `autotests = false` makes reaching it mean writing a `#[test]`, registering it in one of twelve group roots, and running a group target, for a thirty-second probe. So the answer is a **front door onto the builder that already works**, never a second builder: same state names, same verbs, same order, `trial_corpus.rs` the source of truth.

- **The design premise is that the root comes from `mktemp -d`, so there is nothing to tear down.** That is what retires the 390-call shape — which matters because `rm -rf $V/$D` is refused by a **static scan before it runs**, so it prompts a human and *parks a delegated agent*, leaving no transcript. The rig therefore ships **no `--clean` and no `--reset`**: a reset flag is a destructive-command generator with a friendly name, and it would reintroduce exactly the shape this exists to remove.
- **The parity fence is a set comparison, not a gate inside the gate.** `crates/cli/tests/dev_rig_parity.rs` asks the rig for `--list-states` (which refuses to list a state carrying no builder) and asserts set equality with `State::ALL`, so a state added to one half and not the other reddens the gate. A second arm scans `dev/` for a recursive removal on a variable path, and a third proves that scanner can say **no** — the fence is otherwise decorative. Construction parity is deliberately **not** asserted: it would mean building six corpora inside the gate, the ~38 s of serial subprocess time [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §4 already refuses to pay twice.
- **Running it and printing it are two dispositions of one script text.** `--print-only` cannot drift from what the rig does, because it is the same bytes; the construction runs inside a brace group redirected to stderr (rather than `exec 3>&1 1>&2`) precisely so the printed form stays paste-runnable without permanently redirecting an interactive shell.
- **`--repin` is the most-repeated non-rig ritual in the corpus** (29 agents, 77 scripts): reshape a schema, read the recomputed `schema-hash` out of the pack-load refusal, write it back. The rig loops it — the freeze assert names one doctype per pass — and ends by asserting the pack loads **clean**, which is the half a hand-rolled repin skips. It keeps the copied `config/schema-manifest.yaml` for that reason, where bare `--pack-from-dev` drops it (a manifest-less constituent is freeze-exempt, so the copy is a different *unfrozen* pack rather than a forged v1 dev pack).

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 12 / T4: flow 50 — six arms, and every one says what kind of set it iterates

The wave's composite acceptance (`crates/cli/tests/flow50_acceptance.rs`, twelve `#[test]`s over the real binary; `design/worked-examples.md` → flow 50) proves one claim — **a fence applied where its wave pointed is not applied at all, and the cost of that is silent, committed data corruption**. Four set-kinds are used and each is **named where it is used**, because getting that wrong would be the law-1 defect this wave exists to remove, one file later: a **code-side registry** (`VERB_KINDS ▸ Read`, `SetKind::ALL`, `MINT_DOORS`, `DOCTYPE_DOORS`), the **class's defining case-set** (`SchemaChange`, matched exhaustively), a **derivation stated as one** (the two layers a schema can arrive from; the item-addressing write doors, derived from `DOCTYPE_DOORS` minus the read verbs and minus `doc rename`, whose address names a document identity), and — arm 1 — a **manufactured shape space**, which the settle record required be written as a deliberate departure or *"an increment will loop over the registry and call two cells axis-complete."*

**Arm 1 ends at a commit, and that is the arm's whole addition.** `item_region_shape_space.rs` already drives the eighteen `shape × op` cells over the **staged** copy; re-driving them here would be a second copy of an axis with one home. What the composite adds is the cost the claim names: each of the six shapes is carried past the second `set-field` through `jigc task finalize` to a real `git` commit, and the committed bytes, the tracked path, the committed `doc show --format json` read-back and the store sweep are each asserted. Verified non-masking by an applied mutant — dropping the schema-keying from `item_own_leaf_region` (the depth-only boundary this wave replaced) reddens the arm.

**The shape generator is lifted, not copied.** `Shape` / `SHAPES` / `shape_schema` move to `crates/cli/tests/support/shape_space.rs` with one added axis — an optional `location:` home, which is what lets a shape be finalized — and `shape_schema(s) == shape_schema_at(s, None)` byte for byte, so the eighteen-cell suite's fixtures are unchanged and stay green in the same commit. Two consumers of one axis is one axis; a second copy is a second axis that can silently disagree.

**Two dispositions rather than fourteen citations, deliberately.** `change_cell` matches `SchemaChange` exhaustively and returns *driven here* or *the engine's per-kind fold axis* — whose existence the arm asserts rather than assumes. Minting a per-variant filename map would have been fourteen claims this task did not verify, which is the *"an agent's report is a lead, not a measurement"* rule applied to a test's own citations. And arm 6's unknown-doctype default arm is **sound rather than lazy**, with its reason stated: `unknown_doctype_axis.rs` derives its rows from `DOCTYPE_DOORS` itself, so a new door joins that sweep with no edit — what this arm owes is the pair it drives live, held as an equality so a door marked driven and never run reddens.

**Increment 12's remaining scope gets no arm, recorded as a decision.** The golden regeneration, the two ledgers and the fold-back carry no verb, finding or route for a done-picture walk to reach; the one part of the increment that is code — `MINT_DOORS` — rides arm 2 (the M46 Increment 9 and M48 Increment 11 precedent).

`engine::state::write_staged_snapshot`'s doc-comment said the snapshot is *"written at every task-minting door"* and then named three. **Five** production sites open a working area: `cli::start::mint_in_repo`, `cli::start::mint_migration_in_repo`, `cli::milestone::run_create` — and `engine::milestone::add_task` and `engine::milestone::reseed_sub_task_areas`, which it never named. **The two are exempt, and the exemption is now stated rather than absent** — which is the whole difference the M49 Settle recorded as the carryover refutation's residue. The premise, asserted through the real binary in the red step rather than taken from the planner's note: `jigc task finalize <sub>` refuses a milestone sub-task **first** (`finalize.milestone-sub-task`), so no committing door can consume a snapshot written into a sub-task's area, and the boundary that *does* gate reads the **milestone** area's snapshot. `reseed_sub_task_areas` rides the same premise plus one more — it *rebuilds* an area the committed record already names, so there is no pre-mint index state that belongs to it.

**`engine::state::MINT_DOORS` is the registry**, one entry per production mint carrying its door (the argv shape), its call site, the mint it calls, and `Snapshot::Written` or `Snapshot::Exempt(<reason>)`. `crates/cli/tests/mint_doors.rs` is its two consumers. **(a)** A source-level completeness fence over both crates' **production** code — the shared `support::rust_source` scanner, the `temp_mint_fence.rs` mold — asserts the call-site set of `mint_task` ∪ `mint_milestone` **equals** the declared site set, in both directions. Proven red twice by applied mutant: a sixth production `state::mint_task(…)` reddens as `crates/cli/src/start.rs::mutant_sixth_door` **undeclared**, and a site string moved to a name no call carries reddens as **phantom** *and* panics the driven arm at *"has no driven cell"*. **(b)** One cell per member over a planted pre-staged `foreign.txt`, each returning what it measured on disk, which the driver checks against the declared disposition — so a mis-declared `Written`/`Exempt` reddens rather than reading as documentation, and a member the dispatch does not name is a **hard panic, not a skip**.

**One competing reason died.** `run_create`'s inline comment carried a *second* justification for the sub-task exemption — *"worktrees are provisioned clean and a missing snapshot fails open"* — which is the declared **fail-open bound**, not the premise; it now points at the registry. And the re-seed cell states its own honest half: after a fresh clone the milestone area's snapshot went with the gitignored workbench, so that cell asserts its **absence** and cites the existing pin (`carryover_gate.rs::milestone_missing_snapshot_fails_open`) rather than claiming the `add-task` cell's stronger fact.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T12: the illustrative disclaimer says what it disclaims, in one home

Fourteen of the twenty-eight `design/` part-docs open with a doc-level *"Notation is illustrative"* header. It names what it takes away and never says what it leaves standing, so a reader is free to read it as disclaiming the whole document — and one did: M47 refused D1 with *"No rule. The near-miss citation is killed by 'Notation is illustrative'."* A razor whose leg 1 is *a rule stated in a locked artifact and violated at HEAD* then decides by **which doc an item happens to cite**: the same rule refuses in `storage.md` and passes in `surface-contract.md`. The header was ambiguous about its own scope, and the ambiguity was load-bearing.

- **The home is [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) → *How we work together* → Conventions, and the argument is not "it is the top-level doc".** Three reasons, in weight order. (i) That file already owns the convention that **produced** the fourteen headers — *"Mark illustrative notation as illustrative"* now sits one bullet above the scope — so any other home splits a single convention across two files, which this file's own *one file, one purpose — route by home* rule forbids. (ii) The recorded cost is a **reader** generalising the header before deciding a citation is dead; `CLAUDE.md` is the one document in a session's context unconditionally, so the scope reaches that reader with no link followed. (iii) `structural-grammar.md`, the alternative the plan named, is a **subject-matter** doc about the skeleton grammar — a meta-rule about how all 28 docs are cited is not part of it — and it carries a disclaimer itself, so stating the scope inside a disclaimered doc invites reading the scope as scoped to that doc. The counter, that an outside reader of `design/` may never open `CLAUDE.md`, is answered by the fourteen links: the rule is one hop from every instance, which is the cross-reference discipline the same section mandates.
- **One statement, fourteen references — the shape of the fix is the rule it states.** Each header gains `([what that disclaims](../CLAUDE.md#how-we-work-together))` immediately after the disclaimed word, so the scope is attached to the thing it scopes rather than appended to a paragraph. Nothing is restated: the fourteen say *illustrative* and point, and only the home says what survives.
- **The subject is derived on position, not on wording, because the string was already wrong.** `structural-grammar.md:5` reads *"Notation **below** is illustrative"* and a grep for the common phrasing misses it — the fourteenth. What makes a disclaimer *doc-level* is that it sits in the header region, before the first `##`, where it governs everything after it. That boundary also keeps the two objects apart with no list to maintain: `changelog.md:34`, `self-hosting.md:123` and `validation.md:148` say *illustrative* **inside a section**, caveating one example, and correctly stay as they are.
- **The second fence keys on the rule's three parts, because each pair is a false positive already in the corpus.** A paragraph states the scope only if it names the **object** (a disclaimer), what it **removes** (*illustrative* notation) and what it **leaves** (a *citable* rule). The fourteen references carry the first two and never the third; `worked-examples.md` pairs *illustrative* with `doc-code`'s unrelated sense of a *citable* code unit and never mentions a disclaimer. Both were measured as hits under a two-marker draft before the third was added.
- **Three mutants, all killed, run before the gate.** Dropping the reference from one doc reddens naming that doc; copying the rule into `implementation/pinning.md` reddens with two homes listed; and a **new** `design/` doc whose disclaimer is worded differently — *"The shapes shown here are purely illustrative"* — reddens too, which is the leg that proves the derivation is on the concept rather than on the shipped phrasing.
- **Declared bound, on T11's precedent.** `DECISIONS.md` is outside the scanned set for the reason bound (c) gave one task earlier: it is the dated log of what was believed on its date, and this row's own planning entry quotes the criterion verbatim. A fence that forced that entry to be rewritten would falsify a record to stay green. The cost is stated rather than hidden — an append-only log can carry a stale copy of the rule and nothing here catches it; it is not a home a reader is routed to for current truth.

Four homes carried four numerals for one family — [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) said **nine** three times and **eleven plus one** once, and [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) carried that on as **twelve** — and the planning basis measured a fifth (**16 distinct code names**) against the roadmap's **14**. And `finalize.forward-ref-dangling` **is not** a member and had a table row: **no production producer mints it at all**; it survives only as a unit-test fixture in `finding.rs`, so it was a member of the count and of no code path. So the repair is [validation.md](design/validation.md) → *Exit semantics*' settled rule applied where it never reached: **the table is the enumeration, and its size is stated nowhere**. `cli::render::FINALIZE_FAMILY` is that table, on the `STORE_EXIT_FLIPS` / `BOUNDARY_DOORS` idiom, and it carries each member's **producing module** and **target form** so the contract's sub-table is *rendered from* it rather than re-derived beside it.
- **The registry is derived, not declared.** `crates/cli/tests/finalize_family_registry.rs` scans both crates' production source for `Finding::{graded,block,blocking}` call sites and asserts the `(code, module)` pairs it mints in the namespace **equal** the registry — so a producer added in a fourth file or a fourth crate reddens, which is the failure mode every previous census had. A non-vacuity floor over the constructors examined keeps a lexer regression from reading as agreement with an empty set, and the source view's bound is stated rather than presented as a parser.
- **Three fences, because the count was only one of the three ways this rots.** The **numeral** fence (`assert_uncounted` over the phrases the family is named by, `exit_flip_count_record.rs`' idiom) stops a fifth number; the **row** fence checks the design doc's sub-table against the registry row for row *including each row's declared target form*, which is what nothing checked while `forward-ref-dangling` sat in it; and the **identifier** fence refuses any `finalize.*` identifier a live doc names that is in neither list, which is what makes a phantom member impossible to re-add quietly.
- **The clause boundary is a correction to the borrowed idiom, not a new one.** `exit_flip_count_record.rs`' three-word qualifier window reads the *previous list item's* words as this item's quantifier — the roadmap's own M49 scope line trips it on a `two` belonging to a different bullet — so the lookback now stops at the nearest clause boundary. A quantifier binds inside its clause or not at all.
- **Declared bounds, carried rather than discovered later.** (a) The source scan reads `code` **string literals**, so a member built from a non-literal code would be invisible to it. (b) The numeral fence covers the phrases the family is *named* by; a retired numeral quoted inside a sentence that says it was wrong — the note under the sub-table is exactly that — is deliberately unfenced, because the record of the error is what makes the rule credible. (c) `DECISIONS.md` and `completions/` are outside the live-doc set **by declaration**: they are dated records of what was believed on their date, and rewriting them would falsify the log rather than repair a claim — which is why the roadmap's M42 bullet keeps its argument and loses only its numeral, with the correction stated in place.
