Mutation-proven on the leg that matters: with `assert_when_shape` renamed to `verify_when_line`, the suite still derives it and reddens for the missing row — a fence keyed on the `assert_` prefix would have let the next one join the load path invisibly and quietly re-falsify the file's opening claim ([dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → *a grep is not a fence*). The extractor's two boundaries are rustfmt-guaranteed (column-0 item start, closing `}` at column 0), which the gate's own `cargo fmt --check` keeps true, so nested `impl` / `#[cfg(test)]` helpers are excluded by construction rather than by an exclusion list.
- **The planning basis said six; the derivation says eight, and the two extra are not padding.** `assert_schema_freeze` and `assert_project_schema_shadows` were treated as *already named* — the freeze's **manifest entry** is indeed on the checklist, but the freeze *gate* and its M49 project-layer arm are the same family and are what actually refuse the load. Disposing them is what makes the set a set: a checklist that names six of eight members of a derived family reddens the moment anyone asks the code what the family is.
- **Every row states its condition, because most of the family is conditional.** The row format is `**Fires:**` (when it binds) plus `**Satisfy:**` (how) or `**Out:**` (why it is not a doctype author's obligation) — fenced, not decorative. Eight unconditional-looking rows would be this wave's own defect in miniature: a machine-maintained doctype with no author step (the `milestone-record` precedent) clears the three step-tier fences **by construction**, and `assert_stated_at` binds only if you ship a whole new pack, its code set being jigc's rather than the pack author's.
- **Two members are named by their code-side const rather than enumerated.** `AMBUSH_CLASS_CODES` and `CONSTRAINT_REQUIRED_TOKENS` are the authorities; spelling their members into the checklist would mint a fourth copy that drifts on the next wave that touches either, and neither row needs the members to be actionable.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T8: the permitted stdin form gets named, and the packs' 0× was never the whole count

S-1 is the purest instance of the discoverability lens: a **permitted syntax no composed surface named**. A blind worker under the default permission set reached for `cat payload | jigc doc author … --from-file -`, then for three write-a-scratch-file idioms, drew eleven denials and halted ([findings-verification.md](completions/artifacts/RC-1.0-final/findings-verification.md) → S-1) — while the heredoc attached **directly** to the `jigc` command was permitted the whole time.

**The fact taught is about the harness, never about jigc.** jigc reads stdin either way; what the four-command probe settled is that a harness which *statically analyses* a command before running it can refuse the pipeline (*"contains shell syntax (pipeline) that cannot be statically analyzed"*) and permits the attached heredoc. A step saying jigc rejects the pipeline would have been a fresh law-1 lie, so the shipped sentence says the harness can refuse it **and** that jigc itself accepts it.

**Correction to the planning basis: the permitted form was already named — by jigc, at one producer.** The basis above records *"the permitted form is named 0×"*; that is true of **authored pack text** and false of the composed surface. `engine::compose`'s `{{schema:<T>}}` payload-skeleton projection has emitted `jigc doc author <T> --from-file - … <<'EOF' … EOF` since M43. The two sets are **disjoint** — no step carrying a literal or catalog stdin site also renders a `{{schema:<T>}}` skeleton — which is precisely why one half reached a trial with the form unnamed while the other half had been demonstrating it for two waves. The disjointness is asserted, not claimed: if it stops holding, the suite reddens and the header is revised.

**The 42 was a lead, and the derivation is one member wider than any grep.** A site is a *command line that reads a payload from stdin*, and it has two producers: a literal `jigc … --from-file - …` line (the 42, across 16 files) **and** a `{{cli.<id>}}` ref whose catalog entry carries `--from-file -`, rendered into the composed bytes as a `Run:` line. `packs/methodology/steps/author-commit.yaml` has **no** literal site and two catalog ones, so a grep-shaped owe-set misses it outright: **17** members, not 16. The ref predicate is the pack's own (`cli::pack::cli_refs`, made public for the second consumer rather than re-derived, the `solicits_managed_doc_write` precedent).

**One sentence, once per step, above the sites — with the form demonstrated on that step's own write.** A paragraph per site would ride 17 files × 42 sites and be its own defect; a sentence with no runnable shape teaches nothing. Each member states the same sentence (fenced: `every_member_states_the_form_in_the_same_words` — one fact, one wording) and carries one `<<'EOF'` demonstration **above** its first site, because a naming an agent reaches only after it has run the command is not a naming. Every site is disposed: named by its step's statement, or OUT because the line *is* the naming (it carries the heredoc itself) — the partition that disposes the new demonstrations is the same one that disposes the projection's.

**Three arms, rising in strength**, in `crates/cli/tests/stdin_form_naming.rs`: the source sweep over the derived owe-set; **the composed bytes**, every workflow of both packs through the real binary, asserting a naming above every emitted site (this arm is the one that sees the catalog-rendered `Run:` sites at all); and the emitted demonstration **extracted from a real `jigc start` and executed by `sh`, byte for byte**, with the write read back through `doc show --task`. A form the packs teach and no test runs would be law 1's next entry, not its repair. Executability is derived, never listed: a block runs iff its **command** is placeholder-free and its write is a `set-slot` — inside `<<'EOF'` every byte is literal, so a slot payload has no grammar to satisfy and the demonstration runs exactly as printed, placeholder prose included, which is then what `doc show --task` reads back. A **batch** payload (`doc author`, the projection's own skeleton among them) does have a grammar, so a printed template is not runnable bytes and is not claimed to be.

**The demonstration payloads are placeholders, and that is the second thing the gate taught.** The first cut wrote real example prose (`one line saying what changed`) and the commit-doc solicitation fence went red at 2 — because on the one address that composes fully resolved, a runnable demonstration carrying plausible prose is a write an agent can make by copying, and it would have landed filler in the commit subject with **no finding**, the slot being filled. So every payload took the `<…>` convention the steps already use for `<slug>`.

**A heredoc-opening line is a demonstration, not a solicit** — a distinction three sibling suites now share, because they count or execute composed writes: `commit_solicit_axis`'s `emitted_writes` (which is why it went red — its subject is "the composed text tells you to make this write **once**", and a form example is not a second instruction) and `flow21_measured_run`'s `extract_cmd` (which would otherwise pipe prose into a line that carries its own). The distinction is **structural**, never a name: the line ends in `<<'EOF'` and carries its own payload and closing `EOF`. The M47 defect those fences were built on — `sub-task` soliciting `#summary` twice from two steps — is two plain solicits, both of which still count. Two more law-3 fences (`surface_polish`: the subject-shape and heading-ceiling statements must sit **above** the first solicit) were **not** patched: a demonstration is a place prose gets written, so a ceiling rule below it is a genuine ambush, and the three steps concerned took the placement instead.

**`Pipe the payload on stdin:` is left standing, deliberately.** The projection's cue line sits above its heredoc and is not false — *pipe* reads as *feed on stdin*, and the permitted shape is demonstrated on the very next line. Rewording it is a judgment-tier wording item touching engine prose, three suites and 168 goldens for one non-false word, and this task's contract is the site set the packs author. Recorded rather than done, so the next wording pass has it.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T7: the pack names the two read surfaces it never named, and the fence stops teaching one verb

Four read surfaces ship ([doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md)); the two packs named **one**. Measured at `f0cda4b`: `jigc doc show` 35×, `jigc doc schema` **0×**, `jigc doc list` **0×**, and `jigc doc` once in the two shipped guides — in `MIGRATING.md`, as `doc author`. The producer is jigc's own: M48's read-back fence routes with *"name the staged read-back … `jigc doc show <addr> --task {{task.id}}`"*, so all 31 soliciting steps learned exactly the verb the fence named. This is the discoverability lens that has landed six consecutive trials, with the mechanism visible for once: a fence that names one instance buys one instance.

**The owe-set is the fence's own, by construction.** `assert_staged_read_back_stated`'s solicit test is extracted to `cli::pack::solicits_managed_doc_write` and both consumers call it — the fence, and `crates/cli/tests/read_surface_naming.rs`, which disposes every member. A second, hand-copied predicate would have let the sweep and the fence disagree about which steps are in, which is the failure this task exists to fix one layer down.

**Every member is disposed against each surface, and both dispositions are *derived from bytes the step already renders* — never an exclusion list.** Blanket-sprinkling both verbs across 31 steps was the named failure mode, and it would have been wrong on the facts:

- **`jigc doc schema <T>`** is owed unless the step carries `{{schema:<T>}}`, which renders the shape inline and answers the read in place. **Correction to the planning basis:** that projection is used at **14** sites, not the 3 the decomposition recorded (grep `schema:` over both shipped step trees) — so 14 of 31 members are legitimately OUT and 17 owe it. The corrected count is what makes the OUT branch load-bearing rather than decorative.
- **`jigc doc list <T> --task <id>`** is owed where the step's staged read-back address carries an unresolved `<slug>` placeholder. At **17 of 31** members the sentence M48's fence forced onto the step is *unrunnable as printed*: `jigc doc show adr:<slug> --task <id>` is handed to an agent the step never tells how to obtain `<slug>`. `doc list --task`, shipped at M48 for exactly that question, was named nowhere. The other 14 print the address in full (`commit:{{task.id}}`, `changelog:changelog`, …) and owe nothing.

`the_derivation_is_not_vacuous` fences the derivation itself — all four partitions must stay populated, so a predicate that quietly stops matching reddens instead of passing — and the composed half drives **every** workflow of both packs through `jigc workflow <id> --preview`, asserting the emitted bytes an agent reads. Its step resolution is **pack-local** ([multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md) → Pack-local body-reference resolution), which the first cut got wrong: keyed by id alone, the two methodology workflows including `step:implement` were asserted against dev's ADR text they never render.

**`BOOTSTRAP_READ_RULE` is left unchanged, deliberately.** It already names both verbs — `doc list` as the definition of the managed set, `doc schema` in the derive-jigc's-behaviour-from-the-installed-binary clause — and both statements are true for their own subject. B1's gap is that nothing tells an *authoring* agent the shape read exists *at the point of authoring*, which is fixed where the solicit is. A second framing in `AGENT.md` would restate, not repair.

**The installed guide artifact** (`.claude/skills/jigc/SKILL.md`, whose bytes are `QUICKSTART.md` + `MIGRATING.md` through `setup::guide_body`) gains one block naming the three reads and what `--task` does to two of them, asserted off disk after a real `jigc setup` rather than from the source constant.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T6: `describe` stops projecting the winner, and the catalog's complement gets its reason

Two law-2 holes on the one surface whose job is to say what exists.

- **The command surface is the union of every declaring pack's catalog, attributed.** `describe` read `config/commands` through the composite's winner-take-all whole-file `read`, so the `[dev ▸ methodology]` composition an ordinary `jigc setup` project runs under projected **dev's 16 ids and nothing else** — while composition resolves each workflow's `{{cli.<id>}}` against *its own* origin pack's catalog ([multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md) → Pack-local body-reference resolution). Eleven methodology command-refs that every methodology workflow really composes appeared on no menu at all. The projection now carries **one entry per declaring pack**, keyed `(id, pack)` and sorted by it, enumerated through `PackSource::origin_packs` — the same accessor the pack-load fences use to reach every constituent rather than the winner. **One entry per pack, not one per id**, because four ids (`show-doc`, `finalize-task`, `set-commit-type`, `set-commit-summary`) are declared by both packs with **different argv and different hints**, and both are genuinely reachable: collapsing them onto the winner would hide a real command-ref, which is the defect, not the fix. So the id alone stopped identifying an entry, and the attribution rides both renderings — `<id> (<pack> pack) <hint>` in prose, a `pack` key in the envelope. Not a pinned spend: `Command::Describe`'s own long help declares the `--format json` arm *"as unpinned as the prose, and may change with any pack edit"*, and `doc schema` is the versioned structural read ([command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → Evolution posture, checked rather than assumed). The 31-entry merge is order-invariant by the `(id, pack)` sort, pinned over ≥2 divergent orders with a genuinely colliding id.
- **The suppression fence's subject becomes the catalog's complement, and no second key is minted.** `step:route-to-workflow` promises the reader that every workflow off the catalog carries the reason it is off. The catalog's population is `creates-task: true && selectable: true`, so a workflow falls off it by **either** cause — and M43's fence was keyed on `selectable` alone, which bought half the promise: `router`, `ingest-existing` and `increment` sat off the catalog narrating nothing. The fence now fires on `!(creates_task && selectable)`. **The shape was already right and the pack had already used it**: `milestone-execution` is `creates-task: false` and voluntarily carries a `suppressed:` block, and `suppression_reason` never read `selectable` — so a `creates-task: false`-only key would have been a second vocabulary for one fact. `expires: never` is the honest value for a structural absence exactly as for a permanent-by-design hide. The narration and the `router_hidden` key are unchanged, so M48's parity close is untouched; the router step's promise re-widens to the population the fence now buys. This closes the pre-trial observation logged and deliberately not adjudicated at [RC-1.0-final/pre-trial-findings.md](completions/artifacts/RC-1.0-final/pre-trial-findings.md) — *"nothing on either surface defines 'hidden', so the sentence's truth depends on a distinction the reader has no way to make"* — by making the sentence true under **both** readings rather than by defining the word.

**M46's F1 arm is rewritten on a changed basis, not deleted.** `routing_loop.rs`'s standing arm pinned the *narrowing* M46 chose — the promise may name only the half the fence buys. With the fence covering the complement, that narrowing stops being a repair and becomes a constraint on a sentence that is now true unscoped, so the two prose-shape asserts go and the driven ones get stronger: **every** off-catalog workflow must carry the clause and its reason, **no** catalog member may claim to be hidden from the catalog it is listed on, and the reasonless set must be **empty** where it previously had to be non-empty.

**What is derived rather than listed.** Both arms read the shipped packs on disk: the union expectation is built from each pack's own `config/commands.yaml` + `config/defaults.yaml` `pack-id`, and the reasons arm iterates the catalog's complement computed from every workflow's front-matter — with a non-vacuity assert on each (the two catalogs must genuinely diverge; the complement must be strictly wider than the `selectable: false` set) so neither can pass over an empty derivation. The fence's widened trigger is mutation-proven: narrowed back to `!def.selectable`, the `creates-task: false` arm goes red.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T5: the clap seam is 17 kinds, and one of them panicked

Deriving the axis instead of inheriting its size **falsified two of the planning basis's own facts**, and the second was a live defect.

- **`clap::error::ErrorKind` has 17 variants, not 16.** The planning bullet above (*"exactly 16 variants"*) missed `InvalidUtf8`, declared at `clap_builder-4.6.0/src/error/kind.rs:256` between `MissingSubcommand` and `DisplayHelp`. The count is unverifiable from inside the language — the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]` with no `all()`, so no `match` can be made to redden — which is exactly why the miscount survived a source read. `crates/cli/tests/clap_error_kind_axis.rs` therefore pins the `clap_builder` **release** the table was derived against by reading `Cargo.lock`: an upgrade reddens and the table is re-derived rather than inherited. The same 16 rides [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 49 Increment 11's scope line and the M49 [baseline-ledger](completions/artifacts/M49/baseline-ledger.md) / [settle-record](completions/artifacts/M49/settle-record.md); those are planning-time records of a measurement, so the count is corrected **here**, dated after them, rather than rewritten inside them. **[Corrected 2026-08-31 (M49 Increment 12, T6):** this holds for the two `completions/artifacts/M49/` artifacts and not for `roadmap.md`. The live-doc set is everything under `design/` and `implementation/` plus the root `*.md` **except** `DECISIONS.md` and `completions/` — the boundary T11 declared four tasks later, and applied, correcting a **past** wave's numeral in `roadmap.md` itself. So the M49 section is a live row until this close, and its `2 of 16` is corrected in place here, with the falsified figure kept beside what falsified it. The measurement and the disposition above are untouched.**]
- **A non-UTF-8 argument panicked `jigc` at exit 101** — `thread 'main' panicked … called \`Result::unwrap()\` on an \`Err\` value: "\\xFF"`, no usage, no clap render. `main.rs`'s takeover arm built its argv with `std::env::args()`, which panics on a non-UTF-8 argument, and that arm runs *exactly* when clap has already rejected the argv — `ErrorKind::InvalidUtf8` included, whose whole cause is such an argument. Fixed by reading `args_os()` lossily: the render survives and a lossy token matches no subcommand name, which is the right answer for a token that is not one. The kind now exits 2 with clap's own render, and is the tenth row **reached by driving**.

**Correction, same day, from this increment's own validation: that fix was one site, and the class had two.** The bullet above is true of `main.rs` and was false of the binary. `invocation_log.rs` read the process argv a *second* time — `std::env::args().skip(1)`, for the record's `argv` field — on **every** invocation, after the verb had already emitted. So with the shipped `invocation-log` knob ON (its state in every RC trial this project runs), ANY argv carrying a non-UTF-8 argument still died at exit **101** with a Rust panic printed under the render that had just succeeded: `jigc doc show $'\xff'`, `jigc describe $'\xff'`, `jigc doc schema $'\xff'`, `jigc $'\xff'` alike — confirmed on the installed `1.0.0-rc.12` as well as at HEAD. The axis suite could not see it because **the fixture was an axis too**: every row was driven in a bare `git init` repo, the one state where the log wrapper does not run. Closed by reading `args_os()` lossily there as well, by driving the whole disposition table a second time in a `jigc setup` repo with the knob on (each row asserted to have appended its own log record, so the arm cannot pass vacuously), and by fencing the class where membership is decided — a source sweep over both crates' production code admitting only `env::args_os()` (`no_production_code_reads_the_process_argv_as_strings`), so a third reader cannot arrive in the panicking form.

**The seam's coverage stops being a sentence.** `main.rs` claimed *"Every other clap error kind still prints clap's own render"* with nothing checking it — the charter's own S-4 evidence. It now points at a declared table, one row per kind carrying its disposition (**jigc renders** · **clap stands** · **not producible**) and its reason, with three tiers of proof and no fourth pretended: every producible kind is **driven through the real binary** and its emitted bytes asserted against the disposition; the four kinds absent because of jigc's *own* argument definitions (`NoEquals`, `ValueValidation`, `TooManyValues`/`TooFewValues`/`WrongNumberOfValues`) are fenced over the clap tree, so a `require_equals`, a multi-value `num_args` or a fallible `value_parser` reddens the day it lands; and `Io`/`Format` say out loud that they carry **no** fence and why (they are never constructed by clap's parser at all — a property of clap's source, not of jigc's tree).

**S-4 itself: the takeover widens from positionals to arguments.** `FORECLOSED_POSITIONAL_TIPS` becomes `FORECLOSED_ARGUMENT_TIPS` with a shape per row, and the second row answers `--task` at the top-level `jigc rename` — which drew clap's *"to pass `--task` as a value, use `-- --task`"*, a misdirection twice over (the node's only positional is already filled, and no value form of `--task` exists there). The row is derived, not curated by convenience: a rejected flag earns a row only where the node does not declare it **and** the surface records a sibling form that does take it, so the tip routes somewhere that runs. Measured over the whole tree — 12 leaves declare `--task`, 35 do not — exactly one pair names itself across that line as a task-scope split (`jigc doc rename`, defined as *"the in-task sibling of the top-level `jigc rename`"*); the near misses fail the **second** leg, not the first (`jigc validate` names `jigc task validate <id>`, which takes its id as a positional and would reject `--task` in its turn). The omitting context is tested, not assumed: `jigc task validate --task` keeps clap's render byte for byte.

Cut [Increment 11](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the surface batch, and the docs stop lying*) into **12 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `f0cda4b` (tree clean; increments 1–10 landed). Every basis below was **driven on the debug build of that HEAD** in throwaway repos unless it is explicitly marked a source read. **Basis — driven at `f0cda4b`; nothing carried from the roadmap, the charter or the settle record unverified. Four of its stated facts moved under measurement and are corrected here.**

- **The read-surface naming is worse than "0", and the producer is named.** Across both packs `jigc doc show` is now **35** (increment 10 added one), `doc schema` **0**, `doc list` **0**, and **0** for the bare forms too; in the two shipped guides (`QUICKSTART.md`/`MIGRATING.md`, whose bytes *are* `.claude/skills/jigc/SKILL.md` via `setup::guide_body`) `jigc doc` appears **once**, in `MIGRATING.md`. The cause is at the producer: `pack.rs`'s `assert_staged_read_back_stated` refusal text routes with *"name the staged read-back … `jigc doc show <addr> --task {{task.id}}`"* — the fence names one verb and the pack learned exactly that one. `{{schema:<T>}}` is used at **3** sites, so the pack has almost no schema-shape surface of either kind.
- **`--from-file -` is 42× across 16 files; the permitted form is named 0×** — no `heredoc`, no `<<EOF`, no `<<'EOF'` anywhere in either pack. The permitted form is the heredoc attached **directly to the `jigc` command**; the denied one is the `cat … | jigc` pipeline, refused by the harness with *"contains shell syntax (pipeline) that cannot be statically analyzed"* ([findings-verification.md](completions/artifacts/RC-1.0-final/findings-verification.md) → S-1, four-command probe). The claim being taught is about the **harness's** permission analysis, not about jigc, which accepts both.

Driven: `jigc task validate --task` prints clap's *"tip: to pass '--task' as a value, use `-- --task`"*, the S-4 shape.
- **The unknown-doctype axis: five shapes, driven at every door.** `doc create` and `doc author` → `create.unknown-doctype`, located, routed at `jigc describe` · `doc show`, `doc schema`, `doc list <DOCTYPE>` → `store.unknown-type`, located, routed · **six `doc` write verbs** (`set-field` both arms, `set-slot`, `add-item`, `remove-item`, `retitle-item`, `rename`) → a bare anyhow, no code, no route, leaking a Rust `{:?}`: *"unknown doctype `bogustype`: the embedded pack is missing `bogustype`: no pack resource of kind **Schemas** with id `bogustype`"* — the leak's producer is `engine::packsource::PackError::NotFound`'s `#[error("… kind {kind:?} …")]`, surfaced through `DocCtx::schema`'s `with_context` · `jigc migrate --as` → bare anyhow with a route and the migratable set, no code · `jigc relocate` → bare *"no doctype `bogustype` in the resolved cascade"*, no code, no route, no set.
