## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T4: every refusal at `jigc rename` carries an identity and an exit

Driven at `23595f6`: **PT-A**, the charter's Tier 1 row, reported that `jigc rename`'s occupancy refusal — ``cannot rename to `adr:keeper` — a different doc already exists at docs/decisions/keeper.md`` — carried no finding code and no route, while *the same fault one argument away* did: `jigc doc rename … --task <id>`'s destination-occupancy guard blocks `write.already-present` **with** a route. The source read found it was not one arm but **nine**, and **eight** of them shared the reported shape: every state this door declines before it mutates anything was an `anyhow::bail!` or a bare `anyhow!`, which puts them outside M43's route floor **by construction** — `engine::finding::is_route_exempt` takes a *finding* code and a bail has none — so nothing fenced them and nothing could. The ninth is the unknown doctype, promoted three commits earlier by this increment's own T1; it is a member here because the axis is the *state set*, not the defect set, and its shipped code is read off `engine::store::unknown_doctype` rather than re-spelled.

**The `Finding` promotion, chosen over the anyhow-embedded span, because half of what a refusal owes is an identity.** Two precedents ship: `tests/anyhow_route_spans.rs`' checked `Route::mechanical` written inside an `anyhow` message (M43 Inc 1 / T7), and Increment 10 / T5's `finding_to_err` at `jigc milestone provision`. The span buys a **route** and nothing else. The invocation log was the other half of the defect: every one of these nine reached `Outcome::failure()` — exit 1, `finding_codes: []`, `error_code: null` — so a refused rename was indistinguishable in the log from the eight other ways this door says no, on the very surface M42 built to stop the log lying. `render::finding_error` (the shared funnel Increment 11 / T1 minted) now builds a downcastable `render::BlockedFinding` carrier whose `Display` is byte-identical to the flattened text it already emitted, and the dispatch reads the finding back to log its code. **The printed bytes of the three doors that already used the funnel do not move.**

**Seven of the nine reuse a shipped code; the two mints are the states no other door can be in.** One fault owes one code (T1's rule, applied to refusals), so the unknown/transient/absent trio takes the read path's own `store.unknown-type` · `store.transient-type` · `store.not-found`, the unslugable title takes `write.unslugable-title`, the occupancy arm takes `write.already-present`, and **both** fixed-identity arms — the placement singleton's and the milestone-record's — take `write.identity-change`, joining `jigc doc rename`'s two: the two verbs differ in *what* identity they may move, never in what kind of fault a fixed one is. Only `rename.dirty-tree` and `rename.in-flight` are minted, because only this verb refuses over the working tree it is about to commit in place, and only this verb refuses over an in-flight fan-out whose join key it would change.

**Each row declares its repair, and the two dispositions are behavioural.** A **command** row's route is run verbatim by the sweep: the doctype trio at `jigc describe`, and the two fixed-identity arms at the retitle they *do* support — argv-complete, with the `--slug` that pins the identity, both halves derivable (the slug is the type id or the work-unit id; the title is the caller's own `--to`), so it is a concrete command and not a shape to fill in. A **judgment** row states at the declaration site why no argv is *the* answer: a free slug is the agent's to pick (the reason `doc rename`'s own occupancy guard routes `Human`), committing or stashing is git's move and which one is the operator's call, and finalize-keeps-the-work / discard-drops-it is not jigc's choice — so the route names both exits instead of picking one. There is no third disposition: the route floor admits no route-less blocking finding outside the conformance parse diagnostics, and none of these is one.

**Two non-members, each with its reason at the site.** The **malformed address** stays a code-less `anyhow`: it is a row of the *address-parse* fault axis (Increment 5 / T3), which gave every head fault one sentence and one `jigc describe` route across every door, so a code minted at this door alone would fork one class across two — `anyhow_route_spans::rename_rejects_route_to_describe` now carries that split in writing, one arm each. The **in-transaction** failures are the other, for the opposite reason: they are the transaction's rather than the gate's, each rolls the store back, and a commit-phase rejection already carries `rename.commit-rejected` through the survivable frame. **Declared bounds:** these refusals reach `--format json` inside the `{"error": …}` envelope rather than as the structured finding projection — the posture every door of the shared flattening funnel already ships, inherited rather than introduced; and `apply_and_commit`'s introduced-dangle assertion is inside that transaction and is not driven — the clean-tree gate makes the before/after edge sets equal for a well-formed store, so reaching it needs a corpus engineered to be broken; it keeps its two unit tests and stays outside the driven axis.

The axis is `RefusalKind::ALL` in `crates/cli/src/rename.rs` — an exhaustive match for the code and the repair, so a tenth refusal does not compile without both — swept through the real binary by `flow37_rename::every_rename_refusal_carries_an_identity_and_an_exit`, one scene per arm (**two** for the in-flight guard, which keys on a task marker and a milestone marker and would otherwise ship half-swept). `flow37_rename::rename_onto_a_different_existing_slug_blocks` — PT-A's own report — is **extended**, not duplicated: it keeps the store-untouched half and gains the identity and the route.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T3: an undeclared section is `write.unknown-section` at every write verb, and validation.md's universal becomes true

Driven at `894376e`: [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The `write.*` route split states `write.unknown-section` as a **universal** — *the address names a section the schema does not declare* — and four doors falsified it. `jigc doc set-slot` at `#nope` and `jigc doc set-field` at `#nope/bogus` (both `--value` and `--unset`) bottomed out in the CLI's own target resolvers, which search the schema for a slot or a field, find neither because the section they would live in does not exist, and refused with a bare ``{"error": "no slot addressed by …"}`` — exit 1, **code-less, route-less, outside the finding envelope**, so a driver keying on `(code, target)` saw nothing and the agent got no recovery. The drive found the **fourth producer the M47 census did not count**: `jigc doc author` reaches both resolvers through its batch lowering (a payload section's `set:` key is a field hop; the section's own id is its slot, key-less), so a payload naming an undeclared section produced the same bare form at two more doors — and `author.rs`'s own lowering comment already *claimed* the `write.unknown-section` reject it did not get.

**The seam is the resolver, and the predicate stays single.** `engine::write::undeclared_section_splice` — the rank-1 form the six item-addressing doors already open with — becomes `pub`, and both CLI resolvers ask *it* rather than re-deriving *is this section declared* on the CLI side. So `field_target` returns a `DocFailure` instead of `None` (one producer, three doors: `set-field`, `set-field --unset`, and the batch `SetField` leaf), `slot_target` gains the same guard on its two section-level arms, and *undeclared section* is one predicate, one code, one sentence and one `jigc doc schema <doctype>` read whichever side of the seam adjudicates it. **No code is minted and no contract version moves** — the four doors converge onto a member that has shipped since M47, exactly as the increment's planning entry above declared.

**M47 increment 6's advisory 2 is closed, not re-declared.** Five rows join `write_miss_shape_axis.rs`'s `CELLS`, and the column is now **fenced against the write-verb registry** rather than hand-counted: every `doc` write verb in `cli::cli::VERB_KINDS` either drives an undeclared section hop or is named in `NO_SECTION_HOP` with the reason it takes none (`doc create` takes a bare doctype id; `doc rename` refuses any `#fragment` outright). Shipping over one cell is how this column started, so a ninth write verb is a row to add rather than a rediscovery. **The bound that remains is stated and narrower**: an address with no section hop at all — the single-hop `#<name>` at `set-field` — names no section, so *undeclared section* is not what it got wrong, and it keeps the resolver's own sentence, now rendered in the URI normal form the write-path findings key at.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T2: running jigc outside a git repository answers once, with one text and one route

Driven at `eca9c9c`: **every one of the 47 leaf verbs requires a repository** — the workbench, the committed store, the base pin and the cascade's project layer all hang off the `.git`-bearing root — and 45 of them told a first-time user the *state* and never the *move*. Three spellings, two contract shapes: `locate.rs` bailed ``not inside a git repository (no .git found from X)``; **17** production `with_context` sites carried ``not inside a git repository (from X)``; and `jigc setup` / `jigc uninstall` alone minted routed `Finding`s (`setup.repo-root` / `uninstall.repo-root`), whose message wrapped the bail in *"cannot locate the repository root: …"*.

**One correction to this increment's own baseline, with the falsifying datum.** The 2026-08-31 planning entry (and its baseline row) states **19** `with_context` sites; the count at `eca9c9c` is **17** — `git diff` over the conversion removes 18 lines carrying the sentence, of which one is `locate.rs`'s `bail!`. The roadmap's hedged *"11+ sites"* was never falsified. Corrected here rather than in the dated entry it appeared in.

**One constructor, and the fence is that it is the only one.** `locate::not_in_repo_message` composes the precondition sentence, `locate::not_in_repo_route` the route, `locate::not_in_repo` the anyhow shape the 17 sites and the bail now converge on, and `locate::locate_finding` the `Finding` shape for the two doors whose whole surface is a `Result<_, Finding>`. `tests/not_in_repo_axis.rs`'s **source arm** asserts that `crates/cli/src` carries the sentence in `locate.rs` and nowhere else — which is what keeps the axis closed, because the fourth spelling would arrive exactly as the first three did: a new door copying the neighbour it was written beside.

**The route is `Human`, and says so instead of manufacturing an argv.** There is no `jigc` command that repairs this state from where the user is standing — the moves are `cd` and `git init`, and `git init` is git's to run, not jigc's — so it rides `Route::human` (`design/surface-contract.md` → The route fence: *"a route whose command sits mid-sentence does not fit the constructor, and the constructor is not to be contorted to claim a conversion"*). The shipped text generalizes `setup`'s, which was already the right shape and only ever named its own verb: *"run jigc from inside the target git repository; if this project isn't one yet, `git init` here first"*.

**No promotion beyond the one that shipped.** The 17 anyhow doors stay anyhow; the two `Finding` doors stay findings; **no code is minted and no contract version moves**. What converged is the *text* and the *route*, which is the whole deliverable — the two shapes now say the same sentence, one inline after an em dash, one on its own `route:` line.

**The axis is derived, not remembered.** It is `cli::cli::VERB_KINDS` itself — the table already fenced ⇔ against the real clap tree — so the suite drives *the binary's* 47 leaf verbs, each from a directory with no `.git` above it, asserting per cell: exit **1** (not clap's 2, not a debug-fence panic's 101), the shared message byte-compared against the constructor rather than a copy typed in the test, the shared route **exactly once**, the stem exactly once (a layered answer is two answers), and the retired spelling nowhere. A verb added to the surface reddens the arm fence until someone decides what it says outside a repository.

**Declared bound.** `locate` has one other failure mode — an unset `$HOME` — which is *not* on this axis: no directory you can stand in produces it. That arm keeps its shipped message and route byte-for-byte, and it is a law-1 wobble left standing on purpose: it reports a `<verb>.repo-root` code and a "run it from inside the repository" route for a fault that is neither, and repairing it means minting a code, which is a contract move this task does not own. Named in `locate_finding`'s doc-comment so it is carried, not buried.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 11 / T1: one unknown doctype, one answer, and the door set stops being a remembered list

Driven at `23defc8`: one unknown doctype produced **five** different answers. Three were routed findings (`doc create`/`doc author` → `create.unknown-doctype`; `doc show`/`doc schema`/`doc list` → `store.unknown-type`). The other twelve doors were not surfaces at all: the six `doc` **write** verbs answered ``unknown doctype `x`: the embedded pack is missing `x`: no pack resource of kind Schemas with id `x` `` — no code, no route, and `Schemas` is `engine::packsource::PackResourceKind`'s **`{:?}`**, a Rust enum printed at a reader; `jigc rename` answered a bare ``unknown doctype `x` ``; `jigc task bind` answered ``no such doc `x:y` ``, naming the *doc* when the *doctype* is the fault; `jigc migrate --as` carried a route but no code; `jigc relocate` carried neither.

**The roadmap's "7 doors" is corrected to 15, and the correction is derived rather than counted.** `DOCTYPE_ARG_IDS` names the five clap argument ids that carry a doctype (`type`, `doctype`, `as`, `addr`, `old_slug` — each names a doctype at *every* leaf that carries it, which is what makes the ⇔ hold), and `cli_parse::every_doctype_door_is_registered` walks the real clap tree asserting that a leaf verb carries a `DOCTYPE_DOORS` row **iff** it carries one of those arguments. So the door set is the binary's: a verb added with a doctype argument reddens until it declares how the id arrives, and a row for a verb that lost its doctype argument cannot linger. Six doors take the id **bare**, nine as an **address head**.

**Two answers, and the split is kept on its stated rationale, not collapsed.** A **create-gate** door names a doctype to *mint*, so it blocks `create.unknown-doctype` and names the authorable set; every other door names a doctype that must already **exist** in the resolved cascade, so it blocks `store.unknown-type` — one fault, one code, whether the id arrived bare (`jigc relocate x`) or as an address head (`jigc doc set-slot x:y#z`). **No finding code is minted and no contract-version moves**, exactly as the increment's planning entry declared. Where a door's usable set is *narrower* than the cascade's — only `jigc migrate --as`, which needs a shipped `migrate-<doctype>` workflow — the narrower set stays in the **message** and the code stays the fault. That door's *known-but-not-migratable* arm is a different fault (the doctype exists) and keeps its own sentence and its own `<path>`-carrying re-run route, which `anyhow_route_spans` now drives with `commit` — a doctype that genuinely ships a schema and no migrate workflow — instead of a typo, which also retires that test's own name-lie.

**The `{:?}` leak dies at its producer, not at its six readers.** `PackResourceKind` gains a `Display` naming each family by the directory it ships in, and `PackError::NotFound`'s `#[error]` reads `{kind}` — so every site that renders that error, present and future, is covered. The write verbs' own resolution (`ActiveTask::schema`) now refuses *before* the pack read, keying membership on the pack's schema listing — the same set `CascadeDefs::declared_schemas` builds the doctype map from — which is cheap and adds no failure mode: an unrelated doctype's malformed project shadow must not make every write to a different doctype fail. `engine::store::unknown_doctype` is the one producer of the bare-doctype block, so the doors cannot drift apart again; the read path's own refusal keeps its address-naming message under the same code and route, because there a doc *was* addressed.

**The four doors whose only failure channel is the operational funnel** (`migrate` / `relocate` / `rename` / `task bind`) flatten the finding into the anyhow message through the new shared `render::finding_error` — the shape three private copies (`config`, `describe`, `milestone`) already ship. **Declared bound:** flattening puts the block in the *message*, so under `--format json` those four carry it inside the `{"error": …}` envelope rather than as the structured finding projection. That is the shipped posture of the three copies, not a regression, and closing it is an error-envelope question this task does not own.

**The acceptance is the axis, driven through the real binary.** Sixteen cells (fifteen doors plus `set-field --unset`, which reaches the schema by its own code path) each assert: the call blocks non-zero, the surface carries the door kind's code and names the doctype the caller typed, it carries **exactly one** `route:` line, that route's command **runs verbatim at exit 0**, and its stderr contains no `{:?}` spelling of any `PackResourceKind` variant — matched exhaustively in the suite *and* at the producer, so a sixth variant cannot ship without an author reaching both.

## 2026-08-31 — M49 Increment 10 / T6: `finalize.render-io` tells an absent commit doc from a read fault, at both call sites

Driven at `2cc47df` and again at `b9cde2a`: under `finalize.fan-out.squash = false`, with one sub-task entered and the other merely `git add`-ed in its worktree, `jigc milestone finalize` emitted *"could not read the staged commit doc `…/.jigc/tasks/beta/docs/commit:beta.md`: No such file or directory"* routed at *"resolve the read fault on `…` (a disk or permissions problem)"*. **Both halves are law-1 lies** and they are the *ordinary* state of a fan-out sub-task nobody has entered yet — nothing is faulty, nothing was ever written, and the named recovery is an act on jigc's own gitignored workbench, which is not the operator's to fix.

**The discriminator is `ErrorKind::NotFound`, and the subject is carried rather than guessed.** One constructor serves both renders, so a fix at one call site would have left the identical lie standing at the other — the incomplete-fix shape. `render_io_finding` now takes a `RenderSubject`, the [`Unit`](crates/engine/src/finalize.rs) precedent (M42 T3) applied to the render: absence means something different per subject, so the recovery does too. A **serial task's** commit doc is provisioned once, at compose, so its absence is a working area that lost a file → `jigc doc list --task <id>`, the shipped `ProvisionRoute::AtCompose` answer for this exact state one door over (M46 Inc 8 / B2-1), with the abandon-and-re-start exit in the tail. A **sub-task's** is provisioned on its **first re-entry**, so its absence is *never entered* → `jigc milestone execute <milestone-id>`, which since T3 prints a launch line naming that sub-task's **recorded** workflow, plus `jigc task discard <sub-id>` as the settle. That is why the milestone id is threaded into `render_subtask_messages`: the route is only runnable if it can name the door that prints the line. A genuine fault keeps the shipped text **verbatim** — it really did fail to read, and resolving the fault really is the recovery.

**One cell of the axis is not reachable through the binary, and the suite proves that rather than skipping it.** A milestone `join` reads every staged doc body *before* the per-sub-task render is called, so an **unreadable** `commit:<sub>` is answered by `milestone.area-io` — honestly, with its own read-fault text — and the render is never reached. The CLI arm asserts that hand-off; the render's own unreadable branch for a sub-task has its standing home in the engine, driven over a real unreadable path (a directory in the doc's place, which fails with something other than `NotFound` on every platform). The other three cells are driven end-to-end through the real binary, and both absent routes are **executed as emitted** — the argv split off the printed bytes, run verbatim, required to exit 0, with the sub-task route's own claim (*"it prints the launch line"*) checked in the output rather than trusted.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 10 / T5: the provision → execute handoff reports the real state

Driven before the fix: `jigc milestone execute cache-rework` printed **byte-identical** stdout at exit 0 over a fully provisioned, a half provisioned and a never provisioned milestone — so a `` Spawn: `cd .jigc/worktrees/zebra-fix && …` `` line for a directory that does not exist read exactly like one whose working area was waiting. Both halves of this task are one state (the set of worktrees that exist) and therefore one commit, one finding family and one route.

**The guard's trigger is the PARTIAL set, and the response is an advisory — not a refusal.** The red step's own assumption had to be proved rather than assumed away, and it did not survive contact: the composed walk's **first step is `Run: jigc milestone provision …`**, so `execute` is the orientation read taken *before* provisioning, and a blanket refusal would refuse the read that teaches the repair. Never-provisioned and fully-provisioned are both **settled** states with nothing to add — and the test asserts they stay byte-identical to each other, so the decision is pinned rather than merely left standing. A **mixed** set states what neither can: a provision ran and did not finish. One advisory per live sub-task with no usable worktree — its own locus, its own `(code, target)` key, the carryover gate's per-path shape — beside the composed view and never inside it, so the pinned `{task, text}` contract is byte-untouched and stream discipline puts the advisory on stderr under `--format json` (the `left-out` / migrate-byte-floor precedent). The tail is re-derived per `WorktreeState`: an *absent* path meets a fresh `git worktree add`, an *unreadable* one meets the leftover refusal — one tail for both would be a law-1 lie exactly one command deep.

**A provision that failed mid-phase-2 exited with a bare `anyhow`.** `provision` commits nothing, so it has no `rejection_frame` and its `Err` took the dispatch's `None` arm: no code, no route, no log identity — while the failure had already moved bytes. It now surfaces through the same `finding_to_err` funnel `milestone.leftover-holds-work` uses one screen up, as **`milestone.provision-failed`**, naming the path it stopped at, how many worktrees landed first, the underlying git/IO chain verbatim (the only sentence that says what to clear), and the shared re-run route. The two provision codes are deliberately distinct: phase 1 refuses having moved nothing (*"every path is as you left it"*), phase 2 fails having moved something, and the second claim is the opposite of the first. **Phase 1 keeps its plain context** and that is stated as a decision, not an oversight — it mutates nothing, so it leaves no partial set to explain.

**Two riders.** `render::migrate_source_advisory` becomes `render::advisory_line`: one shape, now two producers, and a name that is the shape rather than one producer is what keeps the second from drifting. And the text/JSON parity census row for `milestone execute` was **wrong before this task and is corrected by it** — it claimed the verb renders through `render::milestone` (it renders through `render::composed`) and that the agent surface differs from the wire by the routing footer alone (now false, by a side channel stream discipline *moves* rather than withholds); it carries its own disposition, naming the arm that proves the document stays one JSON value.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 10 / T4: the milestone id resolves where the task ids already do, and the agent marker gains a fall-back

Driven at `f658792`: one `jigc milestone execute cache-hardening` composed **three** `` Run: `jigc milestone <verb> <MILESTONE_ID>` `` lines beside `Spawn:` lines whose task ids had resolved correctly — the walk knew every id but its own. The three lines now read `jigc milestone provision cache-hardening` / `join` / `finalize` and run **verbatim**; the marker survives exactly where no milestone is bound.

**The elaboration pin — an `agent:` catalog arg may declare an optional `from:` source, and it is the marker's fall-back, not a fourth arg kind.** The two obvious shapes both fail, and the failure is the whole reason this is a design note rather than a one-line catalog edit: a bare `{ from: "milestone.id" }` makes the path's resolution **intrinsic-blocking** where it dangles ([command-catalog.md](design/command-catalog.md) → Validation), and where it merely resolves *absent* it renders an **empty argument** — so the off-verb walk (`jigc start --workflow milestone-execution`, the door `jigc workflow … --preview` routes a `creates-task: false` workflow to) would emit `jigc milestone provision ''`. Keeping the bare `agent:` arg, meanwhile, keeps a lie: the CLI knows the id and tells the LLM to type it, which is the determinism boundary pointing the wrong way. So `{ agent: <name>, hint: <string>, from: <path>? }` — *fill it where the composing door has the state bound, leave the marker where it does not* — the empty-vs-unresolvable stance ([workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) → Leaves) carried into the rendered command line. The `agent:` shape is parsed **before** the bare `from:` kind (it is the one that may carry both keys), its optional source is typed (present-but-not-a-string is the same malformed-arg rejection, never a silent drop back to a marker), and its key set stays closed at `agent`/`hint`/`from`.

**`milestone.id` joins `milestone.tasks` as the root's second leaf, and opens no navigation.** `ComposeContext` gains `milestone_id: Option<String>`, fed — like `.tasks` — by the CLI at the one door that binds a milestone (`cli::start::execute_milestone_in_repo`, reached from `milestone::run_execute`); the resolver does no work-unit I/O. The two travel as one `MilestoneFeed` value because they are one fact: the door that binds a milestone binds both, and every other compose passes `MilestoneFeed::none()`. Unbound, `milestone.id` resolves `Absent` — empty text, **never a finding** — and `milestone` alone, `@milestone.id`, `milestone.id#x`, `milestone.id.y` and any other first hop stay the blocking `workflow-refs.milestone-not-navigable`, the new leaf joining that axis rather than widening it.

**`flow10_acceptance.rs`' marker arm is inverted, not deleted** (the M45 precedent), and widened from the provision line alone to the class the change touches: all three `{ agent: milestone_id }` refs, each lifted from the composed bytes and executed verbatim against the built binary — provision and join at exit 0, finalize reaching its own state refusal, none of them the *`does not exist`* every one of the three verbs gives an id it cannot resolve. Its new sibling pins the marker's remaining home: the off-verb compose keeps all three `<MILESTONE_ID>` markers, emits zero `Spawn:` lines and carries **no finding** — which is also the standing check behind `milestone-execution.yaml`'s `suppressed:` reason, re-verified against the post-change compose and left unchanged because both halves it cites are still true. The **612 compose goldens regenerate with an empty diff**, and that emptiness is the assertion: no golden binds a milestone, so the whole off-verb surface is byte-identical.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 10 / T3: the spawn line runs each sub-task's recorded workflow, and the step's `run:` becomes the fall-back

Driven at `1475543` in a throwaway `[dev ▸ methodology]` repo: a sub-task minted `jigc milestone add-task … --workflow decided-task` was spawned by a launch line reading `` Spawn: `cd .jigc/worktrees/<id> && jigc workflow sub-task --task <id>` ``, and that line — run verbatim from the worktree it names — **exits 1**: *"names workflow `sub-task`, but sub-task `<id>` was minted with `decided-task` — re-entry must compose the recorded workflow"*. The `fan-out` step's front-matter carried **one** `run:` for the whole collection, so the pack told the agent to run a command the binary refuses, and the refusal named the very fact the emit had ignored.

**The fix is where the fact already lives, not a new one.** Increment 9 made the minting workflow a per-item leaf on the `milestone-record` and therefore fresh-clone durable; `milestone execute` now pairs each live sub-task id with the workflow read from **the same working-area file the re-entry W-equality guard reads** (`.jigc/tasks/<id>/workflow`, re-derived from that leaf by the shared re-seed). Reading the guard's own source is what makes agreement structural rather than coincidental — the two cannot disagree about a value they read from one place. `ComposeContext::milestone` becomes a `Vec<SubTask>` of `(id, Option<workflow>)` and `Resolution::Milestone` carries the pairs; **the resolver still does no work-unit I/O** (the determinism boundary — the CLI reads, the engine is fed) and still **sorts on the id**, so the emitted sequence is a pure function of the sub-task set and never of the feed order or of what each sub-task runs (Validation hardening #7).

**The step's `run:` survives as the fall-back, and that is its whole remaining job**: a pre-bump record's item carries no leaf, so its sub-task records no workflow and is spawned under the step's declared `run:` — exactly `DEFAULT_SUB_TASK_WORKFLOW`'s role since Increment 9. No new refusal is owed: the fed workflow id was already validated against the loaded packs at mint (Increment 2).

**Pinned on the emitted bytes, both arms, and run as emitted.** `crates/cli/tests/milestone_spawn_recorded_workflow.rs` drives the real binary over one milestone carrying **both** an overridden and an un-overridden sub-task, asserts the composed `Spawn:` spans byte-for-byte, then executes each span **verbatim** through a `jigc` shim on `PATH` from the repo root — the bytes an agent would copy, never a reconstruction — and requires exit 0 from each. The empty milestone still emits zero spawn lines. Two locked artifacts stated the old behaviour and are corrected rather than left standing: [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) → Emitted format rule 4 (`<W>` is the sub-task's recorded workflow; `run:` is the fall-back) and [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Sub-agent re-entry (which had called `<W>` *"the fan-out step's `run:` workflow"*). The 612 compose goldens are unmoved — every golden composes a milestone with no sub-tasks, so the empty diff is the assertion.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 10 / T2: a fence that mandates a falsehood, and the phrase that was standing in for an axis

`COPY_IN_APPEND_TOKENS` demanded *"would double"* of every copy-in declarer whose solicited singleton repeats — five steps, one of them (`record-changelog`) rendering on **`single-task`**. The binary never doubles: a payload item whose title mints an id the doc already holds is refused with `write.already-present`, the **whole payload** rejected and nothing staged, and the exit is to edit that item in place. So the fence bought a law-1 lie and *reproduced it at every declarer* — the sharpest form of the class, because the mandate makes the lie non-negotiable for the pack author. The clause is now the four facts the binary produces (`append` · `write.already-present` · `whole payload` · `in place`), and the rule it yields is recorded in [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md): **a named-fact token is only ever a fact a standing test drives against the binary** — here `author_write_contract.rs`'s end-to-end append-lands / collision-rejects / nothing-staged arm over a committed singleton, which had been pinning the truth beside the fence demanding its opposite since M47.

**One atomic unit, by construction.** Changing the tokens without the prose reddens pack-load at every door; changing the prose without the tokens reddens it too. Neither half has a green commit boundary alone, so the fence, the six step files, the three inline compose literals and 72 regenerated goldens land together.

**A phrase is not an axis.** `author_write_contract.rs` selected its owe-set on the literal *"existing entries are untouched"*, which missed dev's `author-change` — *"existing **releases** are untouched"*, same clause, different noun, and none of the three collision facts. The selector is now **derived**: every step of both packs whose body renders `T`'s payload skeleton (`{{schema:<T>}}`) **or** carries a literal `jigc doc author <T>` line, with `T` a singleton whose schema declares ≥1 `repeatable:` section — the only place a payload item *can* collide. That set is exactly ten (six fenced-or-schema-soliciting, four literal-command siblings already stating the clause correctly), and it grows with a sibling rather than needing an edit here.

**Declared bound, recorded rather than silently widened.** The pack-load fence still reaches the **declarer family** only, so `author-change` — no `states-constraints:` code, no `{{schema:}}` ref — is outside it and is held by the standing sweep instead. The two halves are bijected (`the_pack_load_fence_demands_exactly_the_clause`) so they cannot drift into disagreeing about what the binary does. `schema-manifest.yaml` and the freeze are untouched: this is step prose and a code-side token list, no schema shape or home moved.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 10 / T1: the delegation sweep names its actors, and the axis admitted a member the report did not name

`plan-review.yaml` had said *"A reader who did NOT author the decisions…"* since M16 — the capability shipped, applied at exactly one site, absent from its class. The sweep generalizes it: the subject is **derived** from the phase steps `planning` / `increment` / `completion` include (minus the `author-*` solicitations and the `*-finalize` commit steps), and **every member is disposed** — `In` with the facts it owes, `Out` with the reason none is owed — in `crates/cli/tests/methodology_delegation_prose.rs`, asserted on the **composed bytes of the real binary** over the `[dev ▸ methodology]` pack-set. jigc dispatches nothing, counts nothing, scores nothing (D7; 2026-06-21 — *the orchestration does not fold*): the step states who must act, and no mechanism checks that it did.

**The derived axis is 14 members; 8 are IN and 6 are OUT, and the reason is executable metadata rather than a silent skip.** IN: `validate` (its locked *"an agent that did not build it and cannot edit or commit"* — the step said only *"independently"*), `settle` and `triage` (the independent robust-case advocate, mandatory in two locked artifacts and named in **zero** pack files at HEAD), `plan-scope` (the ledger is what delegated recon **proved by running the binary**, not what an orchestrator concluded by reading code), `detect-gaps` (several independent readers, none of them the author of the claim it tests), `audit` (*"neither of them run by an agent that built the milestone"*), `fix-gate`, and `plan-review` (already satisfied, held so it cannot rot back). OUT: `decompose` and `plan-gate` / `execute-gate` (the human is the actor and the step already names them), `plan` and `execute` (the locked doc names the actor **of** the phase — the reader the step already addresses — leaving only dispatch shape, which jigc does not own), and `re-verify` (it commissions nobody; the independence it leans on is stated where `audit` commissions those passes).

**`fix-gate` is a member the task's own file list did not name, and it is IN** — the increment's brief-the-fixer rule applied to this fixer ([milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) → *brief the fixer with the finding, never with the finding's boundary*). It composes into **both** `increment` and `completion`, and `increment-workflow.md:110` + `milestone-completion-workflow.md:34` mandate one fixer per finding, strictly serial over the one shared tree, briefed with the finding rather than its site list — three delegations the step stated none of. Disposing it OUT to match the reported boundary would have shipped an incomplete sweep inside the task whose whole claim is that the sweep is complete.

**The omitting axis is swept, and it is what forced the shared-phrase construction.** The advocate sentence is owed by `settle` **and** `triage`, so the absence arm cannot be per-step: a workflow's expected-absent set is every IN fact **minus** those owed by a step it composes. `increment` composes neither, so the advocate must not appear there — a delegation parked in a shared step and counted for a loop that never composes it binds nobody.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 10 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 10](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the pack tells the truth about who acts and what happens*) into **6 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `2cc47df` (tree clean; increments 1–9 landed). Every basis below was **driven on the debug build of that HEAD** in a throwaway repo unless it is explicitly marked a source read. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 49 Increment 10; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M49/settle-record.md) → D7 · Tier 4 · the `milestone provision` residue; [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → the sibling obligation at `:131` (*the contract only binds if the composed workflow says it*, written as an obligation on **the family**); [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → The stated-at fence · the route floor; [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) → data-value roots · Emitted format rule 4; [command-catalog.md](design/command-catalog.md) → The three arg kinds · Validation; [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The lifecycle.

**Basis — driven at `2cc47df`; nothing carried from the roadmap or the settle record unverified.**

- **One `jigc milestone execute` run exhibits three of the eight scope bullets at once.** In a repo with `demo-milestone` holding `first-task` (default) and `second-task` minted `--workflow decided-task`, the composed view emits `Run: `jigc milestone provision <MILESTONE_ID>``, `Run: `jigc milestone join <MILESTONE_ID>`` and `Run: `jigc milestone finalize <MILESTONE_ID>`` — three unsubstituted markers — **beside** `Spawn: `cd .jigc/worktrees/second-task && jigc workflow sub-task --task second-task``, whose task id resolved correctly and whose worktree path is right.
- **That spawn line is not a papercut — the binary refuses the command the pack tells the agent to run.** Provisioned, `cd .jigc/worktrees/second-task && jigc workflow sub-task --task second-task` exits **1**: *"names workflow `sub-task`, but sub-task `second-task` was minted with `decided-task` — re-entry must compose the recorded workflow"*, routing to `jigc workflow decided-task --task second-task`. Increment 9 made the recorded workflow durable and the W-equality guard authoritative; the fan-out spawn line still reads the step's hardcoded `run: workflow:sub-task` (`crates/cli/pack/steps/implement-tasks.yaml:4` → `engine::compose::emit_fan_out_spawns`, which strips `workflow:` off the marker and never consults the unit).
- **`milestone execute` never consults the provisioned set — proven by byte-equality, not by reading.** Its stdout is **byte-identical** across all three states of the same milestone: both worktrees present, exactly one present (`git worktree remove --force` on the other), and none at all — exit 0 every time. That is C7: a half-provisioned set narrated as ready.
- **And the response may not be a blanket refusal**, because the composed walk's own **first** step is `Run: `jigc milestone provision …`` — `execute` is the orientation for the fan-out and is designed to be read *before* provisioning. So the guard's trigger is the **partial** set, and the widened trigger owes a re-derived response ([dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → *widen a guard's trigger, re-derive its response*). Stated as the task's red-step assumption, not assumed away.
- **`milestone provision`'s mid-phase-2 failure carries no identity and no repair** *(source read)*. `provision_worktrees` returns bare `anyhow` at `git worktree add` / `remove_dir_all` / `create_dir_all` (`cli/src/milestone.rs:2057-2125`); `Provision` has no `rejection_frame`, so the dispatch takes the `None` arm — `render::operational_error` + `Outcome::failure()`: no finding code, no route, no error identity in the invocation log. The doc-comment already declares the gap in writing (*"a `git worktree add` that fails partway through phase 2 still leaves the earlier paths provisioned, and nothing here rolls that back"*). The shape to reach for ships in the same file: `leftover_finding` → `finding_to_err`, which renders code · message · `at:` · `route:`.
- **`finalize.render-io` calls a never-composed sub-task a disk fault — driven end to end.** Under `finalize.fan-out.squash = false`, with `alpha-task` composed and authored and `beta-task` merely `git add`-ed inside its worktree, `jigc milestone finalize second-demo` emits `blocking · finalize.render-io — could not read the staged commit doc `…/.jigc/tasks/beta-task/docs/commit:beta-task.md`: No such file or directory (os error 2)` with route *"resolve the read fault on `…` (a disk or permissions problem), then re-run the finalize"*. Both halves are law-1 lies: the cause is a sub-task that never composed, and the route names an internal workbench path the operator has no move against. Reachable only on the `squash: false` per-sub-task path and only for a sub-task that **staged code** (`subtask_patches_and_messages` skips empty patches) — so the arm has to be built exactly that way.
- **The copy-in fence mandates a false consequence, and the truth is already pinned in the tree.** `pack.rs`'s `COPY_IN_APPEND_TOKENS = ["append", "would double"]` fires on any copy-in declarer whose solicited singleton has a `repeatable:` section. Six steps declare `create.singleton-copy-in`; `author-migration-vision`'s `vision` schema has **0** repeatables, so exactly **five** are forced to say *"would double"*: `record-changelog` (dev — and it renders on **`single-task`**), `author-migration` (dev), and methodology's `author-migration-roadmap` / `author-migration-decisions-log` / `author-migration-deferral-ledger`. What the binary does instead is pinned by `crates/cli/tests/author_write_contract.rs` (*a colliding payload item rejects the whole author over a committed singleton*): the payload is refused with `write.already-present` and **nothing is staged** — it does not double.
- **Four unfenced steps state it correctly, and the count is exact** — `author-decisions`, `author-decision`, `author-ledger`, `author-roadmap` each carry the append half **and** all three collision facts (`write.already-present` · *whole payload* · *in place*), verified per file.
- **A tenth step is in the same class and escapes today's sweep, because the selector is a literal phrase.** `author_write_contract.rs` selects on `"existing entries are untouched"`; dev's `author-change.yaml` says *"appends — existing **releases** are untouched"* and carries **none** of the three collision facts. Same clause, different noun — an incomplete sweep inside this bullet's own axis, so it is folded into T2 rather than left for a later task.
- **`validate.yaml` states the check and never the checker** *(source read)*. It opens *"Validate the increment independently"* and names no actor, while [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md)`:19` and `:110` require it be *"run by an agent that **did not build it and cannot edit or commit**"* — the constraint that makes independence real. `plan-review.yaml` already does exactly this at one site (*"A reader who did NOT author the decisions…"*).
- **`settle.yaml` solicits the defer fork and never names the advocate.** It asks the agent to surface *"must-settle-now versus defer-to-a-later milestone"*; [milestone-planning-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md)`:33` and [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md)`:29` both make an **independent robust-case advocate** mandatory *before* a defer recommendation is surfaced, *"never the proposer's lone cheap recommendation"*. `robust-advocate` is named in **zero** pack files (baseline P2, re-verified).
- **The class is not a keyword class, and a keyword selector would miss its hardest member.** `triage.yaml` carries the *same* mandated fork (`milestone-completion-workflow.md:29`) while never using the word *defer* — it says *"a fix too big for the completion-fix lane (recorded as its own task/increment…)"*. So the sweep's subject is derived from the **phase steps the three methodology workflows include** (`planning` / `increment` / `completion`, minus the `author-*` and `*-finalize` members), each disposed **in** with its owed facts or **out** with a stated reason — the `compose_goldens::EXCLUSIONS` idiom, never a hand list and never a grep.
- **`{{milestone.tasks}}` is the only navigable milestone path today** *(source read)*: `data_value.rs:452` rejects anything else with `workflow-refs.milestone-not-navigable`, and `ComposeContext::milestone` is a bare `Vec<String>` fed at exactly one production site (`cli::milestone::run_execute` → `execute_milestone_in_repo`). Both T3 and T4 therefore widen that root — T3 the collection's payload, T4 a new leaf — and the CLI does the unit I/O, per the determinism boundary.
- **The off-verb compose must stay clean, and this is a hard constraint on T4.** `command-catalog.md:122` makes an unresolvable `from:` path an **intrinsic-blocking** finding, while an unfed `milestone` root resolves to the *empty collection* and never a finding (`data_value.rs:469`; the empty-vs-unresolvable stance). `jigc workflow milestone-execution --preview` has no milestone, and `milestone-execution.yaml`'s `suppressed:` reason states the degenerate walk as its rationale. So T4 must keep the off-verb marker and resolve only where a milestone is bound — and re-check that `suppressed:` sentence against the post-change compose.
- **`flow10_acceptance.rs:377-445` pins `<MILESTONE_ID>` as correct output** (*"its documented run-time substitution point"*) and lifts the `Run:` line verbatim. T4 inverts that arm rather than deleting it, in its own commit — the M45 precedent for a test that pinned the old truth.

- **T1 — the delegation prose sweep: steps name the actor and the instrument.** `validate.yaml` gains the *who* its locked doc already mandates (*validated by an agent that did not build it and cannot edit or commit*); `settle.yaml` gains the advocate precondition (*commission an independent robust-advocate brief before recommending a defer*), and so does every other member of the class the derivation admits — `triage.yaml` among them, since its fork is the same one and its prose never says *defer*. jigc **dispatches nothing, counts nothing, scores nothing**: the pack states who must act, nothing spawns (D7; `DECISIONS.md` 2026-06-21 — *the orchestration does not fold*). *Done:* a named standing suite derives the phase-step set from the three methodology workflows' includes, disposes every member **in** (with its owed facts asserted on the **composed** bytes through the real binary) or **out** with a stated reason, and goes red at HEAD on `validate` and `settle`; the affected compose goldens regenerate in the same commit; full gate.
- **T2 — the copy-in contract stops mandating a falsehood, over the whole clause.** `COPY_IN_APPEND_TOKENS`' *"would double"* is replaced by the facts the binary actually produces — authored items append beside the committed ones, and an item whose title mints an id the doc already holds is refused with `write.already-present`, the **whole payload** rejected, the fix being to edit the existing item in place — and the five fenced steps' prose changes with it. **One atomic gate-green unit:** changing the tokens without the prose reddens pack-load at every door, and changing the prose without the tokens reddens it too, so neither half has a green commit boundary alone. The sweep is completed rather than repeated: `author_write_contract.rs`'s literal-phrase selector generalizes to the clause, which pulls dev's `author-change.yaml` in (*"existing **releases** are untouched"*, three collision facts absent) and keeps the four already-correct steps green. *Done:* a red step showing the pre-fix pack-load fence demanding *"would double"*; after, the composed `single-task` bytes (through the real binary) state the reject, no shipped step says *"would double"*, the widened sweep passes over both packs' whole step trees, `crates/cli/pack/config/schema-manifest.yaml` and the freeze are untouched, goldens regenerated; full gate.
- **T3 — the fan-out spawn line runs each sub-task's recorded workflow.** `ComposeContext::milestone` carries each live sub-task's **recorded** workflow beside its id (the CLI reads it — the resolver does no work-unit I/O), `emit_fan_out_spawns` renders `jigc workflow <that workflow> --task <id>`, and the step's `run:` survives as the fall-back for an item carrying no recorded value (a pre-bump record, exactly `DEFAULT_SUB_TASK_WORKFLOW`'s role since increment 9). The fed id is already validated against the loaded packs at mint (increment 2, `3b2b873`), so no new refusal is owed. *Done:* the driven repro above goes green as a standing test — a sub-task minted `--workflow decided-task` emits a `Spawn:` line that, run **verbatim** from the composed bytes inside its own worktree, composes at exit 0 instead of being refused; the un-overridden sibling still emits `sub-task`; the empty/off-verb compose is unchanged; goldens regenerated; full gate.
- **T4 — the milestone id resolves where the task ids already do.** The three `{ agent: milestone_id }` catalog args (`milestone-provision` / `-join` / `-finalize`) render the bound milestone's id on the `jigc milestone execute` path, and keep the `<MILESTONE_ID>` marker where no milestone is bound — the empty-vs-unresolvable stance the sibling roots already take, never an intrinsic-blocking dangling `from:`. `flow10_acceptance.rs`' marker arm is **inverted, not deleted**, and `milestone-execution.yaml`'s `suppressed:` reason is re-checked against the post-change off-verb compose. *Done:* `jigc milestone execute <m>` emits three `Run:` lines runnable **verbatim** (each executed from the composed bytes against the built binary), `jigc workflow milestone-execution --preview` still composes clean with the marker and no finding, goldens regenerated; full gate.
- **T5 — the provision → execute handoff reports the real state.** `milestone execute` consults the provisioned set before narrating the walk, so a **partial** set is named rather than presented as ready — and the blanket case stays a walk, because the composed walk's own first step is the provision. `milestone provision`'s failure gains a finding code and a route through the shipped `finding_to_err` shape, naming which sub-tasks landed and pointing at the idempotent re-run (*it adds a worktree that is missing and leaves one that exists untouched*). Both halves are one concern and one commit: they are the same state — the set of worktrees that exist — and they share a finding family and a route. *Done:* driven — the byte-equality above is broken deliberately (the three states no longer produce identical output, and the partial state is the one that says so), a provision failed mid-phase-2 exits with a coded, routed block rather than a bare `anyhow`, and every existing arm that drives `milestone execute` unprovisioned is re-derived in this commit; full gate.
- **T6 — `finalize.render-io` stops reporting a never-composed sub-task as a disk fault.** The read discriminates `ErrorKind::NotFound` from a genuine I/O fault at **both** its call sites (`finalize.rs:230` the task's own commit doc, `:939` `render_subtask_messages`), so the absent-doc case gets its own message and a route the operator can run — compose the sub-task's **recorded** workflow in its worktree and author the commit doc, or settle the sub-task — while a permissions/disk error keeps the existing text. *Done:* the driven repro above goes green as a standing test over both call sites × {absent, unreadable}, the emitted route runs verbatim, and no route names a `.jigc/tasks/…` path as the operator's subject; full gate.

**Every Grouped-scope bullet maps, and nothing outside the Deliverable rides.** *`validate.yaml`'s missing who* → **T1**; *`settle.yaml`'s absent advocate* → **T1**; *the `create.singleton-copy-in` fence that mandates a false statement on five steps while four unfenced steps state it correctly* → **T2** (both counts verified per file, plus the tenth step the literal-phrase selector was missing); *the fan-out spawn line's hardcoded `run: workflow:sub-task`* → **T3**; *three unsubstituted `<MILESTONE_ID>`* → **T4**; *`finalize.render-io` discriminating `NotFound`* → **T6**; *`milestone execute` checking the provisioned set* → **T5**; *`milestone provision`'s failure gaining a code and a route* → **T5**. The order is risk-first within the increment: the two pack-prose lies an agent reads on every run, then the composed line the binary **refuses**, then the two milestone-surface truths, then the misdiagnosed finalize.

**Two things deliberately not built, named so they are not mistaken for oversights.** No **new pack-load fence** for the delegation class: the M43/M47 stated-at tiers derive their owe-set from a structural signal the step already renders (`{{schema:<T>}}` × `singleton`), and delegation has no such signal — so T1's fence is a standing suite over a derived, dispositioned set (the `author_write_contract.rs` and `compose_goldens::EXCLUSIONS` idiom), which is what this repo uses when the owe-set is a judgment recorded once rather than a signal read every load. And no **delegation primitive in the dialect** — D7 deferred it with a trigger, and nothing here needs jigc to dispatch.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 9 / T7: the gate set gets one home, and the home is fenced

D9 settled `design/methodology-docs.md`'s gate table as the **single home** of the fourteen planning gates. It was not one home: `implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md` carried a second copy of the ids inline — **thirteen** of the fourteen, silently omitting `quote-attributed` — under a paragraph titled *Accretion discipline*, which is the rule that copy broke. That paragraph now cross-references the home and keeps its worked instances as the *why*, and the home says in its own lead-in that it is the home.

**The fence follows the `doctype_map_versions.rs` precedent — a prose file no test reads drifts silently, and this one already had.** `crates/cli/tests/planning_gate_home.rs` derives the gate ids from the **shipped `planning-record` schema** (the embedded methodology pack, loaded through the production `load_pack_schema` path — it hand-lists no gate) and asserts two things: the home's table rows are exactly those gates in schema order, and no blank-line-separated paragraph under `design/` or `implementation/` restates the set. Its sibling `planning_record_schema.rs` fences the other direction (the schema against the table, hints included), so the doc and the doctype move in lockstep.

**The restatement predicate is calibrated on the two real data points, not a round number.** A bare count of three would have condemned the *Settle* paragraph that names five gates as worked instances — exactly what the single-home rule wants **kept** — so the floor is a **majority** of the shipped set (8 of 14): thirteen-in-one-paragraph is a second checklist and is red; five-as-worked-instances is the rationale the home points at and is green. Both arms were driven red before the fix (the majority arm on the real restatement; the equality arm on a mutated table row) rather than shipped green-by-construction. Scope is `design/` + `implementation/`: `DECISIONS.md` is history — a dated entry records what a wave decided and is deliberately outside the rule.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 9 / T6: the forcing function, proven at the shipped door and over the whole gate axis

T5 shipped `planning-record`'s shape and said plainly that a doctype no workflow can create writes nothing. T6 opens the door: `planning.yaml` gains `allows-create: [{type: planning-record, as: gates}]` and a `step:author-planning-record` beside the other author steps, with `config/commands.yaml` carrying the create-fresh `{{cli.create-planning-record}}` ref. The parity walk's declared T5 exclusion **expired on schedule** — driven, not assumed: restored against this commit's pack the arm fails `expired: gating = ["planning"]` — so the doctype joins `METHODOLOGY_DOCTYPES` and its create workflow is mapped, rather than the exclusion being re-argued.

**The step renders `{{schema:planning-record}}`; it does not hand-list fourteen `set-slot` lines.** The projection is the only surface that renders a `hint:`, and a gate's hint *is* what the gate requires recorded — the whole reason the record replaces prose an agent skims. Hand-listing would have re-created the understated-template class M43's generation seam exists to kill, and would owe an edit per new gate; generated, a fifteenth gate composes itself. The cost is honest and accepted: the composed planning workflow roughly triples, because the fourteen cells are the payload, not decoration around it.

**The forcing function is proven over the gate axis, not one reported gate.** `crates/cli/tests/planning_gate_forcing.rs` reads the gate set out of the shipped schema through the binary (`doc schema … --format json`) — it hand-lists no gate — and for **each** gate in turn stages a record carrying every other one: `jigc task finalize` blocks with `schema-conformance.required-slot-present` naming that gate at its own address, no commit lands, and the *identical* finalize then lands the record once the held-out gate is filled. One held-out gate would have proven the mechanism; it would not have proven that *every* gate is a fence, which is the claim the doctype makes. The create is driven from the **emitted bytes** of the composed step (the `Run:` line, run verbatim with only its `<TITLE>` filled), never a rebuilt command.

**A shipped fence was narrowed, on its own stated intent.** `methodology_pack_compose`'s `--task` sweep filtered every emitted line *containing* `jigc doc `; the projection's instruction sentence names the batch verb in prose three lines above the runnable line that carries `--task`, so the fence fired on prose. It now keys on what it always meant — a line that, decoration stripped, *begins* with the invocation, i.e. one an agent copies and runs — joining the `--help` mention as the second recorded non-write exemption. No composed write left the fence.

**Not asserted, deliberately:** anything about what a gate slot *says*. jigc checks a slot is filled and never reads, scores or lints the judgment inside it (the A-3 bound, [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → the pack form), so every gate in the acceptance is answered with the same trivial prose and that is a complete answer by contract.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 9 / T5: `planning-record` ships — fourteen gates, fourteen required slots, free at the freeze

The plan-time gates have lived as a table in [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) since 2026-06-21 and as nine hand-built gate-records; the phase every planning session runs by hand now has a doctype. `packs/methodology/schemas/planning-record.yaml` is **one required slot per gate** and nothing else — no `meta` fields of its own, the stamp injecting its own front-matter — homed at its own `planning-records/`, never `completions/`, because the reconcile sweep parses every file in a location dir against every schema declaring it and two doctypes sharing one home cross-block each other.

**The repeatable shape stays reverted, and the test says why.** D9's first draft made the gate names data — cheaper per new gate — and the design review killed it: `required-slot-present` is the entire forcing function, and a repeatable has no such fence (`min-items` was rejected as a frozen trap; `repeatable-populated` fires only at **zero** items, is advisory, and is store-scope only), so a record carrying 3 of 14 would validate clean and finalize at exit 0. The bump-per-new-gate cost is accepted, and the fourteenth gate is exactly what a `ProseNeeding` bump is for.

**The hints are the table cells, byte-for-byte, and that is asserted on emitted bytes.** `methodology-docs.md:77` committed the M42 cell text to move *verbatim* into the schema's `hint:`; since M47 a slot `hint:` sits **outside** the `schema-hash`, so verbatim costs nothing at the freeze and sharpening a gate's wording later needs no bump. `crates/cli/tests/planning_record_schema.rs` derives all fourteen gates **from the table** — it hand-lists no gate id and no hint — and checks the wording through the `{{schema:<doctype>}}` projection composed by the real binary, because that is the surface that renders a `hint:`; `doc schema` renders none on either format, so asserting there would have asserted nothing, and reading the YAML would have been the masking test.

**A new doctype is free at the freeze, and that is now stated where a doctype author reads it.** `planning-record` owes a manifest entry at schema-version 1 with its own hash — and nothing else: no other hash moves, and it owes **no** `schema-snapshots/` entry, there being no prior shape to diff against. Driven: a corpus holding a committed record sweeps `0 migrated, 1 already current, 0 blocked`. It is deliberately **inert** until T6 — no workflow can create it yet.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 9 / T4: the snapshot store's first two-snapshot doctype, and a deferral re-argued on driven evidence

T2 put `schema-snapshots/milestone-record.v1.yaml` **beside** `.v2.yaml`. The per-doc `from`-selection by stamp has been general in *shape* since M34, but every chain until now was one hop, so `k` had exactly one legal value and *"keyed on the stamp"* and *"the only snapshot there is"* were indistinguishable. `crates/cli/tests/snapshot_store_two_snapshots.rs` is where that stops being reasoning: a v1-stamped and a v2-stamped record, same body, in **one** corpus, migrate in **one** `jigc migrate-corpus` pass — each byte-identical but for its own stamp, neither blocked, neither already-current — plus the two snapshots read out of the embedded pack as **distinct** shapes each matching what its own version declared, a store-completeness fence iterated **from both shipped manifests** (exactly `<ty>.v1 .. v(current-1)`, no gap, no surplus, every one resolvable out of the binary), and the v0 arm folding against the **earliest** snapshot. Red was confirmed by removing `.v2.yaml`: the v2 record blocked `migrate-corpus.missing-snapshot` and the pass exited non-zero.

**The recorded re-trigger fired, so the ledger entry is adjudicated rather than left keyed to a spent condition** — it stays **deferred**, on a basis that is now driven. The failure the set-growth actually opened is a *missing intermediate* snapshot silently stranding every corpus at that stamp; that is now a **build-time redness** on the pack author, which is cheaper than a hash gate and is why hashing stays premature while packs are embedded and cannot drift. **And the bound the entry has carried since M36 is sharpened from hypothesis to demonstration:** every link of this chain is a byte no-op, so the two records migrate to *byte-identical* results — a plausible-but-wrong snapshot is **provably invisible** to the migration's outcome, not merely suspected to be. That is the argument to re-open with when filesystem packs ship. The byte-equality assertion is deliberately load-bearing: it reddens if a link on a two-snapshot chain ever stops being byte-neutral, which is the second re-trigger. Two fired-trigger sentences in [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) are corrected to cross-reference the disposition instead of restating a condition already spent.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 9 / T3: the recorded workflow becomes fresh-clone durable — written into the record, and read back out of it

T2 declared the leaf; this fills it and sources it. `append_task_item` writes the minting workflow beside `intent`/`status`, and the fresh-clone re-seed (`reseed_sub_task_areas`) rebuilds **each** sub-task area under **that item's own** recorded value instead of one caller-supplied default. The defect this closes is not a papercut: a sub-task minted `jigc milestone add-task <m> "<intent>" --workflow decided-task` came back on a fresh clone as `sub-task`, so the operator's own `jigc workflow decided-task --task <sub>` was refused at exit 1 with *"sub-task `<id>` was minted with `sub-task`"* — **the re-seed had written that file itself**, out of a default the record never stated, and the W-equality guard then read it as authority. The guard is not weakened: naming the wrong workflow is still refused, now against the value the record actually carries.

**The CLI default survives as a fall-back, and only there.** An item with no `workflow` leaf — every record committed before the bump, which the migration leaves byte-untouched — falls back to `DEFAULT_SUB_TASK_WORKFLOW`, which is exactly the value `add-task` recorded absent an override, so a pre-bump milestone resumes precisely as it did. All three arms are driven end-to-end through a real `git clone` of a real origin: the override, the un-overridden default, and a pre-bump record built by driving the binary and then *removing* the leaf.

**Two doc-comments and two design paragraphs stated the opposite as settled fact, and are corrected rather than left standing** — `reseed_sub_task_areas`' declared bound (*"making the override durable means putting it in the record … a one-way door, out of charter"*), `run_list_tasks`' sibling sentence (*"a `workflow` file the committed record does not carry and therefore cannot source"*), and [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md)'s **Declared bound** paragraph. The `list-tasks` objection keeps its conclusion on a new ground: the value is no longer invented, but a `VerbKind::Read` leaf may not materialize a working area whatever it would put in it.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 9 / T2: `milestone-record` 2→3 — the record gains the per-task `workflow` leaf

The committed `milestone-record` is what a teammate on a **fresh clone** resumes a milestone from, and the one thing it never carried is *which workflow* each sub-task was minted against. That value lived only in the gitignored `.jigc/` workbench — so the recorded workflow was **not fresh-clone durable**, and a W-equality guard comparing recorded workflows then asserts provenance it cannot actually see, with full confidence. Schema-version 3 declares `{ id: workflow, type: string, set: on-transition }` on the `tasks` item block; **T3 delivers the behaviour**, and the bump lands alone here so its migration is its own red step.

**Machine-maintained, like every other leaf on this doctype — which is what makes the bump free.** `set: on-transition` means it is not author-required, `set-field` refuses it (the M45 settability rule), and the corpus cost is **zero bytes**: the diff classifies `AddedItemField`, and a `default`-less non-author-required leaf folds to the source *unchanged* rather than inventing a value on every committed item, while `required-field-present` never demands it. Both halves of that pair were a source read at planning; the red step **drove** them — a committed v2 record with a real `tasks` item migrates as `1 migrated`, byte-identical but `2`→`3`, and still validates with no `workflow` bullet anywhere.

**The store's first two-snapshot chain.** `schema-snapshots/milestone-record.v2.yaml` ships beside the M42 `.v1.yaml`, and the two are not redundant: `load_prior_schema(ty, <stamp>)` sources the `from` of a below-version doc's migration **at that doc's own stamp**, so a v1-stamped record diffs against `.v1.yaml` and a v2-stamped one against `.v2.yaml`, while the store sweep's managed-vs-foreign classifier reads the whole `1..current` set. The snapshot-completeness question the wave carries is therefore answered by evidence here rather than by assumption — the set grows per prior version, not per doctype.

## 2026-08-30 — M49 Increment 9 / T1: `completion-record` 1→2 — the audit vocabulary, and the enum members we kept on purpose

The doctype the methodology's own completion audit writes shipped a `severity` enum of exactly `[blocking, advisory]`, and **every real audit this repo has ever run grades HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW** — so `jigc doc set-field …#findings/<id>/severity --value HIGH` exited **1** at `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant`, and the record could not record its own audits. Shipped as the **superset** `[blocking, advisory, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW]` plus an **optional `detail`** prose slot on the findings item block: one `schema-version` bump carrying two changes, each a kind the classifier already names, and both **byte no-ops** — so a committed v1 record migrates with the stamp as its only byte delta (driven through the real binary on a `[dev ▸ methodology]` repo: `1 migrated`, byte-identical but `1`→`2`).

**The kept pair is the decision, not an oversight.** `blocking`/`advisory` stay declared because `schema_diff` classifies an `of:` delta `EnumWidened` **iff `new.of ⊇ old.of`** — a *replacement* would be `ValueRemapped`, which owes an authored old→new map, and `blocking → ?` has no defensible answer at either end (it is neither HIGH nor MEDIUM by anything the schema knows). The five-member vocabulary is therefore what the freeze charges here and no more, and the two author steps say which words to reach for rather than pretending the old pair is gone: the audit's own grade when it graded one, the must-fix/not pair when it did not.

**Prose evidence arrives as an added slot, never as a converted field.** `evidence` is a `type: string` field, so turning *it* into the prose leaf would be `RemovedField` + `AddedItemSlot`, and `RemovedField` is refused by design ([corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md):188) — a build increment taking that route reaches `migrate-corpus` and halts. `detail` joins beside it at the **0 → 1** arity, where a lone declared slot renders **bare**, under no sub-heading, so the fold writes zero bytes into every committed record (M49 Increment 4's `AddedItemSlot`).

**One collateral worth recording, because it is the shape that would recur.** Increment 4's axis suite manufactured its 0→1 cell over `completion-record` and hard-coded the manifest bump as `1 → 2`; the real bump made four of its cells red on an incidental *number*, not on the pairs they exist to prove. Its fixture now **reads** the shipped version and pins the target instead of asserting the source (`pin_manifest_version`), and its prior shapes are derived by stripping the shipped `detail` leaf — so the next doctype this repo actually bumps does not re-redden a synthetic axis that has nothing to do with it.

Cut [Increment 9](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the schema bumps, each a single bump*) into **7 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `622dffd` (tree clean; increments 1–8 landed). Every basis below was **driven on a debug build of that HEAD** in a throwaway `[dev ▸ methodology]` repo unless it is explicitly marked a source read. Delete `.jigc/{tasks,milestones}` (the fresh-clone state) and run any operating door — `jigc milestone execute` — and the area comes back with `workflow` = **`sub-task`**. `jigc workflow decided-task --task <sub>` then exits **1**: *"sub-task `<id>` was minted with `sub-task` — re-entry must compose the recorded workflow"*, routing to compose the wrong workflow. False provenance, full confidence, exactly as the roadmap states.
- **The severity enum rejects the audit vocabulary at exit 1.** In a `completion` task: `jigc doc set-field completion-record:m49#findings/<id>/severity --value HIGH` → `blocking · schema-conformance.field-value-conformant — write rejected: "HIGH" is not a member of enum "severity" (allowed: blocking, advisory)`.
- **The `findings` item block carries zero slots today** — the pinned `jigc doc schema completion-record --format json` projects `"slots": []` on the item — so `detail` is the genuine 0→1 arity D10 settled, and it is increment 4's `AddedItemSlot` that carries it (`transform.rs:323`).
- **`EnumWidened` is a superset test, so the settled kind fixes the shape** *(source read, marked as one)*. `schema_diff.rs:602` classifies an `of:` delta `EnumWidened` iff `new.of ⊇ old.of` and `ValueRemapped` otherwise. D10 names the kind **and** calls it a byte no-op, so `severity.of` becomes `[blocking, advisory, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW]` — a member **replacement** would be a rename needing an authored old→new map, and `blocking → ?` has no defensible answer. A build agent that judges the five-member enum wrong must **halt**, never silently re-classify.
- **The freeze is set-equality, so a schema and its manifest entry are one commit.** `engine::manifest::check` (`manifest.rs:326`) errors `MissingEntry` for a shipped schema no manifest declares and `ExtraEntry` for the reverse. Two hand-written enumerations ride along and redden on every task below: `crates/cli/src/pack.rs:3006` (`methodology_schema_manifest_matches_the_frozen_doctype_set` — the ten schemas listed by name, with per-doctype expected versions at `:3062`) and the manifest's own header prose (*"all TEN shipped methodology schemas"*). Each task repairs them in its own commit.
- **The doctype-map fence derives its subject and is strict about the cell** *(source read)*. `crates/cli/tests/doctype_map_versions.rs` enumerates both manifests and requires a row per declared doctype whose **Status** cell states that version — `stated_versions` (`:190`) collects **every** `vN` / `version N` token in the cell and fails if any differs, so a row reading *"v1→v2"* reddens. The scope-pin arm additionally requires the above-v1 set to be named with versions.

M49 charters that bump, so both are T3's to correct.
- **A `set:`-bearing, default-less item leaf costs zero bytes and never blocks** *(source read; T2 drives it rather than trusting it)*. `apply_added_item_field` returns the source unchanged when the leaf carries no `default:` and `is_author_required` is false (`transform.rs:501-506`), and `required-field-present` fires only on author-required fields (`validate.rs:21-24`) — so a `workflow` leaf declared `set: on-transition` migrates a committed record **stamp-only** and pre-bump items simply carry no bullet.

The two doc-comments that state the opposite as settled fact — `engine::milestone::reseed_sub_task_areas` (`:986-994`) and `cli::milestone::run_list_tasks` — are corrected here, not left standing. *Done:* the driven repro above goes green as a standing test — `add-task --workflow decided-task`, wipe `.jigc/{tasks,milestones}`, operate, and `jigc workflow decided-task --task <sub>` composes instead of being refused with `sub-task`; the un-overridden sub-task and the pre-bump-record fallback are arms of the same test; full gate.

The trigger is answered by **driving the store**, not by re-reasoning it: a **v1**-stamped committed record must migrate straight to v3 in one pass (`load_prior_schema(ty, 1)` → the v1 shape → the union diff), a **v2**-stamped one to v3 via its own snapshot, and the entry is then re-recorded — discharged or re-deferred with the driven result as its basis, never left keyed to a trigger that has already fired. *Done:* a named standing test carrying both stamped arms passes (red today: neither snapshot pair exists), and the ledger entry states its new disposition; full gate.
