## 2026-08-29 — M49 Increment 5 (T6): the batch stops re-reading the whole document once per leaf per parse site

**The measurement moved the fix out of the file the plan named.** The decomposition pointed at `crates/cli/src/doc.rs` + `crates/engine/src/write.rs` — the batch's apply chain. It is true that each lowered leaf re-parses the growing buffer three or four times (`item_chain_absent`, the splice's own locate, `validate_after`), and that alone is quadratic; but a `sample(1)` profile of the 800-item run at `ebfc53a` — this increment's HEAD before this task — attributed **3495 of 3554 samples — 98 %** — to one function in a third file: `engine::parse::line_of`, which answered *"which line is this byte on?"* by counting the newlines in the whole prefix, and is called **per structural element** (once per heading in `scan_blocks`, again per item head and per slot span in `parse_items`). That is a second O(n²) *inside one parse*, and its product with the per-leaf re-read is the cube. The fix is therefore entirely in `crates/engine/src/parse.rs`; the apply chain is untouched, and no verb, finding, route or byte moves.

**Two indexes, because the first uncovered the second.** `LineIndex` — every `\n` offset, ascending — makes a line lookup a `partition_point` instead of a prefix rescan. With it in, the *next* term surfaced with the same shape one layer down: the item heads, the field-group sentinel, the slot ceiling and the nested-region boundary each filtered the **whole** block list, once per item. So `Scan` also carries a start-ordered permutation of the blocks behind `blocks_in(from, end)`, and every range-scoped filter in the module reads through it. The permutation is deliberately **not** a sort of `scan_blocks`' output: ~20 `write.rs` call sites consume that vector in document order, and it is not sortable in place safely anyway — a `Block::List` is pushed at its **end** event, so a heading inside a list item lands before the list containing it. Almost-sorted is exactly the input a binary search answers wrongly and silently.

**Measured for this task, one payload, `spec` with three leaves per item, release build — before at `ebfc53a` / after:** 50 → 0.08 s / **0.07**; 100 → 0.27 / **0.14**; 200 → 1.48 / **0.40**; 400 → 10.24 / **1.54**; 800 → 77.26 / **6.69**; 1500 → **25.94** (its "before" is the wave's recorded observation at the earlier `2c6876a`: killed, untimed). Ratio per doubling **before** 3.3 → 5.5 → 6.9 → 7.5 (≈ n²·⁹), **after** 2.0 → 3.0 → 3.8 → 4.3 (≈ n²·¹). Debug, which is what the suite asserts on: before 200 → 52.3 s, 400 → 410.4 s (ratio **7.85**); after 3.6 s / 14.1 s (ratio **3.96**).

**The assertion is a growth ratio, not a stopwatch** — a wall-clock ceiling is a fact about the machine and would redden on a loaded CI box and green on a fast one for reasons unrelated to the code, whereas a constant-factor speedup moves both measurements together and leaves the ratio alone. `crates/cli/tests/author_batch_scaling.rs` drives the real binary at 200 and 400 items, **alternating** the two sizes and taking the minimum of two rounds so a burst of load lands on both, and bounds the ratio at **5.5**: the quadratic residual predicts 4, the cubic path measured 7.85. It was red at HEAD for exactly that reason before a line of the fix was written.

**Byte fidelity is the other arm, and it is a capture, not a reconstruction.** The 800-item document produced at `ebfc53a` was captured verbatim (89 KB, `tests/fixtures/author-batch-scaling/spec-800-items.md`) and the suite re-authors the same payload and compares. It passes: the debug build after the change emits exactly the bytes the release build before it did. The engine's own `LineIndex` equivalence — for **every** offset in an arbitrary source, the binary search returns what the counting definition returned — is a proptest carrying the predecessor's body inline, so it specifies itself rather than leaning on a function that no longer exists.

**One citation rotted and the fence caught it, which is the fence working.** [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → *The item's own leaf region* cites the four sites the boundary is keyed on by `file:line`, and `item_region_rule_stated` resolves each citation against the code rather than trusting it. Moving `parse_items`' `first_nested_heading` call reddened that arm; the citation is repointed (`parse.rs:1057` → `:1172`), not the fence relaxed. The three `write.rs` citations are untouched, because this task does not touch `write.rs`.

**The residual bound is stated where an adopter meets it.** Each leaf still re-reads the whole buffer, so n leaves over an O(n) document remain O(n²) — the extra factor of n is what left. [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) → *What migration does not give you* now says so with the numbers, because every one of the twelve `migrate-*` workflows authors its whole document in one payload and a several-thousand-item source is still minutes.

## 2026-08-29 — M49 Increment 5 (T5): the collision joins the write-verb × miss-shape axis — `write.already-present` stops giving advice you cannot take

**A collision is not a miss, and the route that treated it as one was wrong for the case that matters.** Every other column of the matrix is an *address* miss; this one is the opposite — the section is declared, the shape is right, and the **minted id is taken**. The shipped route was a `Route::human`: *"the target already exists — edit it in place (`set-field`/`set-slot`) instead of re-creating it"*. That is the right answer for a **correction** and the wrong answer for a **second, distinct entry** — two genuinely different titles can slug alike (`1-3-0` and `1.3.0` mint one id) — and it is not runnable at all, so from inside a `doc author` payload (rejected **whole**, nothing staged) it terminated nowhere. T4 made the recovery a command; T5 makes the reject name it.

**One site, because the two doors must not disagree.** The enrichment hangs off `apply_add_item_target` — the single source→source transform the per-leaf `add-item` verb and the batch's `apply_leaf` both call — so the verb and the batch inherit the same route by construction rather than by two matching copies. That is why the door gained a `task_id` parameter (threaded through `apply_leaf`): a copy-runnable route names the task it runs in, the same completeness `enrich_not_present_route`'s `doc show` route already has.

**The route names a free id, not a placeholder, because the suite runs it verbatim.** `--slug <minted>-N` at the first free suffix, probed through `engine::write::item_chain_absent` — the same presence predicate the item-miss doors rank on, so *taken* means here exactly what it means there. It is also the guard against inventing a diagnosis: if the **minted id itself is not present**, the reject was about something other than an item collision and the route is left alone.

**The one place it must stay silent is the enum `id-from`, and that is the fence, not a footnote.** Where the block's id-source is an enum the heading IS the member, so `--slug` is refused as an identity change (T4) — a `--slug` route there would name a command that *blocks when run*, which is precisely the un-followable route this axis exists to forbid. `add_item_locus` returns `None` there and the shipped human route stands, which is the true answer when the id *is* the category. The **doc-level `create`** collision is a different subject and never reaches here; it keeps its own meaning and its own text.

**The acceptance is the axis, and it carries its own omitting context.** Three rows join `crates/cli/tests/write_miss_shape_axis.rs`: the per-leaf verb, the `doc author` batch, and the enum-`id-from` cell that must stay human. The two mechanical rows assert the message names the colliding minted id, that the route names `--slug`, and — run **verbatim** on a private fixture in the same state — that the second item **lands** beside the first, not merely that the command exits 0. The omitting row was mutation-checked: with the enum carve-out removed it emits `--slug changed-2` into a block that refuses overrides, and the row fails.

**Correction (2026-08-29, the increment's validation).** The claim above that the route is *"the same mint … argv-complete and copy-runnable"* **from inside a `doc author` payload** was verified over one of the batch's two provisioning states and was false in the other. `doc author` has a **create** arm — the batch's own `create` is the doc's first write, which is the arm every `migrate-*` workflow drives — and its whole-or-nothing rollback removes the doc the create provisioned, so the emitted `jigc doc add-item … --slug …` named a doc that was no longer there and **exited 1** when run verbatim. The acceptance row masked it by pre-provisioning the doc (`provision()` runs `doc create changelog` before the batch): the fixture was authored in the one case the implementation handled. The enrichment now takes what becomes of the destination as an input (`RejectDestination`, answered by `create_gated`'s `existed`): where the doc survives — staged, or committed for copy-on-first-touch — the mechanical mint stands unchanged; where it is discarded, **no command is offered at all** and the arm is told the recovery that exists, which is to revise the payload and re-run the whole `doc author`. The acceptance iterates that provisioning axis and asserts the property over both arms — *a route that presents a command must run* — so a later payload-level `slug:` key can make this arm mechanical again without rewriting the test.

## 2026-08-29 — M49 Increment 5 (T4): `jigc doc add-item --slug` — an item's id can be decoupled from its title

**The fourth mint door gets the override the other three have carried since M39.** `jigc start`, `jigc doc create` and `jigc migrate` all take a `--slug`; `add-item` did not, so an item's identity **was** `slugify(<heading>)` and nothing else and two genuinely different headings that slug alike could not coexist in one section — the second was refused at the first's id, and inside a `doc author` payload that refusal rejects the **whole batch**. The flag is the same discipline as its three siblings: taken **verbatim**, validated with `engine::slug::is_slug` before a task is resolved or a byte is read, never silently re-slugified, colliding through the shipped `write.already-present` route.

**One derivation per side of the seam, because the ack is where an override goes wrong.** The engine gains `mint_item_id` — the single `slugify(title)`-or-override function both `add_item` and `add_nested_item` mint through, with the anchor-injection reject running either way (the title is still the heading's visible text) and the unslugable-title reject staying on the **derived** arm only (an override is exactly what lets an unslugable title mint). The CLI gains `minted_item_id`, because three CLI sites re-spell the minted id *after* the write returns — the acked `target.item`, the acked top-level address and the acked nested chain — and all three read `slugify(title)` today. An override that moved the anchor but not those three would ack an address the doc does not hold: a write that succeeds and then names something unreadable.

**The one refusal is an enum `id-from`, and it converges rather than mints.** Where the destination block's id-source is an enum (`changelog`'s change-groups), the heading IS the member and the anchor equals it, so `--slug` is a *second identity beside the member*, not an id for it — the same adjudication `jigc doc retitle-item` already makes on the same block shape, so it takes the same shipped **`write.identity-change`** code and routes at the same mint minus the override. Both doors now read **one** `id_from_is_enum` predicate: two doors that must agree about what an enum id-source is are one function, not two matching copies. The refusal is unconditional on the *override*, not on the door — the same mint without `--slug` stays inert, which the suite drives as its omitting context.

**Three `--slug` grammar rejects in one file became one.** `doc create`, `doc rename` and now `add-item` share `reject_malformed_slug`; a fourth spelling of *what a slug is* inside one module is the drift the surface contract forbids. (`jigc start` / `jigc migrate` mint **work-unit** ids from their own crates and keep their own copies — same rule, different family.)

**Deliberately not shipped, and tracked:** the `doc author` payload grammar gains **no** `slug:` key. The roadmap deliverable is the flag on `add-item`, and T5 makes the batch's own collision refusal name it as the escape; the payload-key question is Increment 12's deferral-ledger business.

**The acceptance drives the emitted address and pays for its own fixture.** `crates/cli/tests/add_item_slug.rs`: the collision is **shown** before the override removes it (the un-overridden second mint is refused at the first's id, so the arm proves a real limit rather than decorating a case that never collided); each item reads back at ITS OWN emitted address with `id` equal to the override and its own heading intact; a malformed override moves no bytes; the enum door refuses with a route that runs; and `retitle-item` over an override-minted item leaves the override anchor frozen. The **depth-2** arm needs a nested block with a non-enum `id-from` and **no shipped doctype has one** (`changelog`'s only nested block is `id-from: category`, which the enum arm refuses by design), so it drives a mutated dev-pack copy whose `arch-doc` component block gains one — with the manifest re-pinned through the tool's own `load_pack_schema` + `schema_hash` pair rather than a hand-typed hash, because a copied literal is how a fixture silently stops being the shape it claims.

## 2026-08-29 — M49 Increment 5 (T3): the address reject names its own fault and routes at the surface that answers it

**The six `ParseError` variants split 3/3 on whose fault it is, and the split is the whole repair.** `parse_verb_addr` flattened all six into one sentence (*a doc is addressed as `<type>:<slug>`*) and one route (`jigc describe`). For the three **head** faults — `EmptyType` · `MissingColon` · `EmptySlug` — that is true and followable, so it is kept **unchanged**. For the three **fragment** faults — `EmptyFragment` · `EmptyHop` · `TooManyHops` — the head has already parsed, so the sentence describes the part the caller typed *correctly*, and `jigc describe` lists doctypes rather than addresses: it answers nothing. Those three now state the fragment grammar and route at **`jigc doc schema <type>`** — after T1, the surface that lists only addresses the write path accepts — with the doctype read off the expanded address the fault itself proves parsed (a bare singleton routes at its expanded type: `changelog#` → `jigc doc schema changelog`).

**`TooManyHops` states the budget it broke, generated from the constants rather than typed.** *"the grammar admits at most 6 hops: a section, then two per nesting level (the item id and the nested section that declares the next block), then the leaf — so the deepest addressable leaf write is 2 nesting levels deep"* — both numbers read from `address::MAX_FRAGMENT_HOPS` and `schema::MAX_NESTING_DEPTH`, so the sentence cannot go stale the day the grammar moves. The fault was **depth** and no word of the old message named it.

**The mapping is an exhaustive match, so a seventh variant cannot compile without a message and a route** — the fence is the language, not a reviewer. `ParseError`'s own doc says so at the definition site, which is where an author adding a variant is standing; its `TooManyHops` comment (*"more than the three permitted hops"*) and `Fragment::parse`'s (*"1–3 hops … more than three hops"*) were **false** — the `Deep` arm has admitted up to six since M22 — and are corrected in the same commit, since a variant whose own doc misstates the cap is how a message misstating it gets written.

**The doctype hop is user bytes on a route, so it is rendered as one.** A mechanical route's text is `argv.join(" ")` — bytes an agent pastes — so the hop goes through `task::shell_token`, and a hop that re-lexes as a **flag** (reachable as `jigc doc show -- -x:slug#`) is placed after clap's `--`. Without that it is not a cosmetic issue: `Route::mechanical`'s argv fence would refuse construction and **panic** the debug binary. Driven, not reasoned about.

**The acceptance is the axis as data, one row per variant, bound to the enum.** `crates/cli/tests/address_parse_error_axis.rs` (M47's write-verb × miss-shape shape, applied to the addressing seam) drives each row through `jigc doc show` on the real binary: it blocks non-zero, the message names *this* fault, the surface carries exactly **one** route line, no fragment fault's route is `jigc describe`, the fragment route **runs verbatim at exit 0**, and the six rendered surfaces are **pairwise distinct**. Each row asserts its address really provokes the variant it claims (through `Address::parse` itself) and a test-side exhaustive `variant_name` match means a seventh variant cannot compile without an author arriving here too.

## 2026-08-29 — M49 Increment 5 (T2): the four docs stop stating a cap the tool does not enforce

**Each of the four live homes now states the number *and* its reason, re-derived from what T1 shipped** — [structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md) → Repetition (and its Open-questions echo), [changelog.md](design/changelog.md) (engine work #1 and the *What stays deferred* line), [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → Slot heading-depth ceiling, and [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) (the graduated multi-level-repetition entry and the nesting-beyond-2 trigger). Both halves of the retired fact were false, not one: the **number** is 2, not 4, and the **reason** is the address hop budget, not the `H6` heading ceiling — which each home now names as the *other*, non-binding cap rather than as the cap. Stating the reason is what makes the number checkable instead of memorized, and a number with no reason is exactly how three ceilings drifted apart for three milestones.

**The derivation's arithmetic lives in one home and the other three point at it.** `structural-grammar.md` → Repetition carries `2D + 1` and `(MAX_FRAGMENT_HOPS − 1) / 2`; the rest name the binding constraint and cross-reference. Restating a derivation in four places is how it goes stale in three of them.

**`parsing.md` cites the constant by symbol, not by line.** Its `schema.rs:584` citation was stale *and* wrong, and the planner's replacement (`schema.rs:661`) was already stale by the time T1 landed (`682`). A number that is **computed** is not written down at any line, so a line citation there is a receipt for something that no longer exists — the doc says so in the same breath, so the dropped `file.rs:NNN` form reads as a decision rather than an omission.

**The historical logs are excluded by name, with the reason in the fence itself** — `DECISIONS.md` and [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 22 record what was *built*, this entry included, so rewriting them would falsify the history rather than correct the record (the Increment-4-T3 discipline). `crates/cli/tests/record_nesting_cap.rs` fences the exclusion structurally (the swept and excluded sets are disjoint, and each exclusion carries its why) **without** asserting the historical text: pinning a retired sentence as expected output is how a record sweep turns into a fence protecting the thing it retired.

**The fence is a fact sweep whose needle is generated from the constant.** Seven arms on the `record_item_slot_kind.rs` precedent: the byte-exact falsified statements absent; the retired **number** and the retired **reason** each swept as a *conjunction* with the nesting-cap subject over every line of the four files (so a future pass cannot re-state the fact in fresh words, while naming `H6` as the render ceiling stays legal); the shipped number asserted present as `format!("{MAX_NESTING_DEPTH} nesting levels")` read from `engine::schema::MAX_NESTING_DEPTH`, so the day the address grammar widens, every home that failed to follow the constant reddens instead of quietly going stale — which is the failure mode this task exists to close.

## 2026-08-29 — M49 Increment 5 (T1): the nesting ceiling becomes one derived number, and the projection can no longer advertise an unaddressable address

**`MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` is now computed, not written down** — `(address::MAX_FRAGMENT_HOPS − 1) / 2` = **2**, the deepest nesting level whose *leaf write* still fits the fragment hop budget (`2D + 1` hops, because the chain alternates item id and nested-section id). The loader is **lowered to what the write path already enforced**: no cap is raised and the grammar is not widened. That direction is the whole point — the loader admitted 4, `add-item` reached 3, a leaf write reached 2, and `doc schema` advertised the difference as six real addresses `Address::parse` refuses. Two constants that must agree are now one, so they cannot drift again.

**The comment that hid the drift is the fix's other half.** `address.rs`'s own budget comment modelled *one* hop per nesting level (*"a section hop, up to four item hops, and a leaf"*); it now carries the real two-hops-per-level arithmetic with the diagram, and says which constant is derived from it. `SchemaError::NestingTooDeep` stops naming **the H6 cap** as its reason — `H6` is the *other*, now non-binding, ceiling — and states the binding constraint (the address hop budget), the depth it read, and the number a pack author must meet.

**The two `schema.rs` cap tests are re-derived, not re-typed.** They were the change's forced repairs (they break the instant the constant moves), so they now **generate** their fixture from `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` and check the cap's *tightness against the address grammar itself* — at the cap the deepest leaf address parses, one past it does not. A hand-written five-level fixture asserting the number 4 is exactly how the drift entered; a generated one cannot re-introduce it.

**The acceptance is a manufactured shape space, and that departure is fenced in prose where the set is defined.** The shipped registry's deepest doctype is `changelog` at depth 2, so the existing law-1 round-trip walk in `doc_read_surface.rs` — which iterates the registry — was **green over this hole**. The new arms build a fixture pack whose doctype is generated *to* the cap (every advertised address parses **and** round-trips set → show through the real binary) and one *past* it (refused at pack-load, the refusal naming the depth, the number, and the hop budget rather than `H6`).

## 2026-08-29 — M49 Increment 5 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 5](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the engine capability batch*) into **6 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `2c6876a` (Increments 1–4 landed; tree clean). **Every basis below was driven at this HEAD** — a debug *and* a release build, against a manufactured `JIGC_PACK_DIR` pack carrying a **four-level** nested doctype (`deep`: `l1 → l2 → l3 → l4`, each block a `title` + an optional scalar, its manifest removed so the freeze does not refuse the extra id) over real `git init` repos — so every brick is reproduced, not carried, and the one figure that is not mine is attributed. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 49 Increment 5; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M49/settle-record.md) → *Scope* rows **T1-4** / **T1-5** / **T1-6**; [baseline-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M49/baseline-ledger.md) → Tier 1; [structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md) → Repetition; [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → Slot heading-depth ceiling; [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) → The address grammar; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §2 (*Address grammar*, the law-1 half).

**Why six.** Three limits, and each splits exactly where a gate boundary falls. The ceiling is **one atomic unit** — the constant, the two comments that state its arithmetic, the message that states its reason, and the two `schema.rs` cap tests that break the instant it moves (measured, not assumed: see the basis) — while the four `.md` docs that restate it are the Increment-4-T3 shape, a **fact sweep** landing after the code so it states what shipped. The hop-cap **route** is its own concern at its own producer. `--slug` and the collision **route** are two tasks and the dependency is hard, not stylistic: the route's argv is a `Route::mechanical`, which refuses construction unless it parses against the real CLI, so a route naming `--slug` before the flag exists **panics at construction**. The batch cost is independent of all five and lands last.

**Basis — driven at `2c6876a`.**

- **Three ceilings ship and they are all different.** On the four-level pack: the loader **admits depth 4** (`jigc describe --doctypes` lists `deep`); `add-item` **mints to depth 3** (`deep:probe#l1/one/l2/two/l3` → `…/three`, while the depth-4 mint `#l1/one/l2/two/l3/three/l4` is refused *too many fragment hops*); a **leaf write reaches depth 2** (`set-field deep:probe#l1/one/l2/two/note2` lands; `…/l3/three/note3` is refused the same way). The refusal is the address grammar, never the loader.
- **The arithmetic, and why the caps drifted.** The chain the engine walks (`write::physical_item_chain`) **alternates** item id and nested-section id, so each nesting level costs **two** hops: a leaf write at depth `D` is `1 + (2D−1) + 1 = 2D+1` hops, a mint or retitle at depth `D` is `2D`. Against `MAX_FRAGMENT_HOPS = 6` that is `D ≤ 2` for leaf writes and `D ≤ 3` for mints — the two numbers observed above. `address.rs:167`'s own comment models the budget as *"a section hop, up to four item hops, and a leaf"*, i.e. **one** hop per level, which is how a loader cap of 4 and a write path of 2 sat side by side unnoticed.
- **`doc schema` advertises addresses the write path rejects, and the shipped registry cannot see it.** On the four-level pack the projection emits **six** over-budget addresses — `set-field …#l1/<id>/l2/<id>/l3/<id>/note3` (7 hops), `add-item …/l4` (7), `retitle-item …/l4/<id>` (8), `set-field …/l4/<id>/note4` (9) — every one refused by `Address::parse`. The existing law-1 fence (`crates/cli/tests/doc_read_surface.rs`, *round-trip every address the projection advertises*) is **green over this hole** because it iterates the **shipped registry**, whose deepest member is `changelog` at depth 2. So the acceptance here must be a **manufactured shape space**, the Increment-1 departure, not a registry enumeration.
- **Lowering the loader to the addressable number costs exactly two tests — measured.** With `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` flipped 4 → 2 at this HEAD: `cargo test -p engine` fails **only** `schema::tests::nesting_at_the_h6_cap_loads` and `schema::tests::nesting_deeper_than_h6_is_a_typed_depth_error` (931 passed / 2 failed), and the **entire `cargo test -p cli` suite passes, rc=0** — no golden, no pack-load assert, no acceptance arm depends on the loader admitting depth 3 or 4. The deepest shipped or in-wave doctype is `changelog` at depth 2 (`milestone-record`, `roadmap`, `spec`, `prd` are depth 1; increment 9's three bumps add no nesting). Working tree reverted; the probe left nothing.
- **The hop-cap reject is one message for six faults.** `doc.rs:5116`'s `parse_verb_addr` maps **every** `address::ParseError` variant — `EmptyType` · `MissingColon` · `EmptySlug` · `EmptyFragment` · `EmptyHop` · `TooManyHops` — to the same *"a doc is addressed as `<type>:<slug>`"* sentence and the same `jigc describe` route (all six driven). For the three **head** faults that is true and followable; for the three **fragment** faults the head is already correct and `jigc describe` answers nothing — and for `TooManyHops` the fault is *depth*, which the message never names.
- **`add-item` has no `--slug`, and the collision route is advice you cannot take.** `doc create` and `jigc migrate` both carry `--slug` (verbatim, `engine::slug::is_slug`-validated); `doc add-item` does not. Driven: two genuinely different titles that slug alike are refused `write.already-present` with `route: the target already exists — edit it in place (set-field/set-slot) instead of re-creating it` — a `Route::human` that is (i) wrong for a second, distinct entry, (ii) silent about **which** payload item collided, and (iii) not runnable at all, let alone inside a batch: the whole `doc author` payload is rejected and nothing is staged. The corpus figure — 890 real titles → **884 slugs, 5 collision groups** — is the ledger's T1-6 and is **not** re-measured here; the mechanism is.
- **The batch is superquadratic, and the shape is in the profile.** Release build, one payload, `deep` items with one scalar each: **50 → 0.06 s · 100 → 0.16 · 200 → 0.77 · 400 → 4.97 · 800 → 36.2** (ratio ≈ 6.5–7.3 per doubling ⇒ ≈ n^2.9). Add-items alone are ≈ n²  (100 → 0.047 · 400 → 0.525); the `set:` leaf is what makes it cubic. A `sample(1)` profile of the 800-item run attributes 7006/8907 samples to `cli::doc::apply_leaf`, and under it `apply_field_target` 5716 → `set_item_field_validated` 3490 (`set_item_field_or_insert` 1257 **+** `validate_after` 1255) beside `item_chain_absent` 1285 and `apply_add_item_target` 1899 → `add_item` 1244 — i.e. the chain re-runs a **whole-document `parse_sections` three or four times per leaf** over a buffer that grows with the payload. The 12 `migrate` workflows all author in one payload, so this is the migration surface's cost.

- **T1 — the nesting ceiling becomes one number, derived, and the projection can no longer advertise an address the grammar rejects.** `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` stops being an independent literal and is **derived** from `address::MAX_FRAGMENT_HOPS` by the deepest address the projection can emit (a leaf write at depth `D` = `2D+1` hops ⇒ `(MAX_FRAGMENT_HOPS − 1) / 2` = **2**), so the two constants cannot drift again; `address.rs:167`'s comment is rewritten with the real two-hops-per-level arithmetic; `SchemaError::NestingTooDeep`'s message stops naming *the H6 cap* as its reason (H6 is no longer the binding constraint — the hop budget is) and names the number a pack author must meet; and the two `schema.rs` cap tests are re-derived in the same commit — they are the change's forced repairs and cannot be split from it. **The grammar is not widened and no cap is raised**: the loader is lowered to what the write path already enforced. *Done:* a new **manufactured-shape** arm in `crates/cli/tests/doc_read_surface.rs` (the law-1 half's declared home) builds a fixture pack nested **to the cap** and asserts every address `doc schema --format json` advertises parses via `engine::address::Address::parse` **and** round-trips set → show, plus an arm asserting a pack nested **one level deeper** is refused at pack-load with the depth-naming message — the suite stating in its own module doc that its set is a **manufactured shape space, not a registry enumeration**, and why (the shipped registry's deepest doctype is `changelog` at depth 2, so a registry loop is green over the hole). Red at HEAD. `cargo test -p cli doc_read_surface::` + `cargo test -p engine schema::` green; full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/schema.rs`, `crates/engine/src/address.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/doc_read_surface.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/support/trial_corpus.rs`.)* **No new suite file** — the arm joins the suite that already owns the statement, so no group-root registration is due.
- **T2 — the docs stop stating a cap the tool does not enforce.** The four live homes — [structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md) → Repetition (and its Open-questions echo), [changelog.md](design/changelog.md) (engine work #1 **and** the *"supports up to 4 nesting levels"* line under Open questions), [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → the heading-depth table (whose `schema.rs:584` citation is stale as well as wrong), and [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)'s graduated multi-level-repetition entry — each state the number **and its reason**, re-derived from what T1 shipped: the binding constraint is the **address hop budget**, with H6 named as the *other*, now non-binding, cap. The historical logs (`DECISIONS.md`, `implementation/roadmap.md` → Milestone 22) are **not** rewritten — they record what was built, the Increment-4-T3 discipline. *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli record_nesting_cap::` on the `record_item_slot_kind.rs` precedent — a **fact** sweep, not a phrasing sweep: the retired fact is *repeatable nesting is capped at four levels by H6*, asserted absent from the four record files, with the shipped number read from `engine::schema::MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` (via the lib re-export) and asserted **present** in each, and the historical logs excluded **by name with the reason in the test's own comment**. Red at HEAD. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: the four `.md` above, `crates/cli/tests/record_nesting_cap.rs`, one group root.)* Register the new file in **exactly one** group root (`tests/test_target_registration.rs` fences it).
- **T3 — the address reject names its own fault and routes at the surface that answers it.** `parse_verb_addr` stops flattening six faults into one sentence: the `ParseError` variants are matched **exhaustively** (so a seventh cannot compile without a message and a route), the three **head** faults keep today's `<type>:<slug>` + `jigc describe` shape where it is true, and the three **fragment** faults get the fragment grammar plus `jigc doc schema <type>` — the surface that, after T1, lists only addresses the write path accepts. `TooManyHops` states the **depth budget** derived from the same constants T1 pins, not a generic "malformed". *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli address_parse_error_axis::` driving each of the six variants through a real `doc` verb on the real binary, asserting one distinct message **and** one route per variant, that no fragment fault's route is `jigc describe`, that the `TooManyHops` text names the depth budget, and that the mapping is exhaustive over the enum (a compile-fenced match, asserted by construction in the module doc). Red at HEAD. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/engine/src/address.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/address_parse_error_axis.rs`, one group root.)*
- **T4 — `jigc doc add-item --slug`: an item's id can be decoupled from its title.** The flag `doc create` and `jigc migrate` already carry, on the third minting verb: taken **verbatim**, validated with `engine::slug::is_slug` (malformed rejected, never silently re-slugified), threaded through `engine::write::add_item` / `add_nested_item` and through `apply_add_item_target`'s minted-id ack (which derives the ack address from `slugify(title)` today and must not), so the per-leaf verb reports the id it actually wrote. **Refused when the destination block's `id-from` names an `enum` field** — there the heading *is* the member and the anchor equals it, so an override is an identity change, not a naming choice: the refusal rides `id_from_enum_block`'s existing seam, the `retitle_id_from_refusal` shape. *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli add_item_slug::` driving the real binary: two genuinely different titles that slug alike are both minted (the second with `--slug`), each readable at **its own** address through `doc show --format json` with `id` equal to the override; a nested `add-item --slug` lands at depth 2; a malformed `--slug` is rejected before any bytes move; the enum-`id-from` case (`changelog` `unreleased-changes`) is refused with a route; and `retitle-item` over an override-minted item leaves the anchor frozen. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/add_item_slug.rs`, one group root.)* **Deliberately not in scope:** a `slug:` key on the `doc author` payload item — the roadmap's deliverable is the flag on `add-item`, and T5 makes the batch's own refusal name it as the escape. Increment 12's deferral-ledger pass should record the payload-key question with a trigger.
- **T5 — the collision cell joins the write-verb × miss-shape axis.** `write.already-present` at an **item mint** is the cell M47's matrix never held: the CLI seam enriches it the way `enrich_not_present_route` enriches its sibling (one site — `apply_add_item_target` — so the per-leaf verb **and** the `doc author` batch inherit it together), naming the **colliding minted id**, saying that a batch rejected the whole payload and staged nothing, and carrying a **mechanical** route — `jigc doc add-item <section> --title "<title>" --slug <slug>` — beside the edit-in-place reading, so both intents have an exit. The **doc-level** create collision keeps its own meaning and its own text. *Done:* the new cell is added as a row to `crates/cli/tests/write_miss_shape_axis.rs`'s enumerated axis (its stated shape: *one row per cell, so a verb added later is covered by adding a row*), asserting for the per-verb **and** the batch door that the route is `Route::mechanical`, that its argv parses against the real CLI, that it names `--slug`, and that the message names the minted id; plus an arm running the printed route verbatim and landing the second item.
