It is that increment's approved scope; this note exists so it is met rather than rediscovered.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 Increment 1 (T6): the eighteen-cell shape space, manufactured — and one splice that took a byte it never owned

**The axis is built, not enumerated, and that is a deliberate departure recorded as one.** M45 and M47 established *iterate the code-side registry* as the acceptance pattern, and every suite since has read its members from the shipped model. Here the registry **cannot** supply the axis: across both packs `roadmap.milestones` is the only multi-slot item block and it carries no settable field, and `changelog.releases/changes` the only nested one — so a registry loop would drive two of the eighteen cells and report a swept class. `item_region_shape_space` therefore *generates* one doctype schema per `(slots, nested)` shape and carries it into a real corpus on a `FixturePack`, driving all eighteen cells of `{slotless, single-slot, multi-slot} × {nested, ¬nested} × {insert, update, unset}` through the real binary and asserting **both** faces — the bytes on disk and the pinned `doc show --format json` read-back. **The departure is fenced rather than asserted:** `the_registry_cannot_supply_this_axis` measures the two structural facts the rationale rests on against both packs' loaded schemas, so a pack that grows into the shape space reddens the suite and the prose gets re-read instead of rotting.

**The red is the rc.12 baseline, driven not inferred.** On the installed `1.0.0-rc.12`, six of the eighteen cells fail — the whole multi-slot column: `{multi-slot, ¬nested}` appends a duplicate bullet at exit 0, reads back the stale first value, and refuses the `--unset` with `write.not-present`; `{multi-slot, nested}` rejects the nested `add-item` and then answers `write.wrong-shape` to every write over the skeleton the binary itself emitted. The other twelve pass on rc.12 and pass here — the increment's fix is complete over the axis **and** inert over the shapes that were already right.

**The space found a defect its own repro never reached, and it is a pre-existing one.** The unset cell asserts what a splice-remove owes: insert-then-unset is a **byte round trip** (round-trip clause 2 — only the target's bytes differ; the `--unset` path is *not* the sanctioned item re-render). Three cells failed it — every **nested** shape — at HEAD *and* identically on rc.12. `unset_group_field`'s whole-group drop ended its removal at `list_range.end`, and a `Block::List` range runs past the blank line separating the list from what follows; where the group is the last thing in the region the two coincide, which is why every shipped corpus looked right, and where a nested repeatable follows it inside the item the separator was taken too, gluing the next `#### <heading>` onto the preceding prose. The fix ends the removal at the last bullet's own newline. **The doc-comment above it asserted the two were the same thing** — a recorded rationale that was never checked — and is replaced by one that names the case it was wrong about.

**Two bounds carried in writing rather than pinned.** (i) In the `{slotless, ¬nested}` and `{single-slot, ¬nested}` shapes a `####` heading draws **no** finding, because the item's template reserves nothing at that depth — the schema-keyed answer, and the suite asserts the silence. (ii) But a *slotless* item models no prose at all, so bytes an out-of-band edit puts inside one survive a read and **do not survive** the cold-fill re-render `insert_item_field` performs (driven: a hand-added `#### Stray heading` is gone at exit 0 after the next `set-field`, `jigc validate` silent throughout). That is inside the sanctioned item-bytes exception's declared bound ([parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → *The item-bytes path is the one sanctioned exception*) and its real question is **parse-side** — whether content no leaf models is conformant at all — so it is recorded as owed rather than pinned: a standing test over today's behaviour would pin the loss as expected output.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 Increment 1 (T5): the item-field write paths join validate-after, re-derived over the widened region

**The red was measured, not assumed.** M45 unified the item **slot** paths onto `validate_after`; the item **field** paths were never in its domain — `set_item_field_or_insert` / `set_nested_item_field_or_insert` were called raw from `doc.rs`, with **no re-parse and no confinement clause** at all. T1 then widened an item's own leaf region to span its `#### <Leaf-Title>` prose *and* its trailing field group, and `set_item_field` locates its bullet by a **line scan** over that region. Driven at HEAD against a manufactured `{multi-slot, ¬nested}` pack: with a slot-prose line reading `- status: from prose` (ordinary Markdown, and LLM-owned by the determinism boundary), `jigc doc set-field …/status --value done` **acked at exit 0**, spliced `done` into the *prose*, left the real bullet at `draft`, and the pinned `doc show --format json` returned `"draft"` — contradicting the ack it had just printed — while `jigc task validate` said nothing over the doc. **The guard's response was nothing, because there was no guard.** The same sequence on the installed `1.0.0-rc.12` appends a duplicate bullet instead and never touches the prose, so on a multi-slot item this escape is **newly admitted by the widening**; on a *single-slot* item, whose leaf region was always the whole item, rc.12 escapes into the prose exactly as HEAD does. One guard closes both shapes, so the fix is over the shape axis rather than the cell that reported it.

**Clause (b)'s target is re-derived per path — following [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md)'s write-pipeline table, not the container.** *"On an item path the target is the item region"* was written for the paths that **re-render**, and stays true for them; the item-field surgical splice is the row it had never reached. So: an item with a **present** field group is confined to that **field-group list** — the target of both the bullet splice and the append at its end, and the one target narrower than the item region, which is the only reason the guard has anything to catch; an item with **no** field group takes `insert_item_field`'s cold-fill re-render and is confined to the **item region**; the nested path always re-renders, so it is confined to the item region too. Clause (a) rides every arm, and it has teeth only because **T3 landed first**: a duplicate declared bullet is now a parse-level `conformance.duplicate-field`, so the T1 corruption shape can no longer re-parse clean. The target is derived from the **pre-write** source — read off the edited buffer it would confirm whatever happened.

**The gate is structural for the CLI, a convention inside the engine** — stated rather than overclaimed. All four item-field primitives — the two `*_or_insert` doors and the `set_item_field` / `insert_item_field` halves they dispatch to — drop to `pub(crate)` behind the new `set_item_field_validated`, the item-**slot** precedent where the raw splices went private for the same reason, so no CLI caller can reach one ungated. Two engine-internal callers still reach them directly and are **named rather than glossed**: `crate::transform`'s corpus-migration splices, under their own whole-document fidelity adjudication, and `crate::milestone`'s record writes.

**One truth repair rides along, and one paragraph is rewritten.** `write.target-escape` was recorded at M45 as *unreachable through the real binary without an injected defect* (below, 2026-07-24). **That stopped being true at this commit** — the item-field paths gained a confinement target, and a `set-field` whose located bullet is a slot-prose line escapes it through the real binary — so the unit arm that pinned the claim now says so and names the suite that reaches it. The M45 entry stays as written: it was true when recorded, and this entry is where it is superseded. And `parsing.md`'s validate-after paragraph now states the per-path split as a list instead of a single item-region rule.

**Declared bound:** the guard **rejects** the prose-shadowed write; it does not correct it. Scoping `set_item_field`'s bullet scan to the field-group list would let the write land correctly — a *locator* change, which T1 owns, not a guard change — so an agent whose slot prose shadows a declared key must edit the prose or the field stays put. Blocking a lie beats acking one, and the reject is located, routed and persists nothing; the correction is logged as owed ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → condition-keyed) rather than assumed away.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 Increment 1 (T4): `--unset` of an absent field acks the no-op

Verified at `1.0.0-rc.12` on a **freshly minted, uncorrupted** item: `jigc doc set-field <item>/<field> --unset` answered `blocking · write.not-present — field group for field "note" is not present`, routed at `jigc doc show <doc>#<section> --task <id>`. Following that route verbatim shows the item is right there; re-running reproduces the identical error. **The route does not terminate** — a dead end on a *success* path ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → nothing dead-ends). The cause was never the route: `enrich_not_present_route` rewrites **every** `write.not-present` from a write door to the containing-section read, which is correct for the **item** miss (an id that was never minted) and a dead end for the **field** miss (a present container, no such bullet).

**The call: the field miss is not a miss.** `--unset` asks one question — *is this field present?* — so an eligible field that is already absent is the state the caller asked for, and the door **acks the no-op** (M48's idempotent-`rename` ack is the shipped precedent on the identity verb). The engine gains `UnsetOutcome::{Removed, AlreadyAbsent}`; `AlreadyAbsent` deliberately carries **no buffer**, so no caller can persist bytes for a write that did not happen. Fixed over the **container-depth axis**, not the reported repro — one predicate (`addressed_field_absent`) serves the header scalar, the body field group and the (nested) item alike, because the question it answers is depth-blind. The section arm reproduced the same dead end with a worse lie ("to see the section's current item ids" over a header section that has none). Rank order, both ways: shape → item presence → field declaration → eligibility → **leaf presence**, so an absent *item* still blocks with M44's route and never degrades into a silent no-op.

The ack states which end it reached rather than letting *removed* and *was never there* print identically — `already_absent`, always present, on **both** surfaces (law 1's `create`-`existed` shape applied to removal): an **additive key inside the pre-1.0 window**, declared at [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → *The M49 additive key*, and demanded by M48's standing text/JSON parity fence the moment the text says it. The rule's home is [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `--unset`; [validation.md](design/validation.md)'s statement that `write.not-present` is *an item-id miss* is now made **true** rather than revised.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 Increment 1 (T3): a repeated declared field bullet stops validating clean

The **read-side** half of the item-region class: T1 stopped jigc's own writer from creating the shape, and this catches one that already exists on disk — every corpus a pre-T1 binary wrote, and every hand edit that copies a bullet and forgets to change its key. `read_field_block_str` reported a repeated **undeclared** key once and pushed every repeat of a **declared** one into the parsed field list unchecked (`field_block.rs` has no duplicate handling at all), so three values on a `0..1` enum were conformant to the tool. Driven, before and after: with two `- status:` bullets in one item's field group, `jigc task validate` over an otherwise-clean task **exited 0 with no finding over the doc**, and the pinned `doc show --format json` returned whichever value the first-match lookup reached. The new `conformance.duplicate-field` flips that exit.

**Three calls, each one:** the key is per **`(section/item, key)`** — the granularity `conformance.unknown-field` and the duplicate-`{#id}` guard already use, and the only one `debug_assert_targets_declared` admits, since two lines carrying one key address at one fragment *by construction*; the finding **carries a route**, because `conformance.*` is route-**exempt**, not route-forbidden, and deleting the stray line is a direction rather than a guess — so it takes the shipped hand-repair sanction (M48 Inc 4) **lifted** from the one const its three siblings read (`file_state::OUT_OF_BAND_SANCTION`, now `pub(crate)`), never a fourth wording of it; and the repeat **stays in the parsed set**, because `parse → emit` is byte-exact over the fields it read and dropping a line would make the reader lossy over exactly the doc it is refusing (every consumer resolves a key by first match, so the extra line changes no verdict but this one).

Registered where the inventory lives: `validation.md` → The M49 registration (un-keyed, post-pass-exempt, no new check id — the 34/20/14 tally is unchanged), `command-output-contract.md` → the fourteenth member of the parse-`conformance.*` family, and `parsing.md`'s blocks row, whose case enumeration would otherwise be false the moment this shipped. Landed **before T5**, which needs it to give validate-after's clause (a) teeth: the corrupted doc parses, so a bare re-parse would not have caught it.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 Increment 1 (T2): the parse seam — `{multi-slot ∧ nested}` becomes legal

The same root cause, read side. `parse_items` bounded a nested-bearing item's leaf region at the **first deeper heading** (`first_nested_heading`) and scanned its nested items from the item's `content_start` — so on a template that is **both** multi-slot and nested, the item's own first `#### <Leaf-Title>` sub-label ended the leaf region *and* was then re-read as an anchor-less nested item head. Driven on `1.0.0-rc.12`: a plain top-level `jigc doc add-item` acked at **exit 0** over bytes its own parser rejects — `doc show` answered `store.unparseable`, `task validate` raised two `conformance.item-slot-label-missing` **and** two `conformance.item-heading-unanchored` over the writer's own skeleton, and the nested `add-item` was refused `write.wrong-shape`. So the combination is **fixed, not fenced** ([settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M49/settle-record.md) → D4): a pack-load fence would be inert for exactly the manifest-less adopter packs it would need to bind, and would make three of the eighteen acceptance cells unconstructible.

**The rule is one function, and it gained a conjunct.** T1's boundary predicate moves into the parser as `parse::is_item_slot_sub_label` and both seams call it — the reader asks *where does this item's nested region begin*, the writer asks *where may this item's field group live*, and two implementations of one question is how the class opened. It now also requires the template to be **multi-slot**: a single-slot item renders bare prose under no sub-heading, so exempting its one leaf id would have silently absorbed a heading at a depth `write::slot_ceiling` reserves (its `multi_slot || has_nested` arm). The nested scan starts at `leaf_end` rather than `content_start`; for every template whose leaves render no heading the two coincide, so the shipped nested corpora parse byte-identically.

**The declared bound is discharged as a finding, never a guess.** On a malformed corpus the anchor discriminator is undefined for exactly the documents `conformance.item-heading-unanchored` / `conformance.item-anchor-malformed` exist to report — so the acceptance carries both arms: an **unanchored** deeper heading ends the leaf region and is reported once at its line, with the located message carrying both repairs (the route this route-exempt code ships instead of a verb) while the declared sub-labels around it still parse; a **malformed** anchor is still an anchor, so the heading is a broken nested item rather than a re-read sub-label. `render_item_at`'s doc-comment claimed *"a slot/multi-slot AND nested children in one item is a deferred combination … so the slot and nested paths never coincide here"* — false the moment the reader admits the shape, and the renderer needed no arm for it: it always emitted sub-labels, field group, then children as independent stages. It was the *reader* that banned the shape. The eighteen cells are T6; the prose homes are T7.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 Increment 1 (T1): the item leaf boundary is schema-keyed

`item_own_leaf_region` (`write.rs`) now takes `(schema, section_id, item-chain)` and asks the item's own template where its leaf region ends, at all three write call sites. **The operative rule, as the planning basis settled it:** a **declared slot sub-label of this item's template** does not end the region; anything deeper that is not one does; an `{#id}` anchor is what identifies such a heading as a nested item rather than a defect. The roadmap sentence read literally (an anchored nested item is *not* a boundary) is self-refuting — it would let a parent's leaf region swallow its children's field groups, the corruption the region exists to prevent — so the anchor discriminator points the other way, and the reader's `heading_matches_label` is the writer's sub-label test too (one function, so the two seams cannot disagree). Bug closed: on any ≥2-slot item block, a second `set-field` on one field leaf appended a **second bullet for the same key** at exit 0, `jigc validate` said nothing, and `doc show --format json` returned the stale first value. The shape space is **manufactured, not enumerated** (`settle-record.md` → *Acceptance*): `support::trial_corpus` gains `FixturePack` + `TrialCorpus::build_with_pack`, the declared exception to that module's `JIGC_PACK_DIR`-is-always-removed rule. Parse seam is T2; the eighteen cells are T6.

**Two reds inherited from `a4d8829` were repaired to green the gate, not swept:** the twelve version-bearing compose goldens still read `1.0.0-rc.11` after the rc.12 bump (regenerated; the diff is the version string and nothing else), and `foldback_truth`'s M46 arm still fenced *built, not audited* after M46's audit landed and CLAUDE.md was updated to cite its VERDICT. The second is the fence working, one wave late: it is **flipped, not relaxed** — mirroring the M47 and M48 completions — so the stale pre-audit bound is now the forbidden claim and the cited artifact must exist on disk.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 1](implementation/roadmap.md) (*the item-region class: one root cause, both seams, over the whole shape space*) into **7 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `8a5d73d` (tree clean; no increment landed yet). Every basis below was **driven on the installed `1.0.0-rc.12`** against a manufactured fixture pack, not read out of the settle record. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 49 Increment 1; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M49/settle-record.md) → D3(A) + D4 + *Acceptance*; [planning-gate-record.md](completions/artifacts/M49/planning-gate-record.md) → T0-1; [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md); [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → *a context-dependent rule takes its context as a fence input*; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1.

**Why seven.** The two seams share one predicate but not one observable: the write seam's corrupting cell (**multi-slot ¬nested**) is reachable today, the parse seam's cell (**multi-slot ∧ nested**) is not — the doc cannot be created — so the write fix is provable alone and the parse fix must follow it, never precede it. The remaining four scope bullets are disjoint concerns with their own red steps (a new conformance code · a route repair · a guard's domain · the acceptance axis), and the two doc corrections land last because they restate what the code by then does.

**Basis — driven at `1.0.0-rc.12`, on a fixture pack manufactured for the purpose. Nothing is carried from the roadmap or the settle record unverified.**

- **The manufacturing path works, and it is the acceptance's only possible substrate.** A copy of `crates/cli/pack/` with `config/schema-manifest.yaml` **removed** is freeze-exempt (the six pack-load fences are scoped to constituents that ship a manifest), so a synthetic doctype + a `creates-task: true` workflow carrying `allows-create:` loads through `JIGC_PACK_DIR` and reaches `jigc doc create` / `add-item` / `set-field` / `set-field --unset` end-to-end. Driven: `jigc setup` → `start --workflow` → `doc create` → `add-item` all exit 0 against it. `TrialCorpus` **removes** `JIGC_PACK_DIR` by design (`trial_corpus.rs:296`), so the substrate needs a new, explicit fixture-pack capability — it cannot be reached by the existing helper.
- **The write seam, reproduced to bytes.** On a manufactured `{multi-slot, ¬nested}` doctype (two slot leaves + one optional scalar), two ordinary `jigc doc set-field … --value` writes on the **same** field leaf both ack `set … = <value>` at exit 0 and leave **two bullets** — `- status: draft` / `- status: done`. `jigc task validate` reports **no finding at all** over that doc (only the unrelated empty-slot blocks), and `jigc doc show … --format json` returns exactly one of the two values with no diagnostic. The mechanism, read at the seam: `set_item_field` (`write.rs:1449`) narrows to `item_own_leaf_region` (`:1489`), whose boundary is the first *deeper* heading — for a multi-slot item that is its own `#### Statement` sub-label — so `field_value_in_lines` finds nothing, returns `NotPresent`, and `set_item_field_or_insert` (`:3402`) falls through to `insert_item_field` (`:3300`), whose cold-fill arm re-renders the item from the **parse** (which *does* see the field) and appends the new bullet beside the old.
- **The parse seam, reproduced to a brick.** On a manufactured `{multi-slot, nested}` doctype, `jigc doc add-item …#cases --title "Case A"` **acks `probe2:parse-probe#cases/case` at exit 0** over bytes its own parser rejects: `jigc doc show` then fails `store.unparseable`, and `jigc task validate` raises two `conformance.item-slot-label-missing` **and** two `conformance.item-heading-unanchored`. The nested `add-item` on that item is refused `write.wrong-shape`. Cause: `parse.rs:975` bounds a nested-bearing item's leaf region at `first_nested_heading` (`:638`) — the first heading deeper than the item — which is the item's own first sub-label.
- **The boundary sentence in the roadmap must be read against the code, and one reading is self-refuting.** *"the first deeper heading that is neither a declared slot sub-label of this item template nor an anchored nested item"* — read literally, an anchored nested item is **not** a boundary, so a nested-bearing item's leaf region would swallow its children's field groups, which is precisely the corruption `item_own_leaf_region` was built to prevent (its own doc-comment at `write.rs:2399`: *"the parent's field appended INTO a child's group — the corruption this guards"*), and `parse.rs:975` would return `item_end`, so nested items would never parse at all. A standing test already refuses that reading — `write.rs`'s `top_level_field_write_after_nested_child_lands_in_parent_region` (`:11594`), whose fixture is a release whose nested `#### Added` was authored first. The operative rule is therefore: **a declared slot sub-label of this item's template does not end the region; anything else deeper does, and an `{#id}` anchor is what identifies a deeper heading as a nested item rather than a defect.** The shipped `changelog.releases` block — slotless, nested, with a settable `link` and a `date` — is the live regression witness for it and is named as a done-criterion arm.
- **The repeated bullet has no check at all.** `read_field_block_str` (`parse.rs:795`) reports a repeated *undeclared* key once, and pushes **every** repeat of a *declared* key into the parsed field list unchecked; `field_block.rs` has no duplicate handling. So three values on a `0..1` enum are conformant to the tool.
- **`--unset`'s route does not terminate, and it is wrong on a healthy item too.** Driven on a **freshly-minted, uncorrupted** item: `jigc doc set-field …/note --unset` prints `blocking · write.not-present — field group for field "note" is not present`, routed at `jigc doc show …#cases --task …`. Following it verbatim shows the item exists; re-running the write reproduces the identical error. `enrich_not_present_route` (`doc.rs:899`) rewrites **every** `write.not-present` to the containing-section route — right for the item miss, a dead end for the field miss.
- **The item-*field* write paths carry no validate-after whatsoever.** `set_item_field_or_insert` and `set_nested_item_field_or_insert` are called raw from `doc.rs:755` / `:763` — no re-parse, no confinement clause; `unset_item_field_validated` carries clause (a) only (`reparse_or_reject`, `write.rs:5954`); only the **slot** paths reach `validate_after` (`set_gated_item_slot`, `write.rs:6135`). That gap is why the duplicate bullet committed at exit 0, and it is what the widened region obliges a re-derivation of.
- **The false universal is at `parse.rs:614`, not `:617`, and it has one sibling** — `:259` (*"any `####`+ heading is allowed slot-internal structure"*). `:1371` states the same shape but **parameterized on `reserved_max`**, so it is context-relative and true; the axis is to be derived, not assumed to be all three.
- **The registry cannot supply the axis.** `roadmap.milestones` is the only ≥2-slot item block either pack ships and it has **no settable field** (`packs/methodology/schemas/roadmap.yaml:29-35` — `title` is the id-source, then two slots); `changelog.releases/changes` is the only nested one. The corpus is safe **by accident of shape**, and the shipped registry populates 2 of the 18 cells.
- **The nested field path is not the fix model.** `set_nested_item_field_or_insert` (`write.rs:1833`) re-renders where the top-level splices — refuted at the gate-record as golden-breaking, and not to be adopted here.

- **T1 — the schema-keyed leaf boundary at the three write call sites, proven on a manufactured fixture pack.** `item_own_leaf_region` (`write.rs:2406`) takes the item's template as an input instead of guessing from depth, and the three call sites pass it: `:1347` (`unset_item_field`), `:1489` (`set_item_field`), `:3332` (`insert_item_field`) — all three already hold `schema`, `section_id` and the item chain, so no CLI signature moves. The inputs exist and are reused, not rebuilt: `parse::ItemTemplate::from(chain_repeatable(schema, section_id, chain))` for `slot_ids`/`has_nested`, `heading_matches_label` for the sub-label test, `AnchorRead` for the nested-item test. The fixture-pack capability the red step needs lands here as its first consumer. *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli item_region_boundary::` suite drives the **built binary** against a manufactured `{multi-slot, ¬nested}` pack and asserts (i) two `set-field` writes on one item field leaf leave exactly **one** bullet whose value is the second write's, (ii) `doc show --format json` returns that value, (iii) `task validate` raises no finding over the doc, and (iv) the **regression arm**: on the shipped `changelog`, a `set-field`/`--unset` on a release's `link` does not reach a nested change-group's field group and the bytes round-trip. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/support/trial_corpus.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/item_region_boundary.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/groups/g_item.rs`.)* **Note:** `crates/cli` sets `autotests = false`, so the new suite must be registered in exactly one group root or `tests/test_target_registration.rs` reddens. Any doc-comment inside the touched functions that the widened boundary falsifies is repaired in **this** commit. T1 also delivers the *false* half of the `--unset` scope bullet (the `write.not-present` raised over a corrupted item whose field group is present); the residual half is **T4**.
- **T2 — the parse seam: multi-slot ∧ nested becomes legal.** `first_nested_heading` (`parse.rs:638`) takes the same schema-keyed boundary at its one call site (`:975`), so a multi-slot item's sub-labels stop reading as nested-item starts and `doc add-item` stops acking exit 0 over bytes its own parser rejects. The boundary's behaviour for an **unanchored** and a **malformed-anchor** deeper heading is defined here — the settle record's declared bound is that on a malformed corpus the anchor discriminator is undefined, so it must yield a conformance finding rather than a guess. *Done:* new arms in `item_region_boundary::` — against a manufactured `{multi-slot, nested}` pack, `doc create` + top-level `add-item` yields a doc `jigc doc show` reads at exit 0 with no `conformance.item-slot-label-missing` / `item-heading-unanchored`, a nested `doc add-item` on that item lands, and `doc show --format json` reports the nested item under its parent; plus one arm each for an unanchored and a malformed-anchor deeper heading asserting the conformance finding and its route. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/parse.rs`, `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/item_region_boundary.rs`.)* **Note:** `render_item_at`'s doc-comment (`write.rs:212`) states *"a slot/multi-slot AND nested children in one item is a deferred combination … so the slot and nested paths never coincide here"* — false the moment this lands, and repaired in this commit together with whatever render/`add_item` repair the newly-legal shape forces. The acceptance arms for the whole shape space are **T6**; the declared bound is written into prose by **T7**.
- **T3 — a repeated declared field bullet stops validating clean.** A declared field key appearing more than once in one sentinelled group is a blocking conformance finding, keyed once per `(section/item, key)` — the granularity `conformance.unknown-field` and the duplicate-anchor guard already use, and the one `debug_assert_targets_declared` admits. It carries a route under the route floor; the shipped precedent for a managed at-version doc whose repair is a human edit is M48 Increment 4's hand-repair sanction. *Done:* an engine test asserting exactly one blocking finding with the located `(code, target)` key over a two-bullet field group, plus a CLI arm where `jigc task validate` over such a doc **exits non-zero** and prints the finding with its route. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/parse.rs`, `crates/engine/src/finding.rs`, `design/command-output-contract.md`, `design/validation.md`, `crates/cli/tests/item_region_boundary.rs`.)* **Note:** this is the *read*-side half of the class — T1 stops jigc creating the shape; this catches one that already exists. Land it before T5, which needs it to give clause (a) teeth.
- **T4 — `--unset` of an absent field on a present item stops dead-ending.** The field-miss arm of `write.not-present` gets an answer instead of a route the agent has already satisfied: `enrich_not_present_route` (`doc.rs:899`) rewrites every `write.not-present` to the containing-section route, which is correct for the item miss and a dead end for the field miss. M48's idempotent-`rename` ack (*acks the no-op instead of dressing an empty result as a failure*) is the shipped precedent for the no-op arm. *Done:* a CLI test — `jigc doc set-field <item-field-addr> --unset` on a **present** item whose field is genuinely absent either acks the no-op or blocks with a route that, run verbatim, changes the agent's state; the **item**-miss arm keeps M44's containing-section route unchanged, asserted in the same suite. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/item_region_boundary.rs`.)* **Note:** the other half of this scope bullet — the *false* `write.not-present` over a corrupted item — is delivered by **T1**.
- **T5 — the item-field write paths join validate-after, re-derived over the widened region.** M45 unified the item **slot** paths onto `validate_after`; the item **field** paths were never in its domain, and widening the leaf region widens what those paths may touch ([dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → *widen a guard's trigger, re-derive its response*). Clause (b)'s confinement target on an item path is the **item region**, never the leaf span ([parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md) → *why the item paths re-render rather than splice the leaf*) — a leaf-narrowed target trips `write.target-escape` on every item write. *Done:* the executor's red step must **first demonstrate a write the widened region newly admits and show the guard's current response** — not assume the domain moved — and the task then lands a test in which an item-field write that would persist non-conformant or out-of-target bytes is rejected with the located write finding and nothing partially lands, while every cell T6 will construct re-parses clean. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/item_region_boundary.rs`.)* **Note:** a bare re-parse would not have caught the duplicate bullet — the corrupted doc parses — which is why T3 precedes this task.

Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/tests/item_region_shape_space.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/support/trial_corpus.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/groups/g_item.rs`.)* **Note:** this is a deliberate departure from M45's and M47's registry-enumeration pattern ([settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M49/settle-record.md) → *Acceptance*) and must be written as one; register the file in exactly one group root.
- **T7 — the rule is written where it lives, and the false universal dies over its axis.** [parsing.md](implementation/parsing.md)'s item-region rule states the schema-keyed boundary — *a declared slot sub-label of this item's template does not end the item's leaf region; anything deeper that is not one does, and an `{#id}` anchor is what identifies such a heading as a nested item rather than a defect* — names its four enforcement sites (`write.rs:1347`, `:1489`, `:3332`, `parse.rs:975`), and carries the declared bound verbatim: on a malformed corpus the anchor discriminator is undefined for exactly the documents `conformance.item-heading-unanchored` exists to report, which is acceptable on the write path (jigc's writer always anchors) and yields a finding rather than a guess on the read path. `parse.rs:614`'s *"`####`+ is slot-internal structure"* dies; its **axis is derived**, not assumed — `:259` states the same universal and `:1371` states it parameterized on `reserved_max` and is true, so each sibling is disposed on its own reading. *Done:* the full unscoped gate green, `rg -n 'is slot-internal structure' crates/engine/src/parse.rs` returns **no** unparameterized universal, and `implementation/parsing.md` states the boundary rule, its four sites and the declared bound. *(files: `implementation/parsing.md`, `crates/engine/src/parse.rs`.)* **Note:** [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md)`:85`'s falsified *"no shipped doctype declares a multi-slot repeatable"* is **Increment 11's** approved scope, not this increment's — name it in the commit message so that increment meets it rather than rediscovers it.

**Every Grouped-scope bullet maps, and nothing outside the Deliverable rides.** The shared predicate + its schema inputs → T1 (built) and T2 (applied at the parse site); the repeated-scalar-bullet finding → T3; `--unset`'s false `write.not-present` **and** its non-terminating route → T1 and T4 respectively, each naming the other; M45's item-region validate-after re-derived → T5; the 18-cell acceptance as manufactured fixture packs → T6, with the substrate seeded in T1; the unanchored and malformed-anchor arms with their declared bound → T2 (behaviour), T6 (arms), T7 (prose); `parsing.md`'s item-region rule and `parse.rs`'s false universal → T7. **Ordering constraint carried out of the Settle:** this increment precedes any bump landing a settable field on a ≥2-slot item block — Increment 9's, and `roadmap.status` if it ever returns.

## 2026-09-02 — The audit's own enumerations get the rule the fixers already had, and the concurrency fence fails a third time

**Two halves of one rule, and only one of them existed.** [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) → Fix has said since M46: *"brief the fixer with the finding, never with the finding's boundary — an audit reports the sites it found; the fix is owed over the sites that exist."* That is the **fix** side, it was followed at M49, and it is what found the two unreported data-loss defects. **The report side was missing**: nothing asked an auditor to bound its *own* finding, and step 1's fix-completeness check reads the *wave's* tests, not the auditor's enumerations. Added now — a finding names how its count was derived (the grep and its hit-count, the registry read) or says `instance, unbounded`, and **a finding naming N sites without saying how N was reached is an instance, not a class**. Six-for-six at M49 says the low count is structural, not bad luck: an auditor finds a defect by *hitting* it, and bounding a class is a different act.

**Both halves are now loaded into the agent definitions rather than remembered.** `milestone-code-reviewer` and `milestone-e2e-tester` carry the bounding obligation; `build-fixer` carries the derive-the-axis brief and the concurrency rule. The doc's own words are the reason: *"a rule that lives in prose the actor must remember to read is the same object as a hand-maintained census: it rots at exactly the moment it is needed."* It had rotted — the fixer rule lived only in a doc the orchestrator must re-read, and the three fixer agents named zero of it.

**And the concurrency fence broke a third time, at my hand.** The same doc warns twice, with ⚠, never to run two tree-mutating agents on one working tree; M38 broke it, M42 broke it *"by an orchestrator who had not re-read this doc"*, and **M49's triage ran four fixers concurrently**. Every predicted symptom appeared — a fixer reading a sibling's non-compiling work, ~30 minutes lost to the shared `target/` lock, a gate run against a half-written tree — and it survived only because the fixers **defensively gated in isolation and staged path-explicitly**, verbatim the mitigation the doc says they reach for unprompted. **No new prose was written about it**: the doc already names the tier-1 encode (triage fixes ride `milestone provision`'s per-task worktrees, so two fixers *physically cannot* race one index), and a fourth prose statement of a rule that has failed three times would be the very failure the doc describes. The rule is now in `build-fixer`'s own definition, which is the nearest thing to a fence available without the encode.

**Recorded rather than quietly fixed**, because the orchestrator's failures this session were the same shape as the wave's: reading the audit block that confirmed the expected result and stopping at its edge, and following a doc's rules while missing the one it states twice in bold.

## 2026-09-01 — M49 completion audit: seven findings, seven fixed, and every one a larger class than reported

**Green** ([completions/artifacts/M49/VERDICT.md](completions/artifacts/M49/VERDICT.md)). Re-verified **3155 passed / 0 failed**, clippy + fmt clean; **`1.0.0-rc.13` built and installed after the fixes, not before** — the version-stamp confirmation caught the owed bump unshipped a **fourth** consecutive time.

**The result worth recording is not the count but the pattern: six independent fixers, each told to derive the axis rather than trust the enumeration it was handed, and all six found more** — 6→9 message literals · 5→47 freeze doors · 1→8 `location` concatenation sites · 2→8 untrackable-home movers · one leaked-target branch→nearly every break shape · 1→3 leftover-probe doors. **Two widenings were data loss that appeared in no finding**: `{single-slot, nested}` silently truncated slot prose at exit 0 — the reported cell was a *rejection*, its sibling was *loss* — and **`jigc uninstall` destroyed planted files at exit 0**, because `fanout_worktree_paths` filtered its subject with `path.is_dir()`, a claim about *shape* where the door's question is about *bytes*, leaving a non-directory leftover invisible to M48's destroying-door guard **and** to its loss narration while `remove_dir_all` took it anyway.

**Three root causes are worth carrying past this wave.** `git mv <src> .git/<dst>` **prints `error: invalid path` and exits 0** — it moves the file, drops the source from the index, adds nothing — so the HIGH was never a wrong path but **trusting an exit code that lies**. Two of jigc's own rules disagreed **by one level** (`slot_ceiling` reserves a level; both region seams bounded at *"the first heading deeper than the item"*), so prose at the depth `write.slot-heading-depth` *prescribes* truncated the item's region — following the tool's own advice produced a refusal. And an invariant **stated in a comment and enforced nowhere** (`start.rs:3206`, *"the slash must survive"*) had eight sites concatenating anyway.

**The acceptance suite was green over the centrepiece defect**, because the 18-cell shape space iterated `{slots} × {nested} × {op}` and **not slot position** — the wave's own complete-fix contract, violated by the wave's own acceptance. The fix added slot position and payload shape, with the payload depth **read from `engine::write::slot_ceiling`** rather than written down, on the stated ground that a constant there would re-enact M45's *statement == constant* failure inside the test itself.

**And the orchestrator's own reporting failed once, in the shape this wave is about:** the audit returned two blocks and I read the one that confirmed the result I expected, reporting *"no HIGH"* while `overall_pass` was already `false` and a data-loss HIGH sat in the block beside it. Corrected in the same session, recorded here rather than quietly fixed — *an agent's report is a lead, not a measurement* applies to the orchestrator reading a report as much as to a subagent writing one.

**Cut from the reviewed design and the filled [gate-record](completions/artifacts/M49/planning-gate-record.md)** ([roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 49). **Integrity leads**: the item-region class over its whole shape space, then the doors that lie about state, then the freeze bypass and the pack-typo section-erasure — both **preconditions of PB-1**, which makes project packs real and turns each into an adopter-facing silent-loss path. Then the engine capability the port cannot start without (`AddedItemSlot`), the three adopter-first limits, PB-1 itself, the placement override, the pinned-contract spends, the three single schema bumps, the pack's truth batch, the surface-and-docs batch, and the close.

**Four ordering constraints are hard and stated**: increment 1 before any bump landing a settable field on a ≥2-slot block · increment 3 before increment 6 · increment 4 before increment 9 · the classifier before every non-`EnumWidened` bump. **The acceptance axis is a manufactured shape space, not a registry enumeration** — the shipped registry populates **2 of 18** cells, so an increment looping over it would ship two cells and call the class swept. That is a deliberate departure from M45's and M47's pattern and is written as one.

**The gate-record produced five halts before a line of code was cut** — D10 was un-buildable as drafted (`RemovedField` is refused by design, which the settle record's own corrections table already said), D9's shape deleted its own forcing function, D4's fence was inert for exactly the packs PB-1 ships, the razor could not refuse, and the acceptance axis was not enumerable. Each is recorded with the falsifying datum rather than silently corrected.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 re-scoped as the pre-1.0 completion wave, and the razor is rebuilt to be general

**The order is settled (the human): do the work now → ship 1.0.0 → then port this repo onto jigc.** The port is a *later act*; M49 makes it possible. The charter's contrary reasoning — *"this repo is not self-hosted, so no cheap-now window is being spent"* — was **right about corpus instances and wrong about the pin**: the window that matters is the freeze, not our corpus. `decisions-pending.md`'s *"CLOSED — take neither"* on the frozen methodology bump is **superseded as a basis-has-changed reversal**, not overridden. Scope, evidence and every settled fork: [completions/artifacts/M49/settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M49/settle-record.md), against the driven [baseline-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M49/baseline-ledger.md).

**The port is a discovery mechanism, not a requirements source — so the razor is one razor, general, and its second leg is the load-bearing one:** *demonstrated not asserted · **the fix is right for any adopter, and if the only beneficiary is our layout, naming or process it is refused and we change instead** · timing named · and M46's falsifier kept verbatim (if the razor cannot refuse, the claim is wrong)*. An earlier draft made leg 1 *"the port's own acts touch it"*, which makes our migration the arbiter of the product's shape; that was rejected as backwards. It refuses on the record — the increment tier, `AddedNestedRepeatable`, a delegation primitive, and a placement override argued from our own layout. **PB-1 is admitted by explicit decision rather than by the razor**, recorded as an override rather than bent to fit.

**The baseline corrected the charter in four places and falsified it in one** — P1 (*"two packs describe the same phase incompatibly"*) is **false**: `execute.yaml` is the *increment* tier and `implement-tasks.yaml` the *milestone* tier. P2's missing `robust-advocate` is a **recorded 2026-06-21 decision**, not a gap. The migration seam does **not** land silently (three guards fire). And the depth cap does not block the increment tier.

**The wave's centre is a silent corruption nobody had counted, and a false sentence in a locked doc is why.** An item's own leaf region ends at the first *deeper* heading — but an item's slot sub-labels **are** deeper headings. Two ordinary `set-field` writes on a ≥2-slot item block duplicate the field bullet, **commit at exit 0**, `jigc validate` reports *"validates clean"*, and the pinned 1.0 `doc show --format json` silently returns one of the two values; the parse-side sibling bricks the doc on an exit-0 `add-item`. Driven on **`spec`**, a frozen-v1 *dev-pack* doctype. It has never fired because `roadmap.milestones` is the only shipped 2-slot item block and has no settable field — **the corpus is safe by accident of shape**, and `roadmap.status` is exactly the change that crosses the line. `design/doc-read-surface.md:85` asserts *"no shipped doctype declares a multi-slot repeatable"* — **false since M16** — which is why M47 pinned the *read* side against a synthetic fixture and nobody swept the *write* side.

**The independent design review returned nine blocking findings and every one was accepted — four of them reversing a decision taken the same day.** **The razor could not refuse**: both load-bearing refusals were justified as *"the port does not need it"*, which is port-as-requirements-source operating as an unwritten test, while **PB-1 was recorded as an "override" of a razor that in fact admits it** — a manufactured refusal to be virtuous about. A **leg 0** now writes the necessity test down in product terms (*a one-way door at the pin, or a hole in a declared surface*) and every refusal names its leg. **Multi-slot ∧ nested is fixed, not fenced** — the fence would have been inert for exactly the adopter packs PB-1 ships, falsifying its own not-a-one-way-door ground, and would have made three of the eighteen acceptance cells unconstructible. **`planning-record` reverts to one required slot per gate** — the repeatable shape deleted the `required-slot-present` forcing function that is the doctype's whole purpose, and a record with 3 of 14 gates would have finalized clean. **N2 becomes purely additive** (a top-level integer on `doc show`; `fields` stays uniformly stringy) — the draft's *"unified to number, contract-version 5→6"* was internally contradictory, since `doc schema` already emits a number and is the surface that does not change. And **`completion-record.evidence` stays a scalar** beside a new optional `detail` slot: converting it is `RemovedField`, refused by design, as this record's own corrections table already said. The review also found the settle record disposed ten *forks* and never stated the wave's *scope*; a **Scope section now disposes every baseline row IN / DEFERRED-with-trigger / OUT-with-ground**, with four ordering constraints named and the acceptance corrected — the eighteen-cell axis is a **shape space that must be manufactured**, not a registry to enumerate (the shipped registry populates 2 of 18).

**Settled, ten decisions:** the item-region fix (schema-keyed, never byte-sniffed) and `AddedItemSlot` are IN; `AddedNestedRepeatable` and the **increment tier** are deferred **with written triggers**; multi-slot ∧ nested is **fixed** — the boundary becomes schema-keyed and a nested item is discriminated by its `{#id}` anchor; **PB-1** is in, carrying the listed-pack precedence model and the `--explain` winner defect that is latent for N>2; **we move our own files** to the pack's homes while **`placement.file` becomes cascade-overridable** on the product asymmetry alone (`location:` resolves through `docs-root`, `placement:` through nothing, and `relocate` refuses frozen doctypes); **delegation is prose-only** — a sweep of what `plan-review.yaml` already does at one site, honouring *the orchestration does not fold*; **N1** converges four codes across six doors and **N2 lands additively** as a top-level `schema-version` integer on `doc show`, with the value declared a *machine-maintained typed scalar, not an authored field value*; **`planning-record` ships** with one required slot per gate — the `required-slot-present` block on `finalize` is the forcing function, and the doctype being new makes the freeze free — with the gate set settled at **14** in one home (`milestone-planning-workflow.md:63` lists 13, omitting `quote-attributed`, under a paragraph titled *"Accretion discipline"*); and **`completion-record` 1→2** widens `severity` to HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW and gains an optional `detail` slot.

## 2026-08-28 — M49 chartered as the surface-completion wave, and two one-way doors get a deadline

**Chartered on the 1.0.0 trial's adjudication** ([completions/artifacts/M49/charter.md](completions/artifacts/M49/charter.md); scope keyed in [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)). The trial found **no blocking findings**, so **nothing here blocks the 1.0.0 call** — this is the human's decision to hold v1 to a higher prose-and-routing bar than *"nothing blocks"*, on the ground that prose and routing are what a tool whose whole bet is adapter-ergonomics has to get right.

**The claim is not *fix N prose bugs*, and the difference is the wave.** It is **apply each shipped fence over its axis** — falsifiable, and resting on three independent instances measured at HEAD: the clap-tip seam covers **2 of N error kinds**, and `main.rs` says so in its own words (*"Every other clap error kind still prints clap's own render"*); the route floor binds `Finding`s only, so an anyhow refusal sits outside it **by construction** rather than by oversight; and the packs name `doc show` **34 times** against `doc schema` and `doc list` **zero** — because M48's read-back fence pointed at `doc show` and nowhere else. **The discoverability lens has now landed seven consecutive times across three dedicated surface waves.** A fourth wave of one-off fixes predicts an eighth; applying the seams over their axes is the only version of this wave that could stop it, and if it does not, that is a result worth having.

**Two now-or-never items get a deadline instead of another deferral.** **N1** — a nested-section hop returns **four finding codes across six doors** for one defect, with the `--unset` cell verbatim the sentence a prior commit's own message named as the defect it removed; a stable-key change is cheap pre-1.0 and breaking after. **N2** — `schema-version` is a **number** on `jigc doc schema` and a **string** on `jigc doc show`, two pinned contracts, verified live; the record parked it as *"recorded, not repaired"* precisely because *"a fix wave does not get to make that call by accident"*, while naming its cost (*"comparing the two is exactly the upgrade-path check a driver automates… today that comparison needs a cast"*). Both are **Settle forks, not fixes** — decided in this wave or lost, since after the pin the command-output contract has no version integer and a change means minting a v2.

**F15's structural half is decided OUT rather than left quiet**, so the one-way-door ledger closes: a managed `roadmap-entry → milestone-record` edge is a **feature**, and M48 refused it on three independent grounds — a door on two manifest-frozen doctypes, a per-item `ref` shape **zero shipped doctypes exercise**, and a design decision already settled the other way. **Its prose half is IN**: the justification for the roadmap's prose decomposition (*"repeatable-inside-repeatable is not expressible in the schema model"*) was **falsified at M22**, and the conclusion now survives on entirely different grounds while the stated reason still sits on the page — the exact class this wave is about.

**The razor is M46's, adopted verbatim, including its falsifier**: a rule stated in a locked artifact · violated at HEAD · demonstrable by driving the binary — and *if the razor cannot refuse, the claim is wrong*. Two Tier-2 items fail its first leg today **by their own refusals' terms**, so the rule is the deliverable rather than a formality.

**Preparation only. The decomposition is the next session's**, against a baseline that exercises the binary rather than the charter — every wave since M45 has had charter premises corrected that way, and M48's baseline corrected **19**.

**Built [completions/trial-driver/](completions/trial-driver/)** — apparatus, not roadmap work, and it sits beside the other three trial-tooling homes rather than inside any trial's directory ([CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) → Trial tooling, now four homes). **Why now:** the 1.0.0-gate trial's designed-need instrument returned no data in four sessions of four, and [cue-card-postmortem.md](completions/artifacts/RC-1.0-gate/cue-card-postmortem.md) §2 measured why — an **11–19 second** injection window a human cannot hit. The mechanism is record-once-then-fork: drive turn 1 with `--session-id`, turns 2..n with `--resume`, freeze the CLI's own transcript, and resume it with `--resume … --fork-session` for every measured arm. Nothing is synthesised.

**Increment 0 was run first, alone, and it refuted a bound the plan had written down.** The plan carried `knowledge/17`'s claim that `-p` ignores project allow rules, which would have made `--strict-permissions` misrepresent the adopter's asymmetry rather than merely flatten it. If it cannot reproduce what this repo already settled by hand, the reader is the suspect and nothing it says about a fresh session is readable.

**Two apparatus facts fell out of it, both already compensated for by hand and now reported instead:** `run-session.sh:174`'s counter is labelled `(VERB-ADJACENT, §3.3)` and implements two thirds of it; and **rosewater's registered VERB count of 7 contains two reads that exited 1**. Neither figure was published wrong — the record broke the column out and said so — but both are decisions the *protocol* owns, so the driver carries both numbers and resolves neither.

**Every module was corrected by driving it, and then the review found more than the driving had.** A self-review found one defect; an independent cross-model review found ten, five able to turn apparatus failure into a clean product verdict — a dead CLI scoring as a result because `fork()` printed its exit code and never returned it; a missing transcript becoming `NEITHER`; leading global flags hiding every structured channel at once (`jigc --format json doc show …` is accepted, logged verbatim, and matched nothing); and **every headless run orphaning a container holding the OAuth token** — eleven had accumulated. **Two were claims the code did not keep**, this repo's first-class defect class and both mine: an `Observation.outcome` property that was a second scoring path, which is exactly what `cascade.py`'s docstring says cannot happen; and `gate.py` claiming an uncovered round "is refused" while nothing in a measuring path called it.

Three more carried real defects wrapped in rationale that overstated or missed context already on the record. **The rule this repeats, one layer closer to home than M46 stated it:** an agent's report is a lead, not a measurement — including a reviewer's, and including this session's own exploration subagent, which reported `verify-image.sh` as six checks when it has seven and was nearly believed.

**Honest bound, carried rather than absorbed:** **mid-turn injection is not solved and headless makes it worse** — `-p` runs the arc to completion with no queued-message channel at all, so the 11–19 second window does not widen, it disappears. Automation buys the driving, never the interrupting; the postmortem's answer stands unchanged. And no `drive` verb composes the pieces into one command: which turns, which plants, which answer key and which halt policy are a **trial's data**, and a composition invented before a protocol exists to shape it would be a guess wearing an interface.

And Increment 1's own `state::persist` sweep left `base.json` on truncate-then-fill **one line above** a write it had just converted, in two of the four functions it edited. Neither is a design defect; both are **incomplete sweeps** — the M45 complete-fix lens, turned on M46.

It reproduced the symptom rather than settling for a structural pin: **215 torn reads over 2000 rounds** through the real `mint_milestone` door. F4 as reported was two sites; as fixed it is **three across two crates**.

**The other two fixers each declined an easier answer.** F2's could have parsed the migrated bytes and emitted per-item findings, and refused on a decisive ground — *a repeatable section carrying zero items still has an unfilled leaf*, so a per-item finding is silent for exactly the corpus a doctype author most needs to hear about; it named the address form and routed at the read that lists real ids rather than **fabricating an address to satisfy a format**. F3's found the violated rule was **the code's own comment three lines above it**, and fixed it at the rule — both branches now carry what the run decided — while pinning the exit code from the invocation-log record's own field so a future merge cannot shift it silently.

**Planning corrected itself six times, every one the same shape** — a static read reaching a cleaner conclusion than the binary supports — and **two reached decisions rather than drafts**. The sharpest: **D3 was affirmed and withdrawn the same day**, a decision the human took on the orchestrator's recommendation, resting on a premise checkable in **one command** (`jigc ingest` is register-only, so the unstamped-managed population is refilled continuously by the product's own front door rather than draining to empty). Four waves of release commits carry the same shape (`9cb9b78` rc.11, `e715963` rc.10, `a10e555` rc.9, `7e13e06` rc.8), each landing after its audit.

**`foldback_truth.rs`'s milestone arm is re-aimed, not duplicated — a second time.** It ran in the post-audit direction over `**M48 —` (forbidding the pre-audit bound, requiring `complete` + an existing `VERDICT.md`); it now inverts back to the pre-audit direction over `**M46 —`. Both directions are one rule — *the paragraph may say no more about the audit than the audit found* — and re-aiming keeps **one live pin** in the suite instead of accruing one dead pin per wave (the M48 Increment 12 precedent). The arm was red first for the right reason: the span helper panicked on a `**M46 —` marker that did not exist yet, not on a compile error. The two halves are one unit — neither is green without the other.

**The record repairs are bounded to premises this build verified false, and are three, not a sweep.** [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Increment 3's *"calls the shipped `is_unadopted_foreign` … five call sites and zero here"* and Increment 10's *"the arms with real registries"* are corrected **in place** — they are live rows of the wave being built, and a live row that states a falsehood is the law-1 defect this wave exists to remove — while the dated Increment 3 / T2 entry takes this file's **dated correction bracket**, disposition byte-untouched, because the fix is not in question, only the description of how it couples. That split is the standing convention, not a new call: a record keeps its basis visible beside what falsified it (M47's *"a basis-has-changed rebuttal, not an override"*), a live row is simply made true. *Fence:* `cargo test -p cli foldback_truth::` plus one `rg` sweep — no live doc states a direct `is_unadopted_foreign` call from `migrate_corpus.rs`, and the falsified entry carries its bracket.

## 2026-08-20 — M46 Increment 10 / T1: flow 49 — six arms, and each one says which kind of set it iterates

`crates/cli/tests/flow49_acceptance.rs` (registered in `g_flow`, the one group root) plus the `## 49.` chapter in [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md): the wave's composite done-picture, **ten** `#[test]`s over the real binary — four arms carry a second cell needing its own fixture world, and the chapter states that count from the suite it ships with rather than inheriting flow 48's. The claim the arms carry is the wave's one claim (*every fix reconciles a contradiction the codebase already carries*), and the discipline the plan's declared bound (iii) names is honoured in code and in prose: three arms iterate a **code-side registry** (`DESTROYING_DOORS` read through `DestroyingDoor::code`, `STORE_EXIT_FLIPS`, `GATE_COVERAGE` at `Tier::Previewed`), two iterate the **class's defining case-set** named from the code (`FileStateRecord`'s two `&mut self` mutators — both *called* in the suite, so a rename cannot leave the arm silently narrow — and `HaltReason` matched exhaustively), one iterates a **derivation stated as one**, and **arm 6 states in code and in the chapter that it has no registry and mints none**.

**Arm 2 is scoped to the M46 delta rather than re-driving flow 48, and that is declared, not silent.** M46 Increment 2 already re-aimed `flow48_acceptance`'s arm 1 at the widened axis (`DESTROYING_DOORS` at four members, the `--ignored` narration cell), so re-running the 3×3 `DESTROYING_DOORS × LEFTOVER_VERDICTS` refusal matrix here would be a second copy of a suite this wave had just corrected. Arm 2 instead iterates **all four doors through the `code` discriminator** and asserts the rule Increment 2 / T4 re-derived — *every door answers for what it removes: it refuses what it cannot prove is disposable, **or** it names every byte it destroys, and silence is the one arm no door may take* — with the refusal cells falling on the `Some(code)` members exactly as the decomposition asks. The per-verdict matrix is named in the declared proof split (`provision_leftover_guard.rs`, `uninstall_worktree_guard.rs`, `flow48_acceptance.rs`).

**Two facts the plan did not carry, both found by driving rather than reading.** (1) `STORE_EXIT_FLIPS` is a **precedence** table, and `unmigrated-corpus` outranks `foreign-squatter` — so in a world holding both a below-version managed doc and a foreign squatter the closing line names the *former*. The fifth member can only speak for itself once the managed corpus is current, so arm 3's exit-flip cell moved **after** the migration: `jigc migrate-corpus` lands the control, and the sweep is *still* non-zero and names the squatter's own recorded cause — which is the sharper claim anyway (excluding a foreign file from the migration never becomes a green over a home jigc has never been handed). (2) `jigc migrate-corpus --format json` reports the excluded files under its own **`unadopted[]`** key, not under `findings[]`; the byte-identity comparison reads them there.

**Two members are classified rather than driven, each against a named proof whose existence is asserted** (the `flow48` precedent for `probe-unreliable`, so an unclassified member is a hard panic and never a silent skip): `HaltReason::Parse` is reachable from no shipped doctype pair, and `GATE_COVERAGE`'s `owner-artifact-unstaged` needs the methodology owner-artifact workflow and its own six-cause axis. **Honest bound, carried:** arm 1's concurrent cell spawns all three `jigc` processes before waiting on any, and asserts the outcome — it does not *force* the read-modify-write interleave. The forced interleave, the lock's spin ceiling, the hand-off's non-vacuity and the contrast's applied mutant stay with the suites that own them, and the module doc names each.

Also in this commit: `migrate_corpus_foreign.rs`'s derivation prose stops listing `migrate_corpus.rs` among `is_unadopted_foreign`'s call sites — it has **five**, and `migrate_corpus.rs` reaches the discriminator *through* the `AdoptionInputs` seam, which is the point of the fix rather than an accident of it. ## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 9 / T1: the doctype map states each doctype's shipped `schema-version`

[doctype-map.md](implementation/doctype-map.md) is what the milestone-planning **detect gaps** phase reads to size a doctype change, and at rider **R9**'s discovery it read `adr` as *"✅ frozen v1 (M33)"* while `crates/cli/pack/config/schema-manifest.yaml` had declared **2** since M36 — with nine methodology rows stating no version at all and the scope pin (`:41`) still describing the M40 ten-at-v1 world (*"`schema-snapshots/` starts absent at v1"*, on a disk that carries four snapshots). That is not a typo class: it produced a wrong sizing estimate **inside this wave's own planning**. Every row now states the version its governing manifest declares, with the bump named where there is one (`adr` → v2 at M36's `options` slot · `deferral-ledger` → v2 at M41 F4's `ValueRemapped` · `milestone-record` → v2 at M42's `discarded` member); the pin states the mixed picture and the populated `schema-snapshots/` while keeping its still-true content — *size a methodology schema change against ten, not nine* — intact.

**The fence is the point, not the transcription.** A prose file no test reads drifts silently, and this one had for two milestones. `crates/cli/tests/doctype_map_versions.rs` reads **both** shipped manifests, enumerates every declared entry, and asserts the map's row for each doctype states that entry's current `schema-version` — plus row-set equality both ways, so a doctype cannot join or leave a manifest while the planning aid keeps its old set. Versions are read out of the Status cell in either accepted spelling (`v<N>`, `version <N>`) and **all** stated versions must agree, so a row that keeps a stale number beside a fresh one is as red as a blind one. Red at HEAD on `adr` and the nine version-less rows, exactly as decomposed.

**Keyed per (pack, doctype), and red on divergence.** `commit` is declared in both packs and the map carries **one** row for it; the collapse asserts a single distinct version rather than picking a side, because one row cannot state two — mutation-probed by declaring the methodology `commit` at 3 and confirming all three arms fail with both packs named. The scope-pin arm derives the above-v1 set from the manifests and requires the pin to name each member **with** its version, forbids any clause that both mentions `schema-snapshots/` and calls it absent, and forbids stating one version over the whole ten-schema set while that set is mixed — the last two also mutation-probed, since a guard that has never fired is a guard nobody has checked.

**Scope boundary, named rather than silent.** R9's citation set is `doctype-map.md` `:12`/`:17`/`:25`/`:41`. [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md):52 restates the freeze scope in the same stale terms (*"ten schemas listed, the nine persisted doctypes stamp-injected at schema-version 1"*) and `design/corpus-migration.md`:83 carries the same *"starts absent at v1"* sentence; both are **out** of this increment's approved scope — Increment 10 owns the CLAUDE.md paragraph — so they are named here and in the commit message rather than swept in.


## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 9 / T2: ledger entry 12 is discharged, and its declared bound is struck rather than carried

Entry 12 of the capability ledger ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)) was written at M47 with an honestly **declared bound**: `setup --format json` computed the resolved hooks path but withheld the key, because an additive machine key sat outside that wave's *"changes what surfaces say, never what surfaces exist"* boundary. M48's Increment 7 closed the pre-1.0 additive-key window and shipped it — `hook_file` **and** `hook_committed` — so the bound sentence (*a driver … must read the agent text or re-run `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` itself*) has been false since. Its declared bound is stale and should be struck, not carried"*), and this task executes that: the sentence is **struck, not annotated around**, on the entry-7 precedent — a stale bound left standing is what the next planner sizes work against, which is the failure this increment exists to close.

**Discharged by a driven datum, not a relay.** Re-driven here on the debug binary, not inherited from the plan: a scratch repo at `core.hooksPath=.githooks` → `jigc setup --format json` prints `"hook_file": ".githooks/pre-commit"` with `"hook_committed": true`, exit 0. Both the row's basis cell and the numbered entry now quote that datum **and** the fence that holds the key — `crates/cli/tests/text_json_parity_axis.rs` (the parity axis over `setup`'s envelope, which reddens naming the withheld key if it is deleted) and `crates/cli/tests/setup.rs` (read back through the binary) — so the discharge is re-checkable rather than asserted.

**The ledger gets a fence home.** `crates/cli/tests/ledger_record_truth.rs` asserts the bound sentence at **match count 0** over the whole ledger, that the numbered entry names the datum and the fence, and that the amendment lands in the *basis* cell while the disposition cell stays byte-exact — `ledger_entry_seven_discharged::no_other_entrys_keying_moves` owns the twelve-row keying and stays green untouched. T3 and T4 extend this suite.

The M46 Settle's own opening clause is a promise about [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md): *"Every entry leaves this ledger; none stays deferred on a count."* It fired 2026-08-18 and the promise was unkept — **ten live items still routed their future to it**: numbered capability entries 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10, the two `(D)` blocks that were on its agenda (the demand-counter re-count; the frozen methodology-doctype schema bump), and entry 12 until T2 landed. The `(D)` re-count is **discharged by the table** (its outcome is recorded per entry, so `:14`'s blessed form no longer survives as one standing count), and the schema-bump fork is **CLOSED — take neither**, cross-referenced to *Fork 4* rather than restated.

**The OUT set is named where a planner looks.** The razor's §3 disposed four items by name; three already sat in the Settle's refused-and-re-keyed paragraph, and **S12, the repo publishing floor**, joins them — **discharged by citation**, its live home the entry that already carries the human's 2026-07-16 post-v1 decision and its own trigger. The razor ledger's `:209` line-ref into this file is stale; the citation now names the entry rather than a line number, which is what made it rot.

**The fence is the deliverable's shape, not a summary of it.** `crates/cli/tests/ledger_record_truth.rs` gains one arm enumerating all eighteen items — the twelve numbered entries (each taken **with** its `**Re-counted …**` continuation lines, so a re-key written on the continuation counts and a stale one there reddens), the two `(D)` blocks and the four OUT-set items — asserting of each that its **own text** records its M46 disposition (the table is what a planner scans; the entry is what gets quoted into a scope brief) and that **no forward key it carries names the M46 Settle**. A key is read from its marker to the end of its line, so a re-key cannot be written and then walked back later in the same sentence. The scan is scoped to the capability-wave section: the ledger carries four unrelated `N. **` lists, and an unscoped scan silently fenced the wrong one — caught in the red step, where the arm reported entry 1 as keyless while attributing its trigger to entry 4.
