## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 9 / T4: the M48 adjudication table's falsified rows are re-disposed with the falsifying datum quoted

The M48 adjudication table ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)) is a **dated record**: it says what was decided on 2026-08-13 against the baseline exercised that day. Five of its twelve rows did not survive the M46 razor's driving of the binary — 5, 7, 9 and 11 were admitted **at their stated predicate**, and 10 was re-based off an argument onto measurement — and four of the five were disposed the other way. Left bare the table reads as live guidance, so a planner scanning it finds `stay deferred | untouched` against work that has since shipped, which is the same rot T2 struck entry 12's stale bound for.

**The disposition stays as written; the correction lands beside it.** M47's rule for a call re-taken against its own record is *"a basis-has-changed rebuttal, not an override"* ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-08-09), and this file's own convention for a dated record whose basis has moved is the dated correction bracket (`:998`, `:2376`, `:2771`, `:4706`) — the falsified basis stays visible beside what falsified it. So each of the five keeps its key and its disposition cell **byte-exact**, and its *basis* cell gains a `**[Corrected 2026-08-19 (M46 Increment 9, T4):** …**]**` bracket that quotes the datum and names the M46 row now governing it. Nothing was re-adjudicated here: every quoted datum and every live disposition was read out of the M46 table one screen below.

**The five data, each already driven and recorded.** 5 — the tier reproduced on **three frameworks by three parties**, and the blocking message asserts a symbol *"is absent from"* a file whose **indexed blob** holds it, so *untouched* was false. 7 — the shipped `migrate --as` → `doc author` → `finalize --approve` chain **does** repair a pre-guard corpus, but **only from a fresh clone**; where the corruption happened finalize dies at `reconciliation.conflict-block`, so *motive still largely gone* understated it in the wrong direction. 9 — six concurrent writers lost 3–5 baselines in **5/5** trials at **exit 0**, and a lost baseline silently disables `reconciliation.conflict-block`, which is corruption, not the *contention* the row rested on ([razor-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M46/razor-ledger.md) → N-3). 10 — the `cp -R`/`mv` arms fall to N-2's path-subject fix at **zero stored state** and the fresh-clone arm already refuses at **exit 3**, so the residue is empty on evidence rather than on the advocate's argument. 11 — the exclusion rested on *"for the remainder it narrates"* and a finalize **enumerated one path while destroying two** others unnamed.

**The neighbours are pinned, in both directions.** `crates/cli/tests/ledger_record_truth.rs` gains three arms: the five brackets (each asserted **dated**, saying *falsified*, quoting its datum, and naming both the M46 row key and its disposition); all twelve rows pinned by their first two cells at exactly one occurrence, with the table's row count at twelve, so a correction cannot re-key, re-dispose or drop a neighbour; and the **seven uncorrected rows asserted bare** — a mark meaning *this basis was driven and found false* stops carrying information the moment it decorates rows nobody re-drove. The M48 table is found by its own header (`Basis`, where M46's reads `Basis (exercised unless marked)`), so `ledger_entry_seven_discharged::no_other_entrys_keying_moves` — which keys off the M46 header — stays green untouched, verified in the red step rather than assumed.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 8 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 8](implementation/roadmap.md) (the surface batch) into **8 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `caed1a8` (tree clean; Increments 1–7 landed). Design of record: [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) — law 1 (*nothing lies*), law 2 (*the designated recovery is named by the surfaces that produce that state*), and `:136`'s scope clause (*a statement about a surface is quantified over what that surface actually serves … the repair is **scope**, never a behaviour change* — **and name what the members outside it do instead**); plus [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-08-18 M46 planned (the razor: a rule stated in a locked artifact, violated at HEAD, demonstrable by driving the binary) and → 2026-08-13 the M48 Settle, **`describe`: the filter only, not the positional form** — which bounds T5 to *naming the answer*, never building the single-item lookup. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 46 Increment 8; [razor-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M46/razor-ledger.md) §1 (the seven admitted rows) and §3 (**B2-2's `next:` half** and **the `bind` ack** are the OUT set — neither rides here); [findings-verification.md](completions/artifacts/RC-1.0-gate/findings-verification.md) §2/§3/§4/§6/§8/§9 and S-2; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §3 + its 2026-08-18 addendum, which names **this increment's three citation hazards by name**.

**Why eight.** Seven admitted findings on seven disjoint seams — one renderer clause, one clap `about`, one refusal route, one blanket refusal, one clap-error render, two pack steps — each with its own red step, its own forced repairs and no shared file, so no pair could be folded without one commit answering to two concerns; and the record lands last, once the behaviour it cites exists (the order every increment of this wave has used). Each task is **atomic with the repairs its own change forces**: T3 must keep a byte-exact shipped assertion green, T4 must *revise* the standing assertion that pins the route it changes, and T6/T7 move composed text, so their four byte-constant suites and their goldens are re-blessed **in the same commit** ([pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1).

**Basis — every claim below was read in this tree at `caed1a8`, or driven; nothing is carried from the roadmap or the ledger unverified.**

- **B1-1's clause is per-door and only one door borrows git's word.** The task door's `RejectionFrame.survived` is `task.rs:1594-1597`; `render::commit_rejected` (`render.rs:1419-1428`) frames it. The four siblings were read: `cli.rs:792-795` (rename — names the identity), `milestone.rs:3021-3024`/`:3090-3093` (names each worktree's staged code), `migrate_corpus.rs:295-297` (names the migrated bytes). **No test asserts the "staged changes are still staged" bytes** — a grep across `crates/` returns only `src/task.rs` — and `commit_rejected_axis::drive("jigc task finalize")` stages `code.txt` at `:497-498`, i.e. the **true** branch only. That un-exercised docs-only cell is precisely the `UNPINNED:` reason the conversion ledger records for B1-1.
- **B2-1's predicate is shipped and must not be re-derived.** The refusal is `doc.rs:5187-5206` (`read_staged`), reached from `read_or_copy_in(&self, …)` (`:4893-4922`), which already has `self.workflow_gate()` (`:5021`). The gate arm is `engine::state::create_admission` (`state.rs:1239-1251`) — the same predicate `create.gate-blocked` fires from. `single-task` grants `[adr, changelog]`, `quick-fix` grants `[]`, `sub-task` grants `[adr]`, and **`commit` is in no shipped gate**, so the trial's `commit:<sub>` cell is gate-forbidden under every workflow. `workflow_gate()` is **fallible** (a task with no recorded workflow bails with its own routed error), so the lookup here must be best-effort: on error, today's message stands.
- **B2-1's byte-exact shipped assertion is the admitted cell and must not move.** `anyhow_route_spans::absent_staged_instance_names_the_full_create_form` (`:268-295`) asserts the whole message for `adr:ghost#options` under a task minted from **`single-task`** — which grants `adr` — so the fix leaves it byte-identical or the fix is wrong.
- **B2-2's message is constructed once, and the milestone id is in hand.** `blanket_base_pin_refusal` (`start.rs:1692-1700`) serves both sub-task read doors (`:1765`, `:1867`). `engine::milestone::owning_milestone(jigc_root, id) -> Option<String>` (`engine/src/milestone.rs:752`) **already runs** at `:1765` to decide the unit kind, so the milestone id is free there and one call away at `:1867`.

The `describe` goldens' *"The milestone commit boundary"* comes from the **command catalog** (`crates/cli/pack/config/commands.yaml:129`), not from clap — that hint is terse but carries no internal contradiction and stays **out of scope** (editing it moves six goldens for a finding about one help output).
- **B3b-1's blast radius is counted, not estimated.** The closing text is `crates/cli/pack/steps/route-to-workflow.yaml` (four lines, no front-matter). It ships inside **four whole-output byte constants** — `start_compose.rs:68`, `e2e_audit.rs:939`, `multi_pack_acceptance.rs:101`, `pack_source_determinism.rs:69` — and **18 goldens**. `record-change` is `selectable: false` with a `suppressed:` block whose `expires: never` is correct and **stays**: the razor's citation is `:136`'s second clause (name the scope *and* what sits outside it), never un-hiding the member.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 8 / T1: the hook-rejection frame names the area the task's work actually survives in

The task door's state-truth clause ended *"and your staged changes are still staged"* — one word covering two mechanisms. Driven at HEAD on a **docs-only** task (its whole contribution an in-task ADR, nothing `git add`-ed): the frame prints that sentence while `git diff --cached --name-only` is empty, so a worker who takes the word in git's sense goes looking for a state git cannot show and has to find `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/` for itself (RC-1.0-gate B1-1, confirmed with both branches). Per [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) `:136` the repair is **scope, never behaviour**: the clause now names the two areas separately — *"your task's staged docs are still in `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/`, and anything you had `git add`-ed is still in git's index"* — and nothing about the rollback, the gate or the exit moved.

**Each half is driven, and nothing is asserted about the index that was not.** The refused finalize runs four scoped rollback axes over the index before this text is emitted, so the index state was established live rather than reasoned about: the new `commit_rejected_axis::the_task_door_names_its_own_staged_docs_over_an_empty_git_index` arm — the docs-only cell `drive("jigc task finalize")` never reaches, since its fixture stages `code.txt` — asserts the index is empty **both** going in and at the moment the frame prints, that the emitted clause names the task's staged-doc area and no longer borrows git's word, and that the named area genuinely still holds the staged ADR. The git-index half is the shipped `finalize_message_truth::hook_rejection_says_the_task_is_intact_and_the_rerun_lands`, whose re-run commits exactly the `git add`-ed path and leaves the unstaged edit out. Both shipped assertions (`every_committing_door_frames_its_rejection_names_itself_and_recovers`'s `task <id> is intact`, and `finalize_message_truth`'s) stay green unmodified.

**The scoping is instance-correct, checked rather than assumed: the four sibling clauses each name their own area and none is extended.** `cli.rs` (rename) names the store identity, `milestone.rs` (both commit models) names each provisioned worktree's staged code, and `migrate_corpus.rs` says *"the migrated bytes are written and staged"* — where "staged" **is** git's index and is that door's own mechanism, verified by driving a rejected `jigc migrate-corpus` and reading `docs/decisions/alpha-decision.md` back out of `git diff --cached`. Only the task door held two areas under one word. The three prose restatements of the repaired sentence are corrected in the same commit so no doc keeps the ambiguity alive — [finalize.md](design/finalize.md)'s per-door state-truth list, [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md)'s recovery walk, [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md)'s hook paragraph. Full unscoped gate green.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 8 / T4: the sub-task's base-pin refusal routes where the sub-task's work actually happens

The blanket base-pin refusal offered two exits and **both were wrong for the only case that raises it** (RC-1.0-gate B2-2, driven again at HEAD). `git checkout <pin>` detaches the *shared* checkout onto a base the milestone's own record commits already sit ahead of — under `[dev ▸ methodology]` those commits are what took the sub-task off its pin in the first place, so *seeding* two sub-tasks made both un-resumable. `jigc task discard <sub>` exits **0** and removes the sub-task's working area while the committed record still reads `status: active` and `milestone list-tasks` still lists it: a printed route that contradicts the record it leaves standing ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) law 1). The sub-task arm now names the isolation mechanism the message never named — the worktree at `.jigc/worktrees/<id>`, cut from the very base this checkout has moved off, reached with `jigc milestone provision <m>`.

**One line fits both states, and that is a driven result rather than a convenience.** The refusal is reachable unprovisioned (the trial's state) *and* provisioned, and M48's leftover classifier guards `provision`, so both were driven before the text was written: a second `provision` over a registered worktree reuses it untouched at exit 0, and live work planted inside it survives. The route says exactly that (*"it adds a worktree that is missing and leaves one that exists untouched"*), so it is honest in both states instead of printing one line for a state it did not check — and the test plants the file, so the claim is fenced rather than stated.

**The route is per unit kind, not per door.** The re-entry door takes no membership decision, so a **top-level** task reaches the same refusal — and there both offered exits are right (no record names it, and its own `jigc task discard` really is its teardown), so that arm keeps its bytes. `engine::milestone::owning_milestone` — the same membership test the sub-task finalize refusal is minted from, never a second rule — decides which arm renders, read only on divergence at both doors.

**The standing pin was revised, not doubled** ([pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §3 addendum names this very test as the hazard: it asserts the emitted route, so a correct change meets a red test). `start_resume::sub_task_read_doors_keep_the_blanket_base_pin_refusal` keeps both doors refusing and both provisioning states, and its route assertion now **lifts every `jigc …` span out of the refusal and runs it verbatim from the state that raised it**, then reads the committed record, `milestone list-tasks` and the sub-task's working area back — the old route passes the exit-0 half and fails the record half, which is the defect stated as a test. `anyhow_route_spans::pinned_base_mismatch_routes_to_task_discard` is re-split along the same unit-kind axis and renamed accordingly; the top-level arm keeps the shipped bytes. B2-2's `next:` half stays **refused** ([razor-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M46/razor-ledger.md) §3). Full unscoped gate green.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 8 / T6: the router names what sits outside its catalog

The router's closing text was a **closed list with no exit** (RC-1.0-gate B3b-1, reported independently by two of four sessions, driven again at HEAD): it presents the *selectable* work-workflows and stops, while `record-change` — the workflow whose entire purpose is recording a user-facing change on the changelog — sits outside that set, correctly `selectable: false` with a `suppressed:` reason whose `expires: never` is right. The rationale was readable only *after* you had already found the thing, and the one in-flow surface that ever names it is the F-1 advisory's route, which fires **after** finalize. [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md):136's second clause is the citation: a statement about a surface is quantified over what that surface actually serves, and *the repair is **scope**, never a behaviour change — name the scope, **and name what the members outside it do instead***.

**One addendum to `crates/cli/pack/steps/route-to-workflow.yaml` closes it, and the member stays hidden.** The catalog is named as the selectable subset, a workflow outside it is named as reachable **by name with the same `--workflow` form**, and `jigc describe --workflows` is named as the fuller read that carries each hidden workflow's declared reason. The fix names the *class* and the *read*; it re-lists no suppressed workflow, so `expires: never` keeps meaning what it says — and the new arm asserts `record-change` appears **nowhere** in the router's output, so un-hiding it by prose would redden.

**The emitted read is run, never restated.** `routing_loop::step_6_the_router_closing_text_names_the_fuller_catalog_and_that_read_answers` lifts every backticked span out of the composed router view, takes the single `jigc describe …` span, runs it **verbatim** from the state that printed it, and asserts `record-change` comes back — the one path both trial workers took, now fenced instead of discovered. `step_5_the_live_router_catalog_lists_exactly_the_real_work_workflows` was **verified, not assumed**: its `- <id> — <when>` parse and exact id-set assertion are unaffected by a sentence appended after the re-run line (no added line is an option line), and it stays green.

**The forced repairs ride this commit** ([pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1). The composed text ships inside four whole-output byte constants (`start_compose.rs`, `e2e_audit.rs`, `multi_pack_acceptance.rs`, `pack_source_determinism.rs`) and **18** goldens; the regen moved exactly those 18 router cells — the six `compose/dev/start--router--*` and the twelve composite `start-intent[-json]--*` — and nothing outside the router set. Full unscoped gate green.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 8 / T7: the read-back stops promising a write the step sanctions leaving off

`step:locate-from-spec` printed *"Read your write back … **the write you just made**"* over `jigc doc show spec:<slug> --task <id>` **unconditionally**, while its own prose four paragraphs up sanctions leaving the only spec write in the step off — *"leave `maps-to-test` off a criterion this task did not cover rather than pointing it at a test you have not written and staged"* (RC-1.0-gate B3b-2, driven again at HEAD on both arms: with `maps-to-test` set the read exits 0, with it left off the printed line blocks `store.not-staged`, exit 1, following the step's instructions exactly). The roadmap's binding Note holds — the cause is **misattributed in the scope brief**: the `bind` ack is a preference the razor refuses ([razor-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M46/razor-ledger.md) §3), the pack step is the defect, and no ack changed here.

**The repair is scope, and the refusal underneath stays right** ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md):136). The read-back now names `commit:{{task.id}}` — the write the step solicits **unconditionally**, one line above it — and the paragraph after it names what the member outside that scope does instead: the spec is staged by this task *only* when `maps-to-test` was set, in which case the same `--task` read serves it with the spec's address; when it was left off, nothing of the spec is staged and the task-less `--format json` read the step already prints is the one that serves it. Nothing about staging, the gate or the `maps-to-test` sanction moved — a "fix" that staged the spec regardless would be the behaviour change `:136` forbids, and **arm B pins that**: it asserts the staged spec read really does block `store.not-staged` in the sanctioned state.

**Both arms drive the emitted bytes, never a reconstruction.** `spec_read_back_arms::every_printed_read_answers_whether_or_not_the_optional_spec_write_was_made` mints, binds and re-composes an `implement-from-spec` task twice — arm A wiring a criterion to a real staged test, arm B taking the sanctioned path — runs the step's own emitted `jigc doc set-field` lines (filled only at their agent-fill `<…>` placeholders), then lifts **every** `jigc doc show …` argv the `locate-from-spec` region prints — the standalone line *and* the inline backticked span, unwrapped across its hard wrap — and runs each verbatim, asserting exit 0 in both arms. It also asserts the step keeps stating a staged read-back at all, so the trivially-green repair (delete the promise) reddens.

**The sibling axis was swept and the set is not merely this one, but the live trap is.** Both packs carry **31** read-back sites; three name a doc whose write in that step is sanctioned-optional — `locate-from-spec` (spec), `implement.yaml` (*"If a decision is warranted, create an ADR"*) and `record-changelog.yaml` (*"If the change is user-facing"*), with methodology's `author-decision.yaml` a fourth by wording (*"A task that decided nothing of consequence skips this step"*). Only `locate-from-spec`'s was a **runnable** trap: its read-back sat outside the conditional prose, attributed to a *different*, unconditional write, over an address the agent already holds (the spec it just bound). In the other three the read-back sits inside the conditional block it belongs to, and `implement.yaml`'s argv cannot even be formed without the create that was skipped (`adr:<slug>` has no slug). They are recorded here, not fixed: they are outside the seven admitted rows, and a fix would be prose-scoping over a surface no trial has driven wrong.

**The step stays outside the M48 owe-set, deliberately.** It solicits its writes as literal command lines — no doc-write `{{cli.<id>}}` ref, no `{{schema:<T>}}` — which is the declared bound `pack.rs` names by this step's own name, so it states the read-back voluntarily rather than under the fence; nothing here acquires a ref that would owe `read.staged-read-back` front-matter plus `CONSTRAINT_REQUIRED_TOKENS`' phrases. The regen moved exactly **12** of the **36** golden cells carrying the block — `compose/dev/{start,workflow-preview}--implement-from-spec--*` — leaving the 24 `plan`/`migrate-spec` cells byte-identical, since `author-spec` and `author-migration-spec` write their spec unconditionally and their read-back was never a promise over a sanctioned omission. Full unscoped gate green.

**The pair stops being remembered.** `crates/cli/tests/maps_to_test_caveat_fence.rs` **derives** the owe-set from the shipped trees and asserts each member states the caveat: the checked-field set is every schema field whose *resolved* predicate is `criterion-maps-to-test`, read through the production selector (`engine::target_surface::resolve_check_id` — `field.check ??` the pack-declared type's check), and a step owes the caveat when its body names such a field **and** carries a write signal — a literal `jigc doc <write-verb>` line naming it (the partition is the production `cli::doc::doc_write_verbs`) or a `{{schema:<T>}}` authoring-payload projection of the field's own doctype. Both arms are load-bearing and each is asserted to reach a member the other does not: `locate-from-spec` solicits by literal command and projects no schema; `author-migration-spec` solicits wholly through the projection and carries no write command line at all. **The fence is test-side by decision, and its teeth are proven.** Making it a pack-load fence would mean minting a constraint code and a `states-constraints:` declaration per step — a new surface, which this fixes-only wave's boundary forbids — while the obligation here is derivable from the schema's own `check:` with no declaration to hang it on. The cost of a test-side fence is that it would be green forever after the shipped text is fixed, with nothing showing it can fail; so a **mutation arm on the `read_back_fence.rs` mould** withdraws the caveat from a **copied** step tree, member by member over the derived owe-set, and asserts the fence names that member and only that member, with both withdrawn facts listed. Declared bound, recorded rather than silently narrowed: the tier reads shipped **bytes**, so a step soliciting the write through the projection *without naming the field* carries no structural signal and is outside the derived set — the same bound-by-signal the read-back fence records for its own literal-command case.

Validate's *"`finalize` has no private check path **at this phase**"* is **revised rather than deleted** — T3 made it true again, so the sentence now says what makes it true: one membership (`TaskArea::preview_gates`) reached from **two entry points at their own positions**, and one code-side table (`cli::gate_coverage`) enumerating what every surface says about it, which fences that paragraph's exclusion list among eight sites. Deliberately the second edit to that paragraph in this increment: T3 added a member to a list, T4 changes the claim's basis, and those are different acts.

**The conversion ledger moves in the direction it was built to move.** [findings-verification.md](completions/artifacts/RC-1.0-gate/findings-verification.md) §1 (F-1) and S-4 convert `UNPINNED:` → `pinned-by:`, citing `changelog_write_touch::every_doc_write_verb_reads_as_a_write_touch` + `::every_doc_write_verb_has_a_cell` (the predicate, over the write-verb axis) and `validate_previews_the_gate::{a_granted_but_unused_changelog_gate_is_previewed_at_validate, the_landing_finalize_door_prints_no_dead_argv}` (the doors and the dead argv), each verified by **reading what the cited test asserts** per [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §3. F-1 was `UNPINNED` under §5's *"would pinning it now pin the bug?"*; that rule read from the other end is the conversion rule — the moment the bug is fixed, the cell that would have pinned it is the cell that pins the correct behaviour. The ledger's counts (13 of 17 cited · 4 outright) and its *"shape of the outright rows"* paragraph move with it. Per the increment's pinning rider, neither row cites `changelog_gate_advisory.rs` — it reads apt by name and touches none of these cells — and F-1's block says so out loud.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 6 / T3: the advisory joins the previewed set, and each door names verbs that run at that door

`changelog-recording.gate-granted-unused` ran on the **committing path only**, so `jigc task validate` — the surface every composed step calls *"see what's left before committing"* — was silent about a finding the very next invocation would print, and, once a project spends its one cascade line promoting the key to `blocking`, silent about a state `finalize` was about to **refuse** at exit 3. It is now a member of `preview_gates` ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-08-18 M46 planned, F-E, **Fork 3's narrow arm**: a missing member of the existing rule, not a new rule). The check qualifies on its own stated grounds — its whole subject (the minting workflow's `allows-create`, the staged changelog against its un-authored baseline) exists *before* the commit, it shells out to nothing and mutates nothing, and it is re-run at `finalize` at the same severity. The committing door keeps `GatePreview::Off` and its own computation, at its own position: it is reported twice, never **merged** twice, so finalize's exits, findings and block order are untouched. The **base pin** stays excluded per the M47 Settle, Decision 1.

**The join was a one-row edit, which was T2's whole claim being cashed.** `GATE_COVERAGE` gains `changelog-gate`; the composed `what's-left:` clause regenerated itself, and the fence dragged the member through the other **six** hand-written previewed-tier sites (both packs' `finalize` steps, the `task` tip, the `validate-task` catalog hint, `QUICKSTART.md`, `command-output-contract.md`) by reddening until each named it. The 612-cell golden regeneration moved exactly those three printed cells and nothing else.

**The route becomes the door's** (the `CarryoverBoundary::TaskPreview` mold — one decision, one severity, wording per door because the *facts* differ). The shipped route led with the landed-state form and offered the in-task verbs as *"the before-finalize option (it is live on the `task validate` preview)"* — and that parenthetical was **false**: the advisory did not preview at all, so the only door that ever printed it was the one where `.jigc/tasks/<id>/` had just been deleted, and `jigc doc create changelog --task <id>` copied from there answers ``no task `<id>` `` at exit 1. Three shapes now: the **preview** door leads with the in-task verbs (the working area is open by construction); the **landing** finalize door prints the landed-state form alone; and a **promoted** gate — which refuses the commit and therefore *leaves the task open* — names the in-task verbs plus the one exit a not-user-facing change actually has, since *"no action is needed"* clears no blocking finding. Which shape the committing door takes is resolved through `ValidationReport::new` itself over a throwaway probe finding, never a second copy of the M6 three-step lookup: a route may not disagree with the severity the report will carry.

**Red on the emitted argv, not on the sentence.** `validate_previews_the_gate.rs` extracts every backticked command out of the finding's own `route` on stdout and runs it **verbatim** at the door that printed it: no argv may be answered ``no task``, and a placeholder-free argv must exit 0. That is what made the landing door's dead in-task offer a failing test rather than a reading of the text — and it also caught the honest bound now stated in the suite: `--title <category>` is an enum member the *author* picks (the CLI choosing it would be judgment inside the determinism boundary), so a placeholder-bearing argv is held to the door check alone. `task_lifecycle`'s two no-delta literals were revised **in place** rather than scoped away — the clean render is no longer empty, and the claim that test makes (the M6 post-pass moves no byte) can only be made over what the binary emits. [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → 2. Validate keeps its *"no private check path **at this phase**"* claim and now records what falsified it: the claim was true of the engine sweep and false of the phase, for exactly as long as this advisory ran at one door.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 6 / T2: the coverage enumeration gets one source, and changes not one printed byte

What `jigc task validate` previews — and what only `finalize` decides — was stated on **eight** surfaces, each enumeration written by hand, so a member joining the previewed set joined it eight times or not at all ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-08-18 M46 planned, F-E: *"the exclusion list becomes **generated rather than hand-listed**"*). `cli::gate_coverage::GATE_COVERAGE` (`crates/cli/src/gate_coverage.rs`) is now the single source: eleven rows, each carrying its **member id**, its **door** (previewed, or finalize-only *with the reason it cannot preview* as the enum's payload — so a finalize-only row cannot exist without one), the **tiers** it is stated at, its canonical **surface fragment**, and the **required token**. The composed `what's-left:` clause is **generated** from it (`render.rs`); the other seven sites are **fenced per token** (`crates/cli/tests/gate_coverage_fence.rs`). **Not one printed byte moved** — that is the whole content of this task, and it is asserted rather than claimed: `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` over the golden sweep left `git status --porcelain crates/cli/tests/goldens/` **empty** across all 612 cells.

**Per token, not verbatim, and the record already said why.** [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → the M43 law-3 fence-depth **re-open**: verbatim equality *"bought unrepresentable drift"* the moment one statement varied by context — and these vary legitimately (the `task` tip compresses the carryover gate to *"carryover"*; the `validate-task` catalog hint compresses the whole clause to one line). So the instrument is the M48 named-fact-guard shape (`pack::CONSTRAINT_REQUIRED_TOKENS`), one table over, sharing that fence's **exact** comparison view — `pack::normalized_body` is now `pub(crate)` rather than re-implemented, so a token authored for one table cannot mean something else in the other.

**The exclusion list is stated at two depths, so the table carries two later tiers rather than flattening them.** An agent-facing one-liner names the *phases* that decide the rest (`LaterSummary` — the staged set, promotion, the commit); the two design docs name the *causes* (`LaterCause` — the base pin, the empty-commit guard, `stage-failed`, the untracked `owner-artifact` cause, the commit hook's rejection). A site subscribes to the tiers it enumerates, so neither depth is forced onto a surface it does not belong on, and `promotion` — stated at both, as *"promotion"* in the one-liners and as `promote-clobber` in `finalize.md` — is one row whose token is the stem both spellings share. The base pin stays a finalize-only row per the M47 Settle, Decision 1.

**The fence reads emitted bytes where a surface emits them.** Four of the eight sites come out of the **real binary's** stdout, not the source that produces it: the composed `what's-left:` line **and** the dev pack's `finalize` step body (one `jigc start`), the methodology pack's `finalize` step (a second compose under `JIGC_PACK_DIR`), the `task` tip (a read-shaped `jigc task status`), and the `validate-task` hint (`jigc describe`). The remaining four are documents read as documents, each through a **region** anchored at its own paragraph so a token living elsewhere in the file cannot satisfy it.

**Three reds, none of them a compile error.** (1) The shipped `commands.yaml` hint was mutated to drop *"carryover"* — the fence failed naming the site *and* the member, then the mutation was reverted. (2) A **synthetic previewed row** was added to the table: **all seven** previewed-enumerating sites reddened at once — which is precisely the drag T3 is owed, measured rather than promised. (3) In-tree and permanent, the mutation axis runs **site × owed member** (45 cells): each member's token is cut out of its own site's extracted text and the checker must report exactly that member, so the fence is proven load-bearing at every cell it claims to hold rather than at one witness. A unit test over the checker adds the synthetic-row case at the checker level, and the generated fragment is asserted equal to the sentence that shipped by hand.

**Declared bound, in the module rather than in a reader's head:** the table fences the members every enumerating site must carry; one *additional* phase-specific code beside them (`finalize.render-io` and `promote-clobber` in `finalize.md`, the migration review hold in `command-output-contract.md`) is free prose the fence neither requires nor forbids. And **membership** of the previewed tier stays owned by `preview_gates` — this table states what the surfaces must say about it, which is what makes T3 a one-row edit.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 6 / T1: the advisory stops counting items and starts keying on the write

`changelog-recording.gate-granted-unused` compared the staged changelog's repeatable-**item** count against the committed one, so a task that authored a real entry still drew the advisory whenever the count stood still — rewriting a committed category's `notes`, correcting a release `date`, retitling a cut release (the trial's F-1). That is the check adjudicating the *diff* by proxy, against its own design of record: [validation.md](design/validation.md) → *"It **keys on the gate, never on the diff**."* The predicate is now the **write-touch** the design declares: the staged changelog is compared against its **un-authored baseline**, and any staged write that lands bytes suppresses it. `changelog_entry_count` is retired.

**The baseline is discriminated on the recorded provenance, not on what is on disk.** *"Does the staged doc carry content"* is refuted by the copy-in the shipped suite pins (a `create` over a committed changelog stages a byte-identical copy carrying every committed item, and that cell must keep firing), so the baseline is the bytes the staging primitive materialized at first touch: `Provenance::Created` → the pristine skeleton, rebuilt through the mint's **own** renderer (`engine::state::provisioned_bytes`, split out of `provision_doc`, fed the same `on_create` seeds `jigc doc create` computes — so a skeleton change cannot drift the baseline); otherwise → the committed bytes under the one canonicalization `copy_in` applies. **Provenance, not "a committed file exists"**, because a migration task seeds *blank* over an in-location squatter — reading the squatter as the baseline would suppress the advisory on a create that authored nothing. An unresolvable baseline (a vanished committed source; a pack whose `changelog` is not a fixed-title singleton) keeps the advisory **on**: an unprovable write is not a recorded entry, and the finding is an advisory either way.

**The suite iterates the write surface, not the reported repro.** `crates/cli/tests/changelog_write_touch.rs` keys its cells on the eight `["doc", …]` `VerbKind::Write` members read out of `cli::cli::VERB_KINDS`, and a second fence asserts the table covers that set both ways — so a ninth `doc` write verb cannot ship without stating whether it suppresses. Ten cells over a fixture carrying a **committed** `CHANGELOG.md`: `add-item` · `remove-item` · `retitle-item` · `set-field` · `set-slot` · `author` suppress; `create` over the committed doc and `create` with nothing committed do not; a **refused** `set-field` — which copies the committed doc in and *then* rejects, leaving a staged copy byte-identical to its baseline — does not, an arm proven rather than assumed; and `doc rename` is declared inapplicable with its refusal quoted (`changelog` is a fixed-title singleton). Four cells were red at HEAD — the three F-1 named plus `remove-item`, whose item count moves *down*. Every cell runs before the verdict, so a redness reports the whole axis. Per [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §3 this fix does **not** cite `changelog_gate_advisory.rs`, which pins other arms and touches none of these cells; its shipped arms stayed green, byte-unmodified.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 6 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 6](implementation/roadmap.md) (the changelog gate keys on the gate, and previews what it gates on) into **4 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `f331cea` (tree clean). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-08-18 M46 planned — **F-E, Fork 3 takes the NARROW arm, forced by the record**: the advisory joins `preview_gates` as a missing member of the existing rule, the **base pin stays excluded** per M47 Settle Decision 1, and *"the exclusion list becomes **generated rather than hand-listed** so the enumeration cannot go stale again"* — plus [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The changelog-gate advisory (*"It **keys on the gate, never on the diff**"*), [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → 2. Validate (the *"no private check path **at this phase**"* claim and the hand-written previewed/not-previewed split), and [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → The exit-code taxonomy, third clause (*"position, not scope"*, which carries the same two lists). Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 46 Increment 6; [razor-ledger.md](completions/artifacts/M46/razor-ledger.md) → R8 · R2 · F-E; [gap-findings.md](completions/artifacts/M46/gap-findings.md) → F-E; [findings-verification.md](completions/artifacts/RC-1.0-gate/findings-verification.md) §1 (F-1) and S-4, whose `UNPINNED:` rows this increment converts. **Why four:** the predicate and the door are two properties with two independent red steps (*when the advisory fires* vs *where it is printed*), the coverage enumeration is a third whose entire content is that it changes **nothing** — a byte-identical re-homing of seven hand-written lists onto one code-side source — and it must land **before** the join, because that is the only order in which adding the changelog member is a one-row edit that the fence then drags through every site, rather than an eighth hand-edit that proves the roadmap's point by repeating it; the falsified statements land last, once the behaviour they describe is settled.

**Basis — every claim below was measured against this tree at HEAD `f331cea` or read in it; nothing is carried from the roadmap, the ledger or the trial record.**

- **The join is one line and its inputs are already in scope, and it breaks exactly ONE shipped assertion.** `changelog_gate_advisory(&self.id, schemas)` was added to `preview_gates` (`task.rs:946-985`, which already holds both), the tree built clean, and `cargo test -p cli --no-fail-fast` run: **1880 tests, 1 failed** — `task_lifecycle::no_delta_validate_render_is_byte_identical_to_the_baseline` (`crates/cli/tests/task_lifecycle.rs:322`). `validate_previews_the_gate.rs`, `exit_codes.rs`, `format_json_success_axis.rs`, `text_json_parity_axis.rs`, `route_followability.rs` and every flow suite passed. The experiment was reverted; the tree is clean.
- **That one test moves BOTH its literals, and the second is the visible one.** The first assert panics before reaching it, but `NO_DELTA_CLEAN_VALIDATE_GOLDEN` (`task_lifecycle.rs:47`) is `"no findings — the task validates clean"` over a **conformant `single-task`** — which, having written no changelog, draws the advisory at the new door. So `jigc task validate` stops saying *no findings* on a gate-granting task until the changelog is touched. That is the deliverable, not a side effect, and it is the M6 determinism baseline, so the repair is the two literals, never a relaxed assertion.
- **The advisory has exactly one call site** — `task.rs:1201`, inside `finalize`, after `validate(GatePreview::Off)` — so `task.rs:1896`'s *"(it is live on the `task validate` preview)"* is false as the trial's S-4 says, and the preview door is genuinely new.
- **The predicate's mechanism is constrained, not free.** Suppression must key on a comparison against the doc's **un-authored baseline** (the committed bytes when a changelog is committed; the pristine `create` skeleton when none is). *"Does the staged doc carry content"* is refuted by the copy-in case the shipped suite already pins: `doc create` over a **committed** changelog stages a byte-identical copy that carries every committed item, and `a_created_but_unauthored_changelog_is_not_an_entry` requires that cell to keep firing. A refused write also leaves a staged copy (scope-audit §7, verified there) — byte-identical to the committed file, so the baseline comparison keeps it firing, which is the right answer and is an arm to prove rather than assume.
- **The correct half of the shipped suite is four arms wide and none of them moves.** `changelog_gate_advisory.rs` pins: the granted-and-unused fire (`task:<id>` key, a route, the commit still lands) · the `add-item`-authored silence · the created-but-unauthored fire · the gateless inertness · the promoted-to-blocking gate. Under the write-touch predicate all four verdicts are unchanged — which is the criterion that says the fix did not move the correct half. **Per the pinning rider this suite is not the `pinned-by:` citation for F-1**; it *"touches none of the cells the finding is about"*.
- **The write-verb axis has a real code-side registry.** `cli::cli::VERB_KINDS` (`cli.rs:1372`) bijects the clap leaf tree; its `["doc", …] → VerbKind::Write` members are exactly eight — `create` · `add-item` · `remove-item` · `retitle-item` · `rename` · `set-field` · `set-slot` · `author` — so the acceptance enumerates a registry rather than pinning F-1's repro.
- **The hand-listed enumeration is seven prose sites plus five mirrored literals plus the goldens, and they were counted, not estimated.** Covered-list: `render.rs:304` (the composed `what's-left:` line — every id-carrying compose) · `cli.rs:1571` (the `task` unknown-subcommand tip route) · `crates/cli/pack/config/commands.yaml:37` (the `validate-task` hint `describe` mirrors) · `crates/cli/pack/steps/finalize.yaml:12` · `packs/methodology/steps/finalize.yaml:12` · `QUICKSTART.md:176` · `design/command-output-contract.md:376`. Excluded-list: `design/finalize.md:41` (six items) and `command-output-contract.md:376` (four "unpreviewable in principle" plus "a handful more"). Verbatim mirrors that move with the text: `crates/cli/src/pack.rs:2195`, `crates/engine/src/compose.rs:6797`, `crates/cli/tests/{multi_pack_acceptance,start_compose,config_fill}.rs`, and the compose goldens (M47's own edit of this line moved **342 of 612**).

The doc comment's *"**An entry is an item**"* paragraph goes with the predicate it describes; the *create-and-abandon still fires* rationale it also carries **survives**, because the baseline comparison is what preserves it. Neither door's set of *other* findings moves and no severity changes. *Done:* a new real-binary suite `crates/cli/tests/changelog_write_touch.rs`, registered in exactly one group root (`g_config.rs`, beside the shipped suite; `autotests = false`, `tests/test_target_registration.rs` fences it), **iterating the eight `["doc", …] → VerbKind::Write` members read out of `cli::cli::VERB_KINDS`** rather than the reported repro: each verb driven at the changelog inside a granting task, asserting the rule — *a write that lands bytes suppresses; a refused write, and a `create` that only materializes the copy-in or the skeleton, do not* — with any cell a verb cannot address at the changelog declared inapplicable **with its refusal quoted**, never silently dropped. **Scope coverage, bullet for bullet** ([roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Increment 6): the deliverable's predicate half (*stops counting items, becomes the write-touch*) → **T1** · the deliverable's door half (*joins `preview_gates`*, Fork 3's narrow arm) → **T3** · **R8** → **T1** (behaviour) + **T4** (statement) · **R2** → **T3** (behaviour) + **T4** (statement) · the printed route's in-task arm at a moment when in-task verbs are dead → **T3** · `task.rs:1896`'s false premise → **T3** · `design/finalize.md:41`'s revision → **T4**, with its *list* moved by T3's fence and its *claim* rewritten by T4, deliberately two edits to one paragraph (a member joining a list and a sentence changing its basis are different acts) · the exclusion list becoming **generated rather than hand-listed** → **T2**, exercised by T3 · the pinning rider (`changelog_gate_advisory.rs` is not the citation) → **T1** and **T4**. Nothing is deferred out of the increment. Flow 49 and the full golden regeneration from an emptied root are Increment 10's; the cells T3 moves are regenerated in T3, which is not the same act.

**Declared bounds carried to the executor.** **(1) The narrow arm is the whole arm.** The base pin stays excluded (M47 Settle Decision 1), `plan_finalize` stays fail-fast and is not restructured into a collect-all, and `migrate.review-pending` is not a `Finding` and does not join. Entry 7 of the M46 disposition table (*the item-slot repair verb*) was **retired** at the razor — driving the binary showed a shipped verb chain already repairs a pre-guard corpus, so no repair *verb* was ever the gap — but its basis cell then closed in the future tense: *"What ships is the **route, with two arms**."* A disposition that describes behaviour which has since landed is an open entry a reader must re-derive, and this wave's own claim is that a contradiction gets reconciled where it is written. **The row now records the discharge**: which two clauses shipped (T2 — the migration arm routing at a mechanical `` `jigc unmanage <source>` `` with the cost stated inline, and the general clause gaining `OUT_OF_BAND_SANCTION`), and that the retirement **held**, with T1's standing control named as what holds it (`jigc doc add-item` at the offending address still answers `write.wrong-shape`, exit 1 — so if the verb ever learns to run there the suite reddens and the row is re-taken rather than inherited).

**The roadmap's fork is recorded closed on driven evidence, quoted — a basis-has-changed rebuttal, not an override** (the M47 audit's rule). The deliverable posed *"either the conflict-block route names the migrate entry, or a sanctioned way to drop the stale baseline first"*; arm one is **falsified by the binary** at HEAD `6fa9c84` (the migrate chain is exactly where `reconciliation.conflict-block` fires, at both doors, exit 3 — so naming the migrate entry from inside it is circular), which is why the second arm closed it and needed no new surface. The falsifying datum is quoted **in the row**, not summarized elsewhere: an entry that closes against its own recorded arm has to carry the thing that moved the basis, or the next reader re-opens it.

**Fenced, not asserted in prose.** `crates/cli/tests/ledger_entry_seven_discharged.rs` sweeps the ledger for the retired open-disposition sentence (zero hits), requires entry 7's row to name `jigc unmanage`, both clauses, the T1 control and the falsifying datum, and pins **every other entry's key and disposition byte-exact** over the M46 table — a discharge moves one row and nothing else. The behaviour the row records is driven through the real binary by `crates/cli/tests/pre_guard_repair_route.rs`; this suite asserts only that the ledger says what that suite drives.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 5, validate→fix: the migration-source route stops promising a review it does not get

T2's new exit told the operator that after `jigc unmanage <source>` *"the `--approve` fidelity diff is where that replacement is reviewed."* **It is not.** The fidelity diff renders the **mint-time** source seam — `jigc migrate` persists the foreign bytes into `<task_dir>/source` at mint, and finalize renders *that* against each staged canonical doc — so an edit landing on the file **after** the migration was minted is invisible to the review the route names, and `--approve` then overwrites it at **exit 0**. Reproduced through the real binary: a `POST-MINT` line added after the mint appears nowhere in the exit-4 hold and is gone from disk after `--approve`. The shipped acceptance did not catch it because it plants every external edit *before* `jigc migrate`, which is the one arrangement where the snapshot happens to contain the drift and the promise happens to be true (the fixture-topology mask, [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → hardening #3).

**The route is made true rather than the diff made bigger.** The tail now says what the replacement actually is — the rewrite was authored against the source *as this task recorded it at mint*, so an edit made since is replaced **without** appearing in the `--approve` diff, which renders the recorded source and not what is on disk now — and it **re-names the exit the keyed presentation had dropped**: `` `jigc task discard <the real id>` `` retires the migration and leaves the file untouched. The keyed pair replaces the general pair wholesale (`ConflictBlock::presentation`), so the one exit that preserves the operator's bytes had stopped being offered on exactly the path where the other exit destroys them — surface-contract law 1 on a blocking route whose consequence is silent data loss. Rendering the on-disk bytes as the diff's left side was the other arm and was **not** taken: the diff's subject is the agent's rewrite against the source it was given, and widening it would put a second, contradictory notion of *the source* into the one surface that adjudicates fidelity.

*Done:* `crates/cli/tests/pre_guard_repair_route.rs` gains the post-mint arm — the edit lands **after** `jigc migrate`, the printed `unmanage` argv is run verbatim, the exit-4 hold is asserted to render the recorded seam and **not** the post-mint line (the measurement the wording is held to), and the preserving exit is then lifted out of the route's tail and run verbatim, with the operator's line still on disk afterwards. The engine seam assertion is revised in place. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/file_state.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/pre_guard_repair_route.rs`, `design/reconciliation.md`, `implementation/decisions-pending.md`.)*

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 5 / T2: the conflict route stops ordering an act it never sanctions, and gains the exit that runs from where the user is standing

The shipped repair chain for a pre-guard corruption (`jigc migrate <path> --as <type>` → `doc author` → `finalize --approve`) runs only **from a fresh clone**. In the repo where the hand edit actually happened a `file-state` baseline exists, so the on-disk drift plus the migration's own staged rewrite are `DRIFTED + TOUCHED`: finalize blocks at `reconciliation.conflict-block` (exit 3, at the plain door and under `--approve` alike, verified verbatim at HEAD), and its route offered exactly two exits — `jigc task discard <id>`, which retires the migration, and *"revert the external edit on disk"*, which restores the corruption being repaired **and** is the act `.jigc/AGENT.md`'s routing sentence forbids over a managed doc. A blocking route out of nothing.

**Two clauses of one route, both keyed on what the caller actually holds.** (a) The **migration arm**: a conflict on a migration task's *own recorded source path* routes at a mechanical `` `jigc unmanage <source>` `` with the path substituted, and its tail states the cost inline — the guard is dropped for that path only, the bytes stay on disk, they are **not** merged (this task's staged rewrite replaces them), and — as **corrected in this increment's own validate→fix**, entry above — the rewrite that replaces them was authored against the source *as the task recorded it at mint*, so an edit landing after the mint is replaced without appearing in the `--approve` fidelity diff, and the whole-task discard is named beside the exit as the way to keep the file. (b) The **general clause** gains the sanction its sibling already carried: *the damage was made out-of-band, so it is repaired where it happened*, lifted out of `hand_repair_sanction()` as `OUT_OF_BAND_SANCTION` rather than retyped — M48 Inc 4 / T2's *one source, not two agreeing producers* applied to its own const, now one source and three producers.

**The exit is keyed on the path, deliberately.** A lost baseline does not degrade the reconciliation guarantee, it switches it off ([storage.md](design/storage.md) → What none of this buys), so `jigc unmanage` is only free where the task's staged version is already the intended replacement of exactly that file. The same migration task conflicting on any *other* doc, and every non-migration task, keeps the general route — the widen-a-guard rule applied to a route ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → A route offered on a wider domain must be gated on that domain). Three locked constraints held: `ConflictBlock`'s fields stay private and the classifier still adds nothing of its own (it picks between two **caller-composed** presentations on the one fact it holds, the conflicting path); no placeholder survives on a blocking route; and the general clause stays **single-argv `Mechanical`**, because a two-argv route does not fit the constructor and the constructor is not to be contorted.

**Acceptance drives the emitted bytes.** `crates/cli/tests/pre_guard_repair_route.rs` runs the whole chain from the repo where the corruption happened — over a doc that is a live referrer (`derived-from → prd:gateway-limits`) — lifts the route's argv **out of the printed text** and executes it verbatim, then completes the chain: review hold (exit 4) → `--approve` (exit 0) → `jigc validate` clean → the `derived-from` edge resolving again, since `unmanage` dropped it along with the baseline. The negative control is the scope half: an ordinary task's conflict-block route is byte-equal to the general one, mechanical, placeholder-free, and offers no baseline drop — asserted at the seam (`file_state.rs`, revised in place, never duplicated beside a stale copy) and through the real binary.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 5 / T1: the diagnosis stops naming a verb the state refuses

`conformance.item-heading-unanchored` named `jigc doc add-item` as the *new-item* repair, and that verb cannot run on the doc the finding is about: the unanchored heading is exactly what stops the parse, so `add-item` at the containing section answers an unrelated `write.wrong-shape` ("last item not present"), exit 1 — a law-1 lie on a blocking path (scope audit N-4). **What replaces it is the repair itself rather than a door to it:** the message now shows the anchored heading to write at that line — `` `### <the heading>  {#<id>}` `` with `<id>` a lowercase-kebab slug unique among the section's items — the two-space canonical form the writer itself emits, so the printed bytes are paste-able at the offending coordinate. The slot-prose reading's context-derived demote is untouched. **Both repairs are now hand edits at the named line, and that is the honest shape**: every carrier of this message already sanctions exactly that (`file_state`'s hand-repair sanction on both `reconciliation.conformance-block` arms, `store.unparseable`'s *"fix the committed file so it conforms"*), and `conformance.*` stays route-exempt by declaration — the increment's own *Not in scope*.

**The suite drives the emitted bytes, not a reconstruction.** `crates/cli/tests/pre_guard_repair_route.rs` lifts each repair **out of the message the binary printed** — the demote depth from `` demote it to `####` or deeper ``, the anchored heading from the backticked form — and applies exactly that to the corrupted file; a hand-built `####` or `{#id}` would pass while the emitted repair was wrong. The finding has one producer and three carriers, and the suite asserts all three print the **same** diagnosis (`jigc validate` at store scope · a task door's blocking `reconciliation.conformance-block` on the `DRIFTED + UNTOUCHED` arm · the post-`jigc unmanage` advisory on the `UNKNOWN` arm), so a repair proven at one is proven at all three. Both repairs are then driven to a cleared state: the demote through the shipped chain (`jigc migrate` → `doc author` → review hold → `--approve`) to *"no findings — the committed store validates clean"*, the anchor to `reconciliation.absorb` with the anchored line addressable as a real `criteria` item. The **control** is what keeps the decision from being inherited: `jigc doc add-item` at that address still answers `write.wrong-shape`, so if the verb ever learns to run there the suite reddens and the wording is re-taken.

Cut [Increment 5](implementation/roadmap.md) (the pre-guard repair route, both arms) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `6fa9c84` (tree clean). **The deliverable's open fork is CLOSED on driven evidence, not chosen.** The roadmap poses *"either the conflict-block route names the migrate entry, or a sanctioned way to drop the stale baseline first."* Arm one is **falsified by the binary** (below): with a baseline present the migrate chain **is** where the conflict-block fires, so naming the migrate entry from inside it is circular. Arm two needs **no new surface**: `jigc unmanage <path>` ships, its own `--help` states it *"removes its edges and file-state baseline, leaving the file bytes on disk"*, [storage.md](design/storage.md) already lists it among the sanctioned baseline-absence causes, and it drives the whole chain green. So what ships is a **route**, exactly as ledger entry 7's retirement says — no verb, no flag, no new finding code.

**Basis — every claim below was driven at HEAD `6fa9c84` through the binary built from this tree, or read in the tree; nothing is carried from the roadmap or the ledger.** The fixture is the razor ledger's own pre-guard shape: a `spec`/`prd` built through the tool, committed, then hand-broken with a `###` heading inside item prose and committed again.

- **Both surviving readings have a working repair, and both were driven.** The *slot-prose* reading — demote to `####` — lands through the migrate chain and leaves `jigc validate` clean. The message therefore does not lose an arm; it loses a verb.

**Scope coverage, bullet for bullet** ([roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Increment 5): the deliverable's **arm 1** (baseline present — the conflict-block route names a reachable path) → **T2** · the deliverable's **arm 2** (fresh clone — the shipped chain works and the surface stops mis-naming its repair) → **T1** · grouped-scope bullet 1 (`conformance.item-heading-unanchored`'s own prose stops naming `jigc doc add-item`) → **T1** · grouped-scope bullet 2 (ledger **entry 7 RETIRES**) → **T3** · the stated *Not in scope* (`is_route_exempt`'s `route: null` half, and the measured ceiling of 13 blocking `conformance.*` producers) → deliberately **untouched**, and T1's done-criterion names it so a widening cannot ride in unnoticed. **Declared bounds carried to the executor.** **(1)** The `unmanage` exit is offered **only** on a migration task's own source path, and that narrowness is the point: `unmanage` switches the reconciliation guard off for a path ([storage.md](design/storage.md) → *"A lost baseline therefore does not degrade the guarantee, it switches it off"*), so offering it as a general conflict exit would route users into the hazard **this wave's own Increment 1** exists to close. It is sanctioned here because the on-disk bytes are the task's *declared, reviewed* subject and `--approve` is the review gate. **(2)** `HAND_REPAIR_SANCTION` and the `reconciliation.conformance-block` route family are **not** touched. M48 Inc 4 / T2 settled that split one wave ago and `flow48_acceptance.rs:1642-1652` iterates it (*"adoption advice only where adoption is the answer, migration only where a migration exists, hand-repair only where the file really is the operator's"*); arm 2's route is reachable and effective today, and re-opening a settled split to name a second working path is the improvement the razor refuses. **(3)** T1 changes *which repairs are named*, not *whether the finding routes* — a `conformance.*` finding still carries `route: null` by declaration, and the message remains the repair. **(4)** No new finding code, no new verb, no new flag: if the executor finds itself minting one, the fork above was mis-closed and it is a halt, not a widening.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 4 / T4: the record stops stating the `set:` splice as fact

**R5 + R10 — four statements, one falsified fact.** `corpus-migration.md:131` (the `AddedItemField` per-item semantics) and `:274` (the transform-determinism census row), plus `doctype-authoring.md:35` (the matrix row an author reads *before* a frozen bump) and `:41` (the item-block row), each joined the two mint stories into **one placement claim** — *a leaf carrying `default:` **or** `set:` gets its value placed*. The binary never did that: `is_author_required` exempts a `set:`-derived leaf, so before T1 the arm returned `Unsupported` and the doc collected a route no author could follow, and after T1 it is a **byte no-op the run names**. All four are re-derived on the **one rule the code now holds**: a `default:` places its value; an absence that already conforms — `optional:`, an optional `ref`, a pack type, or a `set:` with no `default:` — is a byte no-op reported as unfilled; required-with-no-value-source stays `ProseNeeding`. `:41` bills itself as a correction of a draft *"wrong for the optional case"*; it was corrected there and left wrong here, so the row now names **both** wrong drafts rather than replacing one with a third.

**The extension point is stated where the design lives, not only in a code comment.** T1 retired nothing about a caller threading a deterministic value in, and that distinction had no home a doctype author reads — which is how a no-op gets misread as a capability loss. `corpus-migration.md` now carries it as its own paragraph (`with_stamp_default` / `authored_remap` hand the value in **as a schema `default:`** and splice through the first arm at both loci; only the nobody-threaded-a-value behaviour changed), and the matrix's new `set:` row says the same in one clause where the bump decision is actually made.

**The matrix gains the ✅/⛔ split the binary holds.** One row became two — `default:` ✅ *the declared value lands* · `set:` with **no** `default:` ✅ *classified, then a byte no-op, named `migrate-corpus.set-field-unfilled`* — and the ⛔ `ProseNeeding` row stops being keyed on *"a required field with no default"*, the phrasing that swept a `set:`-bearing leaf onto the blocking side of a matrix the binary never blocked it on. It is keyed on `validate::is_author_required` instead, the predicate the gate itself asks.

**The sweep is a fact sweep, and it reaches the third home.** `crates/cli/tests/record_set_splice_retired.rs` asserts zero hits for the four falsified byte-forms and exactly one for each replacement — and, taking Increment 3's masking lesson rather than re-learning it, keys arm 2 on the **fact's mechanical shape**: no line may join `` `default:` `` and `` `set:` `` *inside a placement claim*, whatever words carry it. Joining them elsewhere (the projection table, the `PresentationOnly` extent, the tightening refinement, the mint-story checklist) is untouched, because those make no placement claim. That sweep is what pulled in the third home the brief's two-file list omitted: **`SchemaChange::AddedItemField`'s doc-comment** stated the identical retired fact in the file `corpus-migration.md` cross-references, so stopping at the two `.md` files would have left the code contradicting the doc that points at it. `DECISIONS.md` and the roadmap are deliberately **out** of the sweep and the test says so: they are dated append-only logs, and M42's entry recording what M42 built — like this entry quoting the retired bytes — is not a statement of current truth.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 4 / T3: a halted doc is told what actually halted it

`try_migrate_doc` folded **three** causes into one `None` — the transform driver's refusal, a parse failure under the new schema, and the conformance gate's own findings — and the CLI rendered every one of them as `migrate-corpus.prose-needed`: *"`<path>`'s migration mints a new **required** prose slot … author the new required prose, then re-run"*. Driven at HEAD, all three cells printed that **byte-identically**, and two of them are lies: a doc whose *pre-existing* `## Consequences` was empty had nothing minted, and an uncovered enum-member rename is repaired in the **authored old→new map**, not in the doc — a **permanent dead end** followed exactly, the class T1 closes on the transform side. So the halt carries its cause (`engine::transform::HaltReason` — `Transform` · `Parse` · `Gate`) out beside `halted_at`, and the CLI renders it through an **exhaustive** match at both levels: a fourth halt cause, or a transform error the driver learns to raise, cannot be added without deciding what the report says. A **gate** halt keeps `prose-needed` and its route byte-identical (it is the one cause an author clears *from the doc*, which is what the route directs) and **relays the gate's own findings** as its message; every **non-gate** halt takes the new `migrate-corpus.fold-refused` with a **schema-authoring** route — the treatment `unclassified-change` / `narrowed-cardinality` / `removed-field` already get pre-fold, on the file's own recorded reason that the fold's halt route *"would be a lie"*. Both rows are declared in [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → the `migrate-corpus.*` sub-table **in the same commit** as the code that emits them.

**Two elaborations, recorded because they are choices and not transcription.** **(1) The minted cell relays too.** The decomposition asked for a message *"derived from the gate's own findings (relay, never re-word)"* **and** for the genuinely-minted cell to stay *"byte-identical to today"* — no relay can reproduce a sentence that asserts a mint, so the two clauses cannot both hold on the message. Declared bound (4) settles it (*"T3 relays the gate's findings; it must not re-word them — the two surfaces disagreeing about one break is the class this wave exists to close"*): the relay applies to **both** gate cells, and what is byte-identical for the minted one is its **code and its route** — asserted as such in `crates/cli/tests/migrate_corpus_halt_causes.rs`. The minted and un-minted cells therefore read the same, which is the honest outcome: the gate saw one break and says so once. **(2) The value-remap route keys on a named constant.** `engine::transform::VALUE_REMAP_KIND` is spent at the one construction site and matched at the one route site, so the only refusal whose repair is a *migration input* rather than an arm cannot drift off the wire name it claims to match.

**The suite says what it does not reach.** `HaltReason::Parse` is unreachable through any shipped doctype pair (it needs a source the *new* schema cannot parse at all), so it is proven at the engine seam and `proof_of` — an exhaustive match over the variants — names the engine test rather than implying a real-binary cell exists for it.

**Carried, not taken:** the sub-table's *"the seven migration refusals"* count was already falsified before this commit (`schema-version-ahead` and `set-field-unfilled` ship un-counted) and this adds an eighth row. The planner recorded that arithmetic as Increment 9's or the human's; it is not self-authorized here.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 4 / T2: the migration report names the `set:` fields it left unfilled

The loudness rider T1 owed, and the reason it is a **reconciliation** rather than a loosening: after T1 a `set:`-derived leaf with no `default:` folds to **zero bytes** instead of blocking the doc — correct, because the conformance gate never asks for it, and **silent**, because the doc conforms without it. A doctype author who adds a `set:`-bearing field expecting the corpus to carry a value would read `1 migrated` and nothing else. So the run *names* what it left undone: one **advisory** per unfilled leaf, on the text surface (a headline count + an `unfilled <path>#<section>/<field>` line with the code and the route) and in the `--format json` envelope.

**One shared derivation, in the engine, never a fourth private one.** `engine::schema_diff::unfilled_set_leaves` takes the **new schema and the doc's own change list** and returns the added leaves — at **both** loci — whose declaration carries `set:` with no `default:`. It is fed `prep.to`, the **stamp-defaulted** clone the fold actually used, which is what makes the extension point T1 left untouched *also* the exclusion rule here: the CLI hands a deriver's value in **as a `default:`**, so the schema-version stamp is excluded by construction rather than by a second list of exceptions. Fed the raw pack shape it would report the stamp it had just written, on every v0 doc in every corpus — pinned by its own arm (`the_stamp_the_cli_threads_a_value_into_is_never_reported_unfilled`, mutation-checked: dropping the `default.is_none()` clause reddens it).

**It rides a new serialized `Findings` field, never `blocked`.** `blocked`'s emptiness *is* the exit rule (`migrate_corpus.rs` → `run`), and these docs **migrated** — folding them in would turn a report into a refusal and re-open the loop M42 closed, since no author can write a `set:` field and no re-run can clear it. Target `<path>#<section>/<field>` (the family's file-path form plus the leaf fragment) so two unfilled leaves in one doc discriminate; the route splits on the **one** authority `engine::schema::is_machine_maintained_absolute` — **informational** for an absolute nothing may write, **human** at the write path for an author-overridable `on-create`, and **mechanical for neither**, because a `jigc doc set-field` argv needs a task id the report does not hold. The new code and the additive key are **declared as they ship**, in this commit: a row in `command-output-contract.md`'s `migrate-corpus.*` sub-table (marked as the family's one non-refusal member, with the target/route/threaded-value decisions) and its own paragraph under *Evolution posture*, beside Increment 3's `unadopted`.

**Acceptance** extends `crates/cli/tests/migrate_corpus_set_fields.rs` through the shipped binary: the `adr` **simple-locus** arm (the `--format json` envelope's sole `unfilled[]` member keyed `docs/decisions/alpha.md#status/date`, severity `advisory`, a route at the write path — plus the text line, the code, the route line and the `1 left unfilled` headline), the `changelog` **item-locus** arm (`CHANGELOG.md#releases/date`, the release byte-identical but for the stamp), and **two controls**: a migration whose added leaf carries no `set:` at all (the optional `supersedes` ref — the word absent from the text entirely, `unfilled: []` present-always in the envelope) and the stamp arm above. `blocked` empty and exit **0** on every arm.

## 2026-08-19 — M46 Increment 4 / T1: one predicate governs classification and placement, and a conforming absence folds to a byte no-op

`placeable_without_prose` (`schema_diff.rs`) is retired as the **third private re-derivation** of the author-required rule: both added-leaf classifiers now ask `!engine::validate::is_author_required` — the predicate `corpus-migration.md` → The structural projection already **claims** is shared, and which the *tightening* path in the same file already calls — and the `None`-default arms of `apply_added_field` / `apply_added_item_field` key on that **same** predicate. Classification and placement therefore cannot disagree, which is the whole mechanism: the driver only ever sees a kind the gate agrees is placeable.

**The class is four members, not the two the ledger enumerated.** `placeable_without_prose` was `optional || default || set` while `is_author_required` *additionally* exempts an **optional `ref`** and a **pack-declared type**, so `adr`'s `supersedes` and `cites-code` classified `ProseNeeding` and blocked identically to the `set:` case — driven at HEAD, all four. The route those docs collected — *author the new required prose … then re-run* — is a **permanent** dead end for every one of them: `schema_conformance`'s two absent-field arms both gate on `is_author_required`, so the absence produces **zero** findings, no author can write the field, and re-running changes nothing. A migration that refuses what already conforms is the failure; the no-op is the correct fold.

**The extension point is not retired, and the code now says so at all three loci.** The CLI threading a deterministic value in — `with_stamp_default`, `authored_remap` — is untouched: it arrives as a schema `default:` and still splices through the `Some` arm, so the schema-version stamp lands exactly as before. What changed is **only** the behaviour when nobody threads one in. Acceptance iterates the added-leaf axis (`set:`-without-default · optional-ref · pack-typed) at **both** loci at the engine seam — byte no-op and `migrate_corpus` `halted_at == None` — with the `default:`-splices and required-with-no-value-source controls unchanged, plus `crates/cli/tests/migrate_corpus_set_fields.rs` driving the shipped binary over a dev-pack copy (`adr` 2 → 3 adding back its `set: on-create` `date`): red at HEAD as `0 migrated, 0 already current, 1 blocked` / exit 1 / `migrate-corpus.prose-needed`, green as `1 migrated` / exit 0 / the doc byte-identical but for the stamp, `date:` still absent.
