## 2026-08-13 — M48 Increment 2, T2: the write path stops acking success over a title it dropped

`jigc doc create` and `jigc doc author` share **one pre-check** (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs` → `title_pre_check` / `fixed_title_refusal` / `identity_divergence_refusal` / `title_ignored_refusal`), run **before either persists**, so a refused write stages nothing and has nothing to roll back. Design of record: **F2** (DECISIONS → 2026-08-13 the Settle); [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → The four-way write over a committed doc is revised with it, and [validation.md](design/validation.md)'s `write.*` construction-site enumeration gains the new member. Five elaborations worth pinning:

- **The code split is settled the way the task framed it as an assumption to prove, and the assumption held.** The **identity-divergence** shape converges on the shipped `write.identity-change` — the gate entry's `as:` role already binds `<type>:<slug>` and the call would mint another one. The **silent no-op** shape does **not**: the id never moves, and [storage.md](design/storage.md):66 calls an ordinary retitle identity-**stable**, so `write.identity-change` firing there would be a law-1 lie. It mints **`write.title-ignored`**, whose sentence — *the title you supplied will not become this doc's `# H1`* — is true of every cell it fires on. The two keys discriminate: divergence keys the **bound** identity, the no-op keys the **incumbent**.
- **The fixed-title arm is the no-op shape one rank higher, and it is the one arm that does not route at `doc rename`** — which refuses a singleton outright, so routing there would be a dead end. `create` routes at **itself** under the schema's title (mechanical, argv-complete); `author` routes at the payload line to correct (Human — a mechanical re-run of an unedited payload file would promise a fix it cannot deliver). The predicate is **one home**, the new `Schema::fixed_title`, which the mint, the `{{schema:}}` skeleton's `projection_title_value`, the payload's title-less default, and the guard all read — so the fence cannot drift from the byte the mint writes.
- **Admission outranks the title, and it needed an extraction to do so.** `state::create_admission` (unknown doctype → the gate) is lifted out of `create_gated` and called by the pre-check first: a title complaint about a doctype the workflow cannot create at all is a misdirection. `state::create_incumbent` is the second extraction — it answers *what body would this create find* through `create`'s own predicates, **including the in-location-squatter exception**, because a bare `canonical_path` probe would report an incumbent for the one case where the create seeds blank and the title genuinely lands.
- **The reader and the writer of the `# H1` are now one scan.** `rename::rewrite_h1` is re-expressed as `h1_span` + a splice, and `read_h1` is that same span — so the guard compares the supplied title against exactly the bytes `doc rename` would change. Its four shipped unit tests are the equivalence proof.
- **It is a declared behaviour change for a hand-driven second mint, and the reject says so** rather than ambushing: the tail names *"a genuinely separate second document is its own task"*. The blast radius bore that out — **three** shipped suites minted a second doc of one doctype in one task, and each was repaired on its own terms (`write_finding_keys`'s sibling ADR moved to its **own task**, which is what the reject's message names; `arch_doc_acceptance`'s re-author carries the **same** title, since its claim is element-wise `cites` validation; `slug_override`'s re-create carries the same title, since its claim is the `existed` ack).

**The pack itself was lying, which is the finding under the fix.** `packs/methodology/config/commands.yaml` composed `--title Deferral-Ledger` / `--title Decisions-Log` into every planning/completion spine — divergent from the `display-title`s, i.e. the pack instructing the agent to make exactly the miss this guard now blocks. Corrected to `Deferral Ledger` / `Decisions Log`, which makes those the first composed `Run:` lines carrying a **shell-quoted** argument; `methodology_pack_compose.rs` now executes the ledger line **verbatim** (shell-split, not whitespace-split), because a whitespace-split reconstruction would pass while the line an agent pastes broke. Sixteen fixture titles across twelve suites were divergent the same way and are corrected; two suites had *pinned the drop as the fact* (`methodology_running_doctypes`'s "Decoy Title", `singleton_running_doc`'s "Ignored Title") and are **revised on their rationale** — the decoy is now asserted **refused**, which pins the same fact harder than watching it be swallowed. Three doctype sweeps ask `support::create_title` rather than passing one label to every doctype, so a singleton added to either pack joins them.

**Acceptance:** `crates/cli/tests/write_title_divergence.rs` (registered in `g_doc`) drives the real binary — the three reproduced cells, each blocking non-zero with its own `(code, key.target)`, the task's staged doc set **byte-identical and unchanged in membership** across the reject, and the emitted route lifted from the `--format json` finding and **run verbatim** to exit 0; the singleton arm iterates the **loaded schema registry** through the same `fixed_title` predicate and pairs each doctype with an admitting workflow read from the **loaded workflow registry**; and four counter-arms keep the guard from becoming its own defect. The cells join `write_miss_shape_axis.rs` as a **title-miss column** — the matrix's first non-address miss — whose mutating route is run verbatim against a private fixture.

## 2026-08-13 — M48 Increment 2, T1: the in-task title change exists, and the census is the acceptance

**`jigc doc rename <addr> --to "<New Title>" [--slug <s>] [--task <id>]`** ships as a distinct `doc` leaf (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs` → `run_doc_rename` / `fixed_identity_refusal` / `committed_reslug_refusal` / `move_staged_identity`), splitting on committed-store identity. Design of record: **F2** and its committed-store-identity re-settle (DECISIONS → 2026-08-13 the Settle); [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc doc rename` and [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Identity are revised with it. Five elaborations worth pinning:

- **The discriminator is the *persisted* provenance, not a fresh `canonical_path` probe** — and the difference is a live dead-end route, not a preference. `docs/provenance.json` records the outcome of `state::create`'s own copy-in predicate at stage time, **including its in-location-squatter exception**: a migration whose recorded `source-path` IS the doctype's canonical destination stages `created` over a *foreign* file. A bare `canonical_path(..).is_file()` reads that squatter as a committed managed identity and refuses the re-slug with a route at `jigc rename` — which finds no managed doc there *and* refuses anyway on the in-flight task. Same predicate, read where it was already answered.
- **The transient sink refuses, and it is not a fourth cell.** The decomposition placed `commit` under *never committed by construction*; the verb still refuses it, because a transient doctype carries **no doc-level `id-from`** and its slug **IS the task id** `plan_finalize` renders the message from (`commit_slug`, `finalize.rs`) — machine-derived exactly as `milestone-record`'s slug is its milestone id. The done-criterion's own derived-set fence is the proof: for a `commit` doc the old slug *is* the task id, so *"no occurrence of the old slug under `.jigc/tasks/<id>/`"* is unsatisfiable — the re-slug arm is structurally inapplicable, not merely unwise.
- **The refusals converge on `write.identity-change`; no check id is minted.** Three sentences, one code (the singleton, the transient sink, the committed re-slug), joining its shipped producer at `retitle-item`'s enum `id-from`. `validation.md`'s own-construction-sites enumeration — which had never listed the code at all — is corrected in the same motion.
- **The migration `slug-override` moves with the rename** (the decomposition left the cell open, either arm acceptable). Moving it beats refusing: the override is the id the author path re-mints from, so a stale one silently re-creates the doc at the old id on the next `doc author` — the resurrection shape, in a task the agent is still driving.
- **The staged `commit` doc's `implements` edge IS repointed**, where `jigc rename` can only *report* on it (`write-commands.md:97` — transient, no committed file). Inside the task area it is simply another staged doc, which is what makes *"the in-task referrer set is derived, not hand-listed"* true rather than aspirational.

**Acceptance is the census, iterated** (`crates/cli/tests/doc_rename_in_task.rs`, registered in `g_doc`): the arms partition the **loaded pack schema registry** by the three code-side predicates, so a doctype added to either pack joins an arm rather than escaping one; the re-slug arm's fence is a **whole-task-area scan** rather than a checklist of keyed files, and three applied mutants (dropped role rebind · dropped staged-ref repoint · stale `slug-override`) each turn it red. The route on the committed-re-slug refusal is lifted from the JSON finding and **run verbatim**. **Three shipped clap-tree bijections reddened on the new leaf and were repaired in the same commit, each on its own terms** — `flow47_acceptance.rs`'s item-miss matrix gains `rename` as **item-addressing-free** (the verb refuses a `#fragment` outright rather than dropping it onto its container, so a fabricated item-miss row would have been a lie), `exit_codes.rs`'s write-family sweep gains a genuine refused write (the transient-sink refusal, exit 1 exactly), and `format_json_success_axis.rs` gains a real success recipe. That three separate fences demanded a row is the M45 complete-fix contract working: a verb cannot join the surface quietly.

## 2026-08-13 — M48 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 2](implementation/roadmap.md) (the write path stops lying about identity) into **2 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `d72e918` (tree clean; Increment 1 landed). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-08-13 the Settle, **F2** (reject the divergent/no-op `title:` at both verbs, blocking, whole-payload atomic, and ship the in-task title change) and its **re-settle on committed-store identity** (never committed ⇒ re-slug freely in-task with the referrer set **derived**; a committed copy-in ⇒ retitle-only routing at `jigc rename`; placement / `display-title` singletons refuse; enum-`id-from` items already refuse), plus [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename` / The three-way write over a committed doc / The argument convention, and [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Identity. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 48 Increment 2; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M48/settle-record.md) → F2. **Why two:** the reject's route cannot be *constructed* before the verb it names exists (the M43 route fence refuses a `Route::mechanical` whose argv does not parse against the real `Cli`), so the correction's destination is a task, and the reject — one shared pre-check at one seam over both verbs — is the next. Each folds the repairs its own change forces; neither could be split further without leaving a half-swept axis or a red gate.

**Basis — every claim below was read in the tree at HEAD or reproduced through the real binary built from it, never carried from the roadmap or the ledger:**

- **All three cells reproduce at HEAD, and the headline lands.** Built `target/debug/jigc` from `d72e918`, `setup` → `start --workflow single-task`: **cell B** — `doc author adr` titled *Adopt Redis*, then the same payload titled *Adopt Valkey*, both exit 0, **two staged ADRs**; **cell A** — re-authoring with *Adopt Redis!* (which slugs to the same `adopt-redis`) exits 0 and leaves `# Adopt Redis` as the H1, the title silently dropped; **cell C** — `doc create adr --title "Adopt Redis" --slug adopt-memcached` over the staged doc mints a third at exit 0. Then, in a **second** task over the now-**committed** `docs/decisions/adopt-redis.md`: `doc create adr --title "Adopt Redis"` acks *"already existed — copied in for update"* while a divergent author mints its sibling, and **`jigc task finalize` exits 0 committing both** — `docs/decisions/adopt-redis.md` **and** `adopt-valkey.md`. That is the increment's *Proves*, live on this tree.
- **The build-shape call is taken against the code, and it goes to a distinct `doc` leaf.** A `--task` arm on `jigc rename` is **refuted, not merely disfavoured**: `rename.rs:147` refuses whenever `engine::state::list_active_task_ids` is non-empty (*"cannot rename while task `<id>` is in flight"*), so a `rename --task <id>` would be self-contradictory at its own guard; and the verb's body is a committed-store git transaction end to end (clean-tree precondition, committed-index referrer repoint, `git mv`, `git commit -F`, rollback via `git restore`) — an in-task title change uses none of it. `write-commands.md:96` already states the discriminator as the reason `rename` is top-level (*"unlike every `jigc doc <verb>` (which stages into a task working area, promoted at `finalize`) it is task-less and self-committing"*), which makes the in-task sibling a `jigc doc` leaf **by that doc's own rule**. The spelling follows the M42 argument-convention table, whose `--to` row is defined as *"a **rename's** new title"*: **`jigc doc rename <addr> --to "<New Title>" [--slug <s>] [--task <id>]`**, with the same degenerate-retitle arm `jigc rename` already has.
- **The three-cell doctype census, counted from both packs' schema dirs at HEAD (16 files, 15 doctypes — `commit` ships in both).** (a) **slug-identity, `location`-homed, non-singleton — 9**: `adr`, `spec`, `prd`, `arch-doc` (dev) · `completion-record`, `dogfood-record`, `idea`, `milestone-record`, `research` (methodology). (b) **placement + `display-title` singletons — 5**: `changelog` (`CHANGELOG.md`), `vision` (`VISION.md`), `roadmap`, `decisions-log`, `deferral-ledger` (`docs/*.md`). Every one of the five carries **both** keys, so the two knobs never disagree and the cell has one predicate, not two. (c) **transient sink — `commit`**: no `location`, no `placement`, no doc-level `id-from`, so `store::canonical_path` returns `None` and it is *never committed by construction* — a sub-case of (a), not a fourth cell. The **item-level** enum-`id-from` cell the Settle names is item-addressed and already refused (`write.identity-change`, one call site, below), so the doc-level verb owes it nothing but a regression arm.
- **The committed-store discriminator already exists and is already load-bearing — no new concept.** `engine::store::canonical_path(repo_root, schema, slug).is_file()` is the exact predicate `state::create`'s copy-in branch keys on (`state.rs`, step 4), and its outcome is **persisted per staged doc** in `docs/provenance.json` as `Provenance::{Created, EditedFromBase}` — verified live: after copying the committed ADR in, the record reads `"adr:adopt-redis": "edited-from-base"` beside `"adr:adopt-valkey": "created"`.
- **Every shipped gate entry declares an `as:` role, so "the bound identity" is total** — all **31** `allows-create` entries across both packs' 33 workflows carry `as:` (`quick-fix` alone declares the empty set). And every shipped workflow is **one doc per role by design**, in its own prose: `park-idea` — *"Park **one** shaped-but-unscheduled direction … land it as **one commit**"*; `do-research` — *"Investigate **one** question"*. So the divergence reject cannot break a shipped flow that legitimately wants two docs of one doctype in one task: no such flow exists. It **is** a declared behaviour change for a hand-driven second mint, and the reject's message must say so rather than ambush.
- **The pack's own generated payload already agrees with the singleton cell.** `compose.rs:1198 projection_title_value` renders a singleton's `{{schema:<T>}}` skeleton `title:` **literally as the `display-title`** (a per-instance doctype gets the `"<the title>"` fill-me), so the rule *"a singleton's `title:` must be the title it will actually carry"* is what the pack already instructs — the fence ratifies the seam rather than contradicting it. Two **test** suites disagree and redden: `crates/cli/tests/flow20_completion_encode.rs:314` (`create decisions-log --title "Decisions-Log"`) and `crates/cli/tests/migrate_corpus_value_remap.rs:248` (`create deferral-ledger --title "Deferral-Ledger"`) — both divergent from `Decisions Log` / `Deferral Ledger`, both repairable only by the commit that breaks them.
- **A new `doc` leaf reddens a shipped clap-tree bijection with no fix outside its own commit.** `flow47_acceptance.rs:1080`'s `NON_ITEM_ADDRESSING_DOC_VERBS = ["create","author","show","schema","list"]` is unioned with the arm-3 matrix's verb column and asserted **equal to the live clap `doc` leaf set** — so the moment `rename` joins the tree, arm 3 fails until the leaf is declared. It **is** item-addressing-free (it addresses a doc, never an item), so the honest repair is the declaration, not a fabricated item-miss row. Note the Settle's *"its cell joins `write_miss_shape_axis.rs`, whose declared exempt list carries `create`/`author`"* conflates two files: the **cells** live in `write_miss_shape_axis.rs` (a `Cell` struct with no verb column and no bijection), the **exempt list** in `flow47_acceptance.rs`. Both are touched; neither is what the other says it is.
- **`write.identity-change`'s caller sweep is clean — one site.** `crates/cli/src/doc.rs:1802`, `retitle-item` under an **enum** id-from, message and route verb-specific (*"a member change is an identity change, not a retitle"*). Converging the **identity-divergence** shape onto it is honest and mints no check id. Converging the **silent-no-op** shape onto it is **not** available for free: [storage.md](design/storage.md):66 states an ordinary retitle is identity-**stable** (*"changes the title field with the id held frozen"*), so a code named `identity-change` firing on a same-slug title drop would be a law-1 lie. That split is T2's first red step, stated below as an assumption to prove rather than a pin.
- **The task working area is 8 files, and three of them are keyed on the identity a re-slug moves** — `roles.json`, `docs/provenance.json`, `docs/<type>:<slug>.md`, plus the migration-only `slug-override` (bare slug) and `source-path`; `base.json` / `intent` / `workflow` / `staged-snapshot.json` are not. Rather than hand-list them (the Settle's own *"derived, not hand-listed"*), T1's done-criterion is a **whole-task-area scan**: after an in-task re-slug, **no file anywhere under `.jigc/tasks/<id>/` still names the old slug or the old address**. That is what makes the set derived — it catches a keyed file this plan did not enumerate, including the migration `slug-override` cell.
- **`milestone-record` needs no new rule and must be proven to need none**: `doc.rs:478 machine_maintained_guard` refuses **every** `jigc doc` write to it by doctype, above the per-leaf checks, so the new leaf inherits the refusal by calling the shipped guard — asserted, never assumed.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** The one call the record left open — the build shape — is settled above *against the census and the code*, exactly as the roadmap directs, and the two questions it raised underneath (the code split, the migration `slug-override` cell) are both decidable from locked docs plus a red step, so neither is escalated.

- **T1 — the in-task doc-level title change exists, and it splits on committed-store identity.** A new `doc` leaf **`jigc doc rename <addr> --to "<New Title>" [--slug <s>] [--task <id>]`** — the staged sibling of the top-level `jigc rename`, taking the same `--to` convention and the same degenerate-retitle arm. Four cells, each keyed on a predicate the code already computes: a staged doc whose `store::canonical_path` is **absent** re-slugs fully (H1 rewrite · staged file move · every task-area reference **derived and moved**); a staged doc **copied in from the committed store** is **retitle-only** (H1 only), and a `--to` that would re-slug it blocks with a route at `jigc rename`; a **placement / `display-title` singleton** (the five) refuses — identity is fixed to the type and the H1 is CLI-supplied, so there is nothing to change; a **`milestone-record`** refuses through the shipped `machine_maintained_guard`, called not re-implemented. **One atomic commit, because only it repairs what it breaks:** `flow47_acceptance.rs:1080` must gain `rename` in the same motion or the clap-tree bijection reddens with no in-scope fix, and `write-commands.md` gains the verb beside `jigc rename` plus its `--to` row in the argument-convention table. *Done:* a new real-binary suite (registered in **exactly one** group root) whose cell arms are **enumerated from the loaded pack schema registry** — partitioned by the same code-side predicates (`placement.is_some() || display_title.is_some()` · `location.is_some()` · neither), so a doctype added later joins an arm rather than escaping it — asserting per cell: the re-slug arm moves the staged file, rewrites the H1, and leaves **no occurrence of the old slug or old address anywhere under `.jigc/tasks/<id>/`** (the derived-set fence, which also covers a migration task's recorded `slug-override`), with the re-slugged doc still readable through `jigc doc show <new-addr> --task <id>` and still promoting on `finalize`; the copy-in arm rewrites the H1, leaves the slug frozen, and blocks a divergent `--to` with a route that **runs verbatim**; the singleton and `milestone-record` arms refuse non-zero with a route; and `retitle-item`'s shipped enum `write.identity-change` refusal is asserted **unchanged**. Red at HEAD (the verb does not exist — the binary refuses the subcommand). ## 2026-08-13 — M48 Increment 1, T3: `discard` stops asking whether the path is *ours*, and the twice-falsified enumeration is re-derived

The abandon guard's subject moves off `provisioned_worktrees` (the task list ∩ the **registered** set) onto every sub-task worktree-shaped path, through the shared `probe_leftover` (`crates/cli/src/milestone.rs` → `held_subtask_worktrees`). Design of record: **F3** (DECISIONS → 2026-08-13 the Settle) and its fail-closed re-settle. Three elaborations worth pinning:

- **The refusal names each path's fate, because the door is not uniform.** `remove_worktrees` removes a **registered** worktree and skips everything else — so a non-registered leftover is *orphaned*, never deleted, and the widened guard would have lied on every new cell it caught if it had kept the shipped *"discarding it would destroy that work"* text. Each listed path now carries its own disposition (removed-and-destroyed · left-on-disk-with-nothing-naming-it), and the `--force` route states what it really costs on each ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → law 1). The composed-doors property is asserted, not just written: the acceptance forces the abandon and then reads the planted bytes back off disk.
- **A refusal over a door that destroys nothing is still the right answer.** The bytes survive a forced discard, so the loss is not the directory — it is that the abandon settles the record and tears the workbench down, retiring the *only* thing that still names those bytes as work. The guard's question is unchanged in kind (*can I prove this path holds nothing precious?*), and the honest statement of the cost is what the message carries.
- **The enumeration was re-derived, not appended to.** [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md):92 named *the teardowns left to guard* and was falsified twice by that shape — by `uninstall` at the M47 audit, then by `provision`, which no `design/` doc called destructive at all. It is replaced by the rule the three shipped doors satisfy (*every door that removes a worktree-shaped path under `.jigc/worktrees/` probes it first and refuses what it cannot prove is disposable*), so a fourth door inherits the obligation instead of being appended; the landed-finalize teardown stays outside by **satisfying** it (the commit landed first), its M46 bound unchanged. [storage.md](design/storage.md):121's layout line follows.

## 2026-08-13 — M48 Increment 1, T2: `uninstall` stops destroying the two things it had just promised to keep

Both arms land at the one door (`crates/cli/src/setup.rs` → `dirty_fanout_worktrees` re-subjected, `staged_task_prose` minted), with `jigc uninstall --force` as the single consent. Design of record: **F3** (DECISIONS → 2026-08-13 the Settle) and its fail-closed re-settle. Four elaborations worth pinning:

- **The prose arm takes its own identity, `uninstall.staged-prose`.** The Settle's table reads *"the prose arm rides the same door code as `uninstall`'s"*, and the locked docs resolve that rather than a call: `uninstall.dirty-worktree` printed over `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/` with no worktree in sight names the wrong subject ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → law 1). Same door, two codes, each naming what it actually found. The shipped `uninstall.dirty-worktree` **message** moved with the subject for the same reason: it now claims "content", not "uncommitted work", because a path git cannot vouch for is listed by child names and calling those bytes *uncommitted work* is a claim the probe cannot back.
- **The shared derivation was factored, not assumed.** `dropped_staged_docs` was private and takes a `&TaskArea` (whose `resolve` needs a live task id and `make_pack()`) while `uninstall` holds only `repo_root`, so the `<type>:<slug>` derivation moved out as `task::staged_doc_ids(&docs_dir)` — and it gained a `Result`: `task discard`'s ack takes `.unwrap_or_default()` (enumeration must never block a discard), the guard propagates, because *"enumerated nothing"* and *"there is nothing"* are the same bytes to a caller and only one of them is safe to delete on.
- **The declared behaviour change, stated not glossed:** `jigc start` pre-creates `docs/commit:<id>.md` before any write (verified live), so the fail-closed arm refuses `uninstall` while **any** task is open, authored or not. It is provision's sibling under the same settled rule — the binary can no more distinguish a pristine skeleton from authored prose than `junk.txt` from `precious.txt` — with `--force` as the hatch.
- **Two shipped assertions were repairs this commit owed, and a third doc line was repaired unasked.** The clean arm `uninstall_still_tears_down_when_every_provisioned_worktree_is_clean` staged sub-task prose in its fixture, so `setup_fanout` gained a `prose` knob separate from `dirty` — a clean-worktree arm has to isolate one guard. The long help's *"non-destructive on every state it accepts … preserved byte-for-byte"* + *"One state it refuses"* was false in exactly the two ways the task named, and its pin was re-derived to assert **both** codes, both escape hatches, and `--force`, with the two falsified phrases banned. And [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md)'s teardown acceptance — *"One state refuses the teardown outright"*, in no task's file list — was falsified by this commit, so it is corrected here rather than left for the audit: law 1 binds the doc my change made untrue, not only the docs my task enumerated.

## 2026-08-13 — M48 Increment 1, T1: `provision` stops destroying what it cannot prove is junk

The fail-closed classifier is minted (`crates/cli/src/milestone.rs` → `LeftoverVerdict` / `LEFTOVER_VERDICTS` / `probe_leftover`, beside the `registered_worktrees`/`dirty_worktrees` seam its siblings already share) and replaces `provision_worktrees`' unconditional `remove_dir_all` — discharging [M47's declared undischarged bound](completions/artifacts/M47/VERDICT.md) on that call. Design of record: **F3** (DECISIONS → 2026-08-13 the Settle) and its fail-closed re-settle. Three elaborations worth pinning:

- **The refusal's identity is a door-scoped code, `milestone.leftover-holds-work`** (a `Finding` code, not an `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` member) on the `dirty_worktree_finding` mold — and it **reaches stderr**, because `milestone.rs`' own `finding_to_err` prints `severity · code — message` (the M41 round-2 D6h funnel). So the acceptance can assert the door identity on the emitted bytes rather than on prose. The door set ships as a minted `DESTROYING_DOORS` table (provision · discard · uninstall) for T2/T3 and [Increment 12](implementation/roadmap.md)'s flow-48 arms; only `PROVISION_DOOR` has a producer reading from it today.
- **The revised `milestone.rs:2129` arm is the pinned 1.0 contract, and it keeps both halves.** The leftover holding `junk.txt` now **refuses** and its bytes are asserted intact; the test then **empties** the directory and continues into the shipped crashed-run idempotency it always asserted — because an empty leftover is provably safe and still clears. The verdict × `--force` axis lives in the new `provision_leftover_guard.rs`, iterated **from** `LEFTOVER_VERDICTS`, so a fourth verdict cannot be minted without that suite failing to compile.
- **The refusal fires before any removal or add**, so a refused provision leaves *every* sub-task path exactly as it found it — not a half-provisioned set. `--force` lands in the same commit as its route, which the M43 route fence requires (it refuses to construct a `Route::mechanical` whose argv does not parse against the real `Cli`).

## 2026-08-13 — M48 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 1](implementation/roadmap.md) (the destroying-door guard — the guard's subject becomes the path, not the registered set) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `39413cc` (tree clean). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-08-13 the Settle, **F3** (the fail-closed three-verdict classifier at `provision`/`discard`/`uninstall`, the `dropped_staged_docs` prose arm, `--force` at each door, `finalize` unifies the probe only) and its two re-settles (**fail-closed wins — the junk-dir clear stops working**; the subject is **scoped to worktree-shaped paths under `.jigc/worktrees/`**, because taken literally it bricks `uninstall`), plus [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → Abandon refuses on a dirty worktree and [storage.md](design/storage.md) → repository layout. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 48 Increment 1; [settle-record.md](completions/artifacts/M48/settle-record.md) → F3. **Why three:** one task per door, each folding the repairs its own change forces — the two swaps that redden a shipped assertion are inseparable from its revision, so neither could reach a green gate alone.

**Basis — every claim below was exercised against real `git` or read in the tree at HEAD, never carried from the roadmap:**

- **The three verdicts are confirmed against real git, one spike each.** A plain non-`.git` leftover under `.jigc/worktrees/` returns **rc=0 printing the *main repo* root** (git walks up; the `.jigc/` gitignore is irrelevant) ⇒ verdict 3. A `cp -R` copy's worktree returns **rc=0 printing its own path** ⇒ verdict 2, **and reads its own dirt correctly** (`?? precious.txt`) even though the admin record names the source. Copy-then-move-the-source returns **rc=128** (`fatal: not a git repository: …/main/.git/worktrees/wt1`) ⇒ verdict 1, where git can say nothing about dirt. **Comparison must canonicalize** — git prints realpaths (`/private/tmp/…`), so a raw `PathBuf` compare would misfile verdict 2 as verdict 3 under a symlinked temp dir.
- **`git worktree prune` is confirmed a dead end on the ordinary trigger, and the registration mechanism is the loss.** With the source repo present, the copy's `git worktree list --porcelain` reports the worktree at the **source's** path and `prune` removes nothing — so `registered.iter().any(|w| w == &path)` is **false for the copy's own path**, `provision_worktrees` takes its `remove_dir_all` branch, and the copy's uncommitted work dies at exit 0. This is `provision_worktrees`' `remove_dir_all`, carried forward as a **declared undischarged bound** by [M47's VERDICT](completions/artifacts/M47/VERDICT.md) → Honest bounds; this increment discharges it.
- **The outside-charter `uninstall` prose loss reproduced end-to-end on the installed `1.0.0-rc.10`**: `setup` → `start --workflow quick-fix` → `doc set-slot commit:<id>#summary` → `uninstall` → **exit 0**, `.jigc/` gone, the authored summary in no object DB. The doc destroyed is **`docs/commit:<task>.md` — a *transient* doctype**, so the prose arm must **not** filter on `dropped_staged_docs`' `transient` mark, or the reproduced loss stays open.
- **The prose arm's subject is the `*.md` set, never directory-non-emptiness** — `docs/` always also holds `provenance.json`, so a dir-emptiness probe fires on every task. `dropped_staged_docs` already derives exactly the `<type>:<slug>` set (`strip_suffix(".md")`), which is why the Settle names it. **But it is not a drop-in call**: it is private and takes `&TaskArea`, whose `resolve` needs a live task id plus `make_pack()`, while `uninstall` holds only `repo_root` — the executor factors the shared derivation rather than assuming a call, and proves the reuse at the red step.
- **`jigc start` pre-creates the staged skeleton** (`docs/commit:<id>.md` exists after `start`, before any write — verified live). So the fail-closed prose arm **refuses `uninstall` while any task is open**, authored or not: a **declared behaviour change**, the exact sibling of provision's, with `--force` as the hatch. It is a consequence of the settled fail-closed rule, not a new fork — the binary can no more distinguish a pristine skeleton from authored prose than it can `junk.txt` from `precious.txt`, and `milestone discard` already refuses over one untracked file.
- **Two shipped suites pin behaviour these swaps break, and each can only be repaired by the commit that breaks it.** `crates/cli/tests/milestone.rs:2129-2141` (inside `milestone_provision_creates_detached_base_pin_worktrees_idempotently`) plants `junk.txt` in a non-registered leftover and asserts clear-and-exit-0 — **the loss pinned as expected output**. And `uninstall_worktree_guard.rs`' clean arm `uninstall_still_tears_down_when_every_provisioned_worktree_is_clean` runs over a fixture whose `setup_fanout` stages `.jigc/tasks/<sub>/docs/*.md`, so the prose arm reddens it with no in-scope fix elsewhere.
- **The reuse targets exist and are already cross-module.** `milestone::dirty_worktrees` and `milestone::registered_worktrees` are `pub(crate)` and `setup::dirty_fanout_worktrees` already calls both — so the classifier's home beside them is the shipped seam, not a new one. `uninstall.dirty-worktree` / `milestone.dirty-worktree` are **`Finding` codes, not `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` members** (the registry mirrors `COMMITTING_DOORS` member-for-member and closes at 10) — so a new door code mints no registry work, exactly as the Settle records.
- **`--force` must land in the same task as its route.** `route_fence.rs` installs a validator into `Route::mechanical` that **refuses construction** unless the argv parses against the real `Cli` — so a refusal routing at `jigc milestone provision <milestone-id> --force` cannot be built before the flag exists (`<milestone-id>` is already a declared `DUMMY_SUBSTITUTIONS` placeholder).
- **Two prose sites become lies the moment `provision` refuses** and move with it (law 1): `MilestoneCommand::Provision`'s long help (*"Idempotent — reuses a live worktree, **clears a stale leftover from a crashed run**"*) and `provision_worktrees`' doc-comment. The pack step `provision-worktrees.yaml` and the `milestone-provision` catalog entry make **no** such claim — checked, so they are deliberately untouched rather than forgotten.
- **`finalize`'s landed teardown is behaviourally out of scope.** `remove_worktrees` is shared by `discard` and the landed finalize; its narration probe is `discarded_work` (index-column-partitioned), a *different* probe from `dirty_worktrees`. The Settle's *"unifies the probe only"* means no policy change here — M46 entry 11 still governs — so the landed-teardown suites must stay green **unedited**.
- **`discard`'s teardown is not made more destructive.** `remove_worktrees` skips a non-registered leftover today and still will; only the *guard's* subject widens. The robust-advocate's own bound — the question is *"can I prove this path holds nothing precious?"*, never *"is it ours?"* — cuts both ways, so `discard`'s refusal text must state what the door actually does and not assert a destruction it will not perform.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** The one place the record reads two ways — the Settle table's *"the prose arm rides the same door code as `uninstall`'s"* — is resolvable from the locked docs rather than by a call: `uninstall.dirty-worktree` printed over `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/` with no worktree involved is a law-1 lie ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md)), so the arm takes a sibling `uninstall.*` identity under the same door. Naming is tier-2; the fence is that the printed identity names its real subject.

- **T1 — the classifier is minted, and `provision` stops destroying what it cannot prove is junk.** The fail-closed classifier lands beside `registered_worktrees`/`dirty_worktrees` in `milestone.rs` as a **code-side enumeration** (the three verdicts + the destroying-door set — the registry [Increment 12](implementation/roadmap.md)'s flow-48 arms iterate, minted here where none existed), and replaces `provision_worktrees`' unconditional `remove_dir_all`: **verdict 2** reuses the shipped `dirty_worktrees` probe (dirty ⇒ refuse, clean ⇒ clear), **verdicts 1 and 3 refuse on any non-empty directory**, an **empty** leftover still clears, and a registered live worktree is still reused untouched. `jigc milestone provision` gains `--force`; the refusal is a door-scoped blocking `Finding` on the `uninstall.dirty-worktree` mold, naming the path and routing at the `--force` re-run. **One atomic commit, because only it repairs what it breaks:** `crates/cli/tests/milestone.rs:2129-2141` pins the loss as expected output and is **revised to expect the refusal** — whatever lands there is the pinned 1.0 contract — and the two now-false prose sites move in the same motion. *Done:* a new real-binary suite (registered in exactly one group root) **iterating the verdict axis from the minted enumeration, not three hand-written repros** — (i) a plain non-empty leftover dir, (ii) a `cp -R` copy of the repo whose unregistered-but-live worktree holds an untracked file, (iii) that copy with the **source moved away** (rc=128) — each refusing with the door code, naming the path, exiting non-zero, and leaving the planted bytes **byte-intact**; plus the negative controls that keep the guard from being its own defect — an **empty** leftover clears and provisions at exit 0, a second `provision` is still idempotent, and `--force` clears and provisions in all three refusing arms. Red at HEAD on (i)–(iii). Full unscoped gate green (`cargo test --no-fail-fast`, fmt, clippy — measured unpiped). *(files: `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone.rs`, a new suite + one `crates/cli/tests/groups/g_*.rs`.)*
- **T2 — `uninstall` stops destroying the two things it had just promised to keep.** `dirty_fanout_worktrees` swaps its `registered_worktrees`-intersection subject for the classifier over **every** worktree-shaped path under `.jigc/worktrees/` — closing the cell the registered-only probe structurally cannot see (in a copied repo *no* path under the copy's own `.jigc/worktrees/` is registered, so today the guard is inert and `remove_dir_all` takes the lot) — and gains the **second arm**: the `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/` staged-`*.md` set, transient docs **included**, refusing under a sibling `uninstall.*` identity that names its real subject. `jigc uninstall` gains `--force`. **Atomic:** the prose arm reddens the shipped clean arm `uninstall_still_tears_down_when_every_provisioned_worktree_is_clean` (its fixture stages sub-task docs) and `Command::Uninstall`'s long help — *"Idempotent and **non-destructive** on every state it accepts … your own file content is **preserved byte-for-byte**"*, now false in two ways — is corrected here, which moves the shipped help-text suite in the same commit. *Done:* the reproduced repro as a red test — `setup` → `start` → `doc set-slot` → `uninstall` **refuses**, exits non-zero, `.jigc/` still present and the authored prose **byte-intact**, the finding naming `commit:<id>` — plus the unregistered-non-empty-worktree arm, `--force` completing the teardown in both, the two shipped clean arms (**no** worktrees; clean worktrees **with no staged prose**) still exiting 0, and the help suite green on the corrected text. Red at HEAD on the repro arm. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/setup.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/uninstall_worktree_guard.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/uninstall.rs` if the fixture reaches it.)*
- **T3 — `discard` stops asking whether the path is *ours*, and the twice-falsified enumeration is re-derived.** `run_discard`'s guard subject moves off `provisioned_worktrees` (registered ∩ the task list) onto the classifier over the milestone's sub-task worktree-shaped paths, so the leftover it politely **skipped** — orphaning it into the next `provision`'s path, the composition that produces the loss — now refuses instead, with `--force` (already shipped) as the hatch and a refusal that states what the door actually does rather than asserting a removal it will not perform. In the same commit the design of record is **re-derived from the shipped set, not appended to**: [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md):92's *"The un-landed teardowns left are `discard`'s and `jigc uninstall`'s, and both refuse on a dirty sub-task worktree"* — false in two independent ways and now falsified a **third** time by `provision` — is rewritten to enumerate the destroying doors the code enumerates, **gains the `provision` door** (no `design/` doc states today what `provision` does to a pre-existing directory at its target path), and [storage.md](design/storage.md):121's worktree teardown line follows. *Done:* a new arm in `milestone_discard.rs` — a **non-registered, non-empty** `.jigc/worktrees/<sub-id>` refuses the discard naming the path, `--force` settles the record and tears down as before — with the shipped `a_dirty_subtask_worktree_refuses_the_discard`, `force_settles_…`, and the dev-only arm all still green, and **the landed-finalize teardown suites green unedited** (the probe unifies; the policy does not move). ## 2026-08-13 — M48 planning: the Settle — every chartered fork re-posed against an exercised baseline, and seven things refused

**The baseline corrected the charter before a single fork was decided.** Five `capability-auditor` fan-outs **exercised the real binary** (`1.0.0-rc.10`) rather than reading the roadmap, and returned **19 corrected charter premises and 8 defects outside the charter** ([the ledger](completions/artifacts/M48/baseline-ledger.md)). The four that moved the plan most: **F3's trigger is `cp -R` or `mv` of the repo, not a crashed run** (both reproduced — copying a corpus is how every RC trial corpus is made); **a standing test pins F3's loss as expected output** (`milestone.rs:2129` asserts provision clears a non-registered leftover and exits 0, so the fix *revises* an assertion rather than adding one); **F2's class is three cells, and the unreported one mints a second ADR that `finalize` commits at exit 0**; and **F1's named fence precedent reaches 14 of 31 write-soliciting steps**, structurally missing every ordinary `author-*` step — the charter cited M44's D5 as the mold for both the pipeline and the set, and it is only the pipeline. A fifth correction moved how we work: **the gate is ~4–7 min, not 30–50** — M47's twelve-group consolidation cut it, and the old figure also double-counted ~6.4 runs of each suite.

**Then four `gap-detector` dimensions, and all four independently found the same contradiction.** F7's chartered fix — *"omission drops the heading"* — was **settled against at M36 and is foreclosed by two locked docs**: `corpus-migration.md:61` rejects parser-tolerance **by name** (*"two valid byte forms for one schema — forking the frozen canonical form and touching the byte-stable parse core, the #1-retired risk"*) and `document-type-schema.md:173` states the semantic it would invert. `decisions-pending.md:275` already parks it with its real cost, filed under *No firm trigger yet* rather than keyed to a milestone — which is exactly why the charter drafted F7 without it, and why that entry now gains an explicit counted-and-still-deferred line. The decisive fact nobody had established: **the freeze cannot reach the change** — `adr.yaml` is untouched so no `schema_hash` moves, meaning an rc.11-authored ADR would be a hard parse failure on rc.10 **with no version signal**, and `schema_diff` over an unchanged schema is empty so `migrate-corpus` degrades to a pure restamp. **Two byte forms, permanently.** The irony is exact: `schema_diff.rs:149`'s invariant is the *entire justification for the shipped M36 `adr` v1→v2 migration*, so arm 1 would make that migration's own output the artifact F7 calls a defect. **Settled: fix the guidance.** F7 is a **law-1 "nothing lies" defect in pack prose** — the template instructs an omission the format does not have — and it **leaves tier 1**, because the offending string is a `hint:` key that `erase_presentation` strips, so nothing at the freeze moves and no committed byte changes.

**F3 went to an independent robust-advocate, which refuted a charter arm on evidence.** `git worktree prune` is a **dead end** in the ordinary `cp -R` shape (the copy's admin record points at the *source's* still-existing directory, so prune removes nothing) — a refusal routed there would be a law-1 lie. It also corrected the baseline's own discriminator: `rev-parse --show-toplevel` separates **linkage classes, not shapes**, and in the `rc=128` class git cannot say whether the directory is dirty — so the probe is **fail-closed on non-empty**, never a dirty check. And it **declined to overreach**: M46 entry 10's durable provisioned-fact is **not required**, because the guard's question is *"can I prove this path holds nothing precious?"*, never *"is it ours?"* — which keeps a frozen-doctype bump out of the wave. **Settled robust:** the guard's **subject changes from the registered set to every path the call is about to remove**, adopted at `provision`, `discard` and `uninstall`, plus an arm reusing `dropped_staged_docs` so `uninstall` guards `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/` authored prose — **an outside-charter HIGH data loss reproduced end-to-end** (setup → start → `set-slot` → `uninstall` → exit 0, prose in no object DB). The doors **compose**: `discard` politely skips a non-registered leftover, orphaning it, and the next `provision` steps on it. `team-ready-state.md:92` states the property as an enumeration now false in two independent ways — **the second time that sentence has been falsified.**

**The remaining forks.** **F1** — the fence keys on the **union** of `{{cli.*}}`-resolving-to-a-write-verb (18) and `{{schema:<T>}}` (13), covering **30 of 31** steps, the single miss being the one step that already names `doc show`; it **iterates the derivation, never a list**, because `surface-contract.md:74` records the receipt-outlives-contract failure live; `doc show` joins both command catalogs (it is in neither); and the read-surface doors an agent hits first are included (`doc list`'s empty-set route, `doc list --task`). **F2** — reject the divergent-or-dropped title **and** ship the in-task doc-level title change, the only shape answering all three cells; `title` is not a `Field` and is outside `schema_hash`, so there is no schema cost, and CLAUDE.md's identity invariant targets the *untracked move*, which a staged rename is not. **F10** — the human took both halves, which forced a better route than the proposer's: the advisory member **converges on the already-shipped `schema-conformance.unadopted-instance`** rather than splitting the code, so the name stops lying, one file answers one code at both doors, and **no new check id is minted** — the M21 invariant is honoured, not overturned. The real defect behind it: **M42's managed-vs-foreign discriminator swept the store family and never reached the task-scope gate.** **F14** — the charter's premise is refuted (the catalog states the intent verbatim); the defect is **bundling**, and since suppression is twice-declined and a conditional gate is barred by the non-goals, the fix is to state the changelog gate as a **discriminating axis** in the catalog entry. **F8** — `config get`/`config list` ship, and jigc **renders its own message for the unknown-subcommand error kind**, because its curated tip currently appends *below* clap's contradictory suggestion; declared build-time spike with global `suggestions`-off as the fallback. **`describe`** — the **filter** only; `introspection.md:112` forecloses the *positional* form on a boundary argument a filter does not cross.

**The pre-1.0 additive window closes with this wave, and the human took the wide sweep.** `doc-read-surface.md:87` and `command-output-contract.md:367` both permit additive keys **pre-1.0 only**, and neither has a discharge sentence — `:87` is an open ledger of waves rc.4→rc.8. Rather than the proposer's three hand-picked keys, the sweep covers **every machine-output surface**, given an axis so it stays plannable: **a value the human/agent text already prints but the `--format json` envelope withholds is a gap** — enumerated from the clap verb tree the parity suite already bijects against, and shipped as a **standing fence, not a census**. It absorbs M46 entry 12 and catches `describe`'s router-hidden flag (today only a substring of `prose`). Excluded deliberately: keys for values nothing computes.

**Seven refusals, recorded because a wave that cannot refuse cannot halt.** The **search verb** and the **file-state read verb** (M46 entries 4 and 8) — both *missing capabilities, not unnamed ones*, and this wave's lens is *"the capability exists, no composed surface names it"*, which has nothing to name. The **checkpoint record** (entry 2) — the charter contradicted itself, listing F16 in tier 2 while fork 4 deferred the entry that *is* it; fork 4 governs, re-counted at **7 demands**, with the charter's zero price corrected (it lands an eleventh manifest entry or a version bump plus migration). **F15's structural half** — a one-way door on two frozen doctypes, resting on an item-block `ref` shape **zero shipped doctypes exercise**, and `team-ready-state.md:185` settles it the other way; the non-schema half ships. **F7's canonical-form change**, **F14's unbundling**, and **`describe <name>`** as above.

**Two calls went against the proposer's recommendation and both improved the outcome** — the F10 rename (which forced the free convergence route) and the wide parity sweep (which turned three keys into a fenced axis). **One dissent is recorded as a dissent:** the human took a **first slice of adapter-owned instruction files** — VISION's *"a small set of skill/command files that each just call the CLI"*, committed since the founding doc and **never built** (setup's install commit carries seven files, none of them skills). The proposer recommended parking it on the same ground the search verb was refused; the distinguishing argument is that VISION already commits to it and the content exists, so the work is the **ownership mechanism** — stamped with the binary version, replaced on `setup`/`upgrade`, and **refusing to clobber a user-modified copy**, which is the minimal honest form of principle #5. First slice: the guides, not command files. **The manifest-hash fence** (M47's dropped rider, routed here) is built as the **CI git-diff check** — its precondition landed at M47, the one-keystroke silent freeze breach is spike-proven, and 1.0 is when the freeze becomes load-bearing; declared bounds: this repo only, and a build fence rather than a surface. **Its comparison window was corrected at the increment-11 plan halt (2026-08-15):** the settled `HEAD~1` form inspects only the **last commit of a push** (Actions fires one run per push, at the tip) while this repo pushes in large batches — and the one real instance in its history, `6e81d53`, which re-pinned **all 16 doctype hashes at unchanged `schema-version`s in both manifests** and which both manifest headers name as *"the declared genesis exemption and the ONLY one"*, landed **34 commits from its push tip**, over which the settled check is **provably clean**. The fence as settled would have missed the only event it exists to catch. Re-settled with the human: **widen the base ref to the pushed range** (`github.event.before` / the PR base, **falling back to `HEAD~1`** so the approved shape stays the floor), `fetch-depth: 0` at 9.89 MiB. **Flow 48 mints the registries it lacks** (`unknown_subcommand_tip` becomes a table, `STORE_EXIT_FLIPS` goes `pub`, `ConfigAck` gains `ALL`), because hand-listing three arms would make the acceptance the one place the wave does not hold itself to M45's complete-fix contract. **The independent pre-decompose review then refuted two settled claims against the code and forced three re-settles** — the M47 precedent holding one wave later. **F10's convergence collapsed on its only caller:** `conformance_advisory_finding` has exactly one, `reconcile_committed`'s UNKNOWN+non-conformant arm, which carries **no managed-vs-foreign discriminator** — so it fires over *managed* docs too, pinned by a standing suite driving a **v2-stamped, fully-migrated ADR**; so it would have moved a **managed** doc onto a foreign-file code, on what that suite itself calls the dominant `validate` corpus. Re-settled: **discriminate on `is_unadopted_foreign`, then split** — foreign converges, managed keeps `reconciliation.conformance-block`, which is honest for a doc that genuinely drifted, and still no new check id. **Corrected at the increment-4 plan halt (2026-08-14), because this entry carried a misattributed quote:** the string *"ingest, migrate, or move it out of the managed location"* is **`conformance_advisory_finding`'s own route** (`file_state.rs:1088`), not `unadopted_instance`'s (which routes to *"adopt — run `jigc ingest` … it is a foreign file, not an unmigrated managed doc"*). So the lie does not *arrive* with convergence — **it is already on the managed cell today**, live-reproduced on a v2-stamped fully-migrated ADR, and the settled split **keeps** it there. Worse after the fix than before: today the arm serves foreign ∪ managed and the route is right for the foreign majority; after the split it serves managed only, so the route is wrong for **100%** of its population, and Increment 4's own *Proves* (*"no advisory tells a stamped managed doc to migrate itself"*) was undeliverable as written. **The split was right and incomplete — it fixed the code and left the route, and the route is the actual lie.** Settled at the halt: **route on the stamp**, reusing two already-shipped strings — below-version or stamp-absent → the corpus-migration route (`route_schema_conformance`), at-version → the blocking twin's hand-repair sanction (*"this is the one case a managed file is yours to hand-edit"*) — because hand-repair advice over a **stale** managed doc is itself wrong. No new mechanism, no new check id. Two costs the Settle had not priced, now verified: `is_unadopted_foreign`'s `versions`+`priors` **reach none** of the three reconcile functions, so they thread from three CLI doors (one needing its own `make_pack()`); and `GATES_NOWHERE`'s stated **derivation** (*"emitted only on a store-scope path and by no task-scope path"*) becomes false and must be re-derived — membership stays correct. **F3's classifier and its own "the junk-dir clear must keep working" clause were jointly unsatisfiable** — spiked: a plain directory with no `.git` returns the *main repo root* from `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so it lands in the refuse verdict. Re-settled **fail-closed**, on the repo's own argument: the binary cannot distinguish `junk.txt` from `precious.txt`, and the old assertion passes only because the *test author* knew — pinning data loss as expected output, the exact reason the leftover re-`provision` left the latent-surface sweep two days earlier. Provision now refuses where it used to succeed: a declared behaviour change, breaking now rather than after 1.0. **F2's in-task title change was named, not designed** — the reviewer refuted the Settle's carve-out argument (*"task-less and self-committing"* scopes the **verb**, not the **invariant** at `storage.md:66`), and could not write the acceptance test from the settled text. Re-settled on the **committed-store identity boundary**, which is the identity model's own subject: a doc **never committed** re-slugs freely in-task (no committed referrer can exist **by construction**; the in-task set is derived, not hand-listed), a **committed copy-in** is retitle-only and routes to `jigc rename`, placement singletons refuse. Retitle-only-everywhere was rejected because it manufactures the drift VISION cites as the reason `rename` exists (*"a slug that tracks its title beats one frozen out of sync"*) — and it would leave standing a live bug the chosen arm closes: `doc create --slug <other>` over a staged doc mints a **third** doc at exit 0. Five further findings were accepted as corrections: F3's subject rescoped to worktree-shaped paths (taken literally it **bricks `uninstall`**) · **F7's fence cannot be axis-complete** — the omission instruction lives in four hand-authored places and only the `hint:` reaches a seam, so three step strings are an unfenced tier-2 edit stated as a bound rather than a grep-fence the M42 lesson forbids · the adapter slice records a **declared deviation** from principle #5 rather than claiming compliance (refuse-to-clobber is an untracked-fork *detector* with no delta) and **sequences after F4**, which rewrites the same hardcoded path list · F15's bound moves onto the surface that creates the adjacency · F2's rejection gains its severity, both-verb atomicity and matrix cell. Full record: [the settle record](completions/artifacts/M48/settle-record.md); scope + acceptance: [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 48.

## 2026-08-13 — The latent-surface sweep: one arm, and the honest reason there is only one

**The sweep chartered before the 1.0.0 call is discharged** (`20800f7`; [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → the sweep entry). Its scope was derived the way the charter demanded — from the **verb registry and the `verb_suite_coverage` map, minus what the trial walks, minus what a named suite fences** — and never from a changed-file table, which is how the first attempt was built and why it missed three verbs while wrongly including covered ones. **Every disposition was checked by test *content*, not by test name**, per the rule that classification is a claim about the code.

**It found one arm, and that is a result rather than a shortfall** — the charter's own instruction was *"if the derivation turns up nothing beyond those, record it and close, rather than manufacturing arms to justify the increment."* Of the three named candidates: `relocate`'s happy-path move and its frozen-doctype refusal are already fenced, and the verb is **correctly absent from `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`** (it `git mv`s and stages, and calls no commit — not a hole); `milestone join` is driven at five call sites across three suites and commits nothing; and **the leftover re-`provision` stopped being a sweep candidate the moment the pre-1.0.0 trial confirmed it as a data-loss defect** (F3) — writing a standing test over its present behaviour would **pin data loss as expected output**, so it routes to that fix's red test instead. That last one is the sweep's sharpest judgment call and is recorded as such.

**The genuine hole was `relocate`'s foreign-squatter displacement.** It `git rm --cached`s a user's committed-but-unmanaged file at the destination and renames it into the **gitignored** `.jigc/` workbench — F3's shape exactly one door over, except that here the bytes survive. Which is what makes **the ack naming it the entire safety property**: a move into a gitignored tree is indistinguishable from a deletion to anyone who does not read the output, and an in-module unit test — the only thing fencing it until now — cannot fence what the *binary prints*. The new arm asserts the managed doc lands, the foreign bytes survive (**located by content, not by a reconstructed path**, so it does not encode a workbench layout it does not own), and the ack names both paths, with a no-squatter negative control so it cannot pass on a constant string. **Proven live by an applied mutant**: dropping `workbench` from the renderer turns it red, reverting turns it green.

**Process note worth keeping.** The first run of this arm failed for the *wrong* reason — the fixture put the squatter at a bare `notes/` when `docs-root` homes the doctype at `docs/notes/` — and the negative control would have been the only thing passing. A test that goes green without its subject ever occurring is the vacuous pass this repo keeps legislating against; it was caught because the red was read rather than assumed.

## 2026-08-13 — The pre-1.0.0 trial: the plants all fired, and the sixth discoverability landing is on the capability built to answer it

**The acceptance instrument for M47 ran on the installed `1.0.0-rc.10`** — three blind sessions plus the operator-scripted walk, six fresh corpora, **294 logged invocations**, full record in [completions/artifacts/RC-pre-1.0/](completions/artifacts/RC-pre-1.0/trial-record.md) with every claim adversarially verified ([findings-verification.md](completions/artifacts/RC-pre-1.0/findings-verification.md)). **Zero data-loss or corruption defects on any blind path, zero regressions, zero invented state**, and **every designed plant fired without firing silently**: the carryover gate raised one blocking finding **per planted path** — the live per-path confirmation project-alpha-4.0 lost with its machine — the `core.hooksPath` rejection logged `finalize.commit-rejected` with the survivable frame intact and HEAD unmoved, and the foreign-ADR trap was **caught on its harder branch** (G3 found the planted decision, *retracted a premise it had already sold the operator*, named the ADR's own escape hatch, and reached `supersedes` unhinted).

**The lens: the capability exists, the surface the agent stands on does not name it — a sixth consecutive landing, and this time on the very capability built in response to it.** All three blind sessions independently went to the filesystem to read their own in-flight work, while `jigc doc show --task <id>` has shipped since **M43**, where it is recorded as *"demanded three trials running"*, and is stated both in its own help and in line 3 of the AGENT.md preload. The difference from prior trials is that the gap is now **located and countable rather than described**: of **66 pack step files, exactly one names `doc show`**, and it is not an authoring step — the agent is told once at session start, then walked through six write verbs that never mention it again. **[Corrected 2026-08-15 (M48 Increment 12, T1):** the figure recorded here was **69**, an artefact of the counting command rather than of the pack — see the correction on the M48 Settle entry above; the denominator is **66**, measured on the binary the trial ran (1.0.0-rc.10).**]** Three refutations share the shape (`doc schema`, `doc list`, `doc show --task` all ship, none were found), the fifth consecutive trial where headline complaints dissolve into shipped capability.

**Two defects are M45's complete-fix lens turned on M47's own work, and one of them loses data.** `milestone provision` over a **non-registered leftover** destroys staged, unstaged *and* untracked work at **exit 0** under the ordinary success line, the untracked file unrecoverable — while `milestone discard` and `jigc uninstall`, verified in the same walk, both **refuse over a single untracked file**: the same destruction guarded at two doors and unguarded at a third, which meets M46 entry 11's rider trigger with the loss *shown* rather than inferred. And an **idempotent `rename`** (new title slugs to the current id, H1 already matching) dresses git's empty-commit refusal in the survivable-hook-rejection frame — asserting a rejection that never happened and routing to a re-run that can only fail identically — the un-swept point of an axis whose sibling (`same slug, different H1`) *is* fenced. A new **write-surface honesty** pair joins them: `doc author` silently ignores a corrected `title:` while acking the old slug, and an optional section omitted *as its own template instructs* still renders its heading into a committed doc.

**Recorded against ourselves, because a trial that only confirms is not verifying:** two claims died in verification — a pipe hiding `validate`'s real exit code, and `head` truncating a render — and two honesty items are declared rather than discovered later. The prose-vs-code contradiction **two** sessions found independently is the observer's own, introduced when the corpus template was authored, and is **not** a designed trap; what it legitimately evidences is that both doc-first paths surface such a conflict *before* authoring. And the G3 plant was **detectable as back-dated** (body `2026-08-04`, committed mid-session) and G3 said so in its first sentence — the catch is unweakened since everything that mattered concerned the ADR's content, but it is logged as a clean-room risk that did not visibly materialise, with the fix for next time (back-date the commit).

**What it owes onward: the conversion ledger is open, and that is the gate.** Every repro block is currently `UNPINNED` — correctly, since the trial ran under *no mid-trial fixes* — and **the 1.0.0 call is not taken until every row carries `pinned-by:` or a stated reason**; the three refutations owe `pinned_facts/` tests regardless of what else is built. The **latent-surface sweep** stays chartered and owed, its case strengthened by the fact that the one arm reaching an unfenced surface found the trial's only data loss. Two counted demands moved: M46 entry 2 (a walked Checkpoint still leaves no record) is at its **7th**, arriving unprompted from G2.

## 2026-08-09 — A coverage classification is a claim about the code, and it gets a floor under it

**The same mistake three times in two days, twice by agents and once by the reviewer whose whole job was to catch it — always the same shape: the classification was read off the artifact in front of the classifier instead of derived from the code.** `jigc rename` was called *untouched by M47* from a **file-level** diff (true of `rename.rs`, false of the verb — its behaviour moved in `cli.rs`, which gained `rename.commit-rejected` and the survivable frame while `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` went 2 → 10); then a set of surfaces was twice asserted *reached by no probe, therefore needs a trial arm* **without grepping the suites**, and one command dissolved most of the list (`commit_rejected_axis.rs` already drives `rename`, all four milestone record-only doors and `migrate-corpus` under a rejecting hook, its door set derived from `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`; `ingest_flow12.rs` drives the near-miss route). Both halves are our own ***a grep is not a fence*** rule in a new costume: **the census was of files, the property was about behaviours.**

**So: a rule for the judgment half, a fence for the mechanical half.** The rule lands in [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) → §5 (coverage semantics' home) — *derive the classification from the enumeration, the registry, the suites; never from a changed-file list, a charter, or a previous analysis; a file-level diff is a proxy for behaviour, and `reachable` is not `exercised`* — phrased to bind **at the moment of classification**, with a one-line pointer from [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) → triage, where *"is this already covered?"* actually gets asked. The fence is `crates/cli/tests/verb_suite_coverage.rs`: leaf verbs from the **clap tree** (the `format_json_success_axis.rs` enumeration seam, not a hand list), each asserted **named by at least one suite**, with the verb → naming-suites map printed *as the failure message* and, uncapped, by an `#[ignore]`d companion — because the recurrence is people not knowing where to look, so the lookup table has to be the thing the fence hands you.

**Two honesty calls worth recording.** First, **the fence states its own bound in its module doc: "named by a suite" is strictly weaker than "its behaviour is fenced"** — it catches a verb with *zero* coverage, never one with shallow coverage; letting the name imply more would be the law-1 defect this whole line of work is about. Second, **counting `format_json_success_axis.rs` would have made the assertion unfalsifiable** — its per-verb recipes are held exhaustive by a bijection against the same clap tree, so it names all 44 by construction — so it is excluded by a `const` with its reason, which is what converts the property into *some suite named this verb on purpose*. Verified against the tree: **no verb is actually uncovered today**, stated plainly rather than dressed up as a catch; the red was earned by two **applied mutants** (excluding `config_replace_remove_step.rs` → the two `config` step verbs report as holes with the map attached; forcing the matcher to always answer yes → the built-in negative control fires), both removed. A **negative control ships permanently** in the test, since a deliberately loose textual rule must still be able to say *no*.

## 2026-08-09 — M47 completion audit: `jigc uninstall` guards the fan-out worktrees — a declared bound rebutted on its basis, not overridden

**The teardown verb destroyed the state the wave had just promised to keep.** `uninstall`'s first act is `remove_dir_all(<repo>/.jigc)`, and the fan-out worktrees live inside it (`.jigc/worktrees/<sub-task-id>`, since M31 Inc 4/5 the **sole copy** of a sub-agent's code). M47 Increment 3 deliberately stopped the `squash: false` abort arm tearing those worktrees down, which makes *"a provisioned worktree holding uncommitted work"* a **normal, documented, promised-safe** state — and over exactly that state `jigc uninstall` exited **0** with the single line `- removed .jigc/`, having destroyed the sub-tasks' LLM-authored doc prose (in `.jigc/tasks/<id>/docs/`, never in the object DB), the worktrees' unstaged and untracked bytes, and the staged code with them (reduced to a pathless dangling blob). Reproduced live on rc.10. So `uninstall` now runs the **same probe its sibling teardown already runs** — registered worktrees under `.jigc/worktrees/`, then `git status --porcelain` — and blocks with **`uninstall.dirty-worktree`** before removing anything, naming each worktree and its entries and routing at the two honest exits `jigc milestone discard` already ships (get the work out, or `--force` the abandon), then re-run. **No new verb, no new flag:** `uninstall()` was already `Result<_, Finding>` and the dispatcher already renders routed `uninstall.*` findings at a non-zero exit — this is a correctness floor on an existing verb, expressed in the shape the wave standardised. `milestone.rs`'s `registered_worktrees` / `dirty_worktrees` become `pub(crate)` and are **reused rather than re-implemented**, so the two teardowns cannot drift apart on what counts as dirty. The probe **fails closed** under the same code (an unreadable `git` leaves safety *unknown*, and removing on an unverified probe is the defect itself), and it costs nothing when there is no `.jigc/worktrees/` at all — the clean arms (no worktrees; only clean worktrees) still tear down at exit 0, pinned, because a guard that refuses a legitimate teardown is its own defect.

**Why this is a *basis-has-changed rebuttal*, not an override of a declared bound.** [The roadmap's Increment 3 entry](implementation/roadmap.md) named this destroyer as a bound — *"pre-existing and outside M47"* — in the **same sentence** as its `provision_worktrees` sibling, and attached the widening clause (*"T0 makes 'a live worktree holding uncommitted code' a **normal** state"*) to the sibling while withholding it here. But the widening is a property of the **state**, not of either destroyer: the moment the abort arm stopped tearing down, every remaining unguarded remover of `.jigc/worktrees/` inherited it. The declared bound therefore rests on a basis its own increment falsified. This is precisely the reasoning M47 Inc 3 itself used to **invert a passing test** (`milestone_finalize_tears_down_the_provisioned_worktrees_on_an_aborted_finalize` — its rationale predated the worktrees becoming the sole copy), so applying it to the bound the same increment declared is consistency, not licence. [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)'s M46 rider loses its `uninstall` half for the same reason: the clause that justified deferring it — *"on the landed path the staged set … is safely in git"* — is **false for `uninstall`**, which is not on the landed path at all. **Deliberately out of scope, and stated rather than glossed:** `git worktree prune` is *not* added, so a successful teardown still leaves dangling `.git/worktrees/*` admin records — a real but non-destructive issue, left where the rider records it.

## 2026-08-09 — M47 completion audit (LOW): the preload's exit-flip class is the flip, not a cause — and the fence iterates the axis

**The class M47 T1 shipped excluded a real member.** The AGENT.md preload said the store sweep is report-only *"unless the sweep itself could not be trusted"* — true of three of the four conditions in `render::validation_store_exit_flips`, and **false** of `reconciliation.rename`, whose own trailer says the opposite: *"a structural-identity change this commit introduced; the sweep exits non-zero"* — a sweep that worked, reporting a real event it found. [The T1 entry](#2026-08-08--m47-increment-11-planning-decomposition) (2026-07-26 wave, *"The task said 'the one exception'; the tree says four"*) got the **no-enumeration** call right and the **class** wrong: it traded a stale lie for a narrow one on the same law-1 sentence. The clause now claims only what holds over the whole axis — *"unless one of a few conditions flips that exit, such as a doc stamped above this build's schema-version: then it exits non-zero and its closing line names the condition and why"* — the flip **is** the class, the cause stays where it is already stated per condition (the closing line), and the one instance an agent meets stays named. The alternative, listing four codes in a preloaded paragraph, is the content-that-rots the 2026-07-06 meanings-table retirement ruled out, and [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Exit semantics still owns the list itself.

**Why it shipped is the finding worth keeping: the fence checked one member of a four-member axis.** `bootstrap_names_the_ahead_exception` asserted the preload against `AHEAD_STAMP_PHRASE` — the member its author had in mind — so a clause false for `reconciliation.rename` stayed green. That is the incomplete-fix shape [M45's complete-fix contract](implementation/pinning.md) exists to prevent, in the wave built to remove law-1 lies. So the fix is the **axis**, not the sentence: the flipping conditions become one enumerable table (`render.rs` → `STORE_EXIT_FLIPS`) that `validation_store_exit_flips`, the JSON `report_only` field and the store trailer all key on — table order **is** precedence, the four ad-hoc booleans and the if-else chain are gone, and the trailer bytes are unchanged. Each member carries what a fence needs to drive it: a matcher, a **witness finding**, the closing line it renders, the words that line names the condition with, and `sweep_untrustworthy` — whether its flip means the sweep's own result cannot be trusted. `bootstrap_clause_covers_every_store_exit_flip` iterates that table through the **real renderer**: every member flips the exit through the shared predicate, every rendered closing line carries `STORE_EXIT_FLIP_PHRASE` ("exits non-zero", now interpolated into all four trailers) and names its condition, the preload states that promise — and **while any member is a sweep that worked, the preload may not state the class as an untrustworthy one**. A fifth condition must answer all five questions to compile, so it joins the fence in the same motion instead of silently falsifying the preload again.
