## 2026-08-09 — M47 Inc 11 T7: the fold-back, and what the live re-verify caught in the docs it was folding

**The hook-rejection gate lands as [MIGRATING.md](MIGRATING.md) → *Reconciling and backing out* #5, in meeting order** — the ladder is renumbered 1..8 rather than appended to, because the gate's whole claim is *where you meet it*: the commit phase, after the carryover gate and before the back-out verbs. The wave built the frame across the nine committing doors (Inc 3 T7) and **no user-facing doc said so**, which is exactly the state G1's rejecting-hook plant probes. The gate states the three things a rejection owes — git's stderr verbatim, what survived, the line to re-run — and names the **per-door** divergence rather than one flat promise, because there is no flat promise to make: `task finalize` keeps the task and its staged set, `migrate-corpus` keeps the migrated bytes written and staged (its re-run lands them), `milestone create` unwound record write **and** workbench so nothing survives. The chapter's fence is a test, not an `rg` in a commit message: `crates/cli/tests/foldback_truth.rs` asserts the ladder is numbered `1..n` with no gap, that **exactly one** gate owns the hook rejection, and that it names both diverging doors — so a later insert cannot leave two `5.`s or quietly flatten the per-door truth.

**Every claim in the chapter was re-verified against the built binary (the M42-T10 lesson), and the re-verify is what earned its keep — three of the fold-back's edits are catches, not restatements.** (a) **QUICKSTART's `pre-commit` hook claim was a law-1 lie**: *"It never blocks the commit (always exits 0)"* — the installed hook **exits 1** when the commit itself stages an out-of-band managed-doc rename (reproduced live: `git mv` of a managed adr + `git commit` → blocked, HEAD unmoved). That is the **designed M35 A+B amendment** ([reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → Out-of-band rename), so the doc — not the hook — is what was wrong; the bullet now states warn-only *plus* its one narrow refusal and the never-blocks-a-later-unrelated-commit bound. (b) **QUICKSTART placed the changelog at `docs/changelog/`** — the **pre-M38** home; the binary's own finding names `CHANGELOG.md`, so the paragraph gains the placement-vs-location distinction it never had. (c) The install commit's subject is `chore(jigc): install jigc workspace config`, not the `chore(jigc): install` the doc quoted. Two more claims were **stale-not-false** and folded: `--dry-run` now takes the refusing exit over a carryover state (Inc 4 T3) instead of forecasting a green, and the carryover gate is met at `task validate` / `--dry-run` before the commit boundary (Inc 4 T1) — both re-verified live.

**CLAIMED: built. NOT claimed: audited.** [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)'s project state records M47 as **built** as of 2026-08-09 with the roadmap section and flow 47 as its acceptance, and states the bound in the paragraph itself — the completion audit and its verdict are the milestone-completion workflow's next act, then rc.10, then G1–G3, then the 1.0.0 call. The same test fences it: the M47 span must carry `built, not audited` and must **not** carry a clean-audit phrase or a link to a persisted verdict artifact. The 2026-08-02 machine-loss note is kept but re-scoped — the *planning* record is what was recovered byte-exact; the lost build's own audit statistics are dropped, because they describe a build that no longer exists and would read as this one's. ## 2026-08-09 — M47 Inc 11 T3: the refuted facts become standing pins, and the ledger dispositions all 31 rows

**Three new pins, each a repro block made standing** (`crates/cli/tests/pinned_facts/`, pinning.md §3): **C1** — every documented depth of the slice grammar resolves (whole-doc · repeatable/slot/fields-only section · field leaf · item · item leaf · nested item · nested leaf · the bare-singleton alias), with the negative control that makes it a fact rather than a happy path — the address P2 actually ran elides the *section* segment and fails **identically on the write side**, so the claimed read/write asymmetry does not exist; **D10's refuted half** — a **bare path** is accepted as an `implemented-by` code anchor at the write, at `task validate`, at `finalize` and at the store sweep, with a bare path naming *no file* still blocking on `doc-code.symbol-exists` (the control that proves the acceptance is a resolving existence check, not an unchecked string), and the confirmed indistinguishable-projection half explicitly **not** blessed by it; and **A2's `left_out` stderr arm** — the agent-text advisory rides stderr while stdout stays exactly one JSON document, contrasted against a finalize that leaves nothing behind and prints the block on neither stream.

**The red-step obligation was discharged as an obligation, not an assumption.** [Baseline](completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md) §2 premise 6 says the non-empty-`left_out` **stdout** arm is pinned and the **stderr** arm is not; re-checked at HEAD — `finalize_manifest.rs:313` is the stdout/manifest arm, `pinned_facts/finalize_json.rs` is the chatty-hook purity arm, and no suite asserted the advisory's *stream* — so it is a new pin rather than a `pinned-by:` disposition. Verified discriminating by applied mutation: routing the advisory to stdout under `--format json` reddens it on the "stdout is one JSON document" assertion, exactly as P2's merged-stream capture did.

**The ledger dispositions every row, and two boundaries carry the UNPINNED ones.** All 31 RC-alpha4 labels (A1–A5 · B1–B7 · C1–C7 · D1–D12) plus the baseline's eight §2 premises now carry a disposition in `pinned_facts.rs`: confirmed → its fix increment's red test (named), refuted → the module here, everything else **UNPINNED with a stated reason**. The reasons are not shrugs: the wave's razor (*changes what surfaces say, never what surfaces exist*) routes a capability gap to M46, and **a capability gap has no false statement to fence** — pinning its absence would pin the gap as expected output, the anti-pattern the wave's ordering rule exists to prevent. **No duplicate pin is minted for B3** (`set-field --unset`): §3's obligation is that a refuted fact *has* a standing test, and `set_field_unset.rs` has held both halves since M41. **B2's block cites T1's suite by name** (`batch_author_rerun.rs`), so this increment's internal punt is tracked to a landing rather than to "a later task".

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 11 T2: the whole golden tree is a measured fixed point, and the doc that counts it stops estimating

**The regeneration is empty, and that is the result.** With T1 — the wave's last surface-changing fix — landed, `crates/cli/tests/goldens/compose` was deleted whole and rebuilt by `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 cargo test -p cli compose_goldens::`. The rebuilt tree reconciles to the committed bytes **exactly**: 612 files, `git status --porcelain crates/cli/tests/goldens/` empty, check-mode sweep 6/6 green. That proves the three things the check-mode suite structurally cannot — no cell's bytes moved, **no orphan** exists (a file nothing produces and nothing reddens), and no key is missing a file. **No finding:** increments 1–10 and T1 each re-blessed in place, so the empty diff is the wave's discipline holding, not an absent measurement.

**The doc that counts the tree was estimating, and the regeneration let it measure.** [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md):17's *"~1500 golden files … roughly 15% carry state-distinct information"* contradicted `:23`'s 612; correcting the count exposed that the *redundancy argument built on it was also wrong, and wrong in the safe direction*. Measured over the regenerated tree: **4 of 102 members vary across the six states — 24 of 612 files, ~4%**, not 15%. The premise that broke is the sentence's own — *"`start` is the genuinely state-sensitive dimension"*: `start` differs by state for **exactly** `form-vision` and `implement-from-spec`, the same two members whose *previews* differ, and for nothing else. All×all stands harder on the real number, so the argument is re-derived rather than deleted: 98 invariant members are 98 places where state-sensitivity appearing is a finding no narrower sweep would see. The measured wall (**≈13 s**, fixture construction included) replaces the estimated one in the same sentence.

**Three numbers, one adjudication, no back-editing.** `M45/VERDICT.md`'s **558** is now stated in `pinning.md` as what it is — a dated completion artifact, true at its writing — with the arithmetic that reconciles it: 612 − the 24 `creates-task: false` `start` cells the sibling-hunt's filter removal added − the 30 front-door + AGENT.md cells that joined with it. The VERDICT is left untouched (a completion record states its date's truth). **And §2's JSON-purity note is reconciled with what shipped**: its *"the success-path arm rides the golden sweep's invocations"* was not merely superseded but **impossible** — the sweep invokes only compose surfaces, so a verb it never calls is invisible to it, which is exactly how `task diff` shipped parsing `--format` and printing plain text at exit 0. Carried as a dated correction bracket naming M47 Inc 7's `format_json_success_axis.rs` and the bijection that keeps its recipes from being the hand list the rejected registry would have been.

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 11 T1: the one-shot clause dies, and what replaces it states the repeat rather than forbidding it

**The clause is deleted and the sentence re-stated, on all 14 surfaces in one commit.** Shipped: *"(run it instead of the create + per-leaf verbs, **or after them** — the create it implies over a doc this task already staged acks `already existed — copied in for update` and changes nothing)"*, in both the `per-leaf` and `per-entry` wrappings across the 13 pack steps of **both** packs, and its help-surface twin on `doc author --help`. **The replacement answers exactly what the lie got wrong and no more** — it speaks about *the create*, which is the call the false clause claimed was refused, and deliberately does **not** widen into "either order always works": on the four `per-entry` doctypes a payload item whose title mints an id the doc already holds still rejects the whole payload, and those steps' own continuations (M47 Inc 10 T7) already state that. A blanket "re-running is safe" would have swapped one law-1 lie for a subtler one.

**Swept by the sentence, and the fence is the sentence's absence, not its site count.** The 13 steps were selected by the exact four-line span they ship — only 3 wrap it in `<!-- once:batch-author-note -->`, the other 10 carry it inline, so the marker was never the selector. The new suite `crates/cli/tests/batch_author_rerun.rs` (in `g_compose`) fences three axes: the **behaviour** — `create` → `author` → `create` → `author` over one adr identity on one task, all exit 0 through the real binary, the second create acking the copy-in and the second author's prose surviving on `doc show --task`; the **composed surface** — *every* workflow of *both* packs enumerated from the loaded registries, previewed, with both streams checked against a set of rejection wordings (the shipped clause's own tokens **plus** *"only once per task"*, the form the trial's worker read it back in — `RC-alpha4/feedback-P3.md` §2); and the **help surface**, same fence. A non-vacuity arm asserts the batch note still composes into ≥8 workflows, so a sweep that stopped seeing the paragraph cannot pass green. Red at HEAD on the composed and help arms; the behavioural arm was green at HEAD **by construction** — it is the fact the clause contradicted, and B2's *refuted* repro block is discharged by it (pinning.md §3).

**Two pins moved with it rather than being left to redden later.** `help_truth.rs`'s M43 A4 test asserted the lie's presence verbatim (`"INSTEAD of"`, `"never after"`, `"rejects the second create"`) — a test that pinned a defect as expected output, the exact shape the wave's ordering rule exists to prevent — and now pins the **positive** half (the relation plus the copy-in ack), leaving the absence sweep to the new suite. `methodology_pack_compose.rs`'s `BATCH_CAVEAT_SPAN` (the byte-exact span its render-once dedupe asserts) moved to the new wording, and **132 compose goldens** re-blessed here — verified to be *only* the clause lines (144 hunks: 96 `per-leaf`, 48 `per-entry`), i.e. the edit's real blast radius with no unrelated drift riding along. Fenced-token rider: none of the 13 steps declares `states-constraints:` or references `{{schema:…}}`, so Increment 9's `CONSTRAINT_REQUIRED_TOKENS` and the copy-in biconditional carry no obligation here — stated so it is not an unexamined risk.

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Increment 10 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 10](implementation/roadmap.md) (the tier-2 understandability batch) into **9 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `4a0ad94` (tree clean; Inc 1–9 landed). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → the 2026-07-26 Settle — the human's up-front scope call (*"take all of it"*: **tier 2 ships all ~16 declared items**, no overload valve) and the fifteen *"non-fork blocking gaps settle by doing"* that carry N14–N22 and the `describe --format json` contradiction — plus the wave's boundary from the 2026-07-25 charter: **the wave changes what existing surfaces *say*, never what surfaces *exist***. Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 47 Increment 10 (and its ordering rationale: tier 2 lands late *because* its prose edits are the ones most able to silently un-state a contract, which is what Increment 9's named-fact guard now fences); [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) (the three laws + the style guide — the tier this increment serves); [completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md](completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md) §3c (N14–N22) and [RC-alpha4/findings-verification.md](completions/artifacts/RC-alpha4/findings-verification.md) (A3 · B1 · B7 · C3 · C6 · D1 · D3 · D4 · D5 · D12 — every item is keyed to a verified row).

**Basis — every claim below was read in the tree at HEAD, not carried from the charter:**

- **The two lie-pinning goldens are inline asserts, not files under `tests/goldens/`.** The AGENT.md body golden is `crates/cli/src/adapter.rs:1429-1450` (a whole-body expectation over `bootstrap_file()`) plus the substring assert at `:1481` (`body.contains("store-scope \`jigc validate\` is report-only")`); the setup summary is an **`insta` inline snapshot** at `crates/cli/src/render.rs:4586-4593` carrying `- pre-commit hook → .git/hooks/pre-commit` verbatim. Each pins its lie *inside the same file as the fix*, so *"regenerated **with** their fixes, never before"* is satisfied by fixing and re-blessing in one commit — and by nothing else.
- **The hook path is already resolved; only the print is a literal.** `setup::resolve_hooks_dir` (`setup.rs:505`) shells `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks` — honouring `core.hooksPath`, the `.git`-is-a-file worktree case and the linked-worktree common dir — and **both** the install (`:296`) and teardown (`:480`) paths already use it. `SetupSummary` (`:675`) carries `line_file` / `allowlist_file` / `install_commit` and **not** the hook path, so `render::setup_success` (`render.rs:1762`) hardcodes `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. This is a plumb of a value the binary already computes — the roadmap's *"a seam plumb, not a reword"* is **verified**, and the worktree/`hooksPath` cases the literal lies about are the same cases `resolve_hooks_dir` already gets right.
- **The copy-in seam is singular, and "the five edit verbs" is exact.** `Task::read_or_copy_in` (`doc.rs:3652`) is the only production caller of `state::copy_in`, reached from six sites — `run_set_field` (`:479`), `run_unset_field` (`:612`), `run_set_slot` (`:1011`), `run_add_item` (`:1113`), `run_remove_item` (`:1445`), `run_retitle_item` (`:1603`) — i.e. **five verbs**, `set-field` twice (its `--value` and `--unset` arms). `doc author` does **not** ride this seam and is correctly outside the item: its create-arm already discriminates through `DocAck::Created.existed`, whose agent line (`render.rs:1393`, `"{address} (already existed — copied in for update)"`) is the mold the five edit acks copy.
- **The append prose is on four step files, not five — a charter premise corrected here.** `existing entries are untouched` / `appends the new` appears in exactly `packs/methodology/steps/author-{roadmap,ledger,decision,decisions}.yaml`; the charter's fifth surface is `doc author --help` (`doc.rs:199`). The sweep is therefore over **the clause**, never a count.
- **B1's third behaviour is characterized and neither shipped text states it:** new items append (existing entries genuinely untouched) · existing leaves update in place · **a payload item whose title matches any existing item rejects the whole payload atomically** (`write.already-present`, nothing staged, route to `set-field`/`set-slot`). The fix sentence is therefore a three-way statement, not a swap — and the append half is byte-verified accurate and **stays**.
- **`title-names-symbol` asserts a history it never consults.** `target_surface.rs:457-467` emits *"the heading still names a renamed/removed symbol"* from a **pure string heuristic** — a compound (camel/Pascal) identifier token in the item title that is not the anchored symbol — with no code resolution and no history read; the doc-comment directly above (`:436-450`) says exactly that.

The message the trial hit (`` `{address}` names no section `{section_id}` ``) names neither the sections that *do* exist nor the `#section/<item>` form, and its route is generic prose.
- **N22 is one message**: `base_mismatch_finding` (`finalize.rs:1195-1207`) prints `base.short` twice against a full 40-char `head_sha` in the same sentence. **N17 is one route**: `empty_commit_finding` (`finalize.rs:1262-1268`) offers only *"make a change, then re-run `jigc task finalize`"* — no abandon exit, though the shipped `jigc task discard` is the exit the write-path dead-end routes already name (`write.rs:5344-5350`).

So **no new fence was written** — a second comparator over the same two files would be dead weight, and the correction is recorded here instead of in duplicate machinery. The planner note stands corrected: the token was the deliverable; the fence was already load-bearing.

**N20 — the positional/flag split is *stated*, from one source, at both `create` verbs.** `jigc milestone create "<title>"` beside `jigc doc create --title "…"` reads as an inconsistency to an agent that has met only one of them. The rule behind it has been recorded in [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → The argument convention since M42 (a doc verb's title is a value written into a named leaf, so it is a flag; a work-unit's title is the unit's reason for existing, so it is the positional) and was stated on **neither** help. ## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 10 T6: the orientation surfaces stop overstating what they offer

**D1 — the affordance is advertised over the members it serves, and the rest are given their fallback.** `jigc workflow <id> --preview` refuses a `creates-task: false` workflow, and the refusal is *correct*: for a non-minting member the direct `jigc start --workflow <id>` **is** the preview (it composes, prints the steps, mints nothing). The lie was the advertising — orientation's bare `<id>` and `describe`'s *"to read **any one's** full step text"* quantified over the whole catalog, while **nothing in either catalog marks which members mint**, so the reader could not predict which ids the verb would refuse. Fixed by scope, not by behaviour, and not by a catalog marker (a marker is new surface, which this wave's boundary forbids): both lines now name the task-minting scope *and* the direct-run fallback, so a reader who guesses wrong is routed rather than stopped. The correctly-scoped statement had existed exactly once, in `jigc workflow --help` — the classic push/pull split this wave keeps meeting.

**`create-gates:` defines the noun it lists — as a permission, not a verb.** M42 moved the *gate list* off the `create.gate-blocked` refusal onto every composed task; the *meaning* stayed on the refusal, so an agent that had never tripped one met a bare list of doctype ids under a coined term. The line now carries the refusal's own two facts — what the gate grants and that anything else is refused — and the gate-less context still renders **no bytes at all**, definition included. The first wording spelled the grant as `` `jigc doc create` `` and the suite caught it: `methodology_pack_compose` asserts that **every** composed line containing `jigc doc ` carries `--task <id>`, and a definition is not a place to put a task-less command-shaped fragment. Kept as the rule, not the patch: on a composed surface a command-shaped string is an invitation to run it, so a definition names the permission (*"the doc-types this task is allowed to create"*) and leaves the runnable lines to the steps that solicit them.

**D12 — the severity label says whose grading it is, stated where the label prints.** M47 inc-8 fixed the trailer's *count* (severity, not probe family); the residue is the label itself: the trial read two identically-labelled `advisory ·` rows in one report with the trailer as the only discriminator. The note leads the rows rather than following them — a reader meets the qualifier before the labels it qualifies (law 3's shape), and the trailer three lines down was exactly what the trial did not connect to the row. It is **keyed on an `advisory` row being present**: `advisory` is the label whose scope-relativity the finding is about, so a blocking-only report renders no bytes (the omitting-context floor), and the **task** view never renders it — there the severity token *is* the verdict for the transaction in hand, so the note would be false there rather than merely noisy. It quotes **neither a command nor the `(gates at finalize)` marker** — the doors belong to the trailer's claim, which states them only where a gate exists, and the marker is a *per-row* label: printing its literal in a sweep-wide lead over a report with no marked row re-mints, one register up, the exact false-gate-claim class M42 closed. The suite caught that too, through the whole-stdout proxy `validate_leaves_a_gateless_store_finding_unlabelled` pins the closure with — the pin was right and the new line was wrong, so the line moved.

**`describe --format json` — the predicate was always about the prose surface; the arm is unpinned, not unparseable.** `render::describe`'s `Format::Json` arm has emitted a keyed serde object since M11, while the verb's help said *"don't parse it"* and [introspection.md](design/introspection.md)'s format predicate declared the output *"not valid JSON"* — the binary forbidding what the same binary serves through its own documented global flag (the 2026-07-26 Settle's settle-by-doing gap). Settled as a **scoping** correction, with no surface added or removed: the four format properties are properties of the `agent`/`human` prose (the surface the enforcement-by-format argument is about), and the json arm's posture is now stated rather than denied — it parses, it is *as unpinned as the prose* (no version governs it; any pack edit may move it), and the structural read a driver can depend on is `jigc doc schema`, the separately-versioned contract. Non-contractual is preserved by **absence of a promise**, which is what it always meant here; hostile-to-parsing was only ever the prose arm's lever.

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 10 T5: the read surfaces name their own shapes

**N16 — the `*` legend is gated on the marker, not on the `fields:` block, and the predicate is read off the rendered bytes.** `doc schema`'s plain listing printed `fields (* = author-required):` whenever a doctype had *any* top-level field, while `push_field_line` appends the marker at **every** depth. The legend is now one **listing-level** line between `doctype:` and the body, printed **iff a `*` renders**. The predicate is `body.contains(" *\n")` on the assembled body, not a second recursive walk of the contract: `push_field_line` is the sole writer of the marker and always closes the line, so the check *is* the render — a parallel walk is exactly the kind of second source that drifts from what the reader sees. Non-contractual presentation, so no `contract-version` bump; the json arm has carried `author-required` as a per-field boolean throughout and is untouched. 90 compose goldens re-blessed **with** the fix: −90 header parentheticals, +66 legend lines, 24 doctype×state cells losing the legend outright — the arithmetic is the census.

The help now states it; a prose-only pin would have been the same gap one register up, so the statement lands with a witness that drives the emitted bytes across the slice depths (slot slice, fields-only slice, whole doc) with **stderr byte-empty**, plus the omitting context that gives it meaning — a *blocked* read does carry the footer, on stderr, with stdout empty. Purity is a property of the served read, not of the verb. Named bound, not hidden: the whole-doc serve closes with the newline the stored bytes already end in (`println!` over content that ends in `\n`), so the golden compares against `COMMITTED_ADR + "\n"` — a doubled line terminator is neither a footer nor a banner, and folding it away with a `trim` would have been the test lying instead.

The test iterates the branch axis (one staging task, then two), which is the only axis the sentence has.

The projection is lifted verbatim by the store walk, so the one producer edit covers both scopes by construction — asserted at `collect_from_source`, not twice through the binary.

**N17 — the empty-commit block gets its second exit, and the unit-blindness M42 removed from its sibling.** One constructor serves both planners; its route named `jigc task finalize` (no id) for a blocked **milestone** too, and offered only "make a change" for a block whose other honest answer is *this produced nothing; abandon it* — while `jigc task discard` had been the recorded abandon verb one file over since M43. Each arm now re-runs its **own** door with the id filled in and names its **own** abandon verb, and the milestone arm's message stops calling a milestone "task". That is exactly the fix M42 made to `base_mismatch_finding` on this file, applied to the sibling it skipped.

**N22 — one sha form, and the form is the full one.** Both constructors named the pinned base by its git-abbreviated `short` and HEAD by the full 40-char sha in the same sentence, so the two identities being *compared* did not look comparable. The engine is fed only HEAD's full sha (`plan_finalize`/`plan_milestone_finalize` take `head_sha: &str`), and abbreviating it here would print a prefix **git never minted** and could be ambiguous — so the one form available at this seam is `BasePin::sha`, and both sides render in it. Threading a short HEAD in from the CLI would change two public engine signatures for a presentation choice; recorded as considered and declined. The test iterates the producer axis (pin × {task, milestone} ∪ overlap) and asserts, per finding, that **every** sha-shaped token in message *and* route is one width — a property, not three string pins.

**N19 — and the gate the route needed that its sibling never did.** `jigc validate`'s orphan sibling has handed over the runnable `jigc migrate <rel> --as <doctype>` since M40 while `jigc ingest`, over the same file, offered bare prose. It is the same argv here — but the sibling speaks only for the *unregistered* tier, and ingest's near-miss also fires for an **already-adopted** doc that stopped conforming (the M42 stale-stamp case), for which adoption is not the repair at all. So the offer is gated on unregistered **and** migratable (`jigc migrate --as` hard-rejects a doctype with no `migrate-<doctype>` workflow), and each other arm says which of the two it is. This is the *widen-a-guard, re-derive the response across the whole new domain* rule applied to a route: a mechanical route that hard-rejects, or repairs the wrong thing, is law 2 failing one level down.

**The grouped-scope bullet, honestly counted.** Of every route arm reshaped here, exactly **two** have the shape `Route::mechanical` renders — a single leading backticked real argv ± trailing prose: `add-from-spec`'s `jigc doc show <spec-addr>` and ingest's `jigc migrate <rel> --as <doctype>`. The other nine are two-argv or mid-sentence directions and stay `Human`; the constructor was not contorted to reach the roadmap's count. Both carry a `route().kind()` assertion, and the ingest pair is built with the CLI parse fence installed. Rule recorded at [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → The route fence.

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 10 T3: the five edit verbs state the copy-in, off one bit rendered in one place

**The bit was already decided; nobody carried it.** `Task::read_or_copy_in` is the only production caller of `state::copy_in` — six call sites, five verbs (`set-field` twice, its `--value` and `--unset` arms) — and it *knew* which of its three cases ran, then returned a bare `String`. So the five edit doors copied a committed doc into the task and said nothing, while the create door had stated the same effect since M43 (`existed`): an incomplete fix over the **verb** axis, whose cost the trial measured — the worker learned their task had staged (and would re-promote) a committed ADR from the *finalize* output (RC-alpha4 P4-6). The read now returns an `EditBase { source, copied_in }` and the note is appended in **one** place, off a single `DocAck::copied_in()` in `render::doc_ack` — not per-variant at six construction sites — so a verb that later joins the copy-in seam cannot silently stay quiet; `create`/`author` answer `false` there and keep their own lines.

**The note states the consequence, not just the event.** `(copied in for update — the committed doc is now this task's staged copy, re-promoted at finalize)` — `DocAck::Created`'s *"already existed — copied in for update"* in the edit doors' mold, extended by the clause that answers the question the trial's worker actually had unanswered (what happens to it at finalize). It fires on the write that copied in and **only** that write: a second edit in the same task reads the already-staged copy (`read_or_copy_in` case 1) and stays quiet, so the note marks a state transition rather than becoming per-write noise to habituate to.

**Declared bound:** the **JSON ack shape is unchanged** — no new key on any of the six variants. This wave changes what surfaces *say*, not what they *are*, and a driver already reads the fact structurally (the `create` ack's `existed`; the staged copy itself via `jigc doc show <addr> --task <id>`). Recorded here rather than glossed, the same posture T2 took on `setup`'s JSON arm.

**The test iterates the axis and reports the whole axis.** One test, six arms (the five verbs, `set-field` both ways) over the *same* committed `spec`, each in its own freshly minted task so every first write really is a first touch, each followed by a second edit that must stay quiet. Its assertions are **collected, not per-arm**: a bail on arm 1 would leave the other five unmeasured, which is precisely the reporting shape that let the create-door fix look complete. Red at HEAD on all six first-touch arms (`crates/cli/tests/copy_in_ack.rs`).

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 10 T2: the install summary names the hooks dir git resolved, and the JSON arm's silence is a declared bound

**A plumb, not a reword — the value was already computed and thrown away.** `setup::resolve_hooks_dir` has shelled `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path hooks` since M19, and both the install and the teardown use it; only `SetupSummary` never saw it, so the summary printed the literal `.git/hooks/pre-commit` — a law-1 lie in exactly the two cases the resolution exists for (`core.hooksPath` set, and a linked worktree whose hooks live in the **main** checkout's common dir). `install_precommit_hook` now returns the path it wrote and `install` renders it through `display_hook_path`: **repo-root-relative when the hook lives inside the repo** (so the overwhelmingly common case still reads `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, consistent with the two repo-relative neighbours on the same list), **absolute when it does not** — because no repo-relative path can name a hooks dir outside the repo, and the printed path has to be followable from the directory the user ran `setup` in. Both sides are canonicalized before the strip, so a symlinked root (macOS `/var` → `/private/var`) still reads relative rather than falling back to a noisy absolute.

**The test drives the emitted line, and the criterion is resolvability, not string shape.** Both arms (`core.hooksPath`; a linked worktree) run the real binary, extract the path **out of the emitted summary line**, resolve it the way its reader would — absolute as-is, relative against the cwd `setup` ran in — and assert that path *exists* and canonicalizes to the hook the install actually wrote. That is what the literal failed: at HEAD both arms resolved to a non-existent file. The `insta` inline snapshot was re-blessed **with** the fix in this commit, and deliberately re-fixtured to `my-hooks/pre-commit` — a snapshot carrying the old literal would re-pin the lie the moment the plumb regressed.

**Declared bound, not glossed:** `--format json` keeps its four stable keys and gains **no** `hook_file` — additive machine surface is outside this wave's boundary (*"changes what existing surfaces say, never what surfaces exist"*), so a driver parsing the JSON still cannot learn where the hook landed and must read the text or re-run `git rev-parse` itself. Routed to the M46 Settle ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → the capability wave, entry 12); the value is carried in `SetupSummary`, so landing the key later is a one-line addition.

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 10 T1: the preload tier names the exception as a **class**, and one instance by name

**The task said "the one exception"; the tree says four.** `render::validation_store_exit_flips` flips the store sweep's exit for an unreliable pack probe, an out-of-band `reconciliation.rename`, an unmigrated corpus **and** the above-current stamp A3 caught — the four the trailer already distinguishes in prose. Writing A3's literal suggested clause (*"with one exception: a doc stamped above this build's schema-version"*) would have traded a stale lie for a fresh one on the same sentence, in the same law-1 tier, on the surface that is trusted without re-checking. So the shipped clause states the **predicate** — report-only *unless the sweep itself could not be trusted* — and names the one instance an agent actually meets: *"as when a doc is stamped above this build's schema-version: then it exits non-zero and its closing line says why."* The other three stay unenumerated on purpose, by the same rule that retired the per-code meanings table in 2026-07-06: a four-item list in a preloaded paragraph is content that rots, and the closing line the clause points at is the surface that already names whichever one fired. The exception list itself stays owned by [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Exit semantics, not restated in the adapter.

**The fence is an agreement assert, not a wording assert.** The failure mode A3 exposed is not bad wording — it is two surfaces drifting apart about one exit while each is locally plausible. So the shared condition is lifted to `render::AHEAD_STAMP_PHRASE`, the trailer's own words, and the trailer **composes from it** (`ahead_corpus_trailer()`, byte-identical to the literal it replaces) rather than restating it — one source on the output side, the statement-==-constant idiom the exit-code line already uses; `adapter::bootstrap_names_the_ahead_exception` then asserts **both** the emitted `.jigc/AGENT.md` bytes and the rendered trailer carry the phrase and state the non-zero exit. Rewording either surface alone now reddens — which is the property the four-day stale window lacked, and the reason the fix is a seam rather than a sentence. Driven on the emitted body (`bootstrap_file()`), never the raw const; the whole-body golden and the six `agent-md--*` compose goldens were regenerated **with** the fix in this commit, never before it.

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 9 T3: `create.singleton-copy-in` becomes a biconditional with the `{{schema:<T>}}` ref it guards

**Deleting the ref deletes the obligation, and every tier goes quiet by design.** T1/T2 sharpened *ref ⇒ declaration ⇒ named facts*; run the arrow the other way and the sharper sibling opens — delete a declarer's `{{schema:<T>}}` reference and the per-soliciting-step tier plus both named-fact tiers stand down (correctly: there is no solicit left to fence), the pack loads clean, and the step's prose keeps promising a payload that never follows. Demonstrated live before the fix on the dev pack's `record-changelog`: with `{{schema:changelog}}` gone, `jigc start --workflow single-task` exits 0 and composes *"The target schema and its batch payload … follow — one call places the whole entry over the staged buffer:"* above **nothing**, then tells the agent to pick a category from "the enum members the schema above lists". So the pair closes into a **biconditional**: a step declaring `create.singleton-copy-in` must reference a `{{schema:<T>}}` whose `T` resolves to a singleton, or pack load fails naming step + code. [validation.md](design/validation.md)'s `workflow-refs.schema-ref-resolves` guards only the opposite case (ref present, schema absent) and structurally cannot see this one.

**Structural, not token-based — that is what keeps it inside A-3.** The cheap fix is to demand the promise sentence's words; that would put jigc's prose vocabulary on the pack author and leave the presence-never-content bound. The check reads the same enumerable signal the tiers above already read (the `{{schema:<T>}}` ref × `T`'s `singleton` flag, per-origin), so it costs one branch on a load already performed. It lands **inert**: all six shipped declarers reference a singleton today (`record-changelog` + `author-migration` → `changelog`; `author-migration-roadmap` / `-decisions-log` / `-deferral-ledger` / `-vision` → their own). Acceptance sweeps the axis from the trees, never a hand-list: every declarer stripped of its ref in turn through the real binary (dev via `JIGC_PACK_DIR`, methodology via a `packs.yaml` listing, each constituent in isolation), with the shipped compositions and a manifest-less pack staying clean.

**Declared boundary, recorded rather than silently narrowed:** a step that deletes **both** its ref and its declaration leaves the fence family entirely — the approved family is *every step carrying a `states-constraints:` code* — so that case is out of scope by the family's own definition. It is a pack author deliberately retiring an obligation (the review checklist's job), not a receipt outliving what it stands for.

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 9 T2: the append half of the copy-in contract is owed wherever items can double

**A flat map cannot carry a conditional fact without demanding a lie.** T1's `CONSTRAINT_REQUIRED_TOKENS` buys what binds at *every* declarer of a code; the copy-in contract has a second half that binds only where the solicited singleton can hold repeating items — authored items **append** to the committed ones, so re-authoring one the doc already holds **would double** it. Flat-mapping those two tokens onto `create.singleton-copy-in` would force methodology's `author-migration-vision` (whose slot-only `vision` schema correctly says the slots OVERWRITE) to state a falsehood the fence itself demanded — a law-1 lie; omitting the tier leaves five declarers free to un-state half a contract they still declare, exactly the incomplete sweep this wave is named against. So the append half rides a **conditional tier** whose owe-set is derived like the per-soliciting-step tier above it: the solicited singleton's own schema declares ≥1 `repeatable:` section ⇒ the step must also state `cli::pack::COPY_IN_APPEND_TOKENS`. Read off the **same schema load** `assert_singleton_copy_in_stated` already performs — no second signal to drift, and **never an exclusion list**.

**The condition partitions the shipped declarers exactly, so the tier lands inert.** Measured over both trees (enumerated, not hand-listed): the five item-bearing declarers — `record-changelog` + `author-migration` over `changelog`, and `author-migration-roadmap` / `-decisions-log` / `-deferral-ledger` — already state both facts; `author-migration-vision` states neither and owes neither. The acceptance sweeps **both** directions through the real binary (`crates/cli/tests/stated_at_fence.rs`): each owed append fact deleted in turn from each item-bearing declarer blocks pack load naming step, code and token (dev via `JIGC_PACK_DIR`, methodology via a `packs.yaml` listing, each constituent in isolation), and the **omitting context is asserted, not assumed** — the exempt declarer set is computed as declarers minus item-bearing, each member proven to state neither token, and the pack proven to load clean; a manifest-less pack stays unchecked. Same A-3 bound as T1: the *named facts* of a contract jigc itself owns, never prose quality.

## 2026-08-08 — M47 Inc 9 T1: a declared constraint code must buy the contract's named facts, over the whole fence family

**The fence stops buying a receipt.** Both stated-at tiers checked that a code was *declared*; the M47 review deleted 590 characters of copy-in/append contract prose from a migrate step, kept its front-matter code, and every fence stayed green. So each fenced code now carries a **required-token set** in a code-side map (`cli::pack::CONSTRAINT_REQUIRED_TOKENS`), checked at pack-load against the declaring step's own body — the whole **fence family**, every declaring step of every manifest-shipping constituent in **both** packs (10 steps today), not `finalize.yaml` parity: the break was demonstrated on `create.singleton-copy-in`, so a finalize-only guard would not sweep its own axis. Every miss in a pack is reported at once, naming step + code + token, with the M43 route floor's recovery (restate the fact, or drop the code).

**Both normalization halves were chosen from real misses, not from caution.** Matching is over a whitespace-collapsed, ASCII-case-folded view of the body: methodology's `finalize` opens a sentence with *"Unstaged"* (case), and the copy-in sentence wraps across a hard line break in **every** declarer (whitespace). Raw-byte matching would have failed on presentation rather than content. The tokens are authored in that normalized form, fenced by its own unit test so an unsatisfiable token cannot ship, and the map is **bijected** against `AMBUSH_CLASS_CODES` + `SINGLETON_COPY_IN_CODE` iterated from the consts — a fenced code without tokens is back to presence-only; a token demand on a code jigc does not fence would put jigc's prose demands on a pack author's vocabulary.

**This stays inside the A-3 presence-never-content bound** ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md)): what is bought is the *named facts of a contract jigc itself owns* — never register, order, phrasing or quality — and the acceptance sweeps the axis mechanically rather than pinning the repro: every (declaring step × declared code × required token) triple derived from the two shipped trees × the map, deleted in turn from a copied pack, must block the real binary at pack load naming all three (`crates/cli/tests/stated_at_fence.rs`, both seams — a `JIGC_PACK_DIR` dev copy and a `packs.yaml`-listed methodology copy); the deletion is asserted to bite, so the loop also proves the shipped prose really carries every token the map claims, and the covered code set is asserted equal to the map's, so a pack that stopped declaring a code cannot pass by having nothing to sweep. The shipped compositions stay clean (no pack prose is edited here — the fence lands inert) and a manifest-less pack stays unchecked. **Declared bounds, recorded not glossed:** a project-layer forked step (`.jigc/config/steps/*.yaml`) is outside this fence exactly as it is outside every pack-load fence, and a pack-authored code outside jigc's fenced set carries no token requirement. [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md)'s *"no prose-matching"* and *"Presence-only (A-3)"* clauses are revised where they stand — this change is what makes them false.

**One inseparable repair rides along:** `upgrade_v1_v2.rs::build_v2` wrote a synthetic `finalize.yaml` declaring all three staging codes over a body stating none of the facts (its own comment recorded that it stays stated-at-fence-conformant — true of the tier that then existed). The new fence reddens it, so its v2 rewrite now re-states the three contracts; a commit carrying only the fence could never have reached a green gate.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 9 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 9](implementation/roadmap.md) (the named-fact guard — the fences stop buying presence alone) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `759db05` (tree clean; Inc 1–8 landed). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → the 2026-07-26 Settle, **Decision 12** (build the named-fact guard — both stated-at fences are presence-only and were **broken live**: 590 characters of copy-in/append contract prose deleted with the front-matter code kept → clean build, clean pack load, contract gone; and any cross-pack parity must be over **contract facts, never a field list**, because dev shadows methodology — `pack.rs:916`, *"dev first = dev-highest"* — and the two `commit` schemas genuinely differ), **as re-scoped by the pre-decompose review**: the guard covers the whole **fence family** — every step carrying a `states-constraints:` code, in **both** packs — rather than `finalize.yaml` parity alone (the demonstrated break was on the `create.singleton-copy-in` migrate-step fence, so a finalize-only guard would be a fix that does not sweep its own axis, in the wave after the complete-fix contract), and the "named fact" mechanism is pinned as a **`constraint-code → required-token(s)` map checked at pack-load**, the only shape that stays inside the A-3 presence-never-content bound. Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 47 Increment 9; [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → The stated-at fence (the structural tier + the M44 per-soliciting-step tier) and the honest-bounds list; [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) (the A-3 bound — presence-conformance, never content-scoring); [multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md) → Collision resolution (whole-definition shadow, no field-level merge) + the pack-local body-reference rule; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1–§2.

**Basis — every claim below was read in the tree at HEAD or measured over the shipped pack bytes:**

- **The hole is structural, not incidental.** Neither pack-load assert reads one byte of step prose: `assert_stated_at` (`pack.rs:381`) unions each manifest-shipping origin pack's steps' `states_constraints` and checks the 4-member `AMBUSH_CLASS_CODES` const has ≥1 declarer; `assert_singleton_copy_in_stated` (`:471`) derives its owe-set from `schema_refs(&def.body)` × the referenced schema's `singleton` flag. Deleting the contract sentence while keeping the code changes **neither** input — and deleting the `{{schema:<T>}}` ref deletes the **obligation itself**, which is the sharper sibling: the composed text still says the payload *"follows:"* with nothing following, and `workflow-refs.schema-ref-resolves` only guards the opposite direction (a ref whose schema is absent).
- **The compose goldens are not the fence, and the regen is exactly the risk.** The goldens carry these step bodies verbatim, so a shipped-tree prose deletion reddens them *today*; but Increment 11 performs the **full golden regeneration** immediately after the ~16-item tier-2 prose batch, and a golden blesses whatever bytes it is regenerated over. The pack-load guard is what survives a regen — which is precisely the increment's *Proves* clause (*"the tier-2 batch that follows cannot silently un-state a constraint"*).
- **The fence family is exactly 10 steps / 5 codes, enumerated over both packs.** `finalize.left-out` + `finalize.nothing-staged` + `finalize.carried-staged` on dev `steps/finalize.yaml` and methodology `steps/finalize.yaml`; `finalize.promote-clobber` on both packs' `steps/migration-finalize.yaml`; `create.singleton-copy-in` on six — dev `record-changelog` (M47 Inc 8's new declarer) + dev `author-migration`, methodology `author-migration-{roadmap,decisions-log,deferral-ledger,vision}`. **Both copies of each sibling are live**: steps are never precedence-shadowed across packs (a workflow's `{{include: step:X}}` resolves against its *own* pack — [multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md)), and the fences already iterate `origin_packs` **in isolation**, so requiring the same code's facts in each pack's own step **is** the cross-pack parity — over contract facts, with no field list compared anywhere.
- **The token set was measured over the shipped bytes, not guessed.** Whitespace-collapsed + ASCII-lowercased, over all 10 declaring steps: `finalize.left-out` → {`unstaged`, `untracked`, `left out`} · `finalize.nothing-staged` → {`nothing staged`, `refuse`} · `finalize.carried-staged` → {`--carry-staged`, `this task was minted`} · `finalize.promote-clobber` → {`--approve`, `retire`, `fidelity diff`} · `create.singleton-copy-in` → {`copies the committed body in as`, `edit base`, `overwrites`} — **0 misses**. The normalization is load-bearing in **both** directions and was chosen from the misses it fixes: methodology's `finalize` opens a sentence with *"Unstaged"* (case), and the copy-in sentence wraps across a newline in **every** declarer (whitespace). So the fence lands **inert on the shipped packs** and no pack prose is edited by this increment.
- **The append half partitions exactly on a structural signal the step already renders (T2's basis).** `append` + `would double` are present in exactly the **five** declarers whose referenced singleton has ≥1 `repeatable:` section (`changelog` · `roadmap` · `decisions-log` · `deferral-ledger`) and absent from the one that has none (`author-migration-vision` — `vision` is slot-only and states `OVERWRITES` instead). So the append fact is owed **where items can double** and exempt where they cannot — derived from the schema the step already references, the same owe-set style `assert_singleton_copy_in_stated` uses. Flat-mapping it onto the code would demand a false statement of the vision step; dropping it would leave five steps free to un-state half the named contract.
- **One shipped fixture is inseparable from T1.** `upgrade_v1_v2.rs::build_v2` (`:299`) writes a synthetic `finalize.yaml` declaring **all three** staging codes over the body *"Validate and commit the task as one logical commit (v2 rewrite)"* — which states none of the facts — into a pack `dir_pack_with_version` copies **whole from the embedded tree, `config/schema-manifest.yaml` included**; the fixture's own comment records that the declaration is kept *"because a manifest-shipping pack must stay stated-at-fence-conformant (the M43 pack-load fence)"*. The new fence therefore reddens it, and only T1 repairs it: one task, one commit.
- **Two declared bounds, named rather than glossed.** (1) A **project-layer** step (`.jigc/config/steps/*.yaml` — a `config fork`/`replace-step` native file) is outside every pack-load fence, which scopes to manifest-shipping constituents (the freeze-gate skip-on-absent precedent); a forked step's prose stays unguarded. (2) A step that deletes **both** its `{{schema:}}` ref **and** its declaration leaves the fence family entirely — the approved scope is *"every step carrying a `states-constraints:` code"*. Neither is a narrowing of the roadmap's scope: both sit outside the family it names.
- **The jigc side gets the axis fence instead.** A pack-authored code outside jigc's fenced set carries no token requirement (the consts are code-side *"because the obligation is jigc's, not the pack author's"*); what is fenced is a **bijection** between the map's keys and `AMBUSH_CLASS_CODES` + `SINGLETON_COPY_IN_CODE`, iterated from the consts rather than hand-listed, so a future fenced code cannot join with an empty requirement.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** Decision 12 plus the review's re-scope settle the mechanism, its family and its A-3 bound; what remains are elaborations *inside* the settled spec and they are pinned in the tasks (the normalization rule, the three token sets, the schema-derived append tier, the biconditional's direction). **No composed bytes change** — this increment is pack-load code, tests and one design doc, so **no golden moves**; a moving golden means something else was touched.

- **T1 — the fence buys a named fact, not just a declaration.** A code-side `REQUIRED_FACT_TOKENS` map (beside `AMBUSH_CLASS_CODES` / `SINGLETON_COPY_IN_CODE`, same rationale — the obligation is jigc's) carries each fenced code's contract facts as literal tokens, and a new `assert_named_facts_stated` walks **every step of every manifest-shipping origin pack**: for each declared code in the map, every token must appear in that step's body under the measured normalization (ASCII-lowercase + whitespace-collapse — both halves are load-bearing, per the basis). A miss bails at pack-load naming **the step, the code and the missing token**, with a route telling the author to state the contract in the step that solicits the write it gates. Wired into `make_pack` on **both** branches (the memoized embedded pair and the live filesystem path), beside its two siblings. `upgrade_v1_v2.rs::build_v2`'s synthetic v2 `finalize.yaml` is repaired **in this commit** — it declares the three staging codes and must state them; it stays a genuinely *changed* body (that fixture's subject). [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) is revised in the same motion, because this task makes its current text false: the structural tier's *"no prose-matching"* and the per-soliciting-step tier's *"Presence-only (A-3)"* become **presence-of-a-named-token**, the honest bound is restated (the fence buys that the named fact is *present*, never that the prose is *good* — the A-3 line holds), and the cross-pack posture is stated (each manifest-shipping pack is checked alone, so both sibling steps carry the same facts — parity over contract facts, no field list). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli stated_at_fence::` passes with a **mechanically enumerated axis loop** — for every (declaring step × declared code × required token) triple derived from the two shipped pack trees and the map (never a hand-list), deleting that token's occurrences from a copied pack makes pack load **fail naming step, code and token** — plus real-binary seam arms in both packs (a `JIGC_PACK_DIR` dev copy and a `packs.yaml`-listed methodology copy each exit non-zero through `jigc start`), the shipped-composition controls still clean, and the manifest-less control unchecked; and `cargo test -p cli pack::` passes with the map↔const bijection test. The axis loop is **red at HEAD** (deleting the copy-in paragraph while keeping its code loads clean today — the review's live break). The in-process/real-binary split is the declared M43 proof split (seam fences in-process over `FilesystemPack`, the pack-load door proven through the real binary). - **T2 — the append half of the copy-in contract is owed wherever items can double.** T1's map carries the facts that bind at *every* declarer; this task adds the tier that binds **conditionally**, derived from the structural signal the step already renders: when a step declaring `create.singleton-copy-in` references a singleton whose schema has ≥1 `repeatable:` section, its body must also state the append facts ({`append`, `would double`} — measured present in exactly those five steps). The schema is already loaded at this seam by the sibling fence, so the derivation reuses it rather than minting a second signal, and the slot-only `vision` step stays exempt **by construction** — not by an exclusion list, and never by demanding a statement that would be false there. *Done:* `cargo test -p cli stated_at_fence::` passes with the axis extended — deleting the append sentence from **each** of the five item-bearing declarers (enumerated from the trees, both packs) reddens pack load naming the step and the fact, **and** the vision step with no append statement still loads clean (the exemption is asserted, not assumed); red at HEAD for all five.
