[surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md)'s per-soliciting-step tier states the owe-set as a biconditional, with the both-deleted case recorded as the family's declared boundary. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/pack.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/stated_at_fence.rs`, `design/surface-contract.md`.)*

**Why this order.** T1 first because it lands the map, the normalization and the pack-load seam every later arm reuses — and it is the task that makes `surface-contract.md`'s *"no prose-matching"* false, so the doc model is corrected once, at the point of change; T2 completes the **fact** axis on top of that map (the conditional tier is meaningless before the unconditional one exists); T3 is independent of both and closes the **obligation** axis, kept separate because it is a different mechanism (structural, schema-derived) with its own red step and its own boundary statement.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 8 N7 fix: the pin rule is keyed on the task's **unit kind**, and the axis it is pinned over is *door × unit kind*

T1 relaxed `jigc start --task <id>` unconditionally, and `resume_in_repo` resolves `.jigc/tasks/<id>/` for **any** id — so a **milestone sub-task**'s resume door became looser than its only commit boundary, the precise inversion `storage.md` declares the increment avoids. Reproduced live in one repo state: `jigc start --task <sub>` exit 0 (full composed step text, footer advertising that very door as the resume route), `jigc workflow single-task --task <sub>` exit 1, `jigc task finalize <sub>` refusing outright with `finalize.milestone-sub-task`, and `jigc milestone finalize <m>` — the sub-task's *only* commit door — blocking on the moved history because the sub-agent worktrees were cut from the shared pin. Before T1 the resume door also refused, so the inversion was **new**.

**The fix is (a), not (b): discriminate, do not re-document.** The bound in `storage.md` is stated as an invariant with a reason that still holds — a read door may never be looser than its own commit door — so `resume_in_repo` now reads the unit kind with `engine::milestone::owning_milestone`, **the same membership test `jigc task finalize` mints its sub-task refusal from**, never a second rule, and raises the identical blanket refusal `reenter_in_repo` raises. The two doors' prose is one constructor (`blanket_base_pin_refusal`) so it cannot drift. The read sits **inside** the divergence branch, beside the schema load, so a task at its pin still pays for no membership scan.

**Why the suite stayed green is the finding's real lesson: the arm written to pin the non-goal did not iterate the axis.** `sub_task_re_entry_keeps_the_blanket_base_pin_refusal`'s resume half drove a **top-level** id (`top-task`) and only its re-entry half used the sub-task — so the one door × unit-kind cell the relaxation broke was never driven. It is now `sub_task_read_doors_keep_the_blanket_base_pin_refusal`, iterating **both** read doors over the sub-task in one repo state against the top-level control, so a third door added later is covered by construction rather than by memory (the M45 axis rule applied to the axis *this* task's own non-goal lives on).

**The second face — the composed footer — is scoped per unit kind, not deleted** (law 1, the Inc 4 T4 mold). T2's parallel claim ends *"once a sibling task commits a path this one also touches, resuming or finalizing here blocks and names the overlapping paths"*, which on a sub-task is false twice over: finalizing there refuses outright, and the milestone door blocks on *any* moved history, not on overlap. `Composition` gained `sub_task_of`, populated at the **shared** re-compose spine so both doors carry it, and the sub-task arm names the milestone's commit boundary instead. Every other compose door is correct by construction: the three fresh-mint forms and `jigc migrate` mint a task that belongs to no milestone (membership is `add-task`'s alone), and `milestone execute` / `workflow --preview` carry no task id, so the footer is inert there. Because the struct has no `Default`, a new compose door cannot silently inherit the top-level claim — it must decide. `storage.md`, `finalize.md` and `write-commands.md` are revised in the same commit: each named only the re-entry door, and naming one member of a two-member axis is what invited the relaxation.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 8 T5: `jigc milestone create` names what it landed, in both project shapes

N13 landed on the `jigc setup` mold — the door that commits on the operator's behalf says **which** commit — so the ack now names the record's repo-relative path, the record commit's short sha, and the next step as a real argv (`jigc milestone add-task <id> "<intent>"`, built through the checked `Route::mechanical` constructor, so the CLI-seam parse fence covers the printed line for free). Through rc.9 it printed only `minted milestone:<id> (shared base <sha>)` while landing `chore(milestone): open record …` and writing `docs/milestone-records/<id>.md` — a commit the operator discovered later in a `git log`, if at all (law 2, nothing hides).

**The honesty is in the omission, and it is a value, not a string.** The record half is carried as `Option<CreatedRecord>` set by *the same discrimination the door itself makes* — a `[dev ▸ methodology]` project materializes a record and commits it; dev-only does neither — so the dev-only arm renders **no bytes** for those two lines rather than a path and a sha that do not exist. That would have been precisely the law-1 lie this task exists to close, and it is unreachable by construction rather than by remembering. The same posture covers the sha itself: the post-commit `rev-parse --short HEAD` read-back sits on a commit that already landed, so a git hiccup degrades to naming no sha (the `setup` `InstallCommit::Skipped` posture) — never to reporting a landed `create` as failed, and never to printing `unknown`.

**Both arms are driven through the real binary, on the emitted bytes.** `milestone.rs` extracts the named sha from stdout and hands it to `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`, asserting it resolves to the record-opening commit at HEAD, and extracts the named path and stats it; the dev-only arm asserts the commit count is unchanged **and** that neither claim appears. The next step is not pattern-matched but **run**: the test lifts the backticked argv out of the printed line, substitutes a real intent for the `"<intent>"` slot, and executes it — so a next step that stopped being followable reddens. The pinned `--format json` envelope stays exactly `{text, hook_output}`; the growth rides inside `text`, and a third arm asserts the key set verbatim.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 8 T4: the store trailer counts by severity, names the milestone door, and one family it had to scope

N10 landed on both arms — the trailer's count moved from `gates_at_task` (which never consults severity) to the row label's own `gates_at_finalize`, so the row and the trailer can no longer contradict each other in one report, and the door list gained **`jigc milestone finalize`** beside the two task doors, because `milestone_boundary_gate` drives the same shared `validate_task` entry under the same cascade and blocks exit 3 on the same families. **The decomposition's red-step assumption — *"every finding the trailer counts as gating is one the milestone gate can actually see"* — was checked against the emit sites and is FALSE for one family, so the sentence is scoped rather than widened over a falsehood.** `workflow-refs.*` is emitted by the store sweep (family 2) and by **compose** (`crate::start`) and by no task-scope path at all: `engine::validate::validate_task` runs staged-instance conformance, the committed-store reconciler, `ref-resolves` and `doc-code` — there is no workflow↔refs pass in it — so neither task door nor the milestone gate can ever see one. The M42 sentence was therefore already false for that family (proven live: a dangling `{{ include: step:not-a-step }}` shadow printed `blocking (gates at finalize) · workflow-refs.include-resolves` and *"these gate at `jigc task validate` / `jigc task finalize`"*). It is **not** a `GATES_NOWHERE` member — a hard gate does exist, at `jigc start` — so the new `gates_at_compose` predicate *re-doors* the claim instead of withdrawing it, and the exclusion lands in the **shared** predicate so the row label stops lying too. All/none/mixed shapes are unchanged; the mixed sentence gains a compose clause only when such a finding is present. Three arms in `validate_envelope.rs` drive real committed stores through the real binary (advisory-only → no gate claim; advisory + blocking sibling → counts 1 and names all three doors; a workflow-ref break → compose only), and `design/validation.md` is revised in the same commit.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 8 T3: the changelog step authors a real entry, and two premises it corrected on the way

N9 landed as Settle Decision 14 specifies — `record-changelog.yaml` solicits through the `{{schema:changelog}}` seam (schema listing **and** fillable batch payload, generated) with the copy-in/append constraint stated above the solicit and `states-constraints: [create.singleton-copy-in]` declared, the two being inseparable (`pack.rs` → `assert_singleton_copy_in_stated` reddens pack load for the seam without the declaration). The step is **followable end to end with no rejected call**, proven on the emitted bytes: the new `changelog_step_subset.rs` arm extracts the composed step's own `doc create` line and its own `doc author` invocation, runs both verbatim, fills only the `<…>` values of the *emitted* payload skeleton (structure is the pack's, prose is the agent's), and ends at a staged `### added {#added}` group **with notes**, `task validate` exit 0, and a finalize landing that entry in `CHANGELOG.md`. The step directs the entry to `unreleased-changes` and to omit the `releases` entry — work stages a change, cutting a release stays `record-change`'s deliberate pass, which is what makes that workflow's suppression reason (*"routine change recording already rides `single-task`'s record-changelog step"*) true; the reason ships **byte-unchanged**, and the test now anchors it to the step it names.

**Two decomposition premises were wrong and are corrected here rather than worked around.** (a) `{{ cli.create-changelog }}` does **not** expand to the bare literal the step hardcoded — the renderer wraps every `{{cli.<id>}}` ref in the command-ref frame ``Run: `<cmd>` ``, as `single-task`'s four other refs already show. The ref is kept (it is the consistent surface, and `author-change.yaml` solicits the identical create through it), and `changelog_step_subset.rs`'s extractor learned the frame — so the pinned assertions (exactly one create line under `single-task`, zero under `implement-from-spec`/`sub-task`, the emitted line admitted verbatim) hold on the same semantics, with the frame-stripping widening the zero-arms rather than loosening them. (b) The rationale *"an already-staged doc rejects a second create"* is **false** at HEAD: a second `jigc doc create changelog` over a staged or committed singleton is admitted and acks `already existed — copied in for update` (M43 law 2). The new step therefore states no such thing, and create → batch-author is a genuine sequence, not a pair of alternatives. **Observation carried, not fixed here** (out of this task's file scope): `pack/steps/author-change.yaml` still prints that false claim — a law-1 lie on a shipped step, candidate for the wave's tier-2 wording batch.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 8 T2: the two surfaces that promise the multi-task sequence now describe the one the binary runs

**Each claim is driven, not re-worded.** `author-vision.yaml`'s advisory sends the agent away to `do-research`; it now also names the way back — commit the research in a **separate task**, leave this one open, re-compose with the literal `jigc start --task {{task.id}}` — and the step's own RE-COMPOSE paragraph states the condition that makes the return work (a commit landed elsewhere re-pins this task **while its paths stay disjoint** from this task's own). The proof is a new `flow_form_vision.rs` arm that follows *that* ordering end to end through the real binary — mint `form-vision` over an empty store, finalize a whole `do-research` task while it stays open, then re-compose, ground, re-compose, author, finalize — which is the exact sequence the shipped spine arm never ran, because it commits its research **before** minting `form-vision`. Every write in that file now names its `--task`, which is redundant with one task open and the only accepted form with two.

**The footer's parallelism claim is scoped, never deleted** (law 1, the Inc 4 T4 mold): *"…so you can run them in parallel **while their work stays disjoint**; once a sibling task commits a path this one also touches, resuming or finalizing here **blocks and names the overlapping paths**"* — the `decide_base_repin` rule stated where the promise is printed, at both doors it governs. Two `start_compose.rs` arms drive the literal claim rather than assert the sentence: two open tasks each written through its own `--task`, one finalizes and the other resumes and finalizes on top of it (all exit 0, two commits), and the counter-arm where both touch one path, where the resume blocks naming it.

**The regen's blast radius was checked as a set difference, not trusted.** 180 goldens moved: the 174 that carry the footer line, plus exactly the 6 `workflow-preview--form-vision--*` cells the step edit touches (`start--form-vision--*` is inside the 174). No unrelated cell rode along.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 8 T1: the resume door's pin test is the commit door's, and two elaborations it forced

N7 landed as Settle Decision 10 specifies — `jigc start --task <id>` calls the identical `engine::finalize::decide_base_repin` over the identical facts, the re-pin in-memory only — with three elaborations recorded rather than left in the diff. **(a)** The schema set the promote-destination half of the footprint needs is loaded **only on divergence**, so a task at its pin pays nothing for the new decision and the common path stays byte-identical. **(b)** `pinned_base_mismatch_routes_to_task_discard` (`anyhow_route_spans.rs`) was **retargeted to the milestone sub-agent re-entry door**, not converted to an overlapping-resume arm as the decomposition sketched: that file's declared scope is anyhow-embedded spans riding the checked `Route::mechanical` constructor and explicitly excludes `Finding` routes, and after the fix the resume door's block *is* a `Finding` route — while re-entry keeps the byte-identical anyhow span. The overlapping refusal is pinned in `start_resume.rs` instead, where arm (d) contrasts both doors in **one repo state**: resume re-pins, re-entry refuses. **(c)** `write-commands.md`:146 was revised with the pair the decomposition named (`storage.md`, `finalize.md`) — it stated the blanket rule verbatim (*"the CLI never operates a task off its pinned base"*), so leaving it would have shipped a law-1 lie about the very behaviour this task changed.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 8 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 8](implementation/roadmap.md) (the greenfield behaviour batch — N7 resume, N9 the changelog step, N10 the store trailer, N13 the silent mint) into **5 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `e8c615f` (tree clean; Inc 1–7 landed). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → the 2026-07-26 Settle, **Decision 10** (N7 — align the resume door to the overlap-aware rule and revise `storage.md`'s pin paragraph; `finalize.md`'s M17 amendment already revised the rule for one sibling on the rationale *"the unconditional rejection proved wrong for serial-task shapes the methodology itself mandates"*, and its scope bound was drawn against the **milestone** sibling — the *resume* sibling was simply never enumerated) and **Decision 14** (N9 — fix the step so `record-change`'s suppression reason becomes true; it uses the `{{schema:changelog}}` seam, which **newly obligates** `create.singleton-copy-in`, because hand-writing the grammar would re-introduce exactly what M43 Inc 3 deleted from twelve templates; M43's suppression fence is presence-only **by design** and cannot catch a false reason), plus the Settle's non-fork gap list (N10's second arm — the store trailer names only the two task doors while the milestone doors gate on the same findings). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 47 Increment 8; [baseline](completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md) §3b (N7, N9, N10) + §3c (N13); [storage.md](design/storage.md) → The per-task working area; [finalize.md](design/finalize.md):147 (the M17 amendment); [changelog.md](design/changelog.md); [validation.md](design/validation.md):363 (the trailer must not claim a gate that does not exist); [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → law 1 + The stated-at fence; [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The commit model; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1.

**Basis — every claim below was read in the tree at HEAD or reproduced live against the installed `1.0.0-rc.9` in a throwaway `git init` repo:**

- **N7 reproduces exactly, and the three siblings' asymmetry is real.** In one repo state (task `do-a-thing` minted, then an unrelated `UNRELATED.md` committed): `jigc start --task do-a-thing` → *"pinned to base c66731f but you're on 69de81f — switch back with `git checkout …` or `jigc task discard …`"*, exit 1; `jigc task validate do-a-thing` → exit 0; `jigc task finalize do-a-thing` → **landed** `c1e6315`. The read-only door is strictly harsher than the commit door, and its route offers only destructive exits.
- **The guard is one blanket `pinned.sha != head.sha` at two sites, and only one of them is in scope.** `resume_in_repo` (`start.rs:1709`) and `reenter_in_repo` (`:1786`) share byte-identical refusal prose. The **re-entry** sibling is the M31 milestone-shaped door — its commit boundary is `plan_milestone_finalize`, whose base equality `decide_base_repin`'s own doc comment calls *"consciously unchanged"* — so relaxing it would make a read door **looser** than its commit door, the inverse of the defect. It is therefore a **declared, tested non-goal**, not an unswept axis: T1 pins it strict rather than leaving it to inference.
- **The overlap-aware test is a pure engine decision already in hand.** `engine::finalize::decide_base_repin` (`finalize.rs:594`) takes `(task_id, task_dir, base, head_sha, changed_paths, dirty_paths, schemas)` and returns `NoDivergence` / `Repin` / `Err(vec![base_overlap_finding])`; the block's message and route (*"the moved history overlaps the task's work on `…`"* / *"resolve the overlap … or discard the task"*) name the overlapping paths and claim **no** commit, so they are honest at a read-only door as written. The schemas the promote-destination half needs are already loaded in `compose_task_workflow` (`defs.all_schemas`), one call below the guard.
- **The re-pin path needs no compose change to bring the new commit into view.** `compose_task_workflow` already feeds `index::load_committed(…, &head.sha)` and `committed_store(repo_root, …)` from the **actual** HEAD, not the pin — so an accepted re-pin renders the just-committed research without further work. This is what makes the increment's *Proves* reachable.
- **One shipped test pins the blanket refusal and only this fix can repair it.** `pinned_base_mismatch_routes_to_task_discard` (`anyhow_route_spans.rs:429`) commits an unrelated `more.md` and asserts the refusal — a **disjoint** case, so it goes red the moment the rule becomes overlap-aware. It moves in T1's commit, converted to the overlapping arm.
- **The two prose surfaces are real and measured.** The compose footer's *"so you can run them in parallel"* lives at `render.rs:272` (+ its unit at `:3247`) and appears in **174** compose goldens and 4 test literals (`multi_pack_acceptance.rs`, `start_compose.rs`, `config_fill.rs`). `form-vision` mandates the sequence through `packs/methodology/steps/author-vision.yaml` — its research advisory says *"consider running `do-research` first"* and its body then says *"Now RE-COMPOSE … `jigc start --task {{task.id}}`"*, i.e. the exact door N7 dead-ends. The shipped `flow_form_vision.rs` spine commits **both** research docs *before* minting `form-vision`, which is precisely why the defect never showed there.
- **N9 reproduces, and the empty changelog really does validate clean.** Following `record-changelog.yaml` verbatim (`jigc doc create changelog --title Changelog --task <id>`) staged a changelog whose `## Unreleased Changes` and `## Releases` are both empty; `jigc task validate` printed only the `file-state.staged-copy` advisory and exited **0**.
- **The fix shape is buildable and admitted by the gate — checked, not assumed.** `jigc doc author changelog --from-file -` under a `single-task` task (create-gate `{type: changelog, as: change}`) was driven live and produced a conformant `### added  {#added}` group with real notes, exit 0. The `{{schema:changelog}}` seam already renders the schema **and** a fillable `jigc doc author changelog` payload skeleton (`goldens/compose/dev/workflow-preview--migrate-changelog--fresh.txt`), so the step gets its grammar generated rather than hand-written. `{{ cli.create-changelog }}` (`commands.yaml:92`) expands to the identical `jigc doc create changelog --title Changelog --task …` line the step hardcodes today.
- **The new obligation is real and is not migrate-scoped.** `assert_singleton_copy_in_stated` (`pack.rs:471`) iterates **every** step of a manifest-shipping constituent — `owner.list(PackResourceKind::Steps)` — and reddens pack load for any step whose body carries `{{schema:<T>}}` with `T` singleton and whose front matter omits `create.singleton-copy-in`. `changelog` is `singleton: true`. So the seam and the `states-constraints:` declaration are **inseparable**: a task adding only the seam can never reach a green gate. Budgeted into T3 exactly as the *Grouped scope* requires.
- **N10's severity blindness is structural, and the surface already contradicts itself.** `gates_at_task` (`render.rs:664`) consults `GATES_NOWHERE` and the un-baselined per-doc discriminator but **never severity**; the trailer counts with it, while the per-finding label uses the severity-aware `gates_at_finalize` (`:698`). `validation.doc-code.title-names-symbol.severity` defaults **advisory** (`pack/config/knobs.yaml:276`) and the code is **not** in `GATES_NOWHERE` — so a store sweep whose only finding is that one prints the row `advisory · doc-code.title-names-symbol …` and then the trailer *"these gate at `jigc task validate` / `jigc task finalize`"*: the row and the trailer disagree in the same report.
- **The milestone door genuinely sees the same findings.** `milestone_boundary_gate` (`milestone.rs:2834`) copies the persisted merged docs into a scratch staging area and drives the **shared** `validate_task` entry with the same severity cascade, tracked-status predicate and `doc-code` invoker as the per-task gate, then blocks exit 3 committing nothing. Blast radius is small — no golden carries the trailer; four `managed_vs_foreign.rs` / `validate_command.rs` assertions do.
- **N13 reproduces live, including the compounding.** `jigc milestone create "Wave One"` printed exactly `minted milestone:wave-one (shared base c1e6315)` while landing `e3b0103 chore(milestone): open record for milestone:wave-one` and writing `docs/milestone-records/wave-one.md` — commit, path and next step all unnamed, and HEAD moved under every open task. `run_create` (`milestone.rs:451`) returns that one string; `materialize_and_commit_record` returns only the hook stream, so the sha needs the same post-commit `rev-parse --short HEAD` read `commit_install` already does. **No golden and no test asserts the line**, so the ack is free to grow. `--format json` stays `{text, hook_output}`.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** Decisions 10 and 14 settle N7 and N9 including their prose halves; N10 and N13 are Settle non-fork gaps that settle by doing. What is left are elaborations *inside* settled specs, pinned in the tasks below — and the two places where a fact could not be established from the tree are written as **red-step assumptions to prove**, never as bases (T4's milestone-door family coverage; T3's *"the suppression reason becomes true without an edit"*).

- **T1 — the read-only resume door adopts the finalize guard's overlap-aware test.** `resume_in_repo`'s blanket `pinned.sha != head.sha` refusal is replaced by the identical `engine::finalize::decide_base_repin` call the commit door makes — same inputs (base→HEAD changed paths, dirty working-tree paths, the task's promote destinations via the shared `plan_promotions` sweep), **never a re-implementation** — so resume proceeds against HEAD as the *effective* pin on disjoint history and keeps the block, naming the overlapping paths, on overlap. The re-pin is **in-memory only**: `base.json` is never rewritten (finalize's landed-only discipline; a later invocation re-derives the decision). [storage.md](design/storage.md)'s *"A task is **pinned to its base** … switch back or discard"* paragraph and [finalize.md](design/finalize.md):147's M17 amendment are revised **in this commit** to enumerate the resume sibling and state the rule once for both doors. `reenter_in_repo` is **untouched** — the M31 milestone-shaped sibling whose commit boundary is the consciously-strict `plan_milestone_finalize`, so relaxing it would invert the defect. *Done:* `crates/cli/tests/start_resume.rs` (already registered in `g_compose`) gains four arms driving the real binary: **(a)** disjoint — task minted, an unrelated file committed, `jigc start --task <id>` exits **0**, re-composes the task's own workflow, and a doc committed by that intervening commit is **in view** in the composed text; **(b)** overlap — the moved history touches a path in the task's footprint → exit non-zero with `finalize.base-mismatch` whose message **names the overlapping path** and whose route carries no destructive-only exit; **(c)** the un-refusing control the *Grouped scope* demands — `base == HEAD` still resumes exactly as today (no case that succeeds now begins to refuse), and (b)'s repo state is one that **already refuses at HEAD**, so the change is provably only ever refusal→success; **(d)** the declared non-goal pinned — `jigc workflow <W> --task <sub>` off its pin still refuses. `pinned_base_mismatch_routes_to_task_discard` (`anyhow_route_spans.rs:429`) moves **in this commit** — it asserts the disjoint refusal the fix deletes, and only this change repairs it. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/start.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/start_resume.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/anyhow_route_spans.rs`, `design/storage.md`, `design/finalize.md`.)*
- **T2 — the two surfaces that promise the multi-task sequence stop promising one the binary refused.** With the door fixed, `form-vision`'s step and the compose footer are made **followable and true**, each proven by driving its own literal claim rather than by re-wording alone. `packs/methodology/steps/author-vision.yaml`: the research advisory and the re-compose instruction state the supported ordering explicitly — grounding research may be committed **in a separate task** and the vision task re-composed afterwards — so an agent that follows the advisory is carried through instead of dead-ended. `render.rs`'s `task_state_lines` (`:272`, unit at `:3247`): the parallelism claim is **scoped to the truth** (law 1, the Inc 4 T4 mold) — parallel tasks hold while their work stays disjoint; a task whose base moved on **overlapping** paths blocks and names them. *Done:* **(a)** a new arm in `crates/cli/tests/flow_form_vision.rs` follows the step's **own mandated ordering** end-to-end through the real binary — mint `form-vision` first over an empty store (the research advisory renders), then mint + author + **finalize** a `do-research` task, then run the step's literal `jigc start --task <vision-task>` re-compose, `set-field grounded-in`, re-compose, author the three slots, finalize — every call exit 0, the grounding research's `findings` prose present in the second compose, one commit landed; red today at the re-compose. **(b)** an arm proving the footer's claim literally: two open tasks each addressed by its own `--task`, one finalizes, the other resumes and finalizes — both exit 0; plus the overlapping counter-arm, whose refusal is what the scoped wording now describes. The 174 compose goldens and the 4 test literals are regenerated **with** the change (`UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`), never ahead of it. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `packs/methodology/steps/author-vision.yaml`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/flow_form_vision.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/multi_pack_acceptance.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/start_compose.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/config_fill.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/goldens/compose/**`.)*
- **T3 — the changelog step yields a real changelog, and the suppression reason becomes true.** `crates/cli/pack/steps/record-changelog.yaml` is rewritten on the `author-migration.yaml` mold: the create-or-update solicit through `{{ cli.create-changelog }}`, the **`{{schema:changelog}}` seam** (schema + fillable `jigc doc author changelog` payload, generated — no hand-written address grammar, the thing M43 Inc 3 deleted from twelve templates), and the copy-in/append constraint stated **above** the solicit, with `states-constraints: [create.singleton-copy-in]` declared in the same edit — the two are **inseparable**, since `assert_singleton_copy_in_stated` (`pack.rs:471`) reddens pack load for the seam without the declaration, so a task carrying only one can never reach a green gate. The step must be followable with **no rejected call**: the create + per-entry path and the single batch payload are alternatives, never a sequence (an already-staged doc rejects a second create), and the step says so. *Done:* a test drives the composed `single-task` step's own emitted lines **verbatim** through the real binary and ends with a staged changelog carrying a real `unreleased-changes` group **with notes** (not the empty skeleton reproduced above), `jigc task validate` clean, and a finalize landing `CHANGELOG.md` with that entry; `changelog_step_subset.rs`'s subset assertions (exactly one create line under `single-task`, zero under `implement-from-spec`/`sub-task`) stay green, repaired in this commit if the rewrite moves them; the 12 compose goldens + the 3 step-body test literals regenerate with the change. **The red-step assumption this task must prove rather than assume:** `record-change.yaml`'s suppression reason is left **byte-unchanged** on the Settle's *"fixing the step closes both"* — the executor asserts the sentence reads true against the fixed step (routine change recording really does ride it) and, if it does not, **says so and halts** rather than quietly editing the reason and its six `describe` goldens. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/pack/steps/record-changelog.yaml`, `crates/cli/tests/changelog_step_subset.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/start_compose.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/config_fill.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/multi_pack_acceptance.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/goldens/compose/**`, possibly one new suite + its group root.)*
- **T4 — the store trailer classifies by severity, and names the milestone door.** `store_trailer`'s report-only branch counts with a **severity-aware** predicate — the `Blocking && gates_at_task` criterion the per-finding label already uses — so an advisory or demoted finding is never counted as gating and the row and the trailer stop contradicting each other; the all/none/mixed sentences keep their shapes. The gating sentence names the **milestone** boundary alongside the two task doors, because `milestone_boundary_gate` drives the same `validate_task` entry under the same cascade and blocks exit 3. [validation.md](design/validation.md):363–:382 is revised in the same commit — the criterion is stated as *"a gate exists **and would block**"*, and the door list is corrected. *Done:* a test over a real committed store, driven through the real binary: **(a)** the only finding is the advisory-by-default `doc-code.title-names-symbol` → the trailer makes **no** gate claim (the *"gates nowhere"* sentence), red today; **(b)** an advisory finding plus a blocking sibling → the mixed sentence counts **1**, not 2; **(c)** the gating sentence names `jigc milestone finalize` beside `jigc task validate` / `jigc task finalize`; the four shipped trailer assertions (`managed_vs_foreign.rs`, `validate_command.rs`) move with the change where the wording shifts. **The red-step assumption to prove, not assume:** that every finding the trailer counts as gating is one the milestone gate can actually see — the executor checks the counted families against `milestone_boundary_gate`'s inputs and **scopes the sentence** if a family does not reach it, rather than shipping a second door claim that is false for part of the set. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `design/validation.md`, `crates/cli/tests/managed_vs_foreign.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/validate_command.rs`, possibly one new suite + its group root.)*
- **T5 — `jigc milestone create` names its commit, its path, and the next step.** The ack grows from the bare `minted milestone:<id> (shared base <short>)` onto the `jigc setup` mold (`render.rs:1639` — *"install commit → <sha>"*): the record commit's **short sha** (read the way `commit_install` reads its own, after the commit lands), the record's **repo-relative path** (`record_pathspec`, already computed for the stage), and the **next step** as a real, parseable argv (`jigc milestone add-task <id> "<intent>"` — the `Route::mechanical` checked constructor buys the parse fence for free). Honest in both arms: under a dev-only project (`compose-embedded-methodology: false` — no `milestone-record` schema, no record commit) the ack names **no** commit and **no** path, and still names the next step; a law-1 lie in the degraded arm is the failure this task exists to avoid. *Done:* a test drives the real binary in both project shapes — **(a)** methodology composed: stdout names a short sha that `git rev-parse` resolves to the landed `chore(milestone): open record …` commit, names `docs/milestone-records/<id>.md` which exists on disk, and names the next-step argv; **(b)** dev-only: no sha, no path, no false claim, next step still named; **(c)** `--format json` still emits exactly `{text, hook_output}` (the contract is untouched — the growth is inside `text`). Red today on (a) and (b): the line is asserted by **no** shipped test or golden. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, one milestone test suite.)*

**Why this order.** T1 first because every other N7 surface is only *true* once the door works — a prose repair landed ahead of it would ship a new lie; T2 second, carrying the two claims T1 makes keepable plus the 174-golden regen, kept out of T1 so the behaviour diff stays readable; T3, T4 and T5 are mutually independent and follow in the increment's own N9/N10/N13 order, each a self-contained gate-green unit.

## 2026-08-07 — M47 Increment 7 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 7](implementation/roadmap.md) (the machine-output pair — `task diff`'s envelope and `blocking_probes`) into **4 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `b580221` (tree clean; Inc 1–6 landed). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → the 2026-07-26 Settle, **Decision 11** (the `task diff --format json` shape, settled rather than picked at build time, with the non-empty empty state) and **Decision 7** (the hook is re-settled onto a top-level `blocking_probes` array rather than any grep that reaches into finding objects), the pre-decompose review's advisory that replaced `staged_docs[].body` with identity-pointing-at-`doc show`, the cross-model review's Blocker 1 (the pretty-printer makes a line-oriented grep unbindable, so the match is specified in the roadmap and carries two negative controls), and the **2026-08-05 plan halt** (one key, not two; `[[:space:]]`, not `\s`). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 47 Increment 7; [baseline](completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md) §5 (S9 — `--format` is global so all 44 leaf verbs *accept* it and the `adapter.rs` fence stays green if every verb ignores it; S10 — the envelope needs **no new data**) and §5.1 (P4); [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) §2 + Stream discipline; [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The M19 pre-commit backstop; [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md):15; [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) laws 1–2; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1–§2.

**Basis — every claim below was read in the tree at HEAD or reproduced live against `target/debug/jigc` in a throwaway `git init` repo:**

- **The defect reproduces exactly as charted, and the dropped parameter is the whole cause.** `TaskCommand::dispatch` (`task.rs:268`) is `TaskCommand::Diff { id } => run_diff(cwd, &id)` — the only arm of the six that does not take `format`; `run_diff` (`:341`) has no `format` parameter at all. Live: `jigc --format json task diff <id>` printed the plain-text `# staged docs` section (126 bytes of markdown, not JSON), and over a task with an empty `docs/` and no code diff it printed **0 bytes on stdout, 0 on stderr, exit 0**. The roadmap's `task.rs:255` line reference is stale (the file moved under Inc 3/6); the arm is named by symbol below, not by line.
- **S10 re-verified: no new data.** `TaskArea::base()` (`:708`) reads a `BasePin`, which already serializes as `{sha, short}` (`engine/state.rs:449`); `git_diff` returns the diff string; `TaskArea::staged_docs()` (`:1879`) returns path-sorted `(filename, body)` pairs. Everything the envelope needs is in hand inside `run_diff`.
- **The one-key decision has a shipped precedent in this very file.** `dropped_staged_docs` (`task.rs:450`) already derives the `task-discard` ack's `dropped` list by `strip_suffix(".md")` over the same `docs/` dir — i.e. the identity extraction the halt settled is not new code shape, it is the sibling ack's, reused. `staged_docs()` is private and returns bodies; T1 exposes the identity form, never the bodies.
- **`blocking_probes` has exactly one construction site and it is additive.** `render::validation_store` (`render.rs:450`) is the only store-scope JSON renderer; its `Format::Json` arm already re-opens the serialized report as a `serde_json::Value` and inserts `scope` + `report_only`, so a third top-level key is the same move. Live at HEAD the store envelope is `{findings, report_only, schema_version, scope}` — keys **alphabetical**, pretty-printed, exactly as the cross-model review said. No test asserts the exact key **set** (the `report_only` consumers at `flow37_rename.rs:1266`, `managed_vs_foreign.rs:363`, `validate_command.rs:363`/`:413` all read one key), so the addition breaks nothing.
- **The severity split the hook needs is real and cascade-resolved.** `validation.doc-code.symbol-exists.severity` defaults **blocking** and `validation.doc-code.title-names-symbol.severity` defaults **advisory** (`pack/config/knobs.yaml:263`, `:276`), and the store report carries the resolved cascade severity per finding — so an advisory-only `doc-code` report is constructible: `title-names-symbol` fires (`target_surface.rs:442`) when an item title carries a compound identifier that is not its **resolving** anchor's symbol, which is precisely the false-drift class M40 demoted and the hook still warns on today.
- **The specified ERE was run, not trusted — and the newline collapse is load-bearing.** Against `/usr/bin/grep -E` (BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD, Darwin 25) over three real-shaped pretty-printed reports: collapsed with `tr -d '\n'`, `"blocking_probes"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\[[^]]*"doc-code"` **matches** the blocking report, does **not** match an advisory-only report whose `findings` carries `"probe": "doc-code"` while `blocking_probes` holds another probe, and does **not** match an empty `blocking_probes` with the same finding present. Without the collapse it matches **nothing** — so the `tr` is part of the mechanism, not tidiness. *Recorded honestly rather than glossed:* on this machine `/usr/bin/grep` advertises itself *"GNU compatible"* and **does** honour `\s`, so the 2026-08-05 rider's *"never matches on this platform"* is stronger than this box supports; the decision stands unchanged and unweakened — `[[:space:]]` is portable where `\s` is not guaranteed, and it is the idiom `setup.rs:194` already ships.
- **The collapse must stay pipeline-local.** `PRECOMMIT_RENAME_BLOCK` (`setup.rs:248`) greps the *same* `$report` for `git mv …` routes and feeds them to an `awk` that pairs one route per **line**; collapsing `$report` itself would fold every route onto one line and silently break the M35 rename block. Named here so the executor threads `tr` through the doc-code pipeline only.
- **The hook change is a gate-atomic unit — three shipped pins move with it.** `precommit_hook_body_golden` (`setup.rs:1621`) is a **byte** golden of the rendered script; `rendered_hook_warns_iff_doc_code_content_finding_always_exits_zero` (`:1515`) drives the real rendered body under `sh -c` against **canned** reports keyed on `"probe":"doc-code"`; and `precommit_hook_acceptance.rs` drives real `git commit`s. The first two go red the instant the match changes, and only the same change repairs them.
- **The existing hook acceptance survives the severity filter, checked rather than assumed.** `commit_warns_on_stale_anchor_but_succeeds` (`precommit_hook_acceptance.rs:396`) renames a **cited** symbol, so its finding is `doc-code.symbol-exists` — blocking by default, therefore still in `blocking_probes`, therefore still warning. The clean-store, unconfigured-repo, wrapped-hook and both rename arms key on nothing the change touches.
- **P4's enumeration is 44 and its seam already exists; what is missing is the *success* half.** `machine_output.rs:54`'s `leaf_verb_paths()` walks the clap `Command` tree, and walking the real binary's help tree independently yields exactly **44** leaves. That suite asserts the **reject** surface for all 44 and the success surface for **one** verb (a landed finalize). Structurally every other dispatch arm threads `format` into a `render::*` that matches `Format::Json` — `TaskCommand::Diff` is the sole exception in the tree — and a smoke pass over 16 verbs' success paths (`setup`, `describe`, `validate`, `doc list`/`schema`, `task list`, `ingest`, `upgrade`, `start`, `milestone create`/`list-tasks`/`discard`, `config set`, `migrate-corpus`, …) found every one emitting exactly one JSON document on stdout. That is evidence, **not** the proof the roadmap demands, so it is written as T4's red-step assumption, not as a basis for skipping work.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** The key count, the key set, the empty-state posture, the hook mechanism and its exact match are all settled (Settle 7 + 11, the review riders, the 2026-08-05 halt). What remains are elaborations *inside* a settled spec, and they are pinned in the tasks: `op` is **`task-diff`** (the `task-bind`/`task-discard` mold), `code_diff` is **always present, `""` when there is no diff** (the `hook_output` present-always rule — absent-versus-empty is not a discrimination a driver should infer), and `blocking_probes` is scoped to the **store** sweep (`jigc validate`), the surface the hook runs and the one the Settle names.

The **agent-text arm stays byte-identical** (`task_lifecycle.rs:190` keeps passing unchanged). [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) §2 gains `task diff`'s row **in this commit** — the verb appears in none of its enumerations — declaring the shape, joining `task-diff` to the `op` list, stating that **the `id` *is* the read-back address** (`jigc doc show <id> --task <task-id>`), that bodies are refused because they would mint a second unversioned managed-doc content-read path beside the separately-versioned `doc show`, and that `findings` is **structurally always empty** (the exit-code taxonomy restricts exit 3 to the three gate verbs, so this verb can raise none). *Done:* a new `crates/cli/tests/task_diff_envelope.rs` (registered in exactly one group root) driving the real binary: **(a)** over a task carrying a staged doc *and* a working-tree code change, stdout parses as **exactly one** JSON document with `op == "task-diff"`, `task` the id, `base.sha`/`base.short` equal to the task's own pin, `code_diff` containing the changed line, `staged_docs` the sorted identities, `findings == []`, and **no** `address`/`body` key anywhere; **(b)** the **followability** proof of the one-key decision — each `staged_docs[].id` fed **verbatim** to `jigc doc show <id> --task <id>` exits 0 and returns that doc, asserted for a transient `commit` doc and for a `placement` singleton (the one case where identity/address divergence was plausible); **(c)** the **empty state** — a task with no staged docs and no code diff still emits one JSON document, `code_diff: ""`, `staged_docs: []`, stdout > 0 bytes, exit 0 (today: 0 bytes, live-reproduced); **(d)** stderr carries no JSON document on any arm. Full unscoped gate green. *Declared bound, stated not glossed:* the **agent-text** empty state stays silent — it is not in the increment's approved scope, no golden or test pins it, and changing it is a surface edit whose home is the tier-2 batch, not a rider here. *(files: `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `design/command-output-contract.md`, a new `crates/cli/tests/task_diff_envelope.rs`, one `crates/cli/tests/groups/g_*.rs`.)*

Plus the sort/dedup assertion (two blocking findings of one probe yield **one** entry) and `report_only`/`scope`/`findings` unchanged on every arm. Red today on all three (the key does not exist). Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `design/command-output-contract.md`, `crates/cli/tests/validate_envelope.rs`.)*
- **T3 — the installed hook keys on `blocking_probes`, and its acceptance drives the real rendered body against real reports.** `precommit_hook_body` replaces the finding-object grep with the specified match, run over a **pipeline-local** newline collapse: `printf '%s' "$report" | tr -d '\n' | grep -Eq '"blocking_probes"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\[[^]]*"doc-code"'` — POSIX bracket classes, never `\s`; bounded by the array's own `]`, so it **structurally cannot escape into `findings`**; `$report` itself is **not** collapsed, so `PRECOMMIT_RENAME_BLOCK`'s line-oriented `git mv` pairing is byte-unchanged. Three shipped pins move **in this commit, because only this commit can repair them**: the byte golden `precommit_hook_body_golden` (`setup.rs:1621`), and the canned-report unit test `rendered_hook_warns_iff_doc_code_content_finding_always_exits_zero` (`:1515`) whose five cases re-key on the new array — retained for **shape robustness only** (compact vs pretty spacing) and explicitly **not** the acceptance, since a hand-written report cannot see a serde change. *Done:* `crates/cli/tests/precommit_hook_acceptance.rs` gains the three-arm acceptance, each a **real `git commit`** through the hook `jigc setup` installed, over a **real** store swept by the real binary — **(a)** a blocking `doc-code` finding → the drift warning appears, the commit lands (warn-only); **(b)** an **advisory-only** `doc-code` finding present in `findings` and absent from a non-empty `blocking_probes` → **no** warning, commit lands (the false-positive the array bound exists to prevent, and the exact state a non-Rust project following `implement-from-spec` sits in); **(c)** an **empty** `blocking_probes` with a `doc-code` finding present → **no** warning. The existing arms (stale anchor warns, clean store silent, unconfigured repo silent, wrapped foreign hook still fires, both rename arms) stay green unchanged.
