Both the per-leaf verb and the batch `doc author` inherit it in one place (`apply_field_target` is the shared seam). This also **restores the `conformance.*` route exemption to its original scope** rather than overturning it: N3's aftermath is a blocking, route-less `store.unparseable` on jigc's own success path, which the exemption's rationale (*"no CLI verb repairs a hand-broken byte"*) assumed could arrive only out of band. *Done:* a new `crates/cli/tests/undeclared_address_writes.rs` carrying the **field-leaf column** of the 9-cell table as data-driven rows — `set-field` × {top-level item leaf, nested item leaf} and `doc author` × {top-level item leaf, nested item leaf} each block **non-zero** with `write.unknown-field` at a **located** target, the staged file **byte-identical** to before the call, and a follow-up `jigc doc show` of the containing section still resolving (today all four exit **0** with a positive ack and leave the doc unreadable — live-reproduced). The **section-leaf** row of the same column (`set-field` at an undeclared section field → `write.unknown-field`) is asserted as already-correct in the same suite. The **slot-leaf column lands at T5** — named here so the split is tracked to a landing, never left to "a later task". Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, a new `crates/cli/tests/undeclared_address_writes.rs`.)*
- **T5 — no write lands at an undeclared item *slot leaf*, and the read side stops inventing one.** The tightening lands **at the write callers**: `set_item_slot` (`write.rs:1511`) and `set_nested_item_slot` (`:1746`) resolve the addressed leaf against the **template** (`chain_repeatable`'s block) *before* consulting `ParsedItem::slot_span`, so an undeclared leaf is rejected as `write.unknown-field` — instead of silently writing the item's real bare-prose slot (N4) **or** surfacing as the mis-diagnosed dead-end `write.non-reparseable` on the slot-less block arm (both live-reproduced; one call-site rule fixes both faces). **`ParsedItem::slot_span` is deliberately unchanged** — its second consumer is conformance adjudication (`validate.rs:2312`), which needs the lenient single-slot fallback; changing it there would be a different fix wearing this one's clothes. `resolve_leaf` moves in **both** its duplicated locations — `engine/src/store.rs:611` and its CLI twin `leaf_json` (`cli/src/doc.rs:3157`, whose own doc comment names it a mirror of the engine's order) — so a **multi-slot** template whose item parsed with an empty `slots` list stops handing every declared leaf the same bare prose. Per the roadmap's own either/or, the multi-slot arm ships with a **synthetic multi-slot repeatable fixture** (the fixture-pack shape `write_not_present_route.rs` already uses) **or** its bound re-declared in the acceptance with its reason. *Done:* `undeclared_address_writes.rs` completes the **9-cell table** — {`set-field`, `set-slot`, `doc author`} × {section leaf, top-level item leaf, nested item leaf}, one data-driven row per cell, never three hand-written cases — every cell rejecting **non-zero** with the staged bytes **byte-identical** to before the call; plus the read-side arm: `jigc doc show` at an undeclared leaf of a **multi-slot** item is `store.no-such-leaf`, not a neighbouring slot's prose, through **both** read surfaces (`doc show` text and `--format json`, the two duplicated `resolve_leaf` locations), or the multi-slot bound is re-declared in the suite with its reason. Red today on the single-slot write cell (the ack named `phantom`, the prose landed in `notes`). Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/engine/src/store.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/undeclared_address_writes.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/doc_show_item_leaf.rs`.)*
- **T6 — the taxonomy tells the truth about which miss is which, and the override stops claiming to be universal.** [validation.md](design/validation.md):60's `write.*` sentence is revised on both halves: the **taxonomy** — an **item-id miss** is `write.not-present` at *every* write verb that can address an item (not the two the sentence names), `write.wrong-shape` retreats to genuine declared-shape defects, and `write.unknown-field` covers an undeclared **leaf**, field or slot alike — and the over-universalized *"overridden at the CLI write-verb dispatch"*, true of the four enriched verbs and **false** of the batch `doc author` fallback, scoped to what actually overrides with the exception named. **P6 is stated where the route floor's presence half is stated** (the neighbouring paragraph), naming the derivability table and its `<task-id>` carve-out as the fence — *statement == fence*, the wave's own rule. [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md)'s per-verb reject statements and [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md)'s leaf-resolution statement are reconciled with T4/T5 in the same motion. Prose last, behaviour first: a sentence claiming the sweep before the sweep exists is the law-1 lie this increment exists to retire. *Done:* one command exits clean — `rg -n "genuine shape questions" design/validation.md` returns **no match** for the superseded taxonomy clause — while each corrected site is asserted present by its own `rg` pattern (the item-id-miss rule, the scoped override clause with its named exception, the P6/derivability paragraph); every code identifier and line reference the revised paragraphs cite is checked against the tree. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `design/validation.md`, `design/write-commands.md`, `design/doc-read-surface.md`.)*

*Why this order:* **behaviour before speech** (the Inc-3/Inc-4 rule, applied a third time) and **the fence before the code it must guard**. T1 fixes *which* miss a finding claims to be, because a route can only name a followable recovery once the code says which recovery applies — so T2 rides it. T3 then turns route-followability into a property over the routes T1/T2 leave standing, and lands **before** T4/T5 so the new rejects those tasks mint are adjudicated by a live fence rather than by a reviewer's memory. T6 writes the sentences only once all of it is true. **Every *Grouped scope* bullet lands:** P5-4 + N11 → **T1** (codes) and **T2** (routes) · N12 → **T2** (enrichment) and **T3** (the `<address>`/`<task-id>` fill on the batch fallback) · P6 → **T3** · N3 → **T4** · N4 → **T5** · the `command-output-contract.md` authorization clause → **T1**, in the commit it authorizes · the `validation.md`:60 taxonomy revision **and** the over-universalized override clause → **T6** · `write_not_present_route.rs`'s pinned exclusion + the re-pinned genuine shape question → **T1**. The 9-cell table is split by column across T4 (field leaves) and T5 (slot leaves + the whole-table sweep), named in **both** tasks so the split is tracked to a landing. Deliberately **out**, stated rather than smuggled: `ParsedItem::slot_span` itself (its conformance consumer needs the lenient arm), the anyhow-embedded routes (they never reach the finding seam), and human-route prose placeholders (the `<task-id>` carve-out) — each with its reason above.

## 2026-08-04 — M47 Inc 5 T2: the methodology pack carries the same split, and its 7 migrate workflows stop double-soliciting (S1 discharged)

**The same fix, in the pack that had the mirror-image defect.** Methodology put the commit-doc solicit inside `step:finalize` itself — which `step:migration-finalize` includes — so all **seven** methodology migrate workflows solicited a commit doc their own mint had already **pre-filled** (`provision_migration_commit_doc`): a pre-existing double-solicit, not a regression. The solicit half (the four `{{cli.set-commit-*}}` refs + the reserved-depth statement) moves to a new `packs/methodology/steps/author-commit.yaml` — **the same step id as dev's**, which is safe by the pack-local body-reference rule ([multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md) → pack-local resolution): includes resolve per **origin pack**, so methodology's `dev-task` composes methodology's `author-commit` even where dev wins the composite id. The eight task-minting non-migrate workflows include it immediately before their finalize include; `migration-finalize.yaml` is untouched in both packs, so **the double-solicit dies with the split rather than by a special case**.

**The `git add` imperative goes; the contract stays.** `finalize.yaml` keeps every true clause and all three `states-constraints:` codes and loses only the imperative *"`git add` your code edits before you finalize"* — a law-1 lie to the **six** methodology workflows that compose no code-writing step (`do-research` · `form-vision` · `park-idea` · `planning` · `completion` · `record-dogfood`). What remains is **descriptive**: finalize commits the git index — only what you have staged (`git add`), plus the docs it manages. That is true for every workflow that reaches it, including the code-less ones — two of them (`completion` · `record-dogfood`) stage an unmanaged **owner-artifact** by hand — so `methodology_staging_contract.rs`'s four claims hold **unchanged** across the move. [finalize.md](design/finalize.md):131's family obligation is engaged on its rationale and **narrowed** here (it is true only now that both halves have landed): the imperative belongs to the code-writing family, the shared commit step states the consequence.

**S1 is discharged, and the axis proves it.** `crates/cli/tests/commit_solicit_axis.rs` widens from the dev registry to the **composite** one — all 33 workflows, both packs, over the `[dev ▸ methodology]` set a plain `jigc setup` installs. Exactly one write per required `commit` leaf for the **17** task-minting non-migrate workflows, zero for the other **16**; both packs are asserted to contribute members to **both** sides, so a sweep that quietly covered one pack fails loudly. Red before this task on exactly the seven methodology migrate workflows. The followability arm now runs both packs' 17: the composed writes executed **verbatim as printed**, then `jigc task validate` must report no finding targeting `commit:<id>` — and its author-payload substitution reads the placeholder token off the emitted bytes rather than naming it, because the two packs spell it differently (`<COMMIT_TYPE>` vs `<TYPE>`). 180 methodology golden cells regen; **no dev and no composite cell moves**.

## 2026-08-04 — M47 Inc 5 T1: the dev pack's commit-doc solicit becomes one step, composed by every workflow whose gate demands it

**The defect was a *composition* defect, so the fix is composition, not prose.** The commit doc is the one doc every task-minting workflow's finalize gate blocks on, yet its solicitation lived inside the **code-writing** steps (`step:implement` / `step:implement-quick`) and, separately, inside `sub-task`'s own `step:author-commit`. Five dev workflows that reach `step:finalize` without writing code — `architecture-documentation` · `plan` · `record-change` · `record-decision` · `project-setup` (through `project-finalize.yaml`, which is *only* that include) — therefore composed text naming every write **except** the two their gate refuses on (live at HEAD: follow `record-decision` to completion and `jigc task validate` exits **3** on `commit#header/type` + `#summary`). The solicit block leaves both implement steps; `steps/author-commit.yaml` is rewritten as the pack's **one** solicit body (existing prose relocated, not rewritten) and the nine task-minting non-migrate workflows include it immediately before their finalize include — at the **workflow** level, so `project-finalize.yaml` stays the thin include it is and the five migrate workflows, whose mint pre-fills the commit doc, are untouched by construction ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-07-26 the Settle, Decision 5; [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md):186 — the workflow file **is** the ordered list).

**`sub-task`'s double-instruct dies structurally, not by deletion.** Its boundary framing (*"never `git commit` and never `jigc task finalize` here"*) moves to a new `steps/sub-task-commit.yaml` that states it **above** `{{ include: step:author-commit }}` — the `migration-finalize` / `project-finalize` nesting precedent. There is now no second copy of the solicit that could drift back into a second solicitation.

**The reserved-depth statement is path-local, and that is why it did not travel whole.** It is stated once per step that solicits slot prose, above that step's first `set-slot` (law 3: stated before it can fail). `implement.yaml` keeps a copy over the **ADR** slots it still solicits — hoisting it into `author-commit` alone would have put it *below* the first `set-slot` in every `single-task` compose, which is exactly what `surface_polish.rs`'s shipped ceiling fence forbids. [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md):63's conversion table records the dev copy as a pair, with the path-local rule stated.

**The staging imperative is scoped, not deleted.** `finalize.yaml` loses only *"Make sure your code edits are staged (`git add`) first"* — a law-1 lie to the five code-less workflows — and keeps every true clause (what finalize commits, `left-out`, `nothing-staged`, the carryover gate) and all three `states-constraints:` codes, so the per-pack stated-at fence keeps its declarer. This is [finalize.md](design/finalize.md):123's family obligation **engaged on its rationale and narrowed**: the imperative belongs to the code-writing steps that already carry it. **T1 is not shippable alone** — S1 (both packs carry the change) is discharged only when T2 lands methodology's half.

**The proof is an axis, enumerated from the registry** (`crates/cli/tests/commit_solicit_axis.rs`; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1). For **every** dev workflow, `jigc workflow <id> --preview` must name a write for **each required `commit` leaf** — read from the pack's own `commit` schema via `is_author_required`, never typed into the test — exactly once when the workflow mints a task and does not pre-fill the commit doc, zero otherwise. The migrate exemption is derived **twice** (`migrate-<doctype>` over the pack's schema list, and the `step:migration-finalize` include) and the two are asserted to agree, so neither derivation can rot alone. A second arm proves *followability*, which counting cannot: `jigc start --workflow <id>` in a fresh repo, the composed write commands **executed verbatim as printed** (only the author-owned payload substituted — the `<COMMIT_TYPE>` placeholder, itself read from the schema's enum, and the piped prose), then `jigc task validate <id>` must report no finding targeting `commit:<id>`.

*Two shipped bases moved with the composition, each scoped to its own claim rather than relaxed:* `start_compose.rs`'s `project-setup` / `architecture-documentation` arms counted `<<author:` lines over the **whole** compose to assert their author step's slot count — they now exclude the commit directive, which belongs to a different step and whose exactly-once-ness is the new axis suite's claim. The engine's `SINGLE_TASK` compose fixture gains `step:author-commit`: since the split it is the only shipped step carrying the `<<author: {{…}}>>` directive class that fixture's golden exists to pin, so omitting it would have quietly stopped exercising a placeholder class. The 168 moved dev golden cells regen in this commit; no methodology or composite cell moves.

## 2026-08-04 — M47 Increment 5 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 5](implementation/roadmap.md) (N6 — `step:finalize` splits into a solicit half and a commit half) into **2 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `d70679d` (tree clean; Inc 1–4 landed). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-07-26 the Settle, **Decision 5** (split `step:finalize` into a solicit half and a commit half — the "move the writes into finalize" arm reversed on new facts, because `migration-finalize.yaml` includes `step:finalize` in **both** packs and `project-finalize.yaml` is *only* that include, so the naive arm would hand all 12 migrate workflows the doubled solicitation the decision forbade, and the dialect has no conditionals) plus its two riders (the code-less count is **four** by one path + `project-setup` by another; methodology's `finalize.yaml` already solicits, so its 7 migrate workflows double-solicit at HEAD — a pre-existing defect this wave regularizes). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 47 Increment 5; [baseline](completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md) §3b (N6, the verified census) + §5 (S1, S3, S4 — the two unfenced `finalize.yaml`, the regen-less literals, the measured blast radii); [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md):186 (the workflow file **is** the ordered list — compose an existing unit rather than overload one step); [finalize.md](design/finalize.md):123 (the family obligation, engaged on its rationale); [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → law 1 + The stated-at fence; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1.

**Basis — every claim below was read in the tree at HEAD or reproduced live against `target/debug/jigc` (1.0.0-rc.9):**

- **The census is measured, not restated.** Counting commit-doc solicitations (`commit:<id>#type` writes) across all 33 `workflow-preview--*--fresh` goldens: **dev** — `architecture-documentation` · `plan` · `project-setup` · `record-change` · `record-decision` = **0** (the N6 five, the last reached through `project-finalize.yaml`); `sub-task` = **2** (`step:implement` *and* `step:author-commit` — the pre-existing double-instruct); `single-task` / `implement-from-spec` / `quick-fix` = 1; the 5 migrate + `ingest-existing` / `milestone-execution` / `router` = 0. **methodology** — the 8 non-migrate task-minting workflows = 1; the **7 migrate** = **1** (should be 0); `increment` = 0. Target state: **17 at exactly one, 16 at zero**.
- **The defect reproduces live, end-to-end.** Throwaway repo → `jigc setup` → `jigc start --workflow record-decision "record the store choice"` → follow the composed text to completion (`doc create adr`, then the three required slots) → **`jigc task validate` exits 3** with `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` on `commit:<id>#header/type` and `schema-conformance.required-slot-present` on `#summary` — two writes the composed text never names. The routes are followable, but the gate is an ambush: the workflow asks for everything except the two leaves it will block on.
- **Include resolution is per-origin-pack, and that is what makes a same-id step safe in both packs.** Both packs already ship colliding `finalize` / `implement` / `migration-finalize` step ids; dev wins the composite's top-level id (`crates/cli/src/pack.rs` → `colliding_id_origin_is_the_precedence_winner`), yet `goldens/compose/methodology/workflow-preview--dev-task--fresh.txt:35` composes **methodology's** finalize prose ("Land the change as exactly one logical commit"). So a new `steps/author-commit.yaml` in *both* packs resolves to each pack's own body — no shadowing hazard, and the id parity is the S1 mitigation the two `finalize.yaml` never had.
- **The migrate exemption's axis is the CLI's own, not a naming convention.** `crates/cli/src/migrate.rs:135-137` — `migration_workflow(doctype) = format!("migrate-{doctype}")`; `crates/cli/src/start.rs:292-352` `provision_migration_commit_doc` → `migration_commit_form` materializes `type`/`scope` and fills `summary`/`body` from the deterministic template **at mint**. Every one of the 12 migrate workflows includes `step:migration-finalize`, whose body ends `{{ include: step:finalize }}` in both packs — so the commit half reaching them unchanged **is** the structural point of the split, and the expectation function must be derived from the registry (`migrate-<type>` per shipped schema, cross-checked by the `migration-finalize` include), never a hand list ([pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1).
- **The stated-at fence is per-pack presence, so relocating prose inside a pack is fence-safe.** `crates/cli/src/pack.rs:357-419` — `assert_stated_at` requires each of the four `AMBUSH_CLASS_CODES` to have **at least one** declarer among that pack's steps; both `finalize.yaml` keep `[finalize.left-out, finalize.nothing-staged, finalize.carried-staged]` and both `migration-finalize.yaml` keep `finalize.promote-clobber`. The per-soliciting-step tier (`create.singleton-copy-in`) keys on `{{schema:<T>}}` refs, which neither the moved solicit block nor either `finalize.yaml` carries.
- **The `git add` line is scoped, not deleted — and a shipped fence says why.** `crates/cli/tests/methodology_staging_contract.rs:139` asserts that **`planning` and `completion`** — both code-less — compose "`git add`" **and** "only what you have staged"; `completion` genuinely writes an unmanaged file (`completions/artifacts/<milestone>/…`, the recorded `owner-artifact`). So the law-1 defect is the **imperative** — dev's *"Make sure your code edits are staged (`git add`) first"* and methodology's *"`git add` your code edits before you finalize"*, both of which assert the reader has code edits — not the descriptive statement of what finalize commits. The imperative leaves the shared commit half for the code-writing steps that already carry it (`crates/cli/pack/steps/implement.yaml:1-2`, `implement-quick.yaml:1-2`, `packs/methodology/steps/implement.yaml:6-8`); the commit half keeps a family-true statement (what finalize commits, what is left out, the nothing-staged refusal, the carryover gate). This is `finalize.md`:123's obligation **engaged on its rationale and narrowed**, exactly as the Settle directs — and `methodology_staging_contract.rs`'s claims stay green rather than being inverted.
- **The dev pack has three solicit bodies today, not two** — `implement.yaml:10-27`, `implement-quick.yaml:6-11`, `author-commit.yaml:9-13`. Sweeping all three into one shared step is the M45 complete-fix rule applied to this class's axis ("every step that solicits the commit doc"), and it makes `sub-task`'s double-instruct impossible rather than merely fixed: the sub-task-specific framing (*"never `git commit` and never `jigc task finalize` here"*) becomes its own step stating the boundary **above** an include of the shared solicit — the `migration-finalize` / `project-finalize` nesting precedent ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-07-17 M43 Inc 6, *one home per pack instead of 12 restated paragraphs*). `quick-fix`'s count does not move (1 → 1), so sweeping `implement-quick` is zero-risk on the *Proves* clause and is named here rather than slipped in.
- **The blast radius is measured:** of the 612 golden cells, **156** carry the dev finalize staging line, **180** the methodology finalize body, **48** the dev implement/implement-quick opener, **12** the sub-task `author-commit` body. Verbatim inline literals with no regen path (S3): `crates/cli/tests/config_fill.rs:136,197` · `start_compose.rs:97,158` · `multi_pack_acceptance.rs:392,453,502,515` · the two `insta` step snapshots `crates/cli/src/pack.rs:1654,1726` · the step-inventory list `pack.rs:1548-1583` (a new step id joins it, in stem order) · the workflow-body snapshots in the same module · `embedded_methodology_compose.rs:297`. Per [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1 the regen of exactly the cells a task moves rides **that task's own commit** (a red golden has no green commit boundary); increment 11 keeps the **full-tree** regeneration and the wave-level radius review.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** Step ids and include positions are doc-elaboration pins under `workflow-dialect.md`:186; the migrate exemption, the both-packs rule and the staging-line scoping are settled at Decision 5; the golden-regen home is settled at pinning.md §1.

- **T1 — the dev pack's commit-doc solicit becomes one step, composed by every workflow whose gate demands it.** The solicit block leaves `steps/implement.yaml` and `steps/implement-quick.yaml`; `steps/author-commit.yaml` is rewritten as the pack's **one** solicit body (the type + summary command-refs, the `<<author: {{task.commit#summary}}>>` slot, the optional scope/body/trailer lines, the M45 reserved-depth statement — existing prose **relocated, not rewritten**), and the sub-task boundary framing moves to a new `steps/sub-task-commit.yaml` that states it above `{{ include: step:author-commit }}`. Nine workflows gain the solicit immediately before their finalize include (`single-task`, `implement-from-spec`, `quick-fix`, `architecture-documentation`, `plan`, `record-change`, `record-decision`, `project-setup` — at the **workflow** level, leaving `project-finalize.yaml` the thin include it is — and `sub-task`, via `sub-task-commit`); the 5 migrate workflows and `migration-finalize.yaml` are **untouched by construction**. `steps/finalize.yaml` keeps the commit half and loses the imperative *"Make sure your code edits are staged (`git add`) first"*, keeping every true clause (what finalize commits, left-out, nothing-staged, the carryover gate) and its three `states-constraints:` codes. *Done:* a new axis test enumerated from the **dev** pack registry (never a hand list): for every dev workflow, `jigc workflow <id> --preview` names a write for **each required `commit` leaf** (`#type`, `#summary`, read from the pack's own commit schema) **exactly once** for the 9 task-minting non-migrate workflows and **zero** times for the other 8 — red at HEAD (five at 0, `sub-task` at 2); plus a followability arm over those 9: `jigc start --workflow <id>` in a fresh repo, the composed commit-doc write commands executed **verbatim** as the composed text prints them, then `jigc task validate <id>` reports **no finding targeting `commit:<id>`** (red at HEAD for the five — live-reproduced above for `record-decision`). The dev golden cells regen in the same commit and `git diff --name-only` names **only** cells this edit moves; `start_compose.rs`'s sub-task arm still finds the never-`git commit` / never-`jigc task finalize` ban in the composed view. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/pack/steps/{implement,implement-quick,author-commit,sub-task-commit,finalize}.yaml`, `crates/cli/pack/workflows/{single-task,implement-from-spec,quick-fix,architecture-documentation,plan,record-change,record-decision,project-setup,sub-task}.yaml`, `crates/cli/src/pack.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/{config_fill,start_compose,multi_pack_acceptance,config_insert_step,config_replace_remove_step,config_fork_compose,e2e_audit}.rs`, a new `crates/cli/tests/commit_solicit_axis.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/goldens/compose/dev/`, `design/workflow-dialect.md`:264, `design/architecture-documentation.md`:71, `design/project-setup.md`:40, `design/surface-contract.md`:63, `design/worked-examples.md`.)*

Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `packs/methodology/steps/{finalize,author-commit}.yaml`, `packs/methodology/workflows/{completion,decided-task,dev-task,do-research,form-vision,park-idea,planning,record-dogfood}.yaml`, `crates/cli/tests/{commit_solicit_axis,multi_pack_acceptance,methodology_staging_contract,embedded_methodology_compose,methodology_pack_compose}.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/goldens/compose/methodology/`, `design/finalize.md`:123, `design/surface-contract.md`:63, `design/worked-examples.md`:914.)*

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 4 fix: `--dry-run`'s help states the *scope* of its forecast, never a flat promise

**T3 replaced an accurate sentence with an over-broad one, inside the increment whose deliverable is "the surfaces stop lying."** Its long help promised the flag *"never forecasts a green the finalize would refuse"* — unconditional, and false for every one of the six previewable `owner-artifact` causes T2 had just made blocking: the `--dry-run` branch sits ahead of phase 5, so over each of them the forecast prints a manifest at **exit 0** for a state the committing run refuses at **3** (verified live through the binary, all seven causes, both doors). A flat claim of exactly the shape T4 had just retired from five other surfaces ([surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → law 1).

**Scoped, not widened — the fork is named, not slipped.** The help now enumerates the **three** gates the forecast actually runs — this task's validation findings, the empty-commit guard (live-checked: a nothing-staged dry-run blocks at 3 with the same finding the commit emits), and the carryover gate T3 moved into the branch — and says every other gate (`owner-artifact` causes, staging, promotion, the commit hook) is *decided only by the real finalize*, routing on to `jigc task validate` for the owner-artifact causes it does preview. The enumeration is deliberate: *"it forecasts what it can decide read-only"* would be a fresh law-1 lie, since the six `owner-artifact` causes **are** read-only decidable — this door simply does not run them. It is T5's [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) enumeration re-derived for **this** door, which sits one phase later than `task validate`: `empty-commit` / `nothing-staged` is unpreviewable at validate but *is* forecast here, because the dry-run branch runs `plan_finalize` before it returns. Running `preview_gates` **inside** the dry-run branch would make the flat claim true instead — but that widens `--dry-run`'s behaviour past T3's approved scope, so it is a re-Settle for a later wave, deliberately left un-taken.

**The fence carries its own counterexample.** `the_dry_run_forecast_covers_no_gate_borne_cause_and_its_help_says_so` iterates the seven-cause axis through the real binary — forecast vs commit per row, HEAD unmoved — and only then asserts the emitted `--help` bytes. Pinning the sentence without the axis would be a claim about prose; pinning the axis without the sentence would leave the prose free to re-widen.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 4 T5: the eight doc sites reconciled, including the sentence that licensed the lie

**The locked docs stated the flat promise as an *invariant*, which is why scoping it looked optional.** `validation.md` and `write-commands.md` both said what `validate` reports and what `finalize` blocks on *"can never diverge"*; `finalize.md` said *"They cannot diverge"* and then — for the one gate it admits is adjudicated later — *"Same check, same report, later position"*, which is **false**: the later position is exactly what changes the report, and that sentence is what let a reader conclude no scoping was owed. All four now state the true shape: `finalize ≡ validate + **the commit-time gates** + commit`, every check `validate` runs is a check `finalize` blocks on, and `jigc task validate` **previews the gate up to the commit** — a preview of that much, never a prediction of the commit.

**The divergence is *position*, not *scope*, and `command-output-contract.md` had it backwards on both halves.** Its second clause attributed the `task validate` / `task finalize` split to scope, and reached for the **task-scope** owner-artifact gate to carry a **store-scope** claim. The store-scope clause survives on its own honest example (row 0 of the exit table: the store sweep carries content findings at exit 0, some of which do block once a task's scope contains them); the owner-artifact case moves to a new **third** clause that names it for what it is — same scope, same engine, one transaction, a later position — and enumerates the four items **unpreviewable in principle**: `finalize.stage-failed` · the commit hook's rejection · `empty-commit` / `nothing-staged` · the **untracked** `owner-artifact` cause. The existing exit table at :321 becomes true rather than aspirational: `task validate` is now genuinely a task-scope gate that emits 3.

**`finalize.md`'s owner-artifact paragraph is re-derived from the seven causes, not patched.** Six are staging-independent and run at phase 2 (so they preview); the seventh asserts a state phase 5 has not yet produced, so it runs after the stage and only there — *same check, different report, later position*, with M45 Inc 8's Decision 6 cited as **narrowed to its own stated grounds, not overturned**. Two back-references that quoted the retired sentences verbatim (`validation.md` → the milestone-boundary gate; `finalize.md`'s own *"a divergence this document says cannot exist"*) are re-pointed in the same motion, so no dangling quote of a deleted sentence survives.

**One site beyond the eight, found by sweeping the class rather than the list.** `validation.md`'s M45-registrations row for `owner-artifact.present` still said the gate *"moves **after** finalize's stage phase"* full stop — the same lie in table form, in a file already open for this task. It is narrowed there too: only the untracked cause consults the staged index; the other six run at the validate phase.

**Scope held where it was drawn.** The four adjacent mirrors (`bootstrap.md`'s orientation sample, `command-catalog.md`'s hint — now byte-mirroring the shipped `commands.yaml`, `reconciliation.md`'s *"same sweep"* row, `write-commands.md`'s lifecycle line) and `QUICKSTART.md` are scoped too; **`VISION.md` is byte-identical to HEAD** (it asserts no invariant, and a VISION edit stays a flagged event); store-scope `jigc validate` stays exit-0 on task-scope checks; and the internal doc comments are left alone — the class is adjudicated *adjacent, not user-facing* at [baseline](completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md) §4a (which names `crates/cli/src/task.rs:354-355`). Named rather than silently skipped: `crates/engine/src/result.rs:177` paraphrases the retired sentence in a `ValidationReport` doc comment, but scoped to *"`task validate` and `finalize` **phase 2**"* — true as written at that scope, so it is a stale citation, not a live lie, and it stays outside this task's declared file set.

**The claim now matches the coverage, everywhere it is printed.** Five surfaces told an agent that `jigc task validate` *"previews the findings finalize will gate on"* — flat, unqualified, and false by fourteen gate rows ([baseline](completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md) §4b). T1/T2 made the preview cover three of those families; this task makes the five sentences say **that**, and only that: the composed `what's-left:` line (`render.rs` — every id-carrying compose, the highest-traffic surface), both packs' `finalize` steps, the `task status` unknown-subcommand tip, and the `validate-task` catalog hint `describe` mirrors. Law 1 is satisfied by *scoping*, not by promising more — no construction makes the flat promise true (baseline §2.3).

And the verbatim inline sites are **six**, not five: `crates/engine/src/compose.rs`'s command-catalog JSON snapshot carries the hint too (its `COMMANDS_YAML` is `include_bytes!` of the shipped file and needs no edit — `shipped_commands_yaml_is_byte_identical` is what keeps that honest).

**The regen rides this commit, per [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1** (*"the regenerated diff is part of the commit under review"*) — the roadmap's *"regenerated in increment 11, never here"* is reconciled, not ignored: a 348-cell red tree has no green commit boundary, and increment 11 keeps what its ordering rationale actually asks of it (the full-tree regen + the wave-level blast-radius review).

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 4 T3: `finalize --dry-run` stops forecasting a green it will refuse

**The forecast now obeys the gate it forecasts.** `--dry-run` returned at exit **0** over a pre-staged-before-mint plant the committing run refuses at **3**, *and* `relabel_carried` stamped those entries `carried-over` — a consent `--carry-staged` never gave — so the refusing-state and committing-state `--format json` documents came out **byte-identical** (verified live at HEAD before the fix). The flag whose entire job is *"tell me what this finalize will do"* was information-free on the one axis `--carry-staged` decides. The carryover refusal now runs **inside** the dry-run branch as well, ahead of the manifest: one decision (`decide_carryover`, computed once), two doors.

**The refusal *is* the forecast — the build-level call, taken deliberately.** A refusing dry-run emits the findings envelope and the refusing exit, not the manifest: the carried paths and both their exits are the finding's own bytes, and the manifest's `carried-over` discriminator survives in `findings[].key.target`. (The recovered M47 completion audit raised the dropped discriminator as finding 6 and closed it **NOT-A-DEFECT with evidence**; this build does not re-open it.) It remains a pure reader — `blocked` renders and returns, staging and committing nothing.

**Three shipped `carryover_gate.rs` arms pinned the defect and are corrected — basis-has-changed, not an override.** M43 placed the refuse *after* the dry-run branch deliberately, so the forecast would always render, and its arms drove a bare `--dry-run` over a carried state expecting exit 0. That basis is what T3 removes: the forecast rendered, but it rendered a green the finalize refuses. Each arm now declares its carry (`--dry-run --carry-staged`) — the `carried-over` label *is* the rendering of a declared consent, so the surface that carries it is the declared one, and the forecast/landed identical-set arm becomes a comparison of like with like (its landed run was always `--carry-staged`; its forecast was not).

**The diff is the assertion.** The acceptance runs both `--format json` invocations against the *same* planted repo (both side-effect-free, so it is genuinely one state) and asserts the two documents are **no longer byte-identical** — byte-identity was the defect, so equality is the failure. Alongside it: the non-carrying forecast is pinned **verbatim** on both surfaces (bytes captured from the pre-fix binary, asserted after), because *"unchanged"* is a byte claim and the fix must reach the carrying state and nothing else. `--dry-run`'s own long help is corrected in the same commit — it promised *"print the manifest and stop"* unconditionally.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 4 T2: the six staging-independent owner-artifact causes preview at validate; cause 7 stays post-stage

**M45 Decision 6 is narrowed to its own stated grounds, not overturned** — and the narrowing is enforced by a *predicate*, not by a promise. Decision 6 relocated the #5 owner-artifact gate off the shared phase-2 entry because it asserts the artifact is durably **tracked**, a state phase-5 staging can satisfy, so a pre-stage `tracked` check false-positives a finalize that lands at exit 0. That reasoning is sound and live-proven. It also reaches **one of seven** `owned_location_violation` causes: only the untracked one consults `tracked`. The other six — empty · absolute · `..` · not-under-home · names-no-file · symlink-escape — are *staging-independent*: no stage can change their verdict, so previewing them cannot false-positive. The trial's two live blocks were causes 4 and 5, neither of which Decision 6's rationale covers.

**The construction is one argument: `&|_| true`.** `jigc task validate` re-invokes the *same* `engine::validate::owner_artifacts_gate` the committing door runs, at the M47 Inc 4 preview seam, under a **constant-true** `tracked` predicate — so the untracked branch is *structurally unreachable* from that door rather than conditionally skipped. Cause 7 stays post-stage because the code cannot get there, which is why widening the preview later cannot silently widen it to cause 7. The gate is **not** moved back into `validate_task`: finalize's preflight shares that entry, so running it there would re-introduce exactly the false-positive Decision 6 retired. The engine keeps its recorded omission; only the CLI wiring above it changed.

**Swept over the axis, not the two repros.** `crates/cli/tests/owner_artifact_cause_axis.rs` iterates all seven causes × both surfaces through the real binary, comparing the emitted `--format json` finding **objects** byte-for-byte between `task validate` and `task finalize` — a divergence in code, key target, message, location or route fails there. Two facts the sweep established rather than assumed: cause 7's row proves the split live (present-but-gitignored → validate exit 0 with no gate finding, finalize exit 3 with it), and **cause 1 (empty) is pre-empted at the committing door** — an empty `owned-location` is *also* a `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` violation, and finalize's phase-2 abort-chain blocks on it before the stage phase runs, so the row records that code as the committing door's emitter instead of being dropped from the axis.

**Two shipped tests flip their validate-side assertion, and one recorded rationale is corrected.** `owner_artifact_gate.rs`'s absent-artifact arm (cause 5) now expects exit 3 with the gate named; its index-rollback and post-stage assertions are untouched. `validate.rs`'s `owner_artifact_gate_relocated_off_validate_task_to_post_stage` keeps every assertion — the wiring is CLI-side — but its doc's inference *"so `jigc task validate` exits 0 on this state"* no longer follows from them and is corrected in place as a basis-has-changed narrowing, alongside the two production doc sites that stated the same thing.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 4 T1: the carryover gate previews at `jigc task validate`, and `--carry-staged` gives the preview the consent the gate accepts

**A gate that runs only on the committing path is not previewable, and the preview surface was lying by omission.** `jigc task validate` exited **0** over a pre-staged-before-mint plant that `jigc task finalize` refuses at **3** — live-reproduced at HEAD before the fix — so the surface every composed step calls *"see what's left before committing"* could not see the wave's #1-ranked v1 gate, and [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md):321's exit table was aspirational rather than true. `TaskArea::validate` now also runs `engine::finalize::decide_carryover`: the same pure decision over CLI-supplied git facts, the same mint-time snapshot, the same retire and owner-artifact exemptions (`plan_owner_artifacts` goes `pub`, so both doors compute the exemption from **one** function and cannot disagree about which paths are the task's own subject) — **no staging, no mutation**, the preview stays a pure reader.

**The preview is a parameter, never a shared default — the hard invariant.** `validate` has two callers and finalize's preflight is one of them, so wiring the probe into the shared seam would have *moved finalize's block position* (the refuse deliberately sits after the `--dry-run` branch and ahead of the migration review gate; `decide_carryover`'s own doc comment records why it stays on the committing path). The seam takes a `GatePreview`; the preflight passes `Off`. Pinned rather than assumed: the acceptance re-asserts the committing door's message **and** route byte-for-byte, its exit, and that `finalize --carry-staged` still lands the carry-over.

**The new door speaks for itself** (surface-contract law 1). The finding is now read from a verb that has refused nothing, so the inherited *"refusing to let … / re-run the finalize with `--carry-staged`"* would be a lie at the moment of reading. `CarryoverBoundary` gains **`TaskPreview`** — same boundary, same decision, same exemptions, different door — naming the `jigc task finalize` that **will** refuse, and routing at a flag it says is accepted at both doors. The owner exemption keys on a new `is_task_boundary()`, so widening the *door* axis cannot silently widen the *exemption* axis.

**`--carry-staged` joins `task validate`** — the cross-model review's blocker 3, and the wave's third and last deliberate bend of the no-new-surfaces boundary. The non-breaking argument holds only for **default** finalize: with no validate-side equivalent of the consent flag, a driver that always intends to carry would read a permanently-red preview of a finalize that accepts the state. A preview that cannot express the consent the gate accepts is not a preview of that gate.

*Bound, unchanged and now proven at the new door too:* a snapshot-less (pre-M43) task validates clean — `decide_carryover`'s declared fail-open. The six staging-independent `owner-artifact` causes (T2) and the `--dry-run` false green (T3) are this increment's siblings, not this task's.

Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → the 2026-07-26 Settle, **Decision 1** (wire the previewable gates onto `task validate` — the carryover probe + the six staging-independent `owner-artifact` causes — *and* scope the prose on all nine surfaces regardless; **M45 Decision 6 engaged on its rationale and preserved**, cause 7 stays post-stage; `stage-failed` · hook rejection · `empty-commit`/`nothing-staged` · `promote-clobber` · `base-mismatch` deliberately **out**) plus the cross-model review's blocker 3 (the non-breaking argument holds only for *default* finalize, so **`--carry-staged` joins `task validate`** — the third and last deliberate bend of the wave's no-new-surfaces boundary). Stage; [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md):321 (the exit table) / :325 (the counter-statement); [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → law 1 + the route floor; [pinning.md](implementation/pinning.md) §1.

**Basis — every claim below was read in the tree at HEAD or reproduced live against `target/debug/jigc`; line numbers are HEAD's, not the roadmap's pre-Inc-1/2/3 ones:**

- **The defect reproduces live, exactly as charted.** In a throwaway repo: `git add foreign.txt` → `jigc start --workflow single-task` → fill the commit doc → **`jigc task validate` exits 0** ("no findings — the task validates clean") while **`jigc task finalize` exits 3** with `finalize.carried-staged` on the same state. `Task::validate` (`task.rs:755`) runs `validate_task` and nothing else; `decide_carryover` is reached only from the finalize path (`task.rs:1133`) and `owner_artifacts_gate` only from the post-stage site (`task.rs:2349`).

The dry-run branch (`task.rs:~1160`) returns `Ok(Outcome::success())` **before** the carryover refuse (`task.rs:~1180`), and `relabel_carried` (`:2775`) stamps `carried-over` whether or not the carry was ever declared.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 3 T7 (H2): the survivable frame sweeps the whole nine-door committing axis, one error code per door

**The frame was a door-local courtesy; it is now the family's contract.** M42 gave `jigc task finalize` the three things a rejected commit owes — git's bytes verbatim, a sentence saying what survived, its own re-run — and left the other **eight** doors that run a hook-capable `git commit` on the user's behalf printing a bare `{err:#}`: no recoverability statement, no route, no identity in the invocation log. `render::commit_rejected` is therefore generalized off the task idiom onto two parameters only a door can supply (a **state-truth clause** and the door's **own** argv), applied at all nine, with the task door's bytes unchanged.

**Decision 6's per-door mint, with `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`'s recorded rationale revised rather than silently overridden.** *"Deliberately not a per-verb code mint"* was sound while exactly one door framed anything; once eight more do, reusing `finalize.commit-rejected` on them puts a **lying** verb in the log — on the surface M42 built to stop the log lying. The registry closes at **10**: nine door identities + `migrate.review-pending` (a coded stop, not a rejected commit), with [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md):76's prose mirror grown 2 → 10 in the same commit.

**Elaboration pin — the two `milestone finalize` members are the two commit-model *arms*, not aggregate-vs-chain-commit.** The axis prose (`hook_output_axis.rs`) enumerates the nine by *commit site*, which for this verb overlaps: the `squash: false` aggregate belongs to both the "aggregate" and the "chain" entry. That split is unimplementable as *identities* — inside the `squash: false` arm a rejected per-sub-task commit and a rejected chain aggregate reach **one untyped `Err`** (deliberately, per T1: it is what makes the abort arm catch all three rejection causes). So the codes key on the arm the knob selects, `milestone-finalize.commit-rejected` (squash: true) and `milestone-finalize.chain-commit-rejected` (squash: false), which is also the discrimination a log reader can act on. Declared bound recorded at the table: the code names the arm, never the individual commit. Both arms re-run through the identical argv — the *route* is shared, the *identity* is not.

**The re-run is followable, not merely recognizable.** Each door echoes the flags a repeat run genuinely needs to reach the same commit phase again (`--carry-staged`, `--approve`, `--workflow`, `--force`, `--slug`); without them a re-run of a `--carry-staged` boundary refuses at the carryover gate before it ever reaches a commit. Flag-free runs stay byte-identical.

**The state-truth clause is per-door and one door cannot claim rollback — caught in this build, on the first draft.** `add-from-spec` seeds **resumably** (Inc 2 T3), landing one record-only commit per sub-task, so a rejection at the k-th leaves the k−1 earlier commits as *history* — a uniform "the milestone is unchanged" would have been a law-1 lie for every k > 1, and the axis sweep could never have seen it: rejecting the *first* commit of every door is the clause's easy arm, where "nothing survives" is trivially true. So the clause states the partial truth (*"any sub-task this run already recorded stayed committed, and the re-run seeds only the remainder"*) and a dedicated arm drives the k > 0 state with a **counting hook** that passes the first commit and refuses the second, asserting the landed commit is still there, that the frame does not claim it away, and that the lifted re-run seeds exactly the remainder. Generalizable rule this mints: *when a fix's contract is a sentence about state, its acceptance must reach the state where the sentence is hardest to keep true, not only the state the reported repro produced.*

**One list, two consumers — the cross-model review's condition, taken literally.** The producer set is a code-side table (`cli::invocation_log::COMMITTING_DOORS`), never a hand-maintained second list: `registry_mirrors_the_declared_members` *derives* `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` from it, and `crates/cli/tests/commit_rejected_axis.rs` iterates it through the real binary (a member with no arm is a hard `panic!`, never a skip). The axis test reads each door's `error_code` **out of the invocation-log record** — that read is what closes the release hole Decision 6 named: `Outcome::error`'s membership check is a `debug_assert!`, compiled out of the release build rc.10 ships for the trial, so a test exercising only the constructor would prove nothing about the shipped binary. Per door it also asserts the hook's bytes verbatim, the state-truth clause, and the argv **lifted verbatim out of the emitted message** and re-run after the hook is removed — exit 0. `corpus_migration.rs`' `migrate_corpus_fails_loudly_when_a_pre_commit_hook_rejects` **pinned the dead end as correct and is rewritten, not extended**: "it fails loudly" was true of bytes that told the operator nothing to do next, and pinning that as the whole contract is what kept this door outside the frame for five waves.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 3 T6 (N2): `migrate-corpus`' re-run recovers instead of reporting "already current"

**The door's own success banner was the lie, and it split the repo per clone.** `commit_migration` `git add`s the touched paths **before** the commit, so a rejected `pre-commit` hook left the migration *written and staged* but unlanded — and the re-run judged currency from the **worktree**, read back the stamp it had just written itself, reported `0 migrated / N already current` at **exit 0** and, with `touched` empty, committed nothing. Reproduced live before the fix: the operator saw success while **a fresh clone of the same repo still saw an unmigrated corpus** and routed `jigc migrate-corpus` — a permanently stranded migration. That is why this task is **ordered before T7** against the roadmap's narrative order: T7's frame promises every committing door that *a re-run after any rejection recovers*, and for this door the promise was unattainable.

**The currency judgment is keyed on the committed corpus.** `candidate_docs` / `committed_slugs` take a `Corpus` (`Worktree` | `Head`) — the home resolution is identical, only the enumeration primitive differs (`read_dir` vs `git ls-tree -r -z`), so the `HEAD` walk cannot drift from the walk it audits. A doc whose `HEAD` copy is **behind** while the worktree already holds the migrated result **at the current stamp** is *unlanded*: its paths rejoin the pathspec, so the re-run re-stages the identical pathspec the refused run built. It cannot fire on a doc *this* run migrates (that doc's worktree bytes are still the old ones when the residue is computed, before the fold applies) nor on ambient dirt (only the doctypes' own homes are walked).

**Elaboration pin — the commit pathspec is *wider* than the `add` pathspec.** Found by the relocation half of the acceptance going red after the in-place half went green: the earlier run's relocation **source** is already staged as a deletion, so it sits in neither the index nor the worktree and `git add` exits `fatal: pathspec … did not match any files` on it, while `git commit -- <path>` records the deletion from `HEAD` exactly as intended. One predicate for both pathspecs would have landed the **add half alone** — precisely the half-migration the commit boundary exists to prevent, and a fresh clone would then hold *both* copies. So `stageable` gates the `add` and a new `committable` (`stageable` ∪ present-in-`HEAD`) gates the commit.

**The acceptance iterates the candidate-shape axis, not the reported repro** (`migrate_corpus_re_run_after_a_rejected_commit_lands_the_migration`): both shapes in one corpus, one rejection, one recovery — **in-place** (a v0 ADR, source == destination, staged `M`) and **relocation** (the v1 `changelog` → root `CHANGELOG.md`, whose pathspec is *two* paths). Closed by the fresh-clone check the defect was found through: the clone's `jigc validate` must agree with the operator's exit 0. The commit-status line names the recovery rather than claiming this run migrated (law 1). *Declared bound:* the refused run's staged residue is **stated** by T7's frame, not removed — a `migrate-corpus` rollback is not in this increment's approved scope.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 3 T5: the record pathspec joins the captured-pre-image discipline as the fifth axis

**Increment 2 shipped a *"no staged residue"* clause and the fan-out boundary was a live counter-example (call (d)).** Both fan-out arms land through one seam, `overlay_docs_commit_and_ff`, which `git add`s jigc's own contributions — the promoted docs, the config layer, **and the milestone record's pathspec** — into the **live** index so the following `git merge --ff-only` sees them as matching. The promotions and config-layer axes each capture their own contribution; the record's was the gap, and `RecordFlipGuard` restores only the record's *worktree* bytes. So a refused boundary left a **`joined` blob staged for a milestone that never finalized**, with the file itself back at `active` — and the next plain `git commit` would land that lying record. Closed here rather than declared, because a shipped clause with a known counter-example is worse than an admitted gap.

**No new primitive.** The capture/restore is the shared third-axis pair (`capture_owner_artifact_index` / `rollback_owner_artifact_index`), which already models **absent** — so an unstaged record is restored to absent, never conjured — read before the stage arm's live `git add`, where the flip has touched only the worktree file and the index still holds the genuine pre-finalize entry.

**Membership is decided where the pathspec is carried, not by a call-site list** (the set-fence discipline): `StagePolicy::live_index_record_pathspecs` destructures the enum exhaustively, so a stage arm added later that stages a path into the live index must decide there rather than silently escaping the rollback.

**The acceptance iterates the seam's caller axis, not the reported repro** (`crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_ff_rollback.rs`): the defect is in the shared seam, so a fix proven on one arm proves nothing about the other — `squash: true` (`combine_commit`) and `squash: false` (`chain_commit`) each drive the **hookless** cause, ordinary untracked WIP in the main checkout colliding with a path the fan-out commits, which is the only rejection cause that reaches the live-index `git add` before failing (a hook rejection aborts inside the dedicated worktree, upstream of it). Per arm: non-zero exit, `git show :<record>` byte-identical to the pre-finalize index entry, the raw `git ls-files --stage` entry unchanged, no record path in `git diff --cached --name-only`, the worktree bytes back at `active`, and the clause **driven** — a subsequent plain `git commit` cannot land a `joined` record. Verified red on both arms independently.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 3 T4: the landed teardown names the work it destroys, and the over-report is fixed at birth

**A boundary that exits 0 must not also have silently destroyed work (call (c)).** Both landed fan-out arms commit only the **staged** set (`worktree_staged_patch`) and then `git worktree remove --force` the whole checkout — so a sub-agent's unstaged and untracked bytes died at **exit 0, unnarrated, on the *success* path**. The codebase already knew this and said so in a doc comment: `dirty_worktrees` reads `git status --porcelain` precisely because the teardown destroys *"staged, unstaged, and untracked alike"*, and `discard` guards exactly that set behind `--force` while `finalize` guarded nothing. So the loss is now **named on both channels**: a non-blocking pre-removal warning on stderr (every caller, `discard --force` included, where it names what the human's `--force` threw away — the un-forced `discard` refuses earlier, so the two never both speak) and the landing manifest on stdout, additively in the pinned `committed.sub_tasks[].discarded` JSON as well as the prose block, one struct feeding both arms.

**Honest bound, recorded not glossed: visible, *not prevented*.** The staged set — the work explicitly prepared for commit — is safely in git on this path, so the law-1 minimum is proportionate; a `discard`-style refusal + `--force` on the landed path is **new surface**, out of the rc.10 charter, chartered to M46. The acceptance asserts the bound itself (the worktree is gone), so the surface cannot quietly drift into claiming a guarantee it does not give.

**The over-report is fixed at birth, not shipped-then-patched.** The lost build shipped this warning collecting `MM`/`AM` cells as "never staged" and the completion audit caught it (*"worth more than its LOW label"* — the one genuinely new law-1 surface of the wave overstating its own claim, and the seed of the whole git-path cascade). The re-execution therefore folds the fix forward: a **three-way partition keyed on the porcelain index column** — *wholly staged* (`A `/`M `/`R `: every byte is in the patch the boundary commits, so it is **not** reported), *never staged* (`??`/` M`/` D`), *staged only in part* (`MM`/`AM`/`UU`: the indexed version lands, the worktree's later edit dies). The exclusion is mutation-checked, not assumed: reclassifying the wholly-staged cell makes the acceptance red on the landed path.

**Two reader decisions taken with the evidence rather than the default.** `--porcelain -z`, because git display-quotes a path holding a space, a quote or a non-ASCII byte **regardless of `core.quotePath`** (re-probed on this machine's git) and a fan-out worktree holds arbitrary user code — the plain form would name a path the repo does not contain, on the one surface whose entire job is to name what was lost. And `--untracked-files=all`, because git's default collapses a wholly untracked directory to the single entry `notes/`, naming a *directory* where the surface promises the destroyed **paths**; a rename/copy entry's trailing origin record is consumed so the NUL stream stays aligned.

**The acceptance iterates two axes, not the reported repro** (`crates/cli/tests/milestone_teardown_loss.rs`): the three partition cells live in **one** worktree at once (so the wholly-staged exclusion is proven against a live positive, not an empty set), across the **landed-arm axis** — `squash: true` and `false` each call `remove_worktrees` and each build the manifest — and both output surfaces, with a fully-staged sibling sub-task asserted to produce no warning and no manifest row at all. The staged half of the `MM` path is asserted to have actually landed in the commit, so "partly" is proven, not asserted.

**One design statement corrected in the same motion, because this change falsifies it.** [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → Abandon refuses on a dirty worktree justified the unconditional `--force` with *"the commit lands first, so **every byte the worktree held** is already in git"* — true of the *committed set*, false of the worktree. T1 repaired the abort-arm half of that premise; this repairs the landed half and states the new narration + its bound where the justification lives.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 3 T3: the fresh-clone reseed rebuilds the sub-task working areas, so the refusal's route is followable

**A route that is not followable is not a route.** T2's `milestone.zero-contribution` refusal points a fresh-clone operator at `jigc milestone provision <id>` → execute → the emitted `Spawn:` line — and that line dead-ended. The M39 reseed rebuilt only `.jigc/milestones/<id>/{base,tasks}.json`, so the clone knew *which* sub-tasks the milestone carries and nothing else: `.jigc/tasks/<sub-id>/` was never rebuilt, and re-entry answered *"no task `<sub>` — list a milestone's sub-tasks with `jigc milestone list-tasks <milestone-id>`"* — a route back to the surface that names the very sub-task with no area. A **loop**, six doors dead. Verified live at HEAD before the fix (real `git clone` → provision → the emitted span → exit 1). **Pre-existing since M39** (the reseed fn is byte-identical pre-M47) and folded forward into the owning increment per the rebuild hand-off; T2's *Proves* was attainable without it, but T2's new blocking finding is what routes into the dead end, and the M43 route floor makes a dead-ending route a defect in its own right.

**Enforcement of the design of record, not a revision.** [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → Engine capability 2 already promised *"resumes un-joined tasks from scratch — active tasks re-run from their recorded `intent`"*; it under-specified *where* the re-derived state lands. The new `engine::milestone::reseed_sub_task_areas` mints the standard working area (`state::mint_task`, never a second minting discipline) per recorded sub-task: the record's `{#id}` anchor as the **slug override** — never a re-slug of the intent, which would fork the id from the join, the worktree path and the spawn line the moment the slug-rule generation moves — the milestone's shared base pin, and the item's verbatim `intent`. Idempotent and non-destructive: an existing area is skipped untouched, so a live session's areas (and the `--workflow` they really recorded) are never clobbered. It hangs off the **one shared `reseed_cache` site**, after the terminal guard, so every milestone verb inherits it rather than a hand-kept subset — and the acceptance iterates that entry-door axis (`list-tasks`/`provision`/`execute`/`finalize`, each as the *first* op on its own fresh clone; `finalize` too, since the reseed runs ahead of its refusal).

**The masking test is dismantled, not extended.** The lost build stayed green for 20 days because this increment's own suite hand-wrote the state the tool cannot rebuild. So the new arms build their fresh-clone state **only by driving the binary** — a real `git clone` of a real origin — and then run the *emitted* bytes verbatim: the refusal's own `` `…` `` route span as argv, and each `Spawn:` span through `sh -c` with a `jigc` shim on `PATH`, reaching a sub-task compose at exit 0 whose composed text carries the record's intent, then staging code in the worktrees and landing it with a re-run `finalize`. A fixture that reached into `.jigc/tasks/` would prove nothing here.

**Declared bound, recorded not glossed: `--workflow` is workbench-local and not fresh-clone-durable.** The record carries `task-id`/`intent`/`status` and nothing about the minting workflow, so the reseed re-derives the pack's default `sub-task` — correct for every un-overridden sub-task, and for an overridden one the operator's own `jigc workflow <other> --task <id>` re-entry is refused **loudly** by the shipped W-equality guard (pinned as its own arm) rather than composed as something else. Two facts checked live rather than assumed: `milestone execute`'s fan-out `run:` is pack-fixed at `workflow:sub-task`, so an overridden sub-task was already un-drivable through `execute` **with a live workbench** (it blocked on `workflow-refs.workflow-mismatch`); after the reseed that same emitted span composes the `sub-task` workflow it names — the override intent is *forgotten*, which is the honest bound, since it never existed outside the gitignored workbench. Making it durable means putting it in the frozen `milestone-record` schema — a one-way door, out of charter. **Every recorded item is rebuilt, unfiltered:** a non-terminal record has no settled items (both terminals flip the header and every item in one write) and a terminal header never reaches here, so an item-status filter would be unreachable code.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 3 T2: a zero-contribution milestone finalize is refused, and the manifest names who could not contribute

**The refusal (call (b)(i)).** `jigc milestone finalize` now blocks a boundary that would **land no work** — nothing in the plan's promote set, nothing staged in any sub-task worktree — leaving only jigc's own bookkeeping to commit. Reproduced live before the fix on a real clone (the gitignored `.jigc/` workbench is not cloned): `finalize` → **exit 0**, zero work landed, record flipped to the terminal `joined` — the milestone permanently un-finalizable. One routed `milestone.zero-contribution` keyed at `milestone:<id>`, the `RecordFlipGuard` restoring `active` on the way out. It cannot false-fire on a genuine docs-only milestone: that one *promotes* merged docs (pinned as its own arm).

**Widened at build time, with the evidence, not the settled letter: the predicate is the plan's promote set, not `has_diff`.** The settled *"block when `has_diff` rests solely on `record_changed`"* is the motivating case; taken literally it leaves the **identical** zero-work commit reachable one contribution channel over. `has_diff`'s doc term counts every *materialized* address, and a sub-task's `commit:<sub-id>` is **transient** — materialized by the join, never promoted (`plan_promotions`: a doctype with neither `location` nor `placement` has no destination). Probed live before widening: a milestone whose sub-agent authored its commit doc and staged no code → **exit 0**, one commit carrying only `.jigc/.gitignore` + the record burned to `joined`. So the guard keys on **promote set ∪ staged worktree code** — what actually lands — which closes the channel axis at one seam rather than pinning the reported repro (`dev-workflow.md` → *a fix is complete over its class's axis*), and also covers the dev-only variant where there is no record to flip at all. The widened trigger got its response re-derived across the widened domain (the M44 rule): the message's *"burns the terminal `joined`"* clause is **context-fed** on whether a record exists, since a context-independent statement would render that lie on every dev-only boundary. Both members are pinned as an axis-iterating arm.

**Elaboration pin — the refusal sits AFTER the planner, not at the `has_diff` computation.** The task note said only *"block when `has_diff` rests solely on `record_changed`"*. Placing it at the computation (before `plan_milestone_finalize`) pre-empts the base-guard: verified by a shipped test going red — `finalize_finding_keys.rs`'s `a_blocked_milestone_finalize_keys_at_the_milestone` drives a *diverged-base* milestone with no docs and asserts `finalize.base-mismatch`, and it reported the zero-contribution code instead. So the block is placed **beside the empty-commit guard it refines**, immediately after the planner, keeping the carryover gate's recorded precedence order (staging → base-mismatch → empty-commit → this). Both blocks exit 3, so the sibling test at `milestone_record_finalize.rs` now **asserts its reason**, not just its code — two refusals that share an exit code are indistinguishable otherwise.

**The visible degrade (call (b)(ii)) — the clause rides *every* sub-task with no worktree, including a docs-only milestone's.** The isolated worktree is the sole place a sub-agent's code can live, so a sub-task without one contributed no code **by construction** — a fact `code_files: 0` cannot distinguish from "staged nothing". The clause states the *code channel's* absence, so scoping it to partial fan-outs would make it context-dependent (and therefore a lie in the omitted context). `provisioned: bool` joins the `committed.sub_tasks` objects additively — the degrade is data on the machine surface, not only prose.

**Both fixes are knob-independent by construction, not by coverage** (the fix-shape hierarchy: unify the seam > iterate the members): the refusal sits above the `squash` branch and the contribution facts are computed once and handed to both commit channels — one seam per fix, so no `squash`-mode arm is owed. **The fixture sweep is the finding, not a chore: five suites finalized milestones that landed nothing.** `milestone_record_finalize.rs`'s fold test used the *empty* milestone as the cheapest route to the flip — i.e. the refused shape; `carryover_gate.rs`'s milestone arm said so in as many words (*"the record flip is what gives a docs-only milestone a non-empty finalize commit, so the finalize reaches the carryover gate"*) and would have had three arms masked by a block firing ahead of the gate under test; `flow40_acceptance.rs`'s team-ready arc, `milestone_discard.rs`'s `joined`-terminal arm, and both landing arms of `milestone_finalize_base_guard.rs` the same. Each is repaired by giving the boundary **real work** (an authored doc, or staged worktree code where the fixture already provisions worktrees); every existing assertion is preserved. One needed more than a fixture line: `interleaved_milestone_record_bookkeeping_wedges_neither_finalize` asserted **both** milestones land, which was only reachable because neither carried work — once A lands a real doc, B's `base..HEAD` genuinely holds a non-record commit and the base-guard blocks it, correctly. The predicate under test (another milestone's *bookkeeping* must not wedge) is proven by A; B's block is now asserted to be the **honest** divergence, so the arm states what it actually shows.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 3 T1: an aborted fan-out finalize keeps the code it never committed

**The teardown's precondition is "the commit landed", not "the verb was `finalize`".** The `squash: false` abort arm called `remove_worktrees` — `git worktree remove --force` — on a boundary where nothing was committed, and since M31 Inc 4/5 the provisioned worktree is the **sole copy** of a sub-agent's staged code. So the one arm whose whole job is *"leave it intact for the retry"* was the arm that destroyed the retry's input. This is **enforcement of the design of record, not a revision of it**: [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → 6. Commit already promises *"working area intact"*, and [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md)'s justification for the unconditional `--force` is *"the commit lands **first**"* — false here. The `squash: true` abort sibling already tore down nothing; both arms now agree. A *scoped* teardown was considered and rejected: it would need its own justification the fork never produced.

**The acceptance iterates the rejection-cause axis, not the reported repro** (`crates/cli/tests/milestone_abort_survives.rs`). The destroyer sat behind an untyped `Err(err) =>`, so it fired on three causes, not the one the halt report named: an aggregate-hook rejection, a **per-sub-task**-hook rejection, and a `git merge --ff-only` refusal over ordinary untracked main-checkout WIP **with no hook installed at all**. Each is driven through the binary and each is followed by the *identical* re-run once the cause is removed, landing the sub-task code — pinning recovery, not just survival. Verified red on all three independently before the fix.

**`milestone_finalize_tears_down_the_provisioned_worktrees_on_an_aborted_finalize` pinned the defect as correct and is INVERTED — a basis-has-changed rebuttal, not an override.** Its rationale (2026-06-21 M31 Inc 3 T4, below) wired the teardown into the abort path when that path still `reset --hard`ed the live checkout and the worktrees were redundant scratch; M31 Inc 4/5 falsified that basis two increments later, the classic defect-at-a-distance. Renamed to `…_keeps_…`, with the reversal's reasoning carried in the test. `…_aggregate_failure_is_wip_safe_and_resets_to_pre_finalize_head` compares the *main* checkout's porcelain and stays green untouched.

*Two declared bounds, re-recorded not fixed:* `provision_worktrees`' `remove_dir_all` on a non-registered leftover — narrow before, but this task makes "a live worktree holding uncommitted code" a **normal** state, widening it — and `jigc uninstall`'s unconditional `.jigc` wipe, pre-existing and outside M47. *One behaviour change on a second verb, named not discovered:* with the worktrees surviving, `jigc milestone discard` now correctly **refuses** after an aborted finalize with its dirty-worktree route — a safety gain; no shipped `discard` arm runs after an aborted finalize, so none needed repair.
