Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/migrate_corpus.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/corpus_migration.rs`; docs: `design/corpus-migration.md`.)*
- **T7 — the survivable frame sweeps the whole 9-door committing axis, one error code per door.** `CommitRejected` → `pub(crate)`; `render::commit_rejected` generalized off the task idiom to take a **state-truth statement + the door's own re-run argv**; applied at all 9 production doors (`setup`'s install commit excluded with its recorded `--no-verify` reason). Mint **one error code per door** into `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY` — the recorded *"deliberately not a per-verb code mint"* rationale **revised in place with its rationale engaged** — keeping `finalize.commit-rejected` as the task-finalize door's shipped identity, landing the registry at 10 members with `migrate.review-pending`, and growing `surface-contract.md:76`'s prose mirror **in the same commit** (`registry_mirrors_the_declared_members` hard-fails until it does). `finalize.md`:99's frame paragraph is generalized from one door to the family. **The producer set is one code-side list with two consumers** — a `(door, error code)` table in the `cli` lib, consumed by the registry-mirror test **and** the new rejection axis test, never a hand-maintained second list (the cross-model review made its clean bill on per-door codes conditional on exactly this), so a door added without a code is a **red test**, not a silent log entry naming the wrong verb; `hook_output_axis.rs:11-40`'s prose enumeration points at it as the non-blocking sibling. This is one gate-green unit: the registry-vs-producer test is red until every door carries its code, so a partial sweep has no green commit boundary. `crates/cli/tests/corpus_migration.rs:891` (`migrate_corpus_fails_loudly_when_a_pre_commit_hook_rejects`) **pins the dead end as correct and is rewritten, not extended**. *Done:* a new `crates/cli/tests/commit_rejected_axis.rs` iterating the code-side door list through the **real binary** under a rejecting `pre-commit` hook, asserting per door — git's bytes **verbatim and unwrapped**; a state-truth sentence naming what survived; the door's **own** re-run argv; a non-zero exit carrying **that door's** code into the invocation log (`error_code`, asserted from the log record, so the release-build `debug_assert!` gap is closed at test time); and the printed argv **lifted verbatim and re-run** after the hook is removed, exiting 0 — plus the registry-mirror test derived from the same list, and the `--format json` arm keeping the framed text in the `operational_error` envelope. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/cli/src/invocation_log.rs`, `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/src/rename.rs`, `crates/cli/src/migrate_corpus.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/commit_rejected_axis.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/corpus_migration.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/hook_output_axis.rs`; docs: `design/surface-contract.md`, `design/finalize.md`.)*

*Why this order:* **state before speech** — T1–T5 make the state the frame will describe actually survive (T0's four calls, in the halt resolution's own (a)→(d) order), T6 makes the one door whose re-run does **not** recover recover, and only then does T7 write the sentence that claims all of it; a frame written earlier would be the law-1 lie the halt was called on. T3 sits directly behind T2 because it is the followability of T2's own new route. Every *Grouped scope* bullet lands: the inverted test + the RED-comment correction + the basis-has-changed record ride **T1**, as do the two **declared bounds** re-recorded rather than fixed (`provision_worktrees`' `remove_dir_all` on an unregistered leftover, `milestone.rs:1272-1275` — which T1 widens by making "a live worktree holding uncommitted code" normal — and `jigc uninstall`'s unconditional `.jigc` wipe, `setup.rs:1203-1211`, pre-existing and outside M47) and the **named-not-discovered** behaviour change on a second verb (with the worktrees surviving, `jigc milestone discard` now correctly refuses after an aborted finalize with its dirty-worktree route — a safety gain, and any shipped `discard` arm that runs after an aborted finalize is repaired inside T1); the five owed doc revisions ride T1/T2/T5/T7 with their owning change; `corpus_migration.rs:891` is rewritten in **T7** and the axis enumeration is derived, never hand-written. **Added beyond the approved scope, declared not smuggled:** T3, a folded-forward known fix whose reason to land here is written into its bullet — if it proves larger than that bullet, it is a halt, not a silent drop.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 2 T3 fix: the resume skip set is the *record's*, and the mint abort unwinds too

T3's resume asked *"does the milestone already carry this criterion?"* of the **gitignored `tasks.json` cache**. The cache is not the source of truth — the committed record is (`design/team-ready-state.md`) — and this is the one question where the difference decides whether work is **dropped**: any id that reached the workbench but never the record was absorbed as "already seeded", so the criterion was absent from the committed, team-ready record **forever**, at exit 0 with a positive ack. T3's own predecessor hard-blocked there (`milestone.sub-task-collision`); it converted a loud dead end into a silent loss, in the wave that exists to stop quiet loss. **The skip set is now what the record names**, the cache serving only where there is no record home at all (dev-only, where it *is* the only home). The at-entry timing — what keeps a resume distinguishable from an authoring collision — is unchanged; only the list changed.

**And the producer is closed at the same seam.** The reachable producing state was the door's own: two criteria slugging alike abort `add_task` mid-loop, leaving the earlier mints in the cache with no record commit, because the unwind covered only the *record-rejection* half. `add_from_spec` now hands its partial mints back with the finding (`SeedingAborted { finding, minted }`) and the door unwinds them through the identical primitive a rejected k-th commit uses — one seam for both halves, so the divergence is not merely survived but not produced.

*Pinned over the **producer axis**, not the reported repro* (`crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_rollback.rs`): every way the workbench can come to name a sub-task the record does not — a rejected k-th record commit, an engine-side mint abort, and a planted cache residue standing for an unwind that could not finish — each driven through the real binary, each asserting one invariant: **no exit-0 run of `add-from-spec` leaves a criterion of its spec out of the committed record**. Verified red on the mint-abort arm as the trial found it: `seeded 1 sub-task(s) … (2 already seeded, skipped: …)` at exit 0 over a record naming one of three.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 2 T4: the conflict route belongs to the caller, and every caller must be able to say something true

The reported defect was one door's lie, but its cause is a **placement** error: `conflict_block_finding` hard-coded both the mover clause (*"this task's staged writes"*) and the route (`jigc task discard <task-id>`) inside a classifier that holds a path, a hash and a boolean — no task id, and at one of its callers no task at all. So the milestone-record doors blocked with an **inapplicable verb** carrying an **unsubstituted placeholder**, the exact pair the M43 route floor exists to prevent on a *blocking* finding. The fix moves the presentation out to a caller-supplied `engine::file_state::ConflictBlock` (private fields, constructors only): the classifier keeps the invariant `` conflict on `<path>`: `` frame + the location and **contributes no task language of its own**.

**The axis is *callers*, not the reported door, and it has three members — the third was found by sweeping it.** Task scope passes the real id (`ConflictBlock::task`, `TaskArea` gaining an `id` field as the substitution source — the M43 wording survives verbatim, only the placeholder is gone); the record doors name the record and route a **human** revert to what jigc last wrote (an external edit to a machine-maintained record is never merged and never clobbered, so no `jigc` verb resolves it — the same shape as M45's owner-artifact `git add` route); and the **milestone join gate**, which also drives `validate_task` over a merged staging area owned by *no single task*, would otherwise have inherited the identical lie — it routes at `jigc task list` instead.

*Pinned by the emitted bytes, per seam:* the task-scope arm **lifts the printed route argv and runs it verbatim** (it discards the real task — a surviving `<task-id>` fails at `no_such_task`), the record arm asserts the contract at both overwrite doors through a shared checker (names the record · no `jigc task discard` · no `<…>` span left unsubstituted, scanned generically rather than pinned to `<task-id>`), and an engine arm drives an arbitrary caller's presentation through the classifier to prove the message clause **and the route kind** round-trip untouched. The shipped assertions that pinned the old strings are repaired in the same commit, not deleted.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 2 T3: `add-from-spec` recovers by resuming, and the skip set is the list *at entry*

The door that lands N commits cannot be made atomic — the k−1 that landed are history — so its atomicity is redefined to the property that is actually reachable and actually load-bearing: **the workbench names exactly what the record names**. On a rejected k-th commit the mints the record never named are unwound (areas removed, ids dropped from the demoted `tasks.json` through the new `engine::milestone::drop_sub_tasks`, which re-renders the survivors in order and is therefore byte-identical to the cache's k−1 state), and recovery becomes a **resume**: `add_from_spec` returns `SeededFromSpec { added, already_seeded }`, skipping a criterion whose sub-task the milestone already carries instead of dead-ending on `milestone.sub-task-collision`.

**The one elaboration the Settle did not reach: the skip set is the task list *as read at entry*, never the live list.** *(Corrected the same day — see the T3 fix entry above: **at entry** held, but the list was the wrong one; the skip set is the committed record's, never the cache's.)* Keyed on the live list, a resume and an **authoring collision** become the same event — two criteria of one spec slugging alike would be silently absorbed as "already seeded", turning a refusal into a skipped acceptance criterion. Reading the set once, before the first mint, makes an id minted by *this* call absent from it, so the duplicate still blocks and the two stay distinguishable (pinned by its own engine arm, alongside the resume arm).

*Also pinned:* the rejection **prints the resume command** — built through the checked `Route::mechanical` constructor (the M43 route fence), carrying `--workflow` when it is not the default, because a resume that silently records a different minting workflow is the same class of lie — and the axis test **lifts that printed line verbatim** rather than rebuilding an equivalent, since the emitted bytes are what an operator runs. The ack states both halves (`seeded N sub-task(s) … (M already seeded, skipped: …)`); a fully-seeded re-run is a true ack, not a collision.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 2 T2: the unwind is the door's, and the refusal stops claiming a commit

Making `create` and `add-task` atomic forced one elaboration and settled one axis question. **(1) The unwind is a single primitive the doors call, not per-door code.** `unwind_mint(area, restore)` removes the directory *this call* minted and restores a captured file to its pre-append bytes; it is safe **because the engine mints refuse a pre-existing id before creating anything**, so an area reaching it was created by this call and never found — the engine's identity guard is untouched, which is what keeps the unwind a CLI-door concern rather than a relaxation of `add_task`'s collision block. T3's `add-from-spec` mid-loop unwind is the same primitive applied over `k..N`. Its one dependency goes `pub` at the point the name is decided: `engine::milestone::TASKS_FILE`, so the door's capture cannot drift onto a second spelling of the file every writer already agrees on.

**(2) The door axis has an already-safe member and it is asserted, not assumed.** `discard` mints nothing and runs its teardown *after* the record commit, so a rejection already left its workbench intact — the arm now **pins** that (a future teardown-before-commit reddens here) rather than leaving the member unexamined; `add-from-spec` is excluded with its reason (k−1 record commits already landed ⇒ resume, not unwind — T3's). Both recovery arms were verified red **independently of** the unwind assertion, each blocking with exactly the predicted collision (`milestone.serial-collision` / `milestone.sub-task-collision`), so assertion 7 is real coverage and not a shadow of assertion 2b.

**(3) `milestone.record-exists` stops claiming the record was *committed*.** `guard_record_free` probes the record path's **existence** and runs no git read, so it never had grounds for the word — and after T1 the surviving instance is not the rejected-`create` residue but the plain hand-drafted record, which is untracked by construction. That is the law-1 repair's test: an untracked record at the canonical home, `create` refused, the message stating what it found and the route (which was always right) unchanged.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Inc 2 T1: the rollback lives at the seam, and "absent" must mean absent

Building the fifth staged-path family forced two elaborations the Settle did not reach, both load-bearing. **(1) The transaction wraps the shared commit helper, not each door.** All four record-only doors already funnel through one `commit_record_only`, so the rollback rides a `commit_record_transaction` wrapper there and each door's only obligation is to *capture before it writes* — coverage becomes a property of the seam rather than of four callers each remembering, which is the same set-fence discipline `jigc_config_layer_pathspecs` buys the fourth axis. **(2) `bytes: None` means the file was NotFound, never "unreadable".** The absent-file axis is what `create` needs — its pre-image is `(bytes: absent, index: absent)` and the restore is a **delete** — so swallowing an IO/permission error into that same value would convert a rejected commit into the *deletion of a record that still exists*: the one value in this design whose misreading is data loss. Only `ErrorKind::NotFound` yields it; any other read error fails the capture and the door never writes.

*Also pinned, because the test would otherwise be a proxy:* the "no staged residue" clause is proven by **driving** the carryover gate — after each rejected door the suite runs `jigc start` → author → `jigc task finalize` on an unrelated task and demands exit 0 with no `finalize.carried-staged` — never by reading `git status`. Verified red per door against the unfixed tree (all four, each door driven first in the axis order), so the axis is net-new coverage, not an assertion flip.

## 2026-08-03 — M47 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 2](implementation/roadmap.md) (N1 — the record-only doors stop bricking, H2's prerequisite) into **4 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `f88c753` (tree clean; Inc 1 landed). Design of record: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-07-26 the Settle, **Decision 4** (captured-pre-image rollback on rejection — the obvious fix is foreclosed by `reconciliation.md:51`, so rollback honours it untouched and joins the confidence-audit's captured-pre-image discipline as a **fifth staged-path family**; it also clears the compounding staged-residue defect; **N1 precedes H2 on 4 of 9 doors**) and its route half (the M43 route floor: a *blocking* finding may not carry an inapplicable verb, and a placeholder whose value the caller knows must be substituted — the Settle's P6, whose recorded correction is that `<task-id>` is **not** derivable from `key.target` and therefore *"needs a different source"*; the caller **is** that source). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 47 Increment 2.

**Basis, reproduced live against the real binary at HEAD — every claim below was driven through `target/debug/jigc` in throwaway repos, not inherited from the roadmap:**

- **The brick is exactly as N1 describes, and it is three different bricks, not one.** All four doors write the record, `git add` it, commit it, and only then advance the baseline (`milestone.rs:351→362`, `:742→750`, `:1249→1257`); every later milestone write runs `reconcile_record_preflight` (`:470`) **first**. Rejecting a `pre-commit` hook on **`add-task`** leaves the record appended-on-disk, staged (`M  docs/milestone-records/<id>.md`), the baseline at the pre-append hash — and after the hook is fixed **`add-task`, `discard --force` and `finalize` all block with `reconciliation.conflict-block`, permanently**, while `jigc validate` reports blocking `file-state.hash-matches` at **exit 0**. Rejecting **`create`** leaves the record staged as `A `, **no baseline at all**, and the milestone area minted: the re-run blocks with `milestone.record-exists` — *"already has a **committed** record"*, a law-1 lie about a commit that never landed. Rejecting **`discard`** leaves the settled (`status: discarded`) record staged with the teardown un-run.
- **The mid-loop shape is real and its arithmetic is the CLI's, not the engine's.** `add_from_spec` mints **all N** sub-tasks (engine, git-free) and the CLI *then* commits one record append per sub-task (`milestone.rs:809-827`). Driven with a hook rejecting the k-th commit (N=3, k=2): the record on disk carries **alpha+beta** with only alpha committed, `tasks.json` carries **all three**, three task areas exist, gamma never reaches the record — then the re-run conflict-blocks. So the post-rejection state is not merely un-recoverable, it is **internally inconsistent** (cache ≠ record), which is why the unwind and the resume are separate tasks.
- **Nothing pins the current wreckage.** Verified: no test in the tree installs a *rejecting* hook against any of the four doors (`milestone.rs`'s `install_aggregate_rejecting_hook` targets `milestone finalize`; `hook_output_axis.rs` uses a **non-blocking** hook) — so T1/T2/T3 are net-new coverage on a red-first path, not assertion flips. The door axis itself is already enumerated for the non-blocking case at `hook_output_axis.rs:11-40` (producer 6) — the same axis, its rejecting sibling.
- **The restore primitive exists and is index-keyed, so this family does not invent one.** `capture_owner_artifact_index` / `rollback_owner_artifact_index` (`task.rs:2312`, `:2352`) capture `(mode, blob-sha)` **including "absent"** and restore via `update-index --cacheinfo` / `--force-remove`, worktree untouched — the third/fourth-axis discipline. They are private to `task.rs`; `milestone.rs` is a sibling module in the same crate, so `pub(crate)` reaches them. `owner_artifact_is_stageable_shape` (`:2216`) rejects only absolute / `..` paths, so a record path passes.
- **The record's own state has a *third* axis the other families lack: the file may be absent.** `create` writes a record where none existed, so its pre-image is `(bytes: absent, index: absent)` and the restore is a **delete + `--force-remove`**; `add-task`/`add-from-spec`/`discard` restore bytes + a present entry. Any capture that models only "present" silently leaves `create`'s record behind.
- **The conflict route's two defects are one root cause, and the fix's source is available at both seams.** `conflict_block_finding` (`file_state.rs:1045`) hard-codes both the message clause *"this task's staged writes"* and the route `jigc task discard <task-id>` inside the **engine classifier**, which has no task in scope at either caller. Verified the substitution source exists: the store sweep receives the task dir (`validate.rs:292` passes `dir`), and `TaskArea::resolve` builds it as `<jigc_home>/.jigc/tasks/<id>` (`task.rs:629`) — so the id is the dir's file name, and the CLI caller holds it outright; the milestone caller (`milestone.rs:495`) has **no task and needs a different route entirely**. Emission sites are exactly two.
- **The blast radius of the route change is small and named:** the exact-string assertion at `file_state.rs:1332-1337`, plus the loose `"external edit" || "conflict"` assertions in `milestone_record_reconcile.rs:181`/`:222`; `singleton_running_doc.rs:477` and `e2e_audit.rs:794` reference the classifier in prose. **Zero compose goldens are touched** — the 612 goldens are workflow compositions and no pack step names any of these surfaces (grepped), and no test asserts `add-from-spec`'s ack text, so T3 may reshape it without a re-pin wave.
- **The known-fixes checklist is folded forward, not re-discovered.** The lost build shipped this increment as three commits and its **completion audit then found the mid-loop rejection still lying and unrecoverable** (`recovery-report.md` → 4.2 finding 1, fixed post-audit as resumable seeding `SeededFromSpec { added, already_seeded }`). Per the [rebuild hand-off](completions/artifacts/M47/rebuild-handover.md), that fix lands in its **owning increment** this time — and it is not a discretionary addition: the approved *Proves* (*"a rejecting hook on any of the four doors leaves the repo recoverable — fix the hook, re-run, it succeeds"*) is **unattainable for `add-from-spec` without it**, since the k−1 already-landed record commits cannot be unwound. The lost build's four validator advisories are folded into the done-criteria rather than re-earned: the index-restore axis is **asserted on the index** (not "unstaged"), and the *"no staged residue"* clause is proven by **driving the carryover gate**, never by a porcelain proxy.
- **No genuine new fork surfaced.** The one shape question the roadmap leaves open — whether `add-from-spec` unwinds or resumes — is settled by its own approved *Proves* clause plus the recovered post-audit fix, not by a new decision.

- **T1 — the record-commit transaction: the four doors capture and restore the record's pre-image, worktree *and* index.** Before the write, each door captures the record path's `(worktree bytes | absent, index entry | absent)`; on **any** failure of `commit_record_only` (hook rejection or git error) restore both — bytes rewritten or the file deleted, the index entry restored via `update-index --cacheinfo` or dropped via `--force-remove`, the worktree never reset to HEAD — then propagate the error unchanged (the hook's stderr stays verbatim, `finalize.md`'s M40 refinement 3). The baseline is **not** advanced, so `reconciliation.md:51` stands untouched: nothing landed, nothing re-baselines. Reuse the third-axis primitives (`task.rs:2312`/`:2352`, `pub(crate)`) rather than minting a parallel one; extend them for the **absent-file** axis `create` needs. Docs in the same motion: [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → Hash re-baselining gains the **fourth site** (the milestone record-op write, `baseline_record`) so *"exactly three sites"* stops being false and the next commit door is discoverable, plus the § MVP-scope line that enumerates the three; [finalize.md](design/finalize.md) → Rollback discipline gains the **fifth staged-path family** row (the record-only doors, index-keyed, including the absent axis); [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The commit model states the per-op commit is a transaction with a rollback boundary. *Done:* a new axis test (`crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_rollback.rs`) iterating **the four doors × a rejecting `pre-commit` hook** through the **real binary**, asserting per door — exit non-zero with git's stderr verbatim; the record's on-disk bytes byte-identical to the pre-door state (**absent** for `create`); `git ls-files --stage -- <record>` byte-identical to the pre-door entry (**empty** for `create`) — the index axis asserted as an *entry*, not as "not staged"; `git status --porcelain` names nothing under the record's location; `jigc validate` exits 0 with **no** `file-state.hash-matches` and **no** `reconciliation.conflict-block` naming the record; and the **carryover clause driven, not proxied** — after a rejected door, `jigc start "<unrelated intent>"` → author → `jigc task finalize` lands at exit 0 with **no** `finalize.carried-staged` naming the record path (red today: the residue is staged at mint and blocks). Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_rollback.rs`; docs: `design/reconciliation.md`, `design/finalize.md`, `design/team-ready-state.md`.)*
- **T2 — the mint unwinds with its record: `create` and `add-task` become atomic.** T1 restores the *committed* half; the *workbench* half still survives a rejection, so the re-run hits `milestone.serial-collision` (`create`, `engine/src/milestone.rs:201`) or `milestone.sub-task-collision` (`add-task`, `:272`) — an honest block, but not the approved recoverability. On a rejected record commit each appending door unwinds exactly what it minted in the same call: `create` removes the milestone area it created (never one it found); `add-task` removes the sub-task area and restores `tasks.json` to its captured pre-append bytes. Keep `add_task`'s own collision block intact — the unwind is the CLI door's, never a relaxation of the engine's identity guard. Also repair `create`'s law-1 lie surfaced by the repro: `milestone.record-exists` says *"already has a **committed** record"* over a record that was only ever written, so the door's refusal states what it actually found (its route already resolves correctly and stays). *Done:* the T1 axis test grows a **recovery arm** per door — with the hook removed, the identical `create` re-run exits 0 and lands its record commit (and `.jigc/milestones/<id>/` did not exist between the two runs); the identical `add-task` re-run exits 0, and `tasks.json` + `.jigc/tasks/` + the committed record name exactly one `alpha-fix` each (no orphan area, no duplicate item); `jigc milestone list-tasks` and `jigc doc show milestone-record:<id> --format json` agree on the set; `jigc validate` clean at exit 0. Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_rollback.rs`.)*
- **T3 — `add-from-spec`'s mid-loop becomes atomic *and* resumable.** The remaining door is the only one whose rejection can leave the cache and the record disagreeing, and the only one whose recovery cannot be an unwind (the k−1 record commits already landed). Two halves, one motion: (a) on the k-th rejection the CLI unwinds the **un-recorded** mints (T2's primitive, applied over `k..N`) so the task list and the record name the identical k−1 sub-tasks; (b) `add_from_spec` becomes **resumable** — a criterion whose minted id is already in *this milestone's* task list is skipped rather than collided, and the ack states both halves (the recovered `SeededFromSpec { added, already_seeded }` shape; the executor may instead interleave mint-and-record per criterion, which makes (a) singular — either shape is acceptable, the invariant below is not). The rejection message names the **re-run argv that actually works**. *Done:* an axis test iterating **k ∈ 1..=N over an N=3-criteria spec**, rejecting exactly the k-th record commit, asserting for **every** k — the committed record and `tasks.json` name the same k−1 sub-tasks in the same order, the record is unstaged and byte-identical to its k−1 state, no orphan task area exists for the un-recorded criteria; then, hook removed, the re-run **lifted verbatim from the rejection's own printed line** exits 0, seeds exactly the remaining N−k+1, acks the already-seeded count, and the final record + task list name all N **once each**; plus a fully-seeded re-run arm (nothing to seed → a true ack, not a collision). Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_rollback.rs` or a sibling suite.)*
- **T4 — the conflict route belongs to the caller, not the classifier.** `conflict_block_finding` stops hard-coding a task idiom the engine cannot know is true: the caller supplies both the *what-moved* statement and the route, over **both** emission seams (the M45 axis rule — the reported seam is the milestone one; the task seam carries the same unsubstituted placeholder and is swept with it). At **task scope** the real task id is substituted, so the emitted route is a followable argv rather than `jigc task discard <task-id>`. At the **milestone-record preflight** — where no task exists and, after T1–T3, the finding can only mean a genuine out-of-band edit to a machine-owned record — the route names an applicable resolution and the message stops claiming *"this task's staged writes"*. Every mechanical span still rides the checked `Route::mechanical` constructor (the route fence). The shipped assertions that pin the old strings (`engine/src/file_state.rs:1332-1337`, and the loose pair at `milestone_record_reconcile.rs:181`/`:222`) are repaired **in the same commit** — the change makes them false the moment it lands. *Done:* a test iterating **both emission seams** through the real binary: the task-scope seam's emitted route argv, lifted from the printed bytes and **run verbatim**, resolves the real task (no `<task-id>` token survives); the milestone-record seam's emitted finding contains **no** `jigc task discard` and **no** unsubstituted `<…>` placeholder, and its message names the record rather than a task; the route fence's parse assertions still pass; the engine unit test asserts the caller-supplied route round-trips. Docs: [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → Conflict — block at file level (the resolution block currently shows only the task idiom; it gains the machine-owned-record seam). Full unscoped gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/file_state.rs`, `crates/engine/src/validate.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_reconcile.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/singleton_running_doc.rs`; docs: `design/reconciliation.md`.)*

*Why this order:* state before speech — T1 stops the bricking, T2 and T3 make the *"fix the hook, re-run, it succeeds"* clause true door by door (T3 needs T2's unwind primitive), and T4 writes the route last, because only after T1–T3 does a milestone-record conflict-block mean what its new message will say. Every *Grouped scope* bullet lands: `reconciliation.md`'s fourth re-baselining row rides **T1**; `add-from-spec`'s mid-loop shape is **exercised over its whole k-axis** in **T3**, not derived; the two route defects ride **T4**. **Declared out, with its reason rather than silently dropped:** the sibling `file-state.hash-matches` *store-scope* route (*"re-author it through the owning workflow"*, inapplicable to a machine-owned record) — the approved scope names only `conflict-block`, and after T1 that finding no longer fires over jigc's own wreckage; it is a tier-2 wording item, not this increment's. The finalize/join record-write seams (the `joined`-blob-staged ff-refusal axis) are **Increment 3 T0(d)** by the roadmap and stay there.

## 2026-08-02 — M47 Inc 1 T2: the halt-condition measurement, re-measured honestly — and the two conversions it licenses

The Settle's `2383/2` was a *prediction* and the cross-model review demanded it be re-measured after `erase_presentation` + the 16 re-pins landed, with **a third failure, or a different pair, a HALT**. Measured: **2391 passed / 2 failed**, and the two are exactly the forecast pair — `manifest.rs`'s `shape_mutated_without_bump_is_hash_mismatch` (the forecast's `:400`, now `:520` because `erase_presentation` is inserted above it) and `freeze_enforcement.rs:232`'s `methodology_schema_shape_drift_without_manifest_bump_is_blocked`. **The forecast held; the narrowing erased nothing the freeze needs.**

*How that number was arrived at, because the first two attempts did not produce it and the difference is the point.* Run at **default test-threads** the suite failed **8 times**, then **17 times**, with the two sets overlapping in exactly the forecast pair and disagreeing on everything else — the [T1 entry's named, unfixed harness defect](#2026-08-02--m47-inc-1-t1-droppability-is-boundary-relative-and-it-is-what-keeps-the-mint-idempotent) (`TempDir::new` builds its name from pid + `SystemTime` nanos, truncated to microseconds on macOS, so two threads in one binary collide and race a `git init` into `File exists`). Each extra failure was reproduced green in isolation and one was caught in the act, `git init` failing to copy `push-to-checkout.sample`. So the measurement was re-run T1's way — **whole, unscoped, `--test-threads=1`** — over the **pre-conversion tree** (the conversions were reverted from saved copies for the run and restored after, so the measured state is the one the halt condition names). A load-dependent harness race is exactly the kind of noise that turns a *specific* fence into an unreadable one, and the honest fix was to remove the noise, not to widen the fence's tolerance.

**Both conflating tests are converted to a real shape drift, and a third site the forecast missed with them.** `shape_mutated_without_bump_is_hash_mismatch` widens an `enum`; `drift_research_schema` drifts `location:` — mirroring its dev sibling `drift_adr_schema`, which drifted `location:` all along and is why the conflation was visible at all. `manifest.rs`'s `first_violation_is_deterministic_in_sorted_doctype_order` drifted `description` and would have stayed **green** (it asserts `ExtraEntry`), silently ceasing to test the tie-break its comment claims — converted here rather than left. Each conversion lands beside its **invariance arm**, so the pair is what proves the discrimination rather than either half alone: `a_prose_reword_passes_the_freeze_check` (the gate returns `Ok` over an unbumped, un-re-pinned manifest) and `a_reworded_methodology_hint_composes_clean_with_no_bump` (through the **real binary**, the mutation `drift_research_schema` used to make now composes clean).

## 2026-08-02 — M47 Inc 1 T1: droppability is boundary-relative, and it is what keeps the mint idempotent

Building the word-aware edge-stopword drop forced one elaboration the Settle did not reach, and it is load-bearing: **an edge token is droppable when the boundary joining it to the rest of the *remaining* slug is not glue — and a lone token is therefore always droppable.** The obvious alternative (a word remembers it was a compound component, on either side, forever) **breaks idempotency at the char cap**: `slugify("on-" + "z"×60)` retreats to the stranded `on`, which a second pass would drop — so `slugify(slugify(x)) != slugify(x)`, the exact property M41's own edge-stopword change was pinned for. Boundary-relative droppability is idempotent *by construction*: a second pass sees only `-` join chars, so nothing at an edge is separator-delimited, and the one case that could escape (a lone stopword) was already dropped on the first pass. Two consequences pinned rather than discovered: a dash **run** is glue only when every char in it is a literal `-` (so `a - b` is separator-delimited), and a stranded lone stopword normalizes to `""` — the total function's sanctioned escape, where the mint site's type-name fallback takes over. The provenance is carried **positionally** on each word (its own left boundary), never as a value-set of "words seen whole", so `"on On-call"` drops the first and keeps the compound's. `renormalize` is byte-unchanged and `tokenize(x).join("-") == renormalize(x)` is pinned deterministically **and** as a proptest, so the mint cannot smuggle a separator-map change past the four recognition sites.

*Also in this commit, and disclosed rather than buried:* **three pre-existing test-harness reds on the rebuild host** ([the machine loss](#2026-08-02--the-machine-loss-and-the-final-trials-analysis-re-run-posthumously-it-counts-as-rc-input)), each red on the clean tree at `9e6cb17` before this task's first line and each blocking the gate. (1) The golden `<REPO>` redaction replaced the *given* tempdir path before its canonical form, so on a host where the canonical form is the given one prefixed with `/private` (macOS `$TMPDIR`) every golden captured `/private<REPO>` — fixed by replacing the **longest form first**. (2) `setup_fails_loudly_when_install_commit_is_rejected` assumed git refuses to commit without a configured identity, but git *derives* one implicitly on this host, so the fence's precondition never arose — fixed with `user.useConfigOnly`, which makes the rejection deterministic everywhere. (3) `enumeration_is_id_sorted_under_divergent_insertion_and_read_dir_orders` demanded that `read_dir` hand back a non-id order in at least one run — unattainable on an order-preserving filesystem, and asserting a property of the *host*; the demand is now conditional and the fixture's non-divergence is asserted to be the host sorting. None of the three touches a production path. **Not fixed, and named:** the ~50 test files' `TempDir::new` builds its name from pid + `SystemTime` nanos, which macOS truncates to microseconds — two threads in one test binary can collide on a directory and race a `git init` into "File exists". It is a real latent harness defect, it is out of this task's scope to sweep 50 files, and the gate was therefore run **whole and unscoped** at `--test-threads=1`.

## 2026-07-26 — M47 Increment 3 halt resolution: the fan-out abort stops destroying sub-agent code (a mid-build re-scope, taken through the planning gates)

The Increment 3 planner **halted on a genuine fork**: the approved *Proves* clause ("every committing door … states what survived … and a re-run after any rejection recovers") is **unattainable** for `jigc milestone finalize` under `finalize.fan-out.squash: false`. Verified live: a hook-rejected chain finalize tears down the fan-out worktrees, destroying every sub-task's staged uncommitted **code**; the re-run then degrades to the never-provisioned docs-only path and lands at **exit 0** with the code silently gone and a manifest saying "2 docs" per sub-task. The `squash: true` sibling recovers correctly from the identical setup. A frame written before the fix would be a **law-1 lie** — it would state "what survived" about a state that did not survive (the same N1→H2 sequencing already recorded at Increment 2).

Resolving it **widens an approved increment**, so per [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Halt and resume it is a **Settle-grade decision made mid-build** and got the planning gates rather than a momentum pass: a **property census** over the four `remove_worktrees` sites, then an **independent `design-reviewer` adversarial pass** over the re-scoped slice. That gate is not ceremony here — M31's only escaped defect entered at exactly this point, on exactly this code path, when a halt resolution swapped squash:false's mechanism with no review.

**What the review changed.** It confirmed Property A sound and, better, **prior art**: `finalize.md`:157 already promises *"working area intact"* on a rejection, and `team-ready-state.md`:93 justifies the force-removal by *"the commit lands **first**"* — a precondition **false** on the abort arm. So the fix *enforces* the design of record. It also refuted two things:

1. **The census was wrong** on the *landed* sites. I had them as safe ("the commit landed, every byte is in git"); the commit takes only the **staged** set, and `git worktree remove --force` then deletes unstaged and untracked work too — confirmed live, **exit 0, unnarrated, on the success path**. The same shape as the halt, one path over, and a "MUST NOT change" would have closed it.
2. **The trigger set is wider than "hook rejected."** `:2063` catches *any* `Err`, including a `git merge --ff-only` refusal over ordinary untracked WIP in the main checkout — **no hook installed at all**. One call site still fixes it, but the acceptance must iterate the cause axis, and the exposure priced at settlement was understated.

**The three calls.** (1) The abort arm stops tearing down, aligned with its squash:true sibling; the acceptance iterates three rejection causes. (2) The settled *"refuse when recorded as provisioned"* is **withdrawn as unbuildable** — no such record exists, and a `.jigc` marker fails open **by construction** on the fresh-clone case it exists to catch (confirmed: fresh clone → exit 0, zero work landed, record flipped to terminal `joined`). Its only durable home is the committed `milestone-record`, a frozen doctype: `schema-version` 2→3 + corpus migration + manifest re-pin, a **one-way door out of charter → M46**. Replaced by two no-new-state fixes: a refusal on the **zero-contribution** shape (`has_diff` resting solely on `record_changed`) and a landing manifest that **names sub-tasks with no provisioned worktree**. (3) The landed-path loss takes the **law-1 minimum** — warn before removing, name what was discarded — with the honest bound written down: *visible, not prevented*; the `discard`-style refusal is new surface → **M46**. Plus the ff-arm's staged `joined` record joins the captured-pre-image discipline as its **fifth axis**, because leaving it would be a live counter-example to Increment 2's own *"no staged residue"* claim.

**Bounds declared rather than fixed:** `provision_worktrees`' `remove_dir_all` on an unregistered leftover (T0 makes "a live worktree holding uncommitted code" normal, widening that path) and `jigc uninstall`'s unconditional `.jigc` wipe (pre-existing, outside M47). **Named rather than discovered:** `jigc milestone discard` now correctly refuses after an aborted finalize — a behaviour change on a second verb, and a safety gain. The shipped test that pins the defect (`milestone.rs:2313-2375`) is **inverted, not extended**, as a **basis-has-changed rebuttal**: its rationale (2026-06-21, M31 Inc 3 T4) wired teardown in when the abort path still `reset --hard`ed the live checkout — *before* Inc 4/5 made the worktrees the sole copy of the code.

## 2026-07-26 — M47 planning: the cross-model review — three blockers, two of them self-contradictions the same-model pass wrote and blessed; one refuted on test

**Why this pass ran, for whoever reads this cold.** `milestone-planning-workflow.md` → Review says a cross-model second opinion is *suggested, never auto-run*, and specifically **whenever the settled artifact is a one-way door** — because that is where a missed defect is expensive to reverse **and** where the same-model reviewer is weakest. The M41 precedent is the reason: there, the same-model pass did not merely miss four stable-key defects, it **ratified the author's own wrong premise**, which the builder then implemented *and confabulated a justification for*. M47's Settle contains four one-way doors at once (an identity-generation split, a freeze-semantics narrowing, a public exit contract, and two `--format json` keys pinned at 1.0), so the human ran it. **Findings were verified against the repo before being accepted — a cross-model pass is a second opinion, not an oracle, and one of its three blockers was half-wrong in a way that mattered.**

**Blocker 1 — the `blocking_probes` grep: premise right, conclusion refuted on test.** The review flagged that `render::json` is `to_string_pretty` (`crates/cli/src/render.rs:57`), so a JSON array renders **multi-line** and a line-oriented POSIX grep cannot bind the key to a member — and concluded this "risks replacing one shape-grep trap with another." The premise holds and the plan was under-specified. The conclusion does **not** hold, and was refuted by running it: after collapsing newlines, `"blocking_probes"\s*:\s*\[[^]]*"doc-code"` is bounded by the array's **own `]`** and therefore **structurally cannot escape into `findings`** — where the pattern it replaces had to reach across nested `{}`. Both negative controls pass: an advisory-only `doc-code` present in `findings` but absent from `blocking_probes` does **not** match, and an empty `blocking_probes` does **not** match. So the shape stands; what changes is that **the hook's match is now specified in the roadmap rather than left to the builder**, and its acceptance carries those two negative controls as arms. *The distinction matters and is worth stating for the next reader: an array of plain strings is a flat, `]`-delimited region; a findings list is a sequence of nested objects. Greppability is a property of the delimiter you can rely on, not of JSON in general.*

**Blocker 2 — increment 1 forbade its own work.** The same paragraph stated that all 16 doctype hashes re-pin **at unchanged `schema-version`s** and, six lines later, adopted the successor rule *"each hashed entry's hash may move only when its co-located version field moves."* Read literally, the rule forbids the re-pin the increment exists to perform. This is a self-contradiction the same-model pass wrote and then reviewed without noticing — exactly the shared-priors failure the cross-model pass exists to catch. **Fixed by scoping the rule forward and declaring the genesis exemption explicitly:** from that commit onward a *schema-shape* change moves a doctype hash only with its `schema-version`, and a *slug-rule* change moves `slug-rule.hash` only with `slug-rule.version`; increment 1 is the **one** declared exemption, because the projection re-pin moves hashes **by construction** (no schema's shape changes — only what the hash is computed *over*) and the slug re-pin already satisfies the rule by moving its co-located version 2→3. Both land in one commit so the exemption is reviewable as a diff rather than asserted.

**Blocker 3 — "validate exits 3 only where finalize already refuses" was false for the consent flag.** `carry_staged` is declared on the `Finalize` variant alone (`crates/cli/src/task.rs:233`); plain finalize blocks only when `!carry_staged` (`:1176`), and the carryover finding's own route tells you to re-run with it (`crates/engine/src/finalize.rs:727`). So after increment 4 a pre-task staged carryover would make `task validate` exit 3 while `task finalize --carry-staged` succeeds — and a driver that always intends to carry gets a **permanently red** preview. The H1 advocate had named this as a wrinkle; the Settle carried it as a footnote and then stated the non-breaking claim **unscoped**, which is how a true caveat becomes a false headline. **Fixed both ways:** the claim is scoped to *default* finalize, and **`--carry-staged` joins `task validate`** as the parity affordance — the third and last deliberate bend of the wave's no-new-surfaces boundary, taken on the wave's own logic that a preview which cannot express the consent the gate accepts is not a preview of that gate.

**Improvement accepted — `2383/2` is a prediction, not a measurement.** The review could verify every *static* count but not a test result, and correctly declined to treat the schema-hash spike's suite total as independently verified. The baseline now says so and **names the re-measurement**: after `erase_presentation` lands, `cargo test --no-fail-fast` must fail **exactly twice**, at `crates/engine/src/manifest.rs:400` and `crates/cli/tests/freeze_enforcement.rs:232` — both of which use a **`hint` reword as their stand-in for a "shape change"**, which is the conflation the narrowing exists to end. **A third failure, or a different pair, is a halt**: it means the projection erased something the freeze needs.

**Clean bills on the two doors that most needed them, and they are load-bearing for the build.** The **slug fix is confined correctly** — recognition is documented as steps 1–5 (`crates/engine/src/slug.rs:156`) while `slugify` composes over `renormalize` for minting (`:203`), so leaving `renormalize` untouched keeps every recognition site byte-stable; the review looked for a path where an already-committed id is **re-derived** rather than recognized and **found none** (`jigc rename` calls `slugify` only for a *new* title). The **owner-artifact cause split is sound** — seven causes, only the final untracked arm consults `tracked` (`crates/engine/src/validate.rs:1927`). And three enumerations the plan rests on were independently re-counted and hold: **612** compose goldens, **342** carrying the validate promise, 6 dev + 10 methodology schema entries, and **44** leaf verbs derived from the real help tree. Per-door error codes were judged defensible **conditional on the producer-set test being generated from the same 9-door axis rather than hand-maintained** — a condition now written into increment 3.

## 2026-07-26 — M47 planning: the pre-decompose review — ten blocking findings, four re-settled, two Settle claims refuted against the code

The independent review over the settled design returned **10 blocking + 10 advisory** findings, and it earned the phase twice over: it **refuted two factual claims the Settle had asserted**, one of which would have shipped an unbuildable mechanism into an increment. All ten blockers are baked back before decomposition; the four that changed a decision went back to the human.

**The two refuted claims.** (1) **Pack precedence was stated backwards** — the Settle said methodology shadows dev; `crates/cli/src/pack.rs:915` says *"dev first = dev-highest"* and `implementation/pinning.md:17` records *"`commit` ships in both packs and **dev wins by precedence**"*. A builder following the Settle would have edited the wrong `commit` schema. (2) **The finding JSON's key order was stated backwards** — the Settle recorded that serde emits `severity` before `probe`, so the drift-hook fix would key on that adjacency. Running the real binary: keys are emitted **alphabetically** (`check, code, key, location, message, probe, route, severity`), so `severity` comes **after** `probe`. The claim came from a gap-detector that had matched a synthetic fixture rather than real output. Decision 7's mechanism was falsified as written.

**The four re-settles (human):**

- **Decision 5 — split `step:finalize` into a solicit half and a commit half**, reversing the "move the writes into finalize" arm. The review found the arm structurally impossible: `migration-finalize.yaml` in **both** packs ends with `{{ include: step:finalize }}` and `project-finalize.yaml` is *only* that include, so all **12** migrate workflows would inherit exactly the doubled solicitation the decision forbade — and the dialect has no conditionals, so no build-time verification can discharge it. This is a re-decision on new facts, not a reversal of judgment: the arm was chosen on a premise about the include graph that was never checked. Two riders: the count is **four** code-less workflows reaching finalize directly plus `project-setup` through `project-finalize`, not five; and methodology's `finalize.yaml` **already** solicits, so its 7 migrate workflows double-solicit at HEAD today — a pre-existing defect the wave now regularizes.
- **Decision 3's rider-6 fence — dropped, and chartered to M46.** *"Any manifest hash change without a `schema-version` bump is a build error"* has **no implementable mechanism**: a pack-load assert can only verify `hash == entry.hash`; it cannot observe that a value *changed* without a recorded prior, and the decision explicitly forecloses snapshots. Worse, the narrowing itself needs **16 bare re-pins at unchanged versions** — the first thing the fence would forbid. It was also the wave's only piece of genuinely new machinery with no field defect behind it. The narrowing ships alone; the unfenceable-freeze problem is recorded with a trigger.
- **Decision 7 — the hook mechanism is re-settled entirely** rather than patched to the corrected key order. Any JSON-shape grep couples a shipped shell script to serde's emission order, and the corrected pattern would still be that coupling with a nicer face. Shape: **`jigc validate --format json` gains a top-level `blocking_probes` array** — one greppable line, no adjacency assumption, and the hook matches on it. An additive envelope key is contract-touching, which puts it in tier 1 under the wave's own razor rather than outside the boundary.
- **Decision 6's release hole — settled as a test iterating the registry against the producer set**, the repo's own idiom (`registry_mirrors_the_declared_members` already hard-fails on a literal-list mismatch). The Settle had named the `debug_assert!`-compiled-out-in-release gap and settled neither arm — a bound-vs-deferral conflation inside a settled decision, called out as such. Growing the registry 2 → ~10 increases the surface an unenforced check governs, and rc.10 ships as a release build for the trial.

**The six baked back without a re-decision:** the fence-vs-slug-re-pin collision is resolved by stating rider 6's successor rule as *each hashed entry's hash may move only when its **co-located** version field moves* (`slug-rule.version` for the rule, `schema-version` per doctype) — which covers both hashed entries and is strictly stronger than the doctype-only reading · `erase_presentation` is pinned as an **erase-list, not a complement**, with an exhaustive `Schema` destructure so a new field breaks the build rather than silently falling out of the hash (the exact failure the decision cited against reusing `schema_diff`) · **P6 route-followability** gains its seam (the finding-serialization seam, not `Route::mechanical`, which never sees the finding), a per-placeholder derivability table, and the correction that **`<task-id>` is not derivable from `key.target`** under any rule — so it needs a different source or leaves the property · **Decision 12's guard is re-scoped to the fence family** (every step carrying a `states-constraints:` code, in both packs) rather than `finalize.yaml` parity alone, because the break the review demonstrated was on the `create.singleton-copy-in` migrate-step fence — a fix that did not sweep its own axis, in the wave after the complete-fix contract · the "named fact" mechanism is pinned as a `constraint-code → required-token(s)` map checked at pack-load, the only shape that stays inside the A-3 presence-never-content bound · and the **baseline is persisted as a committed artifact** ([completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md](completions/artifacts/M47/baseline.md)) after the review found the scratchpad it lived in had been cleaned mid-planning, taking N1–N22, S1–S16 and every enumeration the decisions cite with it.

**Advisories accepted:** H1's blast radius is **342 of 612 goldens** plus four inline suites (unmeasured in the Settle, and the wave's largest) · `task diff`'s `staged_docs[].body` would mint a **second, unversioned managed-doc content-read path** beside the separately-versioned `doc show`, so it carries identity + address and points at `doc show … --task`, not bodies · `findings: []` on `task diff` is structurally always empty (the exit-code table restricts exit 3 to the three gate verbs) and is declared as such · Decision 10's public-surface behaviour change gains the argument its sibling makes (it is *un*-refusing, i.e. driver-compatible in the safe direction) · Decision 13's re-count is recorded in `decisions-pending.md` with a trigger rather than left as prose · and `design/storage.md` gains the generation-3 row with the adopter note, since every rc.9 corpus spans the rule change.

**One claim the review checked and upheld**, worth recording because it was the riskiest: the seven-cause `owned_location_violation` enumeration is exact (`crates/engine/src/validate.rs:1927-1988`), only the last consults `tracked`, and the six staging-independent causes are already pinned as correct under a constant-true predicate by the shipped suite. Decision 1's substance stands; only its named mechanic was imprecise (`plan_owner_artifacts` is a private staging-path collector, not the gate — the gate `owner_artifacts_gate` is already `pub` and already called).

## 2026-07-26 — M47 planning: the Settle — fourteen forks resolved over a baseline that corrected eight charter premises and found twenty-two defects outside the charter

The rc.10 wave's Settle ran over a **verified baseline** (six capability-auditors + four gap-detectors + three independent robust-advocates, all exercising the real binary at `f4a6a2b` / installed rc.9) rather than over the charter's prose. The baseline **corrected eight charter premises** and surfaced **22 defects the charter never had (N1–N22)**, five of them integrity-tier and five sitting directly on the acceptance trial's own probe routes. **Human scope call, up front: take all of it** — no overload valve, the greenfield-path five are in even where they need step content or a behaviour change, tier 2 ships all ~16 declared items, the wave ships **flow 47**, and **the trial is a report, not a second close** (M47 closes once → rc.10 built + installed → the three-probe blind greenfield trial → then the 1.0.0 call or a new milestone).

**The eight corrected premises, in brief.** (1) H1's fork was mis-posed: the proposed "third arm" — advertise the shipped `finalize --dry-run` — is **dead**, because `plan_finalize` is a sequential abort-chain and dry-run halts at `finalize.empty-commit` in the exact state an agent previews from. (2) The promise is on **nine** surfaces, not four; the highest-traffic (`render.rs:266`, the `what's-left:` line on every id-carrying compose) was missing from the list, along with four design docs and VISION. (3) No construction makes the promise literally true, so prose-scoping is forced in every arm. (4) P5-4's "the field-group-absent miss gets the good route" is false — that case *succeeds*; the real split is `--value` vs `--unset` on the identical address. (5) `task diff` falsifies a recorded clean confirmation (`:749`) and is three nonconformances including a lie in its own generated `--help` and a zero-byte both-streams empty state. (6) Tier 3's "non-empty `left_out` is unpinned" is half wrong — the stdout arm is pinned, the **stderr** arm is not. (7) P3-2 narrows: the append prose is byte-verified **accurate**; the defect is the *collision* case. (8) `M45/VERDICT.md:23` says 558 goldens, `pinning.md:17` says ~1500, the tree holds **612**.

**The three one-way doors, each argued at full strength by an independent robust-advocate before the human chose, all resolved robust:**

**Decision 1 — H1: wire the previewable gates onto `jigc task validate`** (the carryover probe + the six staging-independent `owner-artifact` causes), *in addition to* scoping the prose on all nine surfaces. **M45 Decision 6 is engaged on its rationale and preserved, not overturned**: its feasibility half is sound and live-proven (a pre-stage `tracked` check false-positives a state that finalizes at exit 0), but it reaches **one of seven** `owned_location_violation` causes and **zero words** of carryover — the trial's two blocks were causes 4 and 5 (`not-under-home`, `names-no-file`), neither of which consults `tracked`. Cause 7 stays post-stage. The construction is already pinned as correct by the repo's own green tests (`validate.rs:5696`, `:5849` force `tracked = true` and assert each cause fires), and `command-output-contract.md:321` **already** names `task validate` a task-scope gate emitting 3 on blocking findings — so the robust arm needs no contract change while the cheap arm would need a new clause blessing a divergence no record ever decided. The carryover half is an **undecided defect**, not a design property (the trial verification says so verbatim). Two shipped tests flip their validate-side assertion; `plan_owner_artifacts` goes `pub`. Deliberately **out**: `finalize.stage-failed`, hook rejection, `empty-commit`, `nothing-staged`, cause 7 — and `promote-clobber`/`base-mismatch`, previewable but beyond the field-proven need. Also fixed either way: **`--dry-run` is information-free on this axis** — its refusing-state and committing-state JSON forecasts are byte-identical, and it labels entries `carried-over` when `--carry-staged` was never declared.

**Decision 2 — N5: fix the slug rule now, at `SLUG_RULE_VERSION` 3.** The tokenizer splits a hyphenated compound before the edge-stopword drop, so a leading (**and trailing** — a sibling the charter never named) component in `EDGE_STOPWORDS` is dropped: `"On-call handoff artifact"` → `call-handoff-artifact`, `"Telemetry consent opt-in"` → `telemetry-consent-opt`, minted side by side in one human-reviewed file. **Measured blast radius: zero** — no divergent ids across every keeper corpus (project-alpha-4.0's 192 anchors, project-kb), zero fixtures, zero goldens (`mint_statement` states only the caps, which the fix does not touch). The correct identity is **unreachable through every shipped command in every sequence** — `add-item` has no `--slug`, `rename` is doc-level, `retitle-item` freezes the anchor — across 7 doctypes with free-text item titles, plus `milestone create`, which commits a record at the wrong path and then refuses `rename` while the milestone is in flight. `--slug` appears in **zero** composed step text in either pack, so the escape-hatch defence rests on the pull-tier failure five consecutive trials named. Arm 2 (declare it correct) was refused because M42's record explicitly **cut** a stopword widening on the ground that `slugify(valid_slug) != valid_slug` is a cost — blessing it would overrule that rationale — and because M47's tier 2 *publishes* the slug rule, so the wave would author user-facing text it cannot say straight. Post-1.0 the bump is a pack-load hard block at every door, unshippable in a 1.x minor, breaking exactly the third-party packs that conformed. Fix lives in `slugify`, **never** `renormalize`; both manifests re-pin in one commit; the version bump is a *tested* obligation, since the version arm does not force it.

**Decision 3 — narrow `schema_hash` to a presentation projection, and build the fence it enables.** Three keys leave the hash — `Schema.description`, `Schema.usage`, `Slot.hint`; the six semantics keys (`default` · `set` · `inverse` · `inverse-card` · `check` · `title-names-symbol`) **stay in**. The advocate argued *against* the wide `schema_diff::erase_out_of_projection` reuse this planning first proposed: it would stop the hash moving on `default:`/`set:`, which change what the tool writes into new documents. Two functions, two questions — *can a committed doc's bytes violate this?* (migration) vs *is this a declared change to the contract?* (freeze) — so `erase_presentation` is its own function, written as a complement erase, deliberately not a call into `schema_diff` (whose erase set is designed to grow, and would otherwise silently narrow the freeze). **The decisive argument is not cheap typo fixes: while prose is in the hash, the freeze is unfenceable.** Proven live on rc.9 — reword a hint and re-pin at the same `schema-version` → green; then widen the `adr.status` enum, a real structural change, re-pin again at the same version → **also green, `validate` clean exit 0**. Same keystroke, two meanings, guarded only by a comment saying "never to silence this gate" — the pattern this project has paid three times to retire. Implemented and measured: **2383/2**, zero goldens, zero corpus impact, no bumps, no snapshots, no migration; the two failures are tests that use *a hint reword as their stand-in for a shape change* while their sibling eight lines up drifts `location:` — the conflation's own witnesses. The freeze's declared scope is *shape* in three docs, and `document-type-schema.md:195`'s frozen-format enumeration excludes these three keys. **The human also took the fence** (rider 6): with prose out, *any manifest hash change without a `schema-version` bump* becomes a build error — impossible today, because legitimate prose fixes require bare re-pins. `corpus-migration.md:180` is engaged on its rationale, which was **scope, not principle** ("out of scope *here*", M42-local, written as a flag for the next author) — and two facts postdate it: M42 moved the freeze assert into the pack factory (a drifted hint now bricks every verb) and added the exit-flip that makes the bump compulsory for every adopter.

**The remaining eleven forks:**

**4 — N1: captured-pre-image rollback on rejection.** The four milestone record-only doors brick permanently on one rejected commit — every escape blocks, including `discard --force` and a raw `git commit`, and recovery required hand-editing `.jigc/state/file-state.json`. The obvious fix is **foreclosed by `reconciliation.md:51`** ("durable file-state is persisted only by a landed finalize"), which the code honours exactly; the bug is that rule applied to a door its rationale (*read verbs don't write state*) never contemplated. Rollback honours `:51` untouched and joins the confidence-audit's captured-pre-image discipline as a **fifth staged-path family**. It also clears the un-briefed compounding defect: rejected runs leave record `.md` files staged, which then trip the next unrelated task's carryover gate. **Sequencing: N1 precedes H2's frame on 4 of 9 doors** — until the state is fixed, the frame's "what survived" clause would be a bricking notice.

**5 — N6: move the commit-doc writes from `step:implement` into `step:finalize`** (human call, over the smaller `author-commit` arm). Five code-less dev workflows compose a finalize their own gate refuses because the dev pack sites the writes in the *code-writing* step while the methodology pack sites them in finalize. Moving them matches the methodology shape, gives single-solicitation everywhere, and resolves the pre-existing `sub-task` double-instruct. Build-time verifications it forces: the five **migrate** workflows are exempt (their mint pre-fills the commit doc) and must not acquire a doubled solicitation; and **S1 applies** — both `finalize.yaml` files carry it or the fix lands on half the surface. The same step's *"make sure your code edits are staged"* line is a law-1 lie to five code-less workflows and goes with it; `finalize.md:123`'s family obligation is engaged on its rationale (silent partial commits — sound for code-writing workflows, over-covering the code-less family).

**6 — H2: one error code per door** (human call, over a shared door-agnostic code). Reusing `finalize.commit-rejected` on eight non-finalize doors would put a lying code in the log — a law-1 violation on the surface M42 built to stop the log lying. Per-door codes **contradict `ERROR_CODE_REGISTRY`'s recorded "deliberately not a per-verb code mint"**, so that record is revised with its rationale engaged, not silently overridden; `surface-contract.md:76`'s prose mirror grows 2 → ~10 and `registry_mirrors_the_declared_members` hard-fails until it does. Mechanics: `CommitRejected` → `pub(crate)`; `render::commit_rejected` generalized off the task idiom to take a state-truth statement + the door's own argv. The axis is **9 doors + 1 excluded-by-design** and is already enumerated at `hook_output_axis.rs:11-40` for the non-blocking case with a working harness. `corpus_migration.rs:893` **pins the dead end as correct and is rewritten, not extended**. Noted: the registry's membership check is a `debug_assert!`, compiled out in release — and rc.10 ships as a release build for the trial.

**7 — N8: filter the drift hook to blocking severity.** The hook greps for probe identity with no severity filter, so any non-Rust project following `implement-from-spec` as instructed acquires a permanent false "drift detected". M40 already decided `title-names-symbol` is not worth blocking; warning on it at every commit contradicts that. Not one grep clause: POSIX grep is line-oriented, so the fix needs a single-line match, which works only because serde emits `severity` before `probe` — an unfenced shell-to-struct coupling that gets a fence and a mixed-severity acceptance arm.

**8 — P5-4: sweep the axis, not the instance.** 7 cells / 5 codes (2 correct today), plus `retitle-item` as the un-named sibling, plus a new class: `<doctype>` ships **literal and unsubstituted** on four codes and `<address>`/`<task-id>` on three more outside the write family. They pass the route fence only because they are declared `DUMMY_SUBSTITUTIONS` members — **the fence proves parseability, never followability**. New property **P6**: if a placeholder's value is derivable from the finding's own `key.target`, it must be substituted. Record cost accepted: `command-output-contract.md:337` authorizes a *target value* correction, **not** a `code` change (the paragraph exists because M42 caught itself reasoning by analogy there), so an explicit authorization clause lands plus the `validation.md:60` taxonomy revision.

**9 — N3/N4: guard both undeclared-address writes.** N3 (undeclared item field → exit 0 + positive ack → doc dead, only `task discard` recovers) reuses the guard shape already shipping on the `--unset` sibling. N4 goes at the **write callers**, not `slot_span` — whose two consumers include conformance adjudication — and `resolve_leaf` is duplicated in two places, both moving. The exit-0→exit-1 change is a behaviour change on a public surface, which M45 Decision 6 declined in an analogous case; it is taken here because this is a **data-loss class**, which outranks. N3's aftermath also breaks a declared exemption: `conformance.*` is route-exempt because *"the located message is the repair — no CLI verb repairs a hand-broken byte"*, a rationale that assumed out-of-band bytes. N3 makes them arrive through jigc's own write verb at exit 0, producing a **blocking, route-less finding on the tool's own success path**. Guarding the write **restores the exemption's original scope** rather than overturning it. P5-4 · N11 · N3 · N4 are **one axis**.

## 2026-07-24 — M45 Inc 10 T13: compose-altitude render-once blocks dedupe the shared batch caveat

The batch-authoring caveat is authored identically into `author-roadmap`/`-ledger`/`-decisions`; `planning` composes all three, so it repeated verbatim ×3 in one walk (`RC-alpha3/findings-verification.md` §5 — "no dedupe at compose altitude"). A step-altitude delete is **unsafe** — `author-decisions` is also composed alone by `completion`, where the caveat must still show once. So the seam is **compose altitude**: the pack wraps the span in an `<!-- once:<key> -->` / `<!-- /once -->` HTML-comment pair, and `compose_with_store` renders each key on its **first** occurrence within a composition and drops it on later ones (composition-scoped `seen` set). Chose the **render-once fragment** of the planner's two options over a heuristic byte-identical-paragraph collapse: keyed, explicit, no false collapses, and — because HTML comments are inert to emit / placeholder / fill / shadow checks — it touches **only** the compose loop (no validation-path or new-placeholder surface). The per-doctype `jigc doc author <type>` command each step solicits sits **outside** the block and always survives. Elastic tail (Settle Decision 1) — no closure claim rides on it. Design of record: [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) → Render-once blocks.
