## 2026-07-21 — M44 Increment 6 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 6](implementation/roadmap.md) (the `{{schema:<singleton>}}`-derived stated-at fence + the migrate-step copy-in statements, D5) into **2 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `3d818d8` (tree clean; Inc 1–5 landed). Design of record: the Settle's **B2 baking of the D5 fence** ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-07-21 M44 planning: the Settle, item B2 + line 118/139) — the `authors-into:` marker is **dropped** (circular / a drift-prone second copy of the `{{schema}}` fact), so the fence derives its owe-set from the enumerable structural signal the step already renders: **any step whose body references `{{schema:<T>}}` where `T` is a create-or-update singleton must carry the copy-in/append constraint declaration**, presence-only (A-3), the prose statement guide-tier. A **new per-soliciting-step fence shape** (the M43 `assert_stated_at` is existence-per-code over the 4-member `AMBUSH_CLASS_CODES`, `pack.rs:358-419` — it cannot check "the declaration on *each* schema-bearing singleton step"). Over [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md):46-52 (the stated-at fence, per-soliciting-step extension). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 44 Increment 6.

**Verified bases (read at `3d818d8`, each checked against the code, not assumed):**

- **The create-or-update singleton set = schemas with `singleton: true`** (`Schema.singleton: bool`, `schema.rs:99` — the structural signal, available at pack-load): **changelog** (dev) + **decisions-log · deferral-ledger · roadmap · vision** (methodology) = **5**. Copy-in is the create-or-update path and is `schema.singleton`-conditioned at the destination (`state.rs:891-916`), so `singleton: true` is the correct, stable owe-set signal at this HEAD.
- **The steps referencing `{{schema:<singleton>}}` = exactly 5** (grep `{{ schema:`, the placeholder carries interior spaces): dev `pack/steps/author-migration.yaml` (`{{ schema:changelog }}`); methodology `steps/author-migration-{decisions-log,deferral-ledger,roadmap,vision}.yaml`. The other **7** `{{schema:<T>}}`-bearing steps target **non-singletons** (completion-record · idea · research · adr · prd · spec · arch-doc) and are out of the owe-set by construction (adr's exemption is already recorded at Inc 5's basis). **Charter correction:** the charter's "seven migrate author-steps" conflates the **7 methodology `author-migration-*` steps** with the singleton-authoring subset — the verified owe-set is **5, spanning both packs**; the approved Grouped-scope bullet is "both packs' `steps/author-migration-*.yaml`" (no count), so this is a miscount corrected, **not** a scope narrowing.
- **`states-constraints:` front-matter already exists on `StepDef`** (`compose.rs:1776`, serde `rename = "states-constraints"`, default-empty; declared today by `finalize.yaml` / `migration-finalize.yaml` in both packs) — **not** the dropped `authors-into:` marker (which would name the doctype, duplicating `{{schema:<T>}}`). **No validation rejects an unknown code** in `states-constraints:` (only the M43 existence fence consumes it, `pack.rs:398` `declared.extend(...)`), so adding a new copy-in code is a pure YAML addition. The intended declaration mechanism (executor's elaboration pick, within B2): **reuse `states-constraints:` with a new copy-in constraint code** (e.g. `create.singleton-copy-in`), a **code-side const beside the new fence, per-step-checked** — deliberately **not** added to `AMBUSH_CLASS_CODES` (that set is existence-checked; the copy-in code is per-step-checked, a different fence).
- **The copy-in behavior at HEAD is doctype-blind + records `edited-from-base`** (`state.rs:891-916`, landed M43 Inc-7 T1), with the **migration-squatter blank-seed exception** (source-path == the slug's canonical destination → seed blank, `state.rs:902-903`). So the statement's *factual content* (what happens when a singleton already holds committed content) must be **verified against the binary before authoring** (the M42 design-claim discipline) so it does not lie (law 1) — the exact prose is guide-tier, the fence checks only presence.
- **The pack-load fence mold is `assert_stated_at`** (`pack.rs:381`, wired in `make_pack` at `:698-706` after the workflow-front-matter sweep): it iterates `pack.origin_packs(Config, schema-manifest)`, reads each owner's steps via `owner.list/read(Steps)` + `engine::compose::load_step_def`. The D5 fence reuses this shape + reads schemas (`owner.read(Schemas, …)` → parse → `singleton`) and extracts `{{schema:<T>}}` refs from step bodies (the `inner.trim().strip_prefix("schema:")` extraction, `compose.rs:830`). Per-origin isolation suffices (each of the 5 steps references its **own** pack's singleton).
- **The reddening proof mold is `stated_at_fence.rs` / `freeze_enforcement.rs`** — a copied on-disk pack (`JIGC_PACK_DIR`/listed) with one declarer **stripped** exits non-zero at pack-load naming the code; the unmutated copies + embedded base + composed `[dev ▸ methodology]` pair load clean; a manifest-less pack is unchecked (the freeze opt-in precedent). `strip_states_constraints(pack, step)` (`stated_at_fence.rs:97`) is the ready helper.

**Ordered tasks (id · subject · observable done-criterion):**

- **T1 · State the copy-in/append constraint on every create-or-update-singleton migrate author step (both packs) — guide-tier statement + `states-constraints:` declaration.** To each of the **5** verified singleton-referencing migrate author steps (dev `author-migration.yaml`; methodology `author-migration-{decisions-log,deferral-ledger,roadmap,vision}.yaml`) add: **(a)** the guide-tier copy-in/append prose statement, placed **above** the authoring solicit (law 3 — stated where it binds), describing the actual create-or-update/copy-in-then-append semantic **verified against the binary** at this HEAD (law 1 — no false behavior; the changelog step's existing "creates-or-updates … one call, not hundreds" is the partial mold to complete, the other four say only "creates the singleton"); **(b)** the machine-checkable declaration — a `states-constraints:` entry naming the new copy-in constraint code. **No fence yet** (T2), so the shipped packs still load. *Done:* a **named CLI test** enumerating both shipped packs' steps, selecting those whose body carries a `{{schema:<T>}}` ref with `T` a `singleton: true` doctype, asserts **each** declares the copy-in code in `states_constraints`; `make_pack` still succeeds (embedded + composed pair); any composed-output golden the added prose changes is re-pinned **in the same commit** (an intended addition, adjudicated per the M8 golden-widening discipline — not a leak); **full gate green** (`cargo build && cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`). *Landing note:* the enforcing pack-load fence lands in **T2** (this is a staged split across the increment's own two tasks, tracked — not a cross-increment punt). *(files: `crates/cli/pack/steps/author-migration.yaml`, `packs/methodology/steps/author-migration-{decisions-log,deferral-ledger,roadmap,vision}.yaml`, plus any re-pinned composed-output snapshot files.)*

Both open with the `{{ task.intent }}` framing (the precedents do); both author the three slots; neither carries a `locate`/`scope` step (S1). The constraint: **no removed-prose lie survives** (no mention of a foreign source, a transcribe-the-date rule, or a supersedes-from-foreign edge), and the on-create stamp is not suppressed.
- **A new selectable workflow + new step re-pins three enumerating goldens in the same commit:** `crates/cli/tests/snapshots/describe__describe_byte_snapshot_is_necessary_but_insufficient.snap` (lists every workflow *and* step — the new workflow + `author-adr` insert alphabetically) · `embedded_pack_lists_the_mvp_steps` (`pack.rs:1445`, the sorted step-id list — `author-adr` sorts **first**) · the **router catalog** auto-derives from every default-selectable work-workflow (`present-catalog.yaml` `{{ catalog }}`), so the new workflow **joins the catalog** and any catalog-bearing golden (`describe.rs`, `routing_loop.rs`, `e2e_audit.rs`, `catalog_shape_fence.rs`) re-pins. Re-pin, **in the same commit**, the three enumerating goldens (describe byte snapshot · `embedded_pack_lists_the_mvp_steps` · the router-catalog goldens the new default-selectable workflow joins). **No schema/manifest touch** (adr unchanged); **no `migrate.rs` change** (that is T2). *Done:* a **new** compose→author→finalize integration test driving the real binary (over `JIGC_PACK_DIR` = the on-disk `pack/` tree, real `git init` temp repo) — `jigc start --workflow record-decision "<intent>"` composes the workflow; authoring the three adr slots then `jigc task finalize <id>` (**plain finalize, no `--approve`/review-hold**) commits **one** adr to `decisions/` carrying a **fresh on-create date** (today's stamp, not a transcribed one); the composed step text names **no** foreign source; the workflow appears in the router catalog and `jigc describe`; all three enumerating goldens pass. **Full gate green** (`cargo build && cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`). *(files: `crates/cli/pack/workflows/record-decision.yaml`, `crates/cli/pack/steps/author-adr.yaml`, `crates/cli/src/pack.rs` (step-list golden), the describe/catalog snapshot files, a new `crates/cli/tests/*` acceptance suite.)*

## 2026-07-21 — M44 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 3](implementation/roadmap.md) (the workflow preview — `jigc workflow <id> --preview`, fork 3) into **2 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `3acadae` (tree clean; Inc 1–2 landed). Design of record: the Settle's **fork 3 = build the preview** (`compose_core`-minus-mint; the capability half of change 2, so Inc 4's read-rule amendment is not a trap — [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-07-21 M44 planning: the Settle, item 4 + N3) over [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) law 1/law 2 (nothing lies — `--task <your-task-id>` renders as an identity, never a fictional real id, and `.task` stays null; nothing hides — the read surface names what a work-minting workflow will ask before consent) + [introspection.md](design/introspection.md)/[doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) (the read-surface spine — a preview is a read of the compose output without the mint side-effect). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 44 Increment 3.

**Verified bases (read at `3acadae`, each checked against the code, not assumed):**

- **`compose_core`'s mint arm is gated on `should_provision_commit_doc(&def)`** (`start.rs:1057`) and performs exactly two side-effects the preview must branch around: `mint_in_repo` (`start.rs:1061`, opens the `.jigc/tasks/<id>` working area + reads HEAD) and `provision_commit_doc` (`start.rs:1069`, stages the commit-doc skeleton). It then calls `build_context(&minted.id, intent, &def, &RolesRecord::new(), …)` — **empty roles already** (`start.rs:1076`), which is why review N3 holds (*compose consumes only id + intent + empty roles*). `task_id: Option<String>` (`start.rs:1056`) drives both `view.task` and `minted: task_id.is_some()` (`start.rs:1153`).
- **A synthetic slug is panic-safe through `build_context`.** `build_context` (`start.rs:2018`) resolves `{{task.id}}` from `TaskRoot.id` and constructs `Address::parse("commit:<id>")` under `.expect(…)` (`start.rs:2030-2031`). `Address::parse` (`address.rs:174-193`) applies **no character validation** to the slug (`Slug::from(slug.to_string())`; only non-empty is required), so a fixed synthetic constant (e.g. `your-task-id`) parses cleanly — the mint-side slug validation (`mint_in_repo`) is bypassed on the preview arm, but a controlled constant carries no panic risk.
- **Pack steps reference `{{task.id}}`** (e.g. `author-arch-doc.yaml`, `record-changelog.yaml`, `author-change.yaml`, `author-prd.yaml` — and the dev-pack work-workflows' author/commit steps), so the synthetic slug **surfaces in the composed body** wherever `{{task.id}}` resolves — the `<your-task-id>` identity appears both in-body (from compose) and in the render's mint-first banner.
- **`Command::Workflow` currently requires `task: String`** (`cli.rs:104-112`) and dispatches unconditionally to `run_reenter(format, &workflow, &task)` (`cli.rs:348`). Adding `--preview` makes `task` optional + a clap arg-group requiring exactly one of `--task`/`--preview`, which **breaks that dispatch arm** (the `task` binding is now `Option`) — a same-file compile repair in the same commit as the clap change.
- **`render::composed` keys `minted_header` on `Composition::minted`** (`render.rs:188`) and `task_state_lines` on `view.view.task.is_some()` (`render.rs:212`). With the preview's `view.task = None` + `minted = false`, `composed()` emits **neither** header nor the `resume:`/`what's-left:` lines (so it would not lie) — but it also emits **no mint-first banner** (law 3), so a preview-specific render is owed. The pinned JSON arm is `{task, text}` (`render.rs:153`); `task: null` on preview is the honest law-1 projection (no fictional id in the machine contract).
- **The reject-with-route precedent for the `creates-task: false` guard ships** — `compose_named_no_intent_in_repo` (`start.rs:715-719`) rejects a `creates-task: true` workflow with an actionable message; the mirror (reject a `creates-task: false` `<id>` under `--preview`, routing to the plain `jigc start --workflow <id>` read that already exists) is the same discipline. A preview is meaningful only for a work-minting workflow (the deliverable scopes it to `creates-task: true`).

**Ordered tasks (id · subject · observable done-criterion):**

- **T1 · The `compose_core`-minus-mint preview path (`start.rs`).** Add a `pub fn preview_in_repo(start, workflow_id)` (mirroring `compose_named_in_repo`'s cascade setup) that, for a `creates-task: true` `<workflow_id>`, composes its step text **without minting** — reached via a `preview` branch in `compose_core` (thread a `preview: bool` through `compose_core`/`compose_drained`, default `false` on every existing caller so their bytes stay byte-identical): when `preview && should_provision_commit_doc(&def)`, **skip** `mint_in_repo` **and** `provision_commit_doc`, feed `build_context` a **fixed synthetic valid slug** (`your-task-id`) + empty roles + the given intent, and set `task_id = None` (⇒ `view.task = None`, `minted = false`). A `creates-task: false` `<workflow_id>` is **rejected** with a route to `jigc start --workflow <id>` (the sibling reject discipline). No file I/O side-effect. *Done:* a `start.rs` unit test over a `FixturePack` `creates-task: true` workflow asserts (a) `preview_in_repo`/the preview compose writes **no** `.jigc/tasks/*` dir and provisions no commit doc; (b) the returned `Composition` has `view.task == None` and `minted == false`; (c) **byte-identity to a real mint via an independent oracle** — a real mint compose of the *same* workflow over the *same* intent, with the minted id textually substituted by `your-task-id`, equals the preview's `view.text` (the composed body, not the framed render); (d) `preview_in_repo` on a `creates-task: false` workflow returns the routed rejection. **Full gate green** (`cargo build && cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`). *(files: `crates/cli/src/start.rs`.)*

- **T2 · The `--preview` surface + preview render (`cli.rs`, `render.rs`).** Add `--preview` to `Command::Workflow` (make `task: Option<String>`, add a clap arg-group requiring exactly one of `--task`/`--preview`; repair the `Command::Workflow` dispatch arm in the same commit — route `--preview` to a new `run_preview(format, &workflow)` calling `start::preview_in_repo`, keep `--task` → `run_reenter`). Add `render::composed_preview` (sibling of `composed`): agent/human text leads with a **mint-first banner** (law 3 — nothing ambushes: state that no task was minted and name the mint command `jigc start --workflow <id> "<intent>"`, framing `<your-task-id>` in the body as a placeholder for the id a real mint assigns), followed by the composed body (carrying `your-task-id`), gates line, footer; the `--format json` arm stays the pinned `{task: null, text}` projection (law 1). *Done:* a **new** acceptance driving the real binary — `jigc workflow <creates-task:true-id> --preview` exits 0, its agent/human output carries the mint-first banner + names the mint command + shows `your-task-id` as an identity, contains **no** `task minted:` / `resume:` / `what's-left:` lines, and **creates no `.jigc/tasks/*` directory**; `--format json` emits `"task": null` with the composed `text`; `jigc workflow <creates-task:false-id> --preview` exits non-zero with the routed rejection; the pre-existing `jigc workflow <w> --task <id>` re-entry path still composes (exit 0, unchanged). **Full gate green.** *(files: `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`; a new `crates/cli/tests/*` acceptance suite.)*

*Why this cut:* two genuine single-concerns with **no** inseparable break-repair coupling — T1's `preview: bool` thread is inert on every existing caller (`preview = false`), so it breaks no gate-covered test that T2 must fix, and T2's clap/render change stands on the `preview_in_repo` entry T1 ships. Isolating the compose-without-mint path (the increment's only structural risk, roadmap risk-first note) in T1 lets the **byte-identity oracle** live at the compose layer where it is provable (real-mint vs preview, an independent oracle — not A==A, the M14 lesson); T2's acceptance drives the capability **through the shipped verb** (the M38 lesson — never the core fn beneath its gate). Every Grouped-scope bullet maps: `surface-contract.md` law 2 (+ law 1/3) → T1's `view.task = None` honesty + T2's banner/identity render · `introspection.md`/`doc-read-surface.md` read-surface spine → T1's compose-read path + T2's surfacing · `start.rs (compose_core)` → T1 · `cli.rs` + `render.rs` → T2. Nothing punted. **Status: planned; hand to the executor.**

## 2026-07-21 — M44 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 2](implementation/roadmap.md) (the `write.not-present` route enrichment, the 6th fork) into **1 atomic single-concern task**, grounded at HEAD `df8f8e7` (tree clean, Inc 1 landed). Design of record: [validation.md](design/validation.md):60 (split `write.not-present` out of the shape-question route arm) + [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) law 2 (nothing hides — the route names the followable recovery). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 44 Increment 2.

**Verified bases (read at `df8f8e7`, each checked against the code, not assumed):**

- **Agent-facing `write.not-present` originates *only* from `splice_error_finding`** (`write.rs:5906`, `SpliceError::NotPresent`), reached at **four** CLI dispatch sites: set-slot on an item / nested-item (`doc.rs:800`/`808`, inside `apply_slot_target`) and remove-item top-level / nested (`doc.rs:1119`/`1130`, inside `run_remove_item`). **`set-field` does *not* emit it** — `generate_error_finding` (`write.rs`) maps a wrong item id to `write.wrong-shape`, not `not-present`, which is why the settle's site list omits `doc.rs:497/503/511`. The set-slot **section** site (`doc.rs:794`, `set_slot_validated`) *generates* a missing section rather than rejecting, so it surfaces `not-present` only via a defensive should-never-happen internal (`write.rs:5727`); including it in a uniform enrichment is harmless. **[Corrected 2026-08-09 (M47 Increment 6, T1 — `721c933`):** the *"`set-field` does not emit it"* clause was true when read and is false now. The write-verb × miss-shape sweep minted `GenerateError::NotPresent` and flipped **every item-absent arm** to `write.not-present` — `insert_item_field` (×2) · `set_nested_item_field_or_insert` · `retitle_item` · `add_nested_item`'s absent-parent arm — so `set-field` against an item id that was never minted emits `not-present` today, and the reasoning that omitted `doc.rs:497/503/511` from the enrichment site list no longer holds. A genuine shape question (a section miss, a non-repeatable target) still keeps `write.wrong-shape`: the flip is keyed on *the addressed item is absent*, nothing wider.**]**
- **The engine currently groups `not-present` with the three genuine shape-questions** (`write.rs:5071-5077`) → the generic `jigc doc schema <doctype>` route. Splitting `not-present` into its own arm is the deliverable's engine half; the three shape-questions (`write.unknown-field`/`unknown-section`/`wrong-shape`) keep the generic schema-read route.
- **The engine cannot see the failing address** (`write_route(code)` is code-only, `write.rs:5064`). The CLI holds the parsed address at the `block()` seam (`doc.rs:3608`, `subject` = the URI) but **not** the task id — `task.id` is in scope at the verb entry points (`run_set_field:422`, `run_remove_item:1101`, and the set-slot verb) via `ActiveTask::resolve`. The shared `apply_slot_target` (`doc.rs:785`) / `apply_field_target` (`doc.rs:475`) are **also** called by the batch `doc author` path (`apply_leaf`, `doc.rs:1795`) which passes no task id, so threading `task_id` blindly through the shared `apply_*` would mis-serve the batch path — the enrichment seam is an **(I)** pick (below).
- **The recovery target is the *containing* (top-level) section, not the typed address.** The typed address carries the **wrong** item id (that is *why* it is not present), so substituting the finding's own URI — the existing `readdress_to_uri` `<address>` mechanism (`finding.rs:168-201`) — would point at the wrong target. The write path does **not** run `readdress_to_uri` (that mechanism is store/task-sweep/ingest-only), so there is no conflict; the CLI strips the fragment to its **first section hop** → `<type>:<slug>#<section>` (N2-pinned: the top showable section, e.g. `#releases`, **never** an unshowable field-leaf). `doc_head` (`doc.rs:3643`) already splits head from fragment.
- **The `doc show <addr> --task <id>` route shape ships and parses.** The `store.transient-type` precedent (`store.rs:129-140`) constructs `Route::mechanical(["jigc","doc","show", <addr>, "--task", "<task-id>"])` with a concrete address and ships, so concrete section addresses parse the fence (`Cli::try_parse_from`); the fence dummy table already carries `<address>` (`route_fence.rs:26`) and `<task-id>` (`:23`), so an engine defensive-fallback arm using those placeholders passes the fence and **no new placeholder / no `route_fence.rs` change** is needed. The concrete CLI route re-proves via `Route::mechanical`.
- **No golden pins the current `not-present` route text** — the only test referencing the code (`flow20_completion_encode.rs:573`) uses it as a *rejection* signal, not a route assertion. So the engine arm split reddens no route-text golden; the deliverable needs a **new** acceptance.

**Ordered task (id · subject · observable done-criterion):**

- **T1 · Enrich the `write.not-present` route to the followable containing section.** In the engine, split `write.not-present` out of the shape-question arm in `write_route` (`write.rs:5071-5077`) into its own arm carrying a defensive `Route::mechanical(["jigc","doc","show","<address>","--task","<task-id>"], …)` fallback (placeholders already in the fence table). In the CLI, at the write-verb dispatch — where the real `uri` + resolved `task.id` are in scope — **override** a `write.not-present` finding's route to `jigc doc show <type>:<slug>#<section> --task <id>`, where `<section>` is the typed address stripped to its **top-level (first-hop) showable** section (N2: never a field-leaf) and `<id>` is the resolved task id; the three shape-question codes keep the generic `jigc doc schema <doctype>`. **Impl pick at pickup (I):** either thread `task_id` into `block()` (`doc.rs:3608`) and enrich centrally, **or** apply a post-pass helper at the three verb entry points (`run_set_slot`/`run_set_field`/`run_remove_item`, where `task.id` is in scope) — **must not** thread `task_id` through the shared `apply_slot_target`/`apply_field_target` in a way that mis-targets the batch `doc author` path, and **must not** point the route at the typed (wrong-item) address. Update, in the **same commit**, [validation.md](design/validation.md):60 (split `not-present` out of the "shape questions route the mechanical `jigc doc schema <doctype>` read" parenthetical — it now routes the containing-section `doc show`) and [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) law 2 (name the `not-present`→containing-section route as a law-2 "nothing hides" instance). *Done:* a **new** acceptance driving the real binary — on a repeatable doctype (e.g. `changelog#releases`), (a) `jigc doc set-slot <type>:<slug>#<section>/<nonexistent-item>/<leaf> … --task <id>` and (b) `jigc doc remove-item <type>:<slug>#<section>/<nonexistent-item> --task <id>` each return a blocking `write.not-present` whose `route` (asserted via `--format json`) is `jigc doc show <type>:<slug>#<section> --task <resolved-id>`, and **running that emitted `doc show` verbatim resolves and reveals the section's real item ids**; (c) a **nested / field-leaf** not-present strips to the top showable section (route target resolves, is never a field-leaf); (d) `write.unknown-field`/`unknown-section`/`wrong-shape` still route `jigc doc schema <doctype>`. **Full gate green** (`cargo build && cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`). *(files: `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, a new `crates/cli/tests/*` acceptance suite; docs: `design/validation.md`, `design/surface-contract.md`.)*

*Why one task:* the enrichment is one concern (the `not-present` recovery route). The engine arm split, the CLI real-address override, and the two doc updates are one atomic gate-green unit — the engine split alone would leak an un-substituted `<address>` placeholder on the write path (which does not `readdress`), a broken intermediate with no observable done-criterion, and the doc statements would lie if committed before the behavior lands. Every Grouped-scope bullet maps to T1: `validation.md`:60 · `surface-contract.md` law 2 · `crates/engine/src/write.rs` · `crates/cli/src/doc.rs` (the `block()` seam). Nothing punted. **Status: planned; hand to the executor.**

## 2026-07-21 — M44 Increment 1: T1 landed — every migration id carries a blake3(source-path) disambiguator

Built T1 test-first (red: two collide-today paths, the second serial-collided at the mint; green: both migrate distinct). **Impl pick = the `slug_override` bypass** (not hash-first): `migration_task_id_source` renamed to `migration_task_id`, now returns the **final** id `migrate-<doctype>-<slug>-<hash12>` (or `migrate-<doctype>-<hash12>` when the path slugs away), fed **verbatim** as `mint_task`'s `slug_override` — chosen over hash-first because it is robust to doctype word-count (a hash-first id inside `slugify`'s `MAX_WORDS=5` window can be pushed past the cap by a multi-word doctype; the override bypass can't). The slug portion is bounded by `slugify`'s own `MAX_CHARS` cap (NAME_MAX-safe). No `state.rs` change needed (the `slug_override` param already existed). No `slugify`/`SLUG_RULE_VERSION`/manifest touch — the hash is folded *upstream* of `slugify`, so no version bump, no corpus migration. **Test repair (same commit):** the two `start.rs` unit tests rewritten to the new contract + a mint-path collision-freedom test; the ~19 migration-task-id-hard-coding test files repaired — derivation-helper files (`migrate_adr`/`prd`/`spec`/`arch_doc`, `flow27`/`flow28`) mirror the new `migrate-<ty>-<slug>-<hash>` shape, fixed-source-path files carry the deterministic golden id (hash verified end-to-end by the real finalize, so not a masking const). Workflow ids `migrate-<doctype>` untouched (describe snapshot + routing unaffected). Full gate green, 2159 tests / 0 failed.

## 2026-07-21 — M44 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 1](implementation/roadmap.md) (the task-id path-hash derivation, fork 1) into **1 atomic single-concern task**, grounded at HEAD `04d7feb` (tree clean). Design of record: [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Identity / the slug-rule versioning section — the `slugify` one-way door does **not** apply to this `start.rs` fold (the hash is folded *upstream* of `slugify`, so **no `slug-rule-version` bump and no corpus migration**). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 44 Increment 1.

**Verified bases (read at `04d7feb`, each checked against the code, not assumed):**

- **The collision lives in `mint_task`'s re-slugify, not in `migration_task_id_source` itself.** `mint_migration_task` (`start.rs:191-192`) calls `mint_task(…, intent="", type_name=<migration_task_id_source result>, …, slug_override=None)`; `mint_task` with `slug_override=None` (`state.rs:488-490`) runs `mint_id("", type_name)` → `slugify(type_name)` (`state.rs:666-673`), which **caps to `MAX_WORDS=5` / `MAX_CHARS=50`** (`slug.rs:76,86,201-206`). So `migrate-<doctype>-<folded-path-slug>` is slugified **again** and truncated to its first five words: two long source paths sharing the `migrate <doctype> <w1> <w2>` window (the `…/planning-migration-adr.md`-class, the L1 18-burst) collapse to the same id → the collision. The empty-slug fallback (`start.rs:232-233`) already dodges this with a `blake3` prefix; this increment **generalizes that to every migration id**.
- **The `blake3` primitive already exists in-tree** — `engine::file_state::hash_bytes` (used at `start.rs:232`); no new dependency.
- **`mint_task` already carries the bypass** — its `slug_override: Option<&str>` param (`state.rs:486-490`) is used verbatim (no re-slugify), so the `slug_override` impl path needs **no `state.rs` change**; the hash-first path needs none either. `state.rs` is in scope as the caps' home / the site the fix reasons against, and takes a change only if the executor's impl requires one.
- **The fix necessarily breaks the current "id-source is a fixed point of `slugify`" contract**, which two existing unit tests assert verbatim — `migration_task_id_source_is_per_file_and_path_aware` (`start.rs:3330`, incl. the exact `assert_eq!(…"CHANGELOG.md"…, "migrate-changelog-changelog")` at `:3349`) and `migration_task_id_source_disambiguates_paths_that_slug_to_empty` (`start.rs:3362`, incl. the slugify-identity assert at `:3376`). Folding a hash into every id changes these expected strings, so **both unit tests are repaired in the same commit**.
- **Wide but mechanical test blast radius — all forced repairs, one commit.** Every test that hard-codes or reconstructs a migration **task** id breaks when the hash lands: the per-doctype `migration_task` helpers (`migrate_adr.rs:170`, `migrate_prd.rs:163`, `migrate_spec.rs:164`, `migrate_arch_doc.rs:225`) and the hard-coded constants (`migrate-changelog-history` in `flow41_acceptance`/`finalize_manifest`/`invocation_log`/`migration_dateless_date`/`migration_commit_autoprovision`/`migration_finalize_git_add`/`migrate_retire_adopt`/`carryover_gate`/`migrate_rollback`/`migrate_review_gate`; `migrate-changelog-changelog` + `…-docs-changelog-changelog` in `migrate_seam`/`migrate_retire_safety`; `migrate-vision-old-vision` etc. in `migrate_methodology`/`flow41_acceptance`). **Workflow ids `migrate-<doctype>` are untouched** (only the *task* id changes), so the `describe` snapshot and workflow routing are unaffected.

**Ordered task (id · subject · observable done-criterion):**

- **T1 · Fold a `blake3` path-hash disambiguator into every migration task id (generalize the empty-slug fallback).** Rework `migration_task_id_source` (`start.rs:213-236`) so **every** migration task id — not only the empty-slug case — carries a `blake3(repo-relative-source-path)` disambiguator: deterministic (same path → same id, resume holds) and collision-free (distinct paths → distinct ids) **after** `mint_task`'s id derivation. **Impl pick at pickup (B1-baked):** either **hash-first** (`migrate-<type>-<hash>-<slug-words>`, the hash inside the first-`MAX_WORDS` window so it survives `mint_id`'s `slugify`) **or** pass the fully-built id via `mint_task`'s existing `slug_override` bypass (then bound the slug portion for `NAME_MAX` yourself). **Guardrails:** do **not** touch `engine::slug::slugify` / `SLUG_RULE_VERSION` / either manifest's `slug-rule:` block (the fold is upstream of `slugify` — no rule change, no version bump, no corpus migration); keep `migrate-<doctype>` **workflow** ids unchanged; the `task_id` invocation-log field stays **deferred to 1.1** (out of scope). Repair, in the **same commit**, the two `start.rs` unit tests (`:3330`, `:3362`) and every migration-task-id-hard-coding / reconstructing test file listed in the bases. *Done:* a `start.rs` unit test proves two **distinct long-slug** source paths that collide today (construct two paths sharing the first-`MAX_WORDS` slug window — the `…/planning-migration-adr.md`-class) mint **distinct** ids **measured on the id `mint_task` actually creates** (post-derivation), while the **same** path re-derives to the **same** id; `cargo test -p cli --test migrate_adr` green through the real binary (the resume/re-migrate + distinctness suite held); **full gate green** (`cargo build && cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`). *(files: `crates/cli/src/start.rs`, `crates/engine/src/state.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/migrate_adr.rs` + the migration-id test files named in the bases.)*

*Why one task:* the derivation is a single function whose change **breaks** the two `start.rs` unit tests and every migration-task-id-hard-coding test in the same motion — a task containing only the `start.rs` edit can never reach a green full gate, so the edit and its forced test repairs are one atomic gate-green unit (the increment is deliberately one fork / one function). Every Grouped-scope bullet maps: the slug/id derivation basis (storage.md — design ref) · `start.rs` (the fold) · `state.rs` (the caps' home / bypass, touched) · `migrate_adr.rs` (the held resume test) — all in T1. Nothing punted. **Status: planned; hand to the executor.**

## 2026-07-21 — The M44 retrospective fold-back: "generalize without re-deriving the widened domain" is this wave's shape, landed where each altitude meets it (human call)

M44 shipped its claim, but its three late-caught defects share **one shape worth naming — a check/advisory/derivation generalized past its motivating case without re-deriving its response across the widened domain** — and it appeared at two altitudes, so the lessons land at two surfaces (the jigc "meet it where it'll be met" discipline turned on our own harness):

- **Planning altitude (the near-miss, B1).** The task-id path-hash was accepted as *"generalize the empty-slug fallback that already ships — a few lines in one function"*: the capability-auditor confirmed the primitive exists, the robust-advocate built its decisive case on it, the gate-record's `reuse-exercised` cell was filled ✅ — and all of it was **verified at the primitive and wrong at the composition.** The empty-slug fallback survives the id mint's re-slugify *because it drops the slug entirely* (3 words, under the cap); the settled *append-to-the-slug* form reproduced the exact collision the fix targeted, because the 5-word cap truncated the hash away. Only the pre-decompose **design review** caught it — it would otherwise have shipped a "fix" that does not fix its own motivating case. **Fold:** the `reuse-exercised` gate now requires a *"generalize X to all cases"* claim exercised **in the full pipeline the general case traverses**, with the narrow case's load-bearing property named and checked to survive — [milestone-planning-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md) → Detect gaps (the reuse family) + [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → the `reuse-exercised` gate row (M44 added).
- **Build altitude (the two completion-audit findings).** The byte-floor advisory was widened from `--as adr` to *every* doctype but kept its adr-specific route (misdirecting a `--as changelog` migration to author an **ADR** — the surface-contract law-1 lie the wave itself was built to remove); the fidelity guard was widened from "kill `project-alpha-2.0`" to "reject any dotted run preceded by an alphanumeric" and over-rejected the conventional `v1.0.0`. Both widened a check's *trigger* without re-deriving its *response* across the new domain. **Fold:** a new [dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → Why this shape note — *widen a guard's trigger, re-derive its response across the whole new domain, most sharply at its edges.*

Two smaller notes recorded, not folded to a doc: **(1)** the pre-decompose **design review earned its cost decisively** — it caught **two** blocking flaws (B1 + the circular `authors-into:` fence) in the *settled* design that eight prior agents and the human had blessed, exactly the "an increment inherits every flaw in the design it is cut from" the step exists for; the fold-back's value is **shifting those catches left** (B1 to the reuse gate, the audit shape to the build), not adding a step. **(2)** a self-note, owned without a doc change: the orchestrator marked the `authors-into:` marker "recommended" partly to preserve the human's earlier lean, and it was the circular option — when the human asked "what's better long-term?" and it was reasoned fresh, the answer flipped; a "recommended" label must be reasoned fresh on the fork's merits, never anchored on preserving a prior pick. **Deliberately not encoded:** the shape as a lint or gap-count — it is a judgment prompt (tier-3 at best; a fence can't hold "did you re-check the response across the domain"), so it lands as the reuse-gate sharpening + the build-side prompt, not machinery.

- **Fork 4 mis-cited M43 fork 2 and mis-framed the gap.** M43 fork 2 is about *routability* (un-hiding `decided-task` in the router); `decided-task` authors `decisions-log` (methodology singleton), not `adr` (dev-pack) — "extend `decided-task`" would be the **first-ever cross-pack `allows-create`** (unexercised M14 surface, fails methodology-alone at runtime). No `locate`/`scope` step (per the precedents); schema clean (no required refs).
- **S2 (the byte-floor rider) — pinned:** an **advisory** (aligns with Framing-A / no-content-judgment), firing on the migrate source at mint, below a small byte floor, with its own finding-code + route; the from-knowledge adr path (no source) is naturally exempt.
- **S3 (surface-contract.md) — cross-reference, not restate:** `surface-contract.md:8` *disowns* the AGENT.md body (delegates to assistant-adapter.md); the preload tier joins as a law-2 *surface class* pointer only, `:8` softened consciously if needed — the body content stays in assistant-adapter.md (one-file-one-purpose).

## 2026-07-17 — M43 Inc 8 T3: the AGENT.md read rule + per-tier slices scoping — two elaboration pins

**(1) The read rule is its own paragraph, second — right after the prohibition it makes actionable** (sentence → read rule → framing → contract): "never read managed docs directly" begs "which docs, and how then?", so the answer sits adjacent, not buried beneath the what-jigc-is framing; it names only the two stable verbs (`jigc doc list` as the managed-set discriminator, `jigc doc show <doc>` as the read path) plus the stated complement ("everything else — source, tests, any file not in that set — you read freely"), never a location convention or doc enumeration, so the rot-proof rule that admitted the framing admits it too. **(2) The per-tier scoping is a subordinate clause, not a caveat sentence** — the framing now promises "the doc slices that workflow declares (a quick fix may declare none)": the promise's scope rides in the same breath as the promise, so the zero-slice tier reads as designed, not broken, and the framing stays one line.

## 2026-07-17 — M43 Inc 8 T1: `doc schema` contract-version 3 — three elaboration pins

**(1) The address key IS the verb name** (`set-field` / `set-slot` / `add-item`, value = the concrete address) — "the owning verb named" carried by the key itself, no `{verb, address}` object; the key set is decided by the entry's kind, so a driver never branches on a second discriminator. **(2) The settable predicate: a field carries `set-field` iff it has no `set:` deriver and is not its block's `id-from` leaf** — a `set:`-derived field is CLI-stamped (an emitted address would invite fighting the deriver/freeze gate) and an `id-from` leaf's heading IS the value (`retitle-item` / remove+add territory, no single leaf-address verb); absence means *not directly settable*, never an error — the write-time guards carry the routes. Defaulted fields stay settable (adr `status`, the canonical example). Slot sections / item slots / repeatables (nested included) are unconditionally settable via their verb. **(3) Instance parts placeheld uniformly** — `<slug>` for the doc (singletons included: uniformity over a per-doctype bare-address special case), `<id>` for each enclosing item's minted id at that depth; the real values live on the instance reads (`doc list`, `doc show`'s item `id` key), keeping the projection strictly type-level. The plain listing mirrors the same addresses as parentheticals, non-contractually.

**(1) A present-but-unreadable `<task_dir>/source` is a hard error, never a silent `None`** — composing the migration workflow over an empty seam is exactly the defect the re-feed closes (RC-lacon log surprise 1), so the read fails loud instead of degrading into it. **(2) The re-entry path inherits the re-feed by construction** — resume and sub-agent re-entry share `compose_task_workflow`, and re-entry is equality-guarded to the recorded workflow, so the shared seam read is deliberate, not incidental; no migration workflow fans out today, making the inherited arm inert but honest. **(3) The acceptance is byte-strong, not contains-strong** — the resumed view is asserted byte-identical to the minting compose minus its `task minted:` header (both for the migration task and the omitting non-migration context), pinning that the re-feed changes *only* the seam and nothing else on the resume floor. The collision path needed no repair: `task.serial-collision` already surfaces message+route through `render::operational_error` on the migrate error path — the test now proves it end-to-end.

## 2026-07-17 — M43 Inc 6 T3: the clobber route repaired — three elaboration pins

**(1) The discrimination is the recorded source's presence, not a new key** — `clobber_finding` takes `Option<&str>` (the raw recorded `source-path`, trimmed; the normalized form stays comparison-only), and post-T1 the `source == destination` case never constructs a finding, so `Some` means exactly "a migration colliding at a *different* file" — the `(code, target)` key `(finalize.promote-clobber, <destination>)` is one for both arms (`finalize_finding_keys` untouched). **(2) The migration arm's continuation names the two-step verbatim** — plain `jigc task finalize <id>` to review the fidelity diff, then `--approve` to land (also retiring the recorded source) — the `migration_no_replacement_finding` `<id>`-placeholder precedent, no unit threading. **(3) "Never teaches raw removal" is asserted, not just reworded** — both new engine tests assert message+route contain no "remove"/"delete"/"git rm" (the A4/A7 trap was verbatim the old route's "remove or adopt it" pre-staging a silent `git rm`); the repair verbs are jigc-only: retitle / `jigc doc create --slug` / `jigc task discard` + re-mint with `jigc migrate --slug` (T2) / adopt the occupant via `jigc migrate`. Human-kind route (multi-branch judgment prose), so the Mechanical parse fence deliberately does not bind.

One home per pack instead of 12 restated paragraphs (the cross-reference-never-restate convention; Inc 6 revises exactly one file per pack on the same-path change), and the contract sits directly above the solicit it gates (the style guide's constraints-before-the-solicit rule) without leaking onto non-migration finalizes. **(2) The fence names *all* undeclared members in one failure** — one bail listing every missing ambush-class code per constituent, not first-missing-wins, so a from-scratch pack author repairs in one round. **(3) The staging-pair declaration forced the prose honest** — declaring `finalize.nothing-staged`/`finalize.left-out` on a step whose prose stated neither would make the declaration itself a law-1 lie, so both packs' `finalize.yaml` now state the left-out *and* the nothing-staged-refuse halves alongside the new carried-staged sentence (presence-of-obligation is the fence's bound; making the carried obligation true is the author's).

## 2026-07-16 — M43 Inc 4 T4: the catalog-shape asserts — two elaboration pins

**(1) The `when:` cap is `CATALOG_WHEN_MAX_CHARS = 120`** — the settle fixed a *named code-side const*, not its value; 120 leaves authoring headroom over the longest shipped selectable `when:` (104 chars, `architecture-documentation`) without licensing a paragraph (and sits below `increment.yaml`'s 126, which is `creates-task: false` — out of scope, proving the cap would bind if the scope widened). Chars counted via `chars().count()`, never bytes. **(2) Period-less = no *terminating* period** — the assert rejects only a trailing `.` (the mid-sentence-interpolation defect the craft rule names); an interior period (an `e.g.`) is prose semantics, the same barred-census territory as the declined when-NOT assert. Presence + shape are scoped to `creates-task: true && selectable: true` (the router catalog's exact population), so `sub-task`/`router` mutations load clean by test.

## 2026-07-16 — M43 Inc 4 T3: the eager sweep + suppression fence — three elaboration pins

**(1) Sweep scope = manifest-shipping constituents, each in isolation** — the `assert_schema_freeze` opt-in precedent: a pack joins the pack-load fences by shipping `config/schema-manifest.yaml`, so a manifest-less seeded/project-local pack stays on skip-on-absent (never an error) while a mutated filesystem copy of a shipped tree is fully checked. **(2) Memoized by composition shape, not per-owner** — the sweep caches only for the two purely-in-binary pack-sets (`[dev]` / `[dev ▸ methodology]`, immutable in-process; keyed on the compose marker), and recomputes whenever any filesystem pack is in the set (its tree is live-mutable); `anyhow::Error` isn't `Clone`, so the cache carries the rendered message. **(3) All 17 hides declare `expires: never`** — every current hide is permanent by design (12 `migrate-*` verb-routed · `sub-task` spawned-never-picked · `record-change`/`planning`/`completion`/`record-dogfood` deliberate invoked-by-name lifecycle acts), so no fake expiry was manufactured (law 1); the eager sweep also makes a *malformed* front-matter block at pack-load naming the workflow, where it previously surfaced only when that workflow composed.

## 2026-07-16 — M43 Inc 4 T2: the loader fields — two elaboration pins

**(1) `expires` is a verbatim `String`, not an enum** — the YAML surface is exactly the design's `never | <condition>` (both plain scalars), `never` stays machine-visible by comparison, and the required shape extends to **blank** values: a blank `reason:`/`expires:` blocks alongside a missing one (a blank is neither `never` nor a condition), each a dedicated blocking `workflow-refs.suppressed-malformed` finding; a non-map `suppressed:` fails the whole front-matter parse (`malformed-front-matter`) — still blocking, so the unknown-key tolerance can never eat a malformed block in any shape. **(2) Both new fields are serde skip-on-absent and pass through the CLI fill wrapper** — `WorkflowDef.suppressed`/`StepDef.states_constraints` serialize only when present (the loaded-def goldens stay byte-identical), and `start.rs`'s fill-applying `StepSource` forwards `states_constraints` untouched, so a project-shadowed step's declaration survives to any downstream consumer (the T5 factory assert reads shipped-pack bytes, but the loaded value never silently drops).

## 2026-07-16 — M43 Inc 4 T1: the decided-task flip + the decision-axis catalog rewrite — two elaboration pins

**(1) `quick-fix`'s `when:` line ships byte-unchanged** — "apply a small commit-only fix that touches no documented code and records no decision" already names its two discriminating axes (records-a-decision, managed-docs) and is the exemplar [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md)'s craft convention cites; rewriting it would be churn plus an adopter `needs-rebasing` flip bought for nothing. The neighbours rewrote *around* it: `single-task` takes the decision-positive pole ("recording the decisions it makes" — gerund/plural, so step_5's pairwise >4-char non-overlap holds against quick-fix's "records no decision"), `implement-from-spec` becomes situation-first spec-bound ("a committed spec already covers the intent, with acceptance criteria to build against" — the spec-router-matching catalog-axis rider: the line now names the routing trigger both trials missed), and the methodology pair splits on the same axis (`dev-task` "recording no decision" / `decided-task` "recording the design decision it makes"). **(2) The knobs guard keeps its decided-task negative with a revised rationale** — `default-workflow.of` is the knob's valid-values list, not a selectable mirror (verified: dev's enum omits `architecture-documentation`), so the enum stays the single-entry `[dev-task]` byte-unchanged and only the guard's rationale clauses moved off the retired "off-router" framing.

## 2026-07-16 — M43 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 4](implementation/roadmap.md) (the pack-load fences + the catalog truth pass — fork 2, 3's stated-at half, 6) into **6 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `9fcef19` (tree clean; Inc 1–3 landed, so `finalize.carried-staged` exists and the migrate templates already ride the `{{schema:}}` projection). The design of record is [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → The suppression / catalog-shape / stated-at fences; the gate-record row 4/5 pins bind (eager sweep in the factory · required-shaped fence fields against the loader's tolerance · when-NOT declined · ambush-set as a code-side const · the flip's test pins redden deliberately).

**Verified bases (read at `9fcef19`, each checked against the tree, not assumed):**

- **The census is 32 workflows / 18 hides, not the roadmap's 33/16.** Both shipped packs carry **32** workflow files (16+16); **18** are `selectable: false` today (dev 7: the 5 `migrate-*` + `record-change` + `sub-task`; methodology 11: the 7 `migrate-*` + `planning` + `completion` + `record-dogfood` + `decided-task`) — so after the decided-task flip, **17 permanent hides** need `suppressed:` reasons. The fence rule is "every `selectable: false`", so the counts are incidental; recorded here so the executor trusts the tree, not the stale census.
- **The sweep's pack discriminator is the freeze-assert's opt-in.** The fences must be release-real *and* provable by mutated-filesystem-pack arms (`freeze_enforcement.rs` copies the shipped trees via `JIGC_PACK_DIR`), while project layers stay outside. Keying the sweep on **manifest-shipping constituents, each checked in isolation** (`assert_schema_freeze`'s existing per-owner rule, `pack.rs:226`) satisfies both: shipped packs + their faithful test copies are swept (they ship `schema-manifest.yaml`; fixture packs that ship manifests are **full copies** of the shipped trees — `corpus_migration_backstop.rs:87` `copy_tree` — so they conform once the shipped front-matters do), and handcrafted manifest-less fixture/vendor packs skip, exactly the declared bound.
- **The ambush-class staging pair is `finalize.left-out` + `finalize.nothing-staged`** (the M42 sentence's advisory + the index-empty block, `task.rs:2080`); `finalize.promote-clobber` lives in engine `finalize.rs`, `finalize.carried-staged` landed at Inc 2. **No shipped step states the `--approve`/clobber/retire contract today** (zero `approve` mentions across both packs' steps — it is a live ambush), and Inc 2 landed the carryover refuse with **zero pack prose** — so the stated-at fence cannot land without new statements in the same motion (the every-member-has-a-declarer assert would fail the gate otherwise); Inc 6 then *revises* the `--approve` prose on the same-path behavior change (its named landing: roadmap Inc 6 "stated in the migrate steps").
- **Both packs' `finalize.yaml` already carry the M42 staging sentence** (the natural declarer home for the pair), and **all 32 workflows already author `description:`/`usage:`**; only four non-selectable ones (`sub-task`, `planning`, `completion`, `record-dogfood`) lack `when:` — legal, the presence assert scopes to selectable work-workflows (`creates_task && selectable`), honoring introspection.md:84 via the factory scoping. Longest shipped **selectable** `when:` is 104 chars (`architecture-documentation`; `increment.yaml`'s 126 is `creates-task: false` — out of scope), so a shape cap has room.
- **The flip's test pins are located.** `methodology_increment_off_router.rs`: the catalog/JSON test's three decided-task negatives + the exact `[dev-task, do-research, form-vision, park-idea]` pin redden; the knobs-enum guard's **assert stays green** (`default-workflow.of` is a valid-values list, not a selectable mirror — dev's own enum omits `architecture-documentation` — so no `knobs.yaml` edit; only its decided-task rationale clauses revise). `routing_loop.rs` step_5 pins the dev catalog's **pairwise non-overlap on >4-char content words** — a hard constraint on the axis rewrite (~33 further test sites grep when-fragments; repairs ride the rewrite).
- **Front-matter is tolerant of unknown keys** (`WorkflowFrontMatter`, `compose.rs:117`, no `deny_unknown_fields`) — verified, so the fence fields must be **required-shaped when present** (a malformed `suppressed:` block fails the load, never silently ignores), and the presence check lives in the factory sweep, keeping project shadows on skip-on-absent.

Ordered tasks (id · subject · observable done-criterion):
- **T1 · `decided-task` flips `selectable: true` + the decision-axis catalog rewrite (fork 2 + the spec-router rider).** Flip the front-matter; rewrite the selectable catalog's `when:` one-liners on the decision axes (records-a-decision / test-first / managed-docs / **spec-bound** on `implement-from-spec`) so `decided-task` discriminates against `dev-task`/`single-task`/`quick-fix`; the reddened pins rewritten to assert the new truth (decided-task IS in the methodology catalog; the knobs guard's rationale clauses updated, its assert unchanged). No dev-task fold (the dialect invariant); no `default-workflow.of` change (verified base). *Done:* the rewritten off-router test passes with `decided-task` in both the text catalog and the JSON `workflows` set; `routing_loop` step_5's exact-ids + non-overlap stays green over the rewritten lines; full gate green. *(files: `packs/methodology/workflows/{decided-task,dev-task}.yaml`, `crates/cli/pack/workflows/{single-task,quick-fix,implement-from-spec}.yaml` + neighbours the axes touch, `crates/cli/tests/{methodology_increment_off_router.rs,routing_loop.rs}` + the when-fragment pin sites.)*
- **T2 · The loader fields: `suppressed:` on workflows, `states-constraints:` on steps.** Engine `compose.rs`: `WorkflowFrontMatter`/`WorkflowDef` gain `suppressed: Option<{reason, expires: never|<condition>}>` — **required-shaped when present** (missing/empty `reason` or missing `expires` ⇒ blocking load finding); `StepFrontMatter`/`StepDef` gain `states-constraints: [<finding-code>, …]`, default empty. Workflow-level unknown-key tolerance deliberately unchanged; doc field-list revision is Inc 9's ledger. *Done:* engine unit tests — a well-formed block round-trips onto the def (`never` and a condition string both legal); a malformed block blocks; `states-constraints` parses and defaults empty; full gate green.
- **T3 · The eager memoized sweep in `make_pack` + the suppression fence + the 17 honest reasons.** `pack.rs`: an eager workflow-front-matter sweep beside `assert_schema_freeze`, over **manifest-shipping constituents in isolation** (the verified discriminator), **memoized for the embedded trees** (immutable in-process; 38 `make_pack` call sites); fence: `selectable: false` ⇒ `suppressed` present, else a pack-load error naming the workflow. All 17 permanent hides gain honest `suppressed:` blocks — `expires: never` for permanent-by-design (`sub-task` spawned-never-picked; the 12 `migrate-*` verb-routed), honest reasons for `record-change`/`planning`/`completion`/`record-dogfood` (never a fake expiry — law 1). *Done:* freeze-pattern real-binary arms — a shipped-tree copy with one hide's `suppressed:` stripped exits non-zero naming it; the unmutated copy, the embedded/composed loads, and a manifest-less pack all stay clean; full gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/pack.rs`, the 17 hidden workflow yamls.)*
- **T4 · The catalog-shape asserts: `when:`/`description:`/`usage:` presence + the `when:` mechanical shape.** The T3 sweep gains, per swept pack, for every selectable work-workflow: the three fields present + non-empty, and `when:` mechanically shaped — one line, period-less, length ≤ a named code-side const (room verified: 104-char max today). The when-NOT assert is **not built** (declined, settle 7 — the discipline lives on `usage:` via the review checklist); the lazy `start.rs:1534` catalog assert stays (the factory now fires first). *Done:* mutated-pack arms — a dropped `usage:`, and a multi-line / period-terminated / over-cap `when:`, each exit non-zero; shipped packs pass; full gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/pack.rs`.)*
- **T5 · The stated-at fence: the ambush-class const + the every-member-has-a-declarer assert + the four statements landing.** The code-side const beside the assert: `finalize.promote-clobber` · `finalize.left-out` · `finalize.nothing-staged` · `finalize.carried-staged` (verified members); assert per swept pack: every member appears in ≥1 of that pack's steps' `states-constraints` (each shipped pack loaded alone — the dogfood path — still carries every declarer). Declarations + prose in the same motion (verified base — the assert cannot go green otherwise): both packs' `finalize.yaml` declare the staging pair (the M42 sentence already there) **and** gain + declare the new carried-staged contract sentence; the `--approve`/clobber/retire contract is **stated for the first time** (today's truth) in each pack's migration-finalize-soliciting step(s) and declared — Inc 6 revises that prose on the same-path change. Honest bound: presence-of-obligation, never prose quality. *Done:* a mutated-pack arm stripping one declarer exits non-zero naming the undeclared code; both shipped packs pass; full gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/pack.rs`, `crates/cli/pack/steps/`, `packs/methodology/steps/`.)*
- **T6 · `describe` projects the suppression reason.** The describe entry for a hidden workflow carries the reason (describe already narrates the unfiltered set, `describe.rs:53` — the weave gains the hidden-plus-why clause, style-guide wording), so `describe` and the orient catalog stop contradicting each other; the introspection.md row is Inc 9's ledger. *Done:* a named test — describe over a pack with a hidden workflow prints its `suppressed` reason; the shipped hidden set narrates its reasons; full gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/describe.rs` + `crates/engine/src/introspect.rs` if the projection threads through it.)*

*Why this cut:* T1 first so the suppression census is honest — fence-first would force a `suppressed:` block onto `decided-task` whose expiry already fired, a law-1 violation minted by the fence's own increment; T2 is the pure-additive loader substrate ("the loader field lands first", settle 6); T3 builds the sweep once and lands fence+data atomically (a fence without the 17 reasons can never reach a green gate); T4/T5 are separable asserts riding the same sweep, each atomic with its own data motion (T5's statements are its assert's forced repairs); T6 is the additive projection. Every deliverable clause maps: eager memoized sweep (T3) · `suppressed` required-shaped + 17 honest reasons (T2+T3) · presence/shape asserts, when-NOT declined (T4) · `states-constraints` + ambush const + declarer assert (T2+T5) · the flip + reddened pins + decision-axis one-liners + spec-bound rider (T1) · describe reason projection (T6). Nothing punted; the roadmap's 33/16 counts corrected to the verified 32/17 (rule unchanged). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 43 Increment 4. **Status: planned; hand to the executor.**

## 2026-07-16 — M43 Inc 3 T1: the `{{schema:}}` projection — three elaboration pins

**(1) The skeleton's inclusion rule is one expression on the shared predicate:** a field joins the payload skeleton iff `is_author_required(field) || field.optional` — exactly the leaves whose value only the author can supply. CLI-stamped (`default:`/`set:`) fields, optional refs, and pack-typed fields stay **tree-only** (their stamping/adjudication named there); a migration's deliberate default-override (transcribe the foreign status/date) is judgment prose the T4/T5 templates keep hand-written, not skeleton structure. A repeatable's id-source field is authored as the item's `title:` payload key, never a `set:` entry — and an **enum** id-source offers its members in the `title:` placeholder (the changelog category rule, generated). **(2) The projection embeds the full `jigc doc author <ty> --from-file - [--task <id>] <<'EOF' … EOF` block**, the task id read from the compose context — copy-runnable, and the heredoc markers give the extraction seam the grammar-cannot-lie proof runs verbatim through `sh` (`crates/cli/tests/schema_projection.rs`). A singleton's `title:` renders its **known fixed value** (`display-title:` else the type id), never a fill-me. **(3) Both `compose_core` arms feed the schema map** (the `creates-task: false` arm too): the blocking-when-absent stance means an unfed arm would brick any future `{{schema:}}` in a no-task workflow — feeding everywhere is what makes absence always mean *dangling*, never *unfed-by-the-caller*.

Cut [Increment 3](implementation/roadmap.md) (`{{schema:<doctype>}}` — the law-1 generation seam, engine + CLI + packs) into **5 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `f25f916` (tree clean; Inc 1's checked `Route` + blocking-floor and Inc 2's carryover gate landed). The design of record is [surface-contract.md](design/surface-contract.md) → The schema projection + The stated-at fence; the Settle #2 and fork-6 records bind (generation, not a drift assert; seam-generated constraint text where a code-owned constant exists).

**Verified bases (read at `f25f916`, each checked against the code, not assumed):**

- **`ComposeContext` is constructed at exactly two production sites, both in `start.rs`** — the `creates-task: false` arm (`start.rs:1065`) and `build_context` (`start.rs:1971`, shared by mint + resume); `jigc migrate` and `milestone execute` funnel through them, so "every compose site" is these two. All three callers that will feed the new field (`start.rs:787/1023/1780`) **already hold `defs.all_schemas(pack)`** — the composed cascade's full doctype set keyed by **type id** (`schema.ty`), loaded per-origin-pack and post-`apply_docs_root` (`start.rs:2819-2847`) — so the projection renders **resolved** homes (repo-real under a set `docs-root`) by construction. The renderer must handle the **placement branch** (`location: None`, literal `placement.file` — the CLAUDE.md schema-location gotcha; methodology migrate targets include placement doctypes). Keying is `schema.ty`, **never** the `committed_store` location-stem keying (`store.specs` ≠ `schema:spec` — two different, deliberate keyings).
- **The `{{source}}` mold covers feed mechanics only — the unfedness stance is the opposite.** `{{source}}` unfed emits empty-not-finding (`compose.rs:561-563`); an unfed/dangling `{{schema:}}` **blocks** (`surface-contract.md:36` — "never silently empty, which would be a new lie"). And Inc 1's floor is live (`2e8bdb3`): a blocking finding without a route trips the finding-key seam assert — the new finding must construct a checked `Route` from day one.
- **The store sweep needs no new plumbing to reach the doctype set.** `workflow_refs_store` (`compose.rs:2268`) has one production caller — `validate_store_families` (`validate.rs:433`) — which **already receives** `schemas: &BTreeMap<String, Schema>`, the composed cascade's full set. The new check resolves against that composed set (a methodology step legitimately solicits a dev doctype), **not** per-origin-pack like the command-ref membership path — the design pin, and the one place the two checks deliberately differ.
- **`is_author_required` (`validate.rs:2285`, pub) is the single requiredness authority** — the same predicate the `doc schema` contract (`doc.rs:2174`) and the create skeleton already share (M40 Settle #4). The renderer reuses it; a second predicate would be the drift this increment exists to kill.

The seam-generated statements must be built from these same symbols, so drift has no representation.
- **The generated skeleton's target grammar is the `doc author --from-file -` payload** (sections list, `set:` maps, `items:` for repeatables, **`<<…>>` literal wrapping on slot prose, fold-safe block scalars** — the M41 V1 lesson). The proof that the skeleton cannot lie about the grammar is authoring through it: a filled generated skeleton must be accepted by the real binary.

Ordered tasks (id · subject · observable done-criterion):
- **T1 · The `{{schema:<doctype>}}` placeholder + projection renderer + the CLI schema feed (compose scope).** Engine: `ComposeContext` gains `schemas: BTreeMap<String, Schema>` (keyed by type id; existing struct-literal sites repaired in the same motion); a lone-line `{{schema:<doctype>}}` emit class in `compose.rs` rendering the **section/field/enum tree + author-payload skeleton** via a net-new engine renderer driven by `engine::validate::is_author_required` (enum `of` members rendered; optional/author-required vs CLI-stamped marked; nested repeatables recursed; located homes rendered resolved, placement homes at their literal file). A doctype **absent from the fed map blocks**: `workflow-refs.schema-ref-resolves`, blocking, routed through the checked constructors (the Inc-1 floor). Inline `{{schema:…}}` in prose stays inert (the inline-scan skip discipline). CLI: the two `start.rs` sites feed the already-loaded `all_schemas` map. Docs same motion: the `{{schema:}}` grammar row joins [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md)'s placeholder table (CLI-filled read path, lone-line, blocking-when-dangling). *Done:* engine unit tests — a fixture schema (enum field, optional slot, defaulted/`set:` fields, nested repeatable; one located + one placement fixture) renders the pinned projection golden; `{{schema:ghost}}` → one blocking `workflow-refs.schema-ref-resolves` **with a route** (red today: no such class exists); a CLI integration test composes a fixture workflow carrying `{{schema:adr}}` through the real compose path and the emitted text names all five adr sections incl. `options` at the **resolved** decisions path; a filled generated skeleton is **accepted by `jigc doc author`** through the binary (the grammar-cannot-lie proof); full gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{data_value.rs,compose.rs}`, `crates/cli/src/start.rs`, `design/workflow-dialect.md`.)*

The check id joins [validation.md](design/validation.md)'s inventory (intrinsic-floor, blocking, un-tunable — the workflow-refs count comments updated) **and** both packs' `knobs.yaml` as `validation.workflow-refs.schema-ref-resolves.severity` (`default: blocking, floor: blocking` — the command-ref-resolves row mold), the same motion per the design pin. *Done:* engine tests — a `StoreWorkflow` body with `{{schema:ghost}}` yields the finding; `{{schema:adr}}` in a workflow whose **origin pack does not ship `adr`** resolves clean against the composed set (the not-per-origin pin proven, the deliberate divergence from the command-ref path); both knobs files load under the closed-key-set tests; full gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{compose.rs,validate.rs}`, `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml`, `packs/methodology/config/knobs.yaml`, `design/validation.md`.)*
- **T3 · The heading-depth-ceiling + slug word-cap statements render seam-generated.** A pub statement source co-located with each enforcing constant — the slug rule's statement built from `slug::MAX_WORDS`/`MAX_CHARS` in `slug.rs`, the ceiling's statement co-located with `slot_ceiling_finding` in `write.rs` — and the projection renderer emits them at the soliciting points: the slug statement at the id-source (`title`) line, the ceiling statement with the slot-prose skeleton (law 3: stated where they bind, before they can fail). T1's renderer goldens repaired in the same motion. *Done:* unit tests assert the rendered projection embeds statements **built from the same constant symbols** (string equality against `format!` over `MAX_WORDS`/`MAX_CHARS` and the ceiling rule — shared source, drift unrepresentable); the goldens carry both statements; full gate green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{slug.rs,write.rs,compose.rs}`.)*

Every test pinning the old template bytes is this change's forced repair, same motion (`migrate_adr.rs`, `migrate_arch_doc.rs`, `migrate_workflow.rs`, `spec_loop_prompts.rs`, `migration_slot_fidelity.rs`, flow suites as they grep template prose). *Done:* real-binary integration — a `jigc migrate` compose over a foreign ADR emits the generated projection naming **all five** adr sections incl. `options` and the resolved decisions path (the understatement is now unrepresentable); the spec compose names `derived-from`; the store sweep over the shipped pack stays clean (every new `{{schema:}}` ref resolves); full gate green. *(files: `crates/cli/pack/steps/author-migration*.yaml` + the repaired suites.)*

*Why this cut:* T1 is the atomic seam (placeholder + renderer + feed + the compose-scope block are one motion — a required `ComposeContext` field cannot compile unfed, and an unrouted blocking finding cannot pass the Inc-1 seam assert); T2 is the separable store-scope half with its same-motion inventory/knobs rows (the design's "same increment" pin); T3 lands before the templates so the projection's bytes settle once (statements ride every later golden instead of churning them); T4/T5 split the 12 rewrites on the pack seam — each pack's templates + forced test repairs are gate-green alone, and each proves its own end through the real binary.
