- **T1 · The slug rule gets a declared version + a pack-load fingerprint assert — the fence, built before the change (engine/CLI/pack/docs).** Add `slug::SLUG_RULE_VERSION` (= **1**, the shipped generation) + `slug::rule_fingerprint()` — a `blake3` over the outputs of `slugify` on a **decision-surface-exhaustive** input vector: every printable ASCII char alone *and* framed (`a<c>b`), every `transliterate` table char in both frames, every `EDGE_STOPWORD` at leading/medial/trailing position, and inputs crossing both `MAX_WORDS` and `MAX_CHARS`. **The vector is generated, not hand-picked** — the 2026-07-14 rule binds here: a census keyed on the symptom misses every sibling, so key it on the decision surface (a hand-picked table would wave through a future `+`→`-` mapping). Declare `slug-rule: { version, hash }` in **both** packs' `config/schema-manifest.yaml` (an optional `#[serde(default)]` block on `engine::manifest::Manifest`; ~~**absent = unchecked**, the existing manifest-less posture~~ — **reversed at the completion audit: an absent block blocks**) and compare **both** fields in `engine::manifest::check` — the version too, so re-pinning the hash alone cannot silence the gate. **Extend** `golden_table` over the changed characters (`auth/session` · `1.0` · `10` · `v1.2.3` · `a/b.c`), pinning **today's broken outputs** (`"authsession"`, `"10"`, `"10"`) so T3's fix reads as a reviewable diff — it needs extending, not re-pinning. Fold back `structural-grammar.md:127`'s now-false *"no version-gate rides on it"* clause (cross-ref `storage.md` → the slug rule as a versioned rule). *Done:* `cargo test -p engine manifest` — new arms: a manifest whose `slug-rule.hash` differs from `rule_fingerprint()` → a loud `ManifestError` naming the recomputed hash and routing to *bump `slug-rule-version` + re-pin*; a manifest whose `version` differs from `SLUG_RULE_VERSION` → the same block (the anti-silencing arm); ~~an absent block → `Ok`~~ (**reversed at the completion audit: an absent block blocks**). **And** `cargo test -p cli --test freeze_enforcement` — a new arm over the file's existing helpers (`dev_pack_copy` · `list_pack` · `run_listed` · `init_repo`): a **listed filesystem** pack whose manifest declares a wrong `slug-rule.hash` makes **every** door exit non-zero naming the slug-rule mismatch (`validate` · `describe` · `doc schema adr` · `migrate-corpus` · bare `start`), while an unmutated copy runs clean. Golden snapshot shows the three broken outputs. Full four-command gate. *Red today:* no such key, no such assert — a drifted rule is accepted in silence by all five "fences." *(files: `crates/engine/src/{slug.rs,manifest.rs}`, `crates/cli/pack/config/schema-manifest.yaml`, `packs/methodology/config/schema-manifest.yaml`, `crates/cli/tests/freeze_enforcement.rs`, `design/structural-grammar.md`.)*

- **T2 · The four renormalization sites stop calling the *mint* rule — and the shadow map dies by use (engine/CLI).** Extract `slug::renormalize` (steps 1–5 — the **one** separator map); `slugify` composes over it; the four **recognition** sites switch to it: `parse.rs:426` `heading_matches` · `write.rs:3281` `present_body_sections` · `validate.rs:1880` (the positional compare only) · `migrate_corpus.rs:859` `has_section_heading`. Delete the test-only `slugify_uncapped` shadow (`slug.rs:477-491`) — `cap_truncates_at_word_boundary`'s oracle becomes the production function. **The mint sites keep `slugify` and are not to be swept**: `write.rs:{1818,2640,2831}` (id/anchor mints), `validate.rs:2099` (the `id-from` **enum**-member check — a *mint*-consistency check), `validate.rs:1900` (the surplus finding's **target address** — swapping it would move an Inc-9 stable finding key), `cli/author.rs:302` (`item_hops`, mint-consistent by contract), `state.rs`/`milestone.rs` mints. *Done:* `cargo test -p engine` green with a new deterministic arm — a fixture schema with section id **`in-scope`** renders and re-parses **clean** (red today: a blocking `conformance.section-renamed`, `slugify("In Scope") == "scope"`), plus a predicate arm asserting `renormalize(heading_text(id)) == id` for **every section id shipped by both packs** (the real population, not a sample) and a proptest over `is_slug` inputs; T1's fingerprint assert **still green** (the extraction changed no minted byte — that is what T1 is for); full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{slug.rs,parse.rs,write.rs,validate.rs}`, `crates/cli/src/migrate_corpus.rs`.)*

- **T3 · The rule forks: `/` and `.` map to `-`, at slug-rule-version 2 (engine/pack/test/docs).** The one-line map change in `renormalize`; bump `SLUG_RULE_VERSION` → **2** and re-pin `slug-rule.{version,hash}` in **both** manifests (the fence fires without this, at every door — that *is* the proof); the golden census diff flips (`auth/session` → `auth-session`, `1.0` → `1-0` ≠ `10`); repair the four hardcoded version-derived ids (`doc_show_nested` · `flow24_changelog` ×2 · `flow26_marquee` — `cut-100` → `cut-1-0-0`). Record the **permanent two-id-generation split** in `DECISIONS.md`: ids minted under generation 1 keep their bytes (frozen anchors, frozen paths), ids minted after follow generation 2, **no migration exists or can exist** (no transform kind re-mints an id) — and note the two bounds honestly: `--slug` is the escape hatch on `start`/`rename`, the changelog release anchor has none; and a pack shipping a **non-slug** section id still round-trips by luck (schema ids are not `is_slug`-validated at load — pre-existing, unchanged, out of scope). Fold the shipped generation into `storage.md` → the slug rule as a versioned rule. **No corpus-side gate**: nothing stamps a doc with the generation that minted it, and none is to be invented here. *Done:* `cargo test -p engine slug` — `slugify("auth/session") == "auth-session"`, `slugify("1.0") != slugify("10")`, the golden snapshot carries the flipped outputs; `cargo test -p cli --no-fail-fast` fully green (the four id repairs land in this commit — they cannot land before it); the pack-load assert green **only** because both manifests declare version 2 + the recomputed hash. Full four-command gate. *Depends on T1 (no fence to fire) and T2 (the recognition path must be off the mint rule before the mint rule forks).* *(files: `crates/engine/src/slug.rs`, both `config/schema-manifest.yaml`, `crates/cli/tests/{doc_show_nested,flow24_changelog,flow26_marquee}.rs`, `design/storage.md`, `DECISIONS.md`.)*

*Why this cut:* three concerns, each gate-green alone, in the only order that makes the increment's claim true — **detect** (T1), **decouple** (T2), **change** (T3). T1 is atomic (the struct field, both manifests, the check arm and the census extension are one motion: `deny_unknown_fields` means the key and the field cannot land apart). T2 is atomic (the extraction *is* the shadow-map kill; the four swaps share the one new function). T3 is atomic and is the largest single-concern unit in the increment: the map change **breaks the fingerprint assert at every door** — the whole CLI suite goes red — so the version bump + hash re-pin + golden diff + the four hardcoded ids are inseparable from it by construction. Smallest set delivering both grouped-scope bullets and the *Proves*; no creep into Inc 11's pack prose or Inc 12's fold-back. Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 42 Increment 10. **Status: planned; hand to the executor.**

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Increment 9 / validation fix: the ninth sibling was *non-null and still degenerate* — key the census on the claim, not the symptom

`schema-conformance.required-slot-present` — the **doc-level** section slot — kept a bare `Location::at(line, 1)` while all three of its siblings in the same family were normalized (`check_field`/`check_field_value` → `#<section>/<field>`; the *item*-level `check_item_slot_present` → `#<item-path>/<leaf>`), with `section.id` **in hand at the constructor and spent on the message alone** — the pinned defect verbatim, untouched since M4. Under the path→URI flip it addressed at the bare `type:slug`, so a **pristine `jigc doc create adr`** — three empty required slots — emitted **three byte-identical `(code, target)` keys in one JSON array**, on the first finalize of the first ADR in a fresh repo (the loop's highest-traffic finding), and again on the store funnel (`jigc validate --format json`, the CI-gating contract). Now `#<section>`; the fix is the one-line plumbing its siblings already got. **The lesson is why this entry exists, and it retracts T9's "no ninth sibling" above.** The whole sweep — and the T9 seam check that certified it — hunted `target: null`. This finding was **never null, only under-discriminating**, so it slipped past a null-shaped census *and* past `debug_assert_targets_declared`, whose bar is *"has an address"* and not *"discriminates"* — the check enforces the weaker half of the claim the contract actually makes. A census keyed on the **symptom that made the class visible** (null) misses every member that is degenerate some other way; key it on the **property being claimed** (*stable and discriminating*). Strengthening the seam assert to *prove* discrimination is not mechanically available (it would need per-code knowledge of what a subject is), so the honest state is recorded rather than papered over: the assert catches address-*less* findings, and the contract's `#<fragment>` table is what carries the rest. *(⚠ Retracted 2026-07-14, the same day — **the last sentence is false, and the very next commit falsified it**: `25f7cdf` shipped the strengthening, a uniqueness pass over the emitted slice at the seam, and [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → The membership test says of this claim, in terms, "**That was wrong**." The claim reasoned about the *hard* version of the property — prove each code's subject granularity — and concluded the *easy* one was unavailable; the easy one is the one the contract actually makes: **two findings in one emitted array must not carry one key**, which is a single pass over a slice already in hand. What is genuinely human-checked is only the **residue**: a code that under-discriminates but whose instances never **co-occur in one emitted slice** collides with nothing, so the seam cannot see it — that, and only that, is what the `#<fragment>` table fences. Leaving this entry as written would have left the running record contradicting both the shipped code and the design doc of record, in the increment whose own grounds were "a lying comment authorizes the next wrong pin." The seam has since moved again — off the funnel list and **onto the serialization itself**, where the membership predicate decides membership: `38a52dd`, and [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → The membership test.)*

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Increment 9 / T9: the closure claim is enforced where it is *decided*, not where it is *stated*

The contract's third obligation ships as code: `finding::debug_assert_targets_declared` asserts *every `Finding` reaching a serialization funnel carries a `key.target`, except the declared singletons* (`finding::is_declared_singleton` — `store-version.binary-mismatch` + every `setup.*`/`uninstall.*`, the exception list's **one home**), called at all three funnels (`ValidationReport::new`, `render::doc_ack`, `render::setup_block`). Two elaborations the build settled. **(1) The check lives at the funnel, not in a test that re-walks the tree.** A test enumerating constructors is a census with a compiler — exactly the shape that missed six siblings this wave; asserting *at the seam every serialized finding must pass through* makes the whole suite (1740+ tests, every flow driving the real binary) the proof, so a new family that forgets its target form reddens the gate without anyone remembering to look. **(2) `debug_assert`, deliberately.** The obligation is an invariant of jigc's **own** producers, not a condition on user input — it must fail the build loudly and never turn a user's finding into a release-build panic; `cargo test` is a debug build, so the enforcement is exactly where the claim is checkable. The suite went green **through** the seam on the first full run after T1–T8, which is the mechanical answer to the question the wave kept getting wrong by hand: **no ninth sibling.** *(⚠ Retracted the same day — there **was** one, and this sentence is exactly the over-claim the wave keeps re-minting: the seam asserts an address is **present**, never that it **discriminates**, so it certified `required-slot-present`'s three-identical-keys collision as clean. See the validation-fix entry at the top.)* Six hand-built address-less fixtures (engine `result.rs`/`finalize.rs`, cli `render.rs`) were repaired to carry declared targets in the same commit — a test fixture that ships a degenerate key is a test asserting the defect.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Increment 9 / T8: the task-state acks are a *sibling* envelope, and the dead guard died with its lying comment

`task bind` / `task discard` join the ack envelope exactly as [the contract pins them](design/command-output-contract.md) (§2 — `op` + `task` + `findings: []`, plus `role` + the decomposed `target` on bind; a one-line plain ack in place of the de-facto "success is silence" contract). Two elaborations the build settled. **(1) A sibling `TaskAck`, not new `DocAck` variants** — the subject of a task-state verb is a **work unit**, not a doc, so it carries `task` and (on discard) *no* `target`; folding it into `DocAck` would have forced `Option`-ing that type's two load-bearing invariants (every variant has an address, every variant computes intrinsic findings) onto every doc-write site to serve two verbs that have neither. The **JSON shape** is what the contract pins, and it is identical either way — `AckTarget` is shared, and `findings` is emitted as the literal empty array rather than a stored always-empty `Vec<Finding>` (neither verb writes managed content, so a findings *field* would be dead weight the driver still sees as the pinned key). **(2) The dead guard is gone and its doc comment with it** — `run_discard`'s `if task.dir.exists()` could never be false (`TaskArea::resolve` bails first), and the comment claiming idempotence was the false premise that authorized the `discarded` effect key the design pass had to retract. Removing it is behaviour-neutral **and asserted so**: the suite pins `jigc task discard <absent-id>` at **exit 1 + the error envelope** — which is precisely where *removed* vs *was already gone* lives, one layer up from any ack key.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Increment 9 / T7: `workflow-refs.*` keys where the id *exists* — the boundary, not the constructor

All 37 sites of the family are pure helpers over bytes (`load_workflow_def`, `find_run_shadow`, `parse_data_value`, `data_value.rs`'s nine), so **not one of them holds the id of the definition it is reading** — which is why every one emitted `Location::at(…)` with no address and the whole family projected `(code, null)`. The id is stamped **outward**, at the two boundaries that hold one: the store sweep takes the `workflow_id` its caller loop already has (`validate.rs`) and keys a load/expand/pairing break at `workflow:<id>`, a step-body break at `step:<id>`; the compose gates key each step's break at `step:<id>` from `ComposedStep.id`. **No new decision** — the [contract already pinned these under the pack-resource form](design/command-output-contract.md), and the green is the doc's own granularity: **keyed at the resource, declared non-unique below it**, so two bad refs in one step *correctly* collapse to one key (a workflow-def break means the **pack** is broken — one defect, one repair) and no sub-resource discriminator was built. One elaboration worth the line: the **compose gates stamp the step, not the workflow** — the workflow id is not an input there, and every compose-path finding is `finding_to_err`'d by its CLI caller, so it projects no key at all; the funnel-reaching path (the store sweep) is the one that must carry both, and it does. Threading an id the compose path cannot key with would be inert plumbing.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Increment 9 / T5: the outward assembly nests, so an item's field group keys *under its item*

The parse-`conformance.*` fragments land exactly as [the contract's sub-table](design/command-output-contract.md) pins them, with one shape the table's rows do not literally spell: a finding raised inside a **repeatable item** carries the **item hop** too — an undeclared key in an item's field group keys `#<section>/<item>/<field-key>`, a single-slot item's ceiling violation keys `#<section>/<item>/<leaf>`. **No new decision** — it is the pinned rule read straight (*"the innermost helper sets the leaf/item hop it holds"*, naming `parse_items`), and the table's rows were written from the section-scoped fixtures. Recorded because it is a **target string a driver sees**, and the sub-table alone would surprise the reader: the assembly **nests**, so the same code (`unknown-field`) keys at two depths depending on where the field group lives. The alternative — collapsing an item's fields onto `#<section>/<field-key>` — would re-mint the very collision the task exists to kill (the same key in two items of one section). Also folded in, as the design pass called: `owner-artifact.present` (the eighth un-enumerated sibling) flips off the filesystem path onto the URI form; the `type:slug` head survives every fragment, which is what `gates_at_task`'s un-baselined join reads.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Increment 9 / T4: a blocked **milestone** finalize handed its findings to nobody

Keying `finalize.*` at the work unit (`task:<id>` / `milestone:<id>`) and at the file path (`promote-clobber`/`promote-io`/`render-io`/`migration-no-replacement`) is the plumbing the [contract's finalize sub-table](design/command-output-contract.md) pins. But the **milestone** arm's key reached no driver: `run_milestone_finalize`'s block printed each finding's message + route as **text, in every format** — so `jigc milestone finalize --format json` emitted no envelope at all, and `milestone:<id>` would have been a target nothing could read. The blocked milestone finalize now rides the **same funnel as its task sibling** (JSON envelope on stdout, agent/human text on stderr, exit 3 unchanged) — **no new decision**: §3 already declares the consumer list *descriptive, not constitutive* (*"a verb that hands a driver a `Finding` **is** a consumer of this envelope"*), and this is the code half of that widening. Logged because it is the wave's pattern once more — the sweep that found *twelve* `finalize.*` codes never asked whether the surface they exit through **has** an envelope; two of them did not. Also settled: `no-task` keys at the **unit**, not at the absent working-area path (the unit is what a driver tracks; the path is an artifact of where the workbench happens to sit), and the shared constructors take the unit-ref **as an argument** — a path-derived guess would re-mint the degenerate key the task exists to kill.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Increment 9 / T2: the half-normalized `write.*` targets were four constructors, not one

[command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → the `write.*` row names **one** bare-fragment offender (`write.id-from-field`, `doc.rs`); the sweep found **four** — its `add-item` twin (`id_from_enum_block`), `write.identity-change` (the retitle enum refusal) and the retitle milestone-record refusal all emitted `<section>/<item>/<field>` with no doc head, so two docs' foreign categories collided on one key exactly as the null-target family did. All four now emit the URI normal form; **no new decision** — the doc's rule ("a bare fragment is the same broken key one step short") assigns it on sight, and the "…" in its code list already covered them. Logged because the pattern is the wave's own: *a census keyed on the offender you noticed will miss its siblings.* The CLI stamp is **if-absent** at the `DocFailure::Block` seam, so T1's engine-side `create.*` doctype targets and `create.serial-collision`'s doc URI are never clobbered.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Increment 9 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 9](implementation/roadmap.md) (the command-output contract — every finding gets a stable, discriminating key; [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → the stable finding key / the six target forms / the membership test / the parse-conformance + finalize sub-tables / the `op` enum) into **9 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `3e1ba0a` (tree clean; Inc 1–8 landed, the two Inc-9 halts settled into the design of record). The cut is **one task per target-form family**, then the acks, then the closure — no family's fix breaks a gate another family repairs, so each task is gate-green alone.

**Verified bases (facts read at HEAD, not inherited from the charter):**
- **The `(1,1)` address-only `Location` is the house convention, not a new decision.** `Location` has no address-without-position constructor and `line`/`col` are non-optional, so an address-only finding is `Location::addressed(target, 1, 1)` — already what `attribute_to_doc` (`validate.rs:1586`), `file_state`'s five constructors (`file_state.rs:658`…), `instance_collision_finding` (`state.rs:963`), `machine_maintained_guard` and `join.*`/`ingest.*`/`combine.*` all do. Every task below stamps that way; **no envelope shape change, no new `Finding` constructor is required** — `Finding::graded(Blocking, code, msg, Some(Location::addressed(t,1,1)), route)` replaces the location-less `Finding::block(…)` wherever a target exists (`block` hard-sets `location: None`, `finding.rs:296`).
- **The engine `write.*` constructors cannot self-address** — `set_field_validated(schema, source, section_id, field_key, …)` holds section+field, never `type:slug`; only the CLI holds the parsed `Address`. So `write.*` is stamped **outward at the CLI block boundary** (T2), which is also why the two engine `write.*` `insta` snapshots pinning `"target": null` (`engine__write__*.snap`) stay green — the *engine* finding keeps emitting `null`; the CLI stamps it. `create.*`, by contrast, **is** stamped in the engine (T1): `type_name` is in hand at all three constructors.
- **`plan_finalize`'s `commit_slug` parameter *is* the task id** (`task.rs:769` passes `id`; the commit instance is provisioned `commit:<task-id>`) — so the work-unit ref is already in the engine's hand for the task arm. `plan_milestone_finalize` holds only `staging_dir` and shares three constructors with it, so the shared constructors take an explicit unit-ref argument (`task:<id>` / `milestone:<id>`) rather than deriving one (T4).
- **The `workflow-refs.*` fix is per-resource, and that means the two colliding findings the design's red cites stay collided *by design*** — the contract declares the family **non-unique below the resource** ("two malformed data-values in one workflow collapse to one key"). The red is `target: null`; the green is `target: step:<id>` / `workflow:<id>` — **not** two distinct keys for two bad refs in one step (T7's done-criterion is written accordingly, so the executor does not over-build a sub-resource discriminator the doc rejects).
- **`data_value.rs`'s nine sites reach no funnel** — `compose::compose*` returns `Result<_, Finding>` and **every** CLI caller `.map_err(finding_to_err)`s it (`start.rs:780`, `:1065`, `:1763`), so by the doc's own predicate they project no key. They are nonetheless stamped (T7): the doc pins all 37 sites and names `parse_data_value(text)` in its outward-attribution plan, and the rule it states is *"a constructor whose finding can **reach any** funnel needs a declared form"* — the compose loop (`compose_with_store`, `for step in &composition.steps`) holds the step id, so honouring the pin is two lines, not a build.
- **⚠ The eighth sibling — `owner-artifact.present` (`validate.rs:1652`) is in the projecting set, in NO declared form.** It is emitted at task scope (`validate.rs:241`), reaches `ValidationReport` (`task.rs:644`), and is the **one** doc-node family `attribute_to_doc` never touches — so it keys at `<rel_key>#<section>/<field>`, the **filesystem-path** shape the contract explicitly rejects for a doc node (*"breaks on rename and is not the addressing grammar"*). Its key is **discriminating** (so the T9 predicate would pass it and it is not a collision), which is exactly why a census misses it and why it is caught here: it is a **form** violation, not a uniqueness one. **No new decision** — the doc's rule assigns it the URI form on sight (subject = a node inside a managed doc), and the caller holds `filename`, so the flip is the same one-liner `conformance_for` already does (`validate.rs:1548`). Folded into T5. *(Checked the rest of the projecting set the same way: `join.*`/`ingest.*`/`combine.*`/`reconciliation.*`/`file-state.*`/`store.*` all carry addresses; `milestone.*` and `config.*` are `finding_to_err`'d flat; `setup.*`/`uninstall.*` are the declared singletons.)*
- **Both roadmap hazards confirmed live in the code, and both are honoured below:** `block(&finding, verb, addr)` (`doc.rs:3285`) really does take the **raw CLI arg** (T2 stamps `Address::to_string()`, so Inc-8's now-legal bare `vision#context` keys `vision:vision#context`); `gates_at_task` (`render.rs:463`) really does `split('#')` and match the identity half against the un-baselined set (T5 keeps the `type:slug` prefix, and re-asserts the suppression).

**The four grouped-scope bullets map:** *the five-form target normalization across the clusters* → **T1–T7** (six forms — the sixth, the cascade delta target, is T6 — plus the two settled expansions: `workflow-refs.*` in T7, honouring the pin the arithmetic excluded, and `owner-artifact`'s form in T5); *the `op` enum extension + the two task acks* → **T8** (with `run_discard`'s lying "Idempotent" doc comment corrected in the same commit); *the §3 scope widening* → **already landed in the design doc** (`command-output-contract.md:65-67` names `jigc task finalize` and declares the consumer list *descriptive, not constitutive*) — its **code** obligation is T4, and T9 folds the doc's now-stale "the `write.*` and `create.*` rows are the M42 remainder … at HEAD" paragraph; *a value change under an existing pin* → framing, no task. The closure claim's **owed test** (the doc's third obligation) is **T9**, and it is the increment's real deliverable: it is the only artifact that cannot rot.

- **T1 — `create.*` keys at the bare doctype id (engine).** `unknown_doctype_finding` / `empty_title_finding` / `gate_blocked_finding` (`state.rs:950`, `:982`, `:998`) each take `type_name`, spend it on the message + route, and pass `None` for the location — so in a gate-less task (`quick-fix`, `allows-create: []`) two blocked creates of different doctypes both key `(create.gate-blocked, null)`. Stamp `Location::addressed(type_name, 1, 1)` — the **bare doctype id**, not a URI (no instance exists; a synthesized `type:<invented-slug>` would address nothing and a driver could try to `doc show` it), which is the form `store.unknown-type` already emits (`doc.rs:1724-1729`) and `doc schema <doctype>` already takes. `create.serial-collision` (already URI-addressed, `state.rs:963`) is untouched. *Done:* engine unit tests over the three constructors + a real-binary arm — under a gate-less workflow, `jigc doc create adr --format json` and `jigc doc create spec --format json` emit **distinct** `key.target`s (`adr` / `spec`), red today (`null` / `null`); full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/state.rs`.)*
- **T2 — `write.*` carries the doc URI, stamped from the PARSED address (CLI).** Fifteen `write.*` constructors (`write.rs:5047-5599`) set `Location::at(1,1)` → `target: null`, so `(write.wrong-shape, null)` is **one key for every failed write of that code in the corpus**; `write.id-from-field` (`doc.rs:610-614`) emits a **bare fragment** (`criteria/x/title`) and `write.machine-maintained` (`doc.rs:345`) stamps the **raw argument**. All three land on the URI normal form at the depth the write named. **Hazard 1 is the whole point:** the stamp is `address.to_string()` from `parse_verb_addr`'s **parsed** `Address` — never the raw arg — because Inc 8 just made a bare singleton head legal at the verb boundary, so stamping `addr` verbatim would key `vision#context` instead of `vision:vision#context`. Stamp **if-absent** at the `DocFailure::Block` seam (`block()` at `doc.rs:3285` + the two guards), so a finding that already carries its own target (T1's create family, `create.serial-collision`) is never clobbered. *Done:* a real-binary suite over each blocking write verb — `set-field` (malformed value) keys `adr:<slug>#status/status`, `set-slot` (heading-depth), `add-item` (unslugable title), `remove-item` (not-present), `retitle-item`, the id-from guard (full URI, not the bare fragment), and a **bare-singleton** `set-slot 'vision#context'` keys `vision:vision#context`; two failed writes to two docs no longer share a key; full gate. *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`.)*
- **T3 — `pack-probe-integrity.probe-failure` keys at the probe id (engine).** `ingest_probe_run(probe_id, …)` (`probe.rs:249`) holds the id and spends it on the message; `meta_finding` (`probe.rs:285-296`) passes `None` — so **every** misbehaving probe in one sweep collides on one key, on the family that is *also* the store-scope exit-flip class (the one an operator most needs to tell apart). Thread `probe_id` into `meta_finding` and stamp it as the target (the pack-resource form). *Done:* an engine unit test — two probes in one run, one timing out and one crashing, yield findings with **distinct** `key.target`s (their probe ids), red today (`null` / `null`); the `(probe, check)` severity handle (`timeout`/`crash`/`malformed-output`, set via `with_check`) is unchanged; full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/probe.rs`.)*
- **T4 — `finalize.*` splits: the work unit takes `task:<id>`/`milestone:<id>`, the file takes its path (engine + CLI).** Twelve codes, **every one `location: None`** — so `(finalize.base-mismatch, null)` is one key for every diverged task in every repo, on the single most driver-consumed block in the loop. The subject **splits, and the split is the point**: `no-task` / `base-mismatch` / `empty-commit` / `provenance-io` / `source-path-io` (`finalize.rs`) + `nothing-staged` / `stage-failed` (**`cli/task.rs:1640`, `:1654` — the two the design's own file-scoped census missed**) take the **work-unit ref**; `promote-clobber` / `promote-io` / `render-io` / `migration-no-replacement` take the **file path** they already hold (a destination that may be a *foreign* file with no URI identity — the `file-state` reason exactly); `forward-ref-dangling` is already URI-addressed and untouched. The three constructors **shared** with `plan_milestone_finalize` take an explicit unit-ref argument (the task arm passes `task:<commit_slug>` — verified: `commit_slug` *is* the task id; the milestone arm passes `milestone:<id>`, threaded in), never a path-derived guess. *Done:* a real-binary arm — a task finalize blocked on a moved base keys `task:<id>`, a second task's identical block keys **its own** id; a promote-clobber keys the destination path; a **milestone** finalize base-mismatch keys `milestone:<id>` (the unit-aware route Inc 7 landed now has a unit-aware key); red today on all four (`null`); full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/finalize.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`.)*
- **T5 — the parse-`conformance.*` family gets its discriminating fragment, and the last doc-node family gets the URI form (engine).** Of thirteen codes only `section-missing` carries a fragment, so `attribute_to_doc` addresses the other **twelve** at the bare `type:slug` and **two unknown fields in one doc collide on one key**. The address is assembled **outward in three stages** (no signature churn — none of the parse helpers receives the section id): the innermost helper sets the leaf/item hop it holds (`read_marked_field_group:708`, `read_field_block_str:749`, `parse_items:796`, `parse_item_slots:967`, `ceiling_violations:1218`), `parse_sections` (`:204`, the only fn holding `section.id`) prefixes the section hop, and `attribute_to_doc` (`validate.rs:1577`) prefixes `type:slug`. Fragments exactly as the contract's sub-table pins them (incl. the four **declared non-unique** rows — `item-anchor-missing`, `item-slot-delimiter-shadowed`, `slot-setext-heading`/`slot-heading-depth` — which collapse *deliberately*: their discriminator is the missing identity, or prose that churns under the very edits the key exists to survive). **Hazard 2, asserted not assumed:** `gates_at_task` (`render.rs:463`) splits `location.address` on `#` and matches the identity half against the un-baselined set to decide gating — adding fragments is safe, **dropping the `type:slug` prefix would silently break the gate**, so the task re-asserts un-baselined suppression over a fragment-bearing finding. **Plus `owner-artifact.present`** (`validate.rs:1652`, the eighth sibling above): its `<rel_key>#<section>/<field>` path-form address is flipped to the URI at its emit site (`validate.rs:241` holds `filename`) — the same doc-node form, one line, no new decision. *Done:* engine unit tests — two `unknown-field` findings in one doc carry **distinct** keys (`…#<section>/<key-a>` vs `…#<section>/<key-b>`), red today (identical); each of the twelve codes carries its pinned fragment; a `conformance.*` finding on an **un-baselined** doc is still suppressed at task scope (the gate regression); the moved engine parse/validate expectations repaired in the same commit; full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{parse.rs,validate.rs}`.)*
- **T6 — the SIXTH form: the cascade delta target (engine).** `override-default.*`'s five constructors (`override_default.rs:206,255,308,326,357`) each **compute** the delta's identity string (`format!("scalar:{key}")`, `step:<id>#<fill-id>`, `render_target(…)`), spend it on the message and the route, then call `Finding::block(…)`, which hard-sets `location: None` — so `jigc upgrade --format json` over two orphaned scalar-sets emits **one JSON array with two byte-identical keys**. This is the only cluster that **collides inside a single document** (every other needs two invocations), and the only one in **no** declared form: the subject is a recorded **delta**, not the pack resource it points at, and `scalar:<knob-key>` fits none of the five — which is what forces the call the contract reserves (*"a sixth is a decision, not a default"*). Stamp the string that is already computed. *Done:* a real-binary arm — `jigc upgrade --format json` over a project layer with **two** orphaned scalar-sets emits two findings with **distinct** `key.target`s (`scalar:<a>` / `scalar:<b>`) in one array, red today (byte-identical); a `slot-fill-orphaned` keys `step:<id>#<fill-id>` and a `content-changed` keys its `render_target`; full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/override_default.rs`.)*
- **T7 — `workflow-refs.*` keys at the pack resource — honouring the pin the arithmetic excluded (engine).** 28 codes / 37 sites (`compose.rs` 28, `data_value.rs` 9), all `Location::at()` → `target: null`, while the contract **already pins them** under the pack-resource form. They reach `ValidationReport` through the store sweep (`validate.rs:427` → `:536`), so shipping 1.0 with the doc claiming they are keyed and the code emitting `null` is the same false-claim-at-the-pin this increment exists to fix. The ids are not in hand at the constructors (pure helpers over bytes) but **are** at the two boundaries: `workflow_refs_store` (`compose.rs:2236`) takes the workflow id (the caller loop at `validate.rs:424` holds `workflow.id`) and stamps workflow-level findings `workflow:<id>`, per-step findings `step:<ComposedStep.id>`; the compose loop (`compose_with_store`) stamps the emit-path findings the same way. **Keyed at the resource and declared NON-UNIQUE below it** — two bad refs in one step *correctly* collapse to one key (a broken pack is one defect a pack author fixes once, not a corpus finding a driver tracks). *Done:* a real-binary arm — a pack whose one step carries two unresolvable `{{cli.…}}` refs: `jigc validate --format json` keys **both** at `step:<id>` (red today: `target: null`), while a second workflow's bad include keys `workflow:<id>` — distinct resources, distinct keys; an engine unit test pins the compose-path stamp (`data_value.rs`'s malformed-value); full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{compose.rs,data_value.rs,validate.rs}`.)*
- **T8 — `task bind` / `task discard` join the ack envelope, and the lying comment dies (CLI).** Both mutate durable state and today **print nothing at all, in every format** (`task.rs:259-266`, `:281-284`; `dispatch` takes a `format` and both arms drop it), while `--format json` *does* emit an envelope on their **failure** path — so the gap is precisely the **success** path, and "prints nothing" is itself a de-facto contract. The `op` enum extends with `task-bind` / `task-discard`; the shapes are pinned in the contract (§2): bind carries `task` + `role` + the decomposed `target` (`doctype`+`slug`, from the **parsed** address — `TaskArea::bind` already parses it), discard carries `task` alone. **`task-discard` carries NO effect key** — the settled halt: `jigc task discard <absent-id>` **exits 1** (`TaskArea::resolve`, `task.rs:374-390`, bails before `run_discard`'s `if task.dir.exists()` guard), so a `discarded` key could only ever hold the constant `true`, *removed* vs *was already gone* is already carried by exit 0 + ack vs exit 1 + error envelope, and making it reachable would turn an honest dead end into a lying route on a **milestone** id. `run_discard`'s dead `exists()` guard and its false *"Idempotent: an already-absent area is not an error"* doc comment are corrected in the same commit (a lying comment authorizes the next wrong pin — it authorized this one). Both verbs also gain the one-line plain-text ack. *Done:* a real-binary suite — `jigc task bind <role> <addr> <id> --format json` prints `{"op":"task-bind","task":…,"role":…,"target":{"doctype":…,"slug":…},"findings":[]}` and the plain format prints one line (red today: silence in every format); `task discard` prints its ack; `task discard <absent>` still **exits 1** with the error envelope (the guard's removal changes no behaviour — asserted); full gate. *(files: `crates/cli/src/{task.rs,render.rs}`.)*
- **T9 — the closure claim becomes mechanically checkable: the predicate, the exception list, and the test that outlives the census (engine + docs).** The contract's third obligation, and **the increment's most durable output** — *"a claim checkable only by a census someone must remember to repeat **will** rot"*, and this one has now been false twice at its own pin. Membership is a **predicate**: a finding projects a key **iff it is serialized as a `Finding`** (`Serialize` writes `key` unconditionally, `finding.rs:227`, derived from `Location::address`), through exactly **three funnels** — `ValidationReport`'s `findings[]` (the single constructor `ValidationReport::new`, *the natural seam*), `DocAck`'s `findings[]` (`render.rs:749-801`), and the bare-`Finding` `setup_block` (`render.rs:1008`) — with one escape hatch (`finding_to_err`, which discards the `Finding` entirely). Land the check **at the seam**, keyed on a single declared-exception list in one place: the **singletons** (`store-version.binary-mismatch`; every `setup.*`/`uninstall.*` — fail-fast `Result<_, Finding>`, `setup.rs:693`, `:1173`, no `Vec<Finding>` anywhere, so two instances of one code can never coexist). **It lands LAST deliberately: it is the sweep's own auditor** — if it reddens on a family T1–T8 did not touch, that family is the ninth sibling and it is closed here (a form, or a declared+reasoned exception — never a `null` left silent). Test-fixture findings that reach the seam are repaired in the same commit (same gate-green unit). Same motion: `finding.rs:29-31`'s module doc — *"`target` is `null` for a finding raised before an address resolves"* — is **contradicted by the pin** and rewritten (after this wave `null` is a **declared singleton value**, not a default; left standing it authorizes the next degenerate key by itself), and the contract's now-stale *"the `write.*` and `create.*` rows are the M42 remainder … those still emit their first-column value at HEAD"* paragraph is folded to what shipped. *Done:* a unit test proving the check **fires** on a non-exempt address-less finding reaching the seam and **passes** an exempt one (red today: no such check exists); `cargo test` green across the whole workspace **through the seam** — which is the mechanical proof the sweep is closed; full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{finding.rs,result.rs}`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `design/command-output-contract.md`.)*

**Why this order:** the **form families first, one per task** (T1–T7), ordered independent-first so each reddens a disjoint test set and none breaks a gate another repairs — engine-self-addressing families (T1, T3) before the CLI outward-stamping one (T2, which must *not* clobber T1's targets), then the three that touch shared plumbing (T4 finalize's two planners, T5's three-stage parse assembly + the gate hazard, T7's two boundaries), with T6 (the sixth form) standing alone since it mints a *form*, not just a value; then the acks (T8, independent of every key); then the closure (**T9 last, because it audits T1–T8** — landing it first would redden the gate for eight tasks with no in-scope fix, and landing it at all is what stops this class returning a ninth time). Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 42 → Increment 9. **Status: planned; hand off to task execution.**

## 2026-07-14 — Idea parked: the assumption register

The M42 post-mortem's deepest finding shaped as a parked idea rather than smuggled into a fold-back ([ideas/assumption-register.md](ideas/assumption-register.md); indexed from [VISION.md](VISION.md) → Open questions). **A managed register of the assumptions code makes about a *set*, each carrying a `fenced-by: code-anchor` the `symbol-exists` probe verifies — so an *unfenced* assumption is a visible, gated defect.** The machinery already ships (`code-anchor` + `doc-code`, the `spec` → `maps-to-test` shape).

**Why it is worth having, and where it stops — both stated in the idea, because the overclaim is the thing it exists to guard against.** jigc **cannot write your fence**: a defect-at-a-distance is killed by a `debug_assert`, not a document. What the register does is make the *absence* of the fence impossible to ignore. And its ceiling is honest: **it catches the assumptions you notice**, converting *"I forgot to fence it"* into *"I never wrote it down"* — strictly better, **not a solution**. *(jigc already proves the medicine works in its own domain — the schema-hash freeze assert is precisely "fence the assumption where the set is defined," and it reddens in the gate of the person who changed the set. It just cannot hand that to arbitrary code.)*

**Trigger: the post-1.0 self-migration** — the cheapest possible proof, since **the register's first four rows are the four assumptions that cost M42 nine catches** (*every doctype at v1* · *every pack embedded* · *every finding addressed* · *every serializing surface one of three*).

## 2026-07-14 — Where the bugs came from: two rules the post-mortem earned

**Human question: where did M42's defects come from — was the workflow not good enough?** The provenance was traced, not guessed, and it is more useful than *"we were sloppy."* **The workflow *found* all of them** (the trials, the adversarial audits, the cross-model pass, three build halts). **It found them late** — the `AddedOptionalSection` stranding survived **six milestones, two RC trials, three completion audits and a cross-model review** while corrupting real adopter corpora. The reason is structural: **the workflow reviews *diffs* and *plans*, and three of the four defect origins are visible in neither.**

**The four origins.** (1) **An assumption expired** — a rule true of the set as it was, falsified by a later *correct* change. (2) **The sibling nobody edited** — `reconcile_committed_store` got its branch, its read-only twin didn't; M41's F5 fixed `extract_anchor` **and wrote the hazard into a comment**, then missed `heading_matches`, the sibling the comment described. (3) **The gate fired and produced a wrong artifact** — M38 *ran* the census, wrote it down, even recorded missing one site, and had missed three more; a judgment gate can be passed with a bad judgment. (4) **Capability shipped without prompting** — `maps-to-test` had a working write path, a **live blocking check**, and **zero writes ever**, because the only pack text naming it said *"leave it off."*

**Origin 1 is the one no review can catch, and it is now measured.** `strip_stamp(current)` was written **2026-06-25 and was correct** (every doctype at v1). `adr` bumped to schema-version 2 on **2026-07-03** — **57 commits later**, also correct — and **that commit never touched `migrate_corpus.rs`**. **Two clean diffs; a permanent dead-end bug in the space between them.** A reviewer of either change sees nothing wrong because nothing *in* either change is wrong. **Folded back as *a defect at a distance*** ([dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md)): **when your change rests on an assumption about a *set*, fence it where the set is *defined*, so growing the set reddens the *other* author's gate.** Had that assumption been an assert against the manifest, M36's bump would have failed **its own build**, and the conversation would have happened then, for free. *This is "a grep is not a fence" aimed backwards in time: that rule says don't enforce a property with a list; this says don't leave an assumption unfenced merely because it is true today.*

**And the second rule, which upgrades this very file: a deferral trigger is a claim about the code — so it should be a test.** The freeze-assert hole was deferred with the trigger *"if packs are ever loaded from the filesystem."* **Multi-pack shipped at M14 and made it true. Nothing noticed**, because the trigger was **prose in a ledger** that someone had to remember to re-read. **Pack-shape:** an optional **`trigger-test: code-anchor`** on the `deferral-ledger` entry (`check: symbol-exists`) — the deferral names a test that holds *today* and **reddens on the commit that makes the trigger true**; the `doc-code` probe verifies the test exists. **The trigger fires itself, in the gate of the person who triggered it.** Judgment triggers (*"when an adopter corpus surfaces a measured floor"*) keep the prose field — optional by design, and that boundary is the A-3 bound working, not a gap. *(An added optional field on a repeatable item block was **unclassifiable** by the migration classifier until three days ago; **M42 built `AddedItemField`**, so this is now a routine bump. It lands with the self-hosting encode.)*

**Also folded:** `deliverable-reachable` now covers **prompt-reachability** — *for an agent-facing capability, does the pack ever **tell** an agent to use it?* A capability the composed workflow never names is unreachable **in the only way that matters**, and every code gate will still be green.

**The honest summary of the post-mortem:** the workflow was good enough to **find** these; it was not shaped to **prevent** them, because it inspects *changes* and *plans*, while these bugs live in **assumptions that expire**, **siblings nobody edited**, and **prose nobody reads**. The answer is not more gates — **it is moving the fences to where the assumptions are made.**

## 2026-07-14 — The M42 fold-back, re-authored pack-shaped — and the 2026-06-21 rule had never once bound

**Human direction:** *jigc should enforce the rules and print them at the right time, so we can reduce prose — like our own workflows, which never just bail, they say what to do next.* **That is already the recorded direction, in the human's own words** ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-06-21 Direction): *"the prose-accretion class we keep hand-patching in the methodology docs **is the class jigc exists to solve** — a required slot cannot be skimmed past the way a prose paragraph can; a composed step always appears."* Its first bullet: **new forcing-functions are authored *pack-shaped* from now on**, so the eventual encode is **transcription, not redesign**.

**It has not bound once.** M41's two dev-workflow fold-backs are plain prose. So was M42's first draft, written hours ago. Three weeks, zero applications — *of the rule whose entire subject is that prose you must remember to read does not bind.* The rule was its own counterexample. **Now re-authored:** every M42 fold-back (and, in the same edit region, M41's pair) carries its **pack-shape** — the slot, step, or fence it will become.

**The tiering that fell out, and it is the useful part.** A methodology rule can land at four depths, and only the bottom one is what we have been writing:

1. **Structural** — the property *cannot* be violated. **No prose at all.** (M42's finding-key seam: a finding cannot reach a driver without a discriminating key, and there is no funnel list to forget.)
2. **Gated + routed** — a check fires and the route says what to do next. **The prose is the route string.** *(This is the human's "we never just bail" instinct — and it is already a declared floor: every advisory carries a route, M41.)*
3. **Composed step / required slot** — it *always appears* at the moment it binds; a slot **cannot be skimmed past**. The prose survives, but the actor cannot fail to meet it.
4. **Doc prose** — the actor must remember to read it. **Rots.**

**The reduction is not fewer words — it is moving rules from 4 to 1–3.** And the sharpest finding from doing it: **the parallel-fixer rule is a *tier-1* rule we had been writing as tier-4 prose.** `jigc milestone provision` already isolates every sub-task in its own git worktree keyed by task id — the M31 fan-out primitive, built exactly so concurrent agents cannot share a tree. **The fence existed; we hand-spawned around it, twice** (M38, M42). The encode is simply: **the completion workflow's Fix phase composes `fan-out`/`join` over the confirmed findings**, as the build phase already does over increments — and then two fixers *physically cannot* race one index, and the rule needs **no words at all**. *Always ask whether the rule you are about to write is really a missing fence.*

**The ceiling, and it is the human's own bound (A-3).** jigc enforces the census slot is **filled**; it must **never grade the judgment inside it**. A composed step emitting a `gap-count ≥ N` lint would *hollow* the judgment — barred, and recorded as the `methodology_honesty_artifact` FAIL. So the prose splits, permanently: **reminder prose** (*"don't forget to…"*) **dies** — it becomes a slot, a step, or a route. **Rationale prose** (the *why*, the worked instances, the nine costumes of one bug) **stays, and should** — it is what a reader consults to *understand* rather than to *comply*. Anyone promising jigc deletes the judgment prose is selling the thing this bound forbids.

**Not done here, deliberately:** the live encode. It stays deferred behind external proof + human testing (*"we do not put our own critical-path process docs on the tooling until it is earned elsewhere"*) — now largely discharged (two RC trials, the adoption trial, WHY-JIGC), and chartered into the post-1.0 self-migration. **The markdown is now a faithful spec for that encode**, which was the whole point of the 2026-06-21 rule.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 methodology fold-back: a grep is not a fence, and a rule you must remember is not a rule

**Four lessons folded back into the workflow docs.** M42's transferable output is larger than its code, and it is all one idea seen from four angles.

**(1) "A grep is not a fence" → [dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md), as the sibling of M41's "a proptest is not a gate."** The `census` gate already required a **grep** over a hand-list. M42 obeyed that rule and **still missed members nine times** — because *the pattern encodes an assumption about where the members live*. It greped `schema.location` and missed `prior.location`; greped `finalize.rs` and missed two CLI members; enumerated five finding-clusters and missed two more (47 codes). **Every fix but the last was one level too shallow: we added the missed members, and the list stayed a list.** The rule now reads: *if a property must hold of every member of a growing set, the check must live where membership is **decided** — on the constructor, the trait impl, the serialization — never on a list of the places you currently remember.* **Searched coverage is a finder, not a fence**, exactly as randomized coverage is. *(The tell was in a doc comment the whole time: "call it at each of the three funnels." **A guard that has to ask to be called is not a guard.**)*

**(2) `reuse-exercised` means the SEMANTICS were run, not that the SIGNATURE was read → the [gate table](design/methodology-docs.md).** Three of M42's six wrong gate-cells passed because someone verified a thing **existed** and not that it **meant** what the design needed. The worst read *"`record: &FileStateRecord` is already a parameter — verified by reading the signature."* It **is** a parameter. It is also a **gitignored, rebuildable cache** — so on a fresh clone every managed doc would have looked foreign and the tool would have told a teammate to `ingest` their own corpus. **A cell that cites a type, a parameter, or a call site — rather than a behaviour you observed — is not filled.**

**(3) The design of record is a claim, not a fact → [increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md).** M41's rule bound the *author* of a rationale; this binds the *consumer*. **The increment planner must run the design's load-bearing factual claims against the binary before decomposing** — not its judgments, its *facts* ("this verb is idempotent," "this parameter is already threaded," "this family has nine members"). M42's Increment 9 **halted three times**, every one the planner refusing to build against a design claim that the binary falsified — including a pinned 1.0 contract key resting on an **idempotent no-op that does not exist**, because the code's own doc comment lied and the design pass trusted it. **Every earlier catch in the wave came from a reviewer; these three came from the builder refusing to build.** The gate-record is **necessary and not sufficient**: a cell can be filled confidently and wrongly, and no amount of *reading* catches a claim only the *binary* can falsify.

**(4) And the uncomfortable one.** [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md) **already forbade** running two tree-mutating agents on one working tree — a rule written **because of this exact mistake at M38**, citing that precedent by name, and explicitly extended to hand-spawned fixers. **The M42 orchestrator did it anyway**, having not re-read the doc: three fixers, one tree, a file mid-edit and not compiling. It survived only because the fixers — like M38's — defensively gated in isolated worktrees and staged only their own paths. **The reasoning that got there is this project's signature failure wearing a methodology costume:** *"these three findings touch different concerns, so they're independent"* — a claim about the members being looked at, not about **what they have in common**. What they had in common was the tree.

**So the deepest lesson of M42 is that the methodology has the same disease the code had.** **A rule that lives in prose the actor must remember to read is the same object as a hand-maintained census — and it rots at exactly the moment it is needed.** The four fold-backs above are, unavoidably, *more prose*; that is the honest bound on this entry. **The rule that outranks them: where a property can be enforced structurally, enforce it structurally, and treat the prose as documentation of the fence — never as the fence.** That is what the finding-key seam now does in code, and it is what the harness should eventually do for tree-mutating agents. Until it does, the mitigation is the one both waves' fixers reached for unprompted, and it is now written down: **gate in an isolated worktree, stage only your own paths — prefer that over trusting the rule to be remembered.**

## 2026-07-14 — M42 completion: built, audited, 5 findings fixed + re-verified — ✅ shipped

**M42 (the rc.6 wave) is complete.** 12 increments built via the milestone-build harness (each independently validated), then the completion audit: **code-review + e2e through the real binary** — all six done-picture arms passed, including the headline stale-corpus arm and the `## Options` ADR that **rc.5 stranded permanently**. Verdict: [completions/artifacts/M42/VERDICT.md](completions/artifacts/M42/VERDICT.md). **Five audit findings, all fixed, none deferred**, re-verified at `a309a53`: **1977 passed / 0 failed**, clippy/fmt/build clean.

**Two HIGH findings, and both were the wave's own disease surfacing one layer down.** (1) A **v0-era doc of a doctype at schema-version ≥ 2 was a permanent dead end** — the v0 arm derived the prior shape as `strip_stamp(current)`, which silently asserts *no doctype ever bumped past v1* (false since `adr` went to v2 at M36). So `validate` exited 1 forever while `migrate-corpus` refused with a route that **could not be followed** on any of its three counts — the exact **loud false route** this wave exists to eliminate, on the very population Increment 3's discriminator was built to route (`3da864b`: source the prior shape from the doctype's earliest shipped snapshot). (2) **`discarded` was not terminal** — `provision`/`add-task` resurrected an abandoned milestone from its own settled record and re-appended `status: active`, recreating the lying committed record Increment 7 claims to have eliminated (`a309a53`). Fixed with **one predicate at one site** — *a record in a terminal state does not re-seed a workbench* — placed **ahead of** the cache-present early-return, so an interrupted teardown refuses too, and covering **both** terminals (`discarded` *and* `joined`) rather than shipping two special cases and waiting for the third.

**Two masking tests were caught, and the second one stings.** Flow 43's discard arm asserted the record settled and then **never ran a milestone verb afterwards** — a snapshot assertion where the claim is a *lifecycle invariant*. And **Increment 7's own e2e proof fixture was built on the defect**: `setup_partially_joined_milestone` minted its "partially-joined" record by doing `finalize` → `add-task`. **The fixture that proved the claim was an instance of the bug.** Both now exercise the invariant they assert.

**Two shipped-behaviour changes, stated rather than slipped in.** `jigc migrate-corpus` now **exits non-zero whenever anything is blocked** — including `prose-needed`, the Framing-A waypoint (CLI blocks → LLM authors → operator re-runs). The migration genuinely is not done and a driver must see that, but **a pre-existing driver keying on exit 0 at that waypoint will now see a failure**. And a milestone in a terminal state **refuses all eight workbench verbs**, `list-tasks` included (it reads the *workbench cache*; serving it means rebuilding a workbench for a milestone that has none — the route names `jigc doc show milestone-record:<id>`, which returns strictly more). **A milestone that is over is read, not operated.**

**And an honest retraction.** Increment 7 claimed *"a genuinely joined sub-task stays joined"* as a **verb-reachable e2e path**. It is not — a *mixed* record cannot be reached through the verbs, because `finalize` joins the milestone whole. The per-item rule stands as **engine-level honesty** over a directly-constructed record; **the e2e claim is withdrawn** rather than kept alive by a test that could only demonstrate it by resurrecting a finalized milestone ([team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → *The terminal is terminal*).

**The wave's headline claim holds.** All four routes that lied when M42 opened now tell the truth, proven through the real binary: `validate` exits non-zero over a stale **managed** corpus while a stock brownfield repo stays **exit-0** · an OOB edit to `CHANGELOG.md`/`VISION.md` is **detected and routed** · `migrate-corpus` **finds, migrates and lands** a placement doc through the tool instead of the raw-git drive-around · and a discarded milestone **settles its record**. Plus: the migration *class* is closed (the empty-diff backstop refuses a bump with no kind, and the shipped `AddedOptionalSection` stranding that trapped adopters since **M36** is gone), every finding carries a **stable discriminating key** enforced at the serialization seam, the **slug rule is versioned** (the function that names every id was inside no schema-hash), and **the pack finally states the staging contract** — the verified root cause of the trial's silent partial commits.

**Deliberately not shipped: the `spec` lifecycle bump.** Fork 5's *"last cheap window"* premise self-refuted — **if the window is real, the migration machine has failed its declared purpose** — so the wave fixed the machine. The bump is now a routine `migrate-corpus` run whenever it lands, and the lifecycle gets **designed** rather than shaped by a classifier gap. Deferred with its rationale ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)).

**Process, recorded because it is the transferable part:** the build **halted three times at Increment 9**, each time refusing to proceed against a design-of-record claim that proved false — a pinned effect key resting on an idempotent no-op **that does not exist** (the code's own doc comment was lying, and the design pass trusted it) · a finding-key sweep that **had not closed the class it existed to close** · and an enforcement seam that was **itself a census**. Every earlier catch in this wave came from a *reviewer*; **these three came from the builder refusing to build.** The planning gate-record was **necessary and not sufficient** — a cell can be filled confidently and wrongly, and what caught these was *independent readers with different priors* and *a builder that ran the binary instead of trusting the doc*.

**Next:** version bump + install **1.0.0-rc.6** → **the 1.0.0 call** (the human's; the rc count stays deliberately open).

## 2026-07-14 — The seam rides the serialization: a census cannot enforce a predicate

**The eighth catch, and the one that ends the class.** Increment 9 replaced the finding-key *membership* census with a **predicate** — *a finding projects a key **iff** it is serialized as a `Finding`* — and then **installed the predicate's enforcement as a census**: `debug_assert_targets_declared` called at **three hand-listed funnels**, with the module doc saying *"call it at each of the three funnels."* The increment's own validator found **the fourth** (`jigc ingest`, whose `TriageRow` holds an `Option<Finding>` and therefore serializes a key), and with it a live defect: **the same fault, in the same doc, carried two different keys depending on which verb reported it** — `jigc validate` emitted the URI form, `jigc ingest` re-stamped the file path.

**Settled: the guard moves onto the serialization itself.** If membership *is* "it serializes," then the check belongs **at the serialization**, where membership and enforcement become **the same act**. Presence is now asserted inside `Finding`'s `Serialize` (`finding.rs:452`): a targetless non-singleton finding **cannot be projected on any surface**, and **there is no list of places to check.** Uniqueness needs the *set*, so it rides a **`Findings` newtype** (`finding.rs:312-324`) — the only sanctioned way a findings *collection* serializes. The three funnel call sites, and the instruction to remember them, are **deleted**. A fifth surface cannot bypass the check, because there is nothing to bypass. *(Proved: `validate` and `ingest` now emit one key for one defect. The fix also retired a **third** hand-rolled copy of the path→URI flip.)*

**The honest bound, declared not faked:** uniqueness is enforced **per serializing container**. A container holding findings *indirectly* — `ingest`'s report is a `Vec<TriageRow>`, one `Option<Finding>` each — cannot reach `Findings`' impl, so it runs the same pass from its own `Serialize`. Unbypassable for that type, but **per-type**: a future report-of-rows shape owes the same three lines. **Presence has no such bound — it is universal.**

**Why this entry exists, and it is the milestone's real output.** M42 caught the same failure **eight times**: the `schema.location` census (keyed on the *name* `location` — missed `prior.location`) · the pack-prose census (keyed on the *dev pack* — missed the methodology pack) · the backstop's false-refusal class (swept *one member of nine*) · the `finalize.*` census (keyed on the *file* — missed two CLI members) · the key sweep (keyed on *five clusters someone listed* — missed two more) · a DECISIONS entry that recorded an unchecked premise **while warning against unchecked premises** · and finally the enforcement census above.

**Every one of those fixes was one level too shallow, in the same way.** We kept adding the missed members, and the *list* stayed a list. **A list of places-to-check is the same object as a list of members** — so "replace the census with a predicate" only worked for *membership*, and we hand-enumerated *enforcement* one level up, where it rotted inside the same increment.

**The rule, now paid for eight times: a census cannot enforce a predicate.** If a property must hold of every member of a growing set, the check must live where membership is *decided* — on the constructor, on the trait impl, on the serialization — never on a list of the places you currently remember. **A list you must remember to update is not a fence; it is a note to your future self, and it rots the moment the set grows.** *(The honest tell that we had it wrong: the module doc said "call it at each of the three funnels." A guard that has to *ask* to be called is not a guard.)*

## 2026-07-14 — M42 build halt at Increment 9 (the second): the key sweep was not closed, and the sixth form is minted

**The build halted again, and again it was right.** Increment 9 exists to close the degenerate-finding-key class. Its planner found that **the sweep meant to close the class did not close it** — the **sixth un-enumerated sibling of this wave, found inside the fix for the fifth.**

**The evidence is worse than anything the increment enumerated.** `jigc upgrade --format json` over a project layer with two orphaned scalar-sets emits **one JSON array containing two findings with byte-identical keys** — `{"code": "override-default.scalar-set-orphaned", "target": null}`, twice. Every cluster the increment named needs **two separate invocations** to collide (`create.*` two creates in one task; `probe-failure` two crashed probes in one sweep). **This one collides inside a single JSON document**, so a driver deserializing the array cannot tell the two findings apart at all. And the defect is the pinned one **verbatim**: `scalar_set_orphaned` (`override_default.rs:204-208`) **computes** `format!("scalar:{key}")`, spends it on the message and the route, then calls `Finding::block(…)`, which hard-sets `location: None` — *word for word* what the contract already says about `pack-probe-integrity`. **The same defect, one surface over, un-swept.**

**Settled (1): the sixth target form — the cascade delta target.** The contract's own line — *"there are five declared forms, and a sixth is a decision, not a default"* — is exactly the line this exercises, so the call goes to the human. It covers **`override-default.*` — 5 codes** (the halt named 19; the verification pass cut it to 5, see below) — with **one rationale: the subject of these findings is a recorded DELTA, not the pack resource the delta points at.** Two of the three delta-kind variants (`step:<id>#<fill-id>`, `workflow:<id>#<step-id>`) merely *look* like the pack-resource form — a coincidence of shape, not a statement of subject — and the third (`scalar:<knob-key>`) fits **none** of the five, which is what forced the call. Rejected: widening the pack-resource form (a knob key is not a pack resource; it is a key *into the resolved cascade*, and stretching a form to fit a thing it isn't is how the next reader mis-files the one after that) and a declared non-unique exception (**the discriminating string already exists and is already computed** — declaring an exception while holding the answer is the *precise* `nullable-by-contract` mistake this same increment already caught once).

**Settled (2): `workflow-refs.*` (28 codes / 37 sites) is IN.** The contract **already pins them**; the increment's first cut enumerated five clusters totalling *~28 codes* — **arithmetic that excluded `workflow-refs` entirely**. The planner refused to self-authorize the expansion and halted. Honour the pin: shipping 1.0 with the doc claiming they are keyed and the code emitting `null` is the same false-claim-at-the-pin problem the increment exists to fix.

**Settled (3), and this is the durable one: the closure claim becomes MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE.** The contract pinned *"every finding constructor **in the tree**"* — an over-claim, **and the reason the sweep missed two groups.** Membership needs a **predicate**, not a census: **does the finding project a `key`?** A finding projects a key **iff it is serialized as a `Finding`** (`Serialize` writes `key` unconditionally, `finding.rs:227`, derived from `Location::address`). Three funnels, one escape hatch (`finding_to_err`). The claim is rewritten to the **envelope-projecting set**, and **a test enforces the obligation**: *every `Finding` reaching a funnel carries `Some(Location::address)`, except the declared-exception list.*

**⚠ And this entry's own first draft carried an unchecked rationale — the seventh sibling, inside the entry about the sixth.** It recorded the halt's premise verbatim — *"`config.*`/`setup.*`/`uninstall.*` (31 codes) never project a `key`"* — **and that is false for 24 of the 31.** `setup.*`/`uninstall.*` **do** project keys, through a **third funnel the two-funnel picture did not have** (`setup_block`, `render.rs:1008`, a bare `Finding`): `jigc setup --format json` outside a repo emits a fully serialized finding **with a key**. Only **`config.*` (7 codes)** actually flattens. The keys are nonetheless sound — `setup::run` / `run_uninstall` are `Result<_, Finding>` (`setup.rs:693`, `:1173`), **fail-fast, one finding per invocation, no `Vec<Finding>` anywhere** — so they are genuine **singletons** and fold into that exception, which is now stated **as a predicate** (*at most one instance can exist*) rather than a list. Corrected before commit. **Two further corrections the check forced:** `structural-target.*` (8) + `slot-fill-target.*` (6) — 14 codes — need **no form at all**: every production caller `.map_err(finding_to_err)?`, so they **never project a key** and the predicate excludes them (they were sixth-form candidates on the strength of their siblings' *shape*; the predicate excludes them on where they *go*). So the sixth form covers **`override-default.*` alone — 5 codes**, and the true non-key-projecting set is **21** (`config.*` 7 + the 14), not 31.

*That the entry warning against unchecked rationales itself contained one is not an embarrassment to bury — it is the argument. **Six of these were caught by a reader; the seventh was caught by a predicate.** The census does not fail because people are careless. It fails because it is a census.*

**Why that matters more than the fix:** M42 has now caught the same failure **six times** — the `schema.location` census (keyed on the *name* `location`, missed `prior.location`) · the pack-prose census (keyed on the *dev pack*, missed the methodology pack) · the backstop's false-refusal class (swept *one member of nine*) · the `finalize.*` census (keyed on the *file* `finalize.rs`, missed two CLI members) · and now this (keyed on the *five clusters someone listed*, missed two more). **The pattern is not carelessness; it is structural.** A census is a claim about a set, checked by a human who has to remember to re-check it — and it rots the moment the set grows. **The fix is not "sweep harder." It is to replace the census with a predicate a test can enforce.** That is what this settles, and it is the most valuable thing to come out of the increment.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 build halt at Increment 9: the `task-discard` ack carries no effect key

**The build refused to proceed, and it was right.** Increments 1–8 landed clean (1865 tests / 0 failed). Inc 9's planner then **halted rather than build against the design of record** — because the design of record was **false**.

[command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) §2 pinned a `discarded` effect key on the `task-discard` ack, valued `false` *"on the idempotent already-absent no-op (`task.rs:257-266` — an absent area is not an error)."* The planner ran the binary: **`jigc task discard <absent-id>` exits 1.** `TaskArea::resolve` (`task.rs:374-390`) bails **before** `run_discard`'s `if task.dir.exists()` guard ever runs — so **that guard is dead code, and `run_discard`'s own doc comment claiming idempotence is a lie.** The design pass read the comment, trusted it, and pinned a contract on it. **`discarded` was unreachable-as-`false` and could only ever hold the constant `true` — a dead key, one increment from a 1.0 freeze.**

**Settled: drop `discarded`; keep discard's absent-case bail.** The ack is `{"op": "task-discard", "task": "<id>", "findings": []}`. Engaging the rationale rather than overruling it: the key existed so *"removed"* and *"was already gone"* would stop being indistinguishable — **but they never were.** Exit 0 + the ack says removed; exit 1 + the error envelope says it was already gone. **The distinction it wanted already exists, one layer up.** And the alternative — making the key reachable by making discard idempotent — would have been **worse than a dead key**: an idempotent discard exits 0 on *any* absent id, **including a milestone id**, which `milestone_finalize_base_guard.rs:266-275` asserts must **fail** and which **Increment 7's unit-aware route fix is justified by**. It would have converted an honest dead end into a **lying route** — the exact disease this wave's headline claim exists to cure. *(The lying doc comment is corrected in the same increment. A false comment authorizes the next wrong pin — that is how this one happened.)*

**And the planner found the fifth un-enumerated sibling of the wave.** The design pass enumerated the `finalize.*` family by grepping **`crates/engine/src/finalize.rs`** and reported nine codes. **Two more live in the CLI** (`finalize.nothing-staged`, `finalize.stage-failed` — `cli/task.rs:1640`, `:1654`), emit no location, and sat in **no row** of the pinned normalization table. **The census was scoped to a *file* when the family is scoped to a *concept*.** That is the same shape as the `schema.location` census (scoped to `location`, missed `prior.location`) and the pack-prose census (scoped to the dev pack, missed the methodology pack). **Three for three, so the rule is now explicit: a census keyed on where you expect the members to live will miss the ones that live somewhere else. Key it on what the members *are*.**

**The methodology point, which is the reason to keep this entry:** every prior catch in M42 came from a *reviewer*. This one came from **the builder refusing to build**. The increment planner had a filled gate-record, a pinned contract, and an approved scope — and it still ran the binary, found the premise false, and stopped instead of shipping a contract it could not honour. **That is the loop working as designed**, and it is the strongest evidence yet that the halt-on-a-genuine-fork rule earns its cost.
