Posture, declared now rather than calcified later (the M41 one-way-door lesson): an **index/identity projection**, so it rides `doc show`'s posture — one pinned shape, **no in-band version integer**, additive keys pre-1.0 only, golden-pinned at ship. Shape pinned here to keep the executor from minting a de-facto contract: `--format json` → `{"docs":[{"id":"<type>:<slug>","path":"<repo-relative>","state":"managed"|"unregistered"}]}` — an object wrapper (a bare top-level array can never take an additive key), `type`/`slug` omitted as derivable from `id` by the address grammar the driver already parses; plain → one line per doc, `<id>  <path>  <state>`, sorted by (type, slug). *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli --test doc_list` through the real binary — a repo with a committed `adr` + a **foreign** root `CHANGELOG.md` lists the adr `managed` and `changelog:changelog` **`unregistered`** (the squatter is surfaced, not hidden — hiding it sends the agent to `cat`); `doc list adr` filters; an unknown doctype blocks `store.unknown-type` routed at `jigc describe`; the `--format json` shape is golden-pinned (the `doc_schema.rs` mold); transient doctypes yield no rows; full gate. *Red today:* `unrecognized subcommand 'list'`, exit 2. *(files: `crates/cli/src/{cli.rs,doc.rs}`, `crates/engine/src/validate.rs` (visibility), `crates/cli/tests/doc_list.rs`.)*
- **T7 — `doc show`'s block on an unregistered instance routes to adoption, not hand-repair.** With T6 shipped, three surfaces would otherwise tell three stories about one file: `doc list` says *unregistered*, `validate` says *foreign — adopt it* (verified live: `schema-conformance.unadopted-instance`, routed at `jigc ingest` / `jigc migrate <path> --as <doctype>`), and `doc show` says *"fix the committed file so it conforms to its schema"* (`store.rs:186-192`) — true of a **corrupted managed** doc, a lie about a **never-adopted foreign** one, in the wave whose whole claim is that the tool's own routes tell the truth. The read verb's `store.unparseable` route **splits on the same discriminator** (T6's `is_unadopted_foreign`, at the `doc show` boundary where the versions/priors maps are in hand — the engine's `read_slice` signature and the compose-deref path are untouched: the design scopes this to the read verb). *Done:* real-binary — a stock brownfield repo with a foreign Keep-a-Changelog root `CHANGELOG.md` + `jigc setup`: `doc show changelog:changelog` blocks with a route naming `jigc ingest` / `jigc migrate CHANGELOG.md --as changelog` (matching validate's route verbatim in intent), while a **stamped-but-corrupt** managed doc still blocks with the repair route (the split is real, not a blanket swap); `doc list`, `doc show`, `validate` now tell **one** story on that file; full gate. *Red today:* both cases get the repair route (verified live). *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/managed_vs_foreign.rs`.)*

**Why this order:** the read *grammar* first (T1 → T2: the leaf, then the section it lives in — each closes one wrong-node-exit-0 and neither can be split across the engine/CLI seam without shipping a silent wrong answer at exit 0), then *identity* (T3 → T4: the json key and the plain anchor — the same fact in the two surfaces, sequenced json-first because Inc 10's slug-rule change is explicitly sequenced behind the item-`id` projection), then *ergonomics* (T5, independent), then the *new surface* (T6 → T7: the verb promotes the shared discriminator, and the show-route split consumes it — shipping T7 first would repair a route nothing yet contradicts). Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 42 → Increment 8. **Status: planned; hand off to task execution.**

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Inc-8 T7: `doc show`'s block on a foreign squatter routes at adoption — the third surface joins the one story

A stock brownfield repo's own Keep-a-Changelog `CHANGELOG.md` squats at the `changelog` placement home, and until now `jigc doc show changelog:changelog` blocked `store.unparseable` routed *"fix the committed file so it conforms to its schema"* — hand-repair advice about a file jigc never wrote — while `doc list` (T6) already called it `unregistered` and `jigc validate` already called it *foreign — adopt it*. Three surfaces, three stories about one file, in the wave whose whole claim is that the tool's own routes tell the truth. The read verb's route now splits on the **one** discriminator (`engine::validate::is_unadopted_foreign`) and the three tell one story ([doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) → `jigc doc list`, third bullet).

**Three elaborations worth pinning.** (i) **The *route* splits; the code and the message do not.** `store.unparseable` stays the code (no new id, no inventory row) and the parse complaint stays true of both arms — what was false was only the repair direction, so only it moves. (ii) **The route is single-sourced, not re-worded:** `engine::validate::adoption_route` is factored out of the store sweep's `unadopted_instance` advisory and made `pub`, so `doc show` emits the **same bytes** `validate` does (`jigc ingest` / `jigc migrate <path> --as <ty>`, the M40 two-tier rule intact — the doctype-directed verb only when its `migrate-<ty>` workflow ships). A hand-written second copy would drift, which is exactly the defect being fixed. (iii) **It sits at the verb boundary, and the split is real, not a blanket swap:** the discriminator's inputs (the manifest versions + the shipped prior shapes) are CLI-side, so `engine::store::read_slice`'s signature and the compose-deref path are untouched — this is the read *verb*'s route, not a new engine judgement. A **stamped-but-corrupt managed** doc keeps the hand-repair route (asserted, not assumed): routing jigc's own broken ADR at `jigc migrate` would be the mirror-image lie.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Inc-8 T6: `jigc doc list` ships — one discriminator for the state, and the posture declared in the same commit as the shape

`jigc doc list [<doctype>]` — the **fourth read surface** ([doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) → the fourth read surface): the committed store projected **by identity**, each row `<id>  <path>  <state>`, `--format json` → `{"docs":[{id, path, state}]}`, golden-pinned at ship (`crates/cli/tests/doc_list.rs`). Nothing answered *"which docs exist"* before it, so an agent's only route to the corpus was to guess a slug or `cat` the store — the raw read the adapter rule forbids.

**Three elaborations worth pinning.** (i) **The registration state is *one* rule, promoted — never a second one:** the rows come from `engine::index::committed_instances` (already the census's shared placement-aware enumerator) and each state is adjudicated by `engine::validate::is_unadopted_foreign` (promoted `pub(crate)` → `pub`, fed the CLI's existing `pack::frozen_doctype_versions` + `pack::prior_doctype_schemas`) — so `doc list` says *unregistered* exactly where `validate` says *foreign — adopt it*. A second copy of either would be a second story about one file, in the wave whose whole claim is that the tool's routes tell the truth. (ii) **The posture is declared as it ships** (the M41 one-way-door lesson — an undeclared output calcifies into a de-facto contract): an **index/identity** projection, not a content read, so it rides `doc show`'s posture — one pinned shape, **no in-band version integer**, additive keys pre-1.0 only; the json is an **object wrapper** because a bare top-level array can never take that additive key, and `type`/`slug` are omitted as derivable from `id`. (iii) **An unreadable committed doc is an error, not an omitted row** — the store *sweep* skips one (`continue`: a read race, re-checked next sweep), but a *listing* whose contract is "the store surface" must be complete, so the read failure surfaces as an operational error rather than a silently short list.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Inc-8 T5: the bare singleton expands at the *verb boundary*, and the singleton set is the **placement** set

`jigc doc show changelog` (and `vision`, and `changelog#releases`, and a bare singleton on a **write** verb) now resolves identically to its `<type>:<type>` spelling — the M41 V12 discoverability repair, which reached `rename` only, completed across the `doc` verbs; a bare **non**-singleton still errors, now naming the `<type>:<slug>` form and the `jigc describe` pointer instead of a bare grammar complaint.

**Two elaborations worth pinning.** (i) **The predicate is `placement`, not `singleton: true`** — the two flags are extensionally identical today (all five singletons are placement doctypes), but *placement* is the property that makes the bare form **unambiguous**: a placement doctype's home is one literal file and its slug is fixed to the type id by construction, which is exactly what `engine::store::read_slice` already enforces (it refuses every *other* slug for one). A future folder-homed singleton would not carry that guarantee, so the expansion keys on the guarantee, not on the convention. (ii) **The expansion lives at the verb boundary, not in the grammar** — `engine::address::Address::parse` is untouched (the address grammar is not widened, so nothing else in the system has to learn a second address shape); the CLI gains `parse_verb_addr`, the schema-aware wrapper used at the seven places a human or agent *types* an address, while `parse_addr` stays the pure parse for the addresses the CLI itself composes (already `<type>:<slug>`-headed). Expansion is a convenience of the typing surface; the stored/emitted address form is unchanged.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Inc-8 T2: the fields-only section slice is a canonical re-emit through the *writer's* emitters — one field format, not two

`jigc doc show 'adr:<slug>#status'` served the **empty string at exit 0** over a header carrying `status`/`date`/`schema-version` — the **wrong-node-exit-0** [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) forbids by name (`slice_fragment`'s section-level arm fell through to `render_items` over a section that holds none). It now serves the section's fields: `--format json` → the leaves keyed by leaf id, shaped exactly as the whole-doc `fields` project them (the milestone-record witness's compound `base` pin included); plain → the field lines the writer renders.

**The elaboration worth pinning: the slice is rendered *from the parse*, through `write`'s own emitters** — `emit_bare_fields` for a **header** group (the bare front-matter form), `append_field_group` for a **body** group (the `<!-- fields -->`-sentinelled bullets); both promoted to `pub(crate)` rather than re-implemented. A `ParsedSection` carries no field-group span, so a byte slice was never available here — and a second field format in the reader is exactly the drift the one-writer rule exists to prevent. This is the concrete instance of the retired *"byte-exact … verbatim"* claim: the plain path promises the **canonical render of the addressed node**, and for this node the canonical render *is* the writer's. The whole-doc rule is untouched (verified by regression): a fields-only section still contributes to `fields` **alone** and gains no `sections` entry — a slice is a projection of the addressed node, not a relocation of it.

## 2026-07-14 — M42 Inc-8 T1: the read path stops rejecting an address the tool itself emits — and a section's leaves are exactly its fields

`jigc doc show 'adr:<slug>#status/status'` resolves — the grammar's `unit/leaf` depth on a **non-repeatable** section ([structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md) → Addressing: *"one grammar, every reference"*; [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) → The slice grammar). Not an additive contract revision: a defect fix. `validate` **emits** `#<section>/<field>` targets and `doc set-field` **accepts** the same string at exit 0, while the read path answered `blocking · store.no-such-item` — the tool blocked on an address it hands out. `slice_fragment` gains a `SectionBody::Simple` arm; engine + CLI json ship as **one** commit because the engine branch alone would convert an honest block into a json **wrong-node-exit-0** (`fragment_json`'s Simple arm returned the slot string — `""` for a header), the exact class this wave closes.

**The elaboration worth pinning: a simple section's addressable leaves are exactly its declared *fields*.** Its prose slot *is* the section (`#<section>`), and the parser records no sub-labelled section slots — so `resolve_section_leaf` reads the parsed field group and nothing else. Consequence, deliberate and consistent with the item-leaf precedent: an **optional field the committed doc does not carry** (an unset `supersedes`) blocks `store.no-such-leaf` rather than projecting a `null` the pinned json contract has no shape for — the doc answers for the leaves it *holds*, and the fields-only section slice (T2) is where a driver sees which of them are filled. Honest error or correct answer, never a wrong node at exit 0.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Increment 7 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 7](implementation/roadmap.md) (fork 3 — `jigc milestone discard`; [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The lifecycle / `jigc milestone discard` / What the base-guard is for / The record is not writable through the `jigc doc` verbs, [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → Abandoning a milestone, [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → the `EnumWidened` kind) into **6 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `9e725f4` (tree clean; Inc 1–6 landed — the freeze assert now fires in `make_pack()`, so this increment's frozen bump is gated at **every** door, and `milestone discard` is the new committing write verb Inc 6 was sequenced to protect). The four grouped-scope bullets map: **the frozen bump + migration** → T1; **the base-guard widening + the unit-aware route** → T2 + T3 (separable — the widening is a CLI range predicate, the route an engine finding shape; neither breaks the other's gate); **the verb + its guards + teardown** → T4 + T5 (the engine's in-place flip primitive, then the CLI verb that drives it); **the record write-refusal** → T6. No design-doc task: `team-ready-state.md` §§ *The lifecycle* / *What the base-guard is for* / *The record is not writable* and `write-commands.md` → *Abandoning a milestone* are **already written** (landed with the Settle, verified at HEAD); the wave-wide fold-back + acceptance flow 43 ride Inc 12.

- **T1 — `milestone-record` schema-version 2: the enum widens, and the corpus migrates.** `status` widens to `[active, joined, discarded]` at **both** loci (`packs/methodology/schemas/milestone-record.yaml:41` header, `:48` `tasks` item block) + the net-new `packs/methodology/schema-snapshots/milestone-record.v1.yaml` (the `deferral-ledger.v1.yaml` mold — a full prior-shape snapshot, never a migration recipe) + the manifest bump (`schema-version: 2` + the recomputed `schema-hash`). **One atomic gate-green unit**: the schema edit alone trips the pack-load freeze assert *and* flips `render_fresh_record`'s stamp (the value is read from the manifest — `milestone.rs:219`), so the manifest/snapshot/goldens repair what the edit breaks, in the same motion. *Done:* through the **real binary** on a `[dev ▸ methodology]` repo — a committed `schema-version: 1` `docs/milestone-records/<id>.md` migrates under `jigc migrate-corpus`: **1 migrated**, every byte identical except the stamp `1`→`2` (the widening is a byte no-op — verified: `diff_leaf` is shared by both loci, `schema_diff.rs:658` fields + `:743` item fields, and `new.of ⊇ old.of` → `EnumWidened`, `transform.rs:214` → zero bytes); a fresh `jigc milestone create` mints `schema-version: 2`; the freeze assert stays green at every door. Full gate. *(files: `packs/methodology/{schemas/milestone-record.yaml,schema-snapshots/milestone-record.v1.yaml,config/schema-manifest.yaml}`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_create.rs` + any stamp/enum goldens the bump reddens.)*
- **T2 — the base-guard accepts *any* milestone's record path.** `record_only_range` (`crates/cli/src/milestone.rs:445-495`) today requires every path touched in `base..HEAD` to equal **this** milestone's record path, so a second milestone's **record-only bookkeeping** (`create`/`add-task` — commits that move no code) wedges the first, and interleaved creation deadlocks **both**, unrecoverably (even `git revert` fails). Another milestone's record is **not code**, so it cannot invalidate the M31 worktree-combine: the predicate widens to *every touched path is a milestone-record path* — resolved from the record doctype's cascade-resolved `location` prefix (`docs/milestone-records/`), not the single `<id>.md`. **Load-bearing for T5**: a `discard` commit touches its own record path, which sits *foreign* in another milestone's range, so discard cannot clear even a bookkeeping wedge without this. *Done:* `cargo test -p cli --test milestone_finalize_base_guard` — a new arm interleaving A create → B create → A add-task → B add-task, then finalizing **both**: neither blocks on `base-mismatch` (red today: symmetric deadlock, both exit 3), while the existing foreign-**code**-path arm still blocks (external drift stays caught). Full gate. *(files: `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone_finalize_base_guard.rs`.)*
- **T3 — the `finalize.base-mismatch` route becomes unit-aware, and stops offering `discard` as the exit.** `base_mismatch_finding` (`crates/engine/src/finalize.rs:738-751`) is shared by `plan_finalize` (task) and `plan_milestone_finalize` (milestone) and routes *"discard the task with `jigc task discard`"* — which on a milestone id returns `no task '<id>'`, exit 1: a dead end that calls a milestone "the task". It takes the unit kind; the **milestone** arm **names the cause** (commits landed after the base, so the sub-task worktrees were cut from a base HEAD no longer reflects and the combine cannot be proven sound) and **names the two real options** (land the milestone first, or re-cut onto the new base — both honestly labelled out-of-band git; there is no `milestone rebase` at M42), **never `discard`**. The task arm is byte-unchanged. *Done:* an integration arm — a milestone base-mismatched by a **landed code commit** blocks with a route naming the milestone (not "the task"), naming both options, and containing **no `jigc task discard`** and no `discard`-as-exit (red today: the task route verbatim); the existing task-finalize base-mismatch route tests stay green. Full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/finalize.rs`, `crates/cli/src/milestone.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone_finalize_base_guard.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/flow33_acceptance.rs` if the milestone message text moves.)*
- **T4 — the engine's in-place flip to `discarded`: a joined sub-task stays joined.** `engine::milestone::discard_record` + its pure inner flip, the `join_record`/`flip_record_status_to_joined` sibling (`crates/engine/src/milestone.rs:803-860`) with **one** semantic difference: it is **per-item conditional** — every item whose committed `status` is **not** `joined` flips to `discarded`, a genuinely-**joined** item is left byte-untouched (it really did land; flipping it would make the record lie about landed work), and the header flips to `discarded`. Reads each item's committed `status` from `ParsedItem.fields` (the record is its own source of truth), splices through the same byte-stable item-leaf path. *Done:* engine unit tests — a record with items `[joined, active]` flips to header `discarded` + item2 `discarded` with item1's bytes **identical** (red today: no such function, and `joined`'s unconditional loop would flip both); an all-`joined` record flips the header alone; `render(parse(out)) == out` (byte-stability). Full gate. *(files: `crates/engine/src/milestone.rs`.)*
- **T5 — `jigc milestone discard <id> [--force]`: the verb, the WIP guard, the teardown.** The family's missing terminal verb (`create`/`add-task`/`add-from-spec`/`execute`/`join`/`finalize` + `discard`). Order: reconcile preflight (the `set: on-transition` no-silent-overwrite discipline — `reconcile_record_preflight`) → **dirty-worktree guard** → T4's flip → `commit_record_only` (`chore(milestone): discard record …`) → teardown. **The guard is a property, not a note:** `remove_worktrees` runs `git worktree remove --force` unconditionally — safe at *finalize* (the commit lands first), and on the abandon path the work is **by definition uncommitted**, so the same call destroys it silently at exit 0. Discard **refuses** when any registered sub-task worktree is dirty, naming the paths, unless `--force`. The probe must be broader than the one that exists: `worktrees_have_staged_code` (`milestone.rs:968`) reads `git diff --cached` only — the guard needs `git status --porcelain` (staged ∪ unstaged ∪ **untracked**). **Teardown** removes the sub-task areas, the registered worktrees, **and `.jigc/milestones/<id>/`** — which has no reachable remover today (the milestone area is cleaned only by the landed-finalize executor). *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli --test milestone_discard` through the real binary: (a) a file written into a provisioned sub-task worktree → `discard` **refuses**, exit non-zero, names the path, record + worktree + file **intact** (red today: gone at exit 0, no warning); (b) `--force` → exit 0, the committed record's header `status: discarded`, a joined item still `joined`, an active item `discarded`, exactly **one** record-only commit (unrelated staged/untracked WIP untouched), and `.jigc/milestones/<id>/` + the sub-task areas + the registered worktrees all **gone**; (c) an unknown milestone id → a routed block, nothing removed. Full gate. *(files: `crates/cli/src/{cli.rs,milestone.rs}`, `crates/cli/tests/milestone_discard.rs`.)*
- **T6 — the committed record stops being writable through the `jigc doc` write verbs (A18).** `jigc doc set-field milestone-record:<id>#status --value joined` with **no `--task`** exits **0** today: it silently auto-selects the sole live task, copies the committed record into that task's area, and stages it to promote — a machine-owned record mutated by a verb that never consults milestone state, past a preflight that does not see this path. Every leaf of the doctype is `set:`-bearing (no author-owned prose slot, no author-required field), so **a doctype with no author-owned leaf has no legitimate `jigc doc` write**: the write verbs refuse a `milestone-record` target — `create` · `author` · `set-field` (incl. `--unset`) · `set-slot` · `add-item` · `remove-item` (`retitle-item` **already** refuses, `doc.rs:1091-1122`; **`reorder` is not a shipped verb** — the design's enumeration lists it, `cli.rs` has no such subcommand, and it is not invented here). One shared guard, keyed on the doctype like its siblings, before any bytes are read or copied in; code `write.machine-maintained`, route → the milestone verbs. The **read** verbs (`doc show`/`doc schema`) stay open and unchanged — that uniformity is why the record is a doctype at all. *Done:* a new `cargo test -p cli --test doc_write_milestone_record` — each of the six verbs on a `milestone-record` target exits non-zero with `write.machine-maintained` + the milestone-verb route, the committed record **byte-identical** and **no** staged copy in the task area (red today: `set-field` exits 0 and stages a mutated record); `doc show` + `doc schema` on the same record still exit 0. Full gate. *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/doc_write_milestone_record.rs`.)*

**Why this order:** T1 first because nothing can flip to a member that does not exist (the enum is closed and its members are inside the frozen `schema-hash` — the charter's *"the write primitives exist, it's a wiring job"* was false in exactly this way); T2 before T5 because discard's own record commit is a foreign record path in a concurrent milestone's range, so the verb cannot clear even a bookkeeping wedge without the widening (they ship together, per the design); T3 stands alone (the route is the defect, the constraint underneath it is **real** and routes rather than resolves); T4 before T5 (primitive, then the verb that drives it); T6 last (independent, and the one guard that needs none of the above). **Not built, deliberately:** the chartered *"active record with no live workbench"* store advisory — [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md)`:55` designs that exact state as the **fresh-clone continuation** case, so it would fire on every in-flight milestone, every clone, every CI checkout; abandoned-vs-clone-continuable is not locally observable from the committed store, and the terminal status is what makes it observable. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 42 → Increment 7. **Status: planned; hand off to task execution.**

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-7 T6: a doctype with no author-owned leaf has no legitimate `jigc doc` write — and `create`'s old refusal was a *knob*, not a rule

The six `jigc doc` **write** verbs (`create` · `author` · `set-field` incl. `--unset` · `set-slot` · `add-item` · `remove-item`) now refuse a `milestone-record` target with the blocking `write.machine-maintained` its already-shipped siblings use (`jigc rename`'s reslug refusal, `jigc doc retitle-item`'s item refusal), routed at the milestone verbs ([team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The record is not writable through the `jigc doc` verbs). The rule is **derived, not stipulated**: every leaf of the doctype is `set:`-bearing, so there is nothing an author could legitimately write — the un-enumerated-sibling shape the `schema.location` census already taught us. The **read** verbs stay open, which is the whole reason the record is a doctype and not a raw-JSON island.

Two things the build exposed. **(a) The verb that looked safest was the loudest hole.** `doc create milestone-record` did refuse today — but with `create.gate-blocked`, whose route reads *"to loosen, add `milestone-record` to `allows-create` in project config"*: the refusal was a **permission knob any project could turn off**, not a property of the doctype. Keying the guard on the doctype puts the rule where it cannot be configured away. **(b) The guard's *position* is half the fix.** It fires before `read_or_copy_in`, because the staging **is** the defect: the red `jigc doc set-field milestone-record:<id>#status --value joined` with **no `--task`** exits 0 by silently auto-selecting the sole live task (a milestone sub-task), copying the committed record into that area and staging it to promote at *that sub-task's* finalize — the machine-owned record mutated by a verb that never consults milestone state, and destined to land under a commit that has nothing to do with the milestone. A guard placed after the copy-in would refuse the write and still leave the staged bomb behind. `reorder` is **not** invented (the design enumerates it; `cli.rs` has no such subcommand).

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-7 T1: `milestone-record` v2 — the widening is the *cheapest* frozen bump there is, and that is the point

`milestone-record` is **schema-version 2**: `status` widens to `[active, joined, discarded]` at **both** loci — the `meta` header and the `tasks` item block ([team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The lifecycle — active / joined / discarded). The abandon path had no terminal value to flip to, so a thrown-away milestone's committed record read `active` forever — *the repo is the record*, lying. The fix is a **schema member**, not a detector: abandoned-vs-clone-continuable is not locally observable from the store (an active record with no workbench is the designed **fresh-clone continuation** case), so only a terminal status makes it observable.

The bump ships as one atomic unit because the schema edit alone breaks two things at once — the pack-load freeze assert (M40 A1 froze the methodology manifest; since Inc 6 it fires in `make_pack()`, so *every* door) and `render_fresh_record`'s stamp (read from the manifest), which is exactly the gate working: **the manifest bump + the net-new `schema-snapshots/milestone-record.v1.yaml` + the reddened stamp goldens repair what the edit breaks, in the same motion.** The snapshot is a full prior-shape file (the `deferral-ledger.v1.yaml` mold), never a hand-written recipe — the determinism boundary in its strongest form: the engine diffs two genuine declared schemas and classifies exactly `[EnumWidened{meta/status}, EnumWidened{tasks/status}]` (Inc 5's kind, shared `diff_leaf` at both loci), which folds to **zero bytes**. So the corpus migration moves the stamp and nothing else — proven on the real binary over a committed v1 record carrying **both** a `joined` and an `active` item: `1 migrated`, byte-identical but `schema-version: 1`→`2`, `joined` still `joined`. **The contrast with the sibling is the record worth keeping:** the same doctype family's other v1→v2 (M41 F4's `deferral-ledger` D/I → Decision/Idea) was a *rename* — semantically unrecoverable from the schema pair, so it needed an authored map. A **widening** is recoverable by construction (`new.of ⊇ old.of`: every committed value is still a member and still means what it meant), so the freeze charges its true price here and no more.

- **T2 — the idempotency guard generalizes to every heading-minting kind (the live `adr` strand).** `per_doc_changes`' `_ => true` becomes an **exhaustive** match: every heading-minting kind (`AddedOptionalSection` · `ProseNeeding` · `AddedRepeatableSection` from T6) is dropped iff the doc already carries that `## Heading`; every other kind is kept (the `schema-version` stamp filter preserved). Exhaustive **on purpose** — it forces every later kind in this increment to decide whether it mints a heading, which is the un-enumerated-sibling failure mechanized. *Done:* through the **real binary** on the **embedded** pack (`flow38_adr_options.rs`) — a committed v1-stamped ADR that **already carries `## Options`** migrates: `1 migrated`, exactly one `## Options`, stamp `2`, every prior byte preserved. *(Red today: permanently stranded — verified mechanism below.)*

CLI — the narrowing blocks with a route.

The tighten writes **zero bytes**: the section/field already exists, so T2's guard drops the change and the **shipped per-doc conformance gate** adjudicates — a doc carrying the prose/value migrates and restamps; one that legitimately lacks it **blocks** with the prose route. *Done:* engine — `false→true` is `[OptionalRelaxed]`, folds byte-identical (red: `[]`); `true→false` on an author-required leaf is `[ProseNeeding]` (red: `[]`); on a defaulted field it is the no-op kind. **Why this cut:** T1 closes the **class** first, so from its commit on every unbuilt shape **refuses loudly** instead of stranding — which makes T3–T7 each a clean red→green (*a refusal becomes a classified migration*), and T2 lands the exhaustive guard **before** the one new heading-minting kind exists, so T6 cannot forget to declare itself.

**Verified bases (probed against the real classifier/writer at `db184ab` — not assumed):**

- **All six holes reproduced live.** Diffing real `Schema` pairs through `engine::schema_diff::schema_diff`: a **hint reword** → `[]` · **`default:` add** → `[]` · **`optional` false→true** → `[]` · **`optional` true→false** → `[]` · **removed field** → `[]` · **removed section** → `[]` · **added repeatable section** → `[]` · **added item field** → `[]`. Enum **widening** → `[ValueRemapped{map:{}}]` (blocks with nothing to author). Cardinality, **both directions**: simple locus → `[WidenedCardinality]` *regardless of direction* (a narrowing silently no-ops); item locus → `[]` *in both directions* (so the matrix's ✅ for an item-block card **widen** is a promise the classifier never honoured). Every one of these is a hash-moving change that today stamp-bumps and strands.
- **The `adr` stranding mechanism is `AlreadyPresent`, not a duplicate splice.** The design says the driver *"re-splices a duplicate `## Heading`"*; it does not — `write::generate_section` **rejects** a section already present (`GenerateError::AlreadyPresent`, `write.rs:2587-2591`, reproduced), so the doc halts and collects the **dead-end** `prose_needing_route` (*"author the new required prose … then re-run"* — for a section that is optional and already authored). Same strand, different mechanism; T2's red test must assert the *blocked* outcome, not a duplicated heading.
- **`generate_section` mints a byte-stable, conformant, zero-item repeatable section** (T6's reuse claim — *probed*, not asserted): fed a repeatable section id, it splices `## Heading` at the schema-ordered offset, the result round-trips `render(parse(x)) == x`, parses to **0 items**, and raises **0** conformance findings. The `AddedRepeatableSection` driver is therefore the existing block-insert, with no new primitive.
- **`set_item_field` cannot do T7's job; `set_item_field_or_insert` can.** `set_item_field` is **update-only** — `SpliceError::NotPresent` when the field bullet is absent from the item (`write.rs:1382-1386`), i.e. on **every item, by definition of the kind**. `set_item_field_or_insert` (`write.rs:3186-3216`) splices-or-inserts and **type-adjudicates the value before touching bytes**. (`ValueRemapped` genuinely does drive `set_item_field` — it overwrites an **existing** bullet — which is why the wrong cite looked true.)
- **The narrowing pick rests on a measured fact: nothing enforces a `card` bound anywhere.** `schema_conformance` → `check_field` → `write::check_value` (`write.rs:4839`) type-checks **each scalar** and never counts them; the only cardinality surface in `validate.rs` is family 5's `inverse-cardinality` store **advisory**. So the design's *"validate every committed instance against the new bound"* arm is **net-new validation surface** (a new finding code + knob + inventory row + store sweep) — squarely outside this increment. `NarrowedCardinality` therefore **refuses**, which is strictly better than today's silent no-op past the gate, and the door to the validating arm stays open.
- **The backstop cannot fire on a shipped pair — T1 is gate-green standalone.** All three shipped snapshots diff **non-empty** against their current schemas: `changelog.v1` → `[Relocated, DisplayTitleChanged]`, `deferral-ledger.v1` → `[ValueRemapped]`, `adr.v1` → `[AddedOptionalSection]` (pinned by `flow38_adr_options.rs`). No shipped migration is refused, and none newly emits `PresentationOnly` (that kind fires only when nothing else classifies).
- **The blast radius of a new kind is exactly three files.** `SchemaChange` is matched **only** in `schema_diff.rs`, `transform.rs` (exhaustive — a new variant forces its driver arm in the same commit) and `migrate_corpus.rs`. So each kind task is one atomic gate-green unit; nothing outside the migration path sees the enum.
- **A tighten must not mint.** `ProseNeeding`'s driver *mints an empty section* (`transform.rs:178-191`) — correct for a **new** required section, fatal for a **tightened** existing one (`AlreadyPresent` would hard-block even the docs that carry the prose). T2's guard already drops a `ProseNeeding` whose heading is present, which is what makes T4's tighten a pure gate-adjudicated change — so T4 **depends** on T2, and its acceptance must include a doc that *does* carry the prose and migrates clean.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-5 T7: `AddedItemField` — the three arms — and the insert primitive *was* byte-unstable on a non-trailing item

A field added to a **repeatable item block** now classifies **`AddedItemField`** — the locus where the work-doc family's content actually lives (9 of 14 persisted doctypes carry a repeatable; pre-T7 the item loop classified only *existing* leaves, so an added one diffed to `[]`: an optional one "migrated by accident" — the stamp flipped and the declared `default:` never landed — and a required one was a **permanent mutual dead end**). Its three arms **mirror `classify_added_field`** through one shared `placeable_without_prose` predicate, so the two loci cannot drift (two loops disagreeing is what produced the M42 holes): **`default:`/`set:`** → the value is spliced into every item, through **`write::set_item_field_or_insert`**, the **insert-capable** primitive (`set_item_field` is *update-only* and refuses an absent bullet — i.e. every item, by definition of this kind; it is the right primitive only for `ValueRemapped`, which overwrites an *existing* one) · **optional, no default** → **classified, zero bytes**: an item without the bullet already conforms, and inventing an empty one would fabricate a value · **required, no default** → **`ProseNeeding { leaf: Some }`**, and — T2's guard dropping the mint, since the section heading is already there — the **per-doc conformance gate** is the adjudicator, so the doc blocks with the *prose-authoring* route, not the backstop's *build-the-kind* one (the discriminating assertion: pre-T7 it blocked too, but with a schema-authoring route nobody could act on).

**Elaboration — a per-item idempotency skip, and why it is not the whole-change filter.** An item that **already carries** the bullet is **skipped, never overwritten** (an adopter who hand-authored `kind: Idea` ahead of the bump keeps it): overwriting an authored value with the default is a **No-data-loss** breach, and the skip is what makes the fold **idempotent**. It has to live in the driver, not in `per_doc_changes`: one doc can hold items of *both* kinds, which a whole-change filter cannot express.

**The defect the red found: `write::insert_after_line` broke byte-stability on a *non-trailing* group — live on the shipped `doc set-field` insert half, at BOTH loci.** It landed the new bullet at the **list block's end**, which for a non-trailing group runs *past* the last bullet's newline, over the blank line separating the group from the following `##`/`###` heading — emitting `- a\n\n- b\n### Next`: a doc that re-parses fine and **fails `render(parse(x)) == x`**, the retired #1-risk invariant. Both insert callers were affected (`insert_field` for a simple section's group, `insert_item_field` for an item's), i.e. any `jigc doc set-field` writing a **second** bullet onto a non-last item/section — not only the migration. Fixed at the shared landing offset (retreat over the trailing blank to just past the last content line) and pinned by a regression at **each** caller. It survived because every prior fixture inserted into a *trailing* item/section or a *mint-empty* item (the re-render branch): the **exact T6 shape**, one task later — a byte-fragility invisible to precisely the tests we would rely on to catch it, which is why the fixtures here are non-trailing by construction.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-5 T6: a wholly-new repeatable section mints its empty heading — and the block-insert *was* shape-blind

A section only `v2` declares whose body is a **repeatable** item block now classifies **`AddedRepeatableSection`** (pre-T6 it classified *nothing* — `added_section` handled only the simple-slot cases and closed with the fact in its own comment — so it rode the T1 backstop's residual and the migration **refused**: a doctype could not grow a repeatable section at all). The driver mints the empty `## Heading` at its schema-ordered offset and stops: a **zero-item repeatable conforms** (`repeatable-populated` is a store *advisory*, never a conformance break — [validation.md](design/validation.md)), so this is the migration's final byte-stable form, not a mint-then-author handoff, and the CLI invents **no items**. It joins T2's heading-minting guard (the exhaustive `per_doc_changes` match forced the declaration), so a doc that already carries the section migrates clean instead of stranding on `AlreadyPresent`.

**The recorded rationale was a claim, and it was half true — the elaboration.** The planning note said the existing block-insert suffices, *verified by probe* (round-trips, parses to 0 items, 0 findings) — **no new primitive**. The primitive is indeed the right one, but its rendered block was **shape-blind**: `write::render_generated_section` (its only caller is `generate_section`, whose only production callers are the transform's three mint arms) rendered *every* section as a **simple** body — heading + empty prose + field group — which over-pads a repeatable's zero-item home by **one newline**. The canonical writer's `Repeatable` arm over an empty item list emits no empty-prose terminator, so the spliced doc failed `render(parse(x)) == x` — **in the non-trailing case only**, which is why a probe over a *trailing* section reports clean. The fix is one branch in `render_generated_section` (the `Simple` bytes are unchanged), and the test that caught it is the non-trailing (byte-fragile) fixture — the same reason `AddedOptionalSection`'s fixture is non-trailing.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-5 T5: field removal classifies — and the pick is REFUSE, not strip

A leaf the new schema **drops** now classifies **`RemovedField`** at **both loci** (a simple/header section's fields *and* a repeatable item block's — the two loops iterated `v2`'s leaves and matched back into `v1`, so a dropped leaf was *invisible*), and the driver **refuses** it (`TransformError::Unsupported`; `jigc migrate-corpus` blocks the doc at classification with its own **schema-authoring** route — restore the leaf, or build the strip arm — beside the backstop and the narrowing, and for the same reason: nothing an operator does to *this doc* unblocks it, so the fold's "author the prose, then re-run" would be a lie). The doc's bytes — and the committed value itself — are untouched.

**The pick the design left open** ([corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The two silent-classification holes: *a `RemovedField` kind that strips the field line, or an outright refusal*; **marked open, the increment picks**): **refuse.** **No-data-loss** is a *declared property of this pair* (the property census) and a strip is a knowing exception to it; **no frozen doctype needs a removal** (M42's own bumps *add*; the deferred spec lifecycle *adds*), so building the strip is the premature generality the freeze's minimalism rejects — while the **silent** hole is the actual defect, and refusal closes it at **zero risk**. It is **not a one-way door**: a strip arm with a deliberate data-loss opt-in stays purely additive if a real driver ever appears — which is the *build the kind first* rule this increment mechanizes, applied to itself.

**Why it is a kind and not a backstop ride** (the load-bearing half, easy to miss): the `Unclassified` backstop is a **residual** — it fires only when *nothing* classified. A removal **accompanied** by any classified change (an added optional field, a hint reword) leaves the diff non-empty, so the backstop **never fires** and the removal would be **silently dropped** — the doc migrated and restamped while it still carries a field line the current schema no longer declares. Pinned by the red: pre-T5 that pair diffed to `[AddedOptionalField]` alone. Folded into [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The two silent-classification holes and the [doctype-authoring](implementation/doctype-authoring.md) matrix's *Remove a field* row.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-5 T4: the `optional` flag deltas — a tighten blocks only where the *gate* would

The sixth hole is closed at **both loci and the slot level**: a **relaxation** (`optional: false → true`) classifies the new no-op kind **`OptionalRelaxed`** and folds byte-identical (classify → zero bytes → restamp → ship); a **tightening** (`true → false`) classifies **`ProseNeeding`** and routes the agent (Framing A). The red was **not** the design's stated one, and the difference is worth recording: post-T1 a flag delta no longer strands silently — it fell into the backstop's residual and **every** doc of the doctype was **falsely refused** with the *build the transform kind first* route, the conformant ones included. The backstop turned a silent strand into a loud false refusal, which is exactly the safe direction it was built for.

**The refinement the design's flat rule missed — a tighten is `ProseNeeding` *iff the leaf thereby becomes author-required*.** A slot always does (it carries no value source), but a **field** with `default:`/`set:` (or an optional `ref`, or a pack-declared type) does **not**: `schema_conformance`'s absent-field arm consults `validate::is_author_required`, which exempts exactly those, so **no committed doc can fail** the tightened schema and blocking it would be a **false refusal**. The classifier **calls that predicate** rather than re-deriving it, so the classifier's verdict and the gate's cannot drift; such a tighten classifies the out-of-projection no-op kind and ships.

**A tighten mints nothing** (the T4-depends-on-T2 edge, confirmed live). The change writes **zero bytes**: T2's guard drops a `ProseNeeding` whose heading the doc already carries — minting would hit `generate_section`'s `AlreadyPresent` and hard-block even the conformant docs — so the **shipped per-doc conformance gate** is the sole adjudicator. Acceptance carries both halves over one bump: the brief that **carries** the prose migrates and restamps `1→2`; the brief that legitimately left the optional slot empty is **blocked** with the prose route and its stamp is **not** bumped. Folded into [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The structural projection and the [doctype-authoring](implementation/doctype-authoring.md) matrix's two flag rows.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-5 T3: `card`/`of` classify by direction — and a narrowing is REFUSED

The existing-leaf deltas now read **direction**, through **one** rule applied at **both loci** (a simple/header section's fields *and* a repeatable item block's — pre-M42 the two loops disagreed, which is why `diff_leaf` is shared): **`EnumWidened`** fires iff `new.of ⊇ old.of` — every committed value is still a declared member, so it is a **byte no-op** needing **no authored map** (pre-M42 a widening misclassified as a *rename* and the driver blocked the doc with an empty map — safe, but unusable; the fix **deletes** the identity-map need rather than growing the table). Only a **non-superset** `of:` delta (a rename, a member drop) stays `ValueRemapped`. **`WidenedCardinality`** is restricted to an actual widening (`new.min ≤ old.min ∧ new.max ≥ old.max`, `*` the greatest upper bound) and now fires **inside the item block too** — the matrix's ✅ for an item-block card widen was a promise the classifier never honoured (it emitted nothing).

**The narrowing pick: refuse** (`NarrowedCardinality` → `TransformError::Unsupported`; `jigc migrate-corpus` blocks the doc at classification with its own route, beside the backstop and for the same reason — the fold's "author the prose, then re-run" would be a lie). The design left the call open (*validate every committed instance against the new bound, or refuse*), and the pick rests on a **measured** fact, not a preference: **nothing anywhere counts a committed instance's edges against a `card` bound** (`schema_conformance` → `check_field` → `write::check_value` type-checks each scalar and never counts; `validate.rs`'s only cardinality surface is family 5's `inverse-cardinality` *store advisory*), so the validating arm is a **net-new validation surface** — a finding code + knob + inventory row + store sweep — squarely outside this increment. Refusal is strictly better than the pre-M42 behaviour it replaces (a direction-blind fold to zero bytes that restamped a corpus possibly violating the new bound, **past the gate**), it is **not a one-way door** (the validating arm stays purely additive), and it is exactly the *build the kind first* rule this increment mechanizes, applied to itself. **Elaboration:** direction is read from the **bounds**, so an equal-bounds respelling (`card:` absent — the `"0..1"` default — spelled out) is the **no-op** direction, never a false refusal; a raised *minimum* (`0..*` → `1..*`) narrows; an **unparseable** bound reads as *not* a widening, refusing loudly rather than folding silently. Folded into [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The two silent-classification holes and the [doctype-authoring](implementation/doctype-authoring.md) matrix's *Narrow a card* row.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-5 T2: the idempotency guard generalizes — and the strand's mechanism was *refusal*, not duplication

`per_doc_changes` ([migrate_corpus.rs](crates/cli/src/migrate_corpus.rs)) drops **every heading-minting kind** (`AddedOptionalSection` alongside the already-guarded `ProseNeeding`) when the doc **already carries that `## Heading`**, and the match is now **exhaustive on purpose** — the `_ => true` catch-all is gone, so every kind T3–T7 adds must *declare* whether it mints a heading rather than inheriting the strand. This fixes a defect **live in shipped code**: an adopter who hand-authored `## Options` in an ADR before the v1→v2 bump was **permanently stranded** on rc.5. Acceptance is the real binary on the embedded pack (`flow38_adr_options.rs` → `an_adr_that_already_carries_options_migrates_instead_of_stranding`): `1 migrated`, exactly one `## Options`, stamp `1→2`, and the file differs from its v1 form **only in the stamp digit**.

**The mechanism the design recorded was wrong, and the fix is the same.** [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → *The stranding defect* said the driver *"re-splices a duplicate `## Heading`"*. It does not: `write::generate_section` **refuses** an already-present section (`GenerateError::AlreadyPresent`, `write.rs:2587-2591`), so the doc **halts** and collects the dead-end `prose_needing_route` (*"author the new required prose … then re-run"* — but the section is optional and already authored). Verified against the red, which blocked rather than duplicating; the design prose is corrected in place. The *outcome* the design named — a doc that can never migrate — was right, which is exactly why the wrong mechanism survived unchecked: a rationale nobody re-derives is a claim, not a fact (the 2026-07-11 rule).

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-5 T1: the empty-diff backstop — and the projection is enumerated by its complement

`schema_diff` gains two residual kinds ([corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The empty-diff backstop / The structural projection): **`Unclassified`** — the conformance-relevant projection moved and **no kind classified** ⇒ `transform` refuses (`TransformError::Unclassified`, never a silent fold-to-no-op) and `jigc migrate-corpus` **blocks** the doc at *classification* time (on the **raw** diff, before `per_doc_changes`) with the **build-the-transform-kind-first** route — never the prose-needing route (a lie: there is no prose to author) and never a stamp-bump; and **`PresentationOnly`** — the delta lies wholly outside the projection ⇒ classify → fold to zero bytes → restamp → ship, so a hint typo fix or a `default:` add stays shippable instead of being falsely refused. Both are the **residual**: they fire only when nothing else classified, which is the design's accepted bound (a projection move riding *alongside* a classified kind is not caught — that is why T3–T7 give the six named shapes their own kinds).

**The elaboration: the projection is implemented as its *complement*.** Rather than rebuilding the projection positively (section set + ordering · slot presence + requiredness · field set + requiredness + type incl. a `ref`'s `to:` + `of:` + `card:`), `erase_out_of_projection` clones each schema and **erases the enumerated outside set** (`description` · `usage` · a slot's `hint` · `default` · `set` · `inverse` · `inverse-card` · `check` · `title-names-symbol`, at the simple locus **and** recursively through repeatable/nested item blocks), then compares. Identical observable behaviour over today's schema model — and it makes every key that exists now or is **added later** part of the projection **by default**, so an un-swept new key **refuses loudly** (a false *refusal* the author meets at the migration run) rather than **silently stranding** a corpus (a false *ship* nobody meets). That is the un-enumerated-sibling failure — the one this increment exists to close — turned to point the safe way; a positive re-enumeration would have reproduced it in the fix for it. The design's table stays the statement of record; the code states its complement.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 3](implementation/roadmap.md) (P1c — the managed-vs-foreign discriminator; [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The managed-vs-foreign discriminator + the stamp bound / [storage.md](design/storage.md)`:148`) into **4 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `8e5fdeb` (tree clean; Inc 2 landed — family 5 and the file-state twin now *see* the placement class, which is precisely what makes a wrong route reachable). The grouped scope maps: **T1+T2** = the stamp discriminator in family 5 (the foreign arm, then the managed arm) and with it **both new finding codes**; **T3** = the discriminator in family 3; **T4** = the `binary-mismatch` route. No exit-code change (Inc 4), no `migrate-corpus` change (Inc 5).

**Verified bases (driven through the real binary at `8e5fdeb`, or probed against the engine — not assumed):**

- **The headline red is real and was driven.** A **stock brownfield repo** (a real Keep-a-Changelog `CHANGELOG.md` + `jigc setup`, nothing else) → `jigc validate` prints **4 blocking `conformance.*` findings** on `CHANGELOG.md`, every one routed *"migrate — `CHANGELOG.md` carries no schema-version stamp; run the corpus migration"*, plus a `file-state.un-baselined` advisory routed *"no action needed — the doc is baselined on its next author or finalize"*. Both routes are false: `jigc migrate-corpus` over that repo reports **`0 migrated, 0 already current, 1 blocked`**, and no author/finalize will ever baseline a file jigc does not manage. `jigc ingest` — the surface that is already right — is never named.
- **The stamp-only discriminator is NOT sufficient, and the parse-against-priors arm is load-bearing — probed, not reasoned.** A **v0-era managed ADR** (unstamped, the pre-`options` v1 shape) **does not parse against the current v2 `adr` schema** (`parse_sections` → `Err`; driven: three blocking `conformance.section-renamed`/`section-missing`). Under a naive *"unstamped and unparseable against the **current** schema ⇒ foreign"* rule the tool would tell an operator to **`ingest` their own managed ADR**. Probed directly against the engine: that same doc **parses clean against the shipped `adr.v1` snapshot** (`true`), while a stock Keep-a-Changelog `CHANGELOG.md` parses against **neither** `changelog` v2 **nor** `changelog` v1 (`false`/`false`). So the middle arm is *"parses against **any known** schema version"* — current **or** any shipped `schema-snapshots/<ty>.v<k>.yaml` — exactly as [validation.md](design/validation.md) pins it, and the prior schemas must be **threaded into the engine** (the CLI feeds them; `pack::load_prior_schema` is the loader, engine stays domain-empty).
- **The fresh-clone catch is real: `.jigc/state/` never reaches a clone.** Driven: `git clone` of a managed repo → **no `.jigc/state` directory at all**, and `jigc validate` reports every committed doc `file-state.un-baselined`. A record-keyed discriminator would call **every managed doc foreign** on every teammate's first checkout. The stamp survives the clone; the record does not.
- **A stale managed doc that fails to PARSE carries no machine-readable staleness fact today — so the emission must become unconditional, in BOTH parse arms.** Driven: a **v1-stamped** ADR under the v2 manifest yields three routed `conformance.*` parse findings and **zero `schema-conformance.*` findings** — the `Err` arm only *labels* the route, and the `Ok` arm's version break is gated on `doc_findings.is_empty()`. That guard exists **only** because the reused `field-value-conformant` code would double-report (`validate.rs` says so in comment). With a **distinct** code there is no double-report, and leaving the guard would hand Inc 4's exit predicate **nothing to key on for the commonest stale doc there is** — the false green would survive exactly where it bites hardest. The guard goes; the `Err` arm gains the emission.
- **The `binary-mismatch` false all-clear was driven end-to-end.** On a repo with a stale corpus *and* a stale `.jigc/version`: the advisory routes *"re-run `jigc setup` to re-stamp"* → running `jigc setup` → the advisory is **gone** (0 findings) while **3 stale-corpus findings remain**. Un-keyed, it keeps its emitted `Blocking` severity and `validation_store_exit_flips` still keys only on `pack-probe-integrity.*` — so exit stays **0** through this increment, by construction.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-3 T4: `binary-mismatch` stops handing out a false all-clear

The `store-version.binary-mismatch` advisory's route is now **schema-version-aware** ([storage.md](design/storage.md) → Store provenance — the check). The old route named only *"align versions / re-run `jigc setup`"* — and over a **stale corpus** that is a **false all-clear**: `jigc setup` re-stamps `.jigc/version`, which **self-clears the advisory itself** while every committed doc stays on the old schema, so the next `jigc validate` reads as progress and the verb that would actually fix the corpus was never named. Driven end-to-end through the real binary rather than argued (`crates/cli/tests/managed_vs_foreign.rs`): route → run the routed verb → re-validate → the advisory is gone and the version-currency break still stands. A stale corpus now routes at **`jigc migrate-corpus` first**, the re-stamp after it.

**The handle is T2's finding code, never a route-string prefix** (the coupling the Settle rejected): `cli.rs` asks whether the *just-built* report carries a `schema-conformance.schema-version-current` break and passes that one bool in. The advisory itself stays exactly what it was — advisory, un-keyed, `target: null` (the declared singleton exception), never a gate.

**Pinned in the omitting context too, because that is where a naive fix breaks:** a divergent binary over a **current** corpus keeps the plain align-or-re-stamp route. An unconditional *"name `migrate-corpus`"* would pass the headline test and command a verb with nothing to do (`0 migrated, 1 already current`) — the same false-route failure this increment deletes on the foreign side, re-introduced on the provenance side.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-3 T1: the provenance classifier — and the arm it refuses to assert

Family 5 now classifies every committed instance from **its own committed bytes** before adjudicating it ([validation.md](design/validation.md) → The managed-vs-foreign discriminator): a **stamp** ⇒ managed; else a parse against the **current** shape **or any shipped prior snapshot** (`schema-snapshots/<ty>.v<k>.yaml`, threaded in CLI-side via `pack::prior_doctype_schemas` — the engine stays domain-empty) ⇒ managed, v0-era; else **foreign** — one advisory `schema-conformance.unadopted-instance`, addressed at the **file path** (a foreign file has no managed identity to claim), routed at `jigc ingest` / `jigc migrate <path> --as <ty>` (the `--as` clause conditioned on the `migrate-<ty>` workflow existing — the M40 two-tier route), its structural findings **suppressed**. A stock brownfield repo (real Keep-a-Changelog `CHANGELOG.md` + `jigc setup`) went from **4 blocking findings routed at a verb that reports `1 blocked`** to zero blocking + one adoption advisory, exit 0 (`crates/cli/tests/managed_vs_foreign.rs`, through the real binary).

**The elaboration the build forced: the classifier runs only where a stamp can exist.** Stamp-absence is the discriminator's first signal, and it is evidence *only* for a doctype the CLI actually stamps — the **versioned** set (a governing manifest entry). For an **unversioned** doctype (freeze-exempt / project-defined) no instance ever carries a stamp, so "unstamped" says nothing, and a failed parse would have demoted a **corrupt managed doc** to *"never adopted by jigc — run `jigc ingest`"*: an unfounded claim of exactly the class this increment exists to delete. Unversioned doctypes therefore keep the pre-M42 behavior (structural findings, un-routed — the version-router already returns early for them). Both shipped packs are fully versioned, so nothing in production narrows; what narrows is what the tool is willing to **assert**. Surfaced by an engine test that went red for the *right* reason (an unstamped, unparseable `spec` fixture) — the fixture was not "fixed", the claim was.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-3 T3: one foreign file is one fact — family 3 stops calling it un-baselined

Family 3 (the read-only file↔CLI-state store twin) now asks the **same committed-bytes question** family 5 does before it calls a doc `file-state.un-baselined` ([validation.md](design/validation.md) → *the same discriminator applies to family 3's `un-baselined` advisory*): a **foreign** squatter at a managed home emits **none**. Its route — *"no action needed — the doc is baselined on its next author or finalize"* — is a **promise about a file jigc will never author**, and it fired on every stock brownfield repo the moment Inc 2 pointed the twin at the placement class. The squatter is not left silent (the M36 never-silent property): family 5 gives it the one finding it earns, the `unadopted-instance` adoption advisory. The brownfield arm now pins **exactly one finding, total** — a foreign file is one fact, not two contradictory ones (`crates/cli/tests/managed_vs_foreign.rs`, through the real binary).

**Scoped to the un-baselined arm alone — the elaboration that keeps drift honest.** The classify runs *inside* the record-miss branch, never over the whole instance: a **recorded** doc is managed by construction (jigc baselined it), so both of its outcomes stand **unclassified**. Had the suppression sat at the top of the loop, an out-of-band edit that mangled a managed doc *past parsing* would have read `Foreign` and its `file-state.hash-matches` **drift block would have vanished** — the tool would have offered to "adopt" the doc it was supposed to be protecting, voiding *"out-of-band edits are detected and routed"* for the worst edit there is. Suppression reaches un-baselined, and only un-baselined.

**The precondition is single-sourced, not copied.** Both families call one `validate::is_unadopted_foreign(ty, schema, source, versions, priors)`, which folds in T1's *only-where-a-stamp-can-exist* gate — a second, drifting copy of that rule in `file_state.rs` is exactly how a discriminator this delicate rots. Pinned both ways by an engine unit test over an **empty record** (the fresh-clone state): the managed un-baselined doc **still fires**, the foreign one stays silent — the suppression reaches foreign docs only, never a managed corpus on a teammate's clean checkout.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-3 T2: the version-currency break gets its own code — and its own route

Family 5's *managed* arm now mints **`schema-conformance.schema-version-current`** ([validation.md](design/validation.md) → Version-currency is itself a surfaced break, and the retraction of the *no new check id* pin): a committed instance classified **managed** whose stamp is **absent** (v0-era) or **below** its doctype's manifest version emits one blocking break under its **own** id, addressed at the doc's `<type>:<slug>` URI (one stamp per doc ⇒ `(code, target)` unique — its row is in [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md)'s target table). The M34 reuse of `field-value-conformant` is retired: a stale stamp and an invalid enum value are different facts, and under one code the version break is **indistinguishable to any machine consumer** — including the exit predicate Inc 4 keys on, which sees only `(probe, code)`.

**Emitted unconditionally, in *both* parse arms** — the load-bearing half. The old `doc_findings.is_empty()` guard existed *only* to stop the reused code from double-reporting; with a distinct code there is no double-report, and the guard was hiding the fact for exactly the docs that most need it. Driven: a **v1-stamped ADR** under the v2 manifest does not parse under v2, so before this it emitted **zero** `schema-conformance.*` findings — only routed `conformance.*` parse findings — i.e. the commonest stale doc in a real corpus carried **no machine-readable staleness fact at all**. It now surfaces the break, `jigc migrate-corpus` clears it, and the corpus re-validates clean (`crates/cli/tests/managed_vs_foreign.rs`, through the real binary). Consequence, pinned rather than absorbed: a doc that is stale **and** structurally broken now carries **both** findings (`schema_conformance_routing.rs` — its `route: migrate` count went 2 → 4, the guard-drop made visible).

**The break carries its own route, naming `jigc migrate-corpus` verbatim**, instead of taking the generic `route_schema_conformance` label its sibling findings take (which says "run the corpus migration" but names no verb). Same `migrate` classification token, an executable verb behind it — the wave's own rule (an advisory's route must name the verb that fixes it) applied to the finding that *is* the route's subject. Exit stays **0** through this task by construction (the code is un-keyed until Inc 4; `validation_store_exit_flips` still keys only on `pack-probe-integrity.*`) — asserted, not assumed.

The grouped scope maps: **T1–T4** = the four enumerator branches (F5 · F3 · F1 · `cli::start::committed_store`), each folding back its own census row (`storage.md:178` — *"the obligation binds on the adding side … the entry is part of the change"*); the bound-test flip rides **T1** (it is what T1 breaks); **T5** = the census's **completeness obligation, applied**. No routing change (Inc 3), no exit-code change (Inc 4).

**Verified bases (driven through the real binary / probed at `7d17d62`, not assumed):**

- **The three live reds are real, and each was driven.** (a) **F5** — a committed root `CHANGELOG.md` stamped `schema-version: 1` under a manifest at 2: `jigc validate` emits **zero** schema-conformance findings for it (only the placement-aware hollow advisory `repeatable-populated`), exit 0. (b) **F3** — a **baselined** `CHANGELOG.md` (baseline-adopted by the placement-aware *mutating* reconciler at task scope: `advisory · file-state.baseline-adopt — baseline adopted: CHANGELOG.md`) then hand-edited out of band: `jigc validate` prints **`no findings — the committed store validates clean`**, exit 0 — a false green over a corpus whose managed doc was tampered with, voiding CLAUDE.md's *"out-of-band edits are detected and routed"* **architectural invariant** for the whole placement class. (c) **`cli::start::committed_store`** — a listed filesystem pack whose step body carries `{{ store.specs }}` + `{{ store.changelog }}`, composed over a repo holding a committed spec **and** a committed root `CHANGELOG.md`, renders `> spec:a-spec` and then **an empty line** for the changelog: no address, **no finding**, exit 0 (`compose.rs:966` → `ctx.store.get(doctype).cloned().unwrap_or_default()`, `data_value.rs:412` — an absent key is the *empty* case, never *unresolvable*).
- **F1 is latent, and the reason is checked, not assumed:** no shipped schema in either pack declares a `code-anchor` field on a placement doctype (`grep -rln code-anchor` → `arch-doc`/`adr`/`spec`/`prd`, all `location:` doctypes), so the store-scope doc↔code family has nothing to skip today. Its red is therefore a unit test over a **synthetic** placement schema carrying a `code-anchor` — a real red, not a rationale.

Re-pointing `detect_committed_store` **alone** → **the same single test fails**, on `file-state.un-baselined` for `docs/deferral-ledger.md` (its filter matches any finding whose JSON mentions `deferral-ledger`). **Consequence for the cut:** the bound test flips under *either* task, so T1 must re-assert it as **presence** of the routed migrate finding (never set-equality / `is_empty()`), or T2's added advisory re-breaks it.
- **The enumerator is `pub(crate)`.** `index::committed_instances` (`index.rs:718`) is `pub(crate)` — the three engine sites reach it as-is; **`cli::start::committed_store` cannot**, so T4 widens it to `pub`. It returns `(identity, abs_path)` with the identity **already** `<type>:<slug>` (a placement singleton's `<type>:<type>`) — use it, do not re-derive the slug.
- **The `{{store.<name>}}` key for a placement doctype is settled by the increment charter, not a fork:** the **type id**, its value a one-element list. It **conforms** to the documented grammar (`workflow-dialect.md:156` — *"`store.<doctype-id>` enumerates the committed instances of that doctype"*); the *located* case's location-stem key is the pre-existing deviation (DECISIONS 2026-06-01/06-18) and stays untouched. The one-doctype-per-key assumption is **inherited, not invented** (`target_surface.rs:210` already records *"One doctype per `location:` is **assumed**"*) — record it on the new key, do not build a guard nobody has today.
- **A recorded rationale that is FALSE, corrected here rather than propagated (it appears in the roadmap, `storage.md:150`, and `validation.md:356`):** *"both doctypes at schema-version 2 in either pack are placement doctypes, so the skip covered exactly the stale-able population."* **`adr` is at schema-version 2** (`crates/cli/pack/config/schema-manifest.yaml`) and is a **`location:`** doctype — driven: a v1-stamped committed ADR *is* routed `migrate` by family 5 today. The deliverable is unchanged; the *reason* is now true. T1 fixes the clause where it is asserted.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-2 T5: the census, diffed against its own fence — the fourth application is clean; the fence was not

The completeness obligation ([storage.md](design/storage.md) → Census completeness) ran for the first time as a *check* rather than a rule stated beside a list: the grep at the increment's HEAD, diffed against the census. **No production miss** — every non-test hit maps to a named row, and the residue is now enumerated in the doc so a future diff terminates (test fixtures · `Finding::location` reads the line-based `-v` cannot drop, because rustfmt wraps the field onto its own line · doc-comments naming the field). The rows built in Inc 2 read *built*, not *live hole*.

**Two elaborations the clean diff would otherwise have buried.** (1) **The fence carried the assumption it condemns.** Its `-v` excluded by **accessor shape** (`\.location\.as_ref`), so a home read spelled `schema.location.as_ref()` would have been fenced *out* — the under-inclusion twin of the `prior.location` miss the same pass had just corrected. The exclusions now name **`Finding` bindings only** (`\bf\.location` word-bounded, which also stops it swallowing `self.location`); verified at HEAD the hardened pattern yields the identical hit set plus two adjudicated `Finding`-serializer rows, so it changes the *guarantee*, not the census. The standing rule: an exclusion may only ever **over**-include — an over-included row costs one adjudication, an under-included one costs a silent hole. (2) **A repaired site leaves the grep**, because re-pointing it at `index::committed_instances` stops it reading `location`/`placement` at all — so for those rows the reviewer check **inverts**: a census row with *no* grep hit is **fixed**, not missing. Unstated, the next reader reads five repaired sites' absence as a miss.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-2 T4: `{{store.<placement-type>}}` resolves — and the pack-facing key is *made*, not flagged

`cli::start::committed_store` — the resolver that feeds `{{store.<name>}}` into **every** composed workflow — enumerates through `index::committed_instances` (widened to `pub`; [storage.md](design/storage.md) → The census, the 14th site; [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) → data-value roots), so a placement doctype's committed singleton is no longer invisible at compose time. This was the census's nastiest row: it failed **silently** (an absent `store` key is the empty-vs-unresolvable contract's *empty* case — empty text, never a finding, `compose.rs:966`), so a pack writing `{{store.vision}}` composed a workflow reading *as if no vision were committed*; and it opened on a **bare workflow edit** — no schema change, no gate. Driven red end-to-end through the real binary before the fix: the same step rendered `> spec:a-spec` and then an empty line for `{{store.changelog}}` over a committed root `CHANGELOG.md`.

**The one-way door, now walked:** a placement doctype's **collection key is its type id** (`store.changelog`), its collection the one-element `[changelog:changelog]` singleton list at the literal `placement.file`. It has no location stem to key by — and the type id is precisely what [workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) has always spelled (`store.<doctype-id>`); the **located** case's location-stem key (`docs/specs/` → `store.specs`) is the pre-existing deviation, and it stays. An **absent** singleton contributes **no key**, exactly as an empty location directory does — the omitting context stays inert (proven in both tests, not argued). **No collision guard was invented**: one-doctype-per-key is the *inherited* stance of the located case (`target_surface.rs:210` records it), two placement doctypes cannot collide on a unique type id, and building a guard nobody has today would be scope the census does not own.
