## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-1 T2: the verb lands its own migration — setup's mold, finalize's hook posture

`migrate-corpus` now **commits its own writes** ([corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The commit boundary): a pathspec-limited `git add -- <touched>` + pathspec-limited `git commit`, so the ` D docs/changelog/changelog.md` + `?? CHANGELOG.md` the verb used to leave — landable only through the raw `git add -A` the adapter contract forbids, which is exactly what the adoption trial's agent was forced into — no longer exists. The per-doc fold stays **git-free**; staging happens once, at the boundary.

**Two calls the design left open, picked and recorded.** (1) **The touched-path set is surfaced, not re-derived**: the report carried only *destinations*, so a pathspec built from it would have staged the **add half alone** and landed a half-migration — the silent-partial-commit class this wave exists to kill. The fold now records both halves of every write (destination written, relocation source removed) as it makes them. (2) **The hook posture is `finalize`/`rename`'s, not setup's.** The Settle said "copies setup's real mold" — and the mold (pathspec `add`, `--quiet` idempotence, loud `Err`) *is* setup's, but setup commits **`--no-verify`** on a rationale that **does not transfer**: its commit *"carries install artifacts, not managed docs."* This one carries **managed docs**, so the user's hooks are **policy** — never `--no-verify`; a `pre-commit` rejection surfaces git's stderr verbatim and fails the run non-zero, never a silent skip behind a success banner. Neither existing helper is both shapes (`task::git_commit` has the posture but commits the *whole index*), so the commit is a small, purpose-shaped variant: setup's pathspec form, minus `--no-verify`, with `git_commit`'s bail-on-rejection.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Inc-1 T1: the walk union, and what "dedupe" means when both homes are populated

The corpus walk's two placement branches are now a **union** (prior `location:` home **and** the literal `placement.file`), so a stale root `CHANGELOG.md` is *found* — the pre-fix mutual exclusion made it invisible (`0 migrated, 0 already current, 0 blocked`, stamp stuck at 1). The planner's claim **held**: zero engine change — `SchemaChange::Relocated` folds as a content no-op, so an in-place candidate at the placement home migrates under `[Relocated, DisplayTitleChanged]` + the stamp value-bump.

**The one open call, picked and recorded** ([corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The corpus walk): *dedupe* was carrying two jobs. (1) The **identical pair** (a placement file sitting under its own prior home) is a set-dedupe at enumeration. (2) The **shared destination** — the both-homes state the union first makes reachable — is **not** deduplicable; it is a collision, resolved at the **write boundary against the destination's bytes on disk**, never by candidate order (the pre-fix protection was an ordering accident that inverts on a `docs/x.md` placement with a `docs/y/` prior home — and the red test caught it *clobbering*: the strand overwrote the destination and destroyed its content). The rule: destination holds exactly the relocating doc's migrated bytes ⇒ **interrupted move**, complete it (byte-identical write, strand removed, target reported once as migrated); destination holds anything else ⇒ **blocked with a route**, nothing written, nothing removed. Why refuse rather than merge: **No-data-loss** is a declared property of this pair and no deterministic merge of two documents exists — the same posture as the freeze's unbuilt-kind backstop (refuse, don't strand). Reading from disk is what makes it **order-invariant**.

## 2026-07-13 — M42 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 1](implementation/roadmap.md) (P1a — `migrate-corpus` can SEE a placement doc, and can LAND its result; [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The corpus walk / The commit boundary) into **3 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `47ba83d` (tree clean; M42 Settle recorded, no code landed yet). The two grouped-scope bullets map: **T1** = the walk union; **T2 + T3** = the self-commit + the two flags (split at the seam the two flags actually sit on — `--no-commit` opts out of T2's *commit*, `--dry-run` opts out of the *write*, and both are one signature/plumbing motion). No design-doc task: `corpus-migration.md` §§ *The corpus walk* / *The commit boundary* are **already written** (landed with the Settle) — T1 and T2 each fold back only the one call the doc leaves open (below); the wave-wide fold-back rides Inc 12.

**Verified bases (facts driven through the real binary / read at `47ba83d`, not assumed):**

- **The headline red is real, and it is total silence.** A repo with a **stale root `CHANGELOG.md` stamped `schema-version: 1`** (setup-installed, committed) → `jigc migrate-corpus` prints `corpus migration: 0 migrated, 0 already current, 0 blocked`, exit 0, **stamp still 1**. Cause confirmed by reading `candidate_docs` (`migrate_corpus.rs:626-667`): `changelog` is at manifest v2, `load_prior_schema(changelog, 1)` resolves `crates/cli/pack/schema-snapshots/changelog.v1.yaml`, which carries `location: changelog/` — so `prior_location` is **always** `Some`, the relocation walk runs over an empty `docs/changelog/`, and the in-place branch at `:663` is dead for this doctype. The in-place branch is **not** globally dead (`packs/methodology/schema-snapshots/deferral-ledger.v1.yaml` carries `placement:`, no `location:` → `prior_location == None` → the placement-born arm runs), which is exactly why the mutual exclusion survived: the two live doctypes each exercise one branch and neither exercises the union.
- **`SchemaChange::Relocated` is a content no-op in the engine fold** (`transform.rs:223-230` — "a file move, not a content edit"; the move is the CLI's `target_key` concern), so an **in-place** candidate at the placement home migrates cleanly under the changelog's v1→v2 diff (`[Relocated, DisplayTitleChanged]` + the stamp value-bump): the union needs no engine change. **Zero engine change is a claim T1 must hold, not a licence** — if the fold does need a branch, that is a finding, not a silent widening.
- **The commit-boundary red is real.** A committed v1 changelog at `docs/changelog/changelog.md` → `jigc migrate-corpus` → `1 migrated  CHANGELOG.md`, and `git status --short` leaves ` D docs/changelog/changelog.md` + `?? CHANGELOG.md` — an unstaged delete and an **untracked** file, landable only by raw `git add`. `.jigc/state` is gitignored (it does not appear), so the pathspec is doc paths only.
- **The report drops the source path — the pathspec cannot be built from it today.** `CorpusMigrationReport.migrated: Vec<String>` is pushed the **destination** (`report.migrated.push(target.clone())`); the relocated **source** (`id`, the file `remove_file`d) is never surfaced. So T2 must surface the touched paths (destinations **and** removed sources), or the commit stages only the add half and lands a half-migration — precisely the silent-partial-commit class this wave exists to kill.
- **The commit's mold is `setup`'s, its hook posture is `finalize`/`rename`'s — and no existing helper is both.** `setup::commit_install` (`setup.rs:949-1017`) supplies the pathspec `git add -- <paths>` ("never a blanket `git add -A`"), the `git diff --cached --quiet -- <paths>` idempotence, and the loud `Err` on a genuine git rejection. But it commits with **`--no-verify`**, on a rationale that **does not transfer** (`setup.rs:943-947`, verbatim: the commit "carries install artifacts, not managed docs"). `migrate-corpus` commits **managed docs**, so it follows the standing rule every managed-work commit follows — `task::git_commit` (`task.rs:2107`) and `rename.rs:378` both, **never `--no-verify`**, the user's hooks are policy and a rejection bails loudly. `task::git_commit` is `git commit -F <file>` with **no pathspec** (it commits the whole index), so the needed commit is a small variant — setup's pathspec form, minus `--no-verify`, with `git_commit`'s bail-on-rejection — **not** a reuse of either as-is.
- **`--dry-run` / `--no-commit` are genuinely net-new** (`jigc migrate-corpus --dry-run` → `error: unexpected argument '--dry-run' found`; the verb is a unit variant `Command::MigrateCorpus` taking no args, `cli.rs:188`), and there is **no operator-facing `persist` stage** to skip: `engine::state::persist` is an internal call inside the outcome loop (`migrate_corpus.rs:325`) that writes bytes *and* flips the file-state baseline in one motion. Dry-run = **suppress the write** (bytes, move, file-state save, commit), not "stop before a stage".
- **The one call `corpus-migration.md:192` leaves open: what "dedupe" means when BOTH homes hold an instance.** The union makes that state reachable for the first time. Two shapes exist in it — the *partially-completed relocation* (the same doc at both homes: the write-to-`to`-before-remove-`from` abort the doc already designs for, which should **complete**), and a *different* file at the destination (a foreign squatter). Today a destination collision is protected only by an accident — `prepared` is sorted by source path and the fold halts at the first blocker, so `CHANGELOG.md` happens to sort before `docs/changelog/…` — which does **not** generalize (a `docs/x.md` placement with a `docs/y/` prior home inverts it, and the relocation write would clobber the destination). This is **not a new fork**: the governing property is locked (`corpus-migration.md` → the property census, **No-data-loss**; Relocation-safety, write-before-remove). T1 **picks the shape, tests it, and records it** in the union paragraph, rather than shipping "dedupe" as an undefined word.

- **T2 · CLI: the pathspec-limited self-commit — the verb lands its own migration (CLI + design fold-back).** Surface the migration's **touched paths** (destinations **and** removed relocation sources) on the report; stage exactly those (`git add -- <paths>`, **never** `git add -A`), no-op cleanly when nothing is staged (`git diff --cached --quiet -- <paths>`), and commit them **pathspec-limited with the user's hooks running (never `--no-verify`)**, surfacing a git/hook rejection loudly and non-zero; the report names the commit in both formats. Fold the hook-posture call (setup's `--no-verify` rationale does not transfer to managed docs) into `corpus-migration.md` → The commit boundary. Repairs the existing migrate-corpus suites in the same motion (they now see a committed tree). *Done:* new real-binary arms — after `jigc migrate-corpus` over a repo with a v1 old-home changelog, **`git status --porcelain` is empty** and HEAD advanced by exactly one commit whose `--name-status` carries **both** halves of the move (the add and the delete); an **ambient unrelated dirty/untracked file is still dirty** afterwards (never swept in); a clean **re-run** commits nothing (HEAD unchanged, `0 migrated`); a `pre-commit` hook exiting non-zero makes the verb **fail loudly non-zero** with git's stderr, never a silent skip behind a success banner; every existing `migrate-corpus` suite green; full gate. *Red today (driven):* the verb leaves ` D docs/changelog/changelog.md` + `?? CHANGELOG.md` — the raw-`git add -A` drive-around the adoption trial's agent was forced into. *Depends on T1 (the stale-placement doc must be findable before its landing can be proven end-to-end).* *(files: `crates/cli/src/migrate_corpus.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/corpus_migration.rs`, `design/corpus-migration.md`.)*

## 2026-07-13 — M42 planning: the Settle. Twelve forks, every one resolved robust; the charter was wrong in five places

The M42 planning pass ran the full recon (5 `capability-auditor`s exercising the real binary, 4 `gap-detector`s, 3 `robust-advocate`s). It found that **three of the six chartered clusters are one disease — the tool's own routes lie — and the charter's fixes for them were cosmetic**, that **P6 hid an identity-model change inside a "papercut" batch**, and that **five load-bearing charter premises were factually false**. The charter is restated below before it is settled; a Settle against a fiction is worse than no Settle.

**The five charter corrections (verified against HEAD, each with a live repro).** (1) *"The write primitives exist"* for the abandon — they do, but `milestone-record`'s status enum is **closed at `[active, joined]`** with enum members inside the frozen `schema-hash`: there is no value to flip **to**, so abandon is a **frozen-schema bump**, not a wiring job. (2) *"Copy `setup`'s `--no-commit` opt-out"* — **`--no-commit` does not exist anywhere in the repo**; the flag would be invented, not copied. (3) *"Both false 'lists the gates' sentences"* — **there is one**; `implement-quick.yaml` is 9 lines and carries neither the sentence nor the changelog paragraph (the claim appears in three docs and is true in none). (4) *"`--dry-run` prints the report without `persist`"* — there is **no operator-facing `persist` stage** to skip. (5) **L1** — blocked finalizes **do** log their finding codes and errored verbs **do** write records; the real gap is that `anyhow` bail paths log `finding_codes: []`, so a **hook-rejected finalize is opaque in the log**.

**P1 — the false green is a class, and the chartered fix would have made it worse.** P1 is not "the `validate.rs:561-563` skip." It is an **unfinished census** — and `storage.md:143` already records that the M38 census was run once and *under-counted* ("the 10th site the census missed"). It under-counted by three: **F5** schema-conformance (chartered), **F3 `detect_committed_store`** (`file_state.rs:499` — **live, and in no document**), **F1 `target_surface`** (`:228`, latent). F3 is the one that matters: the *mutating* reconciler got its placement branch (`file_state.rs:361-377`, comment: *"so an OOB edit to a root `CHANGELOG.md` is detected + routed instead of silently skipped"*) and the **read-only twin never did** — so `jigc validate` **cannot see an out-of-band edit to `CHANGELOG.md` or `VISION.md`** (proven live: the ADR's tamper is caught, the CHANGELOG's is not mentioned at all). `storage.md:141` flags that exact site ⚠ as *"silently voiding the 'managed, not a mirror' promise"*, and CLAUDE.md lists detect-and-route as an **architectural invariant**. It does not hold for the placement class — and post-1.0 self-migration puts jigc's own `VISION.md` / roadmap / decisions-log / deferral-ledger on a detector that skips them.

And the chartered three-line fix is a **regression in disguise**: `migrate-corpus` **cannot see a stale `CHANGELOG.md`** (`candidate_docs`' two placement branches are mutually exclusive; `changelog.v1.yaml:18` carries `location: changelog/`, so the relocation walk runs over an empty dir and the in-place branch at `:663` is **dead code** — `0 migrated, 0 already current, 0 blocked`, stamp stays at 1 forever). So lifting the false-green mask without fixing the verb **converts a silent false green into a loud false route** — and lights up the **default brownfield first-run** (a stock Keep-a-Changelog `CHANGELOG.md` + `jigc setup`) with **four blocking findings pointing at a verb that does nothing**, while `jigc ingest` — the surface that is already correct — goes unnamed. That also contradicts `storage.md:148`'s own recorded call: a foreign root `CHANGELOG.md` sits at the canonical destination, so it is the **in-location-squatter adoption case**, not a corpus-migration case.

**Settled: P1 ships the full robust cut (R1–R5).** Finish the census (F5 + F3 + F1) and fold the three sites back into `storage.md` with a stated **completeness obligation** (it has now been wrong twice). **The discriminator** — managed-stale (→ `migrate-corpus`) vs never-adopted-foreign (→ `ingest` / `jigc migrate <path> --as`) — threads the `record: &FileStateRecord` that `validate_store_families` **already receives** (`validate.rs:401`; families 3 and 4 use it, family 5 is called from inside the same function and simply isn't passed it) and reuses **M40's existing two-tier orphan test** (`cli.rs:792`). No engine-empty violation: the record is *state*, not domain content. Rejected: discriminating on the stamp (stamp-absent means *both* "never adopted" *and* "v0-era managed doc" — the v0 case is the headline case the detect-half exists for, per `validation.md:341`) and CLI-side post-filtering (the engine would knowingly emit a wrong finding and `validate_store_families` is a `pub fn`). `candidate_docs`' branches become a **union**. The `binary-mismatch` route's current behaviour is a **false all-clear**, not merely a missing mention — it routes to `jigc setup`, which re-stamps `.jigc/version` and self-clears the advisory while the corpus stays stale.

**Settled: the version-mismatch condition breaks the store-scope exit code — the one genuine one-way door in P1.** Today `jigc validate` exits **0** over an unmigrated corpus while its trailer prints *"these gate at `jigc task validate` / `jigc task finalize`"* — and that sentence is **false**: at task scope the stale docs downgrade to `advisory · reconciliation.conformance-block`, and a **finalize over a doubly-stale corpus was proven to commit**. The version-mismatch family has **no gate anywhere in the system** while the tool prints that it gates. The ask is **narrow and does not touch the report-only rationale** (`validation.md:319` — report-only exists so the sweep never gates on pre-existing unrelated drift, the masking-trap; that stands, conceded in full). Instead the unmigrated-corpus condition **joins the existing exit-flip exception class** (`render.rs:344-349`, today `pack-probe-integrity.*`) **on its existing recorded criterion** — *"the sweep could not produce a trustworthy result"* — which an unmigrated corpus meets **more strongly than a failed probe does**: when the manifest says v2 and the corpus is v1, every other family is parsing docs against a schema those docs do not conform to. A "clean" verdict over an unmigrated corpus is not a clean corpus; it is an untrustworthy sweep. **Why now and not 1.1:** exit codes are the first contract a pipeline binds — no version field, no additive carve-out — and `decisions-pending.md:184` already promises `validate --format json` as a CI-gating contract. Ship 1.0 exiting 0 and every adopter encodes *"unmigrated == green"*; flipping it later turns green pipelines red on a minor upgrade. *(Consequence: P6's "render `blocking (gates at finalize)` per finding" is **not** a papercut — it would print the falsehood more prominently. It is a dependency on this fix.)*

**Settled: fix the corpus-migration classifier; ship fork 3 on the fixed machinery; DECOUPLE fork 5's schema.** The classifier has three holes and **both chartered bumps land in them**: a wholly-new **repeatable section** → empty diff (`schema_diff.rs:294` — exactly `spec-open-decisions`' shape); **any field added to a repeatable item block** → empty diff (`diff_item_fields`, `:250-273` — exactly `spec-criterion-status`' shape; optional → migrates *by accident*, required → a **permanent mutual dead-end** where validate says "run the migration" and migrate says "author the prose"); an enum **widening** misclassified as a rename (`enum_members_renamed`, `:246` — fork 3's shape, blocks). Plus **`AddedOptionalSection` strands a doc that already carries the section** (`migrate_corpus.rs:396-408` guards `ProseNeeding` and not this kind) — which **shipped in the flagship `adr` v1→v2 `options` migration** and **strands real adopters on rc.5 today**, having survived M36–M41, two RC trials, three completion audits, and a cross-model review. That last fact retires "we'd catch it in acceptance": the stranding shape needs a doc that *already has* the section, and every fixture is a historical doc that *lacks* it. **The holes are invisible to exactly the tests we would rely on to catch them.**

The gap is not an edge case: **9 of 14 persisted doctypes carry a repeatable**, and for the work-doc family the item block **is** the document — `decisions-log` has exactly one section and it is a repeatable, so **zero content changes to it are migratable**. `migrate-corpus` cannot migrate the half of the schema model where the corpus's content lives, while `corpus-migration.md:3` sells it as the artifact that **bounds** an adopter's lock-in cost. The recorded over-build line that sanctions the gap (`:61`) rests on *"**no frozen doctype needs them**"* — a clause **the M42 charter itself falsifies twice**. And the same class was ruled on **six days ago** (M41 fork 4: *"a bump-without-a-kind strands the corpus"* — build the kind); the cheap arm asked to reverse that call, on the same defect class, presented as a saving. **Scope:** `EnumWidened` (`new.of ⊇ old.of` → byte no-op; *deletes* the identity-map table rather than growing it), the idempotency guard generalized to every heading-minting kind, `AddedRepeatableSection`, and the item-block leaf diff (`AddedItemField` — **⚠ specified here against `write::set_item_field`, which is the WRONG primitive; see the Review below: it is update-only and refuses when the field is absent, i.e. on every item by definition of the kind. The insert-capable primitive is `set_item_field_or_insert`**). ~90 LOC engine + ~250 tests — calibrated on M41's Inc-5, which built `ValueRemapped` end-to-end in one increment (**⚠ that estimate hung on the wrong function**). Explicitly **out** (the over-build line still holds for these): nested-repeatable edits, section removal/reorder/insert-anywhere, the per-item prose handoff.

**Settled (surfaced mid-Settle, by a doc agent writing the coverage matrix): the empty-diff backstop — close the class, not the instances.** Every hole above shares one shape: an unclassified change diffs to `[]`, and **an empty diff is not a no-op** — the below-version branch stamp-bumps anyway and strands the corpus *silently*. Fixing three shapes leaves the fourth. So: **structural shape moved + zero kinds classified → refuse loudly**, routed to *build the transform kind first*. This is the **mechanical enforcement** of the rule both M41 and M42 paid to learn, which until now was prose in a checklist nobody was gated on. Writing it surfaced **two more holes** in the same class — **field removal never classifies** (the diff loops v2's leaves, so a deleted leaf is invisible) and **cardinality narrowing misclassifies as a widening** (any `card` delta reads as widening regardless of direction, so a narrowing silently no-ops while the corpus may hold violating values); both are now in scope, the field-removal *shape* (declared strip vs. refuse — it trades against the census's **No-data-loss** property) stated in the doc and picked in-increment. **And the backstop's precondition is made true by construction, not asserted:** `Schema` carries `description`/`usage`/`hint` prose (`schema.rs:53,59,222`) and `schema_hash` serializes the **whole struct** (`manifest.rs:44`) — so **rewording an authoring hint is a frozen-schema bump**, which works today (empty diff → restamp → conform) and a *naive* backstop would render **unshippable**. A **presentation-only** kind fires when the structural projection is unchanged but the hash moved: it classifies, folds to zero bytes, restamps — the shape `DisplayTitleChanged` already establishes. *(That schema prose sits inside the frozen hash is a real consequence — an authoring-hint typo fix costs a version bump — recorded honestly rather than left for the next author to discover. Narrowing the hash to a structural projection would be a freeze-semantics change; out of scope.)*

**Fork 5 (the spec lifecycle) is DECOUPLED — and its "last cheap window" premise is what killed it.** The premise self-refutes: **if the window is real, the migration machine has failed its declared purpose.** A working `migrate-corpus` is precisely the artifact that makes a post-1.0 bump cost one command per adopter; the answer to a closing window is to **fix the machine that keeps it open**, not to shove two frozen schema bumps through the holes while it shuts. And the cheap arm's shape — *constrain spec-v2 to what the classifier happens to support* — is the tail wagging the dog with a **genuine data one-way door** at the end of it: an `open-decisions` **slot** re-ships, permanently and in schema form, the exact unstructured-prose bug the feature exists to kill (a slot has no items, so it cannot carry the per-item `resolved-by` ref that is the whole point), and the escape hatch `FixedSlotToRepeatable` **collapses the entire slot into one item named after the section** — per-decision identity and the `resolved-by` edges are never deterministically recoverable. A frozen doctype's permanent content model is not fix-wave work. **Honest cost of deferring, stated not waved away:** three implemented specs assert fixed bugs in present tense under a clean validate, and that rot stands one more milestone. Mitigated in-wave by P5's pack fixes (the `maps-to-test` demand + open-decision recording), which address the *process*; the lying spec is prose a human can read, not a corrupted store. **Bound (important): a NEW doctype costs nothing at 1.0 — it has no corpus to migrate — so the closing-window argument does NOT reach the post-1.0 doctype-completeness milestone.** `reference` / `finding` / `postmortem` / `runbook` stay deferred, correctly. The window covers only bumps to doctypes that already have adopter instances, and the sweep found **no third** such hole.

**Settled: fork 3 = `jigc milestone discard`, full, on the fixed machinery.** Enum widened to `[active, joined, discarded]` via `EnumWidened`. **Per-item semantics:** a sub-task that genuinely joined **stays `joined`** (it really did land); every non-joined item flips to `discarded` — the record stays true on both axes. **A dirty-worktree check before teardown:** `remove_worktrees` runs `git worktree remove --force`, which is safe on the *finalize* path (the commit lands first) and **silently destroys uncommitted work on abandon** (proven: file written into a sub-task worktree, gone at exit 0, no warning) — the M31 WIP-safety shape, secured on the headline path and dropped on the sibling. Abandon refuses on a dirty worktree, or requires `--force`. Also removes `.jigc/milestones/<id>/` (no reachable remover today). **The chartered "milestone-record active with no live workbench" advisory is DROPPED — it was unbuildable.** `team-ready-state.md:55` designed exactly that state as the **fresh-clone continuation** case, so the advisory would fire on every legitimately in-flight milestone on every clone, every teammate, every CI checkout — a false-positive class shipped into the wave whose whole purpose is that the routes tell the truth. Abandoned-vs-clone-continuable is **not locally observable** from the committed store; a **terminal status is what makes it observable**, and that is what this builds.

**Settled (found by checking a rationale before recording it): the milestone "independence constraint" is a BUG, and the guard gets fixed.** A doc agent, writing the constraint M42 chartered ("state it at `milestone create` + in the base-guard message"), *derived* a rationale for it and — per the 2026-07-11 rule, **a recorded rationale is a claim, not a fact** — flagged that it had not checked it. It was checked, against the real binary, and it is **true and worse than the draft asserted**: two concurrently-live milestones **wedge each other**. `record_only_range` requires *every* path touched in `base..head` to equal **this** milestone's record path (`crates/cli/src/milestone.rs:483-487`), so a second milestone's record-only bookkeeping commits land in the first's range as foreign paths → `finalize.base-mismatch`. **Serialized:** only the earlier wedges. **Interleaved** (the shape any real workflow takes): **both wedge — a symmetric deadlock neither can ever leave.** The second `milestone create` exits **0 with no warning**; `jigc validate` over a permanently wedged repo reports **`no findings — the committed store validates clean`, exit 0** (another false green, the same class as U2); **no jigc verb recovers it** — the blocking route says *"discard the task with `jigc task discard`"*, which on a milestone id returns `no task '<id>'` (a dead end that calls a milestone "the task"), and even `git revert` fails (the revert commit *itself* touches the other record — predicted verbatim by a comment at `milestone.rs:470-471`). The only escape is out-of-band history surgery, and the rebase escape **destroys the other milestone's committed record while its workbench survives** — inverting "the committed `.md` is the source of truth."

**So the guard is over-broad** — it exists to prove **no code changed** in `base..head`, so the M31 worktree-combine stays valid, and **another milestone's record is not code.** `record_only_range` will accept commits whose touched paths are **all milestone-record paths (any milestone's)**, which removes the *record-bookkeeping* deadlock. **This is also load-bearing for fork 3:** a `milestone discard` commit still **touches** the other milestone's record path, so **discard cannot clear even a bookkeeping wedge without the guard fix** — the verb and the fix ship together. *(The M42 charter asked us to write the constraint down. Writing it down is what exposed it.)* **⚠ This paragraph's original conclusion — that the constraint was therefore "phantom" and concurrent milestones "stop being a trap" — is WRONG, and the Review below corrects it: the guard was one predicate too narrow *and* the constraint underneath it is real.** Left standing, corrected in place, because a silent fix teaches nobody.

**Settled: P4 is not "additive revisions to a pinned contract" — it is a defect against a grammar the foundation doc already settled.** `structural-grammar.md:54-57` (reading-order #2) pins `fragment := unit ("/" leaf)?` for non-repeatable units and `:72` says *"one grammar, every reference — write commands, **validation targets**, data-values."* The write path honours it; **validate's emit sites honour it** (`validate.rs:1759`, `:1797` emit `#<section>/<field>` targets); **only the read path violates it** — so `jigc validate` **emits an address its own read surface cannot resolve** (blast radius: 11 header sections across 10 doctypes, including `milestone-record`, which `doc-read-surface.md:33` names as the pinned contract's own **conformance witness**; zero tests cover it, which is why the suite is green over a broken round-trip). `doc-read-surface.md`'s slice table is **the drifted doc** and gets corrected, not negotiated. The **header-section slice serves its fields** (today: empty at exit 0 — the wrong-node-exit-0 that `:54` forbids **by name**); since `ParsedSection` carries no `fields_span`, that slice is a **canonical re-emit**, which also forces retiring `:26`'s false *"byte-exact … verbatim"* claim (already false: item renders are anchorless, nested slices re-rooted). Item `id` joins `item_json` (today the json contract **is not closed under its own address grammar** — you can read an item array and address none of it; a release titled `1.0.0` mints id `100`, and a driver slugifying the title guesses `1-0-0` and gets `write.wrong-shape`), and the `id` key is **reserved at schema-load** so a future pack cannot silently collide. **`write.*` joins the stable-key normalization table** — `command-output-contract.md:46` **explicitly scopes blocked writes in** and `:69-72` pins `target` to the URI normal form, but the constructors set no address, so `(write.wrong-shape, null)` is **one key for every failed write in the corpus**; the identity-less sub-family (`create.gate-blocked` — a doctype and no slug) is declared **nullable-by-contract** in the pin rather than synthesised. **⚠ That declaration is WRONG and the Review below retires it** — it violates the uniqueness the same contract claims (two blocked creates in one gate-less task collide on `(code, null)`), and the sweep it prompted found the degenerate-key class is **~28 codes across five clusters**, not one.

**Settled: `doc list` and the task-verb acks declare their posture as they ship.** `command-output-contract.md:9-11` records the lesson bought at M41 — *"an **undeclared** output calcifies into a **de-facto** contract with no evolution rule; the one-way door is the **posture**, not the field count."* Three read surfaces today carry three *different* postures; a fourth shipping undeclared, one wave before the pin, re-opens the door M41 just closed. (`doc list`'s substrate is `index::committed_instances` — **the same placement-aware enumerator P1's family-5 fix needs**. One primitive, two increments; say so or it gets built twice.)

**Settled: fork 1 = commit boundary + `--no-commit` + `--dry-run`.** `migrate-corpus` today leaves an unstaged delete, an unstaged modify, and an **untracked** relocated file — so the only way to land a migration is `git add -A && git commit`, the raw-git drive-around the adapter contract forbids, and **the trial agent did exactly that**. It copies `setup`'s *real* mold (`setup.rs:949-1017` — pathspec `git add`, explicitly *"never a blanket `git add -A`"*, idempotent no-op on clean re-run) and **adds the opt-out flag setup lacks**. *(This also fires a separate recorded `(D)` — the managed-docs enforcement hook, `decisions-pending.md:181`, whose trigger was "the RC trials show agents bypassing the adapter at a rate that costs correctness." The evidence is in hand.)*

**Settled: fork 2 = the pack sentence + a PRE-commit left-out advisory print.** The charter said anything stronger *"engages the recorded M30/B1 'surfaced, not prevented' rationale."* **It over-scoped the record.** That rationale is about **refusing**, and its basis was the *pre-M30* danger of jigc sweeping unrelated files **in**; M30 **inverted** the danger (work left **out**). A pre-commit *print* is still **surfacing** — it does not engage the record at all; only a `--strict` refuse knob would (not built). The record's rationale stands; its scope in the charter was wrong. The mechanism is otherwise sound (empty index + dirty tree already **blocks** with a routed finding). The verified root cause of the trial's silent partial commits: the **methodology pack never says `git add`** — `dev-task`/`planning`/`increment`/`completion` compose **zero** mentions — while the dev pack says it twice, and the methodology finalize step **overloads "Stage" to mean "set the commit-doc slot"**, an active semantic collision in the one step where the git contract belongs. `finalize.md` gains the **sibling obligation** (every work-workflow's implement/finalize step states the contract) so the next pack cannot drop it again.

**Settled: fork 4 = prose demand only.** `maps-to-test` is a **pure prompting failure, not a capability gap** — the field is writable via `set-field` *and* `author`, round-trips through `doc show --format json`, and its `criterion-maps-to-test` check is **live and blocking** on a dangling anchor (exit 3, verified). Zero writes ever because the **only** agent-facing pack text naming it says *"leave `maps-to-test` off the item entirely"* (`author-migration-spec.yaml:50-53` — correct in *its* context, migrating a foreign spec that cites no test) and the step that actually mints specs never names it. No `criterion-without-test` store advisory: over a brownfield corpus that is the archetypal **non-drainable** advisory floor (it drains only by writing a test for every criterion ever authored), which is precisely the trigger condition for the **acknowledge-ledger deferred to 1.1** — a yes would pull that deferral forward by accident, one wave before the pin.

**Settled: fork 6 = a finalize advisory when the changelog gate is granted-and-unused.** The trial's ask was *"if it's optional, I'll skip it; if it matters, gate it."* P5's step-split repairs the *discoverability* bug regardless (verified through the real binary: `single-task` → 1 changelog paragraph, `implement-from-spec` → 0, `sub-task` → 0), leaving the soft-gate question genuinely separable. The advisory keys on **gate-granted-and-unused**, never on the CLI adjudicating whether a diff is user-facing — that is judgment, and the determinism boundary forbids it. Surfaces without refusing.

**Settled: the P6 slug line is an identity-model change and leaves the papercut batch.** The charter's *"mint-time only"* is an **unchecked claim and it is false**: `slugify` is a recognition-by-renormalization predicate at four **production** sites over **committed bytes** — the parse path (`parse.rs:385`, where a mismatch is a **whole-doc parse abort**), the splice path (`write.rs:3263`), validate (`validate.rs:1452`), and — the irony — **`migrate_corpus.rs:470`, the migration engine's own idempotency guard**. The tool that would have to repair a slug change is built on the function being changed. **Applying the exact chartered change: `cargo test -p engine` → 667 passed / 0 failed.** The entire engine goes green on a change to the function that mints every id in every corpus, because **all five "fences" are blind** — `golden_table`'s 18 cases contain **zero** inputs with `/`, `.`, or an edge `and`/`or` (it does not need re-pinning; it needs **extending**), the proptests test shape invariants that survive any separator map, and `cap_truncates_at_word_boundary`'s oracle `slugify_uncapped` is a **hand-copied shadow of the separator map** that drifts silently. The only thing that caught the change was **four CLI flow tests that hardcode a task id in a string literal**. `slugify` is in **no schema-hash and no manifest** (grepped: zero hits) — *the gate that blocks you from renaming a field waves through a change to the function that names every id* — and **no transform kind re-mints an id**, so *"migrate it later"* is **not available**. And the precedent is four weeks old, in the same file, under the same label: M41's Inc-8 "papercut batch," recorded pre-build as *"blast radius verified low,"* broke `slugify` idempotency, passed its own green gate, shipped a false rationale, and forced a **build halt** — after which we committed three separate DECISIONS entries saying, in order, *"a recorded rationale is a claim, not a fact"*, *"the cross-model trigger is the one-way door — a freeze, a pinned contract, **an identity model**"*, and *"an invariant guarded only by a proptest is not gate-enforced."*

**Split by half, because they do not deserve the same verdict.** The **`and`/`or` stopword half is CUT** — it fixes nothing broken (an id ending `-and` is stable, unique, resolvable) and it **pays** by retiring the fixed-point property of already-minted slugs (`slugify("search-and") = "search"`), which is exactly the M41 hazard, feeding the four renormalization sites. Premature generality; dropped. The **`/`·`.` half is a genuine information-destroying bug** — `auth/session` → `authsession` **fuses two words**, and dots **collide**: `1.0` and `10` both slug to `10`, a live collision class in a changelog whose release ids are minted from version strings. It ships as **its own governed increment**, **sequenced behind P4's item-`id` projection** (without which a mixed-generation corpus is *undecodable*: a driver's only route to an item's address is to slugify the title — the exact derivation this forks), carrying: a **`slug-rule-version`** recorded beside the schema manifest with a **pack-load fixed-point assert** (the slug rule is an **unversioned schema** governing every id in every corpus; make it a declared one), the **golden census over the changed characters**, the **shadow map killed**, the **`heading_matches` repair** (`parse.rs:385` re-slugs a **frozen** section id — `in-scope` → renders "In Scope" → re-slugs to `scope` → whole-doc parse abort; latent today because no shipped section id trips it, which is luck, not a fence — and M41's F5 sweep fixed the sibling site `extract_anchor` and **wrote this exact hazard into a code comment** at `parse.rs:1150-1154`, then missed this one), and a DECISIONS entry stating the **permanent generation split** out loud. *(Note the shipped escape hatch the charter never considered: `--slug` already exists on `start` and `rename`, so the task-mint half has a workaround today. Only the changelog release anchor has none — and that is the half touching the frozen `{#id}`.)*

**Settled: the freeze assert moves off the front door.** `assert_schema_freeze` has **one** production call site (`start.rs:859`, the compose path), so a drifted frozen schema lets **`jigc milestone create` write and commit new records** at exit 0 while `validate`/`describe`/`doc schema`/`migrate-corpus` all run clean. This is **not a new fork — it is a recorded deferral whose trigger fired** (`decisions-pending.md:177`: accepted because *"the embedded pack can't drift in a normal install"*, trigger *"packs are ever loaded from the filesystem in production"* — they are; the multi-pack surface shipped at M14 and reads pack directories from `.jigc/config/packs.yaml`). M42 additionally **builds a new milestone-record write verb on exactly the unguarded door**. The assert moves into the pack-source factory (`make_pack`), where ~22 call sites inherit it. *(Build-hygiene note that cost two auditors a false alarm: a stale `target/` carrying old `include_dir!` pack bytes can throw a **spurious** `HashMismatch` red; `cargo clean -p cli` clears it. The gate never goes spuriously **green** — a real pack edit is caught incrementally.)*

**Milestone shape:** one milestone, sequenced risk-first — it is one coherent claim (*the tool's own routes tell the truth*) and every piece serves it. Decomposition in [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 42.

### The Review — and the four defects the Settle itself shipped

The settled design went through **both** review passes before decompose: an independent same-model [design-reviewer](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md) **and** a cross-model **codex** pass (the recorded trigger fired on **all four** of its clauses at once — *a freeze, a pinned contract, an identity model, a stored format*; see 2026-07-11 → the cross-model trigger). **Both found blocking defects, overlapping only partially — the cross-model pass earned its cost for the second wave running.** Four settled calls were **wrong** and are corrected here; the Settle above is left standing and the corrections are recorded *as corrections*, because a silent fix teaches nobody.

1. **The base-guard fix does NOT kill the wedge — I over-corrected.** The Settle called the milestone independence constraint a *"phantom manufactured by an over-broad guard."* Half true. The guard **is** one predicate too narrow (record bookkeeping deadlocks for no reason, and widening it to accept **any** milestone-record path is still right) — **but the constraint underneath it is real.** A milestone finalize **commits code** (`cli/milestone.rs:1324-1360`; `has_diff == false` is itself a hard block), and a milestone's base is pinned at `create` and **never re-pinned** (`:203`) — so once *any* milestone finalizes, every other live milestone's `base..HEAD` holds a **code** commit and is wedged again, permanently. Inc 7's chartered acceptance (*"two interleaved milestones both finalize"*) was **unsatisfiable**. The true property: **a live milestone is invalidated by any code commit landing after its base** — another milestone's finalize, an ordinary `jigc task finalize`, a `rename`, a human's own `git commit`. **That is the M31 worktree-combine guard doing exactly its job.** Settled: keep the widening, **narrow the claim to what it buys**, and **route the real constraint honestly** (today it is unrouted — `finalize.base-mismatch` says *"discard"*, i.e. throw the work away). No base-repin verb; a `milestone rebase` is deferred to its trigger. **The corrected lesson, which is sharper than the one I first wrote:** the tell was never *"the rule is phantom."* The tell was **"the rule has no route."**
2. **The managed-vs-foreign discriminator was broken (codex).** The Settle keyed it on `record.get(&rel).is_some()` — but the file-state record lives in **gitignored, rebuildable `.jigc/state`**, so on a **fresh clone of a managed repo** it is empty and **every managed doc looks foreign**: the tool would tell a teammate to `ingest` their own committed corpus. A discriminator must key on **committed** state. Settled: **the `schema-version` stamp** — stamped ⇒ managed (below-version ⇒ `migrate-corpus`, exit flips); unstamped **and** unparseable against any known version ⇒ foreign (adoption route, **stays exit-0**). The v0-managed objection (`validation.md:341`) is **real but bounded** — M34 shipped the v0→v1 stamp migration for every doctype, so an unstamped *managed* doc exists only in a corpus that never ran it, a population enumerable pre-1.0. Recorded as **a declared bound with an expiry**, not a silent assumption.
3. **The exit flip had no mechanism, and would have fired on a stock brownfield repo.** The version break is emitted as `schema-conformance.field-value-conformant` (`validate.rs:738-750`) — **the same code as an invalid `status` enum on any ADR** — and `validation.md:159` *pins* "no new check id." So the flip would have keyed on a code shared with ordinary content drift (violating the masking-trap rationale the Settle said stands **untouched**) or on a **route-string prefix**. And nothing excluded the *foreign* arm, so `jigc validate` would have gone **non-zero on a stock Keep-a-Changelog repo that had only run `jigc setup`** — the very failure the Settle caught for the *route* and failed to carry across to the *exit code it was minting in the same breath*. Settled: **mint `schema-conformance.schema-version-current`** (intrinsic + keyed), revising `:159`'s pin by engaging its rationale — the pin was right that a version break needs no new *family*, wrong that it needs no new *id*: a stale stamp and an invalid enum value are **different facts with different consequences**, and collapsing them made the version break **undetectable to any machine consumer**, which is the thing M42 exists to fix. The flip is conditioned on the **managed** arm.
4. **The empty-diff backstop's false-refusal class was far bigger than the Settle closed.** `PresentationOnly` covered `description`/`usage`/`hint`. But for a leaf present in **both** schemas the classifier inspects **only `card` and `of`** (`schema_diff.rs:298-320`, `:250-273`) — so `optional: false→true`, `default:`, `set:`, `inverse:`/`inverse-card:`, `check:`, and `title-names-symbol` **all** move the hash, classify to `[]`, and would have been **falsely refused — unshippable**. The Settle made the argument for **one member of the class and never swept the rest** — the same un-enumerated-sibling failure this wave keeps finding, committed *in the fix for it*. Settled: define the backstop's **structural projection** explicitly as the **conformance-relevant** one (section set + ordering; slot presence + requiredness; field set + requiredness + type + enum members + cardinality); everything outside it folds to zero bytes and ships. And the two conformance-relevant flags get named kinds: `optional: false→true` (relax) is a safe **no-op kind**; **`optional: true→false` (tighten) is a real `ProseNeeding`** — it can render a conformant doc **non-conformant** — **a sixth hole nobody had named**, which today diffs to `[]` and silently strands.

**Two more the reviews caught, both recorded-rationale failures of exactly the kind the 2026-07-11 rule forbids:** `AddedItemField` was specified against **`write::set_item_field`**, which is **update-only** and **refuses when the field is absent** (`write.rs:1382-1386`) — i.e. on **every item, by definition of the kind**; the insert-capable primitive is `set_item_field_or_insert` (`:3186-3216`), a different function with a different error type. The *"already-shipped / ~90 LOC"* estimate hung on the wrong function. (And the semantics the wrong cite hid: an **optional-no-default** item field must be a **byte no-op** — an item without the bullet already conforms — not "every item spliced.") And **`corpus-migration.md:51` still pinned family 5 as report-only/exit-0 *including* version-mismatch**, the exact opposite of the new exception — the M42 pass edited the bullet *beside* it and left the bullet that **owns the property** contradicting it. That is the M33 `prd→spec` shape, which halted a build.

**Also folded:** the `schema.location` census was **still incomplete** under the completeness obligation M42 itself declared (`start.rs:1793` `committed_store` — the `{{store.…}}` compose-time resolver — plus eight more sites); `create.gate-blocked` was declared *nullable-by-contract* while the contract claims **unique-per-instance** keys — two distinct blocked creates in one task collide on `(code, null)`, **the same defect class codex caught in this same contract at M41, reintroduced in the fix for it**; `doc list` inherited the foreign-squatter problem on the same enumerator; the item-block `card` widen ships a ✅ the classifier does not honour; and the increments were ordered to ship, for two commits, **the exact "strictly worse" false-route state the design names by that phrase** (reordered: the walk-union lands first).

**The honest summary:** the Settle got twelve forks right and **shipped four defects of its own**, three of them the *same failure modes it was built to fix* — an un-enumerated sibling, a recorded-but-unchecked rationale, and a contract claim contradicted by the code. The reviews are why they are not in the build. **This is the strongest argument yet for the two-reviewer gate, and for the cross-model trigger being the one-way door.**

## 2026-07-11 — A recorded rationale is a claim; and the cross-model trigger is the one-way door

Two more methodology fold-backs from the M41 build, siblings of the proptest lesson below.

**(1) A recorded rationale is a claim, not a fact** — now in [dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → Why this shape. A justification written into `DECISIONS.md`, a doc-comment, or a commit message is **load-bearing**: the next reader (human *or* agent) trusts it and **stops questioning the choice**. M41 produced **two false rationales in one wave** — the increment that retired `slugify`'s idempotency claimed *"the fixed-point set was exactly the valid-slug set within the caps"* (false, and it is *why* the un-reconciled proptest went unnoticed for two increments), and the increment that keyed `ref-resolves` on a slug-only fragment wrote a doc-comment claiming it was *"so two dangling targets yield distinct keys"* (backwards — the full `<type>:<slug>` is strictly *more* distinct). Both passed a green gate and an independent same-model review. **A confident falsehood is worse than an admitted gap: it disables the next reader's skepticism.** Rule: never record a rationale you have not checked; an honest "unverified" is cheap.

**(2) The cross-model review's trigger is the one-way door** — sharpened in [milestone-planning-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md) → Review. The existing decision **stands** (a human-approved *suggestion*, never auto-run — it costs and isn't universally available; that rationale is unchanged). What changes is *when to surface it* and *why*. **Third data point:** codex found **four real stable-key collisions** in the `command-output-contract` — `inverse-cardinality` keyed one-per-doc when the code fans it per-relation, `schema-conformance`/`section-missing` with no discriminating fragment, `mention-resolves` left literally unpinned, `file-state` mis-classed as URI-form — every one verified against the code, **in an artifact the same-model `design-reviewer` had already read and blessed** (it found 6 good findings, and missed these). **The trigger is now the one-way-door lens the project already reasons in** (a freeze, a pinned contract, an identity model, a stored format), not the vaguer "high-stakes." **And the failure mode is named:** the same-model pass did not merely *miss* the defects — it **ratified the author's own wrong premise** (I specified a slug-only key fragment; the reviewer accepted it; the builder implemented it *and confabulated a justification*). Shared priors don't just overlook mistakes — they bless them, and the build then hardens them into code plus a false comment. Without the cross-model pass, a defective key would have frozen into a 1.0 contract.

## 2026-07-11 — A proptest is not a gate: a load-bearing invariant needs a deterministic case

**Methodology fold-back from the M41 build.** The dev-workflow gate's `cargo test` runs the property/fuzz suites over **random** inputs, so a green gate means *"no counterexample was sampled this run,"* **not** *"the invariant holds."* An invariant guarded **only** by a proptest is therefore **not gate-enforced** — and M41 proved it the expensive way: Increment 8's edge-stopword drop broke `slugify` idempotency ("a slug is a fixed point of normalization" — a standing invariant on jigc's **identity-mint** function), **passed its own increment's green gate** because that run didn't sample a counterexample, and surfaced only two increments later when Inc 9's run happened to hit it and persisted the shrink seed (making it deterministic). The break was compounded by a second failure: Inc 8 *retired* the invariant by silence — it left the `idempotent` proptest standing-but-unreconciled and recorded a rationale ("the fixed-point set was exactly the valid-slug set within the caps") that is **demonstrably false**. Had the build agent not refused to mask the red (it declined to discard the regression seed, calling that "masking a discovered production-path defect"), a non-idempotent identity-mint function would have shipped in rc.5 and gone into the adoption trial.

**The rule, now in [dev-workflow.md](implementation/dev-workflow.md) → Gate + *A proptest is not a gate*:** **(1)** a load-bearing invariant gets a **deterministic** case *alongside* its proptest — the proptest **explores**, the point test **enforces**; **(2)** an invariant is never retired by silence — a change that means to drop one must say so, reconcile the test in the same commit, and state a rationale it has actually checked. **Randomized coverage is a finder, not a fence.** *(Why not "ban proptests" or "seed them deterministically": the exploration is genuinely valuable — it *found* this bug, eventually — and pinning a fixed seed would trade a real finder for a weak fence. The fix is to add the fence, not remove the finder.)*

**The rule applied — a sweep of all 24 `proptest!` blocks, and `slugify` was NOT the lone gap.** Every other declared big invariant turned out golden-backed (the #1-risk round-trip over the dev pack by `golden_tricky_fixture_no_op_write` + the per-doctype `canonical`/`spec_roundtrip`/`nested_roundtrip` modules; deterministic composition by `pack_source_determinism.rs`; transactional writes by the `validate_after` module) — **but one real instance of the same hazard remained**: `render(parse(x)) == x` **plus the LF/CRLF parsed-shape equality** over the **nine shipped methodology schemas** was guarded by **proptest alone** (`write.rs` `methodology_roundtrip` — the module carried *no* `#[test]`), with deterministic backup for only 4 of 9 via `migrate_methodology.rs`. So `deferral-ledger` / `dogfood-record` / `research` / `idea` / `milestone-record` — half the doctype corpus, and exactly what the adoption trial authors — could have broken jigc's **#1-risk invariant** and passed a green gate. **Now fenced** (`108cca3`): a table-driven deterministic fixture set over all nine (populated + empty-repeatable + present/absent-optional arms + the BOM/CRLF canonicalization ledger), each with an `insta` golden, plus a coverage test that fails if a tenth persisted doctype ever skips a row; the `is_slug(slugify(x))` *composition* pinned too (`c7ed5a3`). **The sweep found no live defect** — the invariant was intact, only unfenced. Re-verified **1743 / 0**. *(The fixtures are red-meaningful: perturbing the product writer's anchor gap and header fence each fired, and the fixture assert fences independently of the snapshot, so a blind-accepted golden cannot mask a regression.)*

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 8 · T1 built: slug-cap legibility (V7 + F5), and the `extract_anchor` recognizer fix it forced

Shipped V7 (`cap_chars` retreats to the last complete word via `rfind('-')` on a mid-word cut; a single `-`-less long word still hard-truncates at `MAX_CHARS`, the `NAME_MAX` backstop) + F5 (a conservative leading/trailing edge-stopword drop — `a`/`an`/`the`/`of`/`to`/`in`/`on`/`at`/`by`/`for`, greedy at each edge, medial untouched — applied after the 5-word cap). **Elaboration the planning blast-radius missed:** F5 **retires the `slugify`-fixed-point ⟺ `is_slug` equivalence** the codebase leaned on — `is_slug("a-0")` yet `slugify("a-0") == "0"`. `parse.rs::extract_anchor` recognized a well-formed `{#id}` anchor via `slugify(inner) == inner`, so under F5 a valid frozen anchor with a leading/trailing-stopword id (`{#a-0}`, `{#a-plugin-surface}`) was wrongly rejected as malformed **on the production parse path** — a byte-stability/round-trip regression on committed docs. Fix (uniquely determined by the locked design: `is_slug` **is** the recognition predicate, `slugify` the minter): `extract_anchor` now recognizes via `is_slug`. Behaviour-preserving for every pre-F5 anchor and strictly correct post-F5; malformed detection (`{#Bad Id}`, `{#a--0}`) is unchanged (`is_slug` rejects them). **Correction (triage, same day):** this entry originally claimed "the fixed-point set was exactly the valid-slug set within the caps" — that was never the point of the fix and, worse, it papered over a real defect this increment *introduced*: applying the F5 edge-stopword drop **only before** the char cap (step 8) left `slugify` **non-idempotent** — the char cap's word-boundary retreat (V7) can truncate at a boundary that *exposes a fresh trailing edge stopword* step 6 never saw (counterexample `slugify("…") == "aa0-0a0aaaaa0aaa0aa-a"`, whose second pass drops the `-a`), which is a latent identity-corruption footgun and broke the `slug.rs` `idempotent` proptest. Corrected design: the edge-stopword drop is **also applied as a final step after the char cap** (`slugify` step 9, via the extracted `drop_edge_stopwords`), so mint output carries no edge stopword and is a `slugify` fixed point **by construction** — F5 (stopword drop) and V7 (word-boundary retreat) are both preserved, `is_slug`/`extract_anchor` unchanged, the `idempotent` proptest reinstated (a deterministic point regression added). Added a parse-path regression golden (`stopword_edge_anchor_is_recognized_not_malformed`) and corrected the now-false invariant line in `is_slug`'s doc. Fixture repairs across CLI flow/e2e tests + two engine milestone-join fixtures: intents/titles whose slug now drops an edge stopword (`move the session cache to a` → `move-the-session-cache`, `a fresh second task` → `fresh-second-task`, `enforce the rate limit at the gateway` → `enforce-the-rate-limit`, item titles `Criterion A/B` → `Criterion Alpha/Beta`, area `A area` → `Apex area` — a leading `a` can no longer mint an `a-`prefixed id at all). Full gate green.

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 7 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 7](implementation/roadmap.md) (V5 + N2 — `set-field --unset` + the `[]` non-ref-scalar reject; [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → the `--unset` verb + the `[]` reject) into **2 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `ec2efe9` (Inc 1–6 built; tree clean). The two grouped-scope bullets map: **T1** = the splice-remove op + the requiredness/stamp guard + the empty-value route repoint (V5); **T2** = the `check_opaque_scalar` bracket-reject (N2). V5 first (the riskier net-new engine primitive; and N2's reject route can then point at the now-existing `--unset`). No design-doc task — this increment is code-only per the grouped scope; the write-commands.md fold-back rides Inc 9 (the roadmap's docs fold-back).

**Verified bases (facts against the code at `ec2efe9`, not assumed):**

- **No splice-remove primitive exists — net-new, flagged.** `remove_item` deletes whole item blocks; `set_field_validated` (`write.rs:4983`) only splices a present value span or *inserts* an absent field line — neither removes a field line. So `--unset` needs a fresh byte-stable field-line splice-remove, mirroring `set_field_validated`'s header-vs-body split: a **header (front-matter)** field removes its `key: value` line from the `---` block (the inverse of `insert_front_matter_field`); a **body/item field group** removes the `- key: value` bullet and, when it was the **last** field, drops the whole `\n\n<!-- fields -->` group — the sentinel is emitted **iff ≥1 field has a value** (`write.rs:24,296-306`, `FIELD_SENTINEL = "<!-- fields -->"` `:123`), so the last-field removal MUST drop it or the canonical byte form breaks (the #1 retired invariant). The primary proof field, adr `cites-code`, is a **header** field (`adr.yaml:22`, in the `status` header section), so the sentinel-drop path needs a **body/item** fixture field to exercise it — cover both in engine units.

- **The guard is NOT `is_author_required` alone — the `default:` trap is load-bearing.** The scope's shorthand "reject author-required / `set:`-stamped" is **insufficient** for the named `#status` reject: adr `status` is an enum with `default: proposed` (`adr.yaml:19`), and `is_author_required` returns **false** for any field carrying a `default:` or `set:` (`validate.rs:1826-1847`; `required-field-present` treats a defaulted field's absence as conformant — `validate.rs:21-24`). So a guard keyed on `is_author_required` alone would **wrongly allow** `#status --unset`. The correct eligibility predicate that satisfies all four named cases is: **allow unset iff `!is_author_required(field) && field.default.is_none() && field.set.is_none()`** — equivalently, **reject** when the field is author-required **OR** carries a `default:` **OR** carries a `set:` deriver. Witnesses: `status` rejected via the `default` arm; the engine-injected `schema-version` stamp rejected via the `set` arm (`schema.rs:585,591,604-610` — `set: schema-version`; unsetting it corrupts the freeze/version gate); adr `cites-code` allowed (a `code-anchor` = `FieldType::Pack`, `is_author_required` false, no default/set — its absence is conformant, `required-field-present` never checks a Pack field); an optional `0..*` ref like `supersedes` allowed (already clearable via `[]`). Because `is_author_required` is false whenever `default`/`set` is present, the two extra arms are what actually reject `status`/`schema-version` — pin the predicate, and PROVE all four cases as red steps rather than trusting the shorthand.

- **N2's reject is one atomic unit with a `check_ref` reorder (the gate coupling).** `check_scalar` (`write.rs:4674`) routes `String|OwnedLocation` and non-code-anchor `Pack` scalars straight to `check_opaque_scalar` (`:4748`), and `check_ref`/`check_code_anchor` **call `check_opaque_scalar` first** (`:4778,:4883`). A `[]` on a string reaches `check_opaque_scalar`, passes (non-empty, no control char), and splices literal `[]` garbage (`--value "[]"` on `#string-field` = the footgun). Adding the bracket-reject **inside `check_opaque_scalar`** is the scoped fix — but it **breaks `check_ref`**, whose contract is to *accept* `[]` (empty list = no edges, clean) and `[a, b]` (list-replace): the existing unit assertions `check_value(&r_to_adr, &scalar("[]")).is_ok()` and `…"[adr:a, adr:b]"…is_ok()` (`write.rs:5509-5511`) go RED. The **repair in the same motion** is to reorder `check_ref` to strip/validate the bracket-list form **before** delegating to the floor. So the `check_opaque_scalar` reject + the `check_ref` reorder are inseparable (change-A-breaks-the-gate-that-change-B-fixes) — one task, one commit. `check_code_anchor` needs no change: a `[]` has no `#`, so it correctly rejects at the newly-guarding floor (code-anchor is a non-ref scalar, per N2).

Ordered tasks (id · subject · observable done-criterion):
- **T1 · engine+CLI: `set-field --unset` — the byte-stable field-line splice-remove + the eligibility guard + the empty-value route repoint (engine + CLI).** Add a net-new byte-stable field-line splice-remove in `write.rs` (header front-matter line removal; body/item bullet removal that drops the `<!-- fields -->` group when it clears the last field), gated by the eligibility guard (**allow iff `!is_author_required(field) && field.default.is_none() && field.set.is_none()`**); wire `--unset` onto `DocCommand::SetField` (make `--value` `Option`, exactly-one-of `--value`/`--unset`) + the `run_set_field`/`apply_field_target` unset branch; repoint the **empty-value** (`--value ""`) reject's route to name `jigc doc set-field <addr> --unset`. *Done:* named `write.rs` unit tests — removing an **optional header** field line is byte-stable + re-parses; removing the **last** field of a **body/item** field group drops the sentinel (+ its leading blank lines) byte-stably; removing a **non-last** field keeps the sentinel + siblings; **and** a real-binary integration test — `jigc doc set-field <adr>#cites-code --unset` on an adr carrying a `cites-code` value clears it and the doc re-conforms (`doc show`/`validate` shows it absent, byte-stable), `#status --unset` **blocks** with a route, `#schema-version --unset` **blocks**, and the `--value ""` reject's route now names `--unset`; full gate (`cargo build` · `cargo test` · `clippy -D warnings` · `fmt --check`). *Red today:* `--unset` is an unknown clap arg (exit 2) and no splice-remove primitive exists. *(files: `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`.)*
- **T2 · engine+CLI: the `[]` non-ref-scalar reject — the `check_opaque_scalar` bracket-reject + the `check_ref` reorder (N2) (engine + CLI).** Add the bracket-form reject to `check_opaque_scalar` (a non-ref scalar `--value "[]"` — the misapplied ref-clear idiom — rejects instead of splicing literal `[]`); reorder `check_ref` to validate/accept the bracket-list form **before** delegating to the floor so list refs still clear via `[]` and replace via `[a, b]`; route the reject at `--unset` (the scalar has no list to clear). *Done:* named `write.rs`/`doc.rs` tests — `set-field <string-field> --value "[]"` **rejects** (`write.malformed-value`, old value untouched) and a `code-anchor --value "[]"` rejects; the existing `check_value(&r_to_adr, "[]").is_ok()` / `"[adr:a, adr:b]".is_ok()` assertions (`write.rs:5509-5511`) **stay green** (the reorder is the in-task repair) and a `0..*` ref still clears via `[]` through the real binary; a normal non-bracket string value still passes; the reject's route names `jigc doc set-field <addr> --unset`; full gate. *Red today:* `--value "[]"` on a string splices literal `[]` (accepted); and the naive reject alone reds the two ref assertions — proving the atomic coupling. *Depends on T1 (the `--unset` route target must exist). (files: `crates/engine/src/write.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`.)*

*Why this cut:* V5 (the net-new splice-remove op + its guard) and N2 (the value-check bracket-reject) are genuinely distinct concerns, each gate-green alone, so two tasks — not folded, since neither breaks a gate the other repairs. Within each task the true atomic coupling is contained: T1 carries the header-vs-body splice-remove + the guard + the CLI flag + the route repoint as one indivisible feature (the guard is intrinsic to the op's correctness — shipping the splice-remove without the `schema-version`/`default` guard would corrupt the freeze gate / a defaulted field); T2 carries the `check_opaque_scalar` reject **with** the forced `check_ref` reorder in one commit (the existing ref-`[]` assertions are the proof they're inseparable). V5 ordered first so N2's reject route points at a real `--unset`. The smallest set delivering both grouped-scope bullets + the *Proves*, no creep into Inc 9's flow-42 acceptance. Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 41 Increment 7. **Status: planned; hand to the executor.**

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 7 / T1 build: `set-field --unset`

Built the net-new byte-stable field-line splice-remove (V5). New engine primitives in `write.rs`: `unset_field` (header front-matter line removal, or a simple-body bullet via the shared `unset_group_field`) + `unset_item_field` (item chain, scoped to the item's own-leaf region), plus the validated wrappers `unset_field_validated`/`unset_item_field_validated`. **Group-drop is `[sentinel.start - 1 .. list_range.end)`** — `append_field_group` always emits exactly `\n\n<!-- fields -->` before the sentinel, so removing one of the two leading `\n` leaves the body terminated by a single `\n`, byte-identical to the canonical no-field form (uniform across header-less/prose/item bodies). Eligibility guard = **reject when `field.set.is_some()` OR `is_author_required(field)` OR `field.default.is_some()`** — the `set:` arm's message is stamp-specific for `schema-version` (names the freeze gate); routed via `Finding::block`. CLI: `--value` is now `Option`, `--unset` added with clap `conflicts_with`/`required_unless_present` (exactly-one-of); `run_unset_field`/`apply_unset_target` dispatch by `FieldTarget`; the empty-`--value` reject's route repointed to name `jigc doc set-field <addr> --unset` (`repoint_empty_value`). New `DocAck::UnsetField` (op `set-field`, `unset: true`). Guard lives in the engine wrapper (self-protecting: no caller can corrupt the freeze/defaulted-field state). Tests: 7 engine units (byte-stable header/middle removal, item last-drop-sentinel + non-last-keeps, absent→NotPresent, eligible-clear + default/set rejects) + 4 real-binary integration arms (`set_field_unset.rs`: byte-stable clear identical to pre-value buffer + re-conforms, `#status`/`#schema-version` block with route, `--value ""` route names `--unset`) + clap parse. Full gate green (1710 tests / 0 failed). No design-doc change (write-commands.md fold-back rides Inc 9). Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M41 Increment 7.

The grouped-scope bullet's two clauses map: **T1** = the extract seam + filename unit + the dispatch arm (the probe code + its reds); **T2** = the design-doc promotion (validation.md subsection + the ideas de-park). The through-the-real-binary Vue arm is **not** in this increment — it rides the wave-wide flow 42 in Inc 9 (per the roadmap); this increment's *Proves* is discharged at the probe-unit level (`cargo test --manifest-path …`), the M27/M28/M29 grammar-addition precedent.

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Inc 5 T3: the authored value-remap map is CLI-threaded; the detect-side premise corrected to the placement bound

Landed the CLI half of F4: `migrate_corpus.rs` now threads the authored old→new map into each emitted `ValueRemapped` before the engine fold (`enrich_value_remaps` + the `authored_remap` table keyed by `(doctype, section, field)`; the `with_stamp_default` precedent), so the below-version `deferral-ledger` migrates `D→Decision`/`I→Idea` **byte-faithful**, value-bumps the stamp `1→2`, and is idempotent on re-run. A bump with **no** map entry keeps the classifier's empty map → the T1 driver blocks loudly (never a silent strand). Enrichment sits on the below-version path only (the sole one that can surface a `ValueRemapped`: the stamp-absent path diffs `strip_stamp(to)` against `to`, whose members are identical). The e2e (`migrate_corpus_value_remap.rs`) proves byte-faithfulness by a **round-trip oracle** — the v1 fixture is the exact-inverse downgrade of a *real* rendered v2 canonical doc, so a faithful remap reproduces it exactly (drives the file on disk, not a reconstruction). **Correction to the T3 plan's "routed `migrate` by the store detector before" premise:** it is **false** for `deferral-ledger` — a *placement* doctype (`location: None`), which the family-5 store sweep skips (the bound recorded 2026-07-10 M40 Inc 5 T5, and by `methodology_corpus_stamp.rs` for the placement roadmap). `validate` is empirically clean for the v1 fixture (no `field-value` route), so the test asserts the **true** behavior — verb-migratable but not `validate`-routed — rather than forcing a false precondition; extending family 5 to placement version-mismatch stays the recorded known bound, out of T3's file scope.

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 4](implementation/roadmap.md) (V3+V6+V11 — the `doc author` discoverability cluster; [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) → Why json is a contract here) into **two ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `26a3741` (Inc 3 built; tree clean). The two grouped-scope groups map one-to-one: **T1** = the `doc schema` projection change (the two `ContractField` additions + text-listing mirror + version bump/goldens/design-doc); **T2** = the `doc author` long-help payload-shape example. They are independent, gate-green apart, and touch disjoint code (the schema-projection path vs a clap doc-comment) — no atomic-gate coupling.

**Verified bases (facts against the code at `26a3741`, not assumed):** the two projected fields both **exist to project** — enum members live at `Field.of: Option<Vec<String>>` (`schema.rs:259`) with real witnesses across all three inline goldens (`adr.status` `of: [proposed, accepted, superseded]` `adr.yaml:19`; `dogfood-record.case`/`.verdict`; `changelog` item `category`), and the field→section info is **exactly what today's flattening discards** — `schema_contract` merges every simple section's `declared` fields into one flat `fields` vec (`doc.rs:1703-1709`) and `contract_field` (`doc.rs:1737`) takes only the field, never `section.id`. **`ContractField` is the shared projection struct** (`doc.rs:1641`) reused at both the top-level flat `fields` and inside item templates (`contract_item` `doc.rs:1756`), so the two adds are additive to one struct — and because item fields already carry their owning section *structurally* (nested under `sections[].item`), `section` is the natural reading of "un-flattening" only for the **top-level** flat list (item fields keep it absent), while `of` is universal (an enum is an enum at any depth — the `changelog` item `category` witness needs it). The **version bump is not a fork**: `contract-version` is hardcoded `1` (`doc.rs:1728`, doc'd "1 at ship" `:1617-1619`) and the locked design pins "`contract-version` bumps on **any** structural change to this projection" with **no additive carve-out** ([doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) → the pinned JSON block's closing sentence), so adding `of`/`section` keys → 2; the goldens that break in lockstep are the **three inline byte-verbatim** literals in `doc_schema.rs` (`DOGFOOD_RECORD_JSON`/`CHANGELOG_JSON`/`ADR_JSON`) plus the behavioral assert `value["contract-version"] == 1` (`:414`) and the design block's `"contract-version": 1` (`doc-read-surface.md:68`) — so the code change (add keys + bump) and all golden/assert/design repins are **one atomic gate-green unit** (T1); the plain non-contractual listing (`schema_listing`/`push_field_line` `doc.rs:1778-1820`) prints id/type/default/set/`*` today with **no enum members**, so the "text-listing mirror" is a real edit inside T1. For T2, the payload grammar is `title:` + `sections:` (list of `{id, set, items}`), `set:` (leaf key→value map), `items:` (list of `{title, set, sections}`) — verified from `AuthorPayload`/`PayloadSection`/`PayloadItem` (`author.rs:64-92`); the current `Author` long help (`doc.rs:~134-160`) explains the slot `<<…>>`/block-scalar convention but **not** the top-level grammar, and **no `--help` golden exists**, so T2 must ship its own asserting test (a bare help edit has no red step).

Ordered tasks (id · subject · observable done-criterion):
- **T1 · `doc schema` projects enum members + field→section + version bump 1→2 (CLI + design)** — `cargo test -p cli --test doc_schema` green with: the `adr` golden's `status` field carrying its enum members (`of: ["proposed","accepted","superseded"]`); every **top-level** flattened field carrying its owning simple-section id (`section`), item-nested fields unchanged; `of` present on every enum field including the `changelog` item `category`; `contract-version` = **2** across all three inline goldens + the behavioral `value["contract-version"]` assert (`:414`); the plain `--format agent`/human listing showing an enum field's members; [doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md):68 block updated to `contract-version: 2` and the fields shape carrying `of`?/`section`; full gate (`cargo test` · `clippy -D warnings` · `fmt --check`) clean. *Red today:* goldens are `contract-version 1` with no `of`/`section`. *(files: `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/doc_schema.rs`, `design/doc-read-surface.md`.)*

*Why this cut:* two independent single-concern units — the read-contract projection (T1, one atomic code+golden+design unit because the inline goldens break the moment the emitted shape changes) and the disjoint help-string edit (T2, its own red via a new assertion) — the smallest set delivering both grouped-scope bullets with no gate-coupled merge.
