## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 4 · T1: `doc schema` projects enum members + field→section, contract-version 1→2

The pinned `doc schema --format json` projection now carries two new per-field keys and bumped its own version to **2** ([doc-read-surface.md](design/doc-read-surface.md) → Why json is a contract here). `of` = an `enum`'s legal members, **universal across depths** (an enum is an enum at top-level or inside an item template — the `changelog` item `category` witness needs it), so an agent reads the legal values straight from the contract, no failed-write probe. `section` = the owning simple-section id, **top-level only** by design: an item field already carries its section *structurally* (nested under `sections[].item`), so "un-flattening" applies only to the top-level flat `fields` list — `schema_contract` stamps `section` at the point it re-flattens each simple section's fields, and `contract_field` (shared with `contract_item`) defaults it to `None`. The bump is not a fork — the design pin says `contract-version` bumps on **any** structural change with **no additive carve-out**, so adding keys → 2; the code change (add keys + bump + text-listing enum-member mirror) and every golden/assert/design repin land as **one atomic gate-green unit** (the three inline byte-verbatim goldens in `doc_schema.rs` break the instant the shape moves). Two out-of-file-scope repins rode the same emitted-shape change (the `flow41_acceptance` Arm-4 behavioral `contract-version` assert + its name, and the `worked-examples`/design contract-version-1 mentions) — necessary consequences of the emitted contract moving, not scope creep. Full gate clean (1676-suite, 0 failed).

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 3 · T3: write-ack findings-as-data

Every `jigc doc` write verb now emits its intrinsic single-doc advisories as data in the `--format json` `DocAck` `findings[]` (`design/command-output-contract.md` → §2). One pure-function check qualifies today — `schema-conformance.surplus-sections-absent`, the only advisory taking just `(schema, staged-buffer)`, authoring-stage-agnostic — computed from the just-persisted buffer via a shared `write_ack_findings` helper that also flips each finding's `Location::address` fragment to the write's URI target (`<type>:<slug>#<fragment>`, the same `path→URI` flip `attribute_to_doc` installs, so `key.target` reads in URI normal form). Design elaborations worth pinning: (1) **`create` passes `findings: []` structurally, not by scanning** — its effect is the schema-generated skeleton (only declared sections, any in-location squatter blank-seeded), so it is provably surplus-free and holds no buffer to scan; `author` *does* scan its in-memory `buffer` (it chains leaf writes, so scanning is the honest uniform thing even though a strict-parsed payload is also surplus-free in practice). (2) **Completeness stays excluded**: `repeatable-populated`/`required-slot` are expected mid-authoring and the cross-doc/subprocess families answer a corpus question one write can't adjudicate — so `findings: []` means "no intrinsic single-doc advisory," **not** "validated" (the driver runs `jigc validate` for corpus-completeness). Agent-text acks stay terse (findings-as-data is the machine-JSON contract). `cargo test -p cli` green.

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 3 · T2: the universal advisory-route floor

Reified the no-op route as a value: the two route-less advisory constructors — `dangling_mention` (`schema-conformance.mention-resolves`) and `below_inverse_minimum` (`schema-completeness.inverse-cardinality`) — now carry **human repair routes** ("correct or drop the `#…` mention", "author a `<relation>` referrer of `<target>`"), the exact two-kind examples [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → §route names. Design elaboration worth pinning: the floor is scoped to the **validation/advisory** surface, **not** every `Finding` — a purely-positional parser *conformance* diagnostic (a `Severity::Blocking` finding raised before an address resolves) is the parser's own floor and legitimately keeps `route: null` (the `finding.rs` pinned envelope golden, left by T1, is unchanged). So the doc revisions ([validation.md](design/validation.md) → new "The advisory-route floor" subsection, superseding the `:35/:39/:50` "route optional / `none` fine" clauses; [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md) → the output-contract clause) engage the earlier rationale — a null was tolerated only where there is *no mechanical* route — and honor it by reifying that case as an explicit **informational** route ("no action needed") rather than an absence, never flattening a real repair into a no-op. The file-state informational advisories (`baseline-adopt`/`absorb`/`un-baselined`, in `file_state.rs`, outside this task's file scope) remain the informational kind to migrate; command-output-contract already owns the universal claim. `cargo test` green.

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 3 · T1: the stable `(code, target)` key

Landed the stable per-instance finding key. Design elaboration worth pinning: `key` is **derived, never stored** — `Finding::serialize` is hand-written (not `#[derive]`) and computes `key = {code, target}` from `code` + `Location::address` at projection time, so it is a **single source of truth that cannot drift** from the carried address (a stored twin would go stale on every `attribute_to_doc` re-address, and — critically — on every probe-wire *deserialize*, where a stored `key` would default to `None` while the address is set). Two free consequences: the `Finding` **`Debug`** projection is untouched (the 9 parse `.snap` goldens are Debug, not JSON — no churn), and the doc-code probe's own wire `Finding` struct + `ingest_probe_run` deserialize are untouched (the engine recomputes `key` on re-serialize). URI normalization rode the generalized `attribute_to_doc(findings, identity, rel_key)` path→URI flip — the address channel now carries `<type>:<slug>#<fragment>` (message keeps the `rel_key` filesystem path for the operator line); `file-state` stays path-keyed with **no code change** (its constructors already address the path, and `key.target` mirrors it). Per-family fragments per [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → the stable finding key. `cargo test` green (642 engine + full CLI suite, 0 failed).

## 2026-07-11 — M41 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 3](implementation/roadmap.md) (F1b + F2 — the stable finding key, findings-as-data on the write path, and the advisory-route floor; [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → the stable finding key / §findings, [validation.md](design/validation.md) → the route floor) into **three ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded at HEAD `af662d6` (Inc 2 built — the `DocAck` decomposition + the three envelope emitters landed; tree clean). The three grouped-scope bullets map one-to-one: **T1** = the key + URI normalization + fragment synthesis (engine); **T2** = the route-floor sweep across finding constructors + the two doc revisions; **T3** = the write-ack findings emit (CLI). Order **T1 → T2 → T3**: land the finding *identity* (key/target), then complete the finding *envelope* (universal route), then the CLI emits findings-as-data over that completed envelope — T3 needs both T1's `key.target` and T2's routed envelope to emit a contract-conformant surplus finding. **No atomic-gate coupling forces a merge** — each is independently gate-green: T1 leaves `route` untouched (no test requires a non-null route until T2), T2 leaves the key/target untouched, T3 is purely additive on the write path (write-acks emit `findings: []` today). T1 and T2 both edit the same two advisory constructors (`dangling_mention`/`below_inverse_minimum`) and the pinned finding golden serially, but neither breaks a test the other repairs — distinct concerns (identity vs route direction), honoring the increment's own `F1b + F2` split.

**Verified bases (facts against the code at `af662d6`, not assumed):** the path→URI flip generalizes `attribute_to_doc` (`validate.rs:1147`), which today prefixes a **filesystem-path** `rel_key` (`{location}{slug}.md`, `validate.rs:565`) — `(ty, slug)` is in hand at both re-parse callers: `schema_conformance_store` (`ty` from the `(ty, schema)` iter `:560`, `slug` from the `committed_slugs` loop `:564`) and `hollow_surplus_store` (`ty` from the iter `:667`, and the `<type>:<slug>` identity from `committed_instances` `:668` — currently **discarded** as `_identity`, and it **intentionally includes placement docs**, whose identity is `<type>:<type>` per `committed_instances` `index.rs:707-714`, so the flip resolves placement identity). The **route-less** constructors are exactly two, both advisory: `dangling_mention` (`index.rs:662`, `route: None`) and `below_inverse_minimum` (`index.rs:758`, `route: None`); `dangling` (`ref-resolves`, `index.rs:818`) **already carries a route**, and `surplus_sections_absent` (`validate.rs:1449`) **already carries a route** — so the advisory-floor sweep's net-new routes are the mention (a human repair: correct/drop) and the inverse-cardinality (a human repair: author a referrer), not the whole finding population. `surplus_sections_absent` (`validate.rs:1414`, `pub`) is a pure `(schema, source)` trailing-surplus check emitting `Location::at(line, 1)` with **no address** today, so T1 must synthesize its `#<surplus-heading>` fragment. Each write site (`run_set_field` `doc.rs:275`, and the six siblings) holds the resolved `schema` + the `edited` staged buffer + calls `persist` then `render::doc_ack`; the `DocAck` json arm hardcodes `findings: []` (`render.rs:648-671`) — so T3's surplus emit is derivable at each site with no re-parse. The route-floor universality (`route` never `null`) is **pinned by the locked design** ([command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → §route: two kinds, never null) — no fork; the executor applies the floor across constructors per that doc, and T2's done-criterion pins the advisory proof the roadmap Proves line names.

Ordered tasks (id · subject · observable done-criterion):
- **T1 · the stable `(code, target)` key + URI normalization + fragment synthesis (engine)** — an engine test asserts a `0..*` ref with two dangling targets emits **two** findings with **distinct** `(code, target)` keys (`type:slug#<relation>/<to-slug>` each); the re-parse families project URI targets via the generalized `attribute_to_doc` path→URI flip — `schema-conformance` → `#<section>/<field>`, `section-missing` → `#<section>`, `surplus` → `#<surplus-heading>` — with `mention` → `#<token>` (one keyed finding per `(doc, token)`), `inverse-cardinality` → `#<relation>` (per-relation, not one-per-doc), and `file-state` keyed by its filesystem path (the one exception; the flip resolves placement identity too); the pinned finding envelope golden carries `key: {code, target}`. `cargo test -p engine` green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{finding.rs,validate.rs,index.rs,parse.rs,file_state.rs}`; design: [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → the stable finding key.)*
- **T2 · the universal advisory-route floor + the two doc revisions (engine constructors + docs)** — a store-sweep (`jigc validate --format json`, or an engine store-families test) over a corpus carrying a **dangling mention** + a **below-inverse-min** doc emits **no** finding with `route: null`, and the dangling-mention finding's route names a **repair action** (human: correct/drop the mention), **not** the informational "no action needed"; [validation.md](design/validation.md) (the "route optional / `none` fine" clause, `:35/:39/:50`) + [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md) (the route-less-advisory clause, `:48`) revised to the two-kind explicit-route model (rationale engaged, not overridden). `cargo test` green. *(files: `crates/engine/src/{finding.rs,index.rs,validate.rs}`, `design/validation.md`, `design/assistant-adapter.md`; design: [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → §route.)*
- **T3 · write-ack findings-as-data: emit `surplus-sections-absent` on the successful write path (CLI)** — a CLI test authoring/creating a doc that leaves a **trailing surplus** H2 emits a `--format json` `DocAck` whose `findings[]` carries the `schema-conformance.surplus-sections-absent` finding (with `key.target` = `type:slug#<surplus-heading>` and its route), while a clean write emits `findings: []`; completeness (`repeatable-populated`, required-slot) and cross-doc families are **not** emitted (`findings: []` ≠ validated). `cargo test -p cli` green. *(files: `crates/cli/src/{doc.rs,render.rs}`; design: [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) → §2 findings-as-data + §findings.)*

*Why this cut:* the smallest serial set that lands the finding contract in dependency order — identity (T1), then the completed routed envelope (T2), then the CLI findings-as-data consumer (T3) — each a single concern with its own red, no gate-coupled merge. Cross-ref [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 41 Increment 3. **Status: planned; hand to the executor.**

- **T1** — add `task: Option<String>` to engine `ComposedWorkflow`, set it from the in-hand id at every producer (mint → `Some(minted.id)`; resume/reenter/migrate → the given id; router/orient/milestone no-task arm → `None`); the JSON view auto-surfaces `{"task": <id>|null, "text": …}`. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/compose.rs`, `crates/cli/src/start.rs`, tests. *Done-criterion:* `crates/cli/tests/start_compose.rs` — the router-path JSON test (`bare_intent_router_json_format_carries_no_footer`, `:840`) asserts `value["task"]` is `null`; a work-minting arm (Form D `--workflow single-task`) asserts `value["task"]` equals the minted id; every ComposedWorkflow construction site + engine tests recompile; full gate (`cargo test` · `clippy -D warnings` · `fmt --check`) clean. *Red:* today's composed JSON has no `task` key. *Why one task:* adding a struct field breaks every construction site + any `{text}`-shape golden at once — the field, its threading, and the golden repin are one inseparable gate-green unit.

## 2026-07-11 — M41 planning: decomposition

Cut [Milestone 41](implementation/roadmap.md) into **9 ordered increments**, grounded at HEAD 855c0b0 (code identical to the findings-verification sha 074110b — every commit since is `docs:`) and gated by the by-hand [planning gate-record](completions/artifacts/M41/planning-gate-record.md) (per-scope-item table, **no empty cells**). **Ordering** blends risk-first with one value exception: **V1 (the High silent-corruption fix) lands first** — trivial, independent, and it gates the on-rc.5 adoption-trial implementation half (a binary with a known silent-fold bug would pollute the trial); then the risky new engine surfaces (Inc 2–3 the command-output contract, Inc 5 the value-remap transform kind, Inc 6 Vue) before the low-risk mechanical batch (Inc 8), so integration risk surfaces early; acceptance + docs fold-back last (Inc 9). **Increment map:** 1 V1 templates · 2 F1a contract shell (composed task-id + `DocAck` decomposition + the three bare-string verbs into the envelope) · 3 F1b+F2 the stable `(code,target)` key + findings-as-data-on-write + the universal advisory-route floor · 4 V3+V6+V11 the `doc author` discoverability cluster · 5 F4 the `ValueRemapped` kind + `D`/`I` rename + first methodology snapshot · 6 F3 symbol-granular Vue · 7 V5+N2 `--unset` + the `[]` reject · 8 the papercut batch (V7/F5 slug · V8/V13 routes · V12 rename · V9 ingest · V10 arch-doc) · 9 flow 42 acceptance + docs fold-back. ## 2026-07-11 — M41 (rc.5 wave) planning Settle: the five forks + riders

The rc.5 charter's five `(D)` forks are settled with the human (all four capability-auditors + four gap-detectors + four robust-advocates ran; the gap pass reshaped every fork). The human's calls, maximal-robust across the board:

- **Fork 1 — the command-output machine contract: FULL PIN this wave.** rc.5 is the last wave before the 1.0 pin, and jigc's committed identity *is* the machine surface (a context compiler for coding agents; the agent built a Python driver over `--format json` in **both** trial repos). The robust-advocate's reframe holds: the one-way door is the *posture* (is this output a contract; how does it evolve), not the field count — and the project already answered exactly this for `doc show`/`doc schema`. So: **declare a command-output contract surface with its own doc home + evolution posture + version home** (new part-doc [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md)); **composed `start --format json` carries the minted task id** structurally (`{"task": <id>|null, "text": …}`); **`DocAck`'s opaque `address` string decomposes** into structured `{doctype, slug, section?, item?, leaf?}`; **findings-as-data emit on the successful write path** (today findings surface only on the error path — net-new). The human chose full-pin over the advocate's "stage the fields" — pin the whole driver contract now while the pre-1.0 additive window is open, rather than pay the versioned-extension tax post-pin. Reconciles the separately-deferred "stable `validate --format json` as a CI-gating contract" ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)) whose trigger fired (the driver is a non-agent orchestrator) — the findings envelope shape is pinned once, here, and `validate --format json` inherits it.
- **Fork 2 — the advisory acknowledge model: floor-rule now + defer the ledger + mint the stable finding-key.** The per-instance acknowledged-findings ledger is genuinely premature (the undrainable-floor class is *unmeasured today* — V4 drains the entire current steady-state floor of 9; a 1.1 ledger is purely additive, so no one-way door on the ledger file). Ship the **universal floor rule — every advisory carries a route** (revising [validation.md](design/validation.md)'s "route is optional / `none` is fine" and [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md)'s "route-less advisories say 'no action needed'" to reify "no action needed" as an *explicit informational route value*, honoring their rationale rather than overriding it). **Defer the ledger to 1.1, trigger-keyed** (an adopter corpus surfaces a measured, non-drainable steady-state advisory floor). **Rider, fired by Fork 1's full-pin:** mint a stable `(code, stable-target)` finding key *this wave* — pinning findings-as-data on today's unstable line/col `location` (`finding.rs`) would freeze a bad key into the 1.0 contract; the stable key is what makes findings-as-data a sound contract citizen. The future ledger homes as a **rebuildable cache** re-derivable from committed content-hashes (not a committed source of truth — the `.jigc`-is-workbench / repo-is-record split).
- **Fork 3 — `.vue` support: symbol-granular.** Extract the `<script>`/`<script setup>` block and resolve `#symbol` under the **already-vendored** `tree-sitter-typescript` (zero new dependency — the `tree-sitter-vue` route is the one carrying supply-chain risk against the probe's tree-sitter 0.26), **unioned** with a filename-component-name addressable unit (so `AppLayout.vue#AppLayout` *and* `#useCounter` resolve, `#DoesNotExist` blocks). Filename-only would force a bad horn — false-block real composables or ship false-green on fabricated script symbols — holing the flagship "a doc cannot claim code that doesn't exist" property on a mainstream stack at the 1.0 pin; and it delivers *less* than the CSS/YAML bar (both shipped their real addressable units). Existence-only resolution needs names, not offsets, so the extracted block's shifted byte offsets are irrelevant (spike-proven, ~7-line seam). Scope line: script symbols + filename component; **not** template `ref`s, scoped-style classes, or SFC macros (premature). Promote a first-class Vue addressable-units subsection into [validation.md](design/validation.md) (the CSS/YAML precedent) + de-park the tier-1 slice of [ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md](ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md).
- **Fork 4 — rename `deferral-ledger.kind` members `D`/`I` → `Decision`/`Idea`: INCLUDE, build the value-remap transform kind.** The charter's "routine bump, not a one-way door" premise is **false at HEAD**: the machinery to rename a frozen enum value does not exist (`schema_diff` inspects only `card` and drops repeatable→repeatable through its catch-all → an enum `of:` change classifies to an *empty* diff → a version bump strands the whole deferral-ledger corpus). So the value-remap kind gets built now-with-a-live-driver-and-safety-net or later-under-pressure against a live public corpus. Build a new `SchemaChange::ValueRemapped { section, field, map }` kind (the **first parameterized transform kind** — the old→new map is authored, not auto-derived from the schema pair) + classifier branch (enum `of:` delta on simple *and* repeatable-item fields) + driver branch + bootstrap the absent `packs/methodology/schema-snapshots/deferral-ledger.v1.yaml`. This closes a **general** migration-surface hole (adr.status, completion-record's enums need it too), proves the **never-once-driven methodology v1→v2 path** in the last pre-1.0 window, and spares the first public methodology corpus a permanent off-surface-semantics tax (`D`/`I`'s meaning lives only in a YAML comment invisible to every read surface; V3's projection makes them *discoverable*, not *legible*). Revise [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) — **not just the "value-remap not built" scope line** but the **"never a hand-written recipe / auto-derived from the schema pair"** property it asserts *absolutely* at two further points (`:89`, `:124`): `ValueRemapped`'s old→new map is *necessarily* authored (an enum rename is unrecoverable from the schema pair alone), so the revision draws the distinction **structural kinds auto-derive / value-semantic kinds carry an authored map** — the determinism *boundary* (CLI vs LLM) stays intact (the map is a deterministic CLI input, not an LLM call), but the narrower *auto-derivation* property does not hold for this kind, and the doc must not stand as self-contradiction (design-review A2). The "build a kind when a driver earns it" rule holds; D/I is the driver.
- **Fork 5 — slug stopwords: drop leading/trailing.** The V7 char-backstop bugfix (`cap_chars` word-boundary retreat) ships **unconditionally** either way. Stopwords are one-way *per corpus*, so the pre-1.0 window (smallest installed corpus) is when to decide; dropping leading/trailing `the`/`a`/`of`… is the robust ergonomic.

**Smaller decisions (folded in):** **N2 — `--value "[]"` on a non-ref scalar rejects** (the silent-`[]`-garbage footgun found in baseline: `check_ref`'s bracket handling doesn't guard non-ref scalars, so `set-field #string-field --value "[]"` splices literal `[]`) — close it in the V5 motion, a known hole one line from the surface being fixed. **N1 — the V1 post-parse fold advisory: DEFERRED** (the block-scalar template switch covers every *managed* authoring path; the advisory only backstops hand-authored/foreign payloads and would feed the very noise floor V15 drains — if ever built it must carry a route). **V5 `--unset` build notes:** needs a net-new byte-stable field-line splice-remove (no primitive exists — `remove_item` deletes whole blocks; `set_field_validated` splices/inserts, never removes) that drops the field-group sentinel when it removes the last field, and **must refuse the engine-injected `schema-version` stamp field** (a `set:`-derived leaf — unsetting it corrupts the freeze/version gate).

**Doc homes this wave drives:** new part-doc [command-output-contract.md](design/command-output-contract.md) (Fork 1, reads after `doc-read-surface.md` — its write/compose-side machine-contract sibling); [validation.md](design/validation.md) (the advisory-route floor rule + the Vue addressable-units subsection + the stable finding-key); [assistant-adapter.md](design/assistant-adapter.md) (the route-less-advisory clause); [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) (the `ValueRemapped` kind); [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) (`set-field --unset` + the `[]` reject); [ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md](ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md) (the SFC extract seam, tier-1 de-parked). Full scope + acceptance in [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 41 (decomposition to follow).

## 2026-07-11 — dogfood-record stays; RC trials stay naturalistic (no instructed use)

The rerun surfaced that `record-dogfood`/`dogfood-record` (M17's measured-dogfood spine) went unused in a session that was, in substance, a dogfood run. **Decision: keep the doctype/workflow, do NOT instruct trial agents to use it.** The RC trials measure *natural* adoption — instructing a capture workflow contaminates exactly what they observe; the invocation log (introduced for this purpose) + the committed trial artifacts are the trial-side record. `dogfood-record` remains the instrument for M17's *deliberate* measurement protocol (seeded checks, A/B), a different kind of run; and it is one of the ten manifest-frozen methodology schemas, so pre-1.0 removal would re-open a freeze for no gain. If natural use never reaches for it, prune post-1.0 on usage evidence.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 6 T3: an empty declared nested block serializes as a present `[]` key

One executor elaboration of the nested json pin (`design/doc-read-surface.md` → Nested repeatables join the pin): a declared nested repeatable with **zero items** keys the item object with an **empty array** — present, never omitted (`item_json` inserts every declared nested block unconditionally) — mirroring the whole-doc rule that an item-less repeatable section serializes `[]`. Consistency over sparseness: a machine consumer reads the declared shape without existence checks; only an *undeclared* block contributes no key (the additive guard the `doc_show_nested.rs` witness goldens lock, keeping every flat witness byte-unchanged).

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 6 T2: a plain slice is self-rooted, and the leaf hop resolves declared names only

Three executor elaborations of the nested read pin (`design/doc-read-surface.md` → Nested repeatables join the pin), locked by the `store.rs` goldens: **(1)** every plain item/nested-array slice renders **self-rooted at `###`** (the existing `render_item` depth-1 entry), regardless of the node's physical depth — a slice is its own little document, mirroring how a section slice always starts its items at `###`; the node's *own* children still nest one level deeper. **(2)** The trailing leaf hop resolves **declared names only** (a declared slot / the template's `id-from` / a declared field, via the shared `write::chain_repeatable` template): the M39 lenient bare-prose fallback (any leaf name resolving a single-slot item's body) is retired, and `id-from` now beats the bare slot — so `#criteria/<id>/title` returns the heading (the pinned contract) instead of the slot bytes it was shadowed by. Consequence of the honest-block rule ("never wrong-node-exit-0"), applied uniformly rather than only at nested depth — a second grammar per depth is the defect class this increment kills. **(3)** Block codes: a hop naming no declared nested repeatable → `store.no-such-section` (naming the offending segment); the segment-less physical shortcut → `store.no-such-leaf` with a route naming the declared nested section(s) (S1: never treated as an item id, matching the write side).

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 5 T5: placement-born frozen doctypes migrate their literal file in place

The e2e stamp-absent flow (`methodology_corpus_stamp.rs`) surfaced exactly what the planner suspected: `migrate-corpus`'s walk treated every `placement:` doctype as *relocated* (walk the prior snapshot's `location:` home, move to `placement.file`) and **silently skipped** one with no location-bearing prior snapshot — so an unstamped committed roadmap (or vision/decisions-log/deferral-ledger, all placement-born at v1) never migrated. Fixed in the candidate walk (`candidate_docs`): a placement doctype with no prior `location:` migrates its **literal placement file in place** — the relocation arm (changelog v1→v2) unchanged. **Known bound recorded, not fixed** (out of T5's scope; [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → M40 revises the dichotomy): the detect-half's family-5 sweep still walks only `location:`-bearing schemas, so an otherwise-conformant unstamped *placement* doc is verb-migratable but never `validate`-routed `migrate` (the location doctypes route correctly; the hollow/surplus advisories' `committed_instances` walk does cover placement).

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 5 T4: methodology manifest hashes are over the loader-RESOLVED shape

The methodology `schema-manifest.yaml` (all ten schemas, v1) freezes each `schema-hash` over the shape `load_pack_schema` resolves against the methodology pack itself — stamp **injected** for the nine persisted doctypes, bare for the transient `commit` shadow — because that is exactly what `assert_schema_freeze` recomputes (the stamp field is version-independent by design, so this stays a pure fingerprint of the doctype's own shape). Consequence for regeneration: a deliberate versioned change recomputes through the production loader, never the bare engine `load_schema`. Same-motion churn landed as pre-verified: the dogfood-record `doc schema` golden (version 1 + stamp field), the vision `doc show` pinned `fields` (additive-pre-pin), the idea skeleton front-matter witness, the completion-record round-trip's local schema load (stamp-injected to mirror production), and flow40's arm 3 — the moving acceptance re-targeted to a genuinely manifest-less fixture doctype while `research` now asserts the refusal + `migrate-corpus` route.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 5 T3: manifest-walking is a trait primitive — `origin_packs`, the plural sibling

The per-origin unification's enumeration mechanism is a new `PackSource` trait method `origin_packs(kind, id)` — **every** constituent shipping the id, precedence order, empty when none (no `self` fallback, unlike the singular) — because `assert_schema_freeze` holds only `&dyn PackSource` and "walk every manifest-shipping constituent" is unanswerable through the one-winner `origin_pack`. Per-doctype resolution funnels through one `governing_version(pack, ty)` helper (`origin_pack(Schemas, ty)`'s own manifest entry); `frozen_doctype_versions` becomes the governed union keyed off `list(Schemas)` ids (the stem==type convention both shipped packs honor); `frozen_doctype_set` is subsumed and deleted. No-op while methodology is manifest-less — full gate green unchanged.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 5 T2: the census bit — CRLF front-matter parsed only its FIRST field (production parse defect, fixed)

The methodology byte-stability census (9 `arb_doc()` arms, the M33 pattern) surfaced a real one on its first run: `scan_blocks` kept only the **first** `Text` event's range inside the metadata block, and pulldown-cmark emits one `Text` **per line** under CRLF (one for the whole block under LF) — so a CRLF doc's multi-field front-matter silently dropped every field after the first (parse still "ok"; `set_field` on `date`/`verdict` errored `NotPresent`). Dev-pack-wide too, not methodology-specific — the M33 census masked it by only ever editing the *first* header field and asserting parse-*ok*, not parse-*shape*. Fixed by accumulating the Text ranges across the block (`parse.rs::scan_blocks`), pinned by a deterministic CRLF-ADR regression (`parse.rs::crlf_front_matter_parses_every_field`), and the census's clause 1 now asserts LF-vs-CRLF **parsed-structure equality** (same field keys, same item anchors) on every arm, so this defect class can't re-hide behind parse-ok. Census discharges doctype-map.md's recorded freeze precondition ahead of T4's hash-freeze.

## 2026-07-10 — M40 Inc 4 T2: the `doc schema` contract's `required` means presence-in-a-conformant-instance

Three executor elaborations of the pinned contract (`design/doc-read-surface.md` → Why json is a contract here), golden-locked in `crates/cli/tests/doc_schema.rs`: **(1)** a field's `required` = the author must supply it **or** the CLI stamps it (`is_author_required(f) || default || set`) — so an optional `ref` (adr `supersedes`) and a pack-typed anchor read `required: false`, never the misleading raw `!optional:`, while `author-required` stays T1's shared engine predicate verbatim; **(2)** an item slot projects as `{id, optional?}` and a nested repeatable as `{id, item}` (the recursion point) — kind is implied inside an item; **(3)** the unknown-doctype block reuses the read surface's `store.unknown-type` code, routed to `jigc describe` (one failure class, one code — no new id for the same "address names no doctype" fault).

The author-required pre-stamp lands inside `engine::state`'s `empty_instance`/`seeded_instance` (header sections only, merged with the on-create seeds in schema-declared field order), so **every** `provision_doc` consumer inherits it — `doc create`, `doc author`, and the engine test substrate's commit fixtures (whose `provisioned_empty_commit` golden gains `type: `; the *production* commit mint stays on `start.rs::fillable_form`, byte-identical, its all-minus-optional-ref rule now reading the engine's pub `is_optional_ref`). Consequence (the Settle-corrected caveat, now pinned by tests): an un-set author-required field on the 3 affected doctypes blocks at **`field-value-conformant`** (present-but-empty) instead of `required-field-present` — the gate holds, only the finding code/message shifts (flow20/flow21/dogfood-record repairs); repeatable-item fields are NOT stamped, so their absence keeps `required-field-present`.

Commit) honored, its existing test asserting the raw output stays green as-is. *Done:* new test green — a deterministic stage failure (seed `.git/index.lock`) yields the findings envelope with the code + route + the verbatim git stderr, and the rollback ran (promoted copies gone); the commit-phase hook-rejection tests unchanged-green; full gate. ## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 6 build: tee install gated on the knob

The fd-tee is installed **only when the `invocation-log` knob resolves ON** (`enabled_logs_dir()` read once up front, before `Cli::try_parse()`), not unconditionally — because teeing repoints fd 1/2 at a pipe (`isatty` → false), which suppresses clap's terminal colour for `--help`/errors. Gating keeps that cost on the opted-in trial operator alone and matches the rest of `invocation_log`'s "no-op when OFF / outside a jigc repo" posture; the knob read needs no parsed `Cli`, so `--help`/`--version` still tee + log. The two `main()` log sites collapse to one (the clap `Err` arm now returns its `Outcome` instead of early-`return`ing after its own log call). EINTR-retry in the drain loop and a std-stream flush before fd restore keep the count exact and Unix-portable (no glibc-specific errno location). Landed test-first (`output_bytes` absent → red).

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 7 / T3 build: the form-vision empty-research advisory

Mechanism = a **CLI-side marker-block resolve**, not a new engine primitive (the general `state-aware-compose` stays stretch/1.1 per G7). `packs/methodology/steps/author-vision.yaml` carries the advisory prose (pack-owned content, right layer) at its opening, delimited by inert `<!-- research-advisory -->` / `<!-- /research-advisory -->` HTML-comment lines — which the step emitter passes through **verbatim** (comment-drop is top-level workflow-body only, not step bodies). `resolve_research_advisory` post-processes the composed `text`: it **keeps** the inner line when `warrants_research_advisory` (the workflow's `allows-create` admits `vision` **and** `committed_store` has no `research` key — absent ⇔ empty, since `committed_store` omits empty collections), else drops the whole block; the markers are **always** stripped, so they never leak. Applied at **both** compose exits — `compose_core` (mint / `--workflow form-vision`) **and** `compose_task_workflow` (resume), the only two paths that emit `author-vision` — because a strip in one alone would leak markers on the other. Keyed on `allows-create: vision`, not the literal workflow name, so it is not a hardcode. Advisory, never blocking (`grounded-in` is `0..*`; zero research is legal). No engine/schema change → freeze untouched. Test-first: `flow_form_vision_advisory.rs` red on the empty-store assertion (advisory absent) before the pack+CLI landed.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 7 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 7 — minting ergonomics: slug word-cap + `--slug` override + form-vision advisory](implementation/roadmap.md) into **3 ordered, single-concern tasks** (`T1`–`T3`), grounded in the code at HEAD `7fc8f6b` (tree clean). Settled basis: [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-07-06 M39 planning → *Slug (G6)* (word-count cap ~5 + reuse the `jigc rename` `--slug` flag, routed through the reject/resume collision path, **freeze-safe** — mint is CLI behavior, outside `schema-hash`) and *form-vision advisory (G7)* (query committed `research` count → print the route line; `grounded-in` is `0..*`, zero research a legal state). **The three grouped-scope bullets map one-to-one to the three tasks; none narrowed or deferred.** The tasks are independent (each gate-green alone) and ordered per the roadmap.

**Atomic-gate correction — the roadmap parenthetical "golden churn contained there [`slug.rs`]" is verified FALSE and must not be trusted as a pin.** `slugify` is called for *every* minted id (task ids, doc slugs, item anchors, migration ids), so the ~5-word cap re-slugs every existing test that hard-codes a **>5-word-derived** id — grepped at HEAD, **15 `crates/cli/tests/*.rs` suites** pin such literals as `--task` resume args / asserted paths (e.g. `move-the-session-cache-to-a-shared-redis-cluster` → capped `move-the-session-cache-to`; `cache-sessions-in-a-single-in-memory-node`, `enforce-the-rate-limit-at-the-gateway`, `add-a-greeting-helper-to-the-utils-package`, `cite-a-symbol-with-a-dirty-file`, `log-a-habit-in-one-tap`). The cap **breaks** those gate-covered suites and only re-pinning them repairs the gate, so the cap + its dependent-test updates are **one inseparable gate-green motion** (T1) — a `slug.rs`-only task can never reach a green `cargo test -p cli`. The tasks:

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 6 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 6 — invocation-log output-size (fd-level tee)](implementation/roadmap.md) into **one** ordered single-concern task, grounded in the code at HEAD `38ad02f` (tree clean). **The atomic-gate call — why one task, not four:** the fd-tee, the `Record` field, the new dep, and the test are **one inseparable gate-green motion**. Verified against the code: (a) the tee's only observable output is its byte count, which is invisible until threaded into the recorded `output_bytes` field — a "tee-only" task has **no real red step** (a transparent pass-through tee leaves a known verb's output byte-identical, so an "output unchanged" test passes *without* the change); and (b) the dev gate runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `invocation_log` is a **binary-crate** module (`mod invocation_log;` in `main.rs`, driven by integration tests via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc`, never called directly), so a tee fn whose only user is `#[cfg(test)]` is **dead code in the `--bins` compile** → gate fails. Both point the same way: the tee must be wired into `main()`'s live dispatch in the same commit that introduces it. **The `Record` add is verified additive** — the existing `crates/cli/tests/invocation_log.rs` asserts fields by presence over `serde_json::Value` (no exhaustive golden), and `Record` is `#[derive(Serialize)]`-only with no `deny_unknown_fields`, so `output_bytes` breaks no existing test. The task:

- **T1 — the fd-level counting tee + `output_bytes`.** At `main()`, inside the span the timing `Instant` already opens (before `Cli::try_parse()`), save fd 1/2 (`libc::dup`), replace them with pipe write-ends (`libc::dup2`), spawn a per-stream drain thread that reads → counts → forwards to the saved fd; after all emission, restore the fds, close the write-ends, join the threads, read the two counts; add `output_bytes: u128` (stdout+stderr total) to the invocation `Record` and thread the count through `log_invocation`. Add the Unix-only dep (`libc` — the fd-swap needs raw `dup`/`dup2`; `os_pipe` is an optional pipe-construction helper, executor's call per the settled fork). *Red-step assumptions to prove (the tee's load-bearing properties, tested not trusted):* (1) **size == emitted** — a known-output verb's logged `output_bytes` equals the exact stdout+stderr byte count the driven binary emits (`Command`-captured); (2) **captures the clap arm** — `jigc --help` (the differentiator vs the rejected per-emitter tally, which records 0) records `output_bytes` == its emitted-stdout length, which forces the tee to span the `Err(err) => err.print()` arm and be torn down only *after* that emission but *before* the `log_invocation` write; (3) **transparency** — the verb's own captured output is unchanged (the tee forwards, never swallows). *Done:* `cargo test -p cli --test invocation_log` green incl. the new size==emitted + `--help` assertions, and the full dev gate (`build`/`test`/`clippy -D warnings`/`fmt --check`) clean. Files: `crates/cli/src/{main.rs,invocation_log.rs}`, `crates/cli/tests/invocation_log.rs`, `crates/cli/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.toml` (workspace dep).

All four grouped-scope bullets map to T1, none narrowed or deferred: the tee in `main.rs` · the `Record` field · the new dep · the size==emitted test. The design's "captures the true total incl. clap `--help`/`--version`" claim ([measurement.md](design/measurement.md):70 — byte-counts, *not* the deferred stderr-text capture) is pinned as red-step assumption #2, so the executor proves the clap-arm span rather than trusting it. No creep into later increments; the exhaustive reading-order fold-back (incl. `measurement.md` output-size) is Inc 8. *Why:* the tee, its recorded field, its dep, and its proof are one atomic unit — no sub-piece reaches a green gate alone.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 5 / T5: the foreign-squatter move-into-workbench arm + the two-resolutions reconcile

A **collision at a relocation destination** is resolved by the occupant's *kind* (`crates/cli/src/relocate.rs` → `displace_foreign_squatter`, threaded through `relocate_one`; reconciled in `design/reconciliation.md` → Relocation collisions): a **managed** instance already there (baselined in `file-state`) → adopt-in-place (M24), and moving the incoming managed instance *into* it (a managed move-INTO) is **deferred** — surfaced as a **block, never a clobber** (it needs an unmodeled managed-but-uncommitted state); a **foreign** (untracked/unmanaged, un-baselined) file → **moved into the gitignored `.jigc/` workbench**, out of the destination and uncommittable, so the managed instance lands and a stray working file is never committed or silently destroyed. Classification is by baseline — the same managed-vs-foreign line the rest of reconciliation draws. A committed-but-unmanaged squatter's tracked index slot is freed (`git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch`, a no-op for an untracked one) so the managed `git mv` into the vacated destination succeeds. **Workbench-subpath elaboration (the planner left the subpath an executor detail "within Inc 4's gitignore-3→1 collapse"):** a **dedicated `.jigc/displaced/`** entry added to the single-source `gitignore::ENTRIES` (+ the `milestone.rs` golden bumped) rather than reusing an existing ignored dir — every existing ignored subdir is either **enumerated** (`tasks/`/`milestones/`/`worktrees/` — `state.rs`/`milestone.rs` read them back as task/milestone/worktree ids) or a **typed cache** (`state/`/`index/`/`logs/`), so parked foreign detritus there would masquerade as a work-unit or pollute a cache; a dedicated home has no reader. The bound is settled **foreign-only** (the safe half — a foreign file has no identity/referrers); the managed half waits on the state it needs.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 5 / T4: the parallel freeze-exempt relocation path — a new `jigc relocate` verb

The frozen relocation arm (`migrate_corpus`) gates to the manifest set and *derives* each doctype's prior home from the versioned snapshot; a **freeze-exempt** doctype has no snapshot, so nothing pins where its instance *was*. Built the **parallel path** (`crates/cli/src/relocate.rs` → `relocate_freeze_exempt` / `relocate_stranded`): detect the committed instances stranded at a **human-supplied** prior home (`orphan::is_stranded` over `git ls-files`), then `git mv` each to the current schema home via the T1 primitive (`relocate::move_doc`), byte-preserving, file-state re-keyed. **Resolution-surface choice (the planner left this "new flag/verb vs. arm" as executor design):** a **new `jigc relocate <type> --from <prior-home>`** verb — freeze-exempt relocation needs a human-supplied prior home, so a first-class verb taking `--from` is the honest entry point (not an arg on `migrate-corpus`, whose contract is snapshot-derived + version-gated). `--from` parses to a `Home`: a `.md` value is a placement file, else a location dir. **The two paths are reconciled**: `relocate_freeze_exempt` **refuses** a doctype in `frozen_doctype_versions` (routes it to `migrate-corpus`), and `migrate-corpus`'s frozen gate skips the freeze-exempt complement — every persisted doctype relocates through exactly one path, keyed on frozen-vs-exempt. **Scope honesty (F8 / `storage.md:148`):** M39 closes *detect+route+offer-move with a supplied prior home*; it does **not** (cannot) auto-detect a freeze-exempt doctype's prior home — there is no record, by construction. Move is best-effort per-doc (`blocked` surfaced, never fatal), staged-not-committed like the T3 sibling.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 5 / T3: `config set docs-root` detect+route+**moves** (auto-move, staged-not-committed)

`config set docs-root` replaces its M36 warn-then-strand with **detect+route+move** (`crates/cli/src/config.rs` → `route_docs_root_repoint_orphans`): each committed doc the re-point would strand under the prior resolved root is **relocated** to the new root via the shared move primitive (`relocate::move_doc` — `git mv` + file-state re-key) and surfaced. **Auto-move is safe here** because a `docs-root` re-point has a *recorded prior home* — the old resolved root, deterministic from the current cascade (the freeze-exempt path, T4, has no snapshot → human-supplied). The destination is a **whole-path prefix swap** old-root → new-root (`reroot`): `docs-root` is a uniform prefix over every location doctype, so the doc's `<location>/<slug>.md` sub-path is invariant — no per-schema destination math. **Elaboration pins:** (a) the move is **staged, not committed** — it rides the working tree alongside the (already-uncommitted) manifest edit `config set` writes, so the operator commits both together (config-set never committed); (b) **best-effort** — a resolution/store hiccup returns silently and a per-doc move failure is surfaced (route: move by hand) but never fails the write (the set always lands). The `validate` orphan fire-point stays intact for strands that arise *another* way (an out-of-band manifest edit, a cross-machine commit landing before its docs move) — `orphan_detection.rs`'s validate case now re-points via a direct manifest edit to preserve that coverage.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 4 / T7: stale-base detection is a CLI git probe guarding *every* base-reading op; the engine owns only the finding shape

The stale-base edge (`design/team-ready-state.md` → Stale-base edge (history rewrite)) — a base-SHA pin naming a commit a history rewrite orphaned — is caught by a CLI `guard_base_live` run right after each op reads the base pin, *before* any git operation against the missing commit. **Detection is CLI-side** (`git rev-parse --verify --quiet <sha>^{commit}` — exit 0 ⇒ resolves to a commit, non-zero ⇒ gone): the engine does no git I/O, so it owns only the routed `milestone.stale-base` **finding shape** (`engine::milestone::stale_base_finding`, the `unknown_milestone_finding` sibling). **Guarded uniformly across all three base consumers** — `provision` (before `git worktree add`, else a half-provisioned worktree set), `finalize` (before the worktree-combine + base-guard `merge-base`, else materialize/flip/commit against a phantom base), and `join` (before resolving the committed index against a missing commit, which would silently mis-report the cross-area ref walk) — because a stale base is invalid for *every* op that reads it and "routes to the human" must be the same everywhere, not a hole in the omitting ops. The **zero-commit sentinel** (`EMPTY_TREE_SHA`) is exempt (a valid pre-first-commit base, never stale), so the guard adds no block on that path. Pre-fix the ops reached git with the bogus SHA and died with a raw `fatal: invalid reference` / `merge-base` error (provision partially); now a routed block fires first, no corruption/partial write. Proven by `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_stale_base.rs` (a non-existent base SHA re-derived from the record on a fresh clone → provision registers no worktree, finalize makes no commit + does not flip the record).

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 4 / T6: the record reconcile preflight uses `reconcile_committed` (per-doc, `task_touched: true`), not the store sweep

The No-silent-overwrite guard (`design/team-ready-state.md` → F3) runs before every `set: on-transition` record overwrite (`add-task` append, finalize status-flip) and conflict-blocks if the committed `milestone-record` drifted out-of-band. **Elaboration (faithful to F3's intent, not its literal wording):** F3/the T6 planner-note named `reconcile_committed_store`, but that whole-store wrapper *cannot* express the guard F3 mandates. F3 is explicit — "detected + conflict-blocked, **not absorbed**" — yet `reconcile_committed_store` would **absorb** a *conformant* OOB edit (the `DRIFTED + UNTOUCHED` arm silently re-baselines it, e.g. a valid `status: active → joined` hand-edit), which is exactly the silent clobber F3 forbids; and it sweeps sibling records + every unrelated committed doc the milestone op has no business gating on. The CLI op *is* the machine touching the record, so the guard drives the **per-doc primitive** `reconcile_committed` with **`task_touched: true`** — precisely the `DRIFTED + TOUCHED → reconciliation.conflict-block` arm ("both sides moved; no silent merge"), scoped to this one record. Baseline lifecycle: each record **write** (`create`/`add-task`) advances the `.jigc/state/file-state.json` baseline to what the CLI wrote, so a legit sequential op sees `IN_SYNC` (the guard is inert on a clean record) while an OOB edit reads as drift; no edge-index write reaches disk (absorb, the sole mutator, is unreachable under `task_touched: true`). Dev-only (no `milestone-record` schema) is inert. Proven by `crates/cli/tests/milestone_record_reconcile.rs` (a *valid*-enum OOB edit blocks both overwrite sites → the record is not overwritten; the clean path stays green).

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 4 / T4: the `join`-flip folds into the finalize commit, transactionally

`milestone finalize` under `[dev ▸ methodology]` now flips the committed `milestone-record` (`engine::join_record` — every `tasks` item + header `status` active → joined, byte-stable) and **path-adds the flipped record into the ONE finalize commit** alongside the promoted docs (via the shared `overlay_docs_commit_and_ff` pathspecs, threaded through the milestone `StagePolicy::Combine`/`ChainPerSubtask` variants) — never a second commit; the flip's byte-change gates `has_diff` so a docs-only milestone whose only change is the flip is not an empty-commit block. **Elaboration (kept minimal-correct):** a `RecordFlipGuard` restores the pre-flip bytes on any blocked/failed finalize (base-mismatch, hook rejection) and is disarmed only once the commit lands — the flip is a write to a *committed, tracked* path, so "Writes are transactional" (CLAUDE.md) demands it not persist without its commit; the design's "join folds into the commit" ([team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The commit model) implied but did not spell out the block-restore. Dev-only (no `milestone-record` schema) resolves no record → inert, the finalize path byte-untouched.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 build: the milestone-finalize base-guard refinement (Inc 4/T4 fork)

The build halted at Inc 4/T4: the per-op record-commit model (settled 2026-07-06) advances HEAD, but `plan_milestone_finalize`'s preflight requires `base.sha == head_sha` ([finalize.rs:510](crates/engine/src/finalize.rs)) — the M31 worktree-combine external-drift guard — so finalize blocks; and **`record.base` is structurally always ≥1 commit behind HEAD** (a record commit cannot store its own resulting sha), so `base == HEAD` can *never* hold once per-op record commits land, on a fresh clone too. A genuine fork planning missed (the design-review's F4 checked commit *staging*, not the HEAD-advance-vs-finalize-guard interaction; the Inc-4 planner asserted "no new fork"); the build harness caught it and halted rather than guessing. **Settled (human): relax the guard, keep per-op commits.** The preflight becomes: if `base == HEAD` proceed (fast path); else if `base` is a **linear ancestor** of HEAD **and every commit in `base..HEAD` touches only this milestone's record path** (`docs/milestone-records/<id>.md`), advance `base → HEAD` and proceed; else block (`base-mismatch`, unchanged). This matches the guard's *true intent* — catch **external** drift, not the milestone's own bookkeeping — and preserves the M31 worktree-combine guarantee (a record-only commit touches no code, so the combine base is unaffected; any foreign code/doc commit in the range still blocks). The **engine does no git I/O** (invariant intact): the CLI computes the range's linearity + record-only-ness and feeds the result to `plan_milestone_finalize`. Design of record: [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The commit model; owed to finalize.md/storage.md at the Inc-8 reading-order fold-back. Fix lands **test-first** (a foreign commit in range still blocks) as a task before T4 resumes.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 3 T4: the record's `base` field stores both sha and short

Building T4's read-back, the planning claim (e) round-trip obligation resolved **not-lossless**: `short` is `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, a **variable-length** unambiguous abbreviation, so it is *not* a fixed prefix of the full sha and cannot be reconstructed from the sha alone. Per the planner's pre-resolved contingency ("if it isn't lossless, the base field must store both"), the record's `meta.base` header field now stores **both**, space-joined (`base: <sha> <short>`) — mirroring `base.json`, which already persists both. This makes `read_back_record` a lossless inverse of `render_fresh_record`, so deleting the `.jigc` cache and re-deriving from the committed `.md` yields a byte-identical `BasePin` (sha AND short). Cost: T1/T2's byte-goldens gained the short on the `base:` line (freeze-exempt doctype, no version-gate; no CLI/flow golden depends on it — Inc 4 not yet built). The read-back finding for a non-conforming / base-less record is `milestone.record-read-back` (routed, blocking); `reseed_cache_from_record` re-derives both cache files when either is absent, else no-ops. Cross-ref [team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → Engine capability 2.

## 2026-07-07 — M39 Increment 1 / T2: `jigc doc show` + the pinned `--format json` contract

Shipped the `jigc doc show <ref>` read verb (`DocCommand::Show`, task-less — resolves the cascade schema set + repo root the `jigc validate` way) rendering a committed doc/slice two ways: **plain** via the T1-extended `store::read_slice` (byte-exact), **`--format json`** via a net-new serializer whose golden **pins the 1.0 contract** (`crates/cli/tests/doc_show.rs`, driven on the real binary under `[dev ▸ methodology]`, witnessed by `vision` whole-doc + `prd` repeatable). Pins made (one-way door): a whole-doc `{ type, slug, fields, sections }` where **`fields`** flattens every simple-section field (scalar → json string, list-cardinality → json array), **`sections`** carries a slot section as its **trimmed** prose string and a repeatable section as its **item array**, an item object keys the `id-from` leaf by `item.title` + its fields/slots, a `#section` slice returns the array and `#section/<id>` the item object. Two honest calls: (a) the injected `schema-version` header field **is** reflected in `fields` (a real committed field — freeze-exempt `vision`/milestone-record simply have none), not filtered; (b) **nested** repeatable-in-item content is *not* serialized — unpinned, every witness + the milestone-record are flat, deferred until a driver needs it. Full four-command gate green.

No bullet dropped; no creep into the milestone-record (Inc 3), which is the json contract's *later* witness — Inc 1 witnesses the general shape with `vision` (whole-doc) + a repeatable-section doc (item slice + array).

**Grounding (verified against the code, not assumed):** (a) `store::read_slice` (`crates/engine/src/store.rs:90`) has exactly the two blocks the scope names — `store.no-fragment` (`:110-117`, a fragmentless address) and `store.unsliceable-fragment` (`slice_fragment`, `:198-205`, any non-`Unit` fragment: `UnitLeaf`/`UnitItem`/`UnitItemLeaf`/`Deep`); lifting both is **additive** — no test pins either code (grep clean; the only store-read error test is `store.not-found`, `:509`). (c) **Lifting the two blocks is inert for compose:** all three shipped `{{@…}}` derefs carry a `#unit` fragment (`superseded-context.yaml` `#decision`, `locate-from-spec.yaml` `#criteria`, `author-vision.yaml` `#findings`) — none is fragmentless, none is item/leaf/deep — so no existing compose input reaches either lifted block and no golden churns; `deref_content` *does* handle a `None`-fragment landing (`:796-799`) but no pack/test exercises it, so the behavior change (block → whole-doc) has no live witness to break. (d) The json shape is **pinned in the design** ([design/team-ready-state.md](design/team-ready-state.md) → The read surface, line 74): whole-doc = `{ type, slug, fields: {…}, sections: { <section>: [item…] } }`, a `#section` slice returns the item array, an enum leaf serializes as its lowercase string; Inc 1 is chartered to pin the **general** whole-doc + repeatable-section shape *now* (roadmap), so the one detail the design leaves to this increment — a *slot* section's serialization within `sections` — is pinned by T2's golden as slot → prose string, repeatable → item array (the consistent extension of the pinned skeleton), not left vague and not a blind pin. (e) `DocCommand` (`crates/cli/src/doc.rs:39`) `dispatch` already threads `format: Format` and owns a json envelope path, and `run_doc` is wired at `cli.rs:281` — so the Show verb slots into the existing surface. (f) The proof witnesses exist in the packs: `vision` (`packs/methodology/schemas/vision.yaml`, slot sections + a `meta` header ref) for whole-doc; `spec`/`prd` (repeatable `criteria`/`requirements`) for the item slice.

Full four-command gate green. *Why:* one coherent engine concern (the store reader gains the two shapes the read surface needs); additive — verified no test pins the two lifted codes and every live compose deref carries a `#unit` fragment (grounding (a)/(c)), so nothing the gate covers breaks. Files: `crates/engine/src/store.rs` (+ `address.rs` if a fragment-variant helper is needed). - **T2 — cli: the `jigc doc show` verb + dispatch + the stable `--format json` serializer.** Add `DocCommand::Show { addr }` + its `dispatch`/`run_doc` arm, rendering the addressed ref two ways: **plain text** via the T1-extended `read_slice`; **`--format json`** via a net-new serializer emitting the pinned shape `{ type, slug, fields: {…}, sections: { <section>: <slot-prose-string> | [ {…item fields…}, … ] } }` (enum leaves lowercase-string), where a `#section` slice returns the item array. *Done:* a `crates/cli/tests/*.rs` suite drives the **real binary** — (a) `jigc doc show vision:<slug>` round-trips a committed `vision` (plain output carries every section; `--format json` matches a **pinned golden**, the stable contract); (b) `jigc doc show <spec/prd repeatable ref>` returns the item on a `#section/<id>` slice and the item **array** under `--format json`; (c) a bad ref exits non-zero with the routed block envelope (the existing failure funnel). ## 2026-07-06 — M39 planning: decomposition (8 increments, risk-first)

Cut into **8 ordered, single-concern, risk-first increments** ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 39): (1) `jigc doc show` + `read_slice` whole-doc/item/leaf extension + stable `--format json`; (2) compose renders **all** grounded sources (multi-target `walk_edge` + the M37-doc revise + flip the two pinning tests); (3) the `milestone-record` doctype engine core (the `set: on-transition` write with its distinct append/in-place-mutate arms + the read-back authority making the committed `.md` the source of truth); (4) team-ready layout — the `milestone_dir` record/WIP split + path-scoped commit-at-each-op + gitignore 3→1 + fresh-clone resume + OOB conflict-block; (5) the freeze-exempt relocation floor (orphan re-key + extracted rename-move + parallel path + `config set` detect+route); (6) the invocation-log fd-tee output-size (the adoption-trial prerequisite); (7) minting ergonomics (slug word-cap + `--slug` + form-vision advisory); (8) acceptance + the reading-order doc fold-back (the M38 Inc-6 pattern). Ordering: the read surface first (the milestone record witnesses its json contract), the doctype engine before its layout/commit model, the floor after the doctype exists, the self-contained instrumentation + riders late, fold-back last. The planning gate-record ([completions/artifacts/M39/planning-gate-record.md](completions/artifacts/M39/planning-gate-record.md)) filled clean — no halts. **Status: planned; hand off to the build harness** (`milestone-build M39`).

- **Team-ready state → (c) a managed work-unit-record doctype** (not a raw-JSON relocate). The record/WIP split (today one `.jigc`-rooted `milestone_dir`) is drawn **field-granular**: intent/status/task-membership = committed record; `docs/`/worktrees/caches = gitignored WIP. The one genuinely-new engine capability is a **set-on-transition** machine-maintained doctype (a CLI-appended ordered id-list) — assembled from proven primitives (M16 repeatable-section + `add-item`, M22 on-create materialization, M16 singleton-slug, M38 placement).
- **Log output-size → an fd-level counting tee at `main()`** (not a per-emitter tally). Robust-advocate's decider: the robust cut is *smaller* (one file vs 122 scattered print sites), structurally un-bypassable, and captures the clap `--help`/`--version` output the tally records as size 0; the cheap cut silently under-counts the exact mass-output (A7) it exists to measure, feeding a wrong number into the 1.0.0 GO call + the post-1.0 token-budget workstream. Cost accepted: one new dep (`libc`/`os_pipe`) + Unix-only (jigc's target).
- **doc-read-surface → `jigc doc show` ships a stable `--format json` contract from 1.0** (its own one-way door, accepted — the milestone exists to make the read surface something agents rely on). Net-new verb; `store::read_slice` extended for whole-doc + item/leaf (isolated from the write path — cannot regress the writer). Homes at a read-surface part-doc (not `write-commands.md`, which is write-side by charter; not `introspection.md`, which excludes filled-prose reads — its `:24` forward-ref to `doc show` becomes real).

## 2026-07-04 — M38 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [Increment 4 — the relocation transform kinds (engine)](implementation/roadmap.md) into **2 ordered single-concern tasks**, grounded in the code at HEAD `a3302d4` (tree clean; Inc 1's `placement` key + `display-title` knob, Inc 2's reconcile/ownership, Inc 3's `root-render` retire + freeze-exempt relocations all landed). The one grouped-scope bullet ("the two classifier arms + the driver move-arm + the census safety rows — write-order, abort-strands-neither, re-key atomic") maps across the tasks: **the two classifier arms (`schema_diff`) + their transform handling (the `display-title-changed` H1 splice; `relocated` as a content no-op) → T1**; **the git-free move-arm in `migrate-corpus` + all three census safety rows (write-before-remove, abort-strands-neither, re-key `from→to` atomic) → T2**. This is a **substrate** increment proven **synthetically on a reconstructed fixture** (the M34-Inc-2 shape) — the real `changelog` schema flip + snapshot + real-binary acceptance are Inc 5/6, not narrowed away here.

**Grounding (verified against the code, not assumed):** (a) the **only** exhaustive `match` on `SchemaChange` is `transform.rs:144` (`match change`); the CLI's sole `SchemaChange` match (`migrate_corpus.rs:326` `per_doc_changes`) carries a `_ => true` catch-all (`:331`), so adding the two variants **forces** `transform.rs` to gain arms **in the same commit** (else the match is non-exhaustive → compile error → red gate) but does **not** break the CLI compile — so T1 = *variants + their transform arms*, one atomic engine unit, and T1/T2 are separable. (b) `schema_diff` (`schema_diff.rs:91`) today diffs only sections/fields and **never inspects** `location`/`placement`/`display-title`; the two new arms classify **outside** the per-section loop from the two `Schema` values alone (domain-empty, engine-pure): a pure home change (v1 `location` → v2 `placement`) → exactly `[Relocated{from,to}]` (not `[]`), a `display-title` add/change → `[DisplayTitleChanged{to}]`, `from`/`to` auto-derived from the two schemas' declared homes (no hand-written recipe — the determinism boundary). (c) there is **no** existing H1-rewrite primitive in `write.rs` (the H1 is emitted at `write.rs:148` `# {title}`; `set_slot`/`set_field` are the splice siblings) — so T1 builds the byte-stable H1 splice the `display-title-changed` arm needs, following `set_slot`'s re-render-the-region pattern (`write.rs:916` — a bare span splice is not byte-stable). (d) `transform()` (`transform.rs:136`) already carries `source` + `changes` + both schemas, so `DisplayTitleChanged{to}` needs no signature change (the new title rides the variant); `Relocated` is a **content no-op** in `transform()` (the WidenedCardinality sibling — the move is a filesystem op the CLI owns, never a content edit), so a pure relocation folds to byte-identical `v2 == source` and still gates clean, then the CLI move-arm relocates it. (e) the CLI move-arm site: `migrate_committed_corpus` (`migrate_corpus.rs:158`) writes each migrated doc back via `engine::state::persist(&repo_root.join(id), v2)` at the **same** path (`id == rel_key`), and the per-doctype walk keys on `dt.to.location` (`:175`, `continue` on `location: None`) — but a relocated doctype's `to` is `placement` (`location: None`), so the walk must instead key on the **`from`** home (census: "the corpus walk keys on the `from` home … not the empty `to`"); T2 teaches the move-arm to walk `from`, write the gated v2 bytes to `to`, `remove(from)`, and re-key file-state `from→to`. (f) the **abort-strands-neither** test has a precedent: `written_docs_are_baselined_..._when_a_later_write_aborts` (`:766`) forces an `engine::state::persist` failure by pre-occupying the `.tmp` sibling — T2 reuses that fault-injection to prove an abort **between** write-`to` and remove-`from` leaves **both** copies on disk (never zero). (g) both tasks are additive to the shipped surface — **no** shipped doctype declares a `location→placement` relocation until Inc 5, so the new classifier arms emit nothing over the dev/methodology packs and the existing `migrate_corpus` tests stay green; each task reaches a green four-command gate at its own commit (no atomic-gate coupling forces a merge — grounding (a)). (h) file-state re-key uses the existing `FileStateRecord::{get,record}` (`migrate_corpus.rs:280-281`); a re-key is a remove-old-key + record-`to` paired atomically with the move (the per-doc-commit discipline the verb already upholds).

## 2026-07-04 — M38 Increment 3 / T1 landed: `root-render` retired, `vision` managed-at-root

Deleted the whole `root-render` mechanism (`Schema.root_render`, `RootRender`, `FinalizePlan.renders`, `plan_root_renders` + its foreign-file finding, `reject_root_render_promotions` + `milestone_root_render_finding`, CLI `render_roots` + all staging/rollback sites) and relocated `vision.yaml` to `placement: { file: VISION.md }` (dropping `location: vision/`, keeping `display-title: Vision`) — the vision is now **managed directly at root `VISION.md`** (one file, OOB-reconciled), not a `docs/vision/vision.md` source mirrored to root. The milestone-join guard was a pure drop (Inc 1's shared `plan_promotions` handles placement on both paths). Retired-mechanism grep returns zero; foreign-`VISION.md` protection is now the **inherited** `finalize.promote-clobber` (no bespoke guard).

**Elaboration pin — a placement census site the relocation exposed:** the finalize `has_diff` signal (`task.rs`, non-migration arm) computed `staged_promotable` from `schema.location.is_some()` only, so a **placement** doctype (`location: None`) was dropped through the transient arm — a vision-only task whose sole diff is the `VISION.md` promotion tripped `finalize.empty-commit`. `placement_acceptance.rs` passed only incidentally (untracked `.jigc/config` supplied the signal). Fixed to mirror `plan_promotions`' promotability (`location.is_some() || placement.is_some()`); now covered by the re-pointed `flow_form_vision` / `design_altitude_schemas` vision-finalize tests (research committed first, so the placement promotion is the only diff). This is the census gap Inc 1/2's `schema.location` sweep left; the first *shipped* placement doctype surfaced it. `design-altitude-doctypes.md` §4 remains superseded (render → managed-at-root).
