## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 1 / T1 shipped: `FieldType` opened to a pack-declared extension axis

`crates/engine/src/schema.rs` — `FieldType` is no longer a closed `Copy` enum with `CodeAnchor` hardcoded; it is **engine-native unit variants + `Pack(PackFieldType)`**, where `PackFieldType { name, adjudicator: Option<String> }` carries the pack's `(spelling, probe)` binding. The engine ships **no** pack type (engine-empty invariant holds) — `code-anchor` lands in the pack at T3. *Elaboration-pin resolution (the on-disk form + loader signature the planner left to the executor):*

- **Engine representation + loader signature (locked here):** `FieldType` hand-rolls `Serialize`/`Deserialize` as a **bare string** (round-trips the spelling). A non-native `type:` string deserializes to an *unresolved* `Pack { name, adjudicator: None }`; `load_schema_with_types(bytes, &[PackTypeDecl])` then **resolves** each unresolved `Pack` against the supplied set — a declared name is promoted to carry its `adjudicator: Some(probe)`, an **undeclared** name is `SchemaError::UnknownFieldType { field, ty }` (the variant the schema.rs doc-comment named aspirationally, now real; a typed error, never a panic, never a generic serde `Malformed`). `load_schema(bytes)` is preserved as the **native-only** wrapper (`= load_schema_with_types(bytes, &[])`), so the ~60 existing callers compile unchanged and a pack type loads **only** when its declaration is threaded in.
- **The pack's on-disk `field-types:` declaration form is deferred to T3** (the task that introduces a pack file naming `code-anchor → doc-code`). T1 fixes only the engine-side `(name, adjudicator)` carrier (`PackTypeDecl`) the loader threads; how a pack *spells* the declaration on disk is T3's to settle and wire into pack discovery. Within-spec elaboration, not a fork.
- **Knob blast-radius:** `knobs.rs` reuses the `FieldType` vocabulary and deserializes it directly; before this, a typo'd knob `type` was a closed-enum serde error. To preserve that strictness once the vocabulary opened, `load_knobs` now rejects a `Pack`-typed knob with a typed `KnobError::NonNativeType` (a pack field type is never a knob). Equivalent behaviour (non-native knob type still rejected), via a typed error instead of serde.

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 1 / T2 shipped: `check_value` pack-adjudicator dispatch + the `code-anchor` write-time shape check

`crates/engine/src/write.rs` — `check_scalar`'s shared `String | Ref | CodeAnchor` arm is split. `String | Ref` keep their exact prior semantics (non-empty + single-line/no-control-char), now via a `check_opaque_scalar` helper. `FieldType::Pack(pack)` **dispatches on the pack type's spelling**: `code-anchor` runs `check_code_anchor` (the optional **write-time shape check**), any other pack-declared type falls back to the opaque floor. The match moved from `field.ty` to `&field.ty` (the enum is no longer `Copy` post-T1).

- **`code-anchor` write-time shape = non-empty + single-line + parses as `path#symbol`** — a bare `path` (no `#`) is the file-existence form and passes; a value with a `#` requires both a non-empty path and a non-empty symbol, and rejects a second `#`. This is the **cheap local gate only**; the *real* adjudicator is the bound `doc-code` probe at finalize (built in a later increment), so out-of-band-authored anchors are still caught by the probe, not this gate (`design/document-type-schema.md` → Pack-declared field types: Adjudication splits write-time vs finalize-time). `String`/`Ref` are explicitly **not** subject to the shape check (a `ref` carrying `#`/`/` stays accepted) — proven byte-identical by the extended `check_value_types_each_native_kind`.

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 1 / T3 shipped: `code-anchor` declared in the dev pack + both shipped doctypes carry their optional anchor

`code-anchor` is now the **first pack-declared field type** — out of the engine, into the dev pack, bound to `doc-code`. The dev pack ships `crates/cli/pack/config/field-types.yaml` (the on-disk form T1 deferred to here); `adr.yaml`'s `status` header gains an optional `cites-code` (`code-anchor`) field and `spec.yaml`'s `criteria` block gains an optional `maps-to-test` (`code-anchor`) leaf. *Elaboration pins (made by the executor, within the locked schema model):*

- **On-disk declaration form (locked here):** a pack declares its field types in `config/field-types.yaml` — a YAML **sequence** of `{ name, adjudicator }` (`PackTypeDecl`, which gained `Serialize/Deserialize` + `deny_unknown_fields`). The CLI reads it via `pack::pack_field_types(pack)` (an **absent file = empty set**, never an error — a pack need not declare any) and threads it through the new `pack::load_pack_schema(pack, bytes)` wrapper, which is the **single CLI entry point** that replaces the bare engine `load_schema` at every *shipped-pack-schema* load site (`doc`/`task`/`milestone`/`ingest`/`start` schema loaders). The engine stays domain-empty: it ships no `code-anchor`, so the bare `load_schema` still rejects it (`UnknownFieldType`) — proven over the *shipped* bytes by `schema::tests::shipped_adr_and_spec_load_with_the_pack_set_and_fail_without_it` (the loop-closer with T1).
- **A pack-declared field type is author-OPTIONAL (genuine semantics elaboration):** `validate::is_author_required` now exempts any `FieldType::Pack(_)` (alongside the existing optional-`ref` exemption), because a pack type's *adjudication* — not its *presence* — is the finalize-time probe's job, the exact mirror of optional-`ref` ⇒ `ref-resolves`. Without this, the shipped `adr` (whose `cites-code` is always absent at create) would blocking-fail `required-field-present` on **every** task — surfaced by the `ingest`/`finalize` sweeps when the anchors landed, fixed test-first (`validate::…::an_omitted_pack_anchor_field_is_not_author_required`). This realizes the scope's "Both anchor fields are OPTIONAL" and DECISIONS 2026-06-06 (M10 inc-1: anchors optional, the probe blocks only on a *present-but-unresolvable* anchor).
- **Goldens re-pinned (justified, intended output-adding diff — hardening #4):** `schema_adr`/`schema_spec` snapshots gained the `cites-code`/`maps-to-test` rows; every engine test loading the shipped `adr`/`spec` bytes now threads `dev_pack_field_types()` (the bare `load_schema` would now reject them). A hand-authored `adr` carrying `cites-code: <path>#<symbol>` round-trips byte-identical (`write::canonical::adr_with_a_cites_code_anchor_round_trips_byte_identical`).

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 1 / T4 shipped: `set-field` populates an absent optional `adr.cites-code` header field, proven through the binary

The verification-first proof (binary-level integration test `crates/cli/tests/set_field_absent.rs`) ran `jigc doc set-field adr:<slug>#status/cites-code` against a freshly-`create`d ADR and **refuted** the planning assumption that the `commit.implements` machinery already covered the `adr`/`status` shape unchanged. *Genuine gap found + fixed (engine, in T4 scope):*

- **Empty front-matter fence pair was un-insertable.** A `create`d ADR renders its front matter as an **empty** `---\n---` fence (defaults/`on-create` derivers are not materialized at create), and pulldown-cmark emits **no** `Block::Metadata` for a contentless fence — so `insert_front_matter_field` failed with `write.wrong-shape` ("no front-matter block to insert into"). `commit#header/implements` never hit this because the commit doc renders `type:`/`scope:` lines, giving a non-empty fence. Fix (engine/`write.rs`): `front_matter_content` now falls back to `empty_front_matter_content`, which detects a leading empty `---\n---` fence pair directly and returns the **zero-width** inner-content range just past the opening fence, so the first header field slots in between the fences in schema order. Pinned by `write::set_field_generate::absent_field_materializes_into_empty_front_matter_fence` (engine) + the binary test (CLI).
- **No CLI change needed:** `run_set_field` → `set_field_validated` → `insert_front_matter_field` was already wired; the address form `#status/cites-code` resolves through the existing `field_target` two-hop. The fix was purely the engine's empty-fence detection.

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M10 Increment 2 ("the reshaped `Probe` seam + serializable effective-state snapshot + target enumeration — the engine plumbing") into three ordered, single-concern tasks, each with an observable red step. The increment retires the **reshape risk** — admitting the doc-code shape (a `target` + a *serializable* effective-state ctx) onto the seam without breaking the lone existing impl (`override-default`), and giving the engine the means to **name which anchors a task must check** — in isolation, before the subprocess (inc 3) and the real `doc-code` resolver (inc 4) ride on it. **No probe is invoked over the snapshot this increment** beyond an **in-process test probe**; the subprocess invoker + meta-findings are inc 3. *Grounding (read the code at HEAD `f4415d4`, exercised against the M10 inc-2 shape):*

- **(a) The `Probe` seam is the M6 non-task shape — `target`-less and non-serializable.** `crate::probe::Probe::check(&self, ctx: OverrideCtx<'_>) -> Vec<Finding>` (`crates/engine/src/probe.rs:51-55`); `OverrideCtx<'a> { deltas: RecordedDeltas<'a>, pack: &'a dyn PackSource }` is a **live, borrowed, non-serializable** handle (a trait-object pack ref + borrowed delta slices) and carries **no `target`**. The roadmap's reshape is `check(target, ctx)` with a *serializable* effective-state ctx. **The shape this lands on is a verified design point, not assumed:** `override-default`'s ctx genuinely is `(deltas, pack)` — target-less and non-serializable — so the reshaped seam must admit **both** a serializable effective-state ctx (the doc-code shape) **and** `override-default`'s existing non-task shape **with no behaviour change**. T1's red step must *prove* the migrated `override-default` is byte-identical (its findings + their order + severity post-pass unchanged), never assert it. The concrete Rust form of the reshaped trait (e.g. a `target` parameter + a ctx that is either an enum over the two shapes, an associated type, or a generic) and the snapshot struct + its serde form are **doc-elaboration pins** within the locked seam semantics ([module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md) → Probe boundary; [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The wire contract) — made and logged by the executor, not a halt.
- **(b) The lone live caller + the tests that lock byte-identity.** `OverrideDefaultProbe.check(OverrideCtx{…})` is called in exactly one production site (`crates/cli/src/upgrade.rs:68`); the seam's one engine unit test is `probe::tests::override_default_probe_delegates_to_classify`. The flow-8 / upgrade acceptance that must stay green: `crates/cli/tests/flow8_override_default_warning.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/upgrade.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/upgrade_v1_v2.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/severity_tuning.rs`. `OverrideDefaultProbe::check` delegates to `override_default::classify(deltas, pack)` — the reshape changes the *call shape*, never the reconciliation.
- **(c) Effective-state docs are two surfaces, both already reachable.** *Created/edited* (working deltas) are staged under `<task_dir>/docs/<type>:<slug>.md` and enumerated in path-sorted order by `validate::staged_instances` (`crates/engine/src/validate.rs:164`). *Bound read-roles* live as `<type>:<slug>` addresses in the task's `roles.json` (`engine::state::RolesRecord`), resolved to committed `<location>/<slug>.md` bytes the way `start.rs`'s committed-store / overlay path already resolves a bound `{{@task.spec#criteria}}` slice (the M3 proven path). The enumeration walks **both**, and must **skip committed docs not in effective state** (a committed `adr`/`spec` neither edited nor bound contributes nothing) — the design's masking-trap guard ([validation.md](design/validation.md) → Target surface).
- **(d) A `code-anchor` leaf is a typed field, enumerated directly — never the edge index.** Post-inc-1, a `code-anchor` field is `schema::FieldType::Pack(PackFieldType { name: "code-anchor", adjudicator: Some("doc-code") })` (`crates/engine/src/schema.rs`). After parsing a doc against its schema (`parse::parse_sections` → `Document`), the anchor *values* live as opaque text in `parse::ParsedSection.fields` (the `adr.cites-code` **header** field) and `parse::ParsedItem.fields` (the `spec` `criteria/<id>/maps-to-test` **repeatable-item** leaf), each a `field_block::Field { key, value }`. The enumeration matches a field against its schema declaration to find the `code-anchor`-typed leaves and emits `(target-address, anchor-value, check-id)` — **direct field enumeration**, *not* the edge-index blast-radius walk (a `code-anchor` is a field, not an edge; [doctype-map.md](implementation/doctype-map.md), [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Target surface). The check-id is `symbol-exists` for `adr.cites-code` and `criterion-maps-to-test` for `spec` `maps-to-test`, so the probe applies the test predicate only to the latter (the design-itemized snapshot contents, [validation.md](design/validation.md):103).
- **(e) The snapshot is read-only + recompute-on-demand.** The wire contract carries the snapshot **by path-ref** (`effective_state: { snapshot_path }`, [validation.md](design/validation.md):106) — the engine *materializes* it; the actual subprocess hand-off is inc 3. M10 planning resolved findings to **recompute-on-demand** (no cache layer — a subprocess probe is read-only + deterministic). This increment proves only that the engine can **build + serialize** the snapshot (the `(target-address, anchor-value, check-id)` pairs + the working-tree root) and that an **in-process test probe** can consume it over the serialized form.

*No genuine new fork surfaced.* Every shape below is settled: the reshaped-seam target+serializable-ctx in [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The wire contract ("M10 reshapes the seam") + [module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md) → Probe boundary; the direct-enumeration target surface (created/edited ∪ bound, skip committed-not-in-effective-state) in [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Target surface (the design-review B1 fix); the snapshot contents itemized in [validation.md](design/validation.md):103. The only illustrative items — the concrete reshaped-trait Rust signature, the ctx/target carrier shape, and the snapshot struct + serde form — are **doc-elaboration pins** made + logged by the executor. Risk-first, linear: the seam reshape with `override-default` byte-identical first (T1 — retire "don't break the lone impl" before anything rides the new shape), the direct anchor enumeration over effective state next (T2 — the engine names *which* anchors), the serializable snapshot the wire carries by path-ref last (T3 — proven end-to-end with an in-process test probe). *Why this cut:* the smallest set delivering all four *Grouped scope* bullets — the seam reshape + `override-default` migration (bullet 1 → T1), the target-surface enumeration (bullet 2 → T2), the materialized serializable snapshot (bullet 3 → T3). The fourth "Tests (fixtures)" bullet is **not** a fourth task — its four clauses fold into the per-task done-criteria (in-process test probe over a serialized snapshot → T3; enumeration finds anchors in created **and** bound docs + skips committed-not-in-effective-state → T2; `override-default` byte-identical through the reshaped seam → T1). No creep into inc 3 (subprocess invoker + meta-findings) / inc 4 (the `doc-code` executable) / inc 5 (the task-gate wiring + flow 13) — **no real probe is invoked over the snapshot here**, only an in-process test double.

- **T1 (engine — reshape the `Probe` seam to `check(target, ctx)` with a serializable effective-state ctx; migrate `override-default` with no behaviour change):** the seam admits a `target` + a *serializable* effective-state ctx (the doc-code shape) **and** `override-default`'s existing non-task `(deltas, pack)` shape, with `override-default` byte-identical. *Done:* `crates/engine/src/probe.rs` — the `Probe` seam carries a `target` and the ctx surface is reshaped so a serializable effective-state ctx is representable (the concrete carrier — a `target` param + an enum/associated-type/generic over the two ctx shapes — is an executor elaboration pin; log it); `OverrideDefaultProbe` is migrated onto the reshaped seam still delegating to `override_default::classify`; the one live caller (`crates/cli/src/upgrade.rs:68`) compiles against the new shape; an engine unit test proves `OverrideDefaultProbe` over the reshaped seam returns **exactly** what `classify(deltas, pack)` returns over the same `(deltas, pack)` (the migrated-`probe.rs` test), and the flow-8 / upgrade acceptance suite (`flow8_override_default_warning.rs`, `upgrade.rs`, `upgrade_v1_v2.rs`, `severity_tuning.rs`) is **green with goldens untouched** (no behaviour change) — gate green.
- **T2 (engine — target-surface enumeration over the task's effective-state docs):** the engine enumerates every `code-anchor` leaf as a `(target-address, anchor-value, check-id)` pair over the task's effective state — the docs **created/edited** (staged `<dir>/docs/*.md`) ∪ the docs **bound** into read-roles (`roles.json` → committed `<location>/<slug>.md`) — by **direct field enumeration**, never the edge index. *Done:* a new engine enumeration (an `engine` module, e.g. extending `validate`/`state` or a new `target_surface` module) walks the staged instances and the bound committed instances, parses each against its schema, and collects every field whose `FieldType::Pack` names `code-anchor` (header field + repeatable-item leaf) into a deterministically-ordered (stable address-sorted) list of `(target-address, anchor-value, check-id)` pairs, with check-id = `symbol-exists` for `adr.cites-code` / `criterion-maps-to-test` for `spec` `maps-to-test`; a fixture-task test proves (i) anchors in a **created** `adr` **and** a **bound** `spec` are both found, (ii) a committed `adr`/`spec` that is **neither edited nor bound** contributes **zero** pairs (the masking-trap guard — hardening #5: exercised against effective state that **omits** an unrelated committed doc), and (iii) a doc with no `code-anchor` value contributes zero pairs — gate green.
- **T3 (engine — materialize the serializable effective-state snapshot; prove with an in-process test probe):** the engine materializes the read-only snapshot the wire contract carries by path-ref — the enumerated `(target-address, anchor-value, check-id)` pairs (T2) + the working-tree root — as a *serializable* value, and an in-process test probe consumes it over the serialized form. *Done:* a serializable snapshot type (the executor pins its struct + serde form — itemized: the pairs + the working-tree root, [validation.md](design/validation.md):103, recompute-on-demand) is built from T2's enumeration; an engine unit test round-trips the snapshot through its serialization (serialize → deserialize → equal, **serialization unit-proven**); and an **in-process test probe** (an `impl Probe` test double, not a subprocess — that is inc 3) is handed a `(target, ctx)` carrying the **serialized** snapshot and returns findings derived from the pairs it reads (proving the reshaped seam admits a probe consuming the serialized effective-state ctx end-to-end) — gate green.

- *Elaboration pin (T1 — reshaped-trait signature + ctx/target carrier):* the design settles the *semantics* (the seam carries a `target` + a serializable effective-state ctx, and `override-default`'s non-task `(deltas, pack)` shape survives byte-identical) but leaves the concrete Rust carrier illustrative. The executor chooses + logs the form (a `target` parameter plus either an enum over the two ctx shapes, an associated type per probe, or a generic ctx); the binding is that an *in-process* and a *subprocess* probe consume the **same logical input** (a live graph vs. its serialized read-only snapshot + path-ref), [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The wire contract. ## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 2 / T1 shipped: `Probe` seam reshaped to `check(target, ctx)`; `override-default` migrated byte-identical

- **Carrier pin resolved — a `target` parameter + two associated types (`Target`, `Ctx<'a>`).** `trait Probe { type Target; type Ctx<'a>; fn check<'a>(&self, target: &Self::Target, ctx: Self::Ctx<'a>) -> Vec<Finding>; }` (`crates/engine/src/probe.rs`). Chosen over the enum-over-both-ctx-shapes and single-generic-ctx alternatives the pin (DECISIONS 2026-06-06, M10 inc-2 decomposition) left open, because each probe must declare *exactly* its own target + ctx with **no coercion**: an enum variant would force `override-default`'s live `&dyn PackSource` handle to share a type with the serializable doc-code snapshot, and a single generic ctx loses per-probe specificity. Per-probe associated types let `OverrideDefaultProbe` keep `Target = ()` (target-less — its ctx names the override surface it reconciles) + `Ctx<'a> = OverrideCtx<'a>` (the M6 live, non-serializable handle, **unchanged**), while the doc-code probe (inc 3+) will declare `Target = Address` + a serializable snapshot `Ctx`. `Ctx<'a>` is a **GAT** (stable since 1.65; edition-2024 / Rust 1.95 here) so a borrowing ctx (`OverrideCtx<'a>`) and a borrowed-snapshot ctx are both expressible — the binding ("in-process and subprocess probes consume the *same logical input*", validation.md → The wire contract) holds: the serializable ctx is *representable* without the live ctx being forced serializable.
- **`override-default` byte-identical (verified red, not asserted).** The migration changes only the *call shape* (`check(&(), ctx)` — a `target` it ignores), never `override_default::classify`. Red was genuine: the reshaped `check<'a>(target, ctx)` signature does not compile against the M6 `check(&self, ctx)` call sites, so the migrated `probe::tests::override_default_probe_delegates_to_classify` (now driving `check(&(), OverrideCtx{…})`) and the lone live caller (`crates/cli/src/upgrade.rs:68`) had to move onto the new shape before the suite went green. The flow-8/upgrade acceptance suite (`flow8_override_default_warning.rs`, `upgrade.rs`, `upgrade_v1_v2.rs`, `severity_tuning.rs`) passes with **goldens untouched** — no behaviour change. Files: `crates/engine/src/probe.rs`, `crates/cli/src/upgrade.rs`.

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 3 / T1 shipped: the concrete wire request/response contract

- **Elaboration pin resolved — the concrete Rust wire types (within the locked envelope).** `engine::probe::{ProbeRequest, ProbeEffectiveState, ProbeResponse}` (`crates/engine/src/probe.rs`) concretize `validation.md`:106-112's illustrative `{probe_id, target, effective_state:{snapshot_path}, config, schema_version}` → `{findings, schema_version}`. Three pins inside the locked shape: (1) **`target` is the address grammar's string form** (`String`), not the internal [`Address`] enum — the wire carries the flat URI a separate-program probe reads (matching `TargetAnchor.address`, already a `String`); the engine parses it where it needs the typed form. (2) **`config` is `serde_json::Map<String, Value>`** (an opaque object) — always present, projecting `{}` when the cascade resolves none; this keeps the envelope honest without prematurely typing a config schema the design defers. (3) **`schema_version` reuses `result::SCHEMA_VERSION` (=2)** — the wire shares the engine's one contract-evolution marker rather than minting a second; the *versioning policy* stays deferred (`validation.md`:112). Field order is **pinned** on both structs (`probe_id, target, effective_state, config, schema_version` / `findings, schema_version`) and golden-locked — a reorder/rename/serde-slip breaks `probe::tests::request_json_projection_is_the_pinned_envelope` (verified red by a deliberate field swap). The response's `findings` deserialize into the engine's one [`Finding`] shape from **probe-authored** JSON (a probe may omit the `(probe, check)` handle — `#[serde(default)]` — and the engine derives it downstream), and a response round-trips serialize → deserialize → equal. **No invoker, no process spawn, no meta-findings this task** (T2/T3/T4).

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 3 / T2 shipped: the CLI subprocess invoker over real adversarial stub processes

- **Elaboration pins resolved — the wait-timeout mechanism + the raw-outcome carrier shape.** `cli::invoke::invoke_probe` (`crates/cli/src/invoke.rs`) is the subprocess invoker: it writes the T1 request to the child's stdin, enforces a wall-clock `budget`, and returns a **raw, classification-free** outcome. (1) **Mechanism = std-only, no `wait-timeout` crate** (minimal-deps reflex; `std::process::Command` already used across the CLI): the child's stdout is drained on a dedicated reader thread (so a chatty probe can't deadlock on a full pipe), and the main thread keeps the `Child` handle and polls `try_wait` against the deadline at a 10ms interval. The handle is retained *precisely* so a budget overrun can `kill()` + `wait()` (reap) the child — the `wait_with_output`-in-a-thread + `recv_timeout` shape the planner floated was abandoned because it *moves* the child into the waiter, leaving no kill handle on timeout (a leaked process). (2) **Carrier shape:** `ProbeOutcome { stdout: Vec<u8>, status: ProbeStatus }` with `ProbeStatus::{Exited { code: Option<i32> }, TimedOut }` — the invoker classifies **nothing** (a zero/non-zero exit, valid JSON, garbage, or empty stdout are all just *reported*); T3's engine turns these into the `pack-probe-integrity.*` meta-findings. A timed-out outcome carries **empty** stdout (a timed-out probe is untrusted, partial output discarded). (3) **Crate structure:** the `cli` crate gains a `[lib]` target (`src/lib.rs`, `pub mod invoke`) so the invoker is integration-testable against real stub processes independent of the binary's command dispatch; `main.rs`'s module tree is untouched (T3 wires the invoker into the validate path). Proven by `tests/probe_invoker.rs` — four stubs **compiled with `rustc` into a temp dir** (real processes, not mocks): well-behaved (verbatim stdout + zero exit), sleeper (real elapsed bound → `TimedOut`, child killed not leaked — the test asserts it doesn't hang), crasher (non-zero exit reported raw), garbage (raw unparseable bytes + zero exit). **The engine adds NO `std::process` use** (shell-free invariant holds).

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 3 / T3 shipped: response ingestion + the three meta-finding synthesis

- **Elaboration pins resolved — the engine-side raw-outcome mirror + the meta-finding classification.** `engine::probe::ingest_probe_run(probe_id, &ProbeRun) -> Vec<Finding>` (`crates/engine/src/probe.rs`) is the pure synthesis fn, proven in isolation against the four T2 outcome shapes (no `validate_task` wiring — that is inc 5). (1) **Carrier mirror:** the engine cannot depend on `cli` (the dep arrow points the other way), so T3 mints `engine::probe::{ProbeRun, ProbeRunStatus}` mirroring the CLI invoker's `ProbeOutcome`/`ProbeStatus` field-for-field (`stdout: Vec<u8>` + `Exited { code: Option<i32> } | TimedOut`); the inc-5 wiring seam translates the live `cli` outcome into this engine type before calling the synthesis fn. (2) **Classification (the four shapes):** `TimedOut` → one blocking `timeout` (partial stdout discarded); `Exited { code: Some(0) }` + parseable `ProbeResponse` → the probe's own `findings` **unchanged** (severity left for the post-pass — this fn does not grade) + **no** meta-finding; `Exited { code: Some(0) }` + unparseable/empty/valid-JSON-but-not-a-response stdout → one blocking `malformed-output`; any other exit (non-zero, **or signal-terminated `code: None`**) → one blocking `crash`. Empty stdout on a zero exit is `malformed-output`, not clean — a clean adjudication emits `{"findings":[],…}`, never an empty stream. (3) **Code-id reconciliation (like `override-default`):** each meta-finding is built with descriptive code `pack-probe-integrity.probe-failure` carrying the human reason (exit-code / parse-error ride the message per `validation.md`:121-122), then re-keyed via `.with_check(<reason>)` so the **severity handle** is the canonical `(probe, check) = ("pack-probe-integrity", {timeout|crash|malformed-output})` the post-pass + floor (T4) lock on. Severity is synthesized `Blocking` (the intrinsic floor). The fn **never panics** on any stdout shape or status — swept by `ingestion_never_panics_on_any_misbehavior` over the full {empty, truncated, non-JSON, binary, valid-non-response, valid-response} × {exit-0, exit-nonzero, signal, timeout} cross-product. **The engine adds NO `std::process` use** (shell-free invariant holds).

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 3 / T4 shipped: the three meta-findings are intrinsic + floor-locked

- **The three `pack-probe-integrity.{timeout,crash,malformed-output}.severity` keys land in the knob surface, the intrinsic floor-assertion set, and the post-pass inventory** — so a synthesized meta-finding (T3) is post-pass-routed, defaults `blocking`, and a below-`blocking` `scalar-set` is **soft-rejected at cascade resolution**. `knobs.yaml` gains the three (`type: enum`, `of: [blocking, warning, advisory]`, `default: blocking`, `floor: blocking`), placed after `workflow-refs.*` / before `schema-conformance.*`; `engine::knobs::INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS` gains the three (the load-time assertion now floors 16 intrinsic keys — an unfloored/undeclared one still fails loud via the existing `unfloored_intrinsic`/`undeclared_intrinsic` guards); `result::CHECK_INVENTORY` gains the three `(probe, check)` rows. Proven by `knobs::tests::pack_probe_integrity_timeout_demotion_is_soft_rejected`: over the **embedded** bytes through the production floor-wiring (`with_floors`), a project `scalar-set …timeout.severity advisory` resolves the key still `blocking`, is **not** an applied override, and surfaces as a single `RejectedDemotion (advisory, blocking, Project)`. **Additive golden re-pin recorded as intended (hardening #4):** `loaded_knobs_seed_the_pack_default_scalar_surface`, `embedded_knobs_floor_the_intrinsic_checks` (auto-tracks `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS`), and the cli `embedded_pack_config_declares_the_knob_surface` inline snapshot are re-pinned to admit exactly these three. **The two `doc-code.*` tunable rows are NOT here** — they ride to inc 5 (which reconciles the final 25/16/9 count), per the cross-increment punt above (hardening #6).

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M10 Increment 4 ("the `doc-code` probe executable — tree-sitter resolution: symbol-exists + criterion-maps-to-test") into three ordered, single-concern tasks, each with an observable red step. This increment builds **only the `doc-code` program** — the dev pack's first probe executable, a **separate program outside the engine workspace** ([module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md) → Probe boundary: "Probe executables live outside the workspace") — that, given the locked wire request on stdin + the snapshot at the path-ref, resolves each `path#symbol` anchor against the working tree via **tree-sitter** (Rust grammar) and emits `doc-code.symbol-exists` / `doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test` findings, **blocking on a dangling anchor**. It rides the **proven seam + invoker** (inc 3) and is proven **on fixtures only** — the program is driven directly with a crafted request + snapshot; it is **not** scheduled in `validate_task`, not wired to the CLI invoker at finalize, and the flow-13 acceptance + the two `doc-code.*` inventory rows are **inc 5** (see the scope-boundary pin below). Homes of record: [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The `doc-code` probe (anchor grammar, the two checks, blocking semantics, static-parse determinism) + The wire contract (the request/response the program binds to); acceptance scaffolding = [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 13.

*Grounding (read the code at HEAD `04054a3`, exercised against the M10 inc-4 shape):*
- **(a) The wire contract the program binds to is built + golden-locked (inc 3).** `engine::probe::ProbeRequest { probe_id, target: String, effective_state: ProbeEffectiveState { snapshot_path: PathBuf }, config: Map, schema_version }` and `ProbeResponse { findings: Vec<Finding>, schema_version }` (`crates/engine/src/probe.rs`), serde forms pinned by `request_json_projection_is_the_pinned_envelope` / `response_round_trips_through_serde`. The program **reads the request from stdin** (the invoker writes it there — `crates/cli/src/invoke.rs`), **reads the snapshot from the path-ref**, and **emits a `ProbeResponse` JSON on stdout**, exit 0. Because the program is a separate (potentially non-Rust) crate that cannot depend on `engine`, it re-declares the request/response/snapshot/finding shapes as its **own serde structs** matching the locked JSON wire form — `response_findings_deserialize_into_the_one_finding_shape` already proves probe-authored JSON (with `severity`/`code`/`message`/`location{address,line,col}`/`route`, the `(probe,check)` handle `#[serde(default)]` and derived downstream) ingests into the engine's one `Finding` shape, so the program's emit target is locked.
- **(b) The snapshot itemizes exactly what the program needs.** `engine::probe::EffectiveStateSnapshot { anchors: Vec<TargetAnchor>, working_tree_root: PathBuf }`, each `TargetAnchor { address: String, anchor_value: String, check_id: String }` (`crates/engine/src/target_surface.rs`). The program iterates `anchors`, resolves each `anchor_value` (`<path>#<symbol>` or bare `<path>`) against `working_tree_root`, and applies the test predicate **only when `check_id == "criterion-maps-to-test"`** (the engine already extracted the values; the program does no doc parse — `validation.md`:103). The finding's `location.address` is the anchor's `address`.
- **(c) The anchor grammar + the two checks are settled.** `<repo-relative-path>#<symbol>`; a bare `<path>` degrades to a **file-existence** check (`validation.md`:151). `symbol-exists` = the anchor resolves to a real file (and, if a `#symbol` is named, a real symbol); `criterion-maps-to-test` = symbol existence **+ the is-a-test predicate** (Rust `#[test]`-attributed fn) (`validation.md`:146-147). A **dangling** anchor (present, unresolvable) is a **blocking** finding mirroring `ref-resolves`; **absence is not a finding** (the snapshot carries only present anchors) (`validation.md`:161).
- **(d) tree-sitter is buildable here (verified, not assumed).** `cargo add tree-sitter tree-sitter-rust` resolves + locks (registry reachable); a spike compiled the Rust grammar and proved both symbol lookup (top-level `function_item` by name) and the is-a-test predicate (a preceding `attribute_item` containing `test` → `#[test]`). Determinism holds by construction: **static AST parse only — no `cargo`/build/network/wall-clock** (contract rules 1/3/5/6, `validation.md`:153,629); same code + same anchors → same findings.

**Scope-boundary pin (tracked, not a fork) — inc 4 is the program *on fixtures*; the gate-wiring + flow 13 + the `doc-code.*` inventory rows are inc 5.** The roadmap inc-4 *Deliverable* says "proven on fixtures, riding the proven seam + invoker"; inc-5 ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md):634-643) owns scheduling `doc-code` in `validate_task`, the CLI invoker wiring at finalize, the `doc-code.{symbol-exists,criterion-maps-to-test}` (tunable) inventory + `knobs.yaml` rows (which reconcile the 25/16/9 count), and the flow-13 e2e. So inc 4 lands **no `validate_task` scheduling, no invoker call site, no `CHECK_INVENTORY`/`knobs.yaml` change, no flow-13 e2e** — the inc-5 planner owns all of those; the inc-4 validator confirms only that the standalone program resolves anchors correctly when driven directly. The two `doc-code.*` rows already carry their cross-increment punt to inc 5 ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-06-06, M10 inc-3 decomposition).

*No genuine new fork surfaced.* Every shape is settled (grounding a–d). The illustrative items — the program's **crate location + name** (a sibling dir outside `[workspace].members`, e.g. `pack/probes/doc-code/`, so its tree-sitter deps stay out of the engine/cli lock), the internal tree-sitter resolution module structure, the file-extension→grammar dispatch, and the exact finding `message`/`route` wording — are **doc-elaboration pins** made + logged by the executor. Risk-first, linear: the wire-conformant I/O skeleton + **file-existence** resolution first (T1 — the program reads the request/snapshot and emits a valid response before any AST work), then **tree-sitter symbol resolution** for `symbol-exists` (T2 — `#symbol` resolves against the file AST), then the **is-a-test predicate** for `criterion-maps-to-test` + the determinism re-run (T3 — the headline). *Why this cut:* the smallest set delivering all three substantive *Grouped scope* bullets — the executable + its request/snapshot I/O + the bare-path file-existence floor (bullet 1 → T1), `symbol-exists` symbol resolution (the first of bullet 2's two checks → T2), `criterion-maps-to-test` + the is-a-test predicate + the static-parse determinism bullet (bullet 2's second check + bullet 3 → T3). The fourth "Tests (fixtures)" bullet is **not** a fourth task — its four clauses fold into the per-task done-criteria (resolvable symbol/test → no finding: T2/T3; deleted symbol → `symbol-exists` blocks: T2; `maps-to-test` at a non-existent/non-`#[test]` fn → `criterion-maps-to-test` blocks: T3; determinism over repeated runs: T3). No creep into inc 5 (gate wiring + flow 13).

- **T1 (probe crate — the `doc-code` executable skeleton: wire-conformant stdin→stdout + bare-path/file-existence resolution):** a standalone program (outside the workspace members) that reads a `ProbeRequest` from stdin, reads the `EffectiveStateSnapshot` from `effective_state.snapshot_path`, resolves each anchor's **file** (`<path>` before any `#`) against `working_tree_root`, emits a blocking `doc-code.<check_id>` finding (keyed on the anchor's `address`) for a **missing file** and none for a present one, and writes a valid `ProbeResponse` JSON to stdout, exit 0. *Done:* the new probe crate exists outside `[workspace].members` (location/name an executor pin; logged); driven by a fixture test (the program built, then invoked via `cli::invoke::invoke_probe` over a crafted request + a temp working tree + a serialized snapshot) — a snapshot with one anchor at a present file and one at an absent file ingests (via `engine::probe::ingest_probe_run` over the invoker outcome, the inc-3 path) to **exactly one** `doc-code` finding for the absent file, **no** meta-finding; a bare-`<path>` anchor (no `#`) at a present dir/file passes — gate green (`cargo build`/`test`/`clippy -D warnings`/`fmt --check` across the workspace **and** the new crate). *No tree-sitter, no symbol resolution, no `validate_task` wiring.*
- **T2 (probe crate — tree-sitter `symbol-exists`: resolve `#symbol` against the file AST):** for an anchor `<path>#<symbol>`, the program parses `<path>` via tree-sitter (Rust grammar, chosen by file extension) and emits a blocking `doc-code.symbol-exists` finding when `<symbol>` resolves to **no top-level symbol** in the file, none when it resolves. *Done:* `crates/.../doc-code` gains the tree-sitter resolution module; a fixture test over the invoker path asserts a `cites-code`-shaped anchor (`check_id: symbol-exists`) pointing at a **real fn** in a fixture `.rs` file → **no finding**; pointing at a **deleted/renamed symbol** in the same file → one blocking `doc-code.symbol-exists` finding naming the target address; a `#symbol` whose **file** is absent still blocks (file-existence subsumed) — gate green. *The is-a-test predicate is T3.*
- **T3 (probe crate — `criterion-maps-to-test` is-a-test predicate + determinism over repeated runs):** for an anchor with `check_id == "criterion-maps-to-test"`, the program emits a blocking `doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test` finding when the resolved symbol is **not a Rust `#[test]`** fn (or does not exist), none when it resolves to a real `#[test]`; a `symbol-exists` anchor is unaffected (no test predicate). *Done:* a fixture test over the invoker path asserts a `maps-to-test` anchor at a **`#[test]` fn** → no finding; at a **non-`#[test]` fn** → one blocking `doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test`; at a **non-existent fn** → one blocking `doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test`; and a **determinism** assertion — the same request + snapshot driven **twice** yields **byte-identical** `ProbeResponse` stdout (hardening #7: static parse is a pure function of code + anchors; no `cargo`/build/network/wall-clock) — gate green. **This completes the executable**; inc 5 schedules it in the task gate + runs flow 13.

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 4 / T1 shipped: the `doc-code` executable skeleton (wire-conformant stdin→stdout + file-existence resolution)

- **Crate location/name pin (executor elaboration):** the probe is `crates/cli/pack/probes/doc-code/` (binary `doc-code`), a sibling to the embedded pack content (`crates/cli/pack/{config,schemas,steps,workflows}`) so it travels *with* the dev pack but **outside** `[workspace].members`. Detached two ways: the root manifest gains `workspace.exclude = ["crates/cli/pack/probes/doc-code"]` (explicitness) **and** the probe manifest carries an empty `[workspace]` table — required because the package sits under a member's directory tree, where `exclude` alone does not stop cargo's workspace-association (cargo's own error names the empty-`[workspace]` fix). Its deps (`serde`/`serde_json` now; tree-sitter in T2) live in the probe's **own** `Cargo.lock`, never the engine/cli lock. `target/` gitignored locally; `Cargo.lock` committed (standalone binary → reproducible build).
- **Wire shapes re-declared, not depended-on.** The program cannot depend on `engine`, so it re-declares `ProbeRequest`/`ProbeEffectiveState`/`EffectiveStateSnapshot`/`TargetAnchor`/`ProbeResponse`/`Finding`/`Severity`/`Location` as its own serde structs matching the locked JSON form; `engine::probe`'s `response_findings_deserialize_into_the_one_finding_shape` already proves probe-authored JSON ingests into the engine `Finding`. The probe emits `(probe, check)` explicitly (split from `code`) though the engine defaults them — belt-and-suspenders, costs nothing.
- **T1 resolution = file-existence only.** Each anchor's file is `<anchor_value>` up to the first `#` (a bare `<path>` has none → the whole value is the file, the file-existence check `validation.md` specifies); a missing file → one blocking `doc-code.<check_id>` finding keyed on the anchor's `address`, a present file/dir → none. No tree-sitter, no `#symbol` resolution (T2), no `validate_task` wiring (inc 5). Proven by `crates/cli/tests/doc_code_probe.rs`: the program is built via its own manifest, driven through `cli::invoke::invoke_probe` over a crafted request + temp working tree + serialized snapshot, and the invoker outcome ingested through `engine::probe::ingest_probe_run` — a present-file + absent-file + bare-path fixture yields **exactly one** finding (the absent file) with **no** `pack-probe-integrity` meta-finding. Red-verified by inverting the existence test (2 spurious findings).

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 4 / T3 shipped: the `criterion-maps-to-test` is-a-test predicate + determinism by re-execution

- **Is-a-test predicate scope (executor elaboration pin) = the canonical Rust `#[test]` only.** A `criterion-maps-to-test` anchor's resolved `#symbol` satisfies the predicate iff a top-level `function_item` of that name is **immediately preceded** by an `attribute_item` whose `attribute` child text is exactly `test`. This matches the AST shape verified at plan time (a preceding `attribute_item` containing `test`), and deliberately **excludes** `#[cfg(test)]` (attribute path is `cfg`) and `#[tokio::test]` (a `scoped_identifier`, not a bare `test`) — M10 proves Rust's standard `#[test]`, no generality for an attribute form no acceptance exercises (`validation.md`:153). The predicate is layered on symbol existence: a `criterion-maps-to-test` anchor first runs `symbol-exists` (an absent symbol → `dangling_symbol`), then the test predicate (a symbol that resolves but is not a `#[test]` fn → a distinct `not_a_test` message). `symbol-exists` anchors never run the predicate.
- **Determinism by re-execution (hardening #7).** A static AST parse is a pure function of (code + anchors) — no `cargo`/build/network/wall-clock (contract rules 1/3/5/6) — so `doc_code_response_is_byte_identical_across_runs` drives the same request + snapshot **twice** through the invoker and asserts **byte-identical** `ProbeResponse` stdout (over a mixed fixture: a passing `#[test]` fn, a failing non-test fn, a `symbol-exists` anchor), guarded against a vacuous pass by asserting the one expected blocking finding is present. Proven in `crates/cli/tests/doc_code_probe.rs` over the invoker + ingestion path: a `maps-to-test` anchor at a `#[test]` fn → no finding; at a non-`#[test]` fn → one blocking `doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test`; at a non-existent fn → one blocking; a `symbol-exists` anchor at a plain fn → no finding. Red-verified by the non-test-fn case (the pre-T3 impl passed it as plain symbol existence → 0 findings vs the required 1). **This completes the `doc-code` executable**; inc 5 schedules it in `validate_task` + runs flow 13 + lands the two `doc-code.*` inventory rows.

## 2026-06-06 — M10 Increment 5 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M10 Increment 5 ("wire `doc-code` into the task gate + flow 13 acceptance — the headline") into four ordered, single-concern tasks, each with an observable red step. This is the **integration + acceptance** increment: every substrate is built and proven in isolation (inc 1 the pack-declared `code-anchor` + the two doctype anchors + `set-field` absent-insert; inc 2 the reshaped `Probe` seam + `enumerate_target_surface` + the serializable `EffectiveStateSnapshot`; inc 3 the wire contract + the CLI `invoke_probe` + `ingest_probe_run` + the three floor-locked `pack-probe-integrity.*` rows; inc 4 the real tree-sitter `doc-code` executable). Inc 5 connects them at the live `validate`/`finalize` gate and proves the **headline** end-to-end through the binary: documentation drift caught deterministically at the task boundary, the **blocking** case the proof. Homes of record: [validation.md](design/validation.md) → The `doc-code` probe + Target surface + How it gates `finalize` + Severity inventory; acceptance = [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 13.

*Grounding (read the code at HEAD `f4415d4` + the inc 1–4 commits, exercised against the M10 inc-5 shape):*
- **(a) The full probe pipeline exists as separate engine + CLI fns; nothing connects them at the live gate yet.** `engine::target_surface::enumerate_target_surface(task_dir, repo_root, schemas) -> Vec<TargetAnchor>` (inc-2 T2), `engine::probe::EffectiveStateSnapshot::new(anchors, working_tree_root)` + its serde form (inc-2 T3), `engine::probe::{ProbeRequest, ProbeResponse}` (inc-3 T1), `cli::invoke::invoke_probe(program, request, budget) -> ProbeOutcome` (inc-3 T2), and `engine::probe::ingest_probe_run(probe_id, &ProbeRun) -> Vec<Finding>` (inc-3 T3) are all built + tested. But `engine::validate::validate_task` (`crates/engine/src/validate.rs:98`) runs **only** the inline `file-state` / `schema-conformance` / `ref-resolves` sweeps — **no `doc-code` enumeration, no invoke, no ingest**. The CLI's `Task::validate` (`crates/cli/src/task.rs:330`) calls `validate_task` and is the **single** engine entry both `validate` and `finalize` flow through (`task.rs:361` — `finalize` calls `self.validate()`), so wiring `doc-code` into that one path lights both surfaces at once.
- **(b) The engine cannot shell out; the CLI owns the invoker — so "schedule in `validate_task`" is an engine/CLI split, not an engine subprocess call.** The shell-free engine invariant ([finalize.rs](crates/cli/src/finalize.rs) framing, `module-layout.md` → Probe boundary) means `validate_task` itself must not spawn the probe. The settled split ([validation.md](design/validation.md):167-168, [module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md):61): the **engine owns** enumerate + materialize-snapshot + ingest + the severity post-pass; the **CLI owns** the invoke. The precedent is already in the same fn — `head` is read by the CLI via `git` and **passed into** `validate_task` (`task.rs:332,345`), keeping the engine shell-free. So the doc-code probe-runner is threaded into the engine the same way: the engine exposes the target surface + snapshot, the CLI invokes via `invoke_probe`, and the doc-code findings are merged into the same `findings` vector `ValidationReport::new(findings, resolved)` runs the M6 post-pass over (`result.rs:240`) — so they tune through the cascade **for free** once the two `doc-code.*` inventory rows land (grounding (d)). The **concrete seam shape** — whether `validate_task` takes a probe-runner closure/trait the CLI implements with `invoke_probe`, or the CLI orchestrates `enumerate → snapshot → invoke → ingest` around `validate_task` and merges the findings into the report it returns — is a **doc-elaboration pin** made + logged by the executor within this settled split, *not* a fork. (The closure-into-`validate_task` shape keeps "one engine entry, two surfaces" literally true and is the lighter touch; the executor confirms against the code.)
- **(c) The probe **program path** at runtime is the one genuinely-unaddressed mechanism — and it is an executor elaboration pin, not a fork.** The `doc-code` executable lives at `crates/cli/pack/probes/doc-code/` **outside** `[workspace].members` (its own `Cargo.lock`, tree-sitter deps detached — inc-4 T1). The inc-4 *test* builds it on demand via `cargo build --manifest-path …` into the probe's own `target/` (`crates/cli/tests/doc_code_probe.rs:57-76`). Production `jigc` needs to **locate** that binary when it schedules at finalize. The design settles *that* a separate program is invoked (`code-anchor ⇒ doc-code` binding, the probe id from the `PackTypeDecl.adjudicator` read via `cli::pack::pack_field_types`) and *that* the CLI owns the invoke; it leaves the **path-resolution mechanism** illustrative. The executor chooses + logs the concrete form — e.g. an env-var override (`JIGC_DOC_CODE_PROBE`, the M5 `JIGC_PACK_DIR` precedent for an installable seam) the e2e sets to the test-built binary, with a documented production default (a known install-relative path / build-from-pack-source) — a doc-elaboration pin within the settled "CLI owns the invoker, probe lives outside the workspace" architecture, **not** a fork. The acceptance e2e (T3/T4) drives the *real* tree-sitter `doc-code` binary (built from its manifest), never a stub — per flow 13 the stubs appear only for the meta-finding firing (T4).
- **(d) The two `doc-code.*` inventory rows are NOT yet landed; the three `pack-probe-integrity.*` rows ARE (inc-3 T4).** `result::CHECK_INVENTORY` (`result.rs:173-195`) carries the three `pack-probe-integrity.*` rows but **no `doc-code.*` rows**; `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml` has the three `pack-probe-integrity.*.severity` keys but **no `doc-code.*.severity` keys**. The roadmap inc-5 bullet 1 + the inc-3 cross-increment punt ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-06-06, M10 inc-3) make inc 5 own adding the **two tunable** `doc-code.{symbol-exists,criterion-maps-to-test}.severity` keys (`type: enum`, `of: [blocking, warning, advisory]`, `default: blocking`, **no `floor:`** — they are tunable, not intrinsic) + the two `CHECK_INVENTORY` rows, and **reconciling the final count to the [validation.md](design/validation.md):210 inventory (25 checks / 16 intrinsic / 9 tunable)**. The closed-surface knob golden (`knobs.rs` `loaded_knobs_seed_the_pack_default_scalar_surface` :241) + the cli `embedded_pack_config_declares_the_knob_surface` inline snapshot **must be re-pinned** to admit exactly these two (a justified, intended additive diff — hardening #4, recorded here as intended); the intrinsic-set assertion (`embedded_knobs_floor_the_intrinsic_checks`) **must NOT** gain them (they are not floored — adding them there would falsely lock a tunable check). This is the cross-increment punt **landing at its named home**, completing the staged inventory delivery (hardening #6).
- **(e) The acceptance scaffolding is built (M3 `plan` / `implement-from-spec` / `jigc task bind`; inc-1 `jigc doc set-field`).** Flow 13's commands (`jigc start --workflow implement-from-spec`, `jigc task bind spec <addr> <id>`, `jigc start --task <id>`, `jigc doc create adr`, `jigc doc set-field adr:…#cites-code`, `jigc task finalize`) are all built; the spec criterion's `maps-to-test` rides the **editable channel** (raw git edit + commit *before* the work task mints, the M3 flow-6 precedent — committing after mint advances HEAD and blocks, the spiked pin-to-base constraint, [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md):747). So inc 5 builds **no new pack workflow or verb** — roadmap bullet 2 is "already admits / authors via existing surfaces," exercised by the e2e (T3/T4), not a standalone build task.

**Scope-seam confirmed (the cross-increment punt lands here).** Roadmap inc-5 bullet 1 says *both* the `doc-code.*` (tunable) and `pack-probe-integrity.*` (intrinsic) rows "land in `CHECK_INVENTORY` + `knobs.yaml`"; inc-3's punt resolved this — the three `pack-probe-integrity.*` rows landed in inc 3 (required for its floor-rejection proof), the **two `doc-code.*` rows land in inc 5** (need the real probe + the severity-demotion acceptance). Inc 5 owns the two `doc-code.*` rows + the final count reconciliation; it does **not** re-touch the three already-landed `pack-probe-integrity.*` rows except to confirm the count tallies (T2's done-criterion asserts 25/16/9 against [validation.md](design/validation.md):210).

*No genuine new fork surfaced.* Every shape is settled (grounding a–e): the engine/CLI split for scheduling ([validation.md](design/validation.md):167, [module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md):61), the `head`-passed-in precedent for keeping the engine shell-free, the M6 post-pass that tunes ingested findings for free ([result.rs](crates/engine/src/result.rs):240), the target surface (created/edited ∪ bound — inc-2 T2), the blocking-on-dangling semantics ([validation.md](design/validation.md):161), and the flow-13 acceptance bar ([worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md):804-811). The two illustrative items — the **concrete `validate_task`↔invoker seam shape** (closure/trait vs. CLI-orchestration) and the **production probe-program path-resolution mechanism** — are **doc-elaboration pins** made + logged by the executor (grounding (b), (c)). Risk-first, linear: the cascade/inventory surface first (T1 — the two `doc-code.*` rows so a wired finding routes through the post-pass; smallest, unblocks severity tuning), the live-gate wiring next (T2 — enumerate→invoke→ingest threaded into `validate_task`, proven through the binary on a crafted task), then the two-walk integration acceptance (T3 — flow 13 passing + blocking through the *real* probe), then the contract-satisfied + severity-tunable assertions (T4 — meta-finding firing + the severity demotion, the two remaining flow-13 acceptance-bar clauses). *Why this cut:* the smallest set delivering all three *Grouped scope* bullets — the inventory rows + the engine schedule/invoke/ingest wiring (bullet 1 → T1 + T2), the pack create-gate/`set-field`/editable-channel authoring (bullet 2, no code change → exercised by T3/T4), the flow-13 e2e split into the headline passing+blocking walks (bullet 3 walks → T3) and the meta-finding + severity-demotion assertions (bullet 3's remaining acceptance-bar clauses → T4). No creep beyond M10; the deferred items (OS sandboxing + `sandbox-violation`, staleness, store/doc-scope validate, `add-item`, findings caching) stay deferred per [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-06-06 (M10 scope settled).

- **T1 (engine + pack — land the two tunable `doc-code.*` inventory + knob rows; reconcile the count):** the `doc-code.{symbol-exists,criterion-maps-to-test}` checks join the post-pass inventory + the tunable knob surface, so a (T2-)ingested `doc-code` finding is cascade-routed and demotable, while the count tallies to the design inventory. *Done:* `crates/engine/src/result.rs` `CHECK_INVENTORY` gains `("doc-code","symbol-exists")` + `("doc-code","criterion-maps-to-test")`; `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml` gains `validation.doc-code.symbol-exists.severity` + `validation.doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test.severity` (`type: enum`, `of: [blocking, warning, advisory]`, `default: blocking`, **no `floor:`** — tunable, NOT in `INTRINSIC_CHECK_KEYS`); the closed-surface knob golden (`knobs.rs::loaded_knobs_seed_the_pack_default_scalar_surface`) + the cli `embedded_pack_config_declares_the_knob_surface` inline snapshot are **re-pinned** to admit exactly these two (the justified additive diff — grounding (d)); the intrinsic-floor assertion (`embedded_knobs_floor_the_intrinsic_checks`) is **unchanged** (proves the two are tunable, not floored); a test asserts (i) the inventory now totals **25 checks / 16 intrinsic / 9 tunable** matching [validation.md](design/validation.md):210, and (ii) a project `scalar-set validation.doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test.severity warning` **resolves applied** (the demotion is honored, not floor-rejected — the tunable counterpart to inc-3 T4's floor-rejection proof) — gate green.
- **T2 (engine + cli — schedule `doc-code` at the live `validate`/`finalize` gate: enumerate → invoke → ingest):** `validate_task` (via the settled engine/CLI split — the engine enumerates + snapshots + ingests, the CLI invokes the real `doc-code` program) runs `doc-code` over the task's effective-state anchors and merges its findings into the report the gate reads, with **no behaviour change for a task carrying no `code-anchor`** (the inert path). *Done:* the doc-code probe pipeline is wired into the single `validate_task`/`Task::validate` path (`crates/engine/src/validate.rs` + `crates/cli/src/task.rs`): for each `(target-address, anchor-value, check-id)` the engine enumerates over effective state (`enumerate_target_surface` — inc 2), the engine materializes the `EffectiveStateSnapshot`, the CLI invokes the real `doc-code` binary via `cli::invoke::invoke_probe` (the seam carrier + the probe-program path-resolution are executor pins — log them per grounding (b),(c)), and the engine ingests the outcome via `ingest_probe_run`, merging the findings into the `ValidationReport` so the M6 post-pass + the `finalize` blocking gate see them; a **binary-level** integration test (real `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc` + the test-built `doc-code` binary, over a throwaway repo) proves (i) a task whose created `adr` carries a `cites-code` anchor at a **present** symbol → the report **contains** a `doc-code.symbol-exists` finding *resolving* (non-blocking) and `validate` exits clean, (ii) the same anchor pointed at an **absent** symbol → a **blocking** `doc-code.symbol-exists` finding naming the target + route, and (iii) **the masking-trap + omitting-context guard (hardening #5)**: a task carrying **no** `code-anchor` doc produces **zero** `doc-code` findings and behaves byte-identically to the pre-wiring path (the inert/omitting context), while a task **with** an anchor produces the finding (the context that includes the target) — gate green. **No flow-13 finalize-walk e2e yet** (T3); this proves the wiring + the inert path in isolation.
- **T3 (e2e acceptance — flow 13 passing + blocking walks through the real probe):** the headline integration proof — a work task **binds** a `spec` (criterion carrying `maps-to-test`) and **creates** an `adr` (carrying `cites-code`), `doc-code` runs at `finalize`, **passes** (one commit) when both anchors resolve and **blocks** (no commit) when one dangles. *Done:* an e2e integration test (real `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc` + the real tree-sitter `doc-code` binary, throwaway git repo) walks flow 13 ([worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md):752-802): seed a committed `spec` whose `criteria` block carries a `maps-to-test: <path>#<test>` anchor via the **editable channel** (git edit + commit *before* mint); `jigc start --workflow implement-from-spec`; `jigc task bind spec <addr> <id>`; `jigc start --task <id>`; `jigc doc create adr`; `jigc doc set-field adr:…#cites-code --value <path>#<symbol>`; then assert — **passing walk:** with both the test + the symbol present, `finalize` **lands one commit** AND the report **contains both** `doc-code.symbol-exists` (created adr) + `doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test` (bound spec) findings *resolving* — a report with **zero `doc-code` findings fails the bar as hard as a missed block** (the masking guard — hardening #5, [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md):807); **blocking walk:** rename/delete the test (and symmetrically the symbol) so an anchor dangles → `finalize` **blocks**, non-zero exit, the finding names the target + a route, and `git rev-list --count HEAD` is **unchanged** (no commit) — gate green. The probe-program path is supplied to the binary via the pin T2 logged (e.g. an env var pointing at the test-built `doc-code`); both anchor shapes (header-field + repeatable-block-leaf) are exercised, proving both pack-extension axes real ([worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md):809).
- **T4 (e2e acceptance — contract satisfied (meta-finding firing) + severity cascade-tunable):** the two remaining flow-13 acceptance-bar clauses — a misbehaving probe surfaces an intrinsic-blocking meta-finding (the contract *satisfied, not waived*), and a tunable `doc-code` check demotes through the cascade while the intrinsic meta-findings stay floor-locked. *Done:* over the wired finalize gate (T2) in a throwaway repo with a task carrying a dangling `criterion-maps-to-test` anchor — **meta-finding firing:** point the probe-program path at a **stub** that sleeps past the budget → `finalize` blocks with an intrinsic `pack-probe-integrity.timeout` meta-finding (and a second assertion: a stub emitting non-JSON → `pack-probe-integrity.malformed-output`), proving the contract is enforced not stubbed ([worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md):808); **severity demotion (the real probe):** with a project `scalar-set validation.doc-code.criterion-maps-to-test.severity warning` recorded, the *dangling* criterion anchor **surfaces as a warning but does NOT block** — `finalize` lands the commit (the M6 post-pass, no code change) — while a `scalar-set validation.pack-probe-integrity.timeout.severity advisory` is **soft-rejected at resolution** (the meta-finding stays blocking — floor-locked, inc-3 T4) — gate green. This closes flow 13's acceptance bar (clauses 2 + 5, [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md):808,811) and **completes M10's mandated acceptance path**, the last deferred differentiator.

- *Elaboration pin (T2 — the `validate_task`↔invoker seam shape):* the design settles the *split* (engine enumerates/snapshots/ingests, CLI invokes — [validation.md](design/validation.md):167, [module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md):61) but leaves the concrete Rust seam illustrative. The executor chooses + logs the form — a probe-runner closure/trait passed into `validate_task` (keeping "one engine entry, two surfaces" literal, the `head`-passed-in precedent) vs. the CLI orchestrating `enumerate → snapshot → invoke_probe → ingest_probe_run` around `validate_task` and merging the findings into the returned report. The binding is *the engine never spawns; the CLI invokes; the merged findings run through the one M6 post-pass*. A doc-elaboration pin within the settled split, not a fork.
- *Elaboration pin (T2/T3 — the production probe-program path resolution):* the design settles *that* a separate `doc-code` program is invoked (`code-anchor ⇒ doc-code`, the adjudicator binding read via `cli::pack::pack_field_types`) and *that* the CLI owns the invoke, but leaves *how production `jigc` locates the binary* illustrative (the inc-4 test builds it via `cargo build --manifest-path`; production needs a runtime path). The executor chooses + logs the form — an env-var override (the M5 `JIGC_PACK_DIR` precedent) the e2e sets to the test-built binary, with a documented production default. The acceptance drives the **real** tree-sitter probe (never a stub) except for T4's deliberate meta-finding stubs. Within-spec elaboration, not a fork.
- *Cross-increment punt landed (hardening #6):* the two `doc-code.{symbol-exists,criterion-maps-to-test}` tunable inventory rows punted from inc 3 ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) 2026-06-06, M10 inc-3 decomposition) **land in T1**, and T1's done-criterion reconciles the final 25/16/9 count to [validation.md](design/validation.md):210 — the staged inventory delivery completes at its named home; the three `pack-probe-integrity.*` rows (landed inc 3) are not re-touched beyond the count assertion.
