Every bullet maps to a task in this increment; nothing is punted.

## 2026-06-13 — M19 test half: cross-session drift comparison ran — H0 (tie), but the backstop fired + drove repair (on jigc's own drift)

The build half shipped + audited clean (the warn-only `pre-commit` backstop + the finalize success-relay; binary re-pinned `5d64adc`). The **test half** ran the M18-owed regime ([completions/artifacts/M19/cross-session-test/](completions/artifacts/M19/cross-session-test/), pre-reg + appendix frozen first).

- **Design:** genuine cross-session forgetting — a fresh **cold blind subagent per step** (no memory, blind to prior steps touching docs) — over a longer/denser **no-cue** sequence (extended `ratelimit` seed, 16 citations / 4 docs, 8 steps). jigc arm has the warn-only backstop installed; static arm none. n=3 chains/arm (48 cold-subagent runs). Arm-J repair = agent discretion under CLAUDE.md.
- **Result: H0 — tie. All 6 chains ended at 0 stale citations.** Scored mechanically (per-commit citation resolution) + independently re-verified + Codex-passed.
- **The timeline is the finding, and it cuts against the naïve H1:** the **static arm was CLEAN at every commit** (right-first-try diligence — every cold agent fixed its own citation in-step, even cold + no-cue); the **jigc arm was the only one that drifted** — transient stale citations persisting up to 4-commit windows — and recovered via later **detector-prompted** cleanup (J repair commits credit `jigc validate` / "the store-scope doc-code gate" by name). So **unlike M18 (detector never fired), M19's backstop demonstrably fired in anger and drove repair** — a real loop-closure capability gain — **but on drift that arose in jigc's own arm**, and it was **neither a comparative end-state nor timeline win** (static dominated per-commit cleanliness).
- **Honest mechanism (independently challenged, corrected):** *net-dependent cleanup latency*, **not** moral hazard — jigc agents also attempted per-step honesty (a slip was missing a *second* citation site, not negligence). jigc = drift→detect→repair; static = right-first-try; both land clean, but only jigc ever exposed stale citations.
- **Load-bearing bound:** the backstop is **warn-only / advisory** — the loop closed because agents *heeded* the relayed warning, not as a mechanism guarantee (the ergonomic-not-enforced boundary). And static's clean record is N=3 first-try on a small, well-telegraphed citation set — not proven robustness. **The regime where jigc would strictly win** (first-try diligence leaving *residual* final drift the detector catches and the control ships) **was not reached — static didn't fail.** Owed for a real comparative result: denser/larger citation graphs, or truly separated human sessions, where diligence predictably leaves residual drift. Propagated to [VISION.md](VISION.md) → "What is proven (M17–M19)" and [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M19 Outcome.

## 2026-06-14 — Direction: accept scope-bound (option B); reframe the value claim as salience-independence

After the thrice-H0 arc, settled on the handover's **option B** — stop chasing a comparative-superiority benchmark; ship/harden what's built and reframe the value claim to what the evidence + mechanism support. Maurice's observation sharpened it: the three ties all held **instruction salience** fixed — the static arm got a *clean, on-point* "keep citations honest" rule, the best case for static conventions, and **symmetry required that idealization** (a fair test can only give both arms the same clean instruction).

- **The reframe (mechanism, not measurement):** static conventions are **salience-dependent** (work only as well as the agent attends to the relevant line, which decays as the rules file grows); jigc's backstop is **salience-independent** (the `pre-commit` sweep fires identically at 5 or 5,000 lines — a mechanism, not an instruction, so it never competes for attention). Predicts jigc's advantage appears precisely in the regime the tests *excluded* (large, noisy rules surface).
- **Why it stays unmeasured:** reproducing that regime means handing the static arm a realistically bloated rules file — which breaks symmetry and confounds the result (conventions degrade at scale, or *that* file was bad?). Stated as **predicted-by-mechanism, not measured, not cheaply measurable** — the honest scope boundary, not a backdoor superiority claim. Landed in [VISION.md](VISION.md) → "What is proven (M17–M19)".

The probe is a build-script-copied sibling today — **not embedded** — so (b) is net-new, not a swap of (a). ## 2026-06-14 — M20 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Plan, grounded in the actual code on top of Increment 1 (committed `c7a80f8`…`cf33998`). Increment 2 = **complete the `jigc validate` envelope to three targets** — store-wide `jigc validate` reports doc↔code (M18) **plus** (a) workflow-definition referential drift and (b) committed-doc content drift, read-only, never gating, exercised through the real binary over a store carrying a seeded dangling workflow-ref + an out-of-band file edit. Four tasks, **risk-first + isolation-first**: the two net-new engine logic pieces each in isolation on fixtures (the B1 membership-only workflow↔refs path first, then the detect-without-absorb file-state twin), then the `validate_store` reshape that hosts all three families + wires the CLI enumeration under the uniform exit rule, then the end-to-end real-binary acceptance (the *Deliverable* + *Proves*). Cross-references [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M20 Increment 2; design home [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Completing the envelope. *Why:* the two net-new pieces are independent and each carries a distinct trap the design-review pinned (B1's fabricated `task.*` drift; the twin's UNKNOWN/route/rename edges the mutating path resolves *by writing*), so each is retired in isolation before `validate_store` composes them; the headline (no false `task-ref` drift over the real dev pack; mutation-free file-state; exit 0 on content findings) is the *proven* path, exercised through the real binary (the M10 invocation-path-masking lesson — a fixture-only check could mask a store path that mis-resolves over the live pack).

**Grounded facts verified against the real code/tree before writing (reuse-is-a-claim discipline):**
- **The cascade-resolved workflow enumeration already exists, proven, in `describe`.** `describe.rs::load_workflow_defs` (line 71) walks **`pack.list(PackResourceKind::Workflows)`** (which **`.sort()`s its ids** — `pack.rs:92` — so "address-sorted" is the existing listing's property, not net-new) and reads each id layer-aware via **`CascadeDefs::read_workflow(pack, id)`** (`start.rs:2154`), so a project `workflows/` shadow wins at file granularity. This is the **exact** unfiltered, cascade-resolved enumeration the store target needs (every workflow — router/`sub-task` included — not the `creates-task && selectable` catalog). The net-new is the **per-def driver** that runs the task-independent checks over each; the enumeration idiom is reused. Verified by reading `describe.rs` + `start.rs` + `pack.rs`.
- **`workflow_refs` runs the *full* check set including the task-data checks; no task-independent subset exists.** `compose::workflow_refs_with_deltas` (`compose.rs:2053`) runs `body-include-only` (via `load_workflow_def`), `include-resolves`/`include-cycle-absent` (via `expand_includes`), `fan-out-join-paired`, the three `*-marker-not-shadowed` shadow checks, **and** `emit_step_body` per step — and `emit_step_body`→`emit_line` (`compose.rs:504`) is where `command-ref-resolves` does `catalog.get(id)` **then `render_command(cmd, ctx)`**, the latter pulling `task.*` args (`placeholder-resolves` / `at-marker-on-non-scalar`). So the store target needs a **net-new task-independent driver** that runs only the structural subset + a **membership-only** command-ref path (`catalog.get(id)` with **no** `render_command`); it is not a parameter flip on the existing fn. Verified by reading `compose.rs`.
- **The B1 fabricated-drift premise is real over the live dev pack.** `crates/cli/pack/config/commands.yaml` carries **15** `task.*` arg references (`{ from: "task.id" }`, `task.commit#summary`, …) — nearly every command-ref. A task-less full `render_command` would therefore emit `placeholder-resolves`/`task-ref-in-no-task-workflow` for essentially every command-ref: fabricated drift, exactly the B1 trap. The membership-only path is genuinely required, not defensive. Verified by `grep` over `commands.yaml`.
- **The mutating committed-store sweep is barred; its enumeration walk is the twin's template.** `file_state::reconcile_committed_store` (`file_state.rs:251`) walks each persisted schema's `<repo_root>/<location>/*.md` (sorted slugs, line 286), derives the `<location>/<slug>.md` record key + `<type>:<slug>` identity, and routes through `reconcile_committed` — which **mutates** `record` (baseline-adopt/absorb) and `index` (absorb). The read-only twin must **not** call it (it would silently re-baseline the drift it reports); it mirrors only the **walk + key/identity derivation** (path-sorted, `persisted_committed_path`/`identity_of` shape) and compares each on-disk `hash_bytes` (`file_state.rs:41`) to `FileStateRecord::get(path)` (`file_state.rs:76`), emitting findings, **opening no record write**. Verified by reading `file_state.rs`.
- **The three twin edges the mutating path resolves *by writing*, which the read-only twin cannot.** `reconcile_committed` (`file_state.rs:178`): **UNKNOWN** (no recorded hash) *records a baseline* + emits advisory `baseline-adopt`; **DRIFTED** emits `drift_finding` (`file_state.rs:553`) carrying a **`reconcile <path>` route**; **recorded-but-missing** routes to `detect_rename`. The twin must instead: report UNKNOWN as a distinct *un-baselined / not-yet-tracked* informational outcome that does **not** flip the exit code (never silent-clean, never a baseline write); reuse the **`file-state.hash-matches` check id** but emit a **store-scope route variant** (report-only "review / re-author through the owning workflow"), never `reconcile`; and cover **content drift on present docs only** — recorded-but-missing (rename/deletion) stays a task-scope concern, out of the twin. Verified by reading `file_state.rs`.
- **`validate_store` is doc↔code-single-probe-shaped today; the uniform exit rule already only flips on `pack-probe-integrity`.** `validate.rs::validate_store` (line 282) enumerates the committed code-anchor surface, materializes one snapshot, invokes the `doc-code` subprocess, ingests its findings — one family. The CLI handler `cli.rs::run_validate_store` (line 453) already exits non-zero **iff** a `pack-probe-integrity.*` finding is present, else exits 0 (content findings included). ## 2026-06-14 — M20 completion: built + audited clean, 4 LOW findings fixed

Both increments built and **independently validated clean (0 fix rounds)**; the milestone-completion audit (code-review + real-`cargo install` e2e through a 6.4MB installed binary) passed — probe extracts at setup + genuinely fires, one operational error on absence at both store and task scope, three families fold under the uniform exit rule, the file-state twin is byte-for-byte mutation-free, no false drift over the dev pack, order-invariant. Audit raised **4 LOW findings, all fixed (none deferred)** per the completion-triage rule:

- **Probe-extract write policy → heal/upgrade** (commit `2ee6af0`, human-gated at completion). Shipped as pure write-if-absent, which never refreshes the probe after a `jigc` upgrade and never heals a corrupt sibling; changed to **overwrite iff the existing sibling's bytes differ from the embedded probe**. The byte-difference the inc-1 audit flagged (build-tree sibling vs embedded copy) is benign — two non-reproducible *debug* builds of the same probe source (distinct BuildIDs), no debug/release mismatch. Corrected the self-contradictory `module-layout.md` pin label.
- **Store-sweep schemas → cascade-aware** (commit `b978faf`). The sweep resolved doctype schemas pack-only (`load_schema_map`), so a project schema `location:` shadow was invisible — a cascade-invariant violation; swapped to `CascadeDefs::all_schemas` (the reader workflow↔refs already used), removed the now-orphan `load_schema_map`, added a project-shadow store-sweep test.
- **Two doc/test-precision fixes** (folded into `2ee6af0`; size-guard `b91a7de`): a stale QUICKSTART "marker-fenced bootstrap line" → bare `@import`; the binary-size guard now stats the copied install, not the harness artifact.

## 2026-06-14 — Direction: pivot to production-readiness for real-project live testing

After M20, the next aim is **two human-driven manual live tests of jigc on real projects** (separate session, nothing automated): **Flow A** — a new project from scratch (vision → milestones → MVP, docs created on the fly); **Flow B** — an existing project (track its docs into jigc, then clean up). Flow A goes first. Two readiness audits (exercised the real binary, not inferred) found jigc is **not yet a clean go** for either:
- **Flow A:** vision (`project-setup`→`prd`) ✓ and the MVP loop (`plan`→`spec`, `single-task`→`adr`+code) ✓, but **milestones are a hard wall** — the `roadmap` doctype + `planning` workflow live only in the **un-embedded** `packs/methodology/` (binary embeds only `crates/cli/pack` via `include_dir!`), and `jigc setup` never wires a second pack, so a clean-machine project gets **no milestone authoring**. Plus two cold-start bugs: `project-setup` crashes on a zero-commit repo; composed workflows tell the agent to author via `--from-file -` but `set-slot` has no stdin path.
- **Flow B:** `jigc ingest` triage (detect-and-route) + register-only `adopt` of already-conformant docs ✓, but "track *every* doc" hits the **deferred auto-migration core** (foreign-shaped docs are only *flagged*, not adopted — no `jigc adopt --as`; only `adr/prd/spec/arch-doc` map to anything), there's **no cleanup/teardown**, and `finalize` silently `baseline-adopt`s unvetted foreign docs in location dirs (a real trust hazard).

**Decided** (two product calls, via the readiness review): **(1)** milestone planning reaches a real project by **embedding the methodology pack into the binary + auto-wiring it at `jigc setup`** (compose dev + methodology by default, on the built M14 multi-pack rails) — *not* by forking a lighter roadmap into the dev pack; **(2)** scope a **focused production-readiness milestone (M21) first**, before driving the live tests. M21 planning was **deferred to a fresh session** (handover at [completions/artifacts/M20/HANDOVER-next-session.md](completions/artifacts/M20/HANDOVER-next-session.md)); the design forks (KEEP-SUBSUME, embedded-pack composition wiring, how much of Flow B to include) are settled there, not here. Multi-assistant adapter profiles remain deferred ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)).

M20 commits `290c8f9…b91a7de` (14 total, incl. the two planning commits). Tree clean; gate green throughout. **Multi-assistant adapter profiles remain split out** to a future milestone ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)). Roadmap M20 marked ✅ shipped with the Outcome note.

## 2026-06-14 — M21 planning (Scope/Settle): production-readiness — embed methodology + Flow-A cold-start + full Flow-B (minus auto-migration)

**Baseline re-verified, not trusted** (4 `capability-auditor`s + 4 `gap-detector`s, all exercising the real binary at HEAD `71c3df6`). Two roadmap/memory claims **refuted**: the methodology pack is *not* embedded (only the dev pack is), and the `set-slot --from-file -` stdin "bug" is **stale — it already works** (`doc.rs:637`), so it's dropped from M21. The gap probe surfaced **two blocking collisions M14 never solved**, both consequences of M21's central act (auto-wiring dev+methodology): the `knobs.yaml`/`default-workflow` whole-file collision and the `commit` doctype collision.

**Settled forks** (the design home is [multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md) → Embedded second pack + setup auto-wiring; [module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md) → Pack distribution; [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Flow 2 hardening):

- **Embed = a second in-binary `EmbeddedPack`** (a second `include_dir!` of the ~45KB methodology tree; pure data, no `target/` bloat — unlike the M20 probe). `EmbeddedPack` becomes field-carrying (selects which `&'static Dir`). **No extraction, no on-disk `packs.yaml` path** — composed in-binary, which sidesteps the M14 CWD-relative-path landmine. Version ties to the binary release (the `EmbeddedPack` invariant).
- **Compose `[dev ▸ methodology]`, dev highest** — the *inverse* of the listed>base convention, chosen because it resolves both collisions favorably **with zero pack-data edits** (spiked against the binary 2026-06-14): dev wins `knobs` → `default-workflow = router` (the on-ramp menu, **F4**); dev wins `commit` → `implements→spec` **preserved**. methodology's `roadmap`/`planning`/… compose by union; methodology's `dev-task` body still resolves pack-locally to its own test-first `implement` (`origin_pack`). methodology-alone (the dogfood ordering) is **unchanged**. *(This replaced an earlier pack-data-edit settlement of F2/F3 — the spike found the cleaner path.)*
- **Opt-in by a setup-written marker** so the pack-set is `[dev]` (byte-identical to today) until `jigc setup` wires it — existing dev-only tests + the M14 single-pack floor stay green. Writing the marker is a neutral `jigc setup` install step.
- **Zero-commit crash** (confirmed, hits *every* `creates-task` workflow via `read_head` → `git rev-parse HEAD`, twin sites `start.rs:2255` + `milestone.rs:692`): fix with an **empty-tree-sentinel** SHA at both sites so the first task diffs against the empty tree.
- **G4 baseline-adopt trust hazard** (confirmed end-to-end): the `finalize`/`validate` store sweep's `UNKNOWN` arm (`file_state.rs:189-193`) records a foreign doc's hash with **no schema check**. Fix: gate it with the in-module `schema_conformance` call (the sibling DRIFTED arm already makes it), routing non-conformant as **advisory** (not blocking — preserves the M20 clean-store guarantee for conformant fresh-checkouts).
- **Full Flow-B in M21** (the human's call — production-readiness over minimalism): G4 + **recursive scan** (G3) + **ingest-existing discoverability** (G6) + **teardown** (G5 — two verbs: **un-manage a doc** = drop it from file-state/`edges.json`, leave the file; **`jigc uninstall`** = full teardown of the jigc install).
- **On-ramp** = bare `jigc start` → **router** for vision + MVP (falls out of dev winning `knobs`). **`planning` is *not* in the router catalog** (it's `selectable:false` by the M16 off-router invariant — no flip), so the **milestone** half of the on-ramp is delivered by **G6 off-catalog discoverability** — orientation route-prose that names *both* the `planning` and `ingest-existing` verbs (design-review B1: the router alone does not surface `planning`, so "milestones out of the box" needed the discoverability surface, not the menu).

**Design-review bakes** (one `design-reviewer` pass, all findings accepted — 2 BLOCKING + 3 SHOULD + 2 CONSIDER): B1 the planning-not-in-router gap above (corrected the claim + folded planning into the G6 discoverability item); B2 **`jigc uninstall` is repo-local only — it must NOT remove the machine-global `doc-code` probe sibling** (shared across every jigc project on the machine); S1 the opt-in marker is concretely `compose-embedded-methodology: true` in `.jigc/config/packs.yaml` (marker + extra listed packs is out-of-M21-scope); S2 the G4-gated non-conformant doc is **routed-but-not-recorded** so the advisory recurs every finalize until resolved (intended; route names the fix); S3 the **honest Flow-B bound** — adoption reaches only already-conformant docs, so for a foreign project the adoptable subset is often near-empty (the live test is designed against scan+route+adopt-conformant-subset+teardown, not "track every doc"); C1 teardown idempotency/non-destructive acceptance one-liners per verb; C2 the 45KB/39-file/184K-block note.

## 2026-06-15 — M23 inc-1 T1 (source seam): spelling pinned `{{source}}`, lives off the `Path` grammar

**BUILD-PIN — the source-seam placeholder is `{{source}}`** (the design's one delegated open, [auto-migration.md](design/auto-migration.md) → Open questions). A lone `{{source}}` line emits the staged foreign bytes **verbatim**; syntactically distinct from a managed-doc deref (`{{@…}}`) — no `@`, no managed head. T4's acceptance assertion uses this literal. *Why this spelling:* the design named the `{{source}}`-class token directly; shortest distinct name carrying "the foreign source file."

**Where it lives — `ComposeContext.source: Option<String>`, resolved as its own lone class in `emit_line`, NOT in the data-value `Path` grammar.** The seam carries raw bytes, never an [`Address`], and the `Path` grammar is closed over managed state — so `{{source}}` is matched as a lone-placeholder class in `compose::emit_line` (before the `@`/bare-path arms) and resolves straight off the new `ComposeContext.source` field, never reaching `Path::resolve`. An **unfed** seam (`source: None`, every non-migration compose path) emits an **empty line** — empty-not-finding, mirroring an unbound role; the omitting-context guard is tested (the gate clears unfed). Registered in the inline-skip list (`emit_inline_data_values`) so an inline `{{source}}` mention is left verbatim, not tried as a data-value path. CLI feeds the bytes (the `migrate` verb, T2); the resolver does no I/O (the determinism boundary). Landed `crates/engine/src/data_value.rs`, `crates/engine/src/compose.rs`.

**Deferred — each with a trigger** ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)): **(1) G1 auto-migration** (rewriting a foreign doc to conformant shape — research-grade, pressures the determinism boundary) **+ (2) G2 doctype coverage** (new doctypes — `changelog` first, then contributing/runbook/…, each earned from a real driver) → a **single dedicated doctype-expansion + auto-migration milestone**, because the two are coupled (a `changelog` doctype can't track an existing `CHANGELOG.md` without auto-migration). README is **never a doctype**. The commit `scope`/`body` "optional" friction stays the existing optional-slot deferral (pack-data/UX workaround in M21, no engine primitive).

## 2026-06-14 — M21 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Plan, grounded in the actual code at base `b0fca82` (HEAD). Increment 1 = **embed the methodology pack + compose it at setup (the Flow-A milestone wall)** — a clean `jigc setup` that has written the marker gives a real project the in-binary **dev + methodology** surface (`jigc doc create roadmap` resolves, the methodology workflows compose, `default-workflow → router`, the composed `commit` keeps `implements→spec`), with **no** on-disk pack tree and **no** `packs.yaml` path; absent the marker the pack-set is `[dev]`, byte-identical to today. Five tasks, **risk-first + linear:** the field-carrying `EmbeddedPack` + second `include_dir!` first (the highest-uncertainty structural surgery), then the marker-gated factory composition, then the neutral `jigc setup` marker-write, then the end-to-end real-binary acceptance (the *Deliverable* + *Proves*, which composes the prior three), then the worked-example doc. Cross-references [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M21 Increment 1; design homes [multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md) → Embedded second pack + setup auto-wiring, [module-layout.md](implementation/module-layout.md) → Pack distribution. *Why:* the embed (a new `&'static Dir` carrying field) and the factory's compose-on-marker are *separate* sites (the struct change is inert until a path selects the second Dir; the marker read is inert until the factory acts on it), so each is its own task; the compose-both surface is the *proven* path (the M3 "mirrors X"/M10 invocation-path-masking lessons — a unit-only check could mask a composition that mis-resolves over the real binary), so the headline is exercised through a real rebuilt `jigc` with the marker present **and** absent.

**Grounded facts verified against the real code/tree before writing (reuse-is-a-claim discipline):**

Parameterizing over a selected `&'static Dir` is therefore a real struct change rippling `new`/`Default`/`list`/`read` (4 sites), **not** a field add — `EmbeddedPack::new()` has 12 call sites across `pack.rs` tests + `make_base_pack`. The marker is a **net-new sibling parse** (`read_compose_marker`) over the same `packs.yaml` the listed-pack discovery already reads (a separate `MarkerFile { compose_embedded_methodology: bool }`, `#[serde(rename = "compose-embedded-methodology", default)]`), keyed off the same CWD-walk (`discover_compose_marker`) — no new discovery walk. **M21 inc-1 / T2b — store-sweep command-ref pack-locality seam (2026-06-14):** the store sweep now resolves each workflow's command-refs/includes against **its own origin pack**, mirroring `start.rs`'s `origin_pack` → `load_catalog(origin)` idiom (the compose/start path already complied; the sweep predated two-pack composition). Seam shape: (1) `validate_store_families`'s `workflows: &[Vec<u8>]` + single `catalog` collapsed into `workflows: &[engine::validate::StoreWorkflow]`, each bundle carrying `{ id, bytes, catalog }` where `catalog` is the workflow's **origin-pack** catalog (built CLI-side by `enumerate_store_workflows`, which replaces `enumerate_workflow_bytes`); (2) per-workflow step resolution threads through a new **defaulted** `StepSource::scope_to_workflow(&self, _workflow_id)` trait method (no-op default — every single-pack / engine-test source stays inert), overridden by the CLI's `CascadeStepSource` (the same `origin.set(origin_pack(...))` it already did for `jigc start`, lifted from an inherent method to the trait impl). The engine loop scopes the source to each workflow's id, then runs `workflow_refs_store` against that workflow's own catalog. For a single pack each origin *is* the one pack, so the dev-only sweep is byte-identical (the existing `validate_envelope.rs` dev-only tests pass unchanged). Schemas/field-types already resolved per-origin via `all_schemas`'s `origin_pack` lookup — no change owed there. Not a new check id, severity, or exit rule; settled-design compliance per [multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md) → Pack-local body-reference resolution.

## 2026-06-14 — M21 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Plan, grounded in the actual code at base `bcd6d1c` (HEAD, increment 1 landed). Increment 2 = **Flow-A cold-start: zero-commit survival + off-catalog discoverability** — the literal first commands of a new project run on a **fresh `git init` (zero commits)**, and a bare `jigc start` orientation **names the off-catalog `planning` + `ingest-existing` verbs** so milestones (and the existing-project on-ramp) are discoverable without prior knowledge. Two tasks, **linear:** the zero-commit sentinel first (the crash that blocks every Flow-A first command — the harder, broader change touching mint **and** finalize), then the orientation route-prose (additive, read-only). Cross-references [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M21 Increment 2; design home [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Flow 2 hardening. *Why:* the two grouped-scope bullets are independent surfaces (the git-HEAD sentinel on the mint/finalize git path vs. orientation route-prose on the read-only `jigc start` path), so each is its own single-concern task; the sentinel lands first because it is the Flow-A *wall* (no first command runs without it) and the discoverability prose is inert next-step text that rides on top.

**Grounded facts verified against the real code / real `git` before writing (reuse-is-a-claim discipline):**
- **The zero-commit crash has THREE git-HEAD read sites, not two — the roadmap bullet names two (mint), the third is finalize.** `read_head` (`start.rs:2272`, mint) and its milestone twin `read_head` (`milestone.rs:691`, milestone mint) both shell `git rev-parse HEAD` and bail on a non-zero exit — the two the bullet names. **But finalize re-reads HEAD via a *third* function**, `task::git_head` (`task.rs:1102`, `git rev-parse HEAD`), used by **both** single-task finalize (`task.rs:492`) and milestone finalize (`milestone.rs:491`); that head feeds the pin-mismatch guard (`start.rs:1027,1097` compare `pinned.sha != head.sha` on resume) and `git_changed_paths` (`task.rs:1012`, `git diff --no-renames --name-only <base> <head>`). So the *Proves* clause "the first finalize diffs against the empty tree and commits cleanly" is **unreachable** if only the two mint sites are fixed — finalize would re-crash on `git rev-parse HEAD`, and the pin guard would compare a real-SHA head against a sentinel-SHA pin. **All three functions must sentinel-ize the unborn HEAD** for the bullet's *Proves* to hold. Verified by reading `start.rs`/`milestone.rs`/`task.rs` + tracing the finalize call chain.
- **The canonical empty-tree SHA works as a real git diff base in a zero-commit repo — confirmed against the real `git`.** `git hash-object -t tree /dev/null` = `4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904` (git's well-known empty-tree object, present in every repo). In a fresh `git init` with a working-tree file: `git diff 4b825dc…` emits the correct add-everything diff (exit 0), `git diff --no-renames --name-only 4b825dc… 4b825dc…` is empty (exit 0, the no-op pin-equals-head case), and `git rev-parse --short 4b825dc…` returns `4b825dc` (so a sentinel `BasePin::new(<empty-tree-sha>, "4b825dc")` is well-formed). So a sentinel pin diffs against the empty tree and the first finalize commits the whole working tree cleanly — **no empty-commit-guard false-abort** (there *is* a diff vs. the empty tree). Verified by running the real `git` in a throwaway zero-commit repo.
- **The unborn-HEAD condition is cleanly detectable, distinct from "git missing / real error".** `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` exits **1 with no stderr** when HEAD is unborn in a valid repo, vs. exit **0 + the SHA** when a commit exists (contrast bare `git rev-parse HEAD`, which exits 128 with a `fatal:` line). So the sentinel branch keys on "repo is valid AND HEAD unborn" (the `--verify -q` exit-1 probe, or equivalently catching the specific unborn-HEAD failure), and a genuinely broken/absent git still bails — the fix narrows to exactly the zero-commit case and does **not** swallow real git failures. Verified by running `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` in the zero-commit repo.
- **`ingest-existing` ships in the dev pack (always present); `planning` ships only in methodology (present under the M21 marker).** `crates/cli/pack/workflows/ingest-existing.yaml` (`creates-task: false`) is in the dev pack — always in the composed set. `packs/methodology/workflows/planning.yaml` (`creates-task: true, selectable: false`) is methodology-only — present only when the inc-1 marker composes `[dev ▸ methodology]`, absent in a dev-only (no-marker) orientation. ## 2026-06-14 — M21 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Plan, grounded in the actual code at base `2a79135` (HEAD, increments 1+2 landed; tree clean). Increment 3 = **Flow-B safety + reach: the G4 baseline-adopt gate + recursive scan** — `finalize`/`validate`'s committed-store sweep no longer silently baseline-adopts an unvetted foreign doc squatting in a `location:` dir (it conformance-gates first and routes the non-conformant case as a recurring **advisory**), and `jigc ingest` discovers docs in **nested** directories so a real existing project's doc landscape is seen. Two tasks, **linear, safety-first:** the G4 conformance gate first (the trust hazard — the one correctness bug, biting `finalize` directly), then the recursive scan (read-only reach extension on the ingest path). Cross-references [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M21 Increment 3; design home [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Flow 2 hardening. *Why:* the two grouped-scope bullets are independent surfaces (the `reconcile_committed` UNKNOWN-arm gate on the mutating finalize/validate store sweep vs. `discover_candidates`' read-only ingest walk), so each is its own single-concern task; G4 lands first because it closes the trust hazard the deliverable names, and the recursive scan is an additive reach extension that rides independently.

**Grounded facts verified against the real code/tree before writing (reuse-is-a-claim discipline):**

The UNKNOWN arm (`:189-193`) today does `record.record(path, current); vec![baseline_adopt_finding(path)]` with **no** conformance check. So the G4 fix lifts the existing parse→conformance call into the UNKNOWN arm **before** recording — **no signature change, no new inputs**, the exact call its sibling already makes. Verified by reading `file_state.rs:178-227`.
- **The sole production caller of `reconcile_committed` is the store sweep on the finalize/validate path — the working-area `file_state()` probe is a DIFFERENT function and is OUT of scope.** `grep` shows `reconcile_committed(` is called once in production: `reconcile_committed_store` (`file_state.rs:297`), reached from `engine::validate::validate_store` (`validate.rs:207`) — `finalize`'s preflight + `jigc validate`. The inc-4 working-area probe `file_state()` (`file_state.rs:133`, also has an UNKNOWN→baseline-adopt arm) has **no** schema in scope and is **not** named by the G4 scope bullet — it is left untouched. The non-conformant UNKNOWN case therefore carries the existing **`reconciliation.conformance-block`** code (the code the sibling DRIFTED arm already emits for a conformance failure — semantically exact: "this file fails conformance") but at **`Severity::Advisory`**, not `Blocking` — honoring both "advisory, never blocking" (project-setup.md → Flow 2 hardening, G4) and "no new check ids". The code is **not** knob-remapped (no `reconciliation.*` key in `crates/cli/pack/config/knobs.yaml`; reconcile findings set severity directly via `Finding::graded`), so an Advisory-graded finding stays advisory and never flips the exit code. Verified by reading `ingest.rs:49-101` + the roadmap targets.

[roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M21 Increment 3 (G4 bullet) + the M21 header "no new check ids" invariant. *Note:* covers grouped-scope bullet 1 (the G4 conformance gate). ## 2026-06-14 — M21 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Plan, grounded in the actual code at base `8a99737` (HEAD, increments 1+2+3 landed; tree clean). Increment 4 = **Flow-B teardown: un-manage a doc + repo-local `jigc uninstall`** — two cleanup verbs that reverse jigc's footprint, both idempotent and non-destructive to the user's file bytes. Two tasks, **linear, smaller-blast-radius-first:** the doc-scoped un-manage (engine inverse mutation + a store-scope command, touching only jigc's own index/state) first, then the repo-wide `jigc uninstall` (the larger teardown that removes `.jigc/` + unwires the setup-written host-file edits). Cross-references [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M21 Increment 4; design home [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Flow 2 hardening → Teardown / cleanup (G5); the design-review B2 bake (uninstall is repo-local — it must NOT remove the machine-global `doc-code` probe sibling). *Why:* the two grouped-scope bullets are independent surfaces (un-manage mutates `FileStateRecord` + `edges.json` for **one** doc, leaving the file; `jigc uninstall` removes `.jigc/` + unwires `CLAUDE.md`/`settings.json` for the **whole** repo-local install), so each is its own single-concern task + command + acceptance; un-manage lands first as the narrower, lower-risk change (it never deletes a host file, only edits jigc's own state) and is referenced nowhere by uninstall (they are orthogonal — uninstall removes the *whole* `.jigc/` tree wholesale, not doc-by-doc).

**Grounded facts verified against the real code/tree before writing (reuse-is-a-claim discipline):**
- **Un-manage is the *exact* inverse of `adopt`'s two recorded mutations — both surfaces are present and neither has a drop primitive yet.** `engine::ingest::adopt` (`crates/engine/src/ingest.rs:204-230`) records a doc by (1) `index.absorb_doc(schema, &from, &doc)` and (2) `record.record(rel_path, hash_bytes(bytes))`, where `from = "<schema.ty>:<slug>"` and `slug` is `rel_path`'s `.md`-stripped filename stem. The inverse must (1) drop every edge whose `from == "<type>:<slug>"` from the `EdgeIndex`, and (2) remove `rel_path` from `FileStateRecord.hashes`. **Neither primitive exists:** `EdgeIndex` (`index.rs:85-124`) has `absorb_doc` (which `retain(|e| e.from != from)` *then re-adds* the doc's fresh edges) but **no** plain drop-by-`from`; `FileStateRecord` (`file_state.rs:59-109`) has `record`/`get` but **no** `forget`/remove. So two small net-new inverse methods are owed (`EdgeIndex::drop_doc(&mut self, from: &str)` = the `retain` half of `absorb_doc` with no re-add; `FileStateRecord::forget(&mut self, path: &str) -> bool` = `self.hashes.remove(path).is_some()`), each landing beside its existing sibling. Verified by reading `ingest.rs:204-230` + `index.rs:85-124` + `file_state.rs:59-109`.
- **The file-state key IS the rel_path `adopt` records (`decisions/<slug>.md`); the edge `from` is derivable from that path + the schema-location map exactly as `adopt` derives it.** `adopt` keys file-state on `rel_path` and derives `from` from `rel_path`'s stem + `schema.ty`; so un-manage takes the **same rel_path address** (the managed doc's repo-relative path — the key already in `file-state.json`) and re-derives `<type>:<slug>` by finding which schema's `location:` the path sits under (the `classify` location-match idiom, `ingest.rs:127-160`) + the stem. **No new addressing scheme is invented** — un-manage's address is the file-state key, symmetric with `adopt`. A path under no schema `location:` (or a type with no edges) simply drops the file-state entry and finds zero edges to drop — still a clean removal. Verified by reading `adopt` + `classify` + the `FileStateRecord` key shape.
- **Idempotency falls out of the remove-returns-bool shape — no separate "already unmanaged" check.** Because `FileStateRecord::forget` returns whether anything was removed and `EdgeIndex::drop_doc` is a `retain` (a no-op when nothing matches), a re-run on an already-unmanaged doc removes nothing, persists a byte-identical record+index (or skips the write), and reports "already unmanaged" — a **clean no-op, not an error** (the roadmap's idempotency clause). The doc's on-disk bytes are **never read or written** by un-manage (it touches only `.jigc/state/file-state.json` + `.jigc/index/edges.json`), so "leaves the file bytes on disk" is structural — un-manage has no file-write path at all. Verified by the `BTreeMap::remove`/`Vec::retain` semantics + tracing that un-manage never opens the managed file.
- **Both teardown verbs are store-scope, NOT task-working-area scope — they belong as top-level commands, siblings of `Ingest`/`Setup`/`Validate`, sharing the `require_project_layer` locate preamble.** Every `DocCommand` verb (`doc.rs:38-90`) takes `--task` and writes a task working area; un-manage + uninstall operate on the **committed store** (`.jigc/` itself + the host files), so they are top-level `Command` variants (`cli.rs:52`), not `jigc doc` sub-verbs. The locate preamble is the proven `require_project_layer(cwd)` → `repo_root` idiom (`cli.rs:555-563`, shared by `ingest`/`upgrade`/`validate`), with `jigc_root = repo_root.join(".jigc")` (the `FileStateRecord::load`/`EdgeIndex` home, `cli.rs:519`). Verified by reading `doc.rs` + `cli.rs:52-173,490-563`.
- **`jigc setup`'s repo-local writes are an enumerated, locatable set — uninstall reverses exactly them, and the `doc-code` probe is the ONE machine-global write it must skip.** `setup::install` (`crates/cli/src/setup.rs:363-509`) writes, **repo-locally:** (1) `.jigc/AGENT.md` (the managed bootstrap) + the `## Project interface`/`@.jigc/AGENT.md` import line in `<repo>/CLAUDE.md` (`adapter::write_bootstrap_file` + `adapter::inject_reference`, `adapter.rs:405,423`); (2) the `.jigc/config/` project layer (`init_project_layer`); (3) the `compose-embedded-methodology` marker in `.jigc/config/packs.yaml` (`write_compose_marker`); (4) the `jigc *` allowlist permit in `.claude/settings.json`'s `permissions.allow` array (`adapter::inject_allowlist`, `adapter.rs:470`) + (5) the SessionStart hook + (6) the repo's `pre-commit` hook; and — **step 6 (`extract_doc_code_probe`, `setup.rs:493`) — the ONE machine-global write:** `<jigc-bin-dir>/doc-code` (`current_exe().parent()/doc-code`, shared across every jigc repo). The roadmap/design name uninstall's removal set as **`.jigc/` + the `CLAUDE.md` import line + the `.claude/settings.json` allowlist entry + the marker** (the marker lives *inside* `.jigc/`, so removing `.jigc/` subsumes it; items 1's bootstrap-file, 2 config-layer, 3 marker all sit under `.jigc/`). The `BOOTSTRAP_IMPORT_LINE = "@.jigc/AGENT.md"` constant + the `## Project interface` heading (`adapter.rs:425,652`) is the exact CLAUDE.md text to unwire; the allowlist permit is the structure-aware-JSON `"jigc *"` entry in `permissions.allow` (the inverse of `inject_allowlist`, removing the permit + preserving unrelated keys). Verified by reading `setup.rs:363-509` + `adapter.rs:405-511,634-652`.
- **`jigc uninstall` is its own top-level verb, distinct from `cargo uninstall jigc` + manual probe removal (the machine-global path).** No `uninstall`/`unmanage` verb or code exists today (`grep -rn` over `crates/` outside tests/pack-prose returns nothing). The design (project-setup.md:111, the B2 bake) is explicit: uninstall is **repo-local only**; machine-global removal (the `doc-code` probe sibling + the installed binary) is `cargo uninstall jigc` + manual probe deletion, **never** the per-project verb — so uninstall leaving the probe intact is a **load-bearing acceptance** (a sibling repo's `jigc validate` still resolves the probe after `uninstall`). Verified by `grep -rn uninstall\|unmanage crates/` + reading project-setup.md:111.
- **The acceptance harnesses already exist and are the homes to extend.** `crates/cli/tests/setup.rs` is the real-binary `jigc setup` home (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc` over a `git init` temp repo); `ingest.rs`/`ingest_flow12.rs` drive ingest/adopt over the binary (the adopt→un-manage round-trip home); `store_sweep_acceptance.rs` drives the file-state record through `validate`. A new `unmanage.rs` + `uninstall.rs` acceptance (or extensions of `setup.rs`/`ingest_flow12.rs`) follow the established `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc` + temp-repo idiom. Verified by `ls crates/cli/tests/`.

**Scope note — no worked-example flow task is owed this increment.** Unlike Increment 1 (whose *Grouped scope* carried an explicit "add a worked-example flow" bullet), Increment 4's *Grouped scope* has **exactly two bullets** (un-manage, `jigc uninstall`), neither a doc-flow bullet; the design home (project-setup.md → Flow 2 hardening → Teardown/cleanup) names no acceptance worked-example flow for teardown. So this cut is two code+test tasks with **no** `design/` doc task — every *Grouped scope* bullet maps to exactly one task in **this** increment, nothing punted.

Ordered tasks:
- **T1 — Un-manage a doc: the inverse of `adopt`'s register-only mutation, behind a store-scope `jigc unmanage <path>` verb.** Add the two net-new engine inverse primitives — `EdgeIndex::drop_doc(&mut self, from: &str)` (`crates/engine/src/index.rs`, the `retain(|e| e.from != from)` half of `absorb_doc` with **no** re-add) and `FileStateRecord::forget(&mut self, path: &str) -> bool` (`crates/engine/src/file_state.rs`, `self.hashes.remove(path).is_some()`) — then an engine `ingest::unmanage(record, index, schemas, rel_path) -> bool` (the inverse of `adopt`: derive `<type>:<slug>` from `rel_path`'s stem + the matching schema `location:` via the `classify` idiom, `index.drop_doc(&from)`, return `record.forget(rel_path)`; **never reads or writes the managed file**). Wire a top-level `Command::Unmanage { path }` (`crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, a sibling of `Ingest`/`Validate`) whose handler uses the `require_project_layer` → `repo_root`/`jigc_root` preamble, loads the record + edge index, runs `ingest::unmanage`, and **persists the advanced record + index only when something was removed** (the `adopt` persist idiom); a re-run on an already-unmanaged doc removes nothing, is a byte-identical no-op, and exits 0 reporting "already unmanaged" (idempotent, never an error). *Done (red proves the round-trip drop + bytes-unchanged + idempotency, through the binary):* (a) an **engine** unit test asserts: after `adopt`-ing a conformant `adr` (records the `supersedes` edge + the file-state hash), `unmanage` drops **both** — `record.get(rel_path) == None` **and** the edge index carries no edge whose `from == "adr:<slug>"` (`drop_doc` removed it) — and a second `unmanage` returns `false` with the record+index byte-identical (idempotent no-op); (b) a **real-binary** acceptance (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc` over a `git init` temp repo, the `ingest_flow12.rs`/`setup.rs` idiom): `jigc setup` → seed a conformant `decisions/<slug>.md` → `jigc ingest` (adopts it: it enters `file-state.json` + `edges.json`) → record the doc file's on-disk bytes → `jigc unmanage decisions/<slug>.md` exits 0, the path is **gone** from `.jigc/state/file-state.json` and its edges **gone** from `.jigc/index/edges.json`, **and the doc file's on-disk bytes are byte-identical** to before (un-manage never touched the file) → a **second** `jigc unmanage decisions/<slug>.md` exits 0 as a clean no-op (the "re-run on an already-unmanaged doc" idempotency clause). `cargo build` + `cargo test` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` clean. *Files:* `crates/engine/src/index.rs`, `crates/engine/src/file_state.rs`, `crates/engine/src/ingest.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/` (a new `unmanage.rs` acceptance, or an extension of `ingest_flow12.rs`). *Design:* [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Flow 2 hardening → Teardown / cleanup (G5), bullet (a) un-manage a doc; [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M21 Increment 4 (un-manage bullet). *Note:* covers grouped-scope bullet 1 (un-manage a doc). The address is the file-state rel_path key (symmetric with `adopt`, no new addressing scheme); "leaves the file bytes on disk" is structural (un-manage has no file-write path) and is asserted explicitly via a before/after byte-compare of the managed doc; idempotency is asserted via the second no-op run. The `<type>:<slug>` derivation reuses the `classify` location-match — a path under no schema `location:` drops only the file-state entry (zero edges), still a clean removal.
- **T2 — `jigc uninstall`: repo-local teardown that removes `.jigc/` + unwires the host-file edits, leaving the machine-global `doc-code` probe intact.** Wire a top-level `Command::Uninstall` (`crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, sibling of `Setup`) whose handler, over the `require_project_layer` → `repo_root` preamble, reverses **exactly** the enumerated repo-local setup-created set: (1) `std::fs::remove_dir_all(<repo>/.jigc)` (subsumes the bootstrap `AGENT.md`, the `.jigc/config/` layer, the `compose-embedded-methodology` marker, the index + state); (2) unwire the `CLAUDE.md` import line — remove the `## Project interface` section + the bare `@.jigc/AGENT.md` line (`BOOTSTRAP_IMPORT_LINE`) the `adapter::inject_reference` wrote, preserving all surrounding host content (the inverse of `inject_reference`, in `crates/cli/src/setup.rs`/`adapter.rs`); (3) remove the `jigc *` permit from `.claude/settings.json`'s `permissions.allow` array via the structure-aware-JSON inverse of `inject_allowlist` (drop the permit string, preserve unrelated keys/permits; leave the file valid JSON). **Explicitly NOT removed (design-review B2):** the machine-global `<jigc-bin-dir>/doc-code` probe sibling (shared across repos — removing it would break doc↔code validation for *other* jigc projects); machine-global removal stays `cargo uninstall jigc` + manual probe deletion. **Idempotent:** a second `jigc uninstall` (with `.jigc/` already gone, the import line already absent, the permit already removed) is a clean no-op exiting 0, each removal guarded so an already-absent target is success, never an error. *Done (red proves the repo-local footprint is removed, the probe survives, and a second run is a clean no-op — through the binary):* a **real-binary** acceptance (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc` over a `git init` temp repo, the `setup.rs` idiom): `jigc setup` (writes the full set: `.jigc/`, the `CLAUDE.md` import line, the `.claude/settings.json` `jigc *` permit, and the machine-global `doc-code` probe beside the binary) → `jigc uninstall` exits 0 and (i) `<repo>/.jigc/` **does not exist**, (ii) `<repo>/CLAUDE.md` no longer contains `@.jigc/AGENT.md` (and any pre-existing non-jigc CLAUDE.md content is preserved byte-for-byte), (iii) `.claude/settings.json`'s `permissions.allow` no longer contains `"jigc *"` (and any unrelated permit/key is preserved, the file is still valid JSON), **and (iv) the machine-global `<bin-dir>/doc-code` probe still exists** (the B2 guarantee — a sibling repo set up against the same binary still resolves the probe, asserted by `require_doc_code_probe`-equivalent file-existence at the probe path); then (v) a **second** `jigc uninstall` exits 0 as a clean no-op (every target already absent — idempotent). `cargo build` + `cargo test` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` clean. *Files:* `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/src/setup.rs` (or `crates/cli/src/adapter.rs` for the unwire inverses), `crates/cli/tests/` (a new `uninstall.rs` acceptance). *Design:* [project-setup.md](design/project-setup.md) → Flow 2 hardening → Teardown / cleanup (G5), bullet (b) `jigc uninstall` (repo-local; NOT the probe sibling — design-review B2); [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M21 Increment 4 (`jigc uninstall` bullet). *Note:* covers grouped-scope bullet 2 (`jigc uninstall` repo-local). The probe-survives assertion (iv) is the hardening #5 "exercise a context that OMITS the target" face — uninstall must leave the machine-global probe untouched, so the acceptance asserts its **continued presence** after uninstall (the omitted-target stays inert, never deleted). The SessionStart + pre-commit hooks setup also writes are **not** named by the roadmap/design uninstall set (which enumerates `.jigc/` + CLAUDE.md import + allowlist + marker); leaving them is the design's enumerated bound, not a silent narrowing — if the live test surfaces them as residue, that is a separate, owner-approved addition, not self-authorized here.

### M21 Increment 4 — T1 built (un-manage a doc)

- **`ingest::unmanage` takes the already-derived `from`, not the schema set — the `<type>:<slug>` re-derivation lives in the CLI.** The plan sketched `ingest::unmanage(record, index, schemas, rel_path)`; landed as `ingest::unmanage(record, index, from, rel_path) -> bool` (the pure inverse of `adopt`'s two mutations: `index.drop_doc(from) | record.forget(rel_path)`), with the location-match `<type>:<slug>` derivation in `crate::unmanage::identity_of` (CLI). Keeps the engine fn schema-free + total (a path under no schema location passes a `from` matching no edge — only the file-state entry drops), mirroring how the CLI already owns the cascade/pack feed. `|` (not `||`) so both surfaces always evaluate. Within the locked design, not a scope change.

### M21 Increment 4 — T2 built (`jigc uninstall` — repo-local teardown)

- **The two unwire inverses live in `adapter.rs` (beside their `inject_*` siblings); the orchestration in `setup.rs` (`run_uninstall`/`uninstall`, mirroring `run`/`install`).** `adapter::unwire_reference` (inverse of `inject_reference`) strips jigc's appended `## Project interface`/`@.jigc/AGENT.md` section by matching the exact append form — `inject_reference` writes `existing + "\n" + section`, so stripping `"\n" + section` restores `existing` byte-for-byte; a setup-**created** `CLAUDE.md` (the file *is* the section) is removed entirely; a section-free file is a clean no-op. `adapter::remove_allowlist` (structure-aware-JSON inverse of `inject_allowlist`) `retain`s the `permissions.allow` array minus the profile permits, leaving unrelated keys/permits intact + the file valid JSON; absent file / absent `allow` / permit-already-gone are byte-untouched no-ops. `.jigc/` is removed wholesale via `remove_dir_all` (subsumes the bootstrap `AGENT.md`, the config layer, the compose marker, index+state). The machine-global `<bin-dir>/doc-code` probe is **never touched** (design-review B2 — asserted by the acceptance's probe-survives clause). `uninstall` locates the repo root only (not `require_project_layer`), so a second run over an already-gone `.jigc/` still exits 0. Failures map to blocking `uninstall.*` findings carrying routes (rendered via the shared `setup_block` envelope). Within the locked design, not a scope change.

**Scope coverage:** grouped-scope bullet 1 (un-manage a doc — drop one managed doc from `FileStateRecord` + its `edges.json` entries, the inverse of `adopt`'s register-only mutation, leaving the file bytes on disk; idempotent re-run is a clean no-op) → **T1** (the two engine inverse primitives + `ingest::unmanage` + the `jigc unmanage <path>` verb + the round-trip/bytes-unchanged/idempotency acceptance); bullet 2 (`jigc uninstall` repo-local only — remove `.jigc/`, unwire the `CLAUDE.md` import line + the `.claude/settings.json` allowlist entry + the marker; NOT the machine-global `doc-code` probe sibling; idempotent; removes exactly the enumerated repo-local set) → **T2** (the `jigc uninstall` verb reversing the enumerated repo-local set + the probe-survives + idempotent-no-op acceptance). Both grouped-scope bullets map to a task in **this** increment; nothing is punted to a later one (and no worked-example-flow bullet exists this increment — see the scope note above). The increment's *Proves* (un-manage drops a doc from jigc's index/state with on-disk bytes unchanged + is idempotent; `jigc uninstall` removes the repo-local footprint, leaves the probe sibling intact so a sibling repo's `jigc validate` still works, and a second `uninstall` is a clean no-op) is delivered jointly by T1 (un-manage round-trip + bytes-unchanged + idempotency) and T2 (uninstall + probe-survives + idempotent no-op), each exercised through the **real rebuilt binary** (the binary changes — two new top-level verbs — so `CARGO_BIN_EXE_jigc` rebuilds before each acceptance runs). Two task decisions are made *within* the locked design (neither a scope reduction nor a new fork): un-manage's address is the **file-state rel_path key** (symmetric with `adopt`; no new addressing scheme), and uninstall's removal set is **exactly the design-enumerated repo-local writes** (`.jigc/` + CLAUDE.md import line + allowlist permit; the marker subsumed under `.jigc/`), the machine-global `doc-code` probe **explicitly preserved** per design-review B2.

## 2026-06-14 — M21 completion: built + audited clean, 1 LOW finding fixed

All four increments built; the build harness **halted once** mid-increment-1 (T3, the marker write) on **M14 debt** that only surfaces when `[dev ▸ methodology]` first composes through the committed paths: the `jigc validate` store sweep resolved command-refs against one flat (precedence-winner) catalog rather than **pack-locally per workflow's origin pack** ([multi-pack.md](design/multi-pack.md):79), and T2 had inverted `JIGC_PACK_DIR` precedence. Both are settled-design compliance (no fork, no new check id) — landed as inserted tasks **T2a** (`JIGC_PACK_DIR` supersedes the marker, `8c0bc13`) and **T2b** (store-sweep resolves command-refs via `origin_pack`, mirroring `start.rs`'s `load_catalog(origin)`, `fa9a9e7`) **before** T3. The halt was correct — shipping T3 without T2b would have floored every composed-store `jigc validate` on false `command-ref-resolves` findings. Increment 1 was finished manually + **independently validated clean**, then a `skipThrough:1` re-launch built increments 2–4.

**Milestone-completion audit (code-review + e2e) passed.** All 10 e2e scenarios green through the freshly-built real binary: embed+compose dev-highest behind the `compose-embedded-methodology` marker (`default-workflow → router`, `commit` keeps `implements→spec`), the marker-absent single-pack byte-identity floor, the zero-commit empty-tree sentinel + clean first finalize, G6 off-catalog discoverability (`planning` + `ingest-existing` named in orientation), the G4 baseline-adopt conformance gate on **both** the store-sweep and the finalize-post-commit paths (advisory, routed-not-recorded), recursive ingest scan, and `jigc unmanage` + repo-local `jigc uninstall` (machine-global `doc-code` probe intact). **1 LOW finding, fixed** (not deferred): `inject_reference` was lossy (an original with vs without a trailing newline collapsed to identical injected bytes), so the `CLAUDE.md` setup→uninstall round-trip wasn't byte-identical for a non-newline-terminated original — made `inject` reversible (append a fixed `"\n" + section`), restoring byte-identity for both (`4facedf`). Commits `0567357…4facedf` (20). Roadmap M21 marked ✅ shipped.

**Net:** a fresh `jigc setup` now gives a real project the methodology pack embedded + auto-wired (vision→milestones→MVP out of the box), the Flow-A cold-start blockers are gone, and full Flow-B (scan/route/G4-gate/teardown) lands — **minus** auto-migration (G1) + doctype coverage (G2), deferred paired to a dedicated post-M21 milestone. The human's two manual live tests can now run on a clean install.

## 2026-06-14 — Split the paired doctype-expansion + auto-migration milestone into two (overturns the M21-planning pairing)

The M21-planning deferral paired **G2 (doctype coverage)** + **G1 (auto-migration)** into one post-M21 milestone, on the rationale that a `changelog` doctype can't *track an existing* `CHANGELOG.md` without migration. **Reversed (human call):** that rationale is about **delivering to Flow B (existing projects)**, not about milestone sizing. G2 serves **Flow A (new project authors a managed doc *through* jigc)** with **no** dependence on G1 — a tractable, cleanly-provable win (bounded engine-defect fixes + N doctype schemas + N new-project drivers). G1 is the research-grade core that **relaxes the determinism boundary** (VISION's hard contract) and carries its own forks (boundary-relaxation extent, migration-quality measure). Splitting (a) banks the Flow-A doctype win behind its own completion verdict + a re-pinned binary the human can live-test *before* the research bet, (b) **isolates the determinism-boundary risk** so the doctype value isn't held hostage to the migration outcome, (c) draws the milestone boundary at a seam the build order already has — migration needs the doctypes to exist as targets first. Honest bound carried forward: until G1 lands, a new `changelog` doctype helps a *new* project author one, but an existing `CHANGELOG.md` still routes `needs-reconcile` — the same bounded-capability posture M21 already took. **Ordering:** doctype-expansion milestone first, auto-migration milestone after; numbers minted at each one's planning. `decisions-pending.md` splits the single paired entry into the two milestone-keyed deferrals accordingly.

## 2026-06-14 — Doctype-expansion milestone planning (Scope/Settle): `changelog` doctype + build the four engine lifts it earns

Design of record: [design/changelog.md](design/changelog.md). Scope verified by 3 `capability-auditor`s (the four latent-defect shapes + the proven write/persist/finalize spine) + 4 `gap-detector`s (one **spiked both schema shapes against the real engine** — the route-around byte-stable, multi-level a ~36-site engine change). Settled forks:

- **Build width — BUILD `changelog` only, MAP the rest** (human call at Scope). The candidate set is settled as a forward map in [doctype-map.md](implementation/doctype-map.md): `contributing`/`runbook` map-only (unscheduled drivers); `SECURITY`/`license`/`code-of-conduct`/`api-docs`/`release-notes` argued **out** (boilerplate / generated / bespoke / duplicate); **README never a doctype** (charter-locked). Acceptance = cold-create → warm-append, byte-stable + finalize gate (worked-examples flow 24).
- **Build all four engine capabilities — do NOT route around them** (human call, overturning the planner's minimal-scope recommendation). Rationale: "we'll need them; the point is now" — and a faithful changelog + the existing `adr` give **each** capability a real in-milestone target, so none is speculative: **`Leaf::Repeatable`** (release→change-group nesting) built as general recursion, heading-depth = 2+nesting, capped at H6 (4 levels); **multi-word section-id** parser fix (target: the changelog's `## Unreleased Changes`; also narrows the deferred `prd` requirements blocker); **optional slot/field** `optional:` flag (target: a release's optional `summary` slot); **doc-level `set: on-create` + `default:`** materialization (target: honor `adr`'s long-broken doc-level `date` + `status: proposed` — CLI-side deriver, engine stays clock-free). The four corresponding deferrals **graduate** out of [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md).
- **Changelog schema** — dev-pack, **singleton**, `location: changelog/`, **edge-free** (a changelog→commit edge fails: `commit` is transient + needs the deferred repeatable-edge lift). `## Unreleased Changes` (multi-word, single-level repeatable change-groups) + `## Releases` (two-level: release item → nested `changes` change-groups; item-level `date`, optional `summary`). Entries are **prose in a `notes` slot**, not a third repeatable level (faithful to Keep-a-Changelog; keeps nesting at the one level proven).
- **Driver — standalone + fold-in, both pack-local** (human call). A standalone `record-change` workflow (`creates-task:true, selectable:false`, the proven off-router authoring spine) for cutting a release; **plus** `single-task` gains `allows-create:[{changelog, as: change}]` beside its existing `{adr, as: decision}` — the everyday-task fold-in that keeps the changelog maintained as work lands (the M17 stale-doc lesson), pack-local so **no cross-pack create risk**. The methodology `dev-task` cross-pack fold-in is **deferred** (unexercised M14 surface).
- **Honest bounds recorded** (so completion can't charge them): Flow-A-only (existing `CHANGELOG.md` still routes `needs-reconcile` until G1); 3rd+ nesting level supported-but-unexercised; multi-slot-leaves + nested-repeatable in one block deferred.

New doc `design/changelog.md` wired into the reading order after `project-setup.md` ([CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)).

**Independent design review (1 BLOCKING + 4 SHOULD + 5 CONSIDER) — all baked before decompose.** BLOCKING **B1**: the release item's leading `summary` *slot* would swallow the nested `#### Added` groups (bare-prose item body runs to the next `###`/section boundary) — **resolved by dropping the leading slot**: a release carries only scalar fields + the nested repeatable, and the optional-lift target becomes an optional **`link` field** (renders in the fields block, before nested content — zero boundary problem, more faithful to KaC); "leading prose then nested items" is logged as a deferred capability. **S1**: nested addressing is a **parent-scoped path-locator rewrite** (replacing the global single-level `locate_item_block`), not a vocabulary extension — sized into engine-work #1. **S2**: lift #4 (doc-level on-create) is `adr`-scoped — decomposed as its **own isolated increment** so its front-matter-test churn doesn't tangle the LARGE lift's verdict. **S3**: the change-group duplication (unreleased vs releases.changes) noted deliberate. **C1**: parent-scoped anchor uniqueness made a red obligation. Determinism boundary confirmed **not** relaxed (that's G1).

**Decomposed (roadmap M22) — five increments, risk-first + linear:** (1) `Leaf::Repeatable` LARGE lift [headline risk, schema can't load without it]; (2) multi-word section-id parser fix; (3) optional slot/field flag; (4) doc-level `set: on-create`+`default:` (adr-scoped, isolated); (5) the `changelog` doctype + `record-change` workflow + `single-task` fold-in + flow-24 acceptance [consumes 1–3]. Binary changes → rebuild + re-pin before exercise. Ready for `milestone-build`.

## 2026-06-14 — M22 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut per the [increment workflow](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → Plan, grounded in the actual code at base `5c80b49` (HEAD). Increment 1 = **`Leaf::Repeatable`: the multi-level repetition lift** — the schema model expresses a repeatable nested inside a repeatable, and a two-level instance parses, renders, validates, and is addressable, round-tripping byte-stable; general recursion with a documented H6/4-level cap, the changelog exercising exactly two levels. Five tasks, **risk-first + linear**, each ending in one commit over the shared tree: the **schema variant + recursive loader** first (the schema can't load a nested `repeatable:` without it, and the cap/heading-depth grammar is settled here); then the **depth-aware recursive parse** (a deeper heading is a sub-item boundary, `seen` resets per parent); then the **recursive render closing the byte-stable round-trip cold and warm** (the #1 risk, proven over the two-level fixture in both empty-then-filled and warm-append states); then the **recursive validate** (the nested required-slot block naming the nested address, parent-scoped anchor uniqueness); then the **parent-scoped path locator + nested addressing wired through the binary** (replace the global single-level `locate_item_block`, grow the `Fragment` grammar past 3 hops, thread the setters, prove nested `add-item`/`set-slot`/`set-field` reach the nested item via real `jigc doc` verbs). Cross-references [roadmap](implementation/roadmap.md) → M22 Increment 1; design home [changelog.md](design/changelog.md) → engine work #1 (the six mapped sites + the C1/S1 red obligations). *Why:* each named site (schema / parse / render / validate / addressing) is its own single concern, and they layer — render's round-trip can't be proven until parse maps the nested items; validate runs over the parsed nested items; addressing's locator rewrite consumes the same recursive structure — so the spine is serial and risk-first (the schema-model + parse + render trio retires the headline round-trip risk before the validate/addressing surfaces ride on it).

**Grounded facts verified against the real code/tree before writing (reuse-is-a-claim discipline):**
- **`Leaf` is a two-variant untagged enum today; the consumers that walk `repeatable.block` are the four sites the scope names + two `filter_map`s.** `schema.rs:138` `pub enum Leaf { Slot{id, slot}, Field(Box<Field>) }` `#[serde(untagged)]`. Exhaustive `match leaf` appears at `parse.rs:967` (`ItemTemplate::from`) and `validate.rs:748` (`check_repeatable`); non-exhaustive `filter_map` over `.block` at `target_surface.rs:356` (`collect_repeatable`) and `doc.rs:303` (`on_create_item_fields`). The loader's `load_schema_with_types` (`schema.rs:445`) iterates `repeatable.block` resolving **only** direct `Leaf::Field` — it does **not** recurse, so a nested repeatable's field types would go unresolved. So adding `Leaf::Repeatable(Repeatable)` is a real variant add + a loader recursion, and the two exhaustive matches must each gain a recursive arm; the `filter_map`s compile unchanged but must recurse to reach nested anchors (out of scope for inc-1, but the arms must not silently drop nested blocks). Verified by reading `schema.rs` + `grep "match leaf\|\.block"`.
- **Parse is single-level by construction at three named sites.** `parse_items` (`parse.rs:714`) collects only `HeadingLevel::H3` item heads (`parse.rs:726`), and its `seen` dup-check (`parse.rs:740`) is **flat per section** (not per parent). `next_section_heading` (`parse.rs:524`) bounds a section at `H2` only. `is_reserved_depth` (`parse.rs:1060`) is `H2 | H3` — so a `####` nested-item heading inside an item body is **today** treated as allowed slot-internal structure (not a violation), but once `####` is a *schema-reserved* item depth it must be depth-aware so a `####` at the schema's nested-item depth is a sub-item boundary, not slot prose, while a `####` *deeper* than the schema declares stays a slot-ceiling violation. `ItemTemplate::from` (`parse.rs:963`) flattens one level. Verified by reading `parse.rs:195-345,524,714-995,1060`.
- **Render hardcodes `###` and recurses into `slots`/`fields` only — there is no nested-items carrier.** `render_item` (`write.rs:193`) emits `### <title>  {#id}` (`write.rs:195`, depth fixed) then the bare-prose/`slots`/`fields` body; `ItemContent` (`write.rs:93`) has `slot`/`slots`/`fields` but **no** nested `items` field. `render_section` (`write.rs:160`) maps `items.iter().map(render_item)`. So render needs a schema-depth thread + an `ItemContent.items` (mirror in `ParsedItem`) + recursion. The arch-doc round-trip tests (`schema.rs:1119,1163`) are the proven golden+idempotent harness shape to mirror for the two-level fixture. Verified by reading `write.rs:117-220`.
- **Validate's `check_repeatable` walks one block level and addresses at `#section/item/leaf`.** `validate.rs:739` iterates `parsed.items` × `repeatable.block`, the slot/field arms calling `check_item_slot_present`/`check_item_field` which build `item_leaf_address` = `section/item/leaf` (`validate.rs:840`). The `required-slot-present` finding code is `schema-conformance.required-slot-present` (`validate.rs:786`) — the exact code the *Proves* requires the nested empty-slot block to carry, now naming the **nested** address. Verified by reading `validate.rs:700-842`.
- **Addressing is the heaviest sub-deliverable: the locator is global single-level, the `Fragment` grammar caps at 3 hops, and the setters take flat args.** `write::locate_item_block` (`write.rs:1165`) matches an item by anchor **at `H3` only, globally over the whole source**, bounding at the next `H3 | H2` (`write.rs:1185`) — so it cannot find a `####` nested item, is **ambiguous** across parents (two releases each with `#added`), and mis-bounds the span. It is consumed by `set_item_field` (`write.rs:992`), `set_item_slot` (`write.rs:1059`), and `insert_item_field` (`write.rs:1828`). The `Fragment` grammar (`address.rs:79`) has fixed variants capped at 3 hops — `Fragment::parse` (`address.rs:131`) returns `ParseError::TooManyHops` for a 4th hop — yet changelog.md S1's worked address is `changelog:changelog#releases/1-2-0/changes/added/notes` (5 hops). The CLI `field_target`/`slot_target`/`section_hop` (`doc.rs:673,730,755`) match the fixed `Fragment` variants and hand the engine setters flat `(section_id, item_id, field_key/leaf_id)` args (`doc.rs:190,230,268`). So nested addressing requires: a variable-depth fragment path, a parent-scoped recursive locator (walk each segment within its parent's byte region), the setters threaded by a path, and the doc.rs target resolution extended. Verified by reading `address.rs:60-178`, `write.rs:955-1199,1797-1884`, `doc.rs:160-270,655-760`.
- **The address-grammar hop extension is settled-spec elaboration, NOT a new fork.** changelog.md → engine work #1 (the addressing bullet) and DECISIONS.md → 2026-06-14 doctype-expansion planning (S1) both name the multi-hop nested address (`#section/item/subitem/leaf`) as the *required* resolution target of the "parent-scoped path-locator rewrite," and the roadmap *Proves* mandates "nested `add-item`/`set-slot`/`set-field` reach the nested item." Growing `Fragment` past 3 hops is the mechanical means of resolving that named address — an elaboration within the locked spec, made + logged by the executor (the doc-elaboration pin discipline), not a halt. No fork surfaced.

**Pin (T1 executor, 2026-06-14 — shape within the settled spec, no new fork):** the nested-repeatable leaf is a **struct variant** `Leaf::Repeatable { id, repeatable: Repeatable }` (not a tuple `Leaf::Repeatable(Repeatable)` as the task title sketches) — the leaf needs its own `id` (the nested section's stable id / heading source, the sibling of a `Leaf::Slot`'s `id`), distinct from the inner `Repeatable`'s `id-from`; on disk it is `{ id: changes, repeatable: { id-from, block } }`. Untagged-enum arm order is **`Slot` → `Repeatable` → `Field`** so the `{id, repeatable}` shape resolves before the flat field form (a `Slot` lacks `repeatable`, a `Field` lacks both — no ambiguity). The **H6/4-level cap** is enforced in the loader's recursion (`resolve_block(block, depth, pack_types)`, `depth` 1-based = items' nesting level, `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 4`): a block whose own depth exceeds 4 is `SchemaError::NestingTooDeep { depth }` — the same recursion that resolves each nested `Leaf::Field`'s type at every level (today's loader resolved only the top block). The two exhaustive `Leaf` matches in `parse.rs`/`validate.rs` gain an `unreachable!("… M22 inc-1 T2/T4")` arm — no shipped schema declares a nested repeatable yet (the changelog schema is authored later), so the arm is genuinely unreachable from production data this commit; T2/T4 replace it with real recursion. Landed `crates/engine/src/schema.rs` (+ compile-only arms in `parse.rs`/`validate.rs`). Flips [structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md) "one bounded level" → "bounded by depth (4 levels)".

**Pin (T3 executor, 2026-06-14 — render spacing elaboration within the settled spec, no new fork):** `render_item` becomes `render_item_at(item, depth)` (the depth-1 entry point `render_item` stays for the section renderer + splice helpers): heading level is `item_heading_level(depth) = 2 + depth` (the writer-side dual of the parser's `item_level_num`), multi-slot leaf sub-headings render one level deeper, and after `append_field_group` the item recurses into a new `ItemContent.items` carrier (mirroring T2's `ParsedItem.items`, skip-on-empty serde) rendering each child at `depth + 1`, joined by one blank line and EOF-normalized to one `\n`. The one genuine elaboration: a **slotless** item (`slot.is_none() && slots.is_empty()` — the M22 nested-parent / fields-only case, e.g. a changelog release: `date` field then nested `#### change-group` items, which by review-finding B1 carries **no** slot leaf) suppresses the post-heading blank line so its field group / nested items sit at a single-blank-line gap (`### …\n\n<!-- fields -->`), whereas a slot-bearing item keeps the existing post-heading blank — preserving byte-for-byte the empty-single-slot `### …\n\n\n\n<!-- fields -->` form `add_item`/`insert_item_field` already mint. The slot-AND-nested combination is a deferred shape the changelog avoids, so the two paths never coincide. An **empty** nested change-group renders the empty-single-slot body (`#### …{#id}` + two blank lines, the shape `add_item` mints + the parser round-trips), so the cold-skeleton fixtures carry that form. Landed `crates/engine/src/write.rs` (the `nested_roundtrip` suite: canonical two-level round-trip + cold incremental-fill + warm append, each asserting `render(parse(x)) == x` over the whole document).

**Pin (T4 executor, 2026-06-14 — recursion shape within the settled spec, no new fork):** `check_repeatable` keeps its `(section, repeatable, parsed, source, findings)` signature but lifts its per-item body into a recursive `check_item_leaves(item_path, repeatable, item, source, findings)`, where `item_path` is the accumulated address path **up to and including** the item (`section/item` at the top level, `…/parent/child` one segment deeper per nesting level). The `Leaf::Repeatable` arm (formerly an `unreachable!("… M22 inc-1 T4")`) now recurses over the parent item's `ParsedItem.items` (T2's nested carrier) against the nested `Repeatable`, so all three synthetic checks run at every level with the `id-from` heading-field exemption applied per nested block (`field.id == repeatable.id_from` at the level being walked). The leaf finding address is `{item_path}/{leaf_id}` — one hop deeper than before for a nested leaf (`releases/1-2-0/added/notes`). The one mechanical elaboration: the per-item check helpers (`check_item_slot_present`/`check_item_field`) drop their `section` parameter in favour of `item_path` (which already begins with the section id), and their **messages** now name `item_path` instead of `item.id` + `section.id` — preserving the CLI methodology-completion-record test's `findings`+`disposition` substring match (the `item_path` is `findings/half-authored`, which contains the section id `findings`). Landed `crates/engine/src/validate.rs` (the `nested_repeatable_conformance_tests` suite: conformant two-level clean, empty nested slot blocks naming the nested address, malformed nested field value blocks at the nested address).

**Pin (T5 executor, 2026-06-14 — addressing-convention + locator shape within the settled spec, no new fork):** the variable-depth fragment is an **additive `Fragment::Deep(Vec<String>)` variant** for **≥4 hops** — the four shipped ≤3-hop variants (`Unit`/`UnitLeaf`/`UnitItem`/`UnitItemLeaf`) are byte-identical (Display + every existing match unchanged), and the H6 cap stays real as `MAX_FRAGMENT_HOPS = 6` (section + up to four item hops + a leaf; a 7th hop is `TooManyHops`, the one repurposed error). The **canonical nested-leaf address is the 4-hop `#section/item/child/leaf` form** (no nested-section hop) — the form T4's validate already emits and the binary's nested `add-item` mints; S1's 5-hop `…/changes/added/…` example is the *naming* form used **only on the `add-item` target** (`#section/parent/nested-section`, which picks *which* nested repeatable receives the item), never on the minted/set address. So `add-item` carries the nested-section hop, while `set-slot`/`set-field` and the minted address carry item-ids only — internally consistent with T4's address builder. The locator is a single **parent-scoped path walker** `locate_item_path(schema, source, section, item_ids)` (heading level per chain index = `2 + depth`, each segment bounded to its parent's byte region); the existing single-level setters keep their signatures (top-level anchors are section-unique → unambiguous), and **new** depth-aware siblings `set_nested_item_slot` / `set_nested_item_field_or_insert` / `add_nested_item` carry the chain for the nested case (re-rendering the located item at `render_item_at(content, chain_len)` + splicing with the canonical separator). `doc.rs` resolves `Fragment::Deep` into `FieldTarget::NestedItem` / `SlotTarget::NestedItem` (split off section + trailing leaf, the middle hops are the chain) and `add_item_target` into `AddItemTarget::{TopLevel, Nested}` (replacing `section_hop`). A mis-named parent → `None` from the locator → a routed block (never a wrong-item write onto a same-anchor sibling). Landed `crates/engine/src/address.rs` + `crates/engine/src/write.rs` + `crates/cli/src/doc.rs` + `crates/cli/tests/nested_item_addressing.rs` (the real-binary nested-addressing acceptance over a fixture changelog pack).
