## 2026-06-19 — M27 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 27 Increment 2 (the remaining four grammars: JavaScript, Python, PHP, bash + shebang dispatch) into **four ordered, single-concern tasks** against [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Multi-language resolution (the JS/Python/PHP/bash allowlist rows + the dispatch extensions + the shebang-precedence rule) and the settled M27 forks F1 (all-declarations-any-nesting via the per-language node-kind allowlist) / F3 (bash = `.sh`/`.bash` + shebang-sniff for extensionless scripts, functions-only). **No pack/engine/CLI/schema change** (probe-internal — Inc 1 verified the only `resolve::` callers are `main.rs:208/212/225` and the probe is a detached workspace whose deps never enter the engine/cli lock graph). **Grounded in HEAD (verified by spike, not assumed):** Inc 1 landed the dispatch seam — `grammar_for(path) -> Option<Grammar>` (`resolve.rs:142`), the `Grammar` enum `{Rust, TypeScript, Tsx}` (`:34`), `with_root(src, grammar, f)` (`:126`), and `item_names`→`is_ts_citable` allowlist dispatch (`:160`/`:180`); each new grammar is a `Grammar` variant + a `grammar_for` extension arm + an `item_names` dispatch arm + an allowlist predicate, and is independently red-testable via `symbol_exists(src, sym, Grammar::X)` (the same harness Inc 1's TS tests use). A **fresh spike of all four grammars against the probe's pinned `tree-sitter 0.26.9`** (`-javascript 0.25.0`, `-python 0.25.0`, `-php 0.24.2`, `-bash 0.25.1` — all compile) dumped the real ASTs and verified every allowlist node-kind + the over-match negatives: **JS** — `function_declaration`/`class_declaration`, `method_definition` (parent `class_body` for a class method, `object` for an object-literal method), `variable_declarator` (parent-chain `lexical_declaration`→`statement_block` for a function-local `let`, →`program`/`export_statement` for top-level) — **identical node-kinds + value-position semantics to TS**, so JS **reuses `is_ts_citable` verbatim** (the TS-only kinds `interface_declaration`/`type_alias_declaration`/`enum_declaration`/`abstract_class_declaration` simply never appear in a JS AST); JSX parses **natively under `tree_sitter_javascript::LANGUAGE`** (`has_error=false` — *no* separate JSX grammar, unlike TS/TSX), so `.js`/`.jsx`/`.mjs`/`.cjs` all map to one `Grammar::JavaScript`. **Python** — `function_definition`/`class_definition`, a nested `def` sits under a `block` and resolves at any nesting; an `import` is an `import_statement` carrying a `name` field (the over-match the allowlist must exclude). **PHP** (`LANGUAGE_PHP`) — `function_definition`, `class_declaration` (an abstract class is the **same kind** with an `abstract_modifier` child), `method_declaration`, `interface_declaration`, `trait_declaration`, `enum_declaration` — all six confirmed (the review's interface/trait/enum false-block fix). **bash** — both `function f { }` and `f() { }` parse to `function_definition`; a bare call is a `command` node carrying `name=` (the over-match — functions-only), and a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang-led script parses cleanly under `tree_sitter_bash::LANGUAGE` (`has_error=false`). **Why four tasks, not one or two:** each grammar is a genuinely-independent allowlist + dispatch arm with its own red obligation in *Proves* and its own hostile-input fixture — four parallel concerns, not one; and bash's shebang-sniff is inseparable from bash (bash is the *only* grammar a `#!…sh` shebang resolves to), so it rides with bash as one gate-green unit. The four grammar deps land **distributed** — each task adds its own dep, inseparable from its allowlist compiling — and all four deliver the *Grouped scope* "add the four deps" bullet. **The shebang reshape:** `grammar_for(&Path)` cannot sniff a shebang (it has only the path); T4 widens the dispatch so that when the extension yields no grammar the caller reads the file's **first line** and maps `#!…sh`→bash (extension always wins; pure file-bytes read, no wall-clock/network — determinism intact). Gate green (fmt/clippy/build/test; the detached probe suite 57 passed). **Honest bounds carried:** `symbol-exists` is multi-language but **`criterion-maps-to-test`'s is-a-test predicate stays Rust-only** (a non-Rust test symbol blocks on vanish, advises on the test-half); bash is functions-only; CSS + docker-compose are parked (take the unsupported-language advisory). The M17-friction **doc-code non-Rust silent symbol pass is closed** in the wild for TS + Python.

## 2026-06-19 — multi-language doc↔code north-star: the hard design settled (shaped, unscheduled)

Direction set (a design discussion, no build): **doc↔code validation must reach every language a real project uses** — the [VISION.md](VISION.md) principle-#6 north-star, made explicit (a Rust-only validator is a Rust tool, not a context compiler for coding agents). Recorded as the strategic target; shaped in [ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md](ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md), indexed from VISION → Open questions. **Not scheduled** — promotes into [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Multi-language resolution milestone by milestone as each tier earns it.

**Four hard designs settled (the frontiers, so the roadmap rests on settled ground):** **HD1 (the keystone) — "symbol" generalizes to "addressable unit."** The per-language allowlist generalizes from "(node-kind, read `.name`)" to "(node-kind → an extractor yielding a unit name)"; CSS contributes class/id/keyframe/custom-property names (sigils stripped), YAML/JSON contribute keys, programming languages keep the `.name` read as one extractor kind. The address stays `path#name` ("any addressable unit named name"); a typed `path#kind:name` qualifier is a deferred escape hatch. `symbol-exists` is reinterpreted as "addressable-unit-exists" — **same check-id, same `code-anchor` field-type, zero schema change** (probe-internal, the M27 property). This is what makes "support language N" one uniform move, not N special cases. **HD2 — JS/TS call-based tests get full label-addressing now** (chosen over deferring): `path#test:"label"` matches a `test`/`it`/`describe` call's string arg; an **exact match → blocking-eligible** (not a heuristic), with the label-mutability fragility documented and knob-demotable. (Correction to an earlier framing: this does *not* breach the determinism boundary — it's a static parse; it bumps the stable-ID *philosophy*, a quality tension, not a hard invariant.) **HD3 — is-a-test confidence tiers:** attribute-based markers (Rust `#[test]`, PHP `#[Test]`) are **blocking-eligible** (exact); name-convention tests (pytest `test_*`, shunit2) are **advisory only** (heuristic — `symbol-exists` stays the hard floor, the test-half merely warns). **HD4 — grammar scaling:** bundle-all now (one probe, one embed-extract; raise the size guard per-milestone as M27 did), keep `grammar_for` + the allowlist as one centralized registry seam so pluggability stays possible later; **defer** dynamic/`.so`-pluggable grammars (native-code execution, a determinism/trust wrinkle) until binary size forces it. **Unifying rule across all of it: exact resolution blocks, heuristic resolution advises.** The honest ceiling: the determinism contract forbids running anything, so every predicate is a static heuristic — exact for *existence*, convention-bounded for *is-a-test*. **Tiered roadmap (unscheduled):** symbol-exists breadth (CSS first) → Camp-A is-a-test advisory → JS/TS label-addressing → grammar-scaling when it bites. **Subsumes** the CSS+docker-compose park and the non-Rust-is-a-test deferral ([decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)) — both now have a shaped design home, awaiting scheduling.

## 2026-06-20 — M28 planning: CSS symbol-exists (the first breadth target; proves the HD1 "addressable unit" generalization)

Milestone **created + planned** (the spine ended at M27; M28 is the doctype-expansion track's first breadth target). Generalizes the `doc-code` probe's resolution model from M27's *"(per-grammar citable predicate) → read the `.name` child field"* (fused across all six grammars at `resolve.rs:234-237`) to **"(node-kind + optional predicate) → an extractor yielding a unit name"** — the **HD1 keystone** ([ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md](ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md) → HD1). CSS is the proof because it is the most-different model (no `.name`-field declarations — only selectors / `@keyframes` / custom properties). **Scope: probe-internal only** — zero engine/CLI/pack-schema change (baseline-verified by exercise: `field-types.yaml`'s `code-anchor`, the three code-anchor doctypes, the engine, and the wire contract are all language-blind; a `styles.css#card` string is structurally accepted everywhere — the only language constraint lives in the probe's `grammar_for`). **CSS-only this milestone**; YAML/docker-compose stays deferred (the next breadth increment, same HD1 model). **is-a-test is N/A for CSS** (CSS has no tests) — out of scope.

**Baseline-verified by exercise** (3 `capability-auditor`s + 4 `gap-detector`s, the latter **spiking real tree-sitter-css ASTs** — compiling `tree-sitter-css 0.23.2` against the probe's pinned `tree-sitter 0.26.9` and dumping S-expressions of real CSS): the probe test suite is **58 passing** at HEAD (`e775d41`; the M27 completion record's "57" is stale — one unit added in `0d4875b`); the detached-workspace invariant holds (`cargo metadata` confirms `doc-code` is not a workspace member → tree-sitter-css cannot enter the engine/cli lock graph); the embed/extract/re-pin path is grammar-count-agnostic (no `setup.rs`/`build.rs`/`invoke.rs` edit); the size guard (90 MiB ceiling, ~18.7 MiB headroom over the 71.3 MiB debug artifact) holds with huge margin — CSS is the **smallest** grammar (`parser.c` 440 KB).

**The two blocking forks the spike surfaced and settled** (both the M27 over-match shape — a `name`-bearing non-declaration node false-*PASSING* a citation, the exact rot the probe exists to catch): **(1) Pseudo-class over-match.** A pseudo-class (`:hover`, `:root`, `:focus`) parses as `pseudo_class_selector > class_name` — the **same `class_name` node-kind** a real `.class` uses. The class extractor therefore **parent-constrains** `class_name` to a direct child of `class_selector` (the M27 `method_definition`→`class_body` / `variable_declarator`→`program` pattern); pseudo-elements (`::before`) parse as `tag_name`, already excluded. **(2) Custom-property is not a node-kind.** `--color: red` and `color: red` both parse as `declaration > property_name`; the extractor reads `property_name` text and **gates on `starts_with("--")`** (else every CSS property `color`/`display`/`margin` false-resolves). This is why the extractor model is **node-kind + predicate**, not pure node-kind.

**Forks settled** (the handover's six + the spike's corrections): **F1 — the CSS addressable-unit set** = **class / id / `@keyframes` / custom-property** names; **exclude** element/type (`div`), attribute (`[data-x]`), universal (`*`), and pseudo-class/pseudo-element selectors (they're either unverified by intent or the over-match traps above). `@font-face` is an anonymous at-rule (nothing to cite) — correctly dropped. **Compound/chained/descendant selectors contribute ALL their class/id names** (`.card > .title`, `.card.active` — each `class_selector` is visited by the existing full-tree walk; no walk change). **F2 — custom-property naming = KEEP the `--`** (human-decided 2026-06-20): cite as `styles.css#--color` — the `--` is genuinely part of the CSS identifier (`var(--color)`), unlike the `.`/`#` selector sigils (which the **grammar already separates** into sibling tokens — `class_name`.text is already `"btn"`, so class/id/`@keyframes` need **no stripping**; `--` is the only token kept verbatim). Collision-safe (`.color`→`#color` and `--color`→`#--color` stay distinct). **F3 — extractor-refactor scope** = generalize the seam cleanly (add one `Grammar::Css` match arm dispatching to a `css_item_names`; the six grammars keep the `.name`-field read as the other arm, **behaviorally byte-identical** — `item_names`/`symbol_exists` signatures unchanged, the 58 units the regression guard). `css_item_names` is **four node-kind arms** (review-confirmed, not just the two over-match traps the narrative foregrounds): `class_selector`→`class_name` (parent-constrained), `id_selector`→`id_name`, `keyframes_statement`→`keyframes_name`, and `declaration`→`property_name` gated on `--`. No language secretly needs multi-name; CSS is the first multi-name producer and the `Vec<String>` return already supports it. **F4 — acceptance** = `arch-doc.implemented-by` a real CSS class (single anchor per component, mirroring M27 flow 29); `adr.cites-code` over a CSS selector also works by construction (same `code-anchor`→`symbol-exists` path, zero per-doctype code). **F5 — severity** = exact→blocking, the unified rule; no heuristic creep (a selector in a `/* comment */` parses as `comment` and never false-resolves; `@import`ed sheets are not followed — single-file parse, cite the file that defines it). **F6 — version pin** = `tree-sitter-css 0.23.2` (the spiked-green version the node-kind table was verified against); re-spike if a newer pin is chosen.

**Honest bounds the milestone ORIGINATES** (HD1 is silent on these — written into `validation.md` as part of the milestone, not copied): element/type, attribute, universal, and pseudo-class selectors are **intentionally unverified** (not addressable units); `@import`ed stylesheets are **not followed** (single-file parse — a class living in an imported sheet blocks, by design, the same rule as Rust not following `use`); a class `.x` and an id `#x` **collide** under the existence-only `path#name` model (the typed `#kind:name` qualifier stays the HD1-deferred escape hatch — no real ambiguity in the acceptance, so not built). **G3 — `implemented-by` single-cardinality bound, recorded:** a real component often has several classes (`.card`/`.card--active`/`.card__title`), but `arch-doc.implemented-by` is a bare scalar `code-anchor` and the engine **blocks list-valued anchors** (`target_surface.rs:421` `multi-valued-anchor` guard); multi-class-per-component is **deferred engine work** (a `0..*` code-anchor with list-element enumeration), **not** an M28 schema knob — the acceptance uses one representative CSS class per component.

**Doc fold-back + drift** (T3 qualify-never-rewrite, the M27 discipline): promote the HD1 addressable-unit model into [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Multi-language resolution (reframe "read the `.name` field" → "extractor per node-kind", add a CSS row + an extractor column; **keep the `#multi-language-resolution-m27` anchor stable** — ~9 inbound links — add a subsection, don't rename); qualify the falsified sites (`validation.md:178/:188/:215`, [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md):86 CSS-half → GRADUATED with the compose/YAML half still pending, `VISION.md` Open-questions index, [ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md](ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md) status line + tiered roadmap — CSS shipped, the doc stays for YAML/HD2/HD3/HD4); a new worked-examples **flow 30** (the CSS arm, mirror flow 29). **No CLAUDE.md reading-order change** (validation.md already in order; CSS adds no design doc). **Test-flip census** (build-scope, named — review-corrected into two buckets so the stays-green sites aren't shipped as green-but-lying exemplars): **(a) genuinely flips RED, the assertion must change** — `probes/doc-code/src/main.rs:407` (`un_grammared_file_with_symbol_emits_unsupported_language_advisory`) + `tests/doc_code_probe.rs:703` (`unsupported_language_css_emits_one_advisory`): a `.css#symbol` now resolves to 0 findings, not 1 advisory. **(b) stays GREEN but the exemplar goes stale** — must be re-pointed *deliberately* (no red signal to catch them): `main.rs:436` (`bare_path…`, bare path never consults the grammar), `main.rs:449` (`missing…blocks`, dangling-file fires before dispatch), and **`crates/engine/src/result.rs:972`** (`unsupported_language_advisory_flows_through…`, a manually-constructed finding using `styles/site.css` as its unsupported exemplar — the census's 5th site, originally missed). **Re-point target = `.pl`** (off-roadmap), NOT `.yaml` — YAML/compose is the *next* breadth milestone and would re-churn any `.yaml` exemplar (and `main.rs:407` already carries a pre-existing `compose.yaml` exemplar = already-owed YAML-milestone debt). The `cargo_install_probe.rs:41` "a seventh grammar blows it" comment is now false → update. **Substrate-riding** → the forward-harness review is **skipped**: M28's one novel risk (the CSS over-match) is the same failure class M27 already hit and gated (negative-case over-match unit tests), so the existing gate shape covers it.

## 2026-06-20 — M29 planning: YAML/docker-compose symbol-exists (the second breadth target; the first language that RIDES the HD1 seam)

Milestone **created + planned** (the doctype-expansion track's second breadth target of the multi-language doc↔code north-star — [ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md](ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md) → HD1; CSS was #1 at M28). The reframe is the **inverse of M28's**: M28 *forced and built* the HD1 keystone (the per-grammar extractor seam — `item_names` dispatch); M29 is the first language that **rides** the finished seam, so it is the proof the keystone *generalizes cheaply* — "support language N = one uniform move (define N's addressable units), not N special cases." YAML's addressable units = **mapping keys** (a docker-compose service `web` is a mapping key under `services:`); `path#name` = "any mapping key named `name`," over the same `code-anchor` field-type, the same `symbol-exists` check-id, **zero engine/CLI/pack-schema change** (probe-internal — verified end-to-end by exercise: `code-anchor`'s value flows opaque through `field-types.yaml` → `check_code_anchor` write-validation → conformance → `target_surface` enumeration → probe `split_anchor`; the **only** extension-inspecting code is the probe's `grammar_for`). **is-a-test is N/A for YAML** (YAML has no tests) — out of scope, carried forward.

**Baseline-verified by exercise** (3 `capability-auditor`s + 4 `gap-detector`s, the latter **spiking the real grammar** in `/tmp/yamlspike` — `tree-sitter-yaml 0.7.2` compiled against the probe's pinned `tree-sitter 0.26.9`, dumping S-expressions of a real `compose.yaml` + a hostile `census.yaml`): the per-grammar extractor dispatch seam is live and clean (`item_names` `resolve.rs:234-254` short-circuits `Grammar::Css → css_item_names` `:348-359`; a `Grammar::Yaml` arm slots in identically, both `match`es exhaustive so a missed arm can't ship silently); the detached-workspace invariant is **double-detached** (own `[workspace]` + root `exclude`) → `cargo metadata` confirms `doc-code` is invisible to the engine/cli graph → tree-sitter-yaml cannot enter the lock graph; the embed/extract/re-pin spine is grammar-count-agnostic (no `setup.rs`/`build.rs`/`invoke.rs` edit); the size guard (90 MiB ceiling, ~18.5 MiB headroom over the ~72 MB debug artifact) holds with huge margin — YAML's parser is **tiny** (~310 KB `.o`, one of the smallest grammars); the probe suite is **68 passing** at HEAD (`734feeb`); `arch-doc.implemented-by` / `adr.cites-code` are bare-scalar `symbol-exists` anchors (fit); `spec.maps-to-test` is **unusable** (its `criterion-maps-to-test` override routes a non-Rust file to the is-a-test path → advisory, never blocks).

**The over-match census — the keystone risk (where M28's energy went), spike-settled.** The verified citable-node rule: **admit a name iff `node.kind()` ∈ {`block_mapping_pair`, `flow_pair`}, take `child_by_field_name("key")`, strip a single pair of surrounding matched quotes.** The `[key]`-field constraint is the YAML analogue of CSS's `class_name`-under-`class_selector` parent-constraint — it **structurally excludes** every over-match negative (an **anchor** `&web`→`anchor_name`, an **alias** `*web`→`alias_name`, a **tag** `!!str web`, a mapping **value** `WEB_HOST: web`, a **sequence item** `- web`, and `#`-comment text all live under the `[value]` field or as sequence children, never `[key]`). Proven: the key-field extractor over a real `compose.yaml` admits exactly the keys (`services`, `web`, `build`, `image`, `depends_on`, `db`, …) and excludes `.`/`nginx`/`postgres` and the value `web`. **Two `unverified-reuse` busts the spike surfaced — the extractor is NOT a pure `css_item_names` mirror:** **(B1) flow mappings need a second arm** — `{a: 1}` parses as `flow_mapping → flow_pair`, **not** `block_mapping_pair`; a single-arm extractor silently drops flow-map keys → **false-blocks a valid anchor** (under-match = false negative). **(B2) keys need quote-stripping; CSS did not** — the YAML `[key]` field returns the raw source span *including quotes* (`"web":` → `"\"web\""`), so a quoted key won't match `compose.yaml#web` without stripping. CSS's `css_child_text` (first-child-by-*kind*) is the wrong helper; the read is `child_by_field_name("key")` (by *field*) + quote-normalization.

**Forks settled** (the handover's six + two the handover omitted): **F1 — addressable-unit set** = **mapping keys** (both block `block_mapping_pair` and flow `flow_pair`), at **any nesting** via the existing `find_named_item` walk; **exclude** anchors/aliases/tags/values/sequence-items/comments. **Merge-key correction (review-caught 2026-06-20, spike-verified):** a merge `<<: *anchor` parses as an ordinary `block_mapping_pair` whose `[key]` is the scalar `<<`, so the rule **admits `<<`** — only the merge's *aliased value* (`*anchor`) is excluded (it lives under `[value]`). This is **harmless and left as-is** (`compose.yaml#<<` is never a real citation; filtering it would be code for nothing — *keep it minimal*); the original "merge-keys excluded" claim was **false** and is dropped — **do NOT cut a `<<`-does-not-resolve negative test** (it would fail). **F2 — key naming = STRIP surrounding matched quotes** (human-decided 2026-06-20): a quoted key `"web":`/`'web':` cites as `#web` — the deliberate **opposite of M28's keep-the-`--`**, because quotes are NOT part of the YAML identifier (`"web"` and `web` are the same key), whereas CSS's `--` genuinely is part of the identifier. **Bound (review-caught):** the strip removes only the *surrounding* matched quotes — internal YAML escapes (`"a\"b"`, `'a''b'`) and decorated/complex/anchored keys (`? [a,b]`, `&k web:`) are **not** normalized and resolve only against their raw inner span (rare for compose keys; the `#kind:name`/key-path qualifier stays the deferred escape hatch). **F3 — extractor scope** = one `Grammar::Yaml` match arm dispatching to a new `yaml_item_names` (the **2 node-kinds + quote-strip**, not a copy of CSS); the seven existing grammars keep their arms **behaviorally byte-identical** (`item_names`/`symbol_exists` signatures unchanged, the **68** probe units the regression guard). **F4 — acceptance** = `arch-doc.implemented-by` a real compose service key (single anchor per component, mirroring flow 30/29 — gets per-item disambiguation via the repeatable `components` block); `adr.cites-code` over a service key also works by construction; `spec.maps-to-test` is excluded (is-a-test path). **F5 — severity** = exact→blocking, the unified rule (the taxonomy table already lists `compose.yaml#web` as blocking-exact). **F6 — version pin** = `tree-sitter-yaml 0.7.2` (the maintained `tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-yaml` org, spiked-green against `tree-sitter 0.26.9` — no fork needed). **F7 — compose-blind breadth, ACCEPTED + recorded** (human-decided 2026-06-20; the handover's six omit this): **`.yaml` AND `.yml`** both dispatch, **extension-only, no `compose.yaml`/`docker-compose.yml` filename special-casing** (`grammar_for` stays purely extension-keyed; filename matching would be new machinery + compose semantics, against the schema-blind invariant). Consequence recorded: M29 resolves `#name` on **any** YAML (k8s manifests, GitHub Actions, app config), broader than docker-compose — `compose.yaml#web` means "a YAML key named `web` exists," **not** "a compose *service* named `web`." **F8 — acceptance delivery = the M28 posture, live-repo run as owner-driven hardening** (human-decided 2026-06-20; review-corrected from "hard live-repo gate"): the **build deliverable** is the **hermetic `flow31_acceptance.rs`** regression test (CI, authoring its own representative `compose.yaml` fixture mirroring flow 30 — runs without the external repo) **+ a measured artifact on a representative `compose.yaml`** (the M28-T4 analogue under `completions/artifacts/M29/`). The literal live PHP/TS/Vite + docker-compose run is an **owner-driven hardening step AFTERWARD** — not a completion gate (so the build/completion can't stall on the external repo's presence), exactly the M28 precedent (M28's in-the-wild measure ran on a scratch repo; the literal live run was owner-driven). The intent — *validate against reality* on a real compose service key — is preserved as the owner-driven post-build hardening check.

**Honest bounds the milestone ORIGINATES** (written into `validation.md` as part of the milestone, the M28 discipline): **flat-namespace collision — sharper than CSS's** (generic keys `image`/`ports`/`build`/`environment` recur under *every* service so `compose.yaml#image` resolves trivially-true; a service key `web` is indistinguishable from any same-named key at another path — record it **explicitly**, the M28 completion shipped a LOW for under-documenting exactly this); **compose-schema-blind** (zero docker-compose knowledge — the name must not over-promise); **block + flow mappings both contribute**; **anchors/aliases/tags/merge-keys/values/sequence-items excluded**; **single-file parse** (no `extends:`/`!include`/cross-file anchors followed — cite the file that defines the key, the Rust-`use`/CSS-`@import` rule; multi-document `---` streams resolve **all** docs' keys); the typed `#kind:name` / **key-path `#services.web` qualifier stays the deferred escape hatch** (YAML trigger: *a real citation must disambiguate a mapping key from a same-named key at a different path*). **G3 — `implemented-by` single-cardinality bound carries** (a deployment component often cites several services; `arch-doc.implemented-by` is a bare scalar and the engine **blocks list-valued anchors** at `target_surface.rs:421`, so multi-service-per-component is **enforced-blocked, not silent** — deferred 0..* engine work, not an M29 knob; the acceptance uses one service key per component). **Inventory — do NOT assert a literal count** in any M29 doc edit: M29 adds **no check-id** (rides `doc-code.symbol-exists`; `unsupported-language` is un-keyed), and the 27/24/20 doc drift (validation.md / `CHECK_INVENTORY` / knobs.yaml) **predates M29** — reconciling it is separate doc-hygiene, not M29 scope.

**Doc fold-back + drift** (T3 qualify-never-rewrite, the M28 discipline): promote the YAML addressable-unit model into [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Multi-language resolution (a **YAML row** in the extractor table `:167-175` + a new **`#yaml-addressable-units-m29` subsection** after the CSS one `:191-204`, with the YAML honest bounds; **keep `#multi-language-resolution-m27` and `#css-addressable-units-m28` byte-stable** — add, never rename); qualify the falsified sites (`validation.md:179` unsupported-extensions advisory list, **`:189`** "docker-compose stays parked" — the prime site, `:232` store-scope language list, `:165` non-`.name`-field enumeration); **graduate the whole** [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md):86 CSS+docker-compose entry (the compose/YAML half → SHIPPED at M29, no deferred half remaining); update [ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md](ideas/multi-language-doc-code.md):3 (status) + `:65` (tiered roadmap — YAML/compose ✓ M29, note stays open for JSON/TOML + HD2/HD3/HD4) and `VISION.md:201` (Open-questions breadth index); a new worked-examples **flow 31** (the YAML arm, mirror flow 30). ## 2026-06-20 — address-syntax fork settled: defer `#kind:name`, reserve the `:` namespace (pre-production, dogfood-informed)

Settled during the pre-production hardening pass (the project-alpha-2.0 dogfood, no committed docs in the wild yet → format changes are still free). The `path#name` code-anchor address resolves "any addressable unit named `name`" with a **flat namespace** — a class `.x` / id `#x` / `@keyframes x` (CSS) and a mapping key named `x` at any path (YAML) all collide. The dogfood **confirmed the collision is real structurally** (project-alpha-2.0's `compose.yml` has `broadcast` and `db` as *both* `services:` and `networks:` keys) but **it did not bite in actual authoring** — every real citation resolved to the intended unit because authors cite names unique enough in practice. **Decision (human, 2026-06-20): defer building the typed `#kind:name` qualifier (no premature generality — build when a real collision causes a *wrong* resolution), but RESERVE the syntax now** so deferring stays free: the `:` character in a code-anchor fragment is reserved for the future `path#kind:name` qualifier — no current grammar's extractor emits a unit name containing `:`, so `#kind:name` remains an unambiguous future namespace. A golden test guards the reservation (no extractor yields a `:`-bearing unit name; `path#a:b` stays the reserved form, not a current symbol meaning). **Trigger to build it:** a real project's citation collides across kinds such that `path#name` resolves to the wrong unit (not merely *could*). Recorded so the deferral has a reservation + a trigger and can't be foreclosed by accident. The doc note + the reserve test ride the pre-production hygiene batch.

## 2026-06-20 — M30 planning: finalize change-set scoping (per-task narrowing) + M31 split (worktree fan-out)

Planned via `/milestone-plan` (baseline-audit → 4-dim gap-detect → settle → review → decompose). The A1 deferral's trigger had fired (the project-alpha-2.0 dogfood proved unrelated WIP swept into a task commit). Baseline auditors verified at `83cb9e2`; the gap-detectors confirmed the handover's four forks **and surfaced three new blockers the ready 3-task cut underweighted**, two of which reshaped the milestone.

**The headline scope decision — SPLIT (human, 2026-06-20).** The fan-out/squash path is **not** a naive narrowing — it's a data-loss regression in disguise (the join merges *docs only*; sub-agent code is unstaged-by-design in the shared checkout and reaches the commit solely via `git add --all`; narrowing it drops every line of sub-agent code). Its correct fix is a **worktree-per-sub-agent code-isolation redesign** (the human's call — *"don't lock in the current solution if there's a better one; size is not the constraint"*). So: **M30 = the per-task narrowing only** (the production blocker, ships + unblocks production immediately, gets its own completion audit); **M31 = the worktree fan-out redesign** as its own planned milestone (decomposition + WF settlements parked in [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)). The per-task half is fully independent of all worktree work — risk-first, it lands first.

**M30 forks settled (human, 2026-06-20):**
- **Mechanism pin (G6) — commit the *whole index*, not a curated pathspec.** `owner-artifact` (`completions/artifacts/**`) is agent-written, *not* in `plan.promotions`, and reaches the commit only via the index — so finalize must "stage jigc's promoted docs + first-commit config *into* the index, then `git commit` the existing index," never `git commit -- <promotions+config>` (which would silently drop the owner-artifact even though its `#5` gate passed).
- **Staging policy (G1, per-task half) — `is_migration: bool` → a 3-way `StagePolicy`** (`MigrationFixed` / `IndexHonoring` / `Sweep`). Per-task non-migration → **IndexHonoring** (new); per-task migration → MigrationFixed (the proven `stage_migration` narrowing, `task.rs:1224`); **the milestone squash callers explicitly stay `Sweep`** (no naive narrowing → no data-loss regression), documented + parked to M31.
- **Empty finalize (G2) — block with guidance, PER-TASK ONLY.** On the per-task `IndexHonoring` path, redefine `has_diff` off the *narrowed* set (`git diff --cached` + promotions + config); if that set is empty but the tree is dirty, **block** (*"you staged nothing — `git add` your changes"*), upholding the no-empty-commits invariant. The "commit-only empty commit" is a test-harness artifact (every real persisted doctype promotes; a code task stages code) — no legitimate empty-commit product path. **The milestone path (`milestone.rs:488-490`) stays whole-tree** (it is `Sweep` — sub-agent code is unstaged-by-design; narrowing its `has_diff` would false-block a code-only milestone). Two distinct empty cases now exist on the per-task path: *dirty-tree+nothing-staged* → the "git add" message, *genuinely-clean* → the existing "produced no diff" — the CLI computes both facts and selects the message **CLI-side**; the **shared** `empty_commit_finding` (`finalize.rs:756`, used by both per-task + milestone planners) must NOT be edited (it would flip the milestone message). *(design-review finding 2, baked 2026-06-20.)*
- **Code-anchor citations vs unstaged WIP (G4) — validate the finalize-scope doc↔code probe against the INDEX, in M30.** A doc↔code probe validates the *on-disk* tree (`schedule_doc_code` → `EffectiveStateSnapshot::new(anchors, repo_root)`, `validate.rs:473`), but M30 commits the *index* — so an agent that writes a cited symbol into an already-**tracked** file but doesn't `git add` it would pass the probe (symbol on disk) *and* a path-granular tracked-status gate (file is committed), yet the commit omits the symbol → the marquee *"validate against reality"* link dangles at HEAD. A path-granular `TrackedPredicate` (the owner-artifact `#5` shape) only catches the rarer new-untracked-file case, **not** the common modify-tracked-file case. **Decision (human, 2026-06-20):** do it right — at finalize, after staging, **materialize the index** (`git checkout-index` into a temp tree) and run the finalize-scope `doc-code` probe against *that*, validating exactly what gets committed. Precise (no false-block on a cited file with unrelated unstaged hunks), upholds "validated reality == committed reality." Bounded engine work: a probe-snapshot-root change, not the one-line predicate add. *(design-review finding 1, settled 2026-06-20.)*
- **Agent staging contract (G5) — plain `git add` + adapter allowlist.** The agent stages its own code edits with `git add`; the claude-code adapter allowlist (`permit: ["jigc *"]`) gains `git add` (the agent already edits code directly in the tree — staging is consistent with "adapter-enforced, not sandboxed"). Pack guidance lands in the `implement`/`implement-quick`/`finalize` steps. CLAUDE.md's "agent authors, jigc commits" covered *committing*, not *staging* — staging is new contract surface, now recorded.
- **Left-out surface (G3) — a new "left-out" manifest representation.** `classify_landed_manifest` reads only the *included* set (`git show --name-status HEAD`); it needs a post-commit `git status --porcelain` read for the residual. A staged-then-modified file (`MM`) commits its staged bytes *and* leaves a worktree delta — so a path can be **both included and left-out**; modelled as a separate left-out list, not a `ManifestKind` variant (a kind can't express "partially included"). `predict_manifest`'s non-migration arm splits porcelain X (staged→included) vs Y (unstaged→left-out); `git_status_entries` stops collapsing XY (low blast radius — one consumer).

**M31 forks settled (human, 2026-06-20) — worktree fan-out, design spiked against the code (no hard blocker):**
- **Reopens the 2026-06-04 "no worktree machinery" decision** ([storage.md](design/storage.md) :111/139/143/166) — legitimately: that decision's rationale was *"never let git text-merge structured managed docs,"* which the M31 design **honors** (docs stay on the CLI by-task-id join; code uses **disjoint-apply + block-on-collision, never `git merge`**; `storage.md:144` already permits worktrees for "disjoint code-only" work). The basis changed — 2026-06-04 never weighed the shared-tree code-bleed M30 identifies as the production blocker. The actual `storage.md` amendment is an M31 task, gated first in its decomposition.
- **WF1 — stage-only** (sub-agents `git add` in their worktree; finalize combines the staged indices). Commit-in-worktree is rejected (breaks "sub-agent never commits" + CLI-owned message + the squash knob). Amends `workflow-dialect.md:266` *"never run git"* → *"never commits"* — the same relaxation M30 makes per-task.
- **WF2 — block, route the named colliding paths** (intersect the per-worktree staged name-sets; non-empty → block + name the paths, mirroring the doc same-doc-clash / cross-area-ref routing). Never text-merge.
- **WF3 — split the fused `repo_root` (worktree: code/index/HEAD) from `jigc_home` (main checkout: shared `.jigc/`, docs)**, resolving `.jigc` via `dirname(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)`. Behavior-preserving outside worktrees; touches ~66 `join(".jigc")` sites — the invasive heart of M31. (Per-worktree `.jigc` is rejected — it's the worktree-doc-merge the invariant forbids.)
- **WF4 — a CLI provisioning verb** run as a `Run:` step before the fan-out adds N detached worktrees at the shared base (the launch template can't carry it — one-line schema; compose stays pure). Teardown beside `cleanup_subtask_areas` (`milestone.rs:589`) on success and the abort reset (`:557`).

**Review + decompose.** A `design-reviewer` pass caught two same-model blocking blind spots, both baked back before decompose: **(finding 2)** "Same fix at `milestone.rs:488-490`" contradicted "milestone stays Sweep" — corrected to per-task-only `has_diff` narrowing, shared `empty_commit_finding` untouched; **(finding 1)** the G4 path-granular tracked gate left the *common* dangling-citation case open (a cited symbol written into an already-tracked but unstaged file) — re-settled to validate the finalize-scope `doc-code` probe against the **materialized index**. Decomposed into **4 risk-first linear increments** ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 30): (1) the `IndexHonoring` narrowing + `StagePolicy` + block-on-empty + fixture-wide staging migration (the dogfood red); (2) the left-out manifest surface (G3); (3) the index-validated citation gate (G4); (4) agent-stage contract (G5) + docs + measured acceptance (flow 32) + rebuild/re-pin.

## 2026-06-20 — M30 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M30 Increment 1 ("the per-task `IndexHonoring` narrowing + `StagePolicy` + block-on-empty — the keystone + the dogfood red") into **two ordered, single-concern tasks** along the **expand→contract seam**: T1 stages the sweep-reliant fixtures' authored code *first* (behavior-preserving under today's `git add --all`, so it breaks nothing), then T2 lands the narrowing as one atomic gate-green unit. *Why this cut:* the narrowing changes per-task commit contents, which **breaks** every fixture that `fs::write`s code and relies on the sweep — so the narrowing + the contract-test flips it forces are inseparable (one gate-green commit), but the wide-blast-radius mechanical fixture-staging is separable as a green prep step ahead of it. Grounded at `89bd31d`: `try_execute_finalize_plan` has three callers — per-task (`task.rs:694`), milestone `squash:false` (`milestone.rs:536`), milestone `squash:true` via `execute_finalize_plan` (`task.rs:1000`); `stage_migration` (`task.rs:1224`) + `existing_pathspecs`/`path_at_head` already exist to reuse; `owner_artifact_gate::finalize_lands_on_a_staged_owner_artifact` already `git add`s its artifact (the G6 positive case stays green untouched).

- **T1 (cli/tests — expand):** add a shared `git add` test helper and apply it to every finalize-invoking integration fixture that `fs::write`s repo code and relies on the sweep to commit it. *Done:* the real set is enumerated by grepping the `tests/` for an `fs::write` of repo code paired with a `task`/milestone finalize call lacking a preceding `git add` of that code (candidate set from the roadmap: `finalize_to_git`, `flow13/16/20/28/29`, `e2e_audit`, `arch_doc_acceptance`, `doc_code_gate`, `cold_start_zero_commit`, `file_state_soundness`, … — *enumerate, don't trust the count*); after the helper is applied the full gate (`cargo test` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check`) is green with the sweep still active (behavior-preserving). T2's gate is the completeness backstop — any fixture this prep misses goes red under the narrowing and is folded into T2.
- **T2 (engine+cli — contract, keystone):** replace the per-task non-migration `git add --all` (`task.rs:1090`) with `IndexHonoring`, introduce the 3-way `StagePolicy`, redefine the per-task `has_diff`+block-on-empty, and flip the commit-contents contract inversions, in one atomic commit. *Done:* a new acceptance test (the dogfood repro) stages a task edit, leaves one unrelated untracked file + one unrelated unstaged-modified tracked file, runs `jigc task finalize`, and asserts `git show --name-only HEAD` carries **only** the staged edit + promoted docs while the two unrelated files **remain** in `git status --porcelain` post-commit (RED before the narrowing, GREEN after); a second case proves a dirty-tree-nothing-staged task **blocks** with the *"you staged nothing — `git add` your changes"* message; `owner_artifact_gate::finalize_lands_on_a_staged_owner_artifact` stays green (G6); the migration tests (`migration_finalize_git_add`, `finalize_manifest::migration_dry_run_predicts_the_narrowed_set_not_user_wip`) stay green (`MigrationFixed` ≡ today's `stage_migration`); the named contract inversions are flipped; the full gate is green.

- *Mechanism pin (T2, G6):* `IndexHonoring` = `git add` jigc's promotion `destination`s + `existing_pathspecs(&[".jigc/config", ".jigc/.gitignore"])` (the same existence/`path_at_head` exit-128 guards `stage_migration` uses) **into** the existing index, then the existing whole-index `git_commit` (`git commit -F`, no pathspec) — **never** `git commit -- <pathspec>`, which would drop the agent-`git add`ed, non-promoted `owner-artifact`. It is a subset of `stage_migration` (no retirements on a non-migration task) and adds to, never narrows, the existing index.
- *Mapping pin (T2):* `StagePolicy` { `MigrationFixed` / `IndexHonoring` / `Sweep` } replaces `try_execute_finalize_plan`'s `is_migration: bool`. Per-task (`task.rs:694`) selects `IndexHonoring`|`MigrationFixed` by `source_seam.exists()`; both milestone callers (`milestone.rs:536`; `execute_finalize_plan` at `task.rs:1000`, the `squash:true` path) pass `Sweep` **explicitly** — unchanged behavior, the data-loss-safe choice M31 owns. The `IndexHonoring` variant is introduced *with* its construction site (per-task), never unused (an unconstructed variant fails `clippy -D warnings`, the M2-I2-T2 dead-`pub fn` lesson).
- *Empty-commit pin (T2, G2):* the per-task `has_diff` (`task.rs:617`) is recomputed off the **narrowed** set (`git diff --cached` + `plan.promotions` + the config layer) — required so a WIP-only task does not attempt an empty commit under `IndexHonoring`. When that set is empty the **CLI** selects the message: dirty-tree (unstaged/untracked changes present) → block *"you staged nothing — `git add` your changes"*; genuinely-clean → the existing engine `empty_commit_finding`. The shared `empty_commit_finding` (`finalize.rs:756`) is **not** edited and `milestone.rs:488-490`'s `has_diff` stays whole-tree (editing either would flip the milestone message — design-review finding 2).
- *Manifest-scope pin (T2):* `predict_manifest` (`task.rs:774`) and its `is_migration: bool` are **not** touched in Inc 1 — the `--dry-run` forecast still predicts the sweep (Inc 2 / G3 reworks it to the narrowed + left-out model). Consequence: `finalize_manifest::json_manifest_on_dry_run_and_landed_run` has its **landed** half adjusted in T2 (the stray no longer lands → drop the `committed.manifest carries the stray` assertion) while its **dry-run** half stays asserting `untracked` (predict unchanged) — a consistent interim; Inc 2 reworks both. `dry_run_prints_manifest_and_commits_nothing` (dry-run only, no landed finalize) stays green in Inc 1 untouched.
- *Contract-inversion set (T2):* flip the tests that assert a stray *lands* — `finalize_manifest::normal_finalize_commits_stray_and_surfaces_it_as_untracked` (stray no longer committed), `store_sweep_acceptance::freeform_notes_swept_into_finalize_commit_not_baseline_adopted`, `finalize_outcome_surface::{outcome_space_is_discriminable, landed_finalize_emits_findings}` (the commit-only `{task}.txt` must now be `git add`ed to land) — plus the `json_manifest` landed half above. The gate-green obligation is the real backstop for the full set.

## 2026-06-20 — M30 Increment 1 T2 landed: per-task IndexHonoring narrowing (3 implementation elaborations)

Shipped the keystone (`StagePolicy`{`MigrationFixed`/`IndexHonoring`/`Sweep`}, the per-task narrowed `has_diff`, block-on-empty, contract-flips) per the planning pins. Three elaborations refined the pins against the code:

- **Empty-commit selection is a *post-plan recolor*, not a pre-plan intercept.** The CLI's "you staged nothing" block can't fire *before* `plan_finalize`, or it preempts the validation / forward-ref / base-mismatch blocks that must win (e.g. `flow21`'s seeded schema-conformance block, `implement_from_spec`'s `implements`-edge block). So `plan_finalize` runs first with the narrowed `has_diff`; only when it returns the `finalize.empty-commit` finding **and** the working tree is dirty does the CLI swap in `finalize.nothing-staged` (a routed `Finding::block`). The shared engine `empty_commit_finding` stays untouched; precedence is preserved.
- **Narrowed `has_diff` is *non-migration only*; a migration keeps the whole-tree probe.** A migration's retire-safety blocks (the F1 missing-replacement gate, the clobber guard) live *after* the empty-commit guard inside `plan_finalize`, so a migration must keep `has_diff` on the original `git_diff(base) || staged_docs || untracked` probe — else a no-replacement migration trips empty-commit before F1. `is_migration` is read ahead of `has_diff` and branches it; `MigrationFixed` stages its own fixed set regardless. The narrowed probe excludes the transient commit doc (`plan.promotions`/promotable staged docs, never `staged_docs` wholesale) so a commit-only no-code task reads empty.
- **The OOB-absorb fixture stages its edit (the human-in-git channel `git add`s).** `finalize_outcome_surface`'s absorb scenario relied on `git add --all` sweeping an unstaged OOB edit into the commit; under the narrowing that would leave the absorbed baseline ahead of HEAD (record in-sync with on-disk, HEAD carrying old bytes). Flipped so the human stages the edit → it rides the commit → committed bytes == absorbed baseline ("validated reality == committed reality" held, not bypassed). The absorb advisory still fires from the on-disk preflight sweep.

## 2026-06-20 — M30 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M30 Increment 2 ("the left-out manifest surface (G3): index/worktree split + dry-run/landed symmetry") into **two ordered, single-concern tasks** along the **dry-run vs landed seam** — the only seam that keeps each piece gate-green (a *layer* cut would split atomic units: changing `predict_manifest`'s return shape breaks the render it feeds in the same motion). T1 builds the **dry-run forecast** surface (the `predict_manifest` path + the shared `left_out` representation); T2 builds the **landed residual** surface (the `classify_landed_manifest` path), reusing T1's pinned representation symmetrically. *Why this seam:* the producers are independent and each has exactly one consumer — `git_status_entries` (`task.rs:1615`) + `status_code_to_kind` feed only `predict_manifest` (`task.rs:868`, **verified** — grep shows one caller); `git_commit_name_status` + `classify_landed_manifest` feed only the landed call site (`task.rs:775–776`, **verified**) — so the dry-run cluster and the landed cluster reach a green gate independently. No design edit here: Inc 2 is code+tests only; the `design/finalize.md` B1 "surfaced, not prevented" block revision (and the semantic retirement of the "swept" wording) is **Inc 4**'s doc fold-back, cross-referenced in the roadmap. Grounded at `348522d` (Inc 1 landed): `predict_manifest`'s non-migration arm currently maps each path to **one** `ManifestEntry` via `status_code_to_kind` (collapsing the porcelain XY → one kind); `classify_landed_manifest` reads **only** the included `git show --name-status HEAD`; both render fns (`finalize_manifest`/`finalize_landed` + `Landed`) carry only `manifest: Vec<ManifestEntry>` with the now-stale `ManifestKind::Untracked`→`"swept (was untracked)"` line.

- **T1 (cli — dry-run forecast):** stop `git_status_entries` collapsing the porcelain XY; rewrite `predict_manifest`'s non-migration arm to split **X column → included** / **Y column → left-out** (a path dirty in both columns appears in **both** sets); introduce the shared `left_out` representation + render it in `finalize_manifest` (text line + JSON field). *Done:* a `--dry-run` over a staged task edit + an unrelated untracked file + an unrelated unstaged-modified tracked file + a **staged-then-further-modified (`MM`)** path asserts the included `manifest` carries the staged edit + the X side of `MM` and the **`left_out`** list names the untracked + unstaged-tracked + the Y side of `MM` (the `MM` path in **both**); `--format json --dry-run` carries the `left_out` field; the render unit test `render::tests::render_finalize_manifest_flags_untracked_and_json_carries_dry_run` is flipped (stray → `left-out`, not `swept`); `finalize_manifest::dry_run_prints_manifest_and_commits_nothing` is flipped (stray rendered `left-out`); the **dry-run half** of `finalize_manifest::json_manifest_on_dry_run_and_landed_run` is flipped (stray in `left_out`, no longer `manifest[]` `untracked`); the migration arm is untouched and `migration_dry_run_predicts_the_narrowed_set_not_user_wip` stays green; full gate green.
- **T2 (cli — landed residual symmetry):** add a post-commit `git status --porcelain` read to `classify_landed_manifest` for the residual left-out set; add the `left_out` field to `render::Landed` + render it in `finalize_landed`/`landed_summary` (text + JSON `committed.left_out`), using T1's pinned field name. *Done:* a **landed** finalize over the same fixture (staged edit + unrelated untracked + unrelated unstaged-tracked + `MM`) asserts `committed.manifest` (the commit delta) carries the staged edit + the staged side of `MM` while `committed.left_out` (post-commit porcelain) names the untracked + unstaged-tracked + the `MM` worktree residual (the `MM` path in **both**); `--format json` carries `committed.left_out`; the render unit test `render::tests::render_finalize_landed_carries_the_manifest` is flipped; the **landed half** of `finalize_manifest::json_manifest_on_dry_run_and_landed_run` is flipped (stray now in `committed.left_out`, still absent from `committed.manifest`); `normal_finalize_leaves_unstaged_stray_uncommitted` stays green (gains a left-out assertion); full gate green.

- *Field-name + symmetry pin (settled up front, both tasks — G3 "specify the field name + dry-run/landed symmetry"):* the JSON left-out field is **`left_out`** (snake_case, matching the existing `dry_run`), used **identically** on both surfaces — dry-run emits `{ dry_run, manifest, left_out }`; landed emits `committed: { hash, subject, promoted, files, manifest, left_out }`. The measurement-envelope consumers parse it, so the name is fixed once here and T2 must reuse T1's name verbatim. `left_out` is a **separate list** of `ManifestEntry` (reusing the existing `ManifestEntry`/`ManifestKind`, kind taken from the **Y/worktree** column), **not** a new `ManifestKind` variant — a kind can't express "partially included" (the `MM` case), which is exactly why a path can be in `manifest` *and* `left_out` at once.
- *MM-in-both pin:* a staged-then-further-modified (`MM`) path is reported in **both** the included `manifest` and `left_out`. Mechanism: T1 splits the dry-run forecast by porcelain column (X≠blank → included, Y≠blank → left-out); T2 derives included from the commit's own `git show --name-status HEAD` delta and left-out from a fresh post-commit `git status --porcelain` read (a staged edit lands in the commit *and* its un-restaged worktree delta survives the commit → residual left-out).
- *Bullet-3 split pin (whole-scope tracking):* the two named contract-inversion tests split across the tasks — `dry_run_prints_manifest_and_commits_nothing` flips wholly in **T1**; `json_manifest_on_dry_run_and_landed_run` is staged (its **dry-run half** flips in T1, its **landed half** in T2) — the precedented interim (Inc 1 handled this same test by adjusting one half at a time; the dry-run/landed seam forces it again). Both tasks' done-criteria name their half so the punt is tracked to a landing.
- *Producer blast-radius + migration-untouched pin:* `git_status_entries`/`status_code_to_kind` have one consumer (`predict_manifest`) and `git_commit_name_status`/`classify_landed_manifest` one consumer (the landed site) — **verified by grep**, so the two tasks are independently gate-green and neither touches the other's cluster. `predict_manifest`'s **migration** arm and a migration's landed manifest are unchanged in both tasks (migration is `MigrationFixed` — no user WIP, no left-out); the migration manifest tests stay green untouched.

## 2026-06-20 — M30 Increment 2 T1 landed: dry-run included/left-out split (2 elaborations)

Shipped the dry-run forecast split per the planning pins: `predict_manifest`'s non-migration arm now returns `(included, left_out)` by splitting each porcelain entry's X (index → included) and Y (worktree → left-out) columns (`MM` lands in both); the collapsing `status_code_to_kind` is replaced by a per-column `column_kind`; `finalize_manifest` carries the `left_out` JSON field + render line; the migration arm returns `(entries, vec![])`. - **The left-out render shape is a guidance sub-section, not a per-line flag.** Rendered as a header `  left-out (unstaged/untracked — git add to include):` followed by 4-space-indented paths (factored into a shared `render::left_out_lines` helper). ## 2026-06-20 — M30 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M30 Increment 3 ("the index-validated citation gate (G4): validate doc↔code against what gets committed") into **one atomic, single-concern task** — the deliverable is one inseparable gate-green unit. *Why one task (not the Inc-1/2 expand→contract split):* the Inc-1/2 splits were driven by a **wide fixture-migration blast radius** that the index probe does **not** carry — so the param-add and its only use can't reach independent green gates worth separating, and the change has a clean red step on its own. Grounded at `778dcc3` (Inc 2 landed): `validate_task`/`schedule_doc_code` thread a single `repo_root` (`validate.rs:166`/`455`) used **both** to *enumerate* the doc anchor surface (`enumerate_target_surface`, the docs side) **and** as the `doc-code` snapshot's `working_tree_root` (`EffectiveStateSnapshot::new`, `validate.rs:473`, the code side); the probe resolves each anchor as `working_tree_root.join(path)` (`probe.rs:574`, `doc-code/src/resolve.rs`). `validate_task` has **9 callers** (1 CLI at `task.rs:504` inside `self.validate()`, 8 engine unit tests) — the signature change forces all 9 in one motion. `self.validate()` is the **single shared entry** for both `jigc task validate` (verb, `task.rs:234`) and `jigc task finalize` (`task.rs:610`), so the materialization lives there, never on a finalize-only path — **finalize has no private check path** ([finalize.md](design/finalize.md):41); validate previewing the same index is the *required* consequence, not a divergence.

- **T1 (engine + cli — the index-validated `doc-code` gate):** split the engine's fused `repo_root` so the `doc-code` snapshot's `working_tree_root` is a **separate `code_tree_root` param** (threaded `validate_task` → `schedule_doc_code` → `EffectiveStateSnapshot::new`); enumeration + every other `repo_root` use (`load_committed`/`overlay_working`/`ref_resolves`/`reconcile_committed_store`/the #5 owner-artifact gate) stay `repo_root`. In `self.validate()` (CLI), **materialize the current git index** into a temp tree (`git checkout-index -a --prefix=<temp>/` via `git_run`, the `std::env::temp_dir()`+unique-name+`Drop`-cleanup idiom the engine's `store_scratch_path` / the CLI's `describe.rs::TempDir` already use) and pass that temp-tree path as `code_tree_root`; the 8 engine unit tests pass their working dir (`repo_root`) — byte-identical at engine scope (the engine stays shell-free; "it's the index" lives entirely in the CLI). *Done:* a new acceptance test (`crates/cli/tests/`, real `jigc` binary, `JIGC_DOC_CODE_PROBE`-selected probe) asserts **(a)** an in-task `adr.cites-code` to a symbol the agent wrote into a tracked file **and staged** → finalize **passes**; **(b)** the **same symbol left unstaged** → finalize **blocks** naming the dangling `doc-code.symbol-exists` anchor (RED before — working-tree resolution passes the on-disk symbol; GREEN after); **(c)** a citation to an **already-committed-at-HEAD** symbol still passes (the existing `task_validate_probe_present_resolves_clean_control` covers this — stays green); **(d)** a cited file whose symbol is **staged but carrying an unrelated unstaged hunk** → **passes** (no false-block — the index has the staged symbol, bullet 4); the existing `doc_code_gate` suite stays green (its `present_symbol` is HEAD-committed → in the index); the full gate (`cargo test` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check`) is green.

- *Mechanism pin (T1, G4):* the materialization captures the **agent-staged** index — `self.validate()` runs at `task.rs:610` **before** jigc's `IndexHonoring` promotion/config staging (`try_execute_finalize_plan`, ~`task.rs:1185`), but code anchors resolve only against **code** (the agent stages it under the G5 contract; jigc only ever stages **docs**/config later), so no validate↔staging reorder is needed and the index already holds exactly the about-to-be-committed code. This preserves validation.md:228's original intent ("the probe reads exactly the bytes about to be committed") now that the narrowed commit is the **index**, not the whole working tree.
- *Whole-scope coverage pin:* the mechanism is **doctype-generic** — `enumerate_target_surface` collects every `code-anchor` leaf regardless of type, so `adr.cites-code` / `arch-doc.implemented-by` / `spec.maps-to-test` (roadmap bullet 2) are all covered by the one code path; the acceptance exercises `adr.cites-code` (the in-task-creatable MVP doctype), the others ride the same `code_tree_root`. **Store scope is untouched** (`validate_store`/`store_doc_code` keep `repo_root` — the deliverable is finalize/task scope only).
- *Backstop + doc-debt pin:* any task-scope `doc-code` fixture whose **cited** code is unstaged at validate goes red under the index probe and is folded into T1 (the gate is the completeness backstop — the Inc-1 T2 discipline); the finalize-invoking flow/`arch_doc`/`e2e` fixtures were staged in Inc 1, so the expected fold-in is near-zero. The stale `validation.md:228` "reads the working-tree code" sentence becomes false here but is **left to Inc 4's doc fold-back** (Inc 3 is code+tests only, mirroring Inc 2) — **flagged: Inc 4's doc list (`design/finalize.md`/`storage.md`/`write-commands.md`/`worked-examples.md`) omits `design/validation.md`; Inc-4 planning must add the `:228` index correction.**

## 2026-06-20 — M31 planning: worktree fan-out code isolation

Planned via `/milestone-plan` (baseline-audit → 4-dim gap-detect → settle → review → decompose). The M30 split-off; direction blessed + WF1–WF4 spiked at M30 planning. Baseline verified at HEAD `bc22613` by 4 `capability-auditor`s **exercising the real binary**; 4 `gap-detector`s spiked the **exact new shape** (worktree path, N indices, the combine), not analogy. **M30 foundation confirmed built-and-proven by exercise** — `StagePolicy` 3-way, `IndexHonoring` narrowing, index-validated `doc-code` gate, left-out manifest — no claim-vs-reality gap. **Confirmed negatives (spiked, not assumed):** no new doctype / schema / relation / grammar; **no VISION/CLAUDE invariant edit** (worktree-per-sub-agent *is* "an isolated working area keyed by task ID"; disjoint-apply *is* "in task-ID order"; "CLI orchestrates, git executes" + "the CLI core makes no LLM calls" hold — provisioning/combine are deterministic git shell-outs); git helpers are already worktree-parameterizable (`.current_dir(repo_root)`, no hardcoded paths); **no milestone-path `doc-code` gate exists** → none to build (don't speculatively scope a combined-index gate).

**Baseline corrections to the parked plan (verified, supersede the handover):** `repo_root` is computed by **11 independent walk-up copies** (+ 5 `require_project_layer` copies), not one resolver — WF3 undercounted the *resolver* fragmentation; the ~66 `.jigc` joins is exact (55 cli/src + 11 engine test-setup). The combine mechanism (`git apply` / per-worktree index / `read-tree` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` / `--git-common-dir`) exists **nowhere** outside `setup.rs`'s hooks resolver. Line drift: the `git add --all` sweep is `task.rs:1218` (not `milestone.rs:488-490`, which is the *coupled whole-tree `has_diff`*); `cleanup_subtask_areas` `milestone.rs:598`; abort reset (`git_reset_hard`) `milestone.rs:566`; `empty_commit_finding` `finalize.rs:756` (matches).

**The three human forks settled (2026-06-20) — robust over cheap on all three (the M30 "size is not the constraint" posture):**
- **Sub-agent→worktree binding = REOPEN the M8 one-line spawn-template rule** (over id-derived auto-locate). The worktree path enters the `Spawn:` line. *Engaging the M8 rule's rationale:* its purpose was a decidable, deterministic one-line launch contract (no arbitrary shell); the worktree path is a **pure function of task-id + the provisioning convention**, so a scoped relaxation permitting exactly `cd <deterministic-worktree> && jigc workflow …` (one structured token, validated structurally) **preserves** the determinism rationale rather than discarding it. `validate_spawn_template` (`adapter.rs:222`) + `render_spawn` (`adapter.rs:187`) + `emit_fan_out_spawns` (`compose.rs:872`) gain the worktree-path token. *Why over id-derived:* the agent edits + `git add`s code **directly**, so the agent's **cwd** must be the worktree — jigc resolving its own `repo_root` by id is insufficient; the launch line is the honest place to carry it. (Same locked rule `decisions-pending.md` flags as the multi-assistant milestone's sharpest risk — reopened here first, scoped.)
- **Doc-store seam = BIND to jigc_home** (over leave-on-worktree). The ~31 `repo_root.join(<location>)` committed-doc-store sites (`engine::store::canonical_path` + `file_state`/`index`/`compose`/`state` readers) resolve against **jigc_home**, not the worktree. *Rationale:* the committed doc-store has a single canonical home (the main checkout); resolving docs against a worktree was only ever correct by the base-pin coincidence (two independent spikes showed byte-identity at base). Making jigc_home the **unconditional** doc home matches WF3's own framing ("jigc_home = shared `.jigc`, **docs**") and is correct-by-construction regardless of worktree base — closing the gap pass's latent worktree-doc-bleed (reachable **today** via `sub-task.yaml`'s `allows-create: adr`, which lets a fan-out sub-agent author a committed ADR whose copy-on-first-touch reads the doc-store). *Carried invariant:* main does not advance during the fan-out window; promote always runs from jigc_home.
- **squash:false = REWORK to honest commits** (over remove the knob). Each per-sub-task commit carries that sub-task's **worktree-attributed** code (disjoint-apply that one worktree's staged set per commit + render its commit doc). *Rationale:* squash:false rides `Sweep` (which stages **nothing** under worktrees → the path is *broken*, not merely imperfect), so it must change regardless; the tree-empty `--allow-empty` form was a workaround for the missing code-attribution M31 now provides, so M31 is the moment to make the `commit` doctype **honest** (the message describes the tree it rides), fixing the gap pass's "message lies about its tree" defect. *(review B1/B2, baked 2026-06-20:)* "honest" applies to **code** — each per-sub-task commit's message describes its own code; the **merged docs promote in the parent aggregate** commit, because the by-task-id doc-join is a cross-sub-task merge with **suffix resolution** (`storage.md:161`) that can't be cleanly partitioned per-sub-task — so docs are a milestone-level merge artifact, not a per-sub-task lie. The now-non-empty per-sub-task commits **relay their `pre-commit` hook output each** — the M19 relay-on-aggregate rationale (`finalize.md:74`) assumed *tree-empty* commits and is invalidated; `:74` is **rewired, not reworded**.

**Mechanical resolutions (recorded, not forks):**
- **Combine mechanism = a temp-index off-line build** (review S2, baked 2026-06-20 — over `git apply --index` into the live main index). Build the combined tree off-line: `GIT_INDEX_FILE`=a temp index initialized from the base tree, `git apply --cached` each worktree patch in task-id order, `git write-tree` → `git commit-tree` → fast-forward the ref + checkout. The live worktree/index is **never mutated until a clean commit lands**, so a failed or blocked apply needs **no destructive reset**. *Why not `git apply --index` + `git reset --hard <pre_finalize_head>`:* that rollback resets the main checkout's index **and working tree** → it would wipe unrelated main-checkout WIP on the failure path — the **exact** WIP-destruction hazard M30 existed to kill, re-introduced. The off-line build sidesteps it entirely (and the `--cached`-into-live ` D <file>` drift is moot).
- **The "main does not advance" invariant is enforced by the milestone-finalize `base == main-HEAD` preflight** (review S1, baked 2026-06-20) — **not** the sub-agent base-pin guard, which under WF3 reads the *worktree* HEAD (frozen at the pin) and is a no-op for main-divergence. That preflight is **also** the precondition for clean disjoint-apply (worktree patches are `diff --cached` relative to base; they apply cleanly only while main == base). Inc 4 must preserve it + add an acceptance that an advanced main blocks finalize (HEAD unchanged, nothing applied).
- **WF4 worktree base = the recorded milestone base pin** (`read_base_pin().sha`), **not** `main` HEAD — else the base-pin guard (`start.rs:1440`, reading the *worktree* HEAD under WF3) fires immediately. Policy: main does not advance during the fan-out window.
- **WF2 collision granularity:** block-set = union of {staged path, rename old-path, delete path} per worktree, read from a **rename-aware `git diff --cached --name-status`** (else a rename slips the name-set guard); block across the **whole** fan-out, consistent with squash:true. (A content collision on *different* paths is not a name collision → both apply, accepted.)
- **WF3 layered resolver:** keep `discover_repo_root` as the worktree-finder; add a **separate `jigc_home()`** that shells to git (`dirname(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)`) only when a real `.git` is present — so the ~20 fake-`.git` unit tests (`create_dir_all(".git")` without `git init`) stay green. The mechanism is behavior-preserving outside worktrees (spiked: identical path in the non-worktree case); `setup.rs:244` already has the worktree-common-dir pattern (green test).
- **has_diff narrowing (milestone path):** recompute **CLI-side** as `docs-materialized OR Σ(worktree git diff --cached)`; **do not edit** the shared `empty_commit_finding` (`finalize.rs:756`, used by the per-task path too).

**Off-substrate gate review (per-novel-milestone — the worktree/combine machinery is net-new, not riding the proven substrate):** the failure classes our green gates would pass: **(a) post-finalize working-tree hygiene** — a commit correct at HEAD that leaves the tree dirty-showing-deletions (the `--index` resolution kills it; an acceptance assertion that `git status` is clean post-commit pins it); **(b) code-combine determinism** — hardening #7 (single-execution determinism trust) covers the *doc* join, but the *code* combine is a **new concurrent-merge surface** that must be held to the same bar: byte-identical commit across sub-agent feed/completion orders, applied strictly in task-id order. Both are explicit acceptance obligations in the decomposition.

**Doc work — the gated-first amendment is a REVISE, not a light qualifier (gap pass correction):** `storage.md` `:111/:141/:145/:168` state "fan-out is *not* a worktree case," and `:146` fences fan-out *out* of the worktree path **and** permits `git merge` (which M31 rejects); the "two combine-modes" binary (`:143`) forecloses M31's **third** mode (disjoint-apply, never git-merge). *Engaging the 2026-06-04 rationale* (never text-merge structured managed docs): it **holds** under M31 (docs stay on the CLI by-task-id join; only code uses worktrees, disjoint-applied/blocked, never merged) — so this is a rationale-honoring **revise** that adds the third mode, not an override. The doc-store→jigc_home invariant earns a design-doc home (it lived only in DECISIONS prose). Gated as M31's **first** task, never silent. (`workflow-dialect.md:266` "never run git"→"never commits"; `:343` + `storage.md:167` drifted "no worktrees" pointers; `VISION.md:216` open-question pointer — all fold in.)

**Review + decompose.** A `design-reviewer` pass (independent, verified against the code) returned **2 blocking + 2 should-fix + 2 advisory, all baked** (human-accepted 2026-06-20): **(B1/B2)** squash:false honesty scoped to **code** + **docs-in-aggregate** + **per-commit hook relay**; **(S2)** the combine uses a **temp-index off-line build**, not `git apply --index` + `reset --hard` (M30 WIP-safety on the failure path); **(S1)** the milestone-finalize `base==main-HEAD` preflight named as the "main does not advance" enforcer + an Inc 4 advanced-main-blocks acceptance; **(A1)** the determinism bar asserts byte-identical **tree + message sequence** (not the timestamped commit SHA — the established `milestone.rs:982` bar); **(A2)** teardown-failure **surfaces a warning** naming the leaked worktree + the `git worktree prune` remedy (pinned, not silent-log/block). **Clean negatives verified:** increment linearity (no producer↔consumer reverse-dep; Inc 2/WF3 provable green with zero worktrees), the WF3 census (11 walk-ups + 5 `require_project_layer` + 55 cli / 12 engine joins; the engine already takes `jigc_root` separately → WF3 is overwhelmingly CLI-side), doc-store→jigc_home correctness-by-construction (modulo S1's named enforcer), and **no VISION/CLAUDE invariant edit** survives pressure-testing. Decomposed into **5 risk-first linear increments** ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 31): (1) **gate** — reopen the invariant (`storage.md` revise + `workflow-dialect.md:266/:263/:343` + `VISION.md:216`, doc-only, separate commit); (2) **WF3** root-split + doc-store→jigc_home rebind (highest surface, behavior-preserving outside worktrees — provable green with zero worktrees); (3) **WF4** provisioning verb + M8-template reopen + worktree-path spawn binding; (4) **the combine keystone** (squash:true: per-worktree `diff --cached --name-status` → name-set block+route → `git apply --index` in id order → narrowed has_diff → determinism bar) + flow 33 + `finalize.md`; (5) **squash:false honest rework** + flow 9 fold-back + rebuild/re-pin + measured facts.

## 2026-06-21 — M31 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M31 Increment 2 ("WF3: the `repo_root` / `jigc_home` split + doc-store→jigc_home rebind — the invasive heart, highest surface") into **two ordered, single-concern tasks** — T1 introduces the resolver (the spiked claim turned into a test), T2 is the one CLI-fuser rebind that consumes it. *Why this seam:* the whole increment is **behavior-preserving outside worktrees**, where `jigc_home() == discover_repo_root()`, so **every existing test (all run outside a worktree) stays green regardless of how the threading is staged** — there is **no gate-forced coupling** to honor and no atomic gate-unit to keep whole; the cut is driven purely by single-concern + risk-first + independent verifiability. The rebind is **one fuser concern, not three** — verified against the code: the engine **never shells git** (0 `Command::new("git")` in `crates/engine/src`), so every engine root parameter is a pure doc-store/`.jigc` filesystem read; the engine **already separates `jigc_root` (`.jigc` state: `file_state`/`index`/`state`/`milestone`) from `repo_root` (the committed doc-store: `store`/`compose`)**, and the **CLI is the sole fuser** (e.g. `cli.rs:592`: `let jigc_root = repo_root.join(".jigc")` then passes the *same* walk-up `repo_root` to `validate_store_families`). So the doc-store→jigc_home rebind needs **zero engine signature change** — it is achieved CLI-side by passing `jigc_home` to the doc-store engine entry points; the ~31 `repo_root.join(<location>)` engine sites resolve correctly **by construction** once the CLI feeds them `jigc_home`. Splitting the `.jigc`-join rebind from the doc-store rebind would therefore touch the **same command-entry functions twice** (each entry computes one root and routes it to both `.jigc` joins and doc-store calls) — over-split churn, not a real seam. **No new fork surfaced** — fully covered by the 2026-06-20 M31 planning entry (the doc-store→jigc_home bind fork; the layered resolver; the deliberate base-pin HEAD routing; "the engine already takes `jigc_root` separately → WF3 is overwhelmingly CLI-side") and [storage.md](design/storage.md) (Inc 1). **Grounded at HEAD `711aa17`:** `setup.rs` `resolve_hooks_dir` (~`:244`) is the git-common-dir shell pattern + `setup.rs:1360` `install_precommit_resolves_worktree_common_hooks_dir` already does `git worktree add` in a test (the manual-worktree-spike harness is proven feasible); the cli crate has a `[lib]` (so a `pub fn jigc_home` is **not** `dead_code` → a resolver-first task is gate-green with no production caller yet); 11 `ancestors()` walk-up sites + 9 `discover_repo_root` copies + 5 `require_project_layer` copies (`ingest`/`describe`/`upgrade`/`config`/`cli`); ~15 fake-`.git` fixtures (`create_dir_all(".git")` without `git init`) across cli src+tests rely on the walk-up fallback; `reenter_in_repo` `start.rs:1419` resolves `.jigc`/task-dir **and** reads HEAD off the cwd-derived `repo_root`; the lone existing worktree test (`setup.rs:1360`) exercises *hooks-dir* resolution, **not** `jigc_home`, so behavior-preservation holds.

- **T1 (the `jigc_home()` resolver — risk-first, the spiked claim → a test):** add a **separate `pub fn jigc_home`** to the cli lib — `dirname(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)`, **shelling to git only when a real `.git` is present** (a valid git dir/file), else **falling back to the walk-up** (`discover_repo_root`) so the fake-`.git` fixtures never shell out to a real ancestor repo (`setup.rs:244`'s `resolve_hooks_dir` is the shell pattern). Keep `discover_repo_root` as the worktree-finder (the layered design). ## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 2 T1 build: jigc_home discriminator = `.git`-is-a-file

`jigc_home` (new `crates/cli/src/repo.rs`, `pub mod repo` in the cli lib) shells git **only when `.git` is a *file*** — the exact, sole marker of a linked worktree (a `gitdir:` pointer). A main checkout (`.git` dir) and a fake `create_dir_all(".git")` fixture (`.git` dir, no internals) both return the walk-up `discover_repo_root` directly, no shell-out. *Why this over a general "real `.git` present" probe:* it makes the byte-identity (a) and the fake-`.git` fallback (c) hold **by construction** — outside a worktree `jigc_home` returns the walk-up path *verbatim* (never git's possibly-canonicalized output), and a fake `.git` can never walk up to a real ancestor because we never shell from a directory `.git` (spiked: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` from a fake nested dir *does* bind to the real ancestor — the bug the file-discriminator sidesteps). Equivalent to the planned `dirname(git-common-dir)` shell (a main checkout's common-dir parent *is* its repo root), but strictly stronger on byte-stability.

## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 2 T2 build: the CLI-fuser rebind (`.jigc`/doc-store → jigc_home, code/git/HEAD → worktree)

Threaded `jigc_home` through the CLI so the committed doc-store + `.jigc/` resolve against **jigc_home** (the main checkout) while every `git` shell-out (HEAD/diff/status/add/commit/checkout-index) stays on the worktree `repo_root`. Zero engine signature change — the engine already separates its `repo_root` (doc-store base) from `jigc_root`, so the CLI just passes `jigc_home` to the doc-store entry points (`canonical_path`/`read_slice`/`committed_store`/`index::load_committed`/`validate_task`/`plan_finalize`/`enumerate_target_surface`/`join`/`materialize`/`validate_store_families`). Mechanism: a `pub(crate) start::jigc_home_or_repo` + `require_project_config`; `locate::RunContext` gained a `jigc_home` field (project_config now resolves against it); `require_project_layer` (config/ingest/describe/upgrade/cli) returns jigc_home; `TaskArea`/`ActiveTask` carry jigc_home. `reenter_in_repo`/`resume_in_repo` resolve `.jigc`/task-dir/compose-base via jigc_home but read the base-pin HEAD off the worktree (worktree HEAD == milestone pin under WF4). Behavior-preserving outside worktrees because `jigc_home == discover_repo_root` there (whole existing suite byte-identical green). The 3 now-orphan `discover_repo_root` copies (config/describe/doc) + the `upgrade` copy were removed (own-orphan cleanup); ingest/milestone/task keep theirs for the worktree git/HEAD reads.
