## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 3 T1 build: the worktree provisioning verb (3 elaborations)

Shipped `MilestoneCommand::Provision` + `run_provision`: read the milestone's recorded **base pin** (`read_base_pin().sha`, never main HEAD), enumerate the id-sorted sub-task list, and `git worktree add --detach <path> <base-sha>` one detached worktree per sub-task under `.jigc/worktrees/<sub-task-id>`, shelled on the main checkout `repo_root`. The shared `engine::milestone::worktree_path(id) -> .jigc/worktrees/<id>` helper (relative, a pure function of task-id) is the one convention T3's spawn binding reuses. Three elaborations against the code:

- **Idempotency = prune + reuse-if-registered + clear-stale-leftover, not blind --force.** `git worktree prune` first (drops admin records for dirs a crash deleted), then per sub-task: a worktree **already registered at the exact path** is reused untouched (the crashed-run worktree or a prior provision — it is necessarily this sub-task at this immutable pin, since paths are keyed by sub-task-id); a **non-registered stale leftover dir** (the test injects one) blocks `git worktree add`, so it is `remove_dir_all`'d before the add. Reuse comparison is against canonical paths — `jigc_home` is `canonicalize()`d up front and joined with `worktree_path(id)` so the per-id path matches `git worktree list --porcelain`'s canonical `worktree <path>` lines (git stores the symlink-resolved path at add time).
- **`worktrees/` joins `ensure_jigc_gitignore`'s `ENTRIES`** (was absent) — else the linked worktree dirs pollute the main checkout's `git status` / `git add --all`. The idempotent-rewrite guard now checks **both** `milestones/` **and** `worktrees/` are listed, so an adapter-written `.gitignore` predating either is amended once.
- **Detached HEAD == pin is proven, not assumed** (the WF3 base-pin-guard precondition): the acceptance advances main past the pin *after* minting, then asserts each provisioned worktree's `git rev-parse HEAD` == the pin (C0), not advanced main (C1). The git shell-outs run on `repo_root` (worktree under WF3) while `.jigc/worktrees/` binds to jigc_home — they coincide outside a worktree, where provision actually runs (a `Run:` step in the main checkout).

Deliberate scope boundaries (deferred to WF4/WF5, behavior-preserving outside worktrees): (1) the **finalize promote+commit transaction** (`try_execute_finalize_plan`/`execute_finalize_plan`) keeps `repo_root` = worktree for both the promote-write and the git commit — worktree-finalize promote *placement* (docs live in jigc_home but are never git-merged across worktrees) is the deferred concern; its `.jigc` state-save (post-commit index/file-state) does bind to jigc_home. (2) The **migrate path** (`mint_migration_in_repo`/`compose_migrate_in_repo`/`migrate.rs`) stays uniformly on the worktree `repo_root` — worktree-migrate is deferred; kept uniform to avoid a latent half-threaded state. (3) The **ingest edge-index HEAD stamp** reads the worktree HEAD (the literal HEAD→worktree rule) while its doc-store/index bind to jigc_home. Red→green proof: `crates/cli/tests/worktree_jigc_home.rs` drives `jigc workflow single-task --task <sub>` from a real `git worktree add` over a main checkout whose HEAD was advanced past the milestone pin — it finds the project against jigc_home, provisions into the main checkout's `.jigc/`, and passes the base-pin guard only because HEAD reads the worktree.

## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 3 T3 build: spawn-template reopen (structural tightening) + worktree spawn binding

Reopened the M8 one-line spawn-template rule as a structural **tightening**, not a loosening (verified: the old purely-lexical `validate_spawn_template` already accepted both `cd … && jigc workflow …` and arbitrary `rm -rf … && jigc workflow …`). New `SpawnTemplateReason::DisallowedShellPrefix` clause: the backticked span must be **either** the bare `jigc workflow … --task …` invocation **or** that invocation prefixed by a single `cd <one-whitespace-token> &&` — exactly one token after `cd` (the CLI-filled `{{worktree}}` placeholder, validated structurally, never matched against a value — determinism rationale preserved), and no other shell (a non-`cd` prefix, a multi-token `cd` arg, or any trailing `&&`-chaining rejected). Implemented as `spawn_span_is_permitted` (split the span on the first `&&`; only a `cd <token>` prefix is allowed, remainder must start `jigc workflow` and chain nothing further).

- **Spawn binding lands in two places, both keyed on the shared `engine::milestone::worktree_path(id)` (T1):** `render_spawn` (adapter, launch path) gains a `{{worktree}}` → `.jigc/worktrees/<task_id>` substitution; the engine `emit_fan_out_spawns` (compose) emits `` Spawn: `cd .jigc/worktrees/<id> && jigc workflow <wf> --task <id>` `` per id. The shipped `adapters/claude-code.yaml` template + its `insta` golden updated to the `cd {{worktree}} &&` form (an intended template change, not a re-pin).
- **Executed-bytes contract for the worktree binding:** `spawn_template_executes.rs` + `flow10_acceptance.rs` now provision the worktrees (T1 verb) then execute the rendered `cd <worktree> && jigc workflow …` span **through a shell** (`sh -c`, the built `jigc` prepended to `$PATH`) into the provisioned worktree — it reaches the re-entry verb (exit 0) only because the WF3 jigc_home resolver finds the main checkout's `.jigc/` from inside the worktree. The cd-span needs a real shell + a real worktree, so the bare-argv execution the M8 test used is replaced.
- **Doc home = `assistant-adapter.md` → Bind the spawn mechanism** (the design home of the rule; the roadmap scoped the fold there). Added a structural-span-shape bullet beside the M8 forbidden-patterns bullet + updated the shipped-template example. Left `workflow-dialect.md`/`worked-examples.md` flow-10 narrative (the bare-form Spawn examples) untouched — out of T3's single concern; the worked-examples flow-10 worktree-lifecycle refresh is an M31-wide follow-up (the feature isn't whole until Inc 4/5 teardown+combine).

## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 3 T4 build: worktree teardown on success + abort + the A2 non-blocking leak warning

Added `remove_worktrees(repo_root, jigc_home, list)` beside `cleanup_subtask_areas`: for each id-sorted sub-task whose `<jigc_home>/.jigc/worktrees/<id>` checkout is still a **registered** worktree (`git worktree list --porcelain`, matched on the same canonical-path convention `provision_worktrees` uses), `git worktree remove --force` it, then `git worktree prune` the admin records. Wired into `run_milestone_finalize` at the **two success branches** (squash:false `Ok(hook_output)` + squash:true `code == SUCCESS`) and the **squash:false abort reset** (after `git_reset_hard`). A teardown failure (review A2) surfaces a **non-blocking warning naming the leaked worktree path + the `git worktree prune` remedy** — heavier than `cleanup_subtask_areas`' silent self-heal because a leaked worktree is a registered git object, not gitignored scratch — but never blocks a commit that already landed.

- **Signature deviates from the planner's `remove_worktrees(repo_root, list)`** — it also takes `jigc_home`, needed to compute `canonical_home.join(worktree_path(id))` (the provision path convention). `jigc_home` is already in scope at all three call sites; matching against registered worktrees by id-suffix alone would be fragile.
- **Registered-only teardown** means a non-fan-out finalize (no provision run — every existing finalize test) tears down nothing: the registered check skips all ids and only the harmless `git worktree prune` no-op runs, so the existing suite is behavior-unchanged.
- **Abort still tears down worktrees** (the sub-task *areas* survive for retry, but a leaked worktree is heavier scratch and re-provisions cleanly on retry) — the deliverable's "teardown on success and on abort."
- Test lever for the forced-failure arm: `git worktree lock` makes single-`--force` removal refuse the leaf (needs `--force --force`), so the locked worktree leaks (warning) while its unlocked sibling is still removed, and the commit's exit code is unchanged.

### M31 Inc 4 T1 — the off-line combine engine (`crates/cli/src/combine.rs`)

- **Seam = `combine.rs::combine_worktree_trees(repo_root, base_tree, &[worktree])` → `CombineOutcome::{Combined(tree-sha), Blocked(Finding)}`** — a cli-lib pub fn (dead_code-exempt, no caller until T2), returning a **tree sha, never a commit**, so WIP-safety is provable in isolation (review S2). Lives beside `repo.rs` (the Inc-2 T1 cli-lib pub-fn precedent).
- **Rename-aware *detection*, rename-decomposed *apply*** — collision block-set reads `git diff --cached --name-status --find-renames` (rename old-path enters the set, WF2), but the apply patch is `git diff --cached --binary --no-renames` (renames decomposed to delete+add → applies trivially against base without rename-header fragility). Two separate diffs per worktree.
- **Order-invariance is internal** — the fold sorts the worktree list by task id (the path's final component) before applying, so the combined tree is byte-identical regardless of input order (hardening #7); the collision finding lists colliding paths + contending task ids via `BTreeMap`/`BTreeSet` so its message is byte-stable too. Block code = `combine.code-collision`.
- **Off-line build = a throwaway `GIT_INDEX_FILE` in the system temp dir** (`read-tree` base → `apply --cached` each patch → `write-tree`), removed on Drop; the live `.git/index` and working tree are never touched, so a blocked/failed combine needs no destructive reset and unrelated main WIP survives.

## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 5 fork settled (human): restore the user's hooks on squash:true, WIP-safe, folded into Inc 5

The M31 build **halted at Inc-5 planning** on a genuine settled-decision conflict the planning pass didn't foresee (the hook question was framed only around squash:false relay, fork B2). Inc-4's squash:true combine commits via off-line `git commit-tree` (review S2's WIP-safe build) which runs **no** `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` hook — violating `finalize.md`'s hard contract (`:69`/`:171`: "the CLI never passes `--no-verify`; the user's hooks are policy and the CLI respects them"). squash:true is the **default** knob, so the bypass is on the common path; the basis the Inc-4 executor accepted it on ("no hook in any squash:true test") was **proven false** (`milestone_finalize_relays_only_the_aggregate_hook_output` installs a pre-commit hook on squash:true). The two settled decisions — S2's off-line WIP-safe combine vs. the never-bypass-hooks contract — cannot both hold with `git commit-tree`. The build correctly halted rather than override either.

**Settled (human, 2026-06-21):**
- **MECHANISM = restore the hooks, WIP-safe** (over accepting the carve-out). Run the user's `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` hooks against the combined tree **without touching the main checkout** — reuse M31's worktree machinery (commit the combined tree from / run hooks in a clean dedicated context — e.g. a dedicated worktree where `git commit -F` runs the hooks against the would-be-committed tree — then fast-forward main). This honors **both** finalize.md's hook contract **and** S2's WIP-safety; the conflict is dissolvable (not irreducible) precisely because M31 already builds worktree machinery. The exact shape (dedicated-worktree `git commit` vs. running the hook scripts around the off-line tree) is settled at Inc-5 re-plan. *Rejected — the carve-out (keep commit-tree, accept no hooks on the aggregate, document it):* silently drops the user's hooks on the **default** commit path, a retreat from the contract Inc-1 *just revised the docs to tell the truth about*; the M30 index-validated `doc-code` gate (at validate) is only a **partial** mitigation (covers doc-code, not arbitrary user hooks — formatters, policy checks).
- **SCOPE = fold into Inc 5** (over a separate increment). Both squash:true and squash:false now build through the same Inc-4 combine, so resolving hooks once for both is one coherent motion and makes Inc-5's in-scope `finalize.md:104` fold-back tell **one** honest hook story. Inc 5 grows; the roadmap Inc-5 scope is widened accordingly.
- **squash:false stays independently plannable** (unchanged by this): live-apply each worktree's staged patch (collision-block across the whole fan-out up front, reusing `combine.rs`'s block-set) + `git commit -F` per sub-task (hooks run + relay via the existing `git_commit`/`relay_hook_output`), reset-on-abort; the merged docs ride the parent aggregate. Whatever squash:true mechanism is chosen must be **consistent** with this so finalize.md tells one truth.

The retargeted `milestone_finalize_relays_only_the_aggregate_hook_output` (squash:true currently asserts `HOOK_WARNING == 0` with the marker "Inc 5 restores hook execution") flips back to asserting the hook **fires** on the squash:true aggregate. *Tree clean at halt (HEAD `ea0244e`, Inc-4 landed); this is a plan-phase fork, no code fix needed — record + widen roadmap Inc-5 + resume.*

## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 5 T1 build: squash:true hook restoration (dedicated-worktree commit)

`combine_commit` (`task.rs`) no longer commits via the hook-less `git commit-tree` + `git reset --hard`. The off-line combined tree is still built in a throwaway index (unchanged), then committed via a new `commit_combined_tree_with_hooks`: a `DedicatedWorktree` (a detached `git worktree add` under the gitignored `.jigc/worktrees/.combine-<pid>-<nanos>`, removed on drop) is set to the combined tree with `git read-tree --reset -u <tree>` (HEAD stays at the parent, so the commit's parent = main HEAD and its tree = the combined tree), then the **shared** `git_commit` (`git commit -F`, **never** `--no-verify`) commits it there — so the repo's shared `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` hooks run against the combined tree (a linked worktree shares `.git`, hooks included). The captured hook stream is returned (not `String::new()`) so the existing success-relay surfaces it. Main is fast-forwarded (`git reset --hard <commit>`) **only after** the hook-running commit lands, so a hook rejection lands nothing and unrelated main-checkout WIP survives (review S2 preserved). `git_commit_tree` removed (dead). The squash:true half of `milestone_finalize_relays_only_the_aggregate_hook_output` flips to asserting the non-blocking hook fires exactly once + relays in the `--- hook output ---` section; flow33 (clean tree / order-invariance / WIP-survives-a-blocked-combine) stays green. Concrete shape = the fork settlement's named example (the executor's red-driven plumbing detail).

## 2026-06-21 — M31 Inc 5 T2 build: squash:false honest per-sub-task-code rework (Sweep retired)

The `squash: false` milestone boundary now lays one commit per sub-task carrying **that** sub-task's worktree code. `commit_per_subtask_messages`/`commit_empty_message` (the tree-empty `git commit --allow-empty` form) are replaced: `commit_per_subtask_code` (`milestone.rs`) reads each provisioned worktree's staged patch (`git diff --cached --binary`, id order) and, for each worktree that staged code, applies it onto the **main checkout** (`git apply --index`, via the new `crate::task::commit_subtask_code`) then `git commit -F` its rendered `commit:<sub-id>` doc through the shared `git_commit` — so the user's hooks run on **every** per-sub-task commit and each commit's non-blocking hook output is relayed. **Elaboration:** a worktree with **nothing staged** contributes **no** per-sub-task commit (no `--allow-empty` substitute) — the commit sequence is a pure function of the *code-carrying* sub-task id set; the merged docs ride the parent aggregate (review B1/B2), which now stages over the clean index the per-sub-task commits left via `StagePolicy::IndexHonoring` (the **`Sweep` variant + its match arm are removed** — dead once its sole construction site moved; the M2-I2-T2 clippy lesson). A cross-worktree code collision **blocks up front** before any commit via `combine::detect_code_collision` (the rename-aware `block_set`/`collision_finding` factored out of `combine_worktree_trees`, which now delegates to it). Reset-on-abort: `git_reset_hard` to the captured pre-finalize HEAD undoes the per-sub-task commits on any per-sub-task or aggregate failure (all-or-nothing). The squash:false tests are reworked to provision worktrees + stage disjoint code (`setup_squash_false`), assert each per-sub-task commit's `git show --name-only` carries its files (not an empty tree) + the merged docs land in the aggregate (not partitioned), the relay test (renamed `milestone_finalize_relays_every_fan_out_commit_hook_output`) flips to N+1 relays, and a net-new same-file-collision-blocks test is added. squash:true (T1) untouched. ## 2026-06-21 — Direction: methodology forcing-functions authored pack-shaped; live-repo self-hosting deferred behind external proof

A working-direction call (human, 2026-06-21), from the M31 retrospective. The laziness/prose-accretion class we keep hand-patching in the methodology docs (`milestone-planning-workflow.md`, `increment-workflow.md`, the agent prompts) **is the class jigc exists to solve**: a required *slot* in a managed doc cannot be skimmed-past the way a prose paragraph can; a composed *step* always appears. The "make it a forcing function, not prose" lever *is* the determinism boundary. So:

- **New methodology forcing-functions are authored *pack-shaped* from now on** — framed as the *slot / step / presence-validation* the methodology pack will encode, even while they still live as markdown. This makes the markdown a **spec for the pack**, so the eventual encode is transcription, not redesign — closing the drift between the docs we hand-maintain and the pack the self-hosting arc will encode. (First instance: D, the consolidated plan-time gate-record, designed pack-shaped in [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → The planning gate-record.)
- **Honoring the A-3 honesty bound** ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → What M16 does not prove): the pack-shape is **presence-conformance, never content-scoring**. jigc enforces that the gate-record slot is *filled* (required-slot-present); it never reads/grades the judgment (the #5 owner-artifact "presence, not content" precedent). A composed step that emits a `gap-count ≥ N` lint or auto-checks a checklist would *hollow* the judgment — barred. The checkpoints halt; they never score; the agent authors the judgment into the slot.
- **The honest boundary on what folds:** the working *docs* fold (the M16 doctypes) and the workflow *content* folds (steps/slots/checkpoints/fan-out); the *orchestration* does **not** (the bounded fix-loop, the multi-agent planning fan-out, the 3-round cap stay the `milestone-build` harness's job — no DAGs/runtime, by invariant) and *judgment* stays human (jigc asserts the census is present + the review ran, never that they were good).
- **The live-repo migration stays deferred** behind external proof + human testing — exactly the existing self-hosting sequencing ([roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M16 "jigc's own docs migrate at v1" + M17 external pilots/A-B/measurement). We do **not** put our own critical-path process docs on the tooling until it is earned elsewhere. Recorded so new methodology edits are pack-shaped *now* without triggering a premature self-host.

*Trigger for the encode:* the self-hosting planning-workflow encode / v1 migration (keyed in [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)).

## 2026-06-21 — M32 planning: decouple commit-doc provisioning from `selectable` (settled)

Resolves the M31-completion finding (graduated from [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → M32). Baseline verified **by exercise** (3 capability-auditors + 4 gap-detectors, all at HEAD `92acbc5`):

- **Audit verdict — 1 broken / 10 false-positive.** Eleven workflows are `creates-task: true, selectable: false` and match the gate `!def.creates_task || !def.selectable` in `provision_on_first_entry` (`crates/cli/src/start.rs:335`). Only **`sub-task`** is genuinely broken (exit 1, *"no staged instance — provision it first"* on a real `jigc workflow sub-task --task <id>` re-entry) — it is the **sole fan-out `run:` target** and the **only** workflow whose commit doc is provisioned *exclusively* on the re-entry path (minted by `milestone execute`, never by `compose_core`'s mint arm). The 5 `migrate-*` ride a separate provisioner (`provision_migration_commit_doc`); the 4 methodology + `record-change` are fresh-started via `compose_core`'s mint arm (gates on `creates_task` alone). All 10 verified fine — false-positive matches of the *flag*, never traversing the buggy *function*. Recorded so the "11 matched the predicate" alarm doesn't re-fire blind at a future audit.
- **Root cause = gate-divergence.** The `|| !def.selectable` clause is a byte-identical **transplant** of the router-catalog filter predicate (`selectable_workflows`, `start.rs:1326`) into a provisioning guard where only the `creates_task` half belonged. Added by **`7e5393a`** (2026-06-05) under a commit message entirely about the router catalog — never mentions `provision_on_first_entry`, and left the function's docstring still reading *"Gated on `creates_task`."* No decision-record couples provisioning to `selectable`; the over-reach is confirmed incidental. The decouple *honors* `7e5393a`'s actual rationale (router-catalog exclusion) and M16's authoring-spine rationale ([methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) — `creates-task: true, selectable: false` mints a task *to author managed docs*, which the bug directly contradicts).
- **Fix = robust shared predicate, not the one-line flip (human fork, settled).** Both the mint arm (`compose_core:843`) and `provision_on_first_entry` consult one `should_provision_commit_doc(def) -> bool { def.creates_task }`, so the provisioning property has **one source of truth** and the catalog predicate can't be re-transplanted into it. *Why over the cheaper flip:* the defect *is* the divergence (two hand-synced predicates); a one-liner restores correctness today but leaves the re-diverge vector — a fragility the code has *now* (shipped undetected 16 days), so consolidating is solving the real problem, not premature generality (PRINCIPLES → Keep it minimal = smallest *robust* solution). The `path.exists()` write-once guard (`start.rs:340`) makes the now-reachable re-entry provisioning safe for the 6 mint-provisioned siblings (re-entry finds the doc present → no-op; no clobber of a filled `migrate-*` commit).
- **`selectable`'s contract is now written down** ([workflow-dialect.md](design/workflow-dialect.md) → On-disk definition format + the router section): a boolean (default `true`) governing **router-catalog membership only**, orthogonal to minting/provisioning — *"coupling `selectable` into a minting or provisioning gate is a bug, not a symmetry."* Closes the regression vector (the field was undocumented in the front-matter spec and the router section conflated `selectable ≡ creates-task`).
- **Acceptance (full prevention scope, human fork).** The genuine path no test has ever covered: `milestone execute` → real `jigc workflow sub-task --task <sub>` re-entry → `set-field`/`set-slot` on **`commit:<sub>`** → finalize, in **both** squash modes (the existing flow10 drives genuine re-entry but authors only the ADR, finalizes squash:true, and never asserts the commit doc — green *despite* the bug). Plus a sibling-census regression (a re-entered filled `migrate-*` commit survives byte-untouched) + a resume guard, and the in-code comment corrections (`start.rs:317-328` docstring, `workflow_reentry.rs:204-207`). Decomposition in [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → Milestone 32.
