Files: `crates/engine/src/transform.rs`.

### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-2 T1 landed: the schema-diff classifier (`schema_diff::{schema_diff, SchemaChange}`)

New `crates/engine/src/schema_diff.rs`: `schema_diff(v1, v2) -> Vec<SchemaChange>` over the four kinds, document-order deterministic (output follows `v2`'s section/leaf order; an identical pair → empty). Two design choices made as they landed, both faithful to [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) → The deterministic transform (1. Schema-diff): **(a)** a section-level `<<slot>>` is **anonymous** in the `Schema` model (`SectionBody::Simple { slot: Option<Slot> }` — no id), so `ProseNeeding` carries `leaf: Option<String>` — `None` names the section's own required slot, `Some(id)` a required-without-default field. **(b)** The design *defines* `prose-needing` as a new required slot/field **with no deterministic default**, so a newly-added **required field that carries a `default`/`set`** classifies to `AddedOptionalField` (the deterministic-add branch, not prose-needing) — this is the path the M34 Inc-3 schema-version stamp's `set` deriver rides (the branch-split; the *driver* + deriver are Inc-3, only the *classification* is here). Changes outside the four kinds (removed leaf, type change, narrowed card) are deliberately **not** classified — the conformance detector + transform gate adjudicate those.

### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-2 T2 landed: the net-new `fixed-slot→repeatable-with-default` write primitive (`write::promote_slot_to_repeatable`)

New `pub fn write::promote_slot_to_repeatable(old_schema, new_schema, source, section_id, title)` — the one structural transform with no prior primitive (`add_item` rejects a non-repeatable section). It promotes a section that is a simple `<<slot>>` under `old_schema` into the single-slot repeatable it is under `new_schema`, carrying the old slot prose **verbatim** as the **default first item** (`{#id}` minted from `title`, mirroring `add_item`'s mint-site guard). Proven by its own proptest + unit tests only (no existing test touched): (a) `render(parse(out)) == out` byte-stable, (b) the v1 slot prose survives identically as the first item's slot. Two elaboration pins, scoping the primitive for the T3 driver: **(a)** single-slot only — the new item-template must have **exactly one** slot leaf (`title` id-from + one `<<slot>>`, the reconstructed `prd.requirements` shape); a multi-slot/slot-less target has no deterministic prose mapping and returns `WrongShape` (a separate classified change). **(b)** the post-item separator is **derived** from following-section presence (`\n\n` before a `## `, `\n` at EOF), *not* re-attached from the region tail — because a **simple** empty-slot body carries one extra trailing `\n` vs the canonical repeatable form (`## H\n\n\n` vs `## H\n\n`), debris `add_item`'s analogous branch never meets (it only inserts into already-canonical repeatable bodies).

### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-2 T3 landed: the deterministic transform driver + the reconstructed-shape e2e (`transform::{transform, TransformError}`)

New `crates/engine/src/transform.rs`: `transform(old_schema, new_schema, source, &[SchemaChange]) -> Result<String, TransformError>` — the driver consumes T1's classified diff and folds byte-stable splices over the v0-shaped source, **no LLM in the structural path**. Two structural branches built (the two with no live case, provable only synthetically): `fixed-slot→repeatable-with-default` (via T2's `promote_slot_to_repeatable`) and `widened-cardinality` (an instance-byte **identity** transform — the existing value stays valid under the widened card, so no splice). The reconstructed-shape **engine e2e** replays the M25 `prd.requirements` reshape and a synthetic widened-cardinality reshape on v0-shaped instances, asserting per-instance: byte-stable round-trip (`render(parse(out))==out`), no-data-loss (every prior slot/field value preserved), conformance against the v2 schema (`schema_conformance` clean), and determinism (re-run → identical bytes); the diff is fed from the real `schema_diff` classifier (driver exercised on the emitted classification, not a hand-built list). Two elaboration pins: **(a)** the `fixed-slot→repeatable` **default-item title is the section id** — a deterministic, domain-empty, always-slug-able source (the engine invents no prose; a human may rename the heading as an ordinary edit later). **(b)** the two deferred kinds **block, never silently drop** — `prose-needing` (T4) and `added-optional-field` (M34 Inc-3 stamp dogfood, branch-split) surface as `TransformError::Unsupported`, a typed error a later task replaces with the real branch. Files: `crates/engine/src/transform.rs` (new), `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`.

### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-2 T4 landed: the Framing-A prose-routing branch (`transform` mints a new required slot empty, blocks until authored)

The driver's `ProseNeeding { leaf: None }` branch (a new **required section slot**, no deterministic default) mints the slot **empty** at its schema-ordered home via the existing `write::generate_section(new_schema, out, section, Some(""), &[])` — the CLI owns only placement; it never authors the prose (the determinism boundary, `corpus-migration.md` → Prose routing). The reused **pure task-less** conformance gate (`validate::schema_conformance`, unchanged — `validate.rs` is reuse-only) then fires exactly one blocking `schema-conformance.required-slot-present` on the empty minted slot (blocks until authored); once the agent authors it via `write::set_slot`, the same gate passes clean and the doc round-trips byte-stable. Proven by one engine e2e (a synthetic v1→v2 adding a required `rationale` slot between two slots; diff fed from the real `schema_diff`): mint → gate blocks on the minted slot only → pre-existing slots survive (no-data-loss) → deterministic re-run → author via `set_slot` → gate clean + byte-stable. **Elaboration pin:** the transform's prose routing mints a **slot, not a field** — the `prose-needing` **field** sub-case (`leaf: Some`, a new required field with no default) has no shipped/reconstructed migration case, so its branch stays `TransformError::Unsupported` (un-built branch blocks loudly, never drops), to be built with its own test if a required-field migration is ever needed. Files: `crates/engine/src/transform.rs`.

### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-2 T5 landed: the per-doc-gated corpus fold + the rollback-inventory discipline (`transform::migrate_corpus`)

New `pub fn migrate_corpus(&[CorpusDoc]) -> CorpusMigration` lifts the single-instance `transform` to an **N-doc heterogeneous corpus** (each `CorpusDoc` owns its schema pair + classified diff — the mixed-doctype corpus the Inc-3 verb migrates), upholding *writes-are-transactional* at **per-doc** granularity: each doc is migrated in a **scratch buffer** then gated (re-parse under v2 + zero `schema_conformance` findings); only a clean gate commits `DocOutcome::Migrated`, anything else (a `TransformError`, a parse failure, or a non-empty gate — the `prose-needing` mint-empty that *blocks until authored*) rolls the scratch back to `DocOutcome::Untouched` (byte-identical v0) and **halts the run cleanly** at that doc (`halted_at`); docs after the halt are never touched (**halt-and-stop**, not skip-and-continue — the census "the rest stay at v1"). Proven by an engine e2e over N=4 where instance k=2 is `prose-needing`: docs before k transformed-and-conformant-v2 (round-trip byte-stable), docs at/after k byte-identical v0, no doc half-transformed, deterministic re-run. **Elaboration pin (Inc-2 detection limit):** in Inc-2 a migrated doc is "v2" by *conformance*, but a `fixed-slot→repeatable` / `widened-cardinality` v0 **coincidentally also conforms to v2** (the v2 repeatable accepts an empty form; widening accepts the old value), so conformance alone cannot distinguish migrated-from-unmigrated for those kinds — the post-halt structural doc's atomicity is therefore asserted by **bytes** (it differs from its would-be-migrated form), and the genuine "un-migrated-v0" re-detection rides the `prose-needing` doc (its v0 is truly non-conformant). This is exactly the limitation the **Inc-3 schema-version stamp** resolves (stamp-flips-last). **Rollback inventory pinned in the module doc-comment** (the M35-rename discipline, at *the increment that builds the transform*): a per-doc commit touches/rolls-back three things keyed by the one doc — **path** (the doc's own file, ≤1 per doc; rollback = discard scratch, zero on-disk residue), **file-state** (the `FileStateRecord` re-hash + the schema-version stamp that flips last; rollback = no re-hash/no flip → detector re-routes `migrate`), **index** (the doc's re-extracted edges; rollback = drop the working overlay, committed index untouched). Inc-2 builds the **in-memory** fold only; the on-disk write-back + stamp flip + actual rollback orchestration land in the Inc-3 verb that consumes this model. Files: `crates/engine/src/transform.rs`.

## 2026-06-25 — M34 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut "the in-schema schema-version stamp + the dogfood corpus migration (the loop end-to-end)" into **five ordered single-concern tasks** — the add-field transform branch (T1) → the in-schema stamp field + deriver + manifest re-freeze (T2) → version-aware detector routing (T3) → the user-facing corpus-migration verb + the live dogfood + worked-examples (T4) → rebuild/re-pin + measured facts (T5). *Why this cut:* the increment closes the detect→block→migrate loop end-to-end and retires productive-go **G2**, and its pieces sit on **serial gate-green seams** that each commit at a full unscoped green gate. Risk-first order puts the **net-new `added-optional-field` transform branch** (the branch deferred from Inc-2, currently `TransformError::Unsupported`, and the riskiest net-new piece — it needs a byte-stable field-insertion-into-a-header primitive) first and **isolated** (T1, synthetic engine e2e), before the schema-shape change that consumes it; the **stamp-field injection + all-fixture churn** (T2) is the second-riskiest and is **one atomic task** (see below). Every byte-mutating piece carries the byte-stability obligation (`render(parse(out))==out`). **Grounded against the code at `b00e17b`** (the Inc-2 terminus):

- **The stamp scope is the five *persisted* frozen doctypes — `adr`/`spec`/`prd`/`arch-doc`/`changelog`, never `commit`.** `commit` is transient (no `location:`, sink = the git message — `crates/cli/pack/schemas/commit.yaml:1`), and the detector + corpus walk already skip `location:`-less types (`validate.rs:521` `let Some(location) = … else { continue }`). Design says "every **persisted** doctype carries its authored-against version" (roadmap Inc-3 *Proves*; `storage.md:25`; `document-type-schema.md:193`) — so the stamp injects into the five persisted, `commit`'s git-message render stays stamp-free and its manifest hash unchanged (T2 verifies). Header state: `adr` (`status` header), `spec` (`meta` header from M33 `3c859c6`), `arch-doc` (`meta` header) take the stamp **into an existing `---` block**; `prd`/`changelog` render **zero** front-matter today (`prd.yaml`/`changelog.yaml` have no `header: true` section), so the stamp **introduces a `---` block** for those two — the v0→v1 shape change. (The `storage.md`/`document-type-schema.md` lines still listing `spec` among the header-less are stale pre-M33-Inc-2 — the roadmap is correct; `spec` adds to its existing block.)
- **The stamp completes v1; schema-version stays 1, the manifest *hashes* regenerate (no version bump).** The corpus pre-stamp is "v0" (no `schema-version` field); the migration stamps each doc the doctype's **current manifest version = 1** ("the corpus is stamped v1" — `corpus-migration.md:33,42`, roadmap "v0→v1"). The freeze gate (`engine::manifest::check`, `manifest.rs:139`) is **purely hash-based** — it compares recomputed-hash vs declared-hash + set membership, and **does not** enforce "hash changed ⇒ version bumped" — so T2 regenerating the five hashes at `schema-version: 1` passes the gate; the stamp is definitional of v1, not a v1→v2 transition (the one sanctioned manifest-hash regeneration, the manifest comment's "deliberate, versioned schema change"). The freeze test `shipped_schema_manifest_matches_the_frozen_doctype_set` (`pack.rs:1356`) asserts exactly-six + all-version-1 + every-hash-matches — it stays green over the regenerated hashes.
- **Inject at the production pack loader (`load_pack_schema`, `pack.rs:45`), not the raw engine `load_schema`.** `load_pack_schema` is the convergence point the freeze gate (`pack.rs:1370`), `ingest::load_schemas` (`ingest.rs:292`), and `CascadeDefs::all_schemas` thread through — injecting the stamp there makes the **gate-hash and every runtime schema read see the identical stamped schema** (no divergence). The engine's raw `load_schema` (which `arb_doc()` byte-stability fuzz + engine unit/transform tests use) stays **stamp-free**, so the M33 fuzz harness and the Inc-2 transform e2e are byte-unchanged — bounding T2's blast radius to CLI pack goldens + fixtures (T2 verifies both: `all_schemas` shares the injection; raw `load_schema` does not). The stamp **field declaration** originates engine-side (a single canonical source — "engine-injected uniformly"), applied by the pack loader to the persisted set.
- **The add-field value source: `field.default` (engine-resolvable) or a CLI-supplied derived value (for the stamp's `set` deriver).** `schema_diff::classify_added_field` (`schema_diff.rs:175`) already routes a field carrying `default` **or** `set` to `AddedOptionalField` (the stamp's `set` deriver rides this — shipped Inc-2 T1). `write::set_field` (`write.rs:957`) only *updates a present* field; an **absent** field (and an absent header for `prd`/`changelog`) is a **generation** concern — so T1's branch needs a byte-stable insert/generate-field-in-header primitive (sibling of the proven `generate_section`). The engine transform is **pure** (no clock, no manifest), so its add-field branch fills `field.default` directly and takes the `set`-deriver value from the caller; the **CLI** resolves "current active schema version" = the doctype's manifest `schema-version` (mirroring `doc.rs::today_iso` for dates) and supplies it. T1 proves the `default` path (engine e2e); T4's dogfood proves the `set`/stamp path on the real binary.
- **Version-aware routing reuses existing ids — no inventory growth.** The probe-response contract already carries a `route?` field (`validation.md:112`); `validation.md:301` settles "non-conformant + stamped **below** manifest version ⇒ *migrate*; at-version ⇒ *corrupt*", and `:299` pins "no new check id / knob / inventory growth" (the M33 store-family pattern). So T3 reads each doc's stamp vs the manifest version and labels the **existing** `schema-conformance.*` findings' route; `check_inventory_membership_count_is_stable` (`result.rs:1042`, 25 rows / 28 keyed) stays green (T3 verifies). A stamp-absent v0 doc routes `migrate`.
- **No new verb infra overlap.** `jigc migrate` is foreign-doc adoption (`migrate.rs`), `jigc upgrade` is pack-delta classification (`upgrade.rs`) — both disjoint from the schema-shape corpus transform (the Inc-2 branch-split confirmed zero CLI callers of `transform`/`migrate_corpus`). T4's verb is net-new, consuming `migrate_corpus`; its name/surface (`corpus-migration.md` → Open questions: "settled at the increment that builds it") is the executor's to spell, but the **shape is settled** (consume `migrate_corpus` → write-back per-doc → stamp-flips-last → Framing-A prose route → conformance gate). Done-criterion throughout: the named new test green + the full dev-workflow gate (`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`); T4/T5 add real-binary acceptance. Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M34 Increment 3; design [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md) (the stamp; the transform's add-field branch) + [storage.md](design/storage.md) / [document-type-schema.md](design/document-type-schema.md) (the field) + [validation.md](design/validation.md) (version-aware routing).

- **T1 — the `added-optional-field` transform driver branch (the branch-split's deferred branch) + its byte-stable field-insertion primitive.** Replace the `transform()` `AddedOptionalField => Err(TransformError::Unsupported)` arm (`transform.rs:171`) with the real splice: insert the added field at its schema-ordered home, **generating the header section** when the doctype has none (the `prd`/`changelog` shape), sourcing the value from `field.default` else a caller-supplied derived value (the `set`-deriver path). Add the net-new write primitive it needs (an insert/generate-field-in-header sibling of `write::generate_section`, byte-stable by construction). *Done:* an engine e2e replays a synthetic `added-field` over v0-shaped instances on **both** shapes — adding a defaulted header field to a doctype that **already has a header**, and to one that has **none** (introducing the `---` block) — asserting each output (a) round-trips byte-identical (`render(parse(out))==out`), (b) conforms under v2 (`schema_conformance` clean), (c) preserves every prior slot/field value (no-data-loss), and (d) is deterministic, with **no LLM** in the path; the diff is fed from the real `schema_diff`. The existing `deferred_kinds_surface_as_unsupported` test is updated so `added-optional-field` no longer asserts `Unsupported` (the `prose-needing` **field** sub-case stays `Unsupported`); full gate green. **Pin:** this is the *engine* branch only — the stamp's live `set`-deriver value + the real corpus run land in T4 (the dogfood). ### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-3 T1 landed: the `added-optional-field` transform driver branch + the fence-introducing header-field primitive

Replaced `transform()`'s `AddedOptionalField => Err(Unsupported)` arm (`transform.rs`) with a real splice (`apply_added_field`): the added field is materialized at its schema-ordered home carrying its schema **`default`** value — a **header** field via `write::insert_front_matter_field`, a **body** field via `write::insert_field`. Proven by two engine e2e on the real `schema_diff` over v0-shaped instances — a defaulted header field into a doctype that **already has a `---` header**, and into a **header-less** doctype (introducing the fence) — each asserting byte-stable round-trip (`render(parse(out))==out`), v2 conformance (`schema_conformance` clean), no-data-loss (every prior field/slot value survives), and determinism; no LLM in the path. **Design elaboration (the primitive):** the planner's "set_field:957 only updates / a new generate-field-in-header primitive is needed" was reconciled against the code — `write::insert_front_matter_field` **already** inserts an absent field into a present `---` block (incl. the empty fence pair); the genuine gap was the **header-less** case, so I **extended that primitive** to *introduce* the `---` fence (byte-identical to `render`'s `---\n<bare-fields>---\n\n` header) when the source carries no front-matter at all, rather than adding a parallel primitive (avoids two header-emit paths that could byte-drift). **Value-resolution policy (the three add-field sub-cases):** `default` present ⇒ insert; **`optional:` with no default** ⇒ byte **no-op** (its absence already conforms — the widened-cardinality sibling, the design table's "add optional field" with nothing deterministic to place), proven by `added_optional_field_with_no_default_is_a_byte_no_op`; a **`set`-derived field with no default** (the schema-version stamp) ⇒ still `TransformError::Unsupported` here — its value is the deriver's, threaded in by **T4** (this is the *engine* branch only, per the branch-split). `deferred_kinds_surface_as_unsupported` updated: `added-optional-field` no longer asserts `Unsupported`; the `prose-needing` **field** sub-case still does. ### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-3 T3 landed: version-aware migrate-vs-corrupt routing in the store-scope schema-conformance detector

Extended `validate::schema_conformance_store` (the Inc-1 fifth content family) to **label** each non-conformant committed doc's `schema-conformance.*` finding with a version-aware `route`, reusing the existing `Finding.route` field — **no new check id/knob/inventory row** (`result.rs` → `check_inventory_membership_count_is_stable` stays 25). The detector now reads each doc's per-doc schema-version stamp (`read_schema_version_stamp` over the parsed header, the T2 `SCHEMA_VERSION_FIELD` leaf) and compares it to the doctype's manifest version: **stamp-absent (the v0 corpus state) or below ⇒ `migrate`** (a known-old doc the transform can upgrade); **at-version + non-conformant ⇒ `corrupt`** (human review). The route string **leads with the classification** (`migrate`/`corrupt`) so it is both a human-readable repair direction and a stable machine token the renderer emits verbatim. **Report-only at store scope** (exit 0 unchanged — the blocking counterpart is the transform-transaction migration gate, never this read-only sweep). **Elaboration pins:** (1) the "current version" is threaded in as a `versions: &BTreeMap<String,u32>` param on `validate_store_families`, built CLI-side by new `pack::frozen_doctype_versions` (reads `schema-manifest.yaml` via `origin_pack`, the `frozen_doctype_set` sibling) — the engine stays domain-empty (no baked version). (2) **Routing is scoped to versioned doctypes**: a doctype the caller supplies no manifest version for (`current = None`, e.g. a non-freeze pack → empty map) leaves its findings **un-routed** (reported, never mislabeled, never an error) — the omitting-context inert path, unit-tested by `route_is_inert_when_no_manifest_version`. (3) Inlined the store half of `conformance_for` so the route reads the stamp from the same parse the conformance checks run over (single parse; `unknown-type` can't fire — the type comes from schema iteration). Proven by `crates/cli/tests/schema_conformance_routing.rs` (real `jigc validate` binary: 2×migrate + 1×corrupt route lines over a 3-ADR shadowed store, exit 0; conformant store clean+unrouted) + engine units on `route_schema_conformance`. Files: `crates/engine/src/validate.rs`, `crates/cli/src/pack.rs`, `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/schema_conformance_routing.rs`.

### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-3 T2 landed: the in-schema schema-version stamp (engine-declared, pack-loader-injected) + the current-active-version deriver + manifest re-freeze

Injected the engine-declared per-doc `schema-version` stamp field into every **persisted frozen** doctype at the CLI schema-load convergence point. **Engine side** (`schema.rs`): `schema_version_stamp_field()` declares the stamp **shape only** — `{ id: schema-version, type: int, set: schema-version }`, **version-independent** (no baked value), so a doctype's `schema_hash` stays a pure shape fingerprint and a future v→v+1 bump moves the hash only via the real shape change; `inject_schema_version_stamp(&mut Schema)` appends it to the existing header (`adr`/`spec`/`arch-doc`) or **creates a header section first** for the header-less two (`prd`/`changelog` thereby gain a `---` block — the header must be the document's first section, `parse.rs` → header-first), idempotent on a re-inject. **CLI side** (`pack.rs`): `load_pack_schema` gates injection on `location.is_some()` **and** membership in the pack's freeze manifest (`frozen_doctype_set`, read from `config/schema-manifest.yaml` via `origin_pack`) — so the transient `commit` (in the manifest, no location) and any non-frozen doctype (the methodology pack ships no manifest) stay **inert**; the bare engine `load_schema` (and `arb_doc()` fuzz) is untouched (stamp-free). **The deriver** (`doc.rs`): `current_schema_version() -> u32` (the version analog of `today_iso`) materialized by a new branch in `on_create_block_field` keyed on the `set: schema-version` marker — so `jigc doc create`/`author` of a persisted doctype stamps `schema-version: 1`. **Elaboration pins:** (1) the deriver yields the single active version **1** for the whole frozen v1 set (every frozen doctype is at v1); it becomes doctype-aware when a doctype first advances past v1 (the future migration extends it) — stamping 1 now is correct and durable (a v1 doc *is* v1, no later rewrite), so the constant is minimal-*correct*, not debt. (2) The stamp is **not** migration-suppressed (unlike the on-create date): a freshly-adopted foreign doc is genuinely authored against the current version, never false history. **Manifest re-freeze:** regenerated the five persisted `schema-hash` entries in `schema-manifest.yaml` (versions stay 1); `commit`'s hash is **unchanged** (exclusion verified). The freeze gate `shipped_schema_manifest_matches_the_frozen_doctype_set` passes; a new `load_pack_schema_stamps_persisted_frozen_doctypes_and_is_inert_elsewhere` locks the inject contract incl. the omitting-context inert cases (`commit` + a non-frozen `note`); every affected CLI fixture/round-trip helper now injects the stamp to mirror the binary. Files: `crates/engine/src/schema.rs`, `crates/cli/src/pack.rs`, `crates/cli/src/doc.rs`, `crates/cli/pack/config/schema-manifest.yaml`, `crates/cli/tests/` (18 files).

## 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-3 T4 build halt resolved: version-mismatch is an *emitted* conformance break, not just a route over pre-existing findings

The build halted at Inc-3 T4 on a real cross-doc tension. T3 implemented "version-aware routing" as a **labeler** — `route_schema_conformance` annotates `schema-conformance.*` findings that `schema_conformance()` already produced (validate.rs:600). But the schema-version stamp is `set:`-derived, so `is_author_required` exempts it (validate.rs:1476): a committed doc that **lacks** the stamp (the v0 corpus) or carries it **below** the manifest version is otherwise **fully conformant** → produces no finding → the labeler has nothing to annotate → `jigc validate` stays exit 0. The **pure-stamp v0 corpus is the M34 dogfood**, which has *no other* non-conformance — so the detect-half was silent for its own headline case.

**Resolution (design-determined, not a guess): version-mismatch is itself a surfaced break.** corpus-migration.md's property census (:95) already lists `version-mismatch` among the breaks the fifth family fires "the right `schema-conformance.*` finding" on, and :51/:102 require `jigc validate` to *report* a stranded corpus. validation.md's "Version-aware routing" prose was the under-specified doc ("a *non-conformant* instance stamped below routes migrate" — annotation), so the build faithfully built a labeler. Reconciled validation.md to the census + the dogfood requirement: the fifth family **emits** a `schema-conformance.*` finding when a committed doc's stamp is absent or below its doctype's manifest version, even when structurally clean — emission, not annotation, is what closes the silent-drift hole. The build read the labeler prose; the vision (the detect-half exists to catch a stranded corpus; a below-version stamp *is* the strand) settles it toward emission.

**Mechanism pins (kept minimal, honoring the existing design pins):** reuse an existing `schema-conformance.*` id (no new check id, no knob, `check_inventory` stays 28 — corpus-migration.md:51-52); **`is_author_required` untouched** — the stamp stays author-exempt, version-currency is a *store-scope corpus* rule, not an authoring obligation (so finalize/task scope is unaffected — a task only ever touches at-version docs the on-create deriver already stamped); store-scope only, report-only exit 0. The fix amends the T2/T3 engine layer (outside T4's CLI-only scope), so it lands as a fixer commit before the build resumes at T4. validation.md amended; corpus-migration.md already correct (census + :51). The on-create deriver already stamps created docs at the current version, so created docs stay conformant — only the pre-stamp v0 corpus is surfaced (correctly, as `migrate`).

### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-3 T4 landed: the user-facing `jigc migrate-corpus` verb + the live v0→v1 stamp dogfood + stamp-flips-last

New `crates/cli/src/migrate_corpus.rs` (verb `jigc migrate-corpus`) consuming `engine::transform::migrate_corpus` (Inc-2 T5): it builds the frozen persisted doctypes' v0→v1 jobs from the pack (`from` = the current shape minus the engine stamp, `to` = the stamp-injected shape, `version` = the doctype's manifest schema-version), walks the committed store, and per-doc applies the **real schema-diff** (the live `added-optional-field` stamp) → gates on conformance against v1 → writes back **only on a clean gate**, re-baselining an already-tracked doc's file-state hash. **Stamp value source (pin):** the stamp field is `set:`-derived with no static `default`, so the transform's add-field branch has no value to place; T4 threads the manifest version in as the field `default` (`with_stamp_default`) so the splice is deterministic — the verb supplies the deriver value, the engine stays domain-empty. **Per-doc diff vs fixed diff (pin):** the doctype diff is computed once but **filtered per doc** — the stamp add-field is kept iff the doc lacks the stamp, a prose-needing slot iff the doc lacks that heading (`has_section_heading`, the parser's `slugify(heading)==id` inverse) — so an already-authored doc flips cleanly on a re-run rather than re-minting an existing section (`GenerateError::AlreadyPresent`). **Stamp-flips-last** falls out of the engine fold's per-doc rollback: a combined stamp + prose-needing change mints an empty slot that fails the gate, so the whole scratch (stamp included) rolls back — the doc stays byte-identical v0, unstamped, routed to the agent (Framing A); once authored, a re-run flips the stamp. Real-binary acceptance (`crates/cli/tests/corpus_migration.rs`): the v0 ADR dogfood loop detect→migrate→re-validate clean + the already-current no-op; verb-core coverage (`migrate_corpus.rs` tests) for the header-less fence-introducing case + the combined stamp-flips-last case (no such combined change exists in the frozen-v1 dev pack, so it rides synthetic doctypes through the same core). Disjoint from `jigc migrate` (foreign adoption) and `jigc upgrade` (config). worked-examples.md flow 35. Files: `crates/cli/src/migrate_corpus.rs` (new), `cli.rs`, `main.rs`, `render.rs`, `design/worked-examples.md`.

## 2026-06-25 — M34 audit triage: freeze-discipline reading (Finding 3) — v1 crystallizes across the M33+M34 pair

The M34 completion audit flagged (low, high-confidence) that the stamp injection changed all five persisted frozen doctype `schema-hash`es while each `schema-version` stayed **1** (the doctype YAML was not edited — the shape change is the engine `inject_schema_version_stamp`). Read literally, the CLAUDE.md invariant ("no schema-shape change to a frozen-v1 doctype ships without bumping `schema-version`") makes M34 look self-violating. **Disposition (user-confirmed): sanctioned v0→v1 completion, clarify the invariant.** The M33+M34 pair was always planned as a coupled unit that *jointly* completes v1 ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-06-24 M33+M34 paired; the "completing v1 — the five schema-engine opens" of [corpus-migration.md](design/corpus-migration.md)): M33 froze an interim shape; M34 completes v1 by adding the stamp, shipping the stamp's own v0→v1 corpus migration alongside. So the hash evolving under version 1 across the pair is the baseline *establishing* itself, not an un-versioned post-freeze change. Clarified the CLAUDE.md freeze invariant so it reads correctly: **the v1 baseline crystallizes across the M33+M34 pair, and the version-gate binds *after* that** (every later v1→v2 shape change needs the bump + migration). Doc-only; the freeze gate + `freeze_enforcement` tests are unchanged and green.

## 2026-06-25 — M34 audit triage: Findings 1+2 → build it now as Inc 4 (prior-schema sourcing); storage = versioned snapshot files

The M34 completion audit's headline finding (1, medium): the shipped `jigc migrate-corpus` hardcodes `from = strip_stamp(current)`, so its schema-diff can only ever emit the stamp add-field — the structural transform branches (`fixed-slot→repeatable` / `widened-cardinality` / `prose-needing`), built + unit-proven since Inc 2, are **unreachable through the verb for a real case**. Finding 2 (low) is the same root: a present-but-below stamp is dropped (add-field can't value-bump), so the detector routes `migrate` while the verb says `already-current`. **Disposition (user-confirmed): build it now** as **M34 Inc 4**, rather than defer — the freeze's promise (bounded migration cost) is hollow if the verb can't reach the structural path for a real v1→v2, so G2 retirement moves from Inc 3 to Inc 4.

**The gating one-way-door decision — prior-schema sourcing.** The schema-diff needs two real `Schema` values; a v1→v2 structural change's prior shape is *not* derivable from the current schema, so the pack must **store prior shapes**. The determinism boundary mandates this be *real declared schemas* the engine diffs (not hand-written migration recipes — corpus-migration.md → the transform). **Storage (user-confirmed): a dedicated `schema-snapshots/<type>.v<N>.yaml` pack resource kind**, each snapshot a full reviewable schema file — chosen over a single nested `config/` archive because it honors the "plain, diff-friendly files" invariant and keeps the determinism boundary in its strongest form (the alternative trades a bounded enum-variant ripple for nested-YAML authoring friction). It lives **outside `schemas/`** by necessity (the freeze gate enumerates `schemas/` by doctype and would collide). The verb sources `from` per committed doc by stamp (absent → `strip_stamp(current)`, the unchanged Inc-3 path; `k<current` → snapshot `vk`; missing → blocked-with-route). The stamp **value-bump** (`write::set_field`) handles the v1→v2 transition and closes the Finding-2 divergence. **Snapshot hashing deferred** (user-confirmed): a drifted snapshot fails the transform/round-trip loudly, so a second hash gate is premature; revisit when a real v1→v2 ships and the snapshot set grows. **Acceptance:** the reconstructed M25 `prd.requirements` fixed-slot→repeatable, driven end-to-end through the compiled binary via the `JIGC_PACK_DIR` `FilesystemPack` seam. The engine substrate is already built (Inc 2) — Inc 4 wires the sourcing seam + the bump + the binary proof. Settled in corpus-migration.md (Prior-schema sourcing; resolves the :111 "manifest home + format" open + the :103 migrate-flow overstatement the audit flagged) + roadmap.md (Inc 4).

## 2026-06-25 — M34 Increment 4 planning: decomposition

Cut "prior-schema sourcing + the verb's structural-migration path (G2)" into **four ordered single-concern tasks** — the `schema-snapshots` resource kind + `load_prior_schema` reader (T1) → the per-doc `from`-selection-by-stamp + stamp value-bump rework of the verb (T2) → the reconstructed v1→v2 acceptance through the compiled binary + worked-examples (T3) → rebuild/re-pin + measured facts (T4). *Why this cut:* the increment makes the already-built structural transform branches reachable through the shipped `jigc migrate-corpus` for a real v1→v2 and retires productive-go **G2**, and its pieces sit on serial gate-green seams (a clean producer→consumer: T1 ships the snapshot reader, T2 consumes it). **Grounded against the code at `701238a`** (the Inc-3 terminus + the M33 completion fix). Risk-first within a thin increment: the **enum-variant ripple + the loader** (T1) is isolated first; the **verb rework** (T2 — the Finding-1/2 fix) is the second-riskiest; the real-binary proof (T3) lands last before release (T4).

- **No engine change — verified, not assumed.** `schema_diff` (all four kinds), `transform`, `migrate_corpus` (the per-doc-gated fold), and `promote_slot_to_repeatable` are all built and unit/e2e-proven (Inc-2, `crates/engine/src/{schema_diff,transform,write}.rs`); the reconstructed `prd.requirements` fixed-slot→repeatable is *already* an engine e2e (`transform.rs::fixed_slot_to_repeatable_e2e_replays_the_prd_requirements_reshape`). Inc-4 is **CLI-only**: the snapshot kind (engine `PackResourceKind` variant is a pure-data enum add, no engine logic), the loader, and the verb's sourcing/bump rework.
- **`load_prior_schema` MUST parse through `load_pack_schema`** (`pack.rs:45`, verified) so the snapshot resolves pack field-types **and** gets the schema-version stamp injected **identically** to the current schema. Consequence (verified by reading `load_pack_schema`): for a v1→v2 the stamp is present in **both** `from` (snapshot) and `to` (current), so `schema_diff` emits **only** the structural change, never a spurious stamp add-field — the stamp transition is a **value-bump**, not an add-field. This is *why* the value-bump (T2) is a distinct mechanism from the v0→v1 add-field path.
- **The `PackResourceKind::SchemaSnapshots` variant ripple is bounded to one exhaustive match.** The only exhaustive `match kind` across the workspace is `kind_dir` (`pack.rs:210`); `EmbeddedPack`/`FilesystemPack`/`CompositePack` `read`/`list` are generic over kind, and the engine `TestPack` is HashMap-keyed (no match). The variant also joins the `KINDS` content-hash array (`packsource.rs:215`) so snapshots are provenance-complete — byte-neutral today (no shipped pack ships snapshots, so no `--explain`/provenance golden moves). Snapshot file `<type>.v<N>.yaml` → `file_stem()` = `<type>.v<N>` → `ResourceId`; `load_prior_schema(pack, ty, version)` reads id `format!("{ty}.v{version}")`.
- **The freeze gate does NOT fire on the migrate-corpus path** (`assert_schema_freeze` is called only in `compose_drained`, `start.rs:753` — verified), so the T3 fixture pack's manifest `schema-hash`es need not match its shipped schemas; `migrate-corpus` reads only `frozen_doctype_versions` (the version map, best-effort). The fixture just needs internally-consistent **version numbers** (prd at manifest version 2). This de-risks the reconstructed-case acceptance.
- **The verb's existing `with_stamp_default` add-field path stays** for the **stamp-absent (v0→v1)** doc — `from = strip_stamp(current)`, the add-field branch fills the stamp from the threaded `default` (the unchanged Inc-3 dogfood). The **below-version (v1→v2)** doc takes the new path: `from` = snapshot `vk`, the structural change applied by the fold, the stamp **value-bumped** `k`→current by `write::set_field` (`write.rs:957`, verified — splices a *present* field's value byte-stably). Done-criterion throughout: the named new test green + the full unscoped gate (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo build`). - **T1 — the `schema-snapshots` pack resource kind + `load_prior_schema(pack, ty, version)`.** Add `PackResourceKind::SchemaSnapshots` to `engine/src/packsource.rs` (the variant + its `KINDS` content-hash entry), its `kind_dir` arm `"schema-snapshots"` in `pack.rs`, and `load_prior_schema(pack, ty, version) -> Result<Schema, _>` reading the `SchemaSnapshots` resource id `<ty>.v<version>` and parsing it through `load_pack_schema` (field-types + stamp injection identical to the current schema). *Done:* a unit test where a `FilesystemPack` over a fixture dir carrying `schema-snapshots/prd.v1.yaml` (the fixed-slot prior shape) returns the parsed prior `Schema` via `load_prior_schema(pack, "prd", 1)` with field-types resolved and the stamp injected (asserted equal to the same schema run through `load_pack_schema`); a **missing** snapshot (`prd.v9`) is a **located error**, not a panic (the parser hostile-input pass, increment-workflow #3); `kind_dir`/`EmbeddedPack`/`CompositePack` and their existing tests stay green; full gate green. **Pin:** `load_prior_schema`'s only non-test caller is the T2 verb (a clean producer→consumer seam, like Inc-2 T2's `promote_slot_to_repeatable`); it is wired to production in T2 (so not test-only at increment end).
