### 2026-06-25 — M34 Inc-4 T2 landed: per-doc `from`-selection by stamp + the stamp value-bump (the Finding-1/2 fix)
Reworked `migrate_committed_corpus` to resolve each committed doc's prior shape `from` **by its schema-version stamp**: stamp-absent → `strip_stamp(to)` (the unchanged Inc-3 add-field path); below-version `k<current` → the `schema-snapshots/<ty>.v<k>.yaml` snapshot via `load_prior_schema` (so the structural transform branches are now reachable through the verb for a real v1→v2) + the stamp **value-bumped** `k→current`; a missing snapshot → **blocked with a route**, never silent `already-current` (closing the Inc-3 detector/verb divergence — Finding 2). `DoctypeMigration` drops its per-doctype `from` field; the in-module tests were updated in the same motion (the signature change forced it). **Elaboration pin — the value-bump is POST-fold, not pre-fold:** a committed doc still at its prior shape (e.g. fixed-slot) does not conform to `to`, and an already-prose-authored below-version doc does not conform to `from`, so neither schema bumps the *source* universally; the **gated v2** always conforms to `to`, so `bump_and_regate(to, v2, version)` runs over it (the planner offered pre/post-fold — post-fold is the only one that holds across both shapes). RED proved the bump's necessity (with it disabled the structural change lands but the stamp stays `1`). Detector/verb agreement is the verb-side commitment (below-version ⇒ migrated) over the engine route already proven in `tests/schema_conformance_routing.rs`. Files: `crates/cli/src/migrate_corpus.rs`. Full gate green.

## 2026-06-25 — Planning hardened from the M34 retrospective: the cheap-vs-robust gate is adjudicated by an independent advocate, never self-framed (+ deliverable-reachable, + triage scope)

The M34 retrospective exposed that the `cheap-vs-robust` gate **existed, cited M33, and still did not bind** — because the **proposer (the orchestrator) administered *and framed* it**. At completion-triage the orchestrator recommended deferring M34's *declared* structural-migration deliverable (hollow: the shipped verb hardcoded `from = strip_stamp(to)`, reaching only the stamp add-field), strawmanned the robust fix as "premature generality against a hypothetical," and the human gate decided on that biased framing — the human had to override. A gate the biased party both runs and frames does not constrain the bias. Three binding fixes, following the established accretion discipline (new lesson = a gate-row + a one-line rationale pointer, not inline sprawl):

- **The independent robust-case advocate** — a new `robust-advocate` agent ([.claude/agents/robust-advocate.md](.claude/agents/robust-advocate.md), the sibling of `gap-detector`/`design-reviewer`). For **any** cheap-vs-robust fork — at plan-time *Settle* OR completion-*triage* — the orchestrator must spawn it to argue the vision-robust case at full strength **before** surfacing the fork, so the human decides between two honestly-argued cases, never the proposer's lone cheap recommendation. One-sided by design (the proposer already made the cheap case), with an honesty bound (if the cheap cut genuinely is minimal-correct, say so). Wired as a forcing function into both orchestration surfaces: [the `/milestone-plan` command](.claude/commands/milestone-plan.md) → Settle, and [milestone-build.js](.claude/workflows/milestone-build.js) → the post-audit triage message.
- **`deliverable-reachable`** (new gate-row) — each capability the milestone *declares as its deliverable* must be reachable **end-to-end through the shipped user-facing surface** (verb/CLI/adapter), not only the engine/tests: *built + unit-tested ≠ delivered* if the shipped surface can't invoke it. M34 decomposed the structural transform as "engine built + unit-tested" and called it done, leaving the declared corpus-migration surface hollow; the audit caught it but triage then deferred it.
- **`cheap-vs-robust` now fires at completion-triage, not only plan-time**, with two rationalizations explicitly **barred**: *"no live/production case to test"* ≠ *"not needed"* (a reconstructed/synthetic case proves a now-needed capability — exactly how M34 Inc-4 then proved the structural path), and *"premature generality"* holds only if the trajectory doesn't commit.

Encoded canonically in [methodology-docs.md](design/methodology-docs.md) → the gate-record (the `cheap-vs-robust` row amended, `deliverable-reachable` added, the advocate mechanism), with the worked instance + gate-list in [milestone-planning-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md), the triage gate in [milestone-completion-workflow.md](implementation/milestone-completion-workflow.md), and the forcing functions in the command + workflow. (Pack-encoded enforcement rides the same deferral as the rest of the gate-record — run by hand until the planning workflow is pack-encoded.)

## 2026-06-28 — M35 planning (CLI-owned rename — the cost-win differentiator)

Planned via the [milestone-planning workflow](implementation/milestone-planning-workflow.md) (scope → capability-audit baseline → 4-dimension gap pass → settle → review → decompose). Baseline exercised at HEAD `451a14f`; the gap pass + two independent `robust-advocate` briefs (OOB-backstop, rollback) drove the forks. The eight mechanism opens from [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md) → `(D) CLI-owned rename mechanism` are **graduated** here. The *why*: own the rename as a deterministic, transaction-bound CLI op so jigc is **cheaper per rename** than an agent hand-chasing referrers (the differentiator the cross-doc study said *detection* couldn't prove — [cross-doc VERDICT](completions/artifacts/cross-doc-refint-study/VERDICT.md)).

- **Verb surface = one top-level `jigc rename`, retitle+reslug+repoint unified in one call.** `jigc rename <old-slug> --to "<New Title>"` → new slug = `slugify("<New Title>")` (reuses `engine::slug::slugify`, the create-path slugifier — so a renamed doc is byte-identical to a freshly-created one of that title) · rewrites the moved doc's H1 to the new title · repoints **every persisted referrer** old→new · `git mv` · **one atomic commit**. `--to` is **required**; `--slug <explicit>` (only with `--to`) overrides the derived slug. *Degenerate-case (pinned at review, I2):* a collision check excludes the doc's own slug, and a **no-op reslug** (the new title slugs to the doc's current slug — identity unchanged) **degrades to a retitle-only** (rewrite H1 + commit, no `git mv`, no repoint) — so one command always "makes the title right" and moves identity only when the slug actually changes. *Why one command, not rename + retitle:* the agent's natural act is "this decision is now about X" — splitting forces it to learn two verbs and sequence them; one call gets everything right. *Why top-level, not `jigc doc rename`:* every `doc` verb is task-scoped (writes a working area, promoted at finalize); rename is **task-less + self-committing**, like the other top-level direct-store ops (`unmanage`, `migrate-corpus`). The identity-stable **retitle-*without*-reslug** case the invariant preserves stays on the existing in-task title-edit path (id frozen) — it doesn't need this verb.
- **Identity-model invariant amended (the one-way door — engaged, not bent).** Storage's "identity *is* the path / minted ids frozen / survives a retitle" is **revised**: *IDs are stable under **reorder** and **ordinary retitle-without-reslug**; an identity change (slug/path) is allowed **only** through one explicit, atomic CLI op (`jigc rename`) — never an untracked move.* Reference-*integrity* survives a rename (every referrer repointed in lockstep); identity-*stability* does not (that is the point). The invariant's *intent* (cross-refs never dangle under structural change) is preserved; its *mechanism* moves from immutability to atomic CLI refactoring. **Diff-legibility improves** (a slug that tracks its title beats one frozen out of sync); the **opaque-ID-indirection alternative is rejected** (it would trade away the content-slug legibility). Promoted into the **six** frozen-slug sites the prior-art-reconciliation hunt found, not the charter's three: [VISION.md](VISION.md) §2 + honest-boundary, [storage.md](design/storage.md), [structural-grammar.md](design/structural-grammar.md), [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) invariant bullet, [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md), [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md).
- **OOB-rename backstop = A + B (full robust; robust-advocate adjudicated).** Today (verified) the backstop is hollow: `detect_rename` is wired only at task scope, `detect_committed_store` walks present-docs-only, and `ref_resolves_store` is report-only — so a referrer-less out-of-band `git mv` is **silently exit-0** at store scope. **A:** wire the recorded-missing enumeration + `detect_rename` into the store-scope sweep, with the actionable *"adopt as `jigc rename`"* route, firing **before** `ref-resolves`. *Dedup = scope-subtraction (pinned at review, I1):* the renamed slug's inbound edges are excluded from `ref_resolves_store` for that sweep, so an OOB move-with-referrers surfaces **one** `reconciliation.rename`, **zero** dangling-ref findings for those edges, while `jigc validate` still reports every *other* dangling ref (no short-circuit). **B:** the OOB-rename structural-integrity finding is **blocking / exit-flipping** at store scope and the warn-only pre-commit hook **blocks the commit** on it. *Engaging the M18/M19 report-only-store-sweep + warn-only-hook rationale (record-is-rebuttable):* that stance exists so the sweep never gates on **pre-existing, unrelated content rot** (the masking-trap — a task blocked by drift it didn't cause). An OOB rename is a **structural-identity corruption introduced *by this commit***, not pre-existing content drift — so blocking it is **consistent with** that rationale, and joins the `pack-probe-integrity.*` exit-flipping exception class. *Scoping mechanism (pinned at review, B1 — without it the masking-trap returns):* the hook intersects `detect_rename` hits with **this commit's staged path-status set** (`git diff --cached --name-status`, R/D/A) and **blocks only** when the rename's old+new paths are both staged; a rename hit *outside* the staged set (a pre-existing OOB move left in the tree) is **reported (warn, exit 0)**, never blocked. General content `ref-resolves` stays report-only.
- **Transaction = full pre-image-capture rollback, its own boundary (robust-advocate adjudicated).** Rename mutates committed paths + file-state + edge index directly, so it is **not** under finalize's boundary; the migrate-corpus *no-rollback / idempotent-rerun* model is **rejected** — rename is not idempotent-safe (its re-run keys on `<old>`, which the `git mv` already destroyed, so a half-done rename can't resume and leaves the exact dangling-ref violation M35 prevents). A new `rollback_rename` captures pre-image bytes of the old path + every referrer, mutates, **re-baselines `file-state` (inside the transaction, not best-effort post-commit — pinned at review, I3)** + rebuilds the index, `git mv`, runs the user's git hooks (never `--no-verify` — the M31 commit-path property), commits; on **any** pre-commit failure restores all captured bytes + the `git mv` + **the file-state record**. *Post-commit interruption is self-healing:* the committed tree is authoritative — a committed doc at a new path whose recorded old path is absent from the tree is **re-baseline-adopted as the rename's landing**, never routed to the weak-signal "restore the old file" (which would resurrect a renamed-away doc). Reuses finalize's F3 captured-bytes idiom + `git restore --staged --worktree` + `path_at_head` + `existing_pathspecs` — net-new is ~one function + the crash-window recovery rule (a build RED obligation).
- **Referrer census = all 3 persisted ref-fields**, not the charter's "supersedes/cites": `adr.supersedes`, `arch-doc.cites`, **`spec.derived-from → prd`** (a prd rename dangles spec refs the named pair would miss). `commit.implements → spec` is transient (git-history only) → **report, never rewrite**. Both `supersedes` (widened `0..*` at M25) and `cites` are list-valued → rename must parse-list → swap-member → re-emit the canonical whole-list (the byte-stable splice is per-field-value, not per-element). Methodology doctypes carry no ref-fields → out of scope.
- **`--to` collision blocks** (an identity refactor of an existing doc, never the by-task-id join's silent-suffix); domain = an existing committed slug in the target doctype's cascade-resolved location.
- **Forbidden mid-fan-out = coarse guard, over tasks *and* milestones (extended at review, I4).** Block `jigc rename` whenever **any task working area *or* milestone** is in-flight (keyed on the `.jigc/tasks/` + un-finalized milestone-dir markers, which cover docs-only fan-outs *and* single-task `edited-from-base` doc copies the worktree/tree-clean signal is blind to). A rename changes the by-task-id join's same-doc-clash key, and a task working area holding an old-slug copy would promote stale at its finalize; coarse is both simpler and safer for an identity op.
- **No freeze interaction (recorded clean).** Rename is pure data-value + path + cache mutation; `schema_hash` hashes the Schema *struct*, never instance bytes. **Guardrail:** the verb adds **no persisted doctype field** (no `renamed-from`/alias) — that is the only way it could cross the v1 freeze. Each doc's `schema-version` stamp is **preserved, not flipped** (rename is not a migration) on both the moved-file and referrer-rewrite paths.
- **git-history continuity (open resolved by the unified surface).** Combining the H1 retitle with the `git mv` is safe: the moved file's only content delta is the one-line H1 (well within git's rename-similarity threshold, so `git log --follow` survives), and each referrer edit is a one-line change in a separate file — clean to review.
- **Acceptance = a post-build cost+completeness study** (design now, run post-build — reuses the cross-doc harness): `jigc rename` vs plain vs static (allowed a shell one-liner) on a rename-heavy sequence; headline = **turns/cost per rename**, plus dangling refs (over structured managed refs only) + completeness on a deliberately-constructed non-greppable referrer. Pre-registered win: jigc strictly beats plain on cost **and** ≥ static on completeness. Confounds pre-registered: **verb-engagement is a primary measured quantity** (availability ≠ induced-usage; a hand-edit re-incurs block→recovery), static arm gets a real one-liner, rename-error→recovery cycles + small-N noise controlled. The verb also earns a **`worked-examples` flow** (transaction/rollback/collision/forbid-mid-fan-out), separate from the study. Verdict recorded under `completions/artifacts/M35/`.

## 2026-06-28 — M35 Increment 1 planning: decomposition

Cut "the `jigc rename` verb core + the atomic transaction (the risk spike)" into **five ordered single-concern tasks** — the pure engine rewrite primitive (inverse-edge enumeration + list-valued whole-list re-emit, T1) → the `jigc rename` verb + the committed-in-place atomic transaction with `rollback_rename` (T2, the risk spike) → the up-front validation gate (collision / no-op-reslug / mid-fan-out, T3) → the post-commit crash-window self-heal recovery rule (T4) → the advisory prose/unmanaged-mention report (T5). *Why this cut:* the increment ships one top-level verb that atomically repoints every persisted referrer and rolls back cleanly on failure (= [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) flow 37 #1–#5, #8); the pieces sit on serial gate-green seams — a clean producer→consumer (T1 ships the rewrite primitive, T2 consumes it; T3/T5 add guards/reporting around the T2 verb; T4 is a separable reconciliation rule). Risk-first: the pure primitive (T1) is isolated first, then the **committed-store-mutating transaction + its rollback** (T2 — the spike) lands before the guards refine it. **Grounded against the code at HEAD `451a14f`** (the verified reuse facts below). Done-criterion throughout: the named new test green + the full unscoped dev-workflow gate (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo build`). Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M35 Increment 1; design [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename`, [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Edge index lifecycle, [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → Rename detection (the transaction; A+B), [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 37.

- **Inverse-edge enumeration is net-new — verified, not assumed.** `EdgeIndex` stores **forward edges only** (`Edge { from, relation, to }`, `index.rs:62`); `walk_edge(from, relation)` (`index.rs:345`) is forward and `ref_resolves_store` (`index.rs:399`) iterates all edges for the dangling check — **no "referrers-of-X" function exists** (`grep` over `crates/*/src` for an inverse walk is empty). T1's `referrers_of` is a genuine new surface (filter `edges` where `to == target`). The pre-commit integrity assertion reuses `rebuild_committed` (`index.rs:171`) + `ref_resolves_store` (no new check).
- **The list-valued whole-list rewrite reuses existing byte-stable primitives.** A list-valued ref renders as inline-flow `[a, b, c]` (`field_block::Value::List` Display, `", "` separator, `field_block.rs:161`), and `parse → emit` is byte-exact for canonical content (`field_block.rs` round-trip). So the rewrite = read the field value → if `List`, map the one matching element old→new → render `Value::List(...).to_string()` → splice via `write::set_field` (`write.rs:957` — replaces a *present* field's value span byte-stably; verified on the M34 value-bump). `adr.supersedes` is `card "0..*"` (`adr.yaml:21`, list) and `arch-doc.cites` is list-valued; `spec.derived-from → prd` is scalar `card "0..1"` — all three are header/simple `ref` fields `set_field` reaches.
- **The transaction idioms exist in `crates/cli/src/task.rs` (finalize's F3 path) and are reused, not reinvented.** `git_commit` (`task.rs:1994` — runs the user's hooks, **never** `--no-verify`), `path_at_head`, `existing_pathspecs` (`task.rs:1547`), and the captured-pre-image-bytes + `git restore --staged --worktree` rollback idiom (`rollback_promotions`, `task.rs:1568`). All currently private — T2 lifts the ones it reuses to `pub(crate)`. File-state re-baseline reuses `FileStateRecord::{forget, record, get}` (`file_state.rs:86/71/76`) + `hash_bytes` (`file_state.rs:41`); the verb's load/identity/persist skeleton mirrors `crates/cli/src/unmanage.rs::run` (loads schemas + committed index + file-state, re-derives `<type>:<slug>`, mutates, persists) — the other top-level direct-store self-committing op.
- **The clap surface joins the exhaustive dispatch in one motion.** `Command` (`cli.rs:53`) + its exhaustive `match` (`cli.rs:210–272`, with `Unmanage`/`MigrateCorpus` as the top-level direct-store models) — adding `Command::Rename` *requires* its dispatch arm in the same task (a missing arm is a compile error), so the command + its `run_rename` are inseparable (T2). The mid-fan-out markers are `state::list_active_task_ids` (`state.rs:459`) for tasks and `.jigc/milestones/<id>/` dirs (`milestone.rs`); the prose report's tracked-file set is `git ls-files` (respecting `.gitignore`).

- **T1 — inverse-edge referrer enumeration + the list-valued ref-field rewrite primitive (engine, pure).** Add `referrers_of(index: &EdgeIndex, target: &str) -> Vec<Edge>` (the named reverse-walk: the committed edges whose `to == target`) and a ref-field rewrite that, given a referrer's source bytes + the ref field id + `old`→`new`, parses the current value, swaps the one matching element (scalar **or** inline-flow list — re-emitting the canonical whole list), and splices via `write::set_field`. Net-new (no inverse walk today). *Done:* engine unit tests — (a) `referrers_of` returns **exactly** the edges pointing at the target across all three persisted ref-fields (`adr.supersedes`, `arch-doc.cites`, `spec.derived-from`) and **empty** for a doc with no inbound edges; (b) a scalar `derived-from: prd:old` rewrites to `prd:new`; (c) round-trip `render(parse(out)) == out` over a rewritten referrer; the primitive is the **only** new surface (no existing test touched); full gate green. **RED obligation (prove, don't assert — acceptance #8):** the list-valued sibling rewrite is fed a real 3-element list `cites: [adr:a, adr:old, adr:c]` and the test asserts the **exact emitted bytes** `[adr:a, adr:new, adr:c]` — siblings `a`/`c` byte-identical, order and `", "` separator preserved (the whole-list re-emit swaps only the one element), not a trusted reuse claim. **Pin:** `referrers_of` + the rewrite are consumed by the **T2** verb (a clean producer→consumer seam, like M34 Inc-2 T2's `promote_slot_to_repeatable`); wired to production in T2, so not test-only at increment end. Files: `crates/engine/src/index.rs`, `crates/engine/src/write.rs` (+ `crates/engine/src/field_block.rs` if a list-swap helper is cleaner). design_refs: [storage.md](design/storage.md) → Edge index lifecycle; [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename` (step 3).

### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-1 T1 landed: `referrers_of` + the `repoint_ref` rewrite primitive

Two engine elaborations on the plan: (1) `referrers_of` returns **`Vec<&Edge>`** (zero-copy borrow of the sorted index), not `Vec<Edge>` — the consumer (T2) borrows within its repoint loop; cheaper and idiomatic. (2) The plan's "`Value::List` Display" did **not** exist — the list byte-form lived inline in `field_block::emit`. Rather than duplicate it, added **`Value::render()`** as the single canonical value-byte source and refactored `emit` to call it, so `repoint_ref`'s whole-list re-emit and the writer cannot drift (the `", "` separator is defined once). The rewrite primitive is `write::repoint_ref(schema, source, relation, old, new)` — it locates the ref field's section from the schema (`ref_field_section`, the three persisted refs all live on header sections), swaps the one `old` occurrence (scalar replaced whole / list element-swapped), and splices via `set_field`. Absent relation/field/value → `SpliceError::NotPresent`. RED proven: perturbing the list separator to `,` fails the byte-exact test.

- **T2 — the `jigc rename` verb + the committed-in-place atomic transaction with `rollback_rename` (the risk spike).** Add `Command::Rename { old_slug, to (required), slug (optional, valid only with `--to`) }` to `cli.rs` + its dispatch arm `run_rename`, and a new `crates/cli/src/rename.rs` (modelled on `unmanage.rs::run`). The transaction: derive the new slug = `engine::slug::slugify(--to)` (or `--slug`) — so a renamed doc is byte-identical to a freshly-created one of that title; load schemas + committed index + file-state; walk referrers (T1 `referrers_of`) + rewrite each (T1); rewrite the moved doc's H1 to `<New Title>`; **capture pre-image bytes** of the old path + every referrer; apply the rewrites + `git mv` old→new; **re-baseline `file-state` inside the boundary** (`forget(old)` + `record(new)` + re-record every rewritten referrer) + rebuild the index; stage; run the verb's **own pre-commit integrity assertion** (`rebuild_committed` → `ref_resolves_store`, **refuse-commit + rollback** on any dangling); `git_commit` (hooks run, never `--no-verify`); `rollback_rename` restores every captured pre-image + reverses the `git mv` + **the file-state record** on **any** pre-commit failure (file-state is *inside* the rollback inventory, pin I3). *Done:* a real-binary acceptance (`crates/cli/tests/flow37_rename.rs`) over a committed store (an `adr` superseded by another `adr` + cited by an `arch-doc`) — `jigc rename adr:<old> --to "<Title>"` exits 0, emits **one** commit, **both** referrers repointed (`supersedes` + `cites`, whole-list re-emit), the H1 rewritten, the file `git mv`d (`git log --follow` survives), and a follow-up `jigc validate` exits **clean** (zero `schema-conformance.ref-resolves` findings) — acceptance #1, #2 (boundary: only ref-fields mutated); and a **forced pre-commit failure** (a rejecting git hook *or* an injected post-`git mv` error) leaves the store **byte-identical to pre-rename** (no half-moved slug, no dangling ref) — acceptance #5. **Single-concern note:** the atomic transaction and its rollback are **one inseparable unit** — a mutator of committed paths + file-state + index without a rollback is not *atomic*, and this increment's whole identity is "the risk spike" proving atomic rollback (the RED obligation pairs them), so they land as one task / one commit; the command wiring is the surface the acceptance drives through the binary, and the clap variant + dispatch arm are compile-coupled (one motion). Files: `crates/cli/src/rename.rs` (new), `crates/cli/src/cli.rs`, `crates/cli/src/lib.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs` (lift the reused F3 helpers to `pub(crate)`), `crates/cli/tests/flow37_rename.rs` (new). design_refs: [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename` (steps 1, 3–5); [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → Rename detection (the transaction); [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-06-28 (Transaction = full pre-image-capture rollback, pins I3).

### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-1 T2 landed: the `jigc rename` verb + the committed-in-place atomic transaction

Four implementation elaborations on the plan, all in scope: (1) **The edge index is never persisted during the transaction** — `load_committed` already persists the pre-rename index (stamped at the pre-commit HEAD), the integrity assertion rebuilds a *fresh in-memory* index off the mutated tree (`rebuild_committed` → `ref_resolves_store`), and on success the verb calls `index::invalidate` post-commit so the next read rebuilds against the new HEAD (the finalize post-commit step). So no index rollback is needed: a failed rename leaves the pre-rename persisted index untouched and stamp-valid; a successful one self-heals via the invalidate. (2) **Rollback follows the proven `rollback_promotions` split** — tracked paths (the old doc + every referrer, all committed at HEAD) restore via `git restore --staged --worktree` (= byte-identical to HEAD = pre-image), the move's landing is unstaged + dropped (`path_at_head` false → `remove_file`), and **only** the gitignored, non-git-tracked **file-state record** restores from captured pre-image bytes (pin I3 honored: it rides the rollback inventory by bytes since `git restore` can't recover it). (3) **The commit message is written to a tempfile outside the repo** (`std::env::temp_dir()`), so it never pollutes `git status` and never risks being staged. (4) **Referrers are grouped per source doc** (`BTreeMap<from, Vec<relation>>`) so a doc that references the target through more than one relation rewrites once over a running buffer (correctness if a future schema lets one doc cite + supersede the same target). `RenameReport` (old/new identity, paths, title, sorted repointed referrers) renders through `render::rename` + the json projection. The reused F3 helpers `git_run`/`git_commit`/`path_at_head` were lifted to `pub(crate)`; `lib.rs` needed no change (the verb lives in the binary module tree, `main.rs`). RED proven: a rejecting `pre-commit` hook drives the real rollback — the store is left byte-identical (old slug present, new slug absent, referrers untouched, no commit, no managed doc staged).

- **T3 — the up-front validation gate: collision blocks · no-op reslug → retitle-only · mid-fan-out guard.** Add, **before** the T2 transaction runs: (a) **collision** — the derived/`--slug` new slug must be free in the doctype's cascade-resolved location, **excluding the doc's own current slug**; a collision with a *different* committed doc **blocks** (an identity refactor, never the by-task-id join's silent suffix); (b) **no-op reslug** — when the new slug equals the doc's **own** current slug, **degrade to retitle-only**: rewrite the H1 + commit, with **no `git mv` and no referrer repoint** (no identity change → nothing dangles); (c) **mid-fan-out guard** — **block** whenever **any** task working area (`state::list_active_task_ids`) **or** milestone (`.jigc/milestones/<id>/`) is in-flight (coarse guard). *Done:* `flow37_rename.rs` tests assert — a rename onto a *different* existing slug **blocks** (exit ≠ 0, the collision message; acceptance #3); a rename whose new title slugs to the **same** slug performs a **retitle-only** (H1 changed, **no file move**, no referrer edit, one commit); a rename attempted with an active task **and** (separately) with an in-flight milestone each **blocks** with the mid-fan-out message (acceptance #4); the T2 happy-path acceptance stays green. **Single-context guard (increment-workflow #5):** the mid-fan-out check is exercised both with a marker present (**blocks**) **and** absent (the T2 clean path **proceeds**), so the guard is proven not inert. Files: `crates/cli/src/rename.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/flow37_rename.rs`. design_refs: [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename` (step 2, the degenerate-case pins I2); [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-06-28 (`--to` collision blocks; Forbidden mid-fan-out, pin I4).

### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-1 T3 landed: the up-front validation gate

The collision / no-op-reslug / mid-fan-out gate runs before any mutation in `rename::run`, all in scope. Three implementation notes: (1) **The no-op reslug routes through the existing transaction**, not a parallel retitle path — `is_retitle = new_slug == old_slug` skips the referrer census and `apply_and_commit` skips the `git mv` when `old_rel == new_rel`, so the integrity assertion, file-state re-baseline, commit, and `rollback_rename` are reused unchanged (one boundary, no duplication). (2) **The collision check excludes the doc's own slug** via the `!is_retitle` guard (a same-slug "collision" *is* the no-op case, already routed to retitle), then blocks when a *different* committed doc occupies the new path. (3) **The mid-fan-out marker is a coarse OR** over `state::list_active_task_ids` (tasks) and the first sub-dir under `.jigc/milestones/` (milestones), both sorted so the block message is deterministic; an absent dir is no fan-out (not an error). The guard is proven not inert (increment-workflow #5): the T2 happy path + the retitle/collision tests all proceed past it with no marker, while the two new mid-fan-out tests block with a marker present. RED proven: pre-gate the collision test failed on the missing collision message (git mv's "destination exists" is a different string), the retitle test failed on the same-source/dest `git mv` error, and the mid-fan-out tests proceeded to a successful rename.

- **T4 — the post-commit crash-window self-heal recovery rule (reconciliation).** Amend the `reconcile_committed_store` "recorded but now absent on disk" branch (`file_state.rs:395`, which routes `detect_rename`): a committed doc present at a **new** path whose **recorded old path is absent from the committed tree** is **re-baseline-adopted as the rename's landing** (re-key file-state `old→new`), **not** routed to the weak-signal "restore the old file" (which would resurrect a deliberately-renamed-away doc). *Done:* an engine test simulating the crash window — the rename committed (the new path tracked, referrers already repointed) but the file-state record still keyed on the **old** path — drives the reconcile sweep and asserts it **re-baselines** `old→new` with **no** `reconciliation.rename` restore finding emitted, and **self-heals idempotently** on a second sweep; the existing `detect_rename` / `reconcile_committed_store` task-scope tests (uncommitted bare-`git mv` strong/weak signals) stay green. **RED obligation (prove, don't assert):** the crash-window recovery is *proven* by driving the interrupted state through the sweep, not asserted. **Coupling note (settled, not re-opened):** this is the verb's **own-interruption** recovery; the **store-scope OOB bare-`git mv` detection + blocking pre-commit hook** is **Inc-2** (A+B), and the scope-subtraction dedup between this re-baseline and Inc-2's `detect_rename` is settled in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-06-28 (pins I1/B1) — not a fork here. Files: `crates/engine/src/file_state.rs`. design_refs: [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → Rename detection (the transaction, self-healing); [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename` (step 5).

### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-1 T4 landed: the post-commit crash-window self-heal recovery rule

The self-heal lives in `reconcile_committed_store`'s recorded-missing loop (shell-free engine), all in scope. The discriminator that the shell-free sweep uses to distinguish the verb's interrupted landing from a genuine deletion (new helper `rename_landing_present`): for a recorded-missing old path with **no content-hash match** (a content match is the strong-signal bare-`git mv`, left to `detect_rename`), if an untracked candidate (an on-disk `.md` carrying no recorded hash — the renamed doc's new path, baseline-adopted earlier in the same sweep) is present **under the old path's own `location:`** (a rename preserves the doctype, so the landing shares the directory), `forget(old)` and emit no finding; the walk's baseline-adopt of the new path completes the `old→new` re-key. No landing under that location → falls through to `detect_rename` (weak-signal restore = genuine deletion). `detect_rename` itself is **untouched**, so the task-scope strong/weak tests stay green. RED proven: the interrupted state first emitted the weak-signal `reconciliation.rename` restore finding for the old path and kept the stale key; after the amendment the sweep re-keys `old→new` with no finding and is idempotent on a second sweep.

- **T5 — the advisory prose/unmanaged-mention report.** After the transaction, emit a **boundary-safe report** (never a rewrite, never blocks, never changes exit status) of old-slug occurrences in **managed-doc prose** and **unmanaged tracked files** (READMEs, code, tests): a **word-boundary/token match** on the old slug (so `cache` does not match `caches`), scoped to **tracked worktree files** (`git ls-files`, respecting `.gitignore`). This is the determinism boundary's honest line: the CLI rewrites only structured ref-fields and *reports* the prose it cannot author. *Done:* a `flow37_rename.rs` test where the old slug appears in an `arch-doc`'s slot **prose**, a `README.md`, and a source comment — the rename **reports** all three (listed in the verb output), **rewrites none** of them, the report **never** changes exit status, and a `caches`-style near-match is **not** reported (acceptance #2). **RED obligation (prove, don't assert):** the word-boundary discrimination (the `caches` non-match) is proven, not asserted. Files: `crates/cli/src/rename.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/flow37_rename.rs`. design_refs: [write-commands.md](design/write-commands.md) → `jigc rename` (Boundary — the honest line).

### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-1 T5 landed: the advisory prose/unmanaged-mention report

`scan_prose_mentions` runs **post-commit** over `git ls-files` (tracked, `.gitignore`-respecting) for surviving old-slug occurrences: because the transaction has already rewritten every structured ref-field old→new, what remains is exactly the prose + unmanaged mentions the CLI cannot author — so scanning the post-rename tree *naturally* excludes the ref-fields it owns (no allow/deny list needed). The matcher `line_has_token` treats the slug as a token bounded on both sides by a non-token byte (token byte = ASCII-alnum or the slug separators `-`/`_`), so `single-node-cache` matches but `single-node-caches` / `single-node-cache-v2` / `pre-single-node-cache` do not. **Best-effort + advisory:** a `git`/read failure or a binary file is skipped, never an error — the report never changes the verb's exit status. A **retitle-only reports nothing** (the slug is unchanged, so every occurrence is still legitimately current). Surfaced as `RenameReport.prose_mentions` (sorted `<path>:<line>`), rendered after the referrer list. RED proven two ways: the integration test asserts the report states **exactly 3** mentions (a naive `.contains` scan over-counts the README's `single-node-caches` near-match to 4 → fails), backed by focused `line_has_token` unit tests on the match/near-match split. Reused: `task::git_capture` lifted to `pub(crate)`. Files: `crates/cli/src/rename.rs`, `crates/cli/src/render.rs`, `crates/cli/src/task.rs`, `crates/cli/tests/flow37_rename.rs`.

## 2026-06-28 — M35 Increment 2 planning: decomposition

Cut "the out-of-band backstop (A + B)" into **four ordered single-concern tasks** — the read-only OOB-rename detection at store scope + the scope-subtraction dedup (T1, engine) → the exit-flipping exception for the store-scope rename finding on `jigc validate` (T2, CLI) → the pre-commit hook's this-commit staged-pathset block (T3, CLI, the masking-trap RED) → the reconciliation route-hint flip to advertise `jigc rename` (T4). *Why this cut:* the increment ships the safety net under the new verb — a bare `git mv` committed *without* `jigc rename` is **caught and blocked** (= [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) flow 37 #6, #7). The pieces sit on serial gate-green seams: T1 (engine) makes the store sweep *surface* the OOB rename as one `reconciliation.rename` finding (deduped against the dangling-ref family); T2 and T3 are the two **independent** CLI manifestations of "B blocks" — T2 flips the `jigc validate` *command* exit, T3 makes the warn-only *hook* block the commit — and neither keys on the other (the hook keys on the *finding*, never the exit code, per [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Auto-firing the sweep), so they are separate single concerns each with its own red step; T4 is an isolated route-text flip. T1 lands first because both T2 and T3 consume the finding it surfaces. **Whole-scope coverage:** roadmap bullet 1 → T1; bullet 2 (exit-flipping exception + hook staged-pathset block + masking-trap RED) → T2 + T3; bullet 3 → T4. The A+B mechanism is **fully settled** in the locked design — no fork ([validation.md](design/validation.md) → Store-scope re-validation: recorded-but-missing rename detection (277), Exit semantics — two exit-flipping exceptions (279), The M19 pre-commit backstop — scoped to *this commit's* moves (283); [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → Out-of-band rename, A+B (105–108)). **Grounded against the code at HEAD `77e2e97`** (the verified reuse facts below). Done-criterion throughout: the named new test green + the full unscoped dev-workflow gate (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo build`). Cross-ref [roadmap.md](implementation/roadmap.md) → M35 Increment 2; design [validation.md](design/validation.md) → Store-scope re-validation / Exit semantics / the M19 backstop, [reconciliation.md](design/reconciliation.md) → Rename detection (A+B), [worked-examples.md](design/worked-examples.md) → flow 37.

- **The store-sweep building blocks exist and are reused — verified, not assumed.** `detect_rename` (`file_state.rs:651`) is already **pure + non-mutating** (it reads `path`/`from`/`recorded_hash`/`untracked` and returns findings, no `record`/index write) — so wiring it at store scope keeps the file↔CLI-state family's *detect-without-absorb* bar. The recorded-missing enumeration logic already exists inside `reconcile_committed_store` (`file_state.rs:380–413`: snapshot recorded persisted paths → filter to those absent on disk → collect untracked candidates → `detect_rename`), but **that path mutates** (`record.forget`, baseline-adopt) — T1 must lift a **read-only** enumerator (no record write), not call `reconcile_committed_store`. `referrers_of(index, target)` (`index.rs:150`, the Inc-1 reverse-walk) returns a target's inbound edges → it computes exactly the renamed slug's inbound edges to subtract. `validate_store_families` already builds the in-memory `committed_index` (`validate.rs:440`) immediately before `ref_resolves_store` (`validate.rs:441`) and Family 3 (`detect_committed_store`, present-docs-only) runs before it (`validate.rs:431`) — so the recorded-missing detect slots into the family order *before* `ref_resolves_store` with no reordering of the existing families.

It is called at `validate.rs:441` (the store sweep) **and** `rename.rs:281` (the verb's own pre-commit integrity assertion). Scope-subtraction = skip edges whose `to` is a renamed-away slug; the executor may either add an exclusion-set parameter (both callers update in one commit — `rename.rs` passes empty, since the verb's own transaction has no concurrent OOB rename) **or** filter `ref_resolves_store`'s output inside `validate_store_families` (no signature change). Either is byte-equivalent in behavior; the design pins the *result* (scope-subtraction, not mere ordering — [validation.md](design/validation.md):277), not the mechanism.

These constructors are shared by task scope (`reconcile_committed_store`) and the new store-scope detect, so the assertions to update are bounded: `crates/cli/tests/file_state_soundness.rs` + the `file_state.rs` unit tests (the only sites mentioning the placeholder, `grep` confirmed). ### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-2 T1 landed: read-only OOB-rename detection at store scope + the scope-subtraction dedup

`detect_committed_store_renames` (the non-mutating, read-only lift of `reconcile_committed_store`'s recorded-missing arm) now runs in `validate_store_families`' file↔CLI-state family, **before** Family 4 (`ref_resolves_store`), returning the renamed-away `<type>:<slug>` identities. **Mechanism choice (the planner's executor's-choice fork, settled):** scope-subtraction is an **exclusion-set parameter on `ref_resolves_store`** (both callers updated — `rename.rs:283` passes empty), not an output filter — it skips edges whose `to` is a renamed slug *before* the reachability walk, so the rename's inbound edges never reach the dangling-finding path. The design pins the *result* (one `reconciliation.rename`, zero competing `ref-resolves` dangles), not the mechanism, so either was conformant; the param is the more self-documenting and precise (filters by `to`, which the finding's `from`-keyed address cannot reconstruct). Read-only proven: `record` is borrowed `&`; the `jigc rename` crash-window landing is *suppressed* (skip, no `forget`) — the mutating self-heal stays the task-scope reconcile's job. New engine tests: `validate_store_oob_rename_subtracts_inbound_refs_keeps_unrelated_dangle` (the RED — fails if wired without subtraction) + `validate_store_detects_referrerless_oob_rename`.

### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-2 T2 landed: the exit-flipping exception for the store-scope rename finding (`jigc validate`)

A store-scope `reconciliation.rename` finding now flips `jigc validate`'s exit non-zero with JSON `report_only: false` — the **second** exit-flipping exception ([validation.md](design/validation.md) → Exit semantics), joining `pack-probe-integrity.*`: an OOB `git mv` is a structural-identity event *this commit* introduced, not pre-existing content rot, so flipping its exit honors (does not violate) the report-only rationale. Every other content finding (a `file-state.hash-matches` drift, a dangling `ref-resolves`, a stale `doc-code` anchor) stays report-only / exit 0. **Lockstep choice:** the decision is a single shared `render::validation_store_exit_flips(report)` (keyed on `f.probe == "pack-probe-integrity" || f.code == "reconciliation.rename"`) that the dispatcher's exit code, the JSON `report_only` field, and the human/agent trailer all call — so the three can't diverge. The trailer gains a third (rename) wording distinct from the probe-integrity "could not complete" line; route prose left to T4. New CLI tests: `flow37_rename::store_scope_oob_rename_flips_exit_and_report_only` (real binary, the RED — exits 0 / report_only true before the flip) + `store_scope_content_drift_stays_report_only_exit_zero`; render unit test extended with the rename trailer case.

### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-2 T3 landed: the pre-commit hook blocks on a this-commit rename, masking-trap-safe

The warn-only `precommit_hook_body` now also **blocks** (`exit 1`) when this commit *itself* stages an out-of-band managed-doc rename; the unchanged `doc-code` warn-only path is preserved verbatim ahead of it. **Mechanism choice (the planner's pure-shell-vs-jigc-helper fork, settled to pure shell):** the new `PRECOMMIT_RENAME_BLOCK` is a literal-`&str` shell fragment (interpolated whole into the `format!`, so its `${…}`/`awk {…}` braces stay verbatim) that (1) extracts each rename's path pair from the strong-signal finding's route `git mv <new> <old>` via `grep -o`, (2) computes this commit's staged path set rename-aware (`git diff --cached --name-status --find-renames | cut -f2- | tr '\t' '\n'`, matching `combine.rs`'s R/D/A handling), and (3) blocks iff some pair has **both** paths in the staged set (an `awk` set-membership pass over a `---`-separated two-stream feed — no `awk -v` newline hazard). A rename hit **outside** the staged set warns + exits 0 (the masking-trap guard). Pure shell over a `jigc` helper because it adds **no new CLI surface** (no inventory/describe goldens) and the real-binary acceptance tests fully guard the route-coupling end-to-end — a route reword that broke the grep would fail `commit_blocks_on_this_commit_oob_rename`. The block keys on the **finding + staged-set intersection**, never on `jigc validate`'s exit code (independent of T2). In the wrapped-foreign-hook case the mid-body `exit 1` survives (only the trailing `exit 0` is stripped), so a this-commit rename blocks even when wrapping a foreign hook. New real-binary tests in `precommit_hook_acceptance.rs`: `commit_blocks_on_this_commit_oob_rename` (a) + `commit_does_not_block_when_oob_rename_is_pre_existing` (the masking-trap RED); golden `precommit_hook_body_golden` updated to the spliced body.

## 2026-06-28 — M35 Increment 3 planning: decomposition

Cut "the cost+completeness study (post-build acceptance)" into **five ordered single-concern tasks** — the study corpus + rename-heavy prompts incl. the deliberately non-greppable referrer (T1) → the three arms (jigc-with-`rename` *performs*, static gets a shell one-liner, plain) + the template/runner glue (T2) → the verb-engagement extractor committed in-repo + rename-aware (T3) → the cost+completeness metrics: per-rename cost/turns headline, dangling over structured managed refs only, completeness on the non-greppable referrer, verb-engagement + error→recovery aggregation (T4) → the pre-registration + RUNBOOK with the win condition/confounds/void-tripwires + the no-API "all green at handoff" verification (T5). *Why this cut:* the increment **designs and builds the study, verified runnable at zero API cost**, reusing + extending the cross-doc harness; the pieces sit on a clean producer→consumer chain — T1 fixes the inputs (corpus + prompts) every later piece consumes, T2 builds the runtime arms over that corpus, T3 ships the per-transcript extractor the runner records, T4 measures the committed HEADs + aggregates, T5 documents + certifies the whole. Each is an independent harness file (Python/bash/markdown) with its own selftest/verification — no shared compile gate one task could break, so single-concern cuts cleanly.

- **Scope boundary (settled, not narrowed): design now, run post-build.** The M35-planning settled decision ([DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) → 2026-06-28 M35 planning, *Acceptance*) pins "design now, **run post-build**." The **paid matrix run + the verdict recorded under `completions/artifacts/M35/`** is the **post-build human acceptance step** (the cross-doc [RUNBOOK](completions/artifacts/cross-doc-refint-study/RUNBOOK.md) steps 3–4: live-auth probe → single live certification → matrix → aggregate+judge+verdict) — it needs OAuth + real API spend + docker, which the automated executor cannot do, and it is precedented as a human/orchestrator-driven artifact ([increment-workflow.md](implementation/increment-workflow.md) → the M8 capability-gap artifact). So Inc-3's **executor deliverable is the fully-designed, no-API-verified study** (the cross-doc "State at handoff — all green, no API spent" bar); the *run* is **not** silently dropped — it is the settled post-build human step. The Validate phase asserts the *buildable* deliverable (harness runnable + every selftest green + pre-registration complete), **not** a verdict.

### 2026-06-28 — M35 Inc-3 T2 landed: the three arms (jigc-performs · static one-liner · plain) + template/runner glue

`harness/build-templates-refint.sh` builds **exactly three** arm templates over T1's seed corpus and certifies the four done-criterion bars (3 arms · `docs/` byte-identical across arms · jigc arm exposes `jigc rename` · static arm carries the `git mv`+`sd`/`grep` one-liner); `harness/run-sequence-refint.sh` + `harness/run-matrix-refint.sh` collapse the cross-doc 5-arm ladder to `{jigc, static, plain}`. Three elaborations on the plan, all in scope: (1) **The "real Inc-2 backstop hook" is the native `jigc setup` hook, NOT a copied custom one** — unlike the cross-doc study (which `cp`'d `blocking-pre-commit-refint` because the then-shipped hook was warn-only), the post-Inc-2 `precommit_hook_body` itself blocks a this-commit OOB `git mv` of a managed doc; build-templates asserts the hook is present and carries the `out-of-band managed-doc rename staged in this commit` block (a guard the backstop is genuinely installed), and copies nothing. (2) **Adapter-advertisement = `arms/jigc-CLAUDE.md` appended to the setup-written project `CLAUDE.md`** — the shipped `.jigc/AGENT.md` is generic (never names `rename`), so the verb-engagement confound needs the project-layer advertisement; appended (not replaced) so the `@.jigc/AGENT.md` interface pointer survives, and outside `docs/` so byte-identity holds. (3) **A loud precondition guard** — build-templates runs `jigc rename --help` up front and fails exit-2 if the binary lacks the verb (a stale install), so the no-API handoff bar (T5) fails fast rather than mid-build. The static one-liner (`arms/static-CLAUDE.md`) is a **real** baseline (`git mv` + `sd`, `grep` fallback, post-rename `grep` verification), not a straw manual rule. run-sequence keeps `ANALYZE` pointed out-of-repo — internalizing it is T3's concern (clean producer→consumer seam). Verified: all four done-criterion OK lines print with `JIGC=target/debug/jigc`; the stale-binary precondition fails exit-2; the plain arm builds with no `CLAUDE.md`/`.jigc`/hook and `measure-refint.py --no-jigc` reports 0 dangling (the omitting case is honest, inert, not error). No Rust touched — full gate trivially green.

## 2026-07-02 — M35 acceptance study run: the pre-registered cost-win HOLDS (the spine closes)

The post-build cost+completeness study ran per [RUNBOOK](completions/artifacts/M35/RUNBOOK.md) (auth probe → 1 certified sequence → the paid matrix → aggregate): **22 valid sequences × 8 edits = 176 cold-agent runs**, 0 tripwires, 0 auth failures (one transient-network Opus sequence discarded whole + re-run per protocol), $30.60. **Verdict: WIN** ([VERDICT.md](completions/artifacts/M35/VERDICT.md)) — jigc **strictly cheaper per rename than plain** (Sonnet 4.6 $0.080 vs $0.125; Sonnet 5 $0.129 vs $0.262; Opus 4.8 $0.193 vs $0.266) **and ≥ static on completeness** (1.0 vs 0.875 / 1.0), at **3.5–4.6 turns/rename vs 8.3–14.4** manual. Both pre-registered confounds cleared: **verb-engagement 100%** (64/64 jigc edits used `jigc rename` — availability *did* induce usage) and **0 rename-error→recovery cycles**. **Amendment 1** (recorded pre-run, human-decided): Sonnet 5 shipped between handoff and run, so the pinned Sonnet-4.6+Opus-4.8 matrix carried the verdict unchanged and a supplementary 3-arm **Sonnet-5 cell** ran as the current-generation robustness check — *why:* ecological validity + the harder test. Its finding: **capability closes the correctness gap (plain/static reach 1.0 uninstructed) but widens the cost gap** (plain-5 = 14.4 turns/rename) — the cost win is the durable differentiator, detection the capability-dependent backstop; "own the verb, don't police the mistake" is the empirically-backed rule for future differentiators (flips [cost-of-enforcement](ideas/cost-of-enforcement.md) on this surface). Honest bounds: directional not powered (2–3 reps/cell, flagged underpowered; ordering identical in every rep), synthetic seed, the non-greppable construction is prompt-side only (a thorough agent derives the slug mid-edit — Sonnet 5 did). **With this verdict M35 is complete and the roadmap spine (M1–M35) is closed**; remaining is the go-live decision (which fires the deferred `jigc`-name choice, [decisions-pending.md](implementation/decisions-pending.md)).

The go-live gate ([READINESS-ASSESSMENT.md](READINESS-ASSESSMENT.md), 2026-06-21: "M33 + M34 + a value gate that actually clears") is **adjudicated met** — the stale "Not yet" is superseded by a dated banner on the doc itself.
